Phase 5 Protect: declare biases, mitigations, what the test does not prove, and implicit assumptions.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. No prices; measure effort in time and people.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] There are >= 8 atomic and falsifiable assumptions, with at least one per each of the 4 categories.
- [ ] ONE single riskiest assumption is isolated, justified by high impact + low evidence with explicit scores.
- [ ] The assumption follows the format "We believe that [subject] will do or value [observable behavior] because [reason]".
- [ ] The test is the cheapest available to refute that assumption, consistent with {{RECURSOS_DISPONIBLES}}, and includes protocol and recruitment.
- [ ] The falsification criterion (metric + numeric threshold + minimum sample + window) is defined BEFORE running.
- [ ] The test can return a NO; it does not measure vanity.
- [ ] Closes with conditional pass/fail decision and the next assumption in the queue.
- [ ] Declares biases to control, what the test does NOT prove, and implicit assumptions.
Expected deliverable: RAT design document with the 8 numbered blocks, in neutral and professional English, ready to run this week.
spec-producto_discovery_continuous_inter:
[inputs]
- EQUIPO: {{EQUIPO}} > Composition and capacity of the product trio (PM, design, engineering), weekly hours available for discovery, and prior interviewing experience level
- SEGMENTO_CLIENTE: {{SEGMENTO_CLIENTE}} > Segment or profile to interview (role, context, inclusion and exclusion criteria to avoid fan bias)
- OPORTUNIDAD_O_DECISION: {{OPORTUNIDAD_O_DECISION}} > Opportunity or product decision the interviews should illuminate this cycle
- FUENTES_PARTICIPANTES: {{FUENTES_PARTICIPANTES}} > Channels for recruitment (user base, support, sales, panel, community) and known access restrictions
- HERRAMIENTA_AGENDAMIENTO: {{HERRAMIENTA_AGENDAMIENTO}} > Available scheduling/automation tool (optional; if none, assume manual scheduling and note it)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
The team needs to move from sporadic research to continuous discovery: sustained weekly customer contact that feeds decisions in real time. The challenge is not doing one interview but sustaining the rhythm week after week without it eroding from lack of participants, scattered synthesis, or absence of ownership. Three recurring failure modes to prevent from the design: recruitment dries up, synthesis never touches the roadmap, and only satisfied customers are interviewed. An operable plan unlocks evidence-based decisions from fresh input, reduces the risk of building the wrong thing, and turns learning into a team habit, not a one-time project.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior product discovery coach with experience running continuous interviewing programs in the style of Teresa Torres (Continuous Discovery Habits), supported by opportunity mapping and story-based interviews.

Design a weekly continuous interviewing plan and deliver:
1. Cadence table: realistic interviews/week based on the capacity of {{EQUIPO}} (default rule: start with 1 per week and increase only when synthesis stays current), who conducts and who observes in the trio rotating roles, and a recurring protected calendar time window.
2. Continuous recruitment engine: prioritized sources from {{FUENTES_PARTICIPANTES}} with inclusion and exclusion criteria (avoid interviewing only fans), automated scheduling flow with {{HERRAMIENTA_AGENDAMIENTO}}, non-monetary incentives, and an over-recruitment buffer of 30 to 50 percent against cancellations. Recruitment always runs one week ahead.
3. Brief and respectful invitation template aligned to {{SEGMENTO_CLIENTE}}: subject, body, duration, what is asked of the participant, and no-show/rescheduling policy.
4. Script of 6 to 8 questions based on concrete past stories (not hypothetical or predictive), anchored to {{OPORTUNIDAD_O_DECISION}}, with deep-dive probes (tell me more about that time; what was happening just before; what did you do after).
5. Weekly synthesis routine: note capture, snapshot of the emerging opportunity tree, and explicit connection of each insight with a product decision (keep, discard, deepen, build).
6. Governance loop: brief trio ritual (15-30 min/week) to review findings and adjust course, with a named owner and rhythm health criteria.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Interpretation: confirm the team's real capacity, customer access, and the opportunity/decision under research; if an essential input is missing or ambiguous, ask for it before continuing and do not invent data.
Phase 2 - Cadence and recruitment: size sustainable interviews/week (conservative before ambitious) and design the recruitment engine with buffer; recruitment runs one week ahead.
Phase 3 - Instruments: write invitation and story-based script; anchor each question to the opportunity/decision and eliminate any question that asks to predict the future or validate an already-decided solution.
Phase 4 - Synthesis and governance: define the capture/mapping routine and the trio ritual; close each week by connecting insights to decisions and reviewing rhythm health (show rate, weeks with zero interviews, age of the last actioned insight).
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The cadence is realistic for the declared capacity, starts conservatively, and specifies a protected calendar time window.
- [ ] Recruitment runs one week ahead and includes a 30-50 percent buffer, non-monetary incentives, and an inclusion/exclusion criterion that avoids fan bias.
- [ ] The invitation is brief, respectful, and carries a no-show/rescheduling policy.
- [ ] The script uses past-story-based questions, without hypotheticals or predictive questions, anchored to the opportunity/decision, with deep-dive probes.
- [ ] Each synthesis insight is connected to a concrete product decision (keep/discard/deepen/build).
- [ ] The governance loop defines who decides, how often, and how rhythm health is measured.
- [ ] Assumptions marked [ASSUMPTION] with a list of what still needs confirming; no prices or "free" language; neutral and professional English, no emojis.
Expected deliverable: operable one-page plan (cadence table, invitation template, 6 to 8 question script, synthesis routine format) plus a brief anti-patterns appendix, ready to start next week.
spec-producto_discovery_persona_synthesi:
[inputs]
- PRODUCTO_O_PROBLEMA: {{PRODUCTO_O_PROBLEMA}} > Product, feature, or business problem that motivates the discovery
- FUENTES_DE_INVESTIGACION: {{FUENTES_DE_INVESTIGACION}} > Type and content of the qualitative data: interview notes, support tickets, surveys, usability transcripts
- NUMERO_FUENTES: {{NUMERO_FUENTES}} > Approximate number of participants or records supporting the synthesis
- NUMERO_PERSONAS: {{NUMERO_PERSONAS}} > How many personas to synthesize (recommended 2 to 4; the pattern drives the number) (optional)
- DECISION_A_DESBLOQUEAR: {{DECISION_A_DESBLOQUEAR}} > Pending product decision these personas should inform (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
The team accumulated qualitative research about {{PRODUCTO_O_PROBLEMA}} but the findings are still scattered in {{FUENTES_DE_INVESTIGACION}}, without an actionable structure. Synthesizing them into behavior-based personas converts that noise into a shared language for prioritization: the team stops discussing opinions and starts making decisions based on patterns with evidence. Done well, this unlocks {{DECISION_A_DESBLOQUEAR}} and reduces the risk of building for users who do not exist. Done poorly, it produces decorative marketing personas that nobody uses to decide.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior product researcher specialized in qualitative discovery and jobs-to-be-done synthesis.
Deliverable: {{NUMERO_PERSONAS}} actionable personas from {{FUENTES_DE_INVESTIGACION}} ({{NUMERO_FUENTES}} sources). Steps:
1. Code the findings: extract recurring behaviors, motivations, and pains; label each with its source.
2. Group by similarity of behavior and job-to-be-done, never by demographics; demographics enter only as descriptive context, never as a segmentation axis.
3. For each cluster build a persona with: name and one-line archetype; context and situation; real goals; pains with evidence; concrete triggers that initiate the search for a solution; adoption objections and barriers; 2 to 3 verbatim quotes that support the pattern.
4. Assign each persona a confidence level (high = 3+ coinciding sources; medium = 2; low = 1) based on how many sources support it.
5. Close with a map of what product decisions each persona unlocks and what hypotheses remain open for validation in the next cycle.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Coding: read all the material, extract evidence units with their source, discard unsupported attributes.
Phase 2 Clustering: group by behavior and job-to-be-done; name each cluster's pattern; a cluster supported by a single source is reported as a weak signal, not inflated to a persona.
Phase 3 Synthesis: write each persona with all its fields; every claim is tied to evidence or marked [ASSUMPTION].
Phase 4 Activation: connect each persona to decisions and open hypotheses and assign confidence.
Edge cases: if two clusters share the same job and only differ in context, merge them into one persona with variants instead of duplicating. If a quote contradicts the cluster pattern, record it as a tension to validate, not discard it. If the material is biased toward a single channel (e.g., only support tickets), declare it as a representativeness limit.
If the raw content or number of sources is missing, ask for them before synthesizing; never invent quotes or segments.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- Each persona is sustained by traceable evidence; none mixes demographics with behavior as the grouping criterion.
- Triggers express the real job-to-be-done (the moment that initiates the search), not generic traits or personality descriptions.
- Each persona includes 2 to 3 real verbatim quotes taken from the sources, never fabricated or paraphrased as if textual.
- Each unsupported inference is marked [ASSUMPTION]; each persona has a confidence level with its source-count rule.
- Weak signals (single testimony) are reported separately without being promoted to a persona.
- The representativeness limits of the corpus (channel bias, sample size) are declared.
- The close connects personas to {{DECISION_A_DESBLOQUEAR}} and prioritized open hypotheses.
Expected deliverable: document with {{NUMERO_PERSONAS}} actionable personas, verbatim quotes, confidence levels, weak signals, representativeness limits, and a map of decisions and hypotheses for the next discovery cycle.
spec-producto_discovery_empathy_map:
[inputs]
- SEGMENTO_USUARIO: {{SEGMENTO_USUARIO}} > Segment or persona to map (role, usage context, main jobs)
- OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO: {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} > Decision or outcome the map should enable (prioritize roadmap, align team, validate problem)
- FUENTES_EVIDENCIA: {{FUENTES_EVIDENCIA}} > Available evidence: transcripts, surveys, support tickets, field notes, usage data
- NUM_OPORTUNIDADES: {{NUM_OPORTUNIDADES}} > Number of prioritized opportunities to derive, between 3 and 5 (optional, default 3)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
The product, design, and engineering team operates with different and tacit views of the user, which scatters decisions and priorities. Building an Empathy Map for the segment {{SEGMENTO_USUARIO}} creates a single shared view of whom we serve, translating research evidence into actionable empathy. It unlocks team alignment, evidence-based opportunity prioritization, and a solid discovery foundation for {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}. Limit: the map describes one segment; if {{FUENTES_EVIDENCIA}} mixes several profiles, segment or declare the scope before mapping.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior UX researcher specialized in product discovery, with mastery of the Empathy Map (Dave Gray / XPLANE) and its integration with jobs-to-be-done.

Deliverable: a complete and actionable Empathy Map for {{SEGMENTO_USUARIO}}, derived from {{FUENTES_EVIDENCIA}}, that enables {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}. Steps:
1. Review the available evidence and {{ADJUNTOS}}; if it is missing or insufficient to support inferences, request it before continuing. Do not invent quotes, emotions, or behaviors.
2. Classify each observation in the four quadrants: SAYS (verbatim textual phrases), THINKS (tacit beliefs, doubts, and concerns), DOES (observed actions and behaviors), FEELS (emotion, intensity, and trigger).
3. Anchor each item to its source (quote or paraphrase). Mark as [ASSUMPTION] any inference without direct evidence support.
4. Synthesize PAINS (frustrations, obstacles, risks to avoid) and GAINS (sought outcomes and benefits), derived from the quadrants, not stated in the abstract.
5. Identify at least one revealing tension or contradiction between quadrants (for example, says vs does) and explain why it matters.
6. Derive {{NUM_OPORTUNIDADES}} prioritized product opportunities, each anchored to a concrete map observation, formulated as a problem to solve (not a closed solution), and ordered by impact on {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} and confidence in the evidence.
7. List the key assumptions to validate in the next round, indicating for each how to falsify it (method and expected signal).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Understanding: confirm segment, business objective, and evidence scope; if there are critical gaps or mixed profiles, ask for them or segment.
Phase 2 - Classification: place each observation in its quadrant (Says, Thinks, Does, Feels), citing or paraphrasing the source and tagging [ASSUMPTION] when applicable. If an observation fits two quadrants, assign it to the one with the most direct evidence.
Phase 3 - Synthesis: derive Pains and Gains from the quadrants and highlight revealing contradictions.
Phase 4 - Activation: prioritize opportunities anchored to evidence and consolidate pending assumptions with their falsification criterion.
Phase 5 - Delivery: structure the map in table or list format by section, ready to paste into a collaborative tool and present to the team.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- The four quadrants (Says, Thinks, Does, Feels) are present and differentiated without overlapping.
- Each observation is anchored to evidence (quote or source) or labeled [ASSUMPTION]; zero invented quotes, emotions, or behaviors.
- Pains and Gains are derived from the map, not stated in the abstract.
- At least one revealing tension between quadrants is identified, with its why.
- There are between 3 and 5 prioritized opportunities, each linked to a concrete observation, formulated as a problem, and ordered by impact and confidence.
- Assumptions to validate are listed with their falsification method.
- Segment scope declared; no profile mixing without notice.
Expected deliverable: Empathy Map in table or list format by section (Says / Thinks / Does / Feels / Pains / Gains / Opportunities / Assumptions to validate), in neutral and professional English, ready to paste into a collaborative tool and present to the team.
spec-consulting_diagnostico_situacion_ac:
[inputs]
- PROCESO_O_AREA: {{PROCESO_O_AREA}} > Process or area to diagnose, end-to-end, with its trigger (e.g., "B2B customer billing cycle, from PO issuance to reconciled collection")
- OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO: {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} > Why the diagnosis is being done and what decision it enables (e.g., "reduce the collection cycle to free working capital")
- ACTORES_ROLES: {{ACTORES_ROLES}} > People, teams, or roles involved and their responsibilities in the process
- SISTEMAS_HERRAMIENTAS: {{SISTEMAS_HERRAMIENTAS}} > Systems, platforms, and tools in use, with their role in the flow
- DOLORES_PERCIBIDOS: {{DOLORES_PERCIBIDOS}} > Already known pains, complaints, or symptoms (optional; if none, write "To be assessed")
- EVIDENCIA_DISPONIBLE: {{EVIDENCIA_DISPONIBLE}} > Metrics, documents, records, or interviews to support findings (optional; if none, write "No formal evidence")
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need an honest and verifiable snapshot of the current state (As-Is) of the indicated process or area, before proposing any solution. A rigorous diagnosis converts scattered perceptions into a measurable baseline: it reveals where the real pain is, distinguishes symptom from root cause, exposes which capabilities are missing, and shows what evidence supports each claim. This unlocks intervention prioritization, prevents solving the wrong problem, and provides a comparison point against the future state. The costly mistake this diagnosis prevents is jumping to the To-Be on unvalidated assumptions.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior organizational diagnosis consultant, expert in As-Is assessment, process mapping (SIPOC/BPMN), and capability maturity evaluation.

Produce a current situation diagnosis with these components:
1. Executive summary of 5 to 7 lines with the process status, the dominant finding, and the overall diagnosis confidence (high/medium/low based on evidence).
2. SIPOC table (Supplier, Input, Process, Output, Customer) that delimits the scope, with the process trigger and explicit within/outside boundaries.
3. Numbered step-by-step As-Is flow: for each step, responsible party, system, input/output, decision point, and handoff.
4. Pain table: symptom, probable root cause, evidence or [ASSUMPTION], impact (qualitative or quantitative), frequency.
5. Maturity table across five dimensions (people, process, technology, data, governance) with a 1-5 score and justification per dimension (not just the number).
6. Close: 3 to 5 critical findings prioritized by impact x frequency, gaps against the implicit desired state, and open questions for validation, separated from the findings.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Scope and context: delimit the end-to-end process, its trigger, its boundaries, and the business rationale; confirm what is within and outside scope before mapping.
Phase 2 - As-Is map: produce the SIPOC and activity sequence with responsible parties, systems, decision points, and handoffs; mark where the flow branches or waits.
Phase 3 - Pains and capabilities: identify bottlenecks, rework, waits, errors, and risks with their evidence; for each pain separate symptom from root cause; score capability maturity from 1 to 5.
Phase 4 - Synthesis: prioritize findings by impact x frequency, expose gaps, and leave open validation questions.
Transversal rules: tag each claim as verified data or [ASSUMPTION]; never present inferences as facts. If the evidence is scarce, declare the diagnosis confidence and what additional assessment would raise it. If an essential data point is missing, ask for it in a brief list before executing; do not invent scope or figures.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
- Scope is delimited: trigger, within/outside boundaries, and business rationale explicit.
- SIPOC complete and coherent with the numbered flow; no orphan inputs or outputs.
- Each flow step names the responsible party, system, decision point, and handoff.
- Each pain separates symptom from probable root cause and indicates evidence or [ASSUMPTION]; no inferences disguised as facts.
- The five capabilities are scored 1-5 with justification, not merely asserted.
- Critical findings are prioritized by impact x frequency and distinguished from open questions.
- Overall diagnosis confidence is declared when evidence is partial.
- Neutral and professional English; no premature solutions (this is As-Is, not To-Be).
Expected deliverable: an As-Is diagnosis document with executive summary and overall confidence, SIPOC with trigger and boundaries, numbered flow, pain table with root cause, capability maturity table, and close with prioritized findings and validation questions.
spec-consulting_arbol_problemas_issue_tr:
[inputs]
- PROBLEMA: {{PROBLEMA}} > Symptom or business problem to decompose, in one or two sentences
- METRICA_BASE: {{METRICA_BASE}} > Affected metric with its current baseline and, if applicable, the prior figure
- META_HORIZONTE: {{META_HORIZONTE}} > Target outcome and timeframe to resolve it
- EJE_CORTE: {{EJE_CORTE}} > Preferred axis for splitting the first level: funnel, segment, geography, economic lever, etc. (optional)
- CONTEXTO: {{CONTEXTO}} > Business, revenue model, segments, or relevant constraints (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need to convert a vague business problem into a structured problem tree that allows me to diagnose the root cause and decide where to invest the analysis first. The objective is to move from an unexplained symptom to a MECE map of prioritized hypotheses that unlocks a diagnostic plan, avoiding jumping to solutions before understanding the problem. A well-structured tree converts weeks of scattered exploration into an ordered sequence of validations, and a poor cut (overlapping axes, levels mixing cause and solution) multiplies the work and hides the real cause.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior strategy consultant trained at a top-tier firm (McKinsey/BCG style), expert in problem structuring, MECE logic, and hypothesis-driven diagnosis.

Deliverable: a MECE problem tree (issue tree) of up to three levels, with falsifiable hypotheses per leaf node, a prioritization matrix, and a diagnostic plan. Steps:
1. Reframe {{PROBLEMA}} as a single, specific, and measurable decision question, anchored in {{METRICA_BASE}} and {{META_HORIZONTE}}. If the metric, baseline, goal, horizon, or scope is missing or ambiguous, ask for them before continuing.
2. Declare the tree type: diagnostic (why it occurs, to find root cause) or solution (how to resolve it, if the cause is already known). Justify the choice in one line.
3. Build the tree. Level 1: 3 to 5 branches under a single named cutting axis (use {{EJE_CORTE}} if specified; if not, propose the most explanatory one and explain why). Levels 2 and 3: disaggregate each branch, "one axis per level" rule, until reaching testable hypotheses.
4. For each leaf branch: falsifiable hypothesis + data or analysis that confirms or rules it out + probable data source, using {{CONTEXTO}} and {{ADJUNTOS}}.
5. Prioritize the leaves in an impact potential (high/medium/low) x validation effort (high/medium/low) matrix; mark the 3 branches to tackle first with their justification.
6. Define the diagnostic next steps for those 3 branches and the decision that each finding unlocks.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 — Framing: translate the symptom into a measurable decision question; set the metric, baseline, goal, and horizon.
Phase 2 — Axis selection: select a single cutting criterion for level 1 and verify it MECE (no overlaps between branches, no gaps leaving cases out). If two axes compete, justify which explains more variance.
Phase 3 — Decomposition: branch top-down until reaching falsifiable hypotheses; maintain "one axis per level" and do not mix cause with solution on the same level.
Phase 4 — Hypotheses and evidence: per leaf, write the hypothesis, its falsification test, and the data source; mark every unverified claim with [ASSUMPTION].
Phase 5 — Prioritization: place each leaf in the impact x effort matrix and select the attack front; prioritize quick wins (high impact, low effort) and name causes that could be simultaneous.
Phase 6 — Plan: translate the top 3 branches into diagnostic next steps with the decision they unlock.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reframe what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- The root question is unique, measurable, and time-bound (metric + baseline + goal + horizon).
- The tree type (diagnostic or solution) is declared and justified.
- Level 1 uses a single named cutting axis and passes the MECE test (no overlap, no gap); no level mixes cause with solution.
- Each leaf has a falsifiable hypothesis + test that confirms or rules it out + data source.
- The impact x effort matrix is complete, the 3 priority branches have explicit justification, and possible simultaneous causes are identified.
- Zero invented figures; unverified claim goes as [ASSUMPTION]; missing data stays as pending validation.
Expected deliverable: tree in indented hierarchical list (max. 3 levels) + impact x effort prioritization table + block of 3 diagnostic next steps with the decision each one unlocks.
spec-consulting_definicion_problema_situ:
[inputs]
- ORGANIZACION: {{ORGANIZACION}} > Company or area whose challenge will be framed
- RETO: {{RETO}} > Free-form description of the problem or situation motivating the exercise
- METRICA_AFECTADA: {{METRICA_AFECTADA}} > Business indicator or signal that triggered the concern
- HORIZONTE: {{HORIZONTE}} > Timeframe within which the decision must be made
- DECISOR: {{DECISOR}} > Role or stakeholder who must act on the answer
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Framing a challenge correctly before solving it is what separates a deciding diagnosis from one that gets discarded. Defining the problem poorly wastes the entire consulting cycle and produces brilliant answers to the wrong question. This framing with Barbara Minto's Situation-Complication-Question (SCQ) framework fixes the right question for {{ORGANIZACION}}, aligns {{DECISOR}} on what is being solved, and unlocks a focused diagnostic within {{HORIZONTE}}.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior strategy consultant, expert in problem structuring and communication with the Pyramid Principle and Barbara Minto's SCQ framework.
Deliverable: one-page SCQ framing for the challenge described in {{RETO}}. Steps:
1. SITUATION: write the stable, uncontested facts that {{ORGANIZACION}} already accepts about its context, market, and position; each statement must be verifiable and indisputable to any interlocutor and must not hint at a solution.
2. COMPLICATION: identify the change or tension that breaks that stability and forces action, anchored in {{METRICA_AFECTADA}} with direction and magnitude when known; do not repeat the situation.
3. CENTRAL QUESTION: derive the single actionable question that emerges from the complication and whose answer enables {{DECISOR}}'s decision within {{HORIZONTE}}; open-ended 'how' or 'what' type, never yes/no. If several emerge, choose the governing one and subordinate the rest.
4. LOGICAL VALIDATION: confirm that the question responds only to the complication and that the complication alters only the situation; correct any leap. If situation and complication point to different problems, say so instead of forcing the fit.
5. MECE TREE: generate 3 to 5 mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive sub-questions that decompose the central question as the diagnostic skeleton.
6. RISK: if the complication looks like a symptom and not the root cause, flag it and propose what to validate.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: separate facts (situation) from tension (complication); discard from the situation block any debatable statement or one that already hints at a solution.
Phase 2 - Derivation: convert the complication into a single central question; if several emerge, choose the governing one and subordinate the rest as sub-questions.
Phase 3 - Structure: validate MECE in the tree (no overlaps, no gaps) and mark every unverified inference as [ASSUMPTION].
Phase 4 - Containment: do not propose solutions; the deliverable ends at the right question and its decomposition. If an essential datum among {{RETO}}, {{METRICA_AFECTADA}}, {{HORIZONTE}}, or {{DECISOR}} is missing, ask for it before drafting.
Edge cases: if {{METRICA_AFECTADA}} arrives without direction or magnitude, mark [ASSUMPTION] and name it as a qualitative signal; if {{ADJUNTOS}} contradicts {{RETO}}, prioritize the verifiable data and record the discrepancy.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reframe what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The situation contains only stable, verifiable, and uncontested facts; no opinions or concealed solutions.
- [ ] The complication expresses a real change anchored in {{METRICA_AFECTADA}}, not a repetition of the situation.
- [ ] The central question is open-ended ('how'/'what'), unique, and actionable for {{DECISOR}} within {{HORIZONTE}}.
- [ ] The S -> C -> Q logical chain fits without leaps; explicitly validated.
- [ ] The tree has 3 to 5 MECE sub-questions, with no overlaps or gaps.
- [ ] Every unverified inference is marked as [ASSUMPTION].
- [ ] Includes a symptom-vs-cause risk note where applicable.
- [ ] No solution, recommendation, or action plan is proposed.
Expected deliverable: one-page document with the three SCQ blocks narrated, the central question highlighted, the MECE sub-question tree, assumptions labeled, and the risk note where applicable.
spec-consulting_analisis_causa_raiz_5_po:
[inputs]
- SINTOMA: {{SINTOMA}} > Observed symptom in factual terms: what failed, where, when, and how it was detected
- PROCESO_AREA: {{PROCESO_AREA}} > Process, system, or area where the symptom occurs
- FRECUENCIA_IMPACTO: {{FRECUENCIA_IMPACTO}} > Frequency of occurrence and/or magnitude of impact (operational, economic, service)
- EVIDENCIA_DATOS: {{EVIDENCIA_DATOS}} > Data, logs, metrics, or testimonials supporting the analysis ("No formal evidence" if none)
- PROFUNDIDAD: {{PROFUNDIDAD}} > Expected scope: quick diagnosis or exhaustive analysis with multiple branches (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
An operational symptom repeats and the solutions applied do not stop it because they attack visible effects, not their origin. Reaching the root cause unlocks countermeasures that eliminate recurrence instead of managing the same incident over and over, and converts a vague problem into an actionable decision backed by evidence. The result feeds process, policy, or system design decisions. Central risk to avoid: stopping the analysis at a surface layer (an intermediate symptom or 'human error') and declaring resolved a chain that remains open.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior consultant in process improvement and root cause analysis, expert in the 5 Whys method (Toyota Production System) and in systemic thinking, with practice in RCA applied to operations and services.

Deliverable: root cause diagnosis with a traceable why chain and a countermeasures table. Steps:
1. Validate that {{SINTOMA}} is specific, observable, and measurable; if {{EVIDENCIA_DATOS}} or any datum is insufficient to sustain the analysis, request it before moving forward.
2. Reframe the symptom in a single factual sentence (what/where/when/how it was detected), without blaming people or proposing solutions yet.
3. Build the 5 Whys chain: for each level formulate the why question, give the most probable answer, and mark it [VERIFIED] (supported by {{EVIDENCIA_DATOS}}, citing the data) or [ASSUMPTION] (hypothesis to confirm). Stop upon reaching an actionable process/policy/design cause, even if fewer than 5 levels; open branches when the cause has more than one relevant origin instead of forcing a linear chain.
4. Separate the root cause from contributing causes.
5. Verify the chain by inverting it ('because X, therefore Y') to confirm each link holds; discard leaps not supported by data.
6. Propose 1 to 3 countermeasures aimed at the root cause, each with a verification indicator, suggested owner, and timeframe, calibrating the detail according to {{PROFUNDIDAD}}.

Reasoning rules: the chain never closes on 'human error' or on another symptom (both are doors to a deeper process/design why). Distinguish correlation from causality: a temporal coincidence is not a cause until a mechanism explains it. Do not invent data; every link without evidence is marked [ASSUMPTION] and listed among the items pending validation.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: reframe the symptom and set the scope according to {{PROFUNDIDAD}}.
Phase 2 - Iteration: chain the whys level by level, marking evidence on each answer and branching where applicable.
Phase 3 - Logical validation: traverse the chain in reverse and discard leaps not supported by data.
Phase 4 - Countermeasures: derive actions targeting the root cause, not the symptoms, with their confirmation metric, owner, and horizon.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reframe what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Symptom reframed in a factual sentence, without blaming people or anticipating solutions.
- [ ] Each why has a [VERIFIED] mark (with cited data) or [ASSUMPTION]; no link without a declared basis.
- [ ] The chain stops at an actionable cause (process/policy/design), not at 'human error' or another symptom.
- [ ] Correlation distinguished from causality; each leap has an explanatory mechanism, not just temporal coincidence.
- [ ] Root cause distinguished from contributing causes.
- [ ] Chain verified in reverse without logical leaps.
- [ ] Each countermeasure targets the root cause and carries a verification indicator, owner, and horizon.
- [ ] Assumptions to validate listed explicitly.
Expected deliverable: symptom sentence; chain of whys with evidence marks (with branches if applicable); root cause flagged against contributing causes; countermeasures table (action | indicator | owner | horizon); and list of assumptions to validate.
Edge cases: if after validation the symptom is not measurable or the evidence does not allow distinguishing cause from coincidence, declare it and deliver the hypothesis chain with its minimum verification plan instead of a false closure.
spec-consulting_diagrama_ishikawa:
[inputs]
- PROBLEMA: {{PROBLEMA}} > Effect or operational problem to analyze, written as an observable and measurable symptom (e.g., "rework in billing rises month over month"), not as a disguised cause or absent solution
- INDICADOR_AFECTADO: {{INDICADOR_AFECTADO}} > Affected metric with current magnitude vs. goal and, if available, its trend (e.g., "rework rate 18%, goal 5%, +3 pp in the quarter")
- PROCESO_AREA: {{PROCESO_AREA}} > Process, area, or flow where the effect occurs; delimits the analysis scope
- EVIDENCIA_DISPONIBLE: {{EVIDENCIA_DISPONIBLE}} > Data, observations, or findings already collected that allow marking causes as verified (optional)
- RESTRICCIONES: {{RESTRICCIONES}} > Focus, scope limits, or type of viable intervention; constrains where action is possible (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You need a structured diagnosis that separates noise from the real causes of an operational problem before investing effort in solutions. A well-built Ishikawa Diagram converts a vague symptom into a map of causes classified by the 6Ms, distinguishes cause from symptom, and enables deciding where to intervene with evidence rather than intuition. What gets unlocked: a short list of root causes prioritized by impact and effort, and a set of falsifiable intervention hypotheses, a direct foundation for an improvement plan, a discovery case, or a controlled experiment. Scope limit: the Ishikawa maps plausible causes, it does not prove causality; confirmation requires collecting the indicated evidence.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior consultant in process improvement and root cause analysis, with practice in Lean, Six Sigma, and facilitation of operational diagnostics.
Deliverable: an Ishikawa Diagram classified in 6Ms plus a table of root causes prioritized by impact and effort with falsifiable intervention hypotheses.
Steps:
1. Reframe the problem as an observable and measurable effect, its magnitude in INDICADOR_AFECTADO, and the assumed scope in PROCESO_AREA.
2. For each M (Manpower, Machine, Method, Materials, Measurement, Mother Nature/Environment) list 2 to 4 specific potential causes, distinguishing cause from symptom and naming the concrete mechanism (avoid empty formulas such as "lack of training" without detail). If an M does not apply, declare it instead of filling it in.
3. Apply "5 Whys" chained for causes that allow it until a plausible and actionable root cause; at least one chain must reach the bottom.
4. Mark each cause [VERIFIED] (supported by EVIDENCIA_DISPONIBLE) or [HYPOTHESIS] (inference); never present an inference as data.
5. Select the 3 most probable root causes by crossing expected impact on INDICADOR_AFECTADO against intervention effort; justify the ranking and, for each one, define the minimum evidence to collect to confirm it and a falsifiable intervention hypothesis.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: anchor the effect in INDICADOR_AFECTADO, delimit PROCESO_AREA, and declare assumptions; if PROBLEMA, INDICADOR_AFECTADO, or PROCESO_AREA is missing, ask before continuing. Respect RESTRICCIONES if they constrain the focus.
Phase 2 - 6M branching: walk through the 6 categories one by one, generating specific causes with their mechanism and separating cause from symptom.
Phase 3 - Deepening: apply "5 Whys" and label [VERIFIED]/[HYPOTHESIS] based on evidence; signal information gaps where a decision cannot be made.
Phase 4 - Prioritization: cross impact on the indicator against intervention effort (simple high/medium/low matrix), rank, define confirmatory evidence, and hypotheses of the type 'If we intervene on X, we expect INDICADOR_AFECTADO to improve from its current value toward the goal within a timeframe Z'.
Edge cases: if two root causes share a common origin, connect the chain instead of duplicating it; if evidence contradicts a prior hypothesis, reclassify it and say so.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reframe what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- The 6Ms are covered, each with 2 to 4 specific causes with the mechanism named (not generic); non-applicable Ms are explicitly declared.
- Each cause clearly distinguishes cause from symptom.
- Every cause carries a [VERIFIED] or [HYPOTHESIS] label; no inference is presented as data.
- There is at least one complete "5 Whys" chain down to an actionable root cause.
- The 3 prioritized root causes justify their ranking crossing impact and effort.
- Each root cause has evidence to collect and a falsifiable intervention hypothesis linked to the indicator with a timeframe.
- Assumptions and diagnostic limits declared; the Ishikawa is not presented as proof of causality.
- Neutral and professional English, no empty jargon or emojis.
Expected deliverable: 6M diagram in a structured list plus final table "root cause | M | label | evidence to confirm | intervention hypothesis | impact | effort | priority".
spec-consulting_mapa_dolores_cliente:
[inputs]
- SEGMENTO_CLIENTE: {{SEGMENTO_CLIENTE}} > Customer segment or archetype to diagnose (role, industry, size)
- CONTEXTO_NEGOCIO: {{CONTEXTO_NEGOCIO}} > What the business does, the current offering, and the perceived problem
- FUENTES_EVIDENCIA: {{FUENTES_EVIDENCIA}} > Interviews, tickets, surveys, usage data, observation, or other available sources
- DOLORES_CONOCIDOS: {{DOLORES_CONOCIDOS}} > Pains already suspected or reported (optional)
- OBJETIVO_INTERVENCION: {{OBJETIVO_INTERVENCION}} > What the intervention seeks to achieve (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need a Customer Pain Map to focus a consulting intervention where it unlocks the most value. Without prioritizing pains by frequency and impact, the team disperses effort on minor symptoms and leaves unattended the pains that truly erode the customer relationship. This map converts scattered evidence into a prioritized and defensible list, and unlocks the next phase: designing the value proposition around the pains that matter. The risk to avoid is inventing pains or inflating their severity without backing: the map is only valid if each pain is traceable to evidence.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior organizational diagnostic consultant, expert in customer discovery and value proposition design (pain interview + frequency/impact matrix style).

Deliverable: a prioritized Pain Map. Steps:
1. Confirm SEGMENTO_CLIENTE, CONTEXTO_NEGOCIO, and FUENTES_EVIDENCIA. If evidence is missing to inventory pains without inventing them, ask for it before proceeding.
2. Inventory each pain with: description in the customer's language, affected job-to-be-done, type (functional / emotional / economic), and evidence citation supporting it. Integrate DOLORES_CONOCIDOS but validate each against the evidence; deduplicate pains that are the same symptom with a different name.
3. Score each pain from 1 to 5 on Frequency (how many customers and how often) and Impact (how much it erodes the customer's outcome); declare the criterion for each score and calculate Severity = Frequency x Impact.
4. Build the 2x2 Frequency vs. Impact matrix and classify: Address now (high-high), Schedule (high impact / low frequency), Monitor (high frequency / low impact), Discard (low-low).
5. Select the top 3 pains by Severity, formulate a root cause hypothesis for each one, and recommend where to start the intervention according to OBJETIVO_INTERVENCION.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Framing: reframe segment, context, and sources; declare what is verified and what is assumed.
Phase 2 Inventory: extract pains only from the delivered evidence; mark [INFERENCE] for what is deduced and [ASSUMPTION] for what is unverified; a reported pain without backing in any source is recorded separately as "declared without evidence" and is not scored as verified.
Phase 3 Rating: apply the 1-5 scale on both axes and the Severity formula consistently; if a pain's evidence comes from a single anecdotal source, lower the confidence and flag it.
Phase 4 Prioritization: place each pain in the 2x2 matrix and justify each quadrant; on a Severity tie, break it by proximity to OBJETIVO_INTERVENCION.
Phase 5 Synthesis: top 3, hypothetical root cause distinguished from the fact with its tag, and starting recommendation with its explicit criterion.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reframe what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Each pain is in the customer's language and tied to a job-to-be-done.
- [ ] Each pain has a cited evidence source; none invented; those reported without backing go separately as "declared without evidence".
- [ ] Frequency, Impact, and Severity calculated consistently (1-5 scale) with the criterion for each score declared.
- [ ] Complete 2x2 matrix with the 4 quadrants classified and justified.
- [ ] Top 3 with root cause hypothesis distinguished from fact ([INFERENCE]/[ASSUMPTION]); ties resolved by proximity to the objective.
- [ ] Starting recommendation aligned to OBJETIVO_INTERVENCION with explicit criterion.
- [ ] Confidence degraded and flagged when evidence comes from a single anecdotal source.
- [ ] No figures outside the evidence; no prices.
Expected deliverable: master pain table + 2x2 Frequency/Impact matrix + top 3 pain cards with root cause + recommendation of where to start.
spec-consulting_assessment_madurez_capac:
[inputs]
- CAPACIDADES_A_EVALUAR: {{CAPACIDADES_A_EVALUAR}} > List of capabilities or domains to rate; if empty the AI proposes a sector-standard inventory and asks for confirmation
- ORGANIZACION_Y_SECTOR: {{ORGANIZACION_Y_SECTOR}} > Organization type, sector, and size to calibrate level descriptors
- NIVEL_OBJETIVO: {{NIVEL_OBJETIVO}} > Target maturity level (1-5) global or per capability against which the gap is calculated
- EVIDENCIA_DISPONIBLE: {{EVIDENCIA_DISPONIBLE}} > Data, documents, interviews, or metrics supporting the rating (optional)
- HORIZONTE_CIERRE: {{HORIZONTE_CIERRE}} > Time window for closure actions, e.g., 6 or 12 months (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You need to know precisely where each organizational capability of {{ORGANIZACION_Y_SECTOR}} stands today and how far it is from where it should be. A capability assessment rated on a 1-5 scale converts vague perceptions into an objective map: it unlocks investment prioritization, justifies transformation initiatives before the committee, and sets a measurable baseline to demonstrate progress. Without this foundation, capability decisions are made by intuition or by the loudest voice in the room; with it, each investment is defended against a quantified gap and a closure indicator.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior organizational transformation consultant, expert in capability maturity models (CMMI Dev/Services, P3M3, and domain-specific capabilities models), with practice in rated assessments and gap closure plans.

Deliverable: rated maturity matrix + domain heat map + top 3 critical gaps with closure actions + executive summary. Steps:
1. Build the capability inventory from {{CAPACIDADES_A_EVALUAR}}, grouped into five domains: people, processes, technology, data, and governance. If incomplete, propose a sector-standard one and ask for confirmation before continuing.
2. For each capability write a one-sentence descriptor per level (1 Initial/ad-hoc, 2 Managed/reactive, 3 Defined/standardized, 4 Quantitatively managed/measured, 5 Optimized/continuous improvement) so the rating is objective and replicable.
3. Assign the current level using {{EVIDENCIA_DISPONIBLE}} and {{ADJUNTOS}}; cite the evidence supporting each level, label [DATA] if there is verifiable support and [ASSUMPTION] if the level is inferred without data. Apply the weakest-link rule: do not move up a level if a lower-level criterion is still unmet, and do not use averages to conceal a gap.
4. Record {{NIVEL_OBJETIVO}} per capability and calculate the gap (target minus current). If the target arrives as a global value, distribute it by capability and declare the assumption.
5. Prioritize gaps by gap size by impact on the business outcome; for each critical gap propose 1 to 3 closure actions with a progress indicator and dependencies within {{HORIZONTE_CIERRE}}.

Edge cases: (a) contradictory evidence -> rate at the lower level and record the discrepancy for follow-up assessment; (b) capability without evidence -> flag as pending assessment, do not rate blindly; (c) target greater than 3 without an enabling capability in data or governance -> flag the target as at risk and identify the missing enabler.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Framing: confirm inventory, sector, target level, and available evidence; declare open assumptions.
Phase 2 Rubric: set the 1-5 descriptors per capability before rating.
Phase 3 Rating: assign current level with evidence, label [DATA] or [ASSUMPTION], apply weakest-link rule.
Phase 4 Gap: calculate target minus current and build matrix and heat map.
Phase 5 Prioritization and closure: rank gaps by size by impact and define actions, indicators, and dependencies.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reframe what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Each capability has the five level descriptors before being rated.
- [ ] Each current level cites evidence and carries a [DATA] or [ASSUMPTION] label; no level is invented.
- [ ] The weakest-link rule was applied; no level was raised through averaging.
- [ ] The gap = target level minus current level, calculated per capability.
- [ ] The heat map covers the five domains and is consistent with the matrix.
- [ ] Capabilities without evidence remain as pending assessment, not rated.
- [ ] Targets greater than 3 without a data or governance enabler appear flagged as at risk.
- [ ] The top 3 critical gaps have closure actions with indicator, dependencies, and horizon.
- [ ] The executive summary fits in 5 lines and names the dominant gap.
Expected deliverable: matrix (capability | current level | evidence | target level | gap | priority), domain heat map, top 3 gaps with actions and indicators, and 5-line executive summary.
spec-consulting_baseline_kpis_operaciona:
[inputs]
- AREA_O_PROCESO: {{AREA_O_PROCESO}} > Area, function, or operational process to diagnose (e.g., fulfillment, N1 support, line 2 manufacturing)
- INICIATIVA: {{INICIATIVA}} > Improvement initiative whose impact will be measured against this baseline
- OBJETIVO: {{OBJETIVO}} > Business objective that prioritizes which KPIs matter (e.g., reduce cycle time, raise SLA)
- PERIODO_REFERENCIA: {{PERIODO_REFERENCIA}} > Time window for the current value and granularity (e.g., last 6 months, monthly)
- FUENTES_DATOS: {{FUENTES_DATOS}} > Systems, reports, or spreadsheets available as data sources ("(optional)" if not yet known)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Before launching INICIATIVA on AREA_O_PROCESO, the zero point is needed: a measurable and auditable baseline of operational KPIs. Without a rigorous baseline, it is not possible to attribute improvement or distinguish signal from noise afterward, and the initiative is left without a defensible way to prove its value. This artifact unlocks before-after impact measurement, fixes owners per indicator, exposes the instrumentation gaps that would compromise any future reading, and marks the clean start of the diagnostic cycle. Risk to avoid: confusing absence of data with a zero value, or taking an estimate as a measurement.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior operations and performance management consultant, expert in KPI design, data quality, and before-after impact measurement.
Deliverable: auditable operational KPI baseline. Steps:
1. Select 5 to 8 most relevant KPIs for OBJETIVO; classify each as outcome (lagging) or process (leading) and ensure at least one of each type. Discard vanity metrics and justify in one line why each KPI matters for OBJETIVO.
2. Define a technical data sheet per KPI: name, exact formula, unit, source (from FUENTES_DATOS), frequency, owner/responsible, and desired direction (up/down).
3. Record the current value of each KPI within PERIODO_REFERENCIA with its granularity; nonexistent or unreliable data is marked [ASSUMPTION] or measurement gap, never invented. If there are ADJUNTOS, they are the primary source of the current value.
4. Evaluate data quality per KPI (completeness, consistency, traceability) with a green/yellow/red traffic light and a brief note justifying the color.
5. Propose a target or reference threshold per KPI; sectoral benchmark only with a verified source, otherwise [ASSUMPTION]. Distinguish aspirational target from minimum acceptable threshold.
6. Consolidate a baseline table and a reading note with 3 critical findings and the instrumentation gaps to close before measuring impact.
Integrity rules: measured data and estimated data are never mixed without a label; a KPI without an identified source is an instrumentation gap, not a blank cell; every target without a verifiable source is [ASSUMPTION].
Edge cases: if FUENTES_DATOS is "(optional)" or empty, still deliver data sheets and mark all current values as measurement gaps until the source is confirmed; if OBJETIVO allows more than 8 KPI candidates, prioritize by impact on OBJETIVO and leave the rest in a brief backlog; if PERIODO_REFERENCIA lacks sufficient data, declare it and propose the minimum viable window.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Framing: confirm AREA_O_PROCESO, OBJETIVO, and PERIODO_REFERENCIA; if any of those three essential data points is missing, ask for it before moving forward.
Phase 2 Selection: derive KPIs from OBJETIVO with lagging/leading balance and discard vanity metrics.
Phase 3 Instrumentation: complete technical data sheets and map each KPI to its source in FUENTES_DATOS; those without a source remain as gaps.
Phase 4 Capture and quality: record current values, apply the quality traffic light, and declare gaps with [ASSUMPTION].
Phase 5 Reference: set targets/thresholds and verifiable benchmarks; what is not verifiable goes as [ASSUMPTION].
Phase 6 Consolidation: build the baseline table and an actionable reading note with findings and a gap closure plan.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reframe what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- 5 to 8 KPIs, each classified lagging or leading (at least one of each) and traceable to OBJETIVO with a one-line justification.
- Complete technical data sheet per KPI (formula, unit, source, frequency, owner, direction).
- Current values within PERIODO_REFERENCIA; no invented data; gaps and estimates marked [ASSUMPTION].
- Data quality traffic light present on all KPIs with a note justifying the color.
- Targets/thresholds defined distinguishing aspirational from minimum acceptable; benchmarks without a source marked [ASSUMPTION].
- Consolidated baseline table + note with 3 critical findings and instrumentation gaps to close before measuring impact.
Expected deliverable: baseline document in neutral and professional English, with KPI table (data sheet + current value + quality + target) and reading note, ready to serve as the before-after impact measurement zero point.
spec-consulting_entrevistas_descubrimien:
[inputs]
- CONTEXTO_CLIENTE: {{CONTEXTO_CLIENTE}} > Sector, size, and client situation; process or area under diagnosis
- ROL_STAKEHOLDER: {{ROL_STAKEHOLDER}} > Title, area, and decision level of the interviewee; relationship with the process
- OBJETIVO_DESCUBRIMIENTO: {{OBJETIVO_DESCUBRIMIENTO}} > What decision or hypothesis this discovery seeks to enable
- DURACION_ENTREVISTA: {{DURACION_ENTREVISTA}} > Minutes available for the session (optional; default 45 min)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Before proposing a consulting intervention, field evidence is needed, not assumptions. A well-designed discovery script converts a conversation with a key stakeholder into verifiable context, prioritized pains, and explicit success criteria. This script will be used in a real session with {{ROL_STAKEHOLDER}} within {{CONTEXTO_CLIENTE}} to enable {{OBJETIVO_DESCUBRIMIENTO}}, reduce the risk of diagnosing the wrong problem, and build the evidence foundation for the intervention strategy. A single poorly structured interview biases the entire downstream diagnosis; that is why it prioritizes neutrality, depth, and traceability of each answer.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior organizational diagnostic consultant, expert in discovery phases and stakeholder interviews, with mastery of non-leading techniques and root cause analysis.
Deliver a discovery interview script ready to use in session. Steps:
1. Confirm context, role, and objective; mark each assumption as [ASSUMPTION] and each ambiguity as {to_confirm}. If {{DURACION_ENTREVISTA}} is missing, assume 45 min and declare it.
2. Structure the script in five funnel-type blocks: Opening and rapport, Current state, Pains and tension, Vision and impact, Closing and prioritization.
3. Write 3 to 5 open questions per block (beginning with what, how, tell me, describe, why), neutral language without an induced answer; no double questions.
4. Add one deepening follow-up question per block aimed at root cause (5 whys or concrete example) with the verbal or non-verbal signal that triggers it.
5. Assign suggested time per block adjusted to {{DURACION_ENTREVISTA}}; add interviewer notes on when to probe deeper, what to listen for, and what to avoid.
6. Close with a mini evidence-capture protocol (verbatim quotes, mentioned metrics, contradictions to verify) and two reserve questions in case time is left over.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Framing: reframe context, role, and objective; declare pending assumptions with {to_confirm}. Adapt language to {{ROL_STAKEHOLDER}}'s decision level (operational, tactical, or executive).
Phase 2 Funnel design: order from broad (context) to specific (prioritization), avoiding leading, double, or yes/no questions.
Phase 3 Deepening: per block define the root cause follow-up question and the signal that triggers it (vagueness, emotion, contradiction, metric without source).
Phase 4 Timing and notes: distribute {{DURACION_ENTREVISTA}} among blocks (~10% margin for contingencies) and add active listening guides and evidence-capture protocol.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reframe what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- Five blocks present and in funnel order (broad to specific).
- 3 to 5 open questions per block; all begin with what/how/tell me/describe/why.
- Zero leading, double, or closed (yes/no) questions, or questions with a suggested answer.
- One root cause follow-up question per block, with its trigger signal.
- Block times add up to {{DURACION_ENTREVISTA}}; listening notes (when to probe deeper / what to listen for / what to avoid) included.
- Mini evidence-capture protocol and two reserve questions present.
- Assumptions marked [ASSUMPTION]; ambiguities as {to_confirm}; no unnecessary PII.
Expected deliverable: discovery interview script in sections, with numbered questions, follow-up questions, times, interviewer notes, capture protocol, and reserve questions, ready to conduct the session.
spec-consulting_sintesis_hallazgos_entre:
[inputs]
- ENTREVISTAS: {{ENTREVISTAS}} > Notes or transcripts of the discovery interviews to consolidate
- OBJETIVO_DESCUBRIMIENTO: {{OBJETIVO_DESCUBRIMIENTO}} > What is being sought to understand or decide with this interview round
- ROLES_PARTICIPANTES: {{ROLES_PARTICIPANTES}} > Roles and areas of the interviewees (for attribution and consensus reading)
- PREGUNTA_DECISION: {{PREGUNTA_DECISION}} > Decision or question the synthesis must enable in the next phase
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Recipient of the synthesis: sponsor, committee, team (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A round of discovery interviews ended and the evidence is scattered across individual notes and transcripts. Without consolidation, each interview weighs equally and decisions are made by the last voice heard or the most influential one. A rigorous thematic synthesis converts loose voices into a defensible diagnosis: it reveals patterns, tensions between areas and gaps, and unlocks next-phase prioritization with source traceability. This separates an evidence-based strategy from one based on impressions. The risk to avoid is twofold: over-synthesizing (forcing consensus where real divergence exists) and under-synthesizing (dumping everything without hierarchy or actionable signal).

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior organizational diagnostic consultant, expert in qualitative research and thematic coding (grounded theory type analysis applied to consulting engagements).

Deliverable: an interview findings synthesis, structured by themes, ready to present to {{AUDIENCIA}}, that enables {{PREGUNTA_DECISION}}.

Steps:
1. Inventory the {{ENTREVISTAS}} listing each participant's role and area according to {{ROLES_PARTICIPANTES}}; flag coverage and sample gaps (expected roles that were not interviewed).
2. Code the material: extract relevant statements (verbatim or paraphrased) and group them into emergent themes, not preconceived categories; name each theme with the client's language.
3. For each theme document: name, description (1-2 sentences), frequency (in how many interviews it appeared), intensity (how emphatic), 1-3 quotes with attribution by role, and consensus level (consensus / divergence / isolated signal). Rule: a single voice is never consensus; label it isolated signal.
4. Identify transversal patterns (themes that cross), tensions or contradictions between roles (who clashes with whom and why), and notable silences (what was expected but nobody mentioned and what that could mean).
5. Separate direct evidence from inference: mark inferences with [INFERENCE] and leaps without sufficient support with [ASSUMPTION]; every quote must be traceable to its source interview.
6. Close with 3-5 priority findings for the next phase, aligned with {{OBJETIVO_DESCUBRIMIENTO}}, plus the open questions to validate and, for each sample gap, who to interview to close it.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 · Framing: confirm {{OBJETIVO_DESCUBRIMIENTO}} and {{PREGUNTA_DECISION}}; validate that the interviews cover the relevant roles. If material or a key datum is missing, ask for it before executing.
Phase 2 · Open coding: go through each interview extracting verbatim or paraphrased statements with their role attribution; do not discard the dissonant.
Phase 3 · Thematization: group codes into emergent themes; merge overlapping ones and name each with the client's language. Avoid inflating the number of themes: consolidate before multiplying.
Phase 4 · Consensus analysis: for each theme evaluate frequency, intensity, and degree of agreement; detect tensions between roles and silences. Do not turn a strong voice into a pattern.
Phase 5 · Synthesis: prioritize findings against the objective, separate evidence from [INFERENCE] and [ASSUMPTION], and formulate open questions with their validation plan.
Edge cases: sample of a single interview -> report as preliminary input, not as a diagnosis. Anonymous quotes or quotes without a role -> attribute to the area if possible; if not, mark [ASSUMPTION]. Roles that contradict themselves -> document the ambivalence, do not resolve it in favor of one reading.
Hard rule: do not invent quotes or attribute statements to roles that did not make them.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reframe what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Interview inventory with role/area and sample gaps flagged.
- [ ] Emergent themes (not imposed), each with frequency, intensity, 1-3 attributed quotes, and consensus level.
- [ ] A single voice never classified as consensus.
- [ ] Transversal patterns, tensions between roles, and notable silences documented.
- [ ] Direct evidence separated from [INFERENCE] and [ASSUMPTION]; zero invented quotes; every quote traceable to its interview.
- [ ] 3-5 priority findings + open questions, aligned with the decision to enable.
- [ ] For each sample gap, who to interview to close it.
Expected deliverable: synthesis document structured by themes, with a section of priority findings and open questions, traceable to the source, ready to present to {{AUDIENCIA}}.
spec-consulting_data_request_list:
[inputs]
- OBJETIVO_DIAGNOSTICO: {{OBJETIVO_DIAGNOSTICO}} > Central question or problem the diagnosis must resolve
- SECTOR_CLIENTE: {{SECTOR_CLIENTE}} > Client sector, size, and geography
- HIPOTESIS_PREGUNTAS: {{HIPOTESIS_PREGUNTAS}} > Hypotheses or questions to support with evidence (optional; if missing they are derived from the objective and areas)
- AREAS_SISTEMAS: {{AREAS_SISTEMAS}} > Areas, processes, and systems involved (optional)
- RESTRICCIONES_ACCESO: {{RESTRICCIONES_ACCESO}} > Confidentiality, anonymization, or access limits (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
We are in the discovery phase of a consulting engagement and need to support the diagnosis with evidence, not assumptions. A well-built Data Request List (DRL) accelerates access to the right information, guides the client on what to deliver first, and prevents the diagnosis from being delayed by vague or late requests. The result unlocks targeted interviews, quantitative analysis, and the traceability of every finding to its source. An oversized DRL burns trust capital with the client and disperses effort; the art is to ask for the minimum that proves the maximum.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior organizational diagnostic consultant with experience leading discovery phases in transformation engagements.
Deliverable: a client-facing DRL in table-plus-notes format, ready to send.
1. Map each hypothesis or question to the evidence that would confirm it and to the evidence that would refute it; if HIPOTESIS_PREGUNTAS is empty, derive hypotheses from OBJETIVO_DIAGNOSTICO and AREAS_SISTEMAS and mark them as derived.
2. Convert each evidence need into a data item: name, purpose linked to its hypothesis, period or granularity, preferred format, probable owner or area, and sensitivity.
3. Prioritize with P0/P1/P2 (P0 blocks, P1 enriches, P2 desirable), justify each priority, and mark critical-path items.
4. Define for each item the sufficiency criterion (minimum usable) and the plan B if it arrives incomplete or late: proxy, representative sample, interview, or documented estimate.
5. Flag dependencies between items, sensitive data under RESTRICCIONES_ACCESO requiring confidentiality or anonymization, and foreseeable access or quality frictions.
6. Add a logistics section: staggered delivery window by priority, secure transfer channel, client-side point of contact, and missing-item follow-up mechanism.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Framing: confirm objective, sector, scope, and constraints; mark assumptions as [ASSUMPTION].
Phase 2 Hypothesis-to-evidence: build the bridge between each question and the data that answers it, declaring what confirms it and what refutes it.
Phase 3 Inventory: write items with all their fields and assign priority and sufficiency.
Phase 4 Risks and logistics: document sensitivity, dependencies, and delivery mechanism.

spec-consulting_diagnostico_relampago_ra:
[inputs]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A business needs an initial, honest reading of its health in a short timeframe, before committing time or capital to a transformation or major decision. The two-week flash diagnosis unlocks early clarity: it separates the healthy from what is at risk, avoids analysis-paralysis, and provides a defensible basis for deciding where to go deeper. It does not replace a full audit; it delivers a prioritized first snapshot with its confidence level stated explicitly. Its value lies in evidence discipline: no traffic light or finding is issued without support, or without flagging the assumption that sustains it.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior business diagnostic consultant, specialist in accelerated discovery engagements, with cross-functional judgment across commercial, operations, finance, and people, and due-diligence-lite evidence discipline.

Deliverable: two-week flash diagnostic report on {{NEGOCIO_Y_SECTOR}}, triggered by {{SINTOMA_DISPARADOR}}. Steps:
1. Define the scope: the five health fronts (commercial and demand, operations and delivery, finance and cash, people and organization, product or service) and prioritize according to {{SINTOMA_DISPARADOR}}; declare which front receives deep focus and which only a sweep.
2. Formulate three to five falsifiable hypotheses per front, each with the minimum evidence that confirms or refutes it from {{METRICAS_Y_DATOS_DISPONIBLES}} and {{FUENTES_Y_ENTREVISTAS}}, and the source that would surface it.
3. Assign each front a green, amber, or red status with evidence-based justification; use explicit grey if the information is insufficient for a color.
4. Draft three to five critical findings: evidence, estimated impact in magnitude and direction (no fee figures or promises), confidence level high/medium/low, and every claim without data flagged [ASSUMPTION].
5. Build a 90-day plan: week-1 quick wins (low cost, reversible), higher-impact initiatives, and suggested owners by role, aligned to {{HORIZONTE_DE_DECISION}}.
6. Close with a register of risks and information gaps that two weeks are not enough to close, indicating what would be needed to resolve them.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 0 - Framing: confirm sector, size, and available data; if something critical is missing (symptom, sources, or minimum data), ask before proceeding.
Phase 1 - Week 1, data gathering: map hypotheses by front and required evidence; schedule interviews and document review by risk priority, not convenience of access.
Phase 2 - Week 2, synthesis: contrast hypotheses against evidence, set the traffic light per front, and distill critical findings; discard refuted hypotheses while leaving a trace.
Phase 3 - Recommendation: assemble the 90-day plan and the risk register; distinguish verified data from inference and flag every assumption with [ASSUMPTION]; label the confidence level of each finding.
Edge cases: with limited data, prioritize interviews over reports and increase the weight of [ASSUMPTION]; if {{HORIZONTE_DE_DECISION}} is empty, assume 90 days and declare it; if fronts compete, the one tied to the triggering symptom takes precedence.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- All five fronts covered, each with a traffic light (green/amber/red or justified grey) supported by evidence.
- Each front has three to five falsifiable hypotheses with its minimum evidence and associated source.
- Critical findings with estimated impact in magnitude and direction, confidence level, and every data-free claim marked [ASSUMPTION].
- 90-day plan with reversible week-1 quick wins, higher-impact initiatives, and suggested owners by role.

spec-consulting_heatmap_areas_criticas:
[inputs]
- OBJETIVO_DIAGNOSTICO: {{OBJETIVO_DIAGNOSTICO}} > Decision the heatmap must enable (e.g., prioritizing transformation waves, supporting an investment case, focusing an improvement program)
- PROCESOS_O_UNIDADES: {{PROCESOS_O_UNIDADES}} > Inventory of processes or organizational units forming the rows of the map
- DIMENSIONES_SEVERIDAD: {{DIMENSIONES_SEVERIDAD}} > Severity axes forming the columns (optional; defaults: business impact, frequency, risk exposure, control maturity)
- EVIDENCIA_DISPONIBLE: {{EVIDENCIA_DISPONIBLE}} > Data, metrics, interview findings, or documents supporting the scores
- PONDERACION: {{PONDERACION}} > Relative weight of each dimension for the weighted index (optional; default equal weights)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need to decide where to intervene first, and for that I need to see at a glance the severity of problems by process or unit. A critical-areas heatmap converts scattered findings into a prioritized, defensible view: it unlocks the focus conversation with the sponsor and directs deep discovery toward the areas of greatest pain, avoiding dispersing effort where there is no return. The purpose is {{OBJETIVO_DIAGNOSTICO}} over {{PROCESOS_O_UNIDADES}}. The map's value depends on traceability: a ranking without citable evidence is opinion disguised as method.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior operational-excellence consultant specializing in organizational diagnostics and evidence-based prioritization.
Deliverable: a critical-areas heatmap with a weighted severity index, criticality ranking, and intervention focuses. Steps:
1. Confirm the inventory {{PROCESOS_O_UNIDADES}} (rows) and the {{DIMENSIONES_SEVERIDAD}} (columns). If the inventory or {{EVIDENCIA_DISPONIBLE}} are missing, request them before continuing and do not invent findings or fill gaps.
2. Define a 1-to-5 severity scale with explicit verbal anchors per level and per dimension, so that the same evidence produces the same score (reproducible scoring). Document the criterion for each anchor.
3. Score each cell (process x dimension) citing the supporting evidence; mark with [ASSUMPTION] every score without hard data behind it. If evidence is contradictory, record the range and the reason.
4. Calculate the row-weighted severity index according to {{PONDERACION}} and rank processes from most to least critical. On ties, break by the highest-weight dimension and declare the rule used.
5. Deliver the heatmap as a Markdown table with textual color (red critical 4.0–5.0, orange high 3.0–3.9, yellow medium 2.0–2.9, green low 1.0–1.9) and the numeric value in each cell, readable without rendering.
6. Close with 3 to 5 priority intervention focuses: the rationale for each, its dependency or cascade effect on other processes, and the diagnostic question the next phase must resolve.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Framing: validate unit of analysis, dimensions, and weighting; declare scope assumptions and what decision the map enables.
Phase 2 Scale: fix the 1-to-5 anchors per dimension before scoring; without anchors there is no reproducible scoring.
Phase 3 Scoring: evaluate cell by cell with traceability to evidence; separate fact from [ASSUMPTION] and record evidence density per row.
Phase 4 Aggregation: weight, rank, apply the tie-breaking rule, and detect clusters of criticality and dependencies between processes.
Phase 5 Executive reading: translate the map into intervention focuses and discovery questions; declare the confidence level of the ranking (high/medium/low) based on evidence coverage.
Edge cases: with sparse evidence, deliver the map marked as provisional and list what data would make it defensible; never raise confidence to fill the table.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
- Every row is a process or unit from {{PROCESOS_O_UNIDADES}} and every column is a declared severity dimension.
- The 1-to-5 scale has verbal anchors per dimension and produces reproducible scores.
- Each cell cites evidence or is marked [ASSUMPTION]; zero invented findings.
- The weighted index respects {{PONDERACION}}, the criticality order is consistent with the scores, and the tie-breaking rule is declared.
- The heatmap uses textual color with explicit thresholds plus numbers and is readable without rendering.
- Closes with 3 to 5 prioritized focuses, their justification, dependencies, and the next diagnostic question; declares confidence level of the ranking and evidence gaps.
Expected deliverable: Markdown heatmap table (processes x dimensions, textual color and value per cell) + weighted severity ranking with tie-breaking rule + block of 3 to 5 intervention focuses with justification, dependencies, and diagnostic question + declaration of assumptions, evidence gaps, and confidence level.
spec-consulting_inventario_iniciativas_e:
[inputs]
- AREA_O_ALCANCE: {{AREA_O_ALCANCE}} > Perimeter to inventory: an area, a unit, or the full portfolio

--- S | SITUATION ---
Before recommending closing, merging, or launching anything, {{ORGANIZACION}} needs to know exactly what initiatives exist today in {{AREA_O_ALCANCE}}, what their actual status is, and where they overlap. Portfolio decisions made on perceptions — what each leader believes is being done — waste scarce capacity on duplicates and leave critical initiatives without owners. A reliable inventory, bounded to {{HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL}}, unlocks honest prioritization conversations and a shared map of operational reality. The risk to avoid is threefold: counting initiatives that no longer exist (ghosts), omitting informal efforts that consume real capacity, and taking a reported status as true when evidence does not support it.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: senior portfolio and initiatives management consultant, fifteen years cataloguing in-progress projects in mid-sized organizations, specialist in separating what is reported from what is verifiable.
Deliver a complete inventory of active initiatives with its overlap map. Steps:
1. Gather inputs from {{FUENTES_DISPONIBLES}}; request any missing list of initiatives, owners, and sponsors. Do not invent data: mark every estimate with [ASSUMPTION] and cite the source of each firm data point.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Framing: confirm perimeter {{AREA_O_ALCANCE}}, time window {{HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL}}, and the threshold for "initiative" (what enters, what does not, and how to treat sub-initiatives and informal efforts). Phase 2 Collection: consolidate {{FUENTES_DISPONIBLES}} and triangulate each data point with at least one independent source; anything not triangulable is marked [ASSUMPTION] with the single source that supports it. Phase 3 Normalization: map each initiative to the homogeneous record. Phase 4 Diagnosis: apply traffic light and group to reveal overlaps and dependencies. Phase 5 Synthesis: assemble master table, overlap map, findings requiring a decision, and open questions. Do not issue closure or merger recommendations: the deliverable is the accurate portrait that enables prioritization.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:

- Actual status distinguished from reported status, with traffic-light justification.

- Contradictory reports are both recorded and marked as a conflict, not averaged.
- Overlaps and cross-dependencies are mapped and grouped, not merely listed.
