1. Diagnose LCP, INP, and CLS for {{URL_O_PLANTILLAS}} using {{DATOS_CWV}}; report value, threshold (LCP <= 2.5 s, INP <= 200 ms, CLS <= 0.1), and status per metric, separating {{DISPOSITIVO}} mobile from desktop and field (percentile 75) from lab. When field and lab diverge, status is determined by field; lab is used to diagnose the cause.
2. For each out-of-threshold metric, attribute 2-4 concrete, observable technical causes on {{PLATAFORMA}}, not generic ones: LCP (high TTFB, render-blocking CSS/JS, unprioritized LCP resource, missing preload, image without modern format or without responsive sizing); INP (JavaScript long tasks, blocked main thread, heavy handlers, hydration cost); CLS (images/iframes without width/height, font FOIT/FOUT, content injection or banners above painted content).
3. Build the prioritized plan: per action indicate target metric, cause it addresses, expected impact (high/medium/low), effort, owner (frontend/backend/infra/content), dependencies or regression risk, and field verification signal at 28 days.

Phase 1 - Framing: confirm {{URL_O_PLANTILLAS}}, {{PLATAFORMA}}, {{DATOS_CWV}}, and {{DISPOSITIVO}}. If field or lab data is missing, request it and do not invent figures; every estimate is marked [ASSUMPTION].
Phase 2 - Diagnosis: tabulate per metric the field value (p75), the lab value, and the status, differentiating mobile/desktop. If a URL does not have sufficient field data, mark it 'not evaluable in field' and rely on lab data with the explicit caveat.
Phase 3 - Attribution: link each out-of-threshold metric to its observable technical causes on {{PLATAFORMA}}; separate the measured fact from the hypothesis.
Phase 4 - Prioritization: build the action table (metric, cause, impact, effort, owner, dependencies/risk, verification) ordered by impact/effort.
Phase 5 - Verification: define how to confirm the improvement in field data (CrUX/Search Console) after the 28-day window the p75 percentile needs to reflect the change, and what to watch for to detect regressions.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Phase 1 Framing: confirm PIEZA_O_URL, QUERY_OBJETIVO, AUTOR_Y_BIO, and TIPO_PAGINA; if any is missing, ask and do not proceed. Classify YMYL and declare the threshold.
Phase 2 Diagnosis: review each pillar quoting text fragments; never infer a signal that the text does not show.
Phase 3 Rewriting: intervene only in weak passages, demonstrating experience, expertise, authority, or trust with real data; isolate each assumption with [ASSUMPTION].
Phase 4 Blocks: build authorship and sources only with verifiable information; the unverifiable becomes a gap in the plan. If there is no identifiable author or verifiable credential, say so directly and propose the minimum path to build trust, without fabricating it.
Phase 5 Plan: prioritize actions by impact over effort, separating on-page from off-page.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
- Explicit YMYL classification and declared threshold.
- Table with the 4 pillars, each with quoted fragment, gap, and level; Experience separated from Expertise.
- Between 3 and 6 rewrites; zero invented data; each assumption marked [ASSUMPTION].
- Verifiable authorship block; no credentials or awards without backing.

spec-marketing_datos_estructurados_schem:
[inputs]

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Structured data needs to be implemented on {{URL_O_PAGINA}} to make it eligible for rich results and improve its SERP presentation (stars, FAQ, breadcrumb, sitelinks, brand panel). Risk to control: marking content that is not visible or not representative invalidates eligibility and may lead to a manual action for structured data spam; the same applies to declaring types that Google has already withdrawn as rich results. Solving this correctly unlocks incremental CTR, entity graph consistency at site level, and a reusable technical foundation in templates.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior technical SEO specialist, expert in schema.org and Google's rich results guidelines, with hands-on experience in JSON-LD and entity graph modeling.
Deliverable: markup block ready for production plus validation, deployment, and maintenance plan. Steps:
1. Classify the page against {{TIPO_PAGINA}} and map the relevant schema.org type or types for {{RICH_RESULT_OBJETIVO}}; if missing, infer the viable rich result.
2. Discard types not supported today as rich results (e.g. HowTo; FAQ restricted to government/health authority sites) and justify each choice with [ASSUMPTION] when it depends on current policy.

Phase 1 Diagnosis: confirm page type, intent, and rich result viable today.
Phase 2 Modeling: select schema.org types and map each property to visible content.
Phase 3 Generation: produce the JSON-LD nested in @graph with entity graph and reusable @ids.
Phase 4 Validation and deployment: define tests, interpret errors and warnings, locate the script, and leave a monitoring plan.
Edge cases: page with non-representative reviews (do not mark aggregates without real, visible reviews); FAQ duplicated across multiple URLs (a single canonical block); multilingual (inLanguage + entities per locale); JS-injected content (verify that Google renders it before depending on it).
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- schema.org type or types justified and supported by Google today for the target rich result; withdrawn types discarded with reason.
- Every marked property corresponds to visible content on the same page; assumptions labeled [ASSUMPTION] with the data to confirm.
- Syntactically valid JSON-LD, nested in @graph, with correct @context and @type and reusable @ids; entities deduplicated via sameAs.

- Executable validation plan with both tools, with a reading of errors versus warnings and eligibility criterion.
- Script location guide (server-side preferred), dynamic/multilingual content handling, Search Console monitoring, and explicit list of what NOT to mark.

spec-marketing_seo_local_google_business:
[inputs]
- NEGOCIO: {{NEGOCIO}} > Exact business name as it should appear on the business profile
- UBICACION: {{UBICACION}} > City, neighborhood, or service area targeted for local searches

- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

--- S | SITUATION ---
The business competes to appear in the map pack: the three-result local block with map that Google shows for searches with geographic intent ("near me", category + city). Whoever is not in that block loses the majority of high-intent calls, directions, and visits. Local ranking responds to three levers: relevance (profile-query fit), distance (proximity to the searcher), and prominence (authority and social signals). Optimizing profile, NAP, categories, reviews, and local signals unlocks sustained organic visibility, without depending on paid advertising, and builds a defensible local EstrategIA.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior local SEO specialist with a proven track record of scaling businesses in the map pack and mastering relevance, distance, and prominence.
Deliverable: audit report + 90-day local optimization plan. Steps:
1. Audit the NAP (Name, Address, Phone) character by character across profile, site, and directories/citations; list discrepancies, duplicate listings, and format variations as priority findings.
2. Validate the primary category and propose justified secondary ones; discard inflated categories; map each category to real customer queries.
3. Review profile completeness: hours, service area, attributes, description with natural local keywords, products/services, geotagged photos, UTM link. Flag empty or weak fields.
4. Design the review system: ethical and sustained acquisition (no incentives prohibited by the platform's policy), response templates for positive and negative reviews, cadence and rating target.
5. Recommend local on-page signals: location landing page, LocalBusiness structured data, embedded map, geolocalized content, sector local citations/backlinks.
6. Consolidate everything in a findings table prioritized by impact x effort and a phased plan with metrics.
Limits: do not promise guaranteed rankings or exact indexing timelines; recommendations within platform policies.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Diagnosis: assess current state of NAP, categories, profile, and reviews; detect inconsistencies and gaps.
Phase 2 - Prioritization: order findings by impact on local ranking x effort; separate quick wins from structural initiatives.
Phase 3 - Design: define canonical NAP, category set, review system, and on-page signals.
Phase 4 - Plan: sequence over 90 days (0-30 foundations and NAP, 31-60 local content and reviews, 61-90 citations and authority) with owners and metrics (map pack position, calls, direction requests, site clicks).
Edge cases: service-area business without public address > adjust distance lever and service zones; multi-location > NAP and landing per location; category nonexistent on the platform > use the closest one plus attributes. Missing data > ask before proceeding; never invent verifiable data.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] NAP verified character by character across profile, site, and citations; discrepancies and duplicates listed.
- [ ] Precise primary category + justified secondary ones; no inflated categories; each mapped to queries.
- [ ] Profile without critical empty fields; description with natural, non-forced local keywords.
- [ ] Ethical review system (no prohibited incentives) with response templates and target cadence.
- [ ] On-page signals: local landing page, LocalBusiness schema, embedded map, sector citations.
- [ ] Findings table prioritized by impact x effort.
- [ ] 90-day phased plan with measurable metrics (position, calls, directions, clicks).
- [ ] Applicable edge cases resolved (service-area, multi-location, nonexistent category).
- [ ] Assumptions marked as [ASSUMPTION] when data is missing; no guaranteed rankings.
Expected deliverable: local SEO audit report with canonical NAP, category set, review system, and actionable 90-day plan with KPIs.
spec-marketing_brecha_contenido_competid:
[inputs]
- MI_SITIO: {{MI_SITIO}} > Domain or URL of the site to position
- COMPETIDORES: {{COMPETIDORES}} > 2 to 4 direct competitors by domain or URL
- MERCADO_IDIOMA: {{MERCADO_IDIOMA}} > Target country/region and search language
- OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO: {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} > Business result behind the traffic (leads, sales, subscriptions, authority)
- TEMAS_NUCLEO: {{TEMAS_NUCLEO}} > Central thematic clusters or categories of the site
- DATOS_DISPONIBLES: {{DATOS_DISPONIBLES}} > Keyword exports, Search Console, SEO tools, or "no data" (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need to decide where to invest my content production in the coming quarters. My competitors capture organic traffic on topics and keywords where my site does not appear or ranks weakly, and that gap is existing demand that is currently going to others. Closing the right gaps unlocks qualified traffic without waiting to create new demand: each topic won is an entry door currently closed. This analysis converts my competitors' advantage into my prioritized editorial roadmap, not a list of standalone keywords.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior SEO and content strategist with a decade of closing organic positioning gaps in competitive markets, expert in search intent, thematic cluster architecture, and value-over-effort prioritization.

Deliverable: a content gap analysis with a prioritized closing plan. Steps:
1. Reconstruct the universe of topics and keywords where COMPETIDORES have presence and MI_SITIO does not appear or ranks weakly (page 2 or worse). Separate absolute gaps (the competitor ranks, I do not exist) from strength gaps (both rank but the competitor ranks better): they close differently.
2. Classify each gap by search intent: informational, commercial, transactional.
3. Score each gap by potential value (estimated volume, fit with OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO, proximity to conversion according to intent) and by realistic difficulty (competitor authority, depth of the ranking content, strength of my domain). If a gap is valuable but requires authority I do not have, say so: do not disguise it as a quick win.
4. Prioritize with a value-versus-effort matrix and mark quick wins (high value, low difficulty). Also identify traps (high volume, intent irrelevant to the business) to discard them with an argument.
5. For the top topics, deliver a closing plan: recommended format, differentiating angle versus the content that already ranks (not a clone), intent to satisfy, suggested structure, internal linking toward and from existing pieces, and an editorial calendar by quarter.
6. Close with an executive summary of the 3 highest-impact gaps and the first actionable step of this week.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: confirm MI_SITIO, COMPETIDORES, MERCADO_IDIOMA, and OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO. If DATOS_DISPONIBLES is "no data", declare the limitation at the start and work with ordinal ranges (high/medium/low), never with invented numbers.
Phase 2 - Gap map: list competitor topics/keywords absent or weak on my site, grouped by cluster and intent; distinguish absolute gap from strength gap.
Phase 3 - Scoring: assign value (1-5) and difficulty (1-5) to each gap with explicit criterion per score. Proximity to conversion matters: transactional relevant > informational with high volume but distant from the business.
Phase 4 - Prioritization: place in value/effort matrix, separate quick wins from long-term bets, and mark traps to discard.
Phase 5 - Closing plan: brief per top topic + quarterly editorial calendar with realistic publication capacity + executive summary.
Truth rule: mark [ASSUMPTION] on every estimate not supported in DATOS_DISPONIBLES or a real tool; never present volumes, difficulties, or rankings as verified facts if you do not have them.
Limits: do not recommend cannibalizing own content that already ranks; do not chase keywords unrelated to the business even if they have volume; do not promise rankings or timelines as certainties.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Gaps separated into absolute and strength gaps.
- [ ] Each gap classified by intent (informational/commercial/transactional).
- [ ] Each gap with a value and difficulty score and their explicit justification.
- [ ] Value-versus-effort matrix with quick wins marked and traps discarded with an argument.
- [ ] Each top topic with a differentiating angle versus the content that already ranks, not a clone.
- [ ] Internal linking defined per piece (toward and from existing content).
- [ ] Editorial calendar by quarter with assigned pieces and realistic capacity.
- [ ] Estimates without data marked [ASSUMPTION]; zero figures presented as facts.
- [ ] No cannibalization recommendations or keywords irrelevant to the business.
- [ ] Executive summary with the 3 highest-impact gaps and first step of this week.
Expected deliverable: content gap report with scored gap table, prioritization matrix, top-topic briefs, quarterly editorial calendar, and actionable executive summary.
spec-marketing_seo_canibalizacion_keywor:
[inputs]
- DOMINIO: {{DOMINIO}} > Domain or section of the site under analysis (e.g. blog.empresa.com/recursos)
- LISTADO_URLS: {{LISTADO_URLS}} > URLs suspected of competing with each other, one per line
- KEYWORDS_OBJETIVO: {{KEYWORDS_OBJETIVO}} > Disputed search terms to diagnose
- DATOS_RENDIMIENTO: {{DATOS_RENDIMIENTO}} > Metrics per URL/keyword: average position, impressions, clicks, CTR; ideally a Search Console export (optional)
- OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO: {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} > What to optimize: traffic, conversion, authority of a pillar page (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Several URLs on {{DOMINIO}} compete for the same terms in {{KEYWORDS_OBJETIVO}}, splitting authority, confusing the search engine about which page to rank, and depressing the performance of the entire cluster. Typical symptoms: the search engine alternates the URL it shows for the same query, two URLs appear on the same results page, CTR is split, and no page consolidates its position. This diagnosis unlocks a clean decision per conflict — consolidate or differentiate — to recover positions, concentrate links, and stop competing against the site itself. Not every keyword coincidence is cannibalization: it only is when there is real intent overlap and measurable or inferable harm to performance.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior technical and content SEO specialist with experience diagnosing keyword cannibalization on sites with hundreds of URLs.
Deliver a cannibalization diagnosis with an actionable verdict per conflict. Steps:
1. Group {{LISTADO_URLS}} into cannibalization clusters; per cluster identify the keyword from {{KEYWORDS_OBJETIVO}} in dispute, the involved URLs, and — using {{DATOS_RENDIMIENTO}} — the evidence (overlapping positions, URL the search engine alternates, split CTR, double appearance in results). Without data, infer the indication from title, H1, and body overlap, and mark it [ASSUMPTION].
2. Classify the search intent of each URL: informational, commercial, transactional, or navigational. A shared keyword with different intents is NOT cannibalization: it is legitimate funnel coverage.
3. Decide per cluster: same keyword + same intent + high overlap -> CONSOLIDATE (designate canonical winning URL with explicit criterion: link authority > indexed age > performance > content completeness; 301 from the rest to it, merging useful content). Different intents -> DIFFERENTIATE (assign a unique primary keyword per URL). Edge case: same intent but both URLs have high authority and relevant traffic -> propose phased consolidation or pillar redesign, not a blind 301.
4. Define on-page changes per differentiated URL: title, H1, primary keyword, and internal linking with anchors that separate signals and prevent recurrence.
5. Prioritize the backlog by impact/effort aligned to {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}, with risks per move.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Detection: build the clusters and document the conflict evidence with data; without data, mark the indication with [ASSUMPTION] and name what data would confirm it.
Phase 2 Intent: map intent per URL and contrast within each cluster; discard as a false positive any cluster with divergent intents.
Phase 3 Decision: apply the consolidate/differentiate decision tree; justify the chosen canonical URL with the hierarchical criterion.
Phase 4 Plan: translate into 301 redirects, primary keyword reassignment, on-page changes, and prioritized backlog with risks (temporary ranking loss, internal and external links to update, misapplied canonical or 301, redirect chains, orphan pages). Recommend monitoring positions and indexation 4 to 8 weeks after each move.
Limits: do not invent metrics or URLs; the diagnosis is of architecture, not an audit of speed, technical duplicate content, or external backlinks unless {{DATOS_RENDIMIENTO}} provides them. If {{LISTADO_URLS}} or {{KEYWORDS_OBJETIVO}} is missing, ask before executing: without them the diagnosis is unreliable.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Each cluster names the disputed keyword and all involved URLs.
- [ ] Each URL has a classified search intent; clusters with divergent intent are marked as false positives.
- [ ] Each cluster closes with an unambiguous verdict: consolidate or differentiate.
- [ ] Every CONSOLIDATE designates a canonical winning URL with an explicit hierarchical criterion and a 301 map.
- [ ] Every DIFFERENTIATE assigns a unique primary keyword per URL + changes in title, H1, and internal linking.
- [ ] Backlog prioritized by impact/effort, aligned to {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}, with risks per move and monitoring window.
- [ ] Indications without data marked [ASSUMPTION] with the data that would confirm them; when data is insufficient, it is requested instead of invented.
Expected deliverable: cannibalization cluster table (keyword, URLs, intent, evidence, verdict), 301 redirect map, primary keyword reassignment per URL, on-page change list, and prioritized backlog with risks and monitoring window.
spec-marketing_estrategia_aeo_geo_ia:
[inputs]
- MARCA_O_PRODUCTO: {{MARCA_O_PRODUCTO}} > Name of the brand, product, or service to position as a cited source in AI responses
- CATEGORIA: {{CATEGORIA}} > Category or topic in which you want to be cited when someone asks an assistant
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Profile of the prospect querying the AI engines (role, sector, maturity level, language)
- CONTENIDO_ACTUAL: {{CONTENIDO_ACTUAL}} > URLs or text of existing content to audit
- COMPETIDORES: {{COMPETIDORES}} > Reference brands to compare in share of voice (optional)
- ACCION_OBJETIVO: {{ACCION_OBJETIVO}} > Expected action from the user after seeing your brand cited (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Purchase decisions began to be resolved within the assistant's response: the user asks and ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, or Google AI Overviews respond citing a handful of sources. If your brand is not the source the model extracts and attributes, it does not exist in the conversation. Classic SEO optimizes to rank a link; AEO optimizes to be the extracted answer and GEO to be the source cited in the generative synthesis. This unlocks brand presence at the exact decision point, referral traffic from generative responses, and measurable category authority as share of voice against competitors. Structural limit: generative ranking is not controllable like a SERP; it is influenced, not guaranteed, and each engine weights sources differently.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) and Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) strategist, with experience making B2B and B2C brands cited in ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, and Google AI Overviews, and in instrumenting share of voice in AI responses.

Deliverable: a ready-to-execute citability EstrategIA. Produce, in this order:
1. Bank of conversational intents: 15 to 25 real questions that a {{AUDIENCIA}} prospect would ask an assistant about {{CATEGORIA}}, grouped by stage (discovery, comparison, decision) and by expected response format (definition, list, comparison, step-by-step).
2. Passage-by-passage extractability audit table of {{CONTENIDO_ACTUAL}}: per passage, extractable/not-extractable verdict, 0-3 score (0 unusable, 3 citable as-is), and root cause (buried answer, non-self-contained claim, data without source or date, ambiguous context, non-parseable format). If a passage is extractable in one engine and not in another, indicate it.
3. Rewritten before/after blocks: convert weak passages into citable blocks with the answer-first pattern (the assertion in the first sentence), self-contained claims, data with source and date, and semantic structure; each block names the root cause it corrects.
4. Authority and entity backlog: signals to reinforce so the model associates {{MARCA_O_PRODUCTO}} with {{CATEGORIA}}, prioritized by impact and effort, comparing against {{COMPETIDORES}} (entity consistency in directories/profiles, expert attribution with identifiable author, proprietary primary data, presence in third-party sources models read, schema.org structured data).
5. Measurement dashboard: per row metric + test query + cadence, with share of voice defined as % of responses where you appear cited out of total queries in the set, oriented toward {{ACCION_OBJETIVO}}.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Interpret: reformulate business objective, {{CATEGORIA}}, {{AUDIENCIA}}, and {{ACCION_OBJETIVO}}. If {{CATEGORIA}}, {{AUDIENCIA}}, or {{CONTENIDO_ACTUAL}} is missing, ask before continuing.
Phase 2 Map: derive conversational intents from category and audience; write them as a human would say them to an assistant, not as keywords.
Phase 3 Audit: diagnose extractability passage by passage with score and root cause; flag divergences between engines when applicable.
Phase 4 Rewrite: deliver each citable block before/after, ready to publish, with the assertion in the first sentence and data validity date.
Phase 5 Reinforce: prioritized authority and entity backlog (entity consistency, expert attribution, proprietary primary data, third parties models read, structured data) with effort and impact.
Phase 6 Measure: citation tracking protocol, share of voice definition, and recurring test queries; set a cadence because each engine's index changes and a passage cited today may no longer be tomorrow.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
- Each conversational intent is written as a real human question, not as a keyword.
- Each rewritten passage passes the extraction test: it is citable out of context in a single sentence, without an ambiguous antecedent.
- Every relevant claim carries data and date, or is marked [ASSUMPTION]; no invented data.
- Each before/after block names the root cause it corrects.
- The authority backlog is prioritized by impact and effort, not as a flat list.
- The dashboard defines per row metric + test query + cadence, with share of voice expressed as a percentage against {{COMPETIDORES}}.
- No guaranteed position or citation is promised; the output distinguishes what is controlled from what is influenced.
Expected deliverable: single document with (a) intent bank, (b) extractability audit table with score, (c) rewritten before/after blocks, (d) prioritized authority and entity backlog, (e) share of voice dashboard in AI engines.
spec-marketing_calendario_editorial_trim:
[inputs]
- MARCA_E_INDUSTRIA: {{MARCA_E_INDUSTRIA}} > Brand name and the sector it operates in

The team publishes reactively and loses alignment with objectives. --- C | CRITERIA ---

spec-marketing_modelo_pilares_contenido:
[inputs]

--- S | SITUATION ---
The brand produces reactive content, without a stable editorial axis: the message disperses and authority dilutes. Defining 3 to 5 pillars fixes the thematic territories where the brand has the right to speak, aligns each piece with a business objective, and unlocks a coherent editorial calendar, reusable by anyone on the team and by AI. A pillar is not a trending topic or a product line: it is a sustainable authority territory.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: senior brand content strategist with more than ten years designing editorial architectures for professional services brands.
Deliverable: a model of 3 to 5 content pillars with editorial mix and risks. Steps:
1. Synthesize the brand territory: positioning in one sentence and the topics with real legitimacy, from MARCA, PROMESA_CENTRAL, AUDIENCIA_PRIMARIA, and DIFERENCIADOR.
2. Derive each pillar from the intersection of audience need, brand authority, and differentiation (relevance zone); discard overlaps and product categories disguised as topics.
3. Document per pillar: memorable name, one-sentence definition, why it matters to the audience, objective from OBJETIVOS_NEGOCIO it serves, 4 to 6 concrete angles, formats per channel from CANALES, and observable and measurable success signal.
4. Define the editorial mix: percentage weight per pillar summing to 100 (justify the weight by priority objective) and an operable cadence rule.
5. Close with three risks (cannibalization between pillars, pillar without traction, pillar outside legitimacy) with an observable trigger alert and concrete mitigation.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Diagnosis: extract territory and legitimacy from the inputs. If DIFERENCIADOR or TONO_DE_MARCA is missing, infer and mark [ASSUMPTION]. If AUDIENCIA_PRIMARIA or PROMESA_CENTRAL is missing, stop and ask: without them the pillars would be arbitrary.
Phase 2 Derivation: apply the relevance zone model to generate candidates and prune the redundant ones down to 3 to 5. Edge case: if only one legitimate territory emerges, deliver it with sub-territories and flag the monotopical risk instead of inflating to 3.
Phase 3 Documentation: complete the pillar card and table; angles must be piece headlines, not labels.
Phase 4 Balancing: assign percentage weights according to OBJETIVOS_NEGOCIO (greater weight to the period's priority objective) and set an operable cadence per channel.
Phase 5 Risk control: validate overlaps, projected traction, and legitimacy; each risk with trigger and mitigation.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- Between 3 and 5 pillars (or 1 substantiated with sub-territories if only one legitimate territory exists), mutually exclusive and collectively sufficient.
- No pillar is a product category or a trending topic; each one originates from the relevance zone.
- Each pillar ties to an objective from OBJETIVOS_NEGOCIO and brings 4 to 6 actionable angles written as headlines.
- Each pillar has an observable and measurable success signal.
- Percentage weights sum to exactly 100, justified by priority objective; there is an explicit cadence rule.
- Three risks, each with an observable trigger alert and concrete mitigation.
- No prices, without the word free, neutral professional Spanish, no emojis.
- Assumptions marked as [ASSUMPTION]; critical missing data requested before executing.
Expected deliverable: pillar table (name, definition, objective, angles, formats per channel, success signal), editorial mix block with justified percentages and cadence, and three-risk section with trigger and mitigation.

--- S | SITUATION ---
A pillar piece concentrates hours of work and a message that deserves more than one exposure. Published once, it exhausts its reach in days and wastes its density. This prompt converts that piece into a system of channel-specific derivative assets — not mechanical excerpts: each derivative respects the native logic of its platform and maintains traceability to the parent message. It unlocks sustained presence, message reinforcement through strategic repetition, and a reusable distribution engine campaign after campaign.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior content and multichannel distribution strategist, with a track record building repurposing engines for B2B and personal-authority brands.
Deliverable: system of derivative assets from {{PIEZA_PILAR}} for {{PUBLICO_OBJETIVO}}, optimized for {{CANALES_PRIORITARIOS}} and aligned with {{OBJETIVO_CAMPANA}}, plus a distribution calendar and traceability map.
1. Dissect the pillar piece and extract its value cores: central thesis, supporting arguments, memorable data or examples, phrases with standalone power, and objections it resolves. Do not invent content absent from the original.
2. Mark each core with its dominant angle: educational, counter-intuitive, narrative, tactical, or inspirational. If a core supports two angles, derive two distinct assets rather than diluting them into one.
3. Map each core to the channel in {{CANALES_PRIORITARIOS}} where it performs best according to that channel's native logic; do not force a core into a channel where it cannot breathe. The same core can feed two channels if the reformatting changes the format, not just the length.
4. Draft each derivative asset ready to publish or as an actionable script, with an opening hook, development, and a close with a call to action coherent with the channel and {{OBJETIVO_CAMPANA}}.
5. Order the assets in a {{HORIZONTE_DISTRIBUCION}} distribution calendar: open with the one with the highest expected traction, stagger the cadence, avoid cannibalization, and maintain a through-line back to the pillar piece.
6. Build a traceability map connecting each derivative asset to the value core it originates from.

Phase 1 Dissection: read the pillar piece in full and isolate the value cores before thinking about formats; label each one with its dominant angle. If the piece, the audience, the channels, or the objective is missing, ask for them; do not assume the source content.
Phase 2 Channel-core assignment: cross each core against the native logic of each priority channel and justify in one line why that core belongs in that channel; if a core does not fit any channel, leave it out and record it.
Phase 3 Production: generate the text or script for each asset respecting native length, tone, and format; each piece is self-contained but recognizably part of the same body. Estimate traction as a hypothesis, not a guarantee.
Phase 4 Orchestration: sequence the assets in the calendar and draw the core-to-asset map to audit that nothing lost the parent message.
Default assumptions: if {{HORIZONTE_DISTRIBUCION}} is omitted, use 14 days; if no cadence is specified, do not exceed one asset per channel per day to avoid fatigue. Declare all assumptions at the outset.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- Each derivative asset traces back to an identified value core from the pillar piece (no invention of content absent from the original).
- Every figure or data point cited is marked as coming from the pillar piece; no new statistics are introduced.
- Each asset respects the native logic of its channel: length, format, tone, and opening mechanic.
- No core is forced into a channel where it cannot breathe; assignments are justified in one line and cores without a channel are recorded.
- The calendar staggers the assets, opens with the one with the highest expected traction, respects the declared maximum cadence, and avoids cannibalization.
- Each asset closes with a call to action coherent with the channel and the campaign objective.
- Expected traction is presented as a hypothesis, never as a guaranteed result.

- [ ] Angle differentiated from what already exists (not generic), with a reason for credibility.
- [ ] Primary keyword with search intent + 3 to 5 coherent secondary keywords.

spec-marketing_guion_video_corto_hook:

--- S | SITUATION ---
In vertical feeds, the decision to keep watching or swipe away happens in the first 3 seconds, and retention drops quickly after that; winning back someone who almost left requires an attention shift every few seconds. A script with a deliberate hook-retention structure unlocks higher view time, more positive algorithm signals (saves, comments, shares, retention), and a CTA that converts attention into action. This prompt produces a ready-to-record script about {{TEMA}}, calibrated to {{PLATAFORMA}}, {{AUDIENCIA}}, and {{OBJETIVO}}, without improvising on set and without promising what the body does not deliver.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior vertical content scriptwriter and retention strategist, with mastery of direct-response copywriting and the attention levers native to the short format.
Deliverable: complete 9:16 vertical video script ready to record. Steps:
1. Confirm or request in a single round the missing inputs (TEMA, PLATAFORMA, AUDIENCIA, OBJETIVO, DURACION_SEGUNDOS, ACCION_CTA); review {{ADJUNTOS}} if they exist.
2. Define the single central idea of the video and the explicit promise the hook must deliver; adjust the angle to the awareness level of {{AUDIENCIA}}.
3. Write three HOOK variants of up to 3 seconds (A/B/C), each with a different lever: tension or contradiction, concrete promise, uncomfortable question, surprising data, or common mistake.
4. Develop the body with sustained retention: escalating curiosity, fast pacing, transitions that renew attention, and zero filler; respect {{DURACION_SEGUNDOS}}.
5. Close with a single low-friction CTA aligned with {{OBJETIVO}} using {{ACCION_CTA}}.
6. Present the script scene by scene with approximate timestamp and parallel columns for spoken audio, visual indication, and on-screen text.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: fix the central idea, promise, and angle for {{AUDIENCIA}}; mark assumptions with [ASSUMPTION] if context is missing. Constraint: one single promise; if the topic forces two, cut or propose splitting into two videos.
Phase 2 - Hooks: draft A/B/C, each readable aloud in <=3 seconds, with a distinct lever and without promising what the body does not deliver; indicate which lever each one uses.
Phase 3 - Retention: structure the development in 2–4 beats with an explicit continuity hook between each (open loop, escalation, contrast); validate that no segment exceeds ~7 seconds without an attention shift. Edge case: if {{DURACION_SEGUNDOS}} is very short (<25 s), reduce beats rather than accelerating to an unreadable pace.
Phase 4 - Close: single CTA, concrete and low-friction; coherent with {{OBJETIVO}}. If {{OBJETIVO}} and {{ACCION_CTA}} do not align, propose the CTA most aligned with the objective and mark the trade-off.
Phase 5 - Assembly: tabulate scenes with timestamp, audio (spoken script), visual, and on-screen text; verify total duration against {{DURACION_SEGUNDOS}} (+/- 5 s) and that the on-screen text reinforces without literally duplicating the audio.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need a narrative manifesto that organizes how my brand tells its story to the market. The purpose is to stop talking about the brand as the protagonist and position the customer as the hero, with the brand in the role of guide. A single coherent narrative source must feed the sales page, email sequence, video script, and commercial pitch, all derived from the same arc, to avoid contradictory messages across channels.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior brand narrative strategist, expert in Donald Miller's StoryBrand framework applied to Joseph Campbell's hero's journey, with a focus on ethical conversion (without manipulation or exaggerated fear).

Deliverable: a narrative manifesto structured according to the StoryBrand arc, with the customer as hero and the brand as guide. Produce, in order:
1. Hero: define {{CLIENTE_IDEAL}} and their concrete desire (a single dominant objective, not a list).
2. Problem in three layers: external (tangible), internal (emotional), and philosophical (why it is unjust for it to continue), all derived from {{PROBLEMA_CENTRAL}}.
3. Guide: two phrases that show empathy and two that show authority from {{MARCA}}, without stealing the spotlight from the hero and without inventing credentials, awards, or figures not provided.
4. Plan: exactly three numbered and sequential steps the customer follows with the brand.
5. Call to action: one direct and one transitional, drafted as invitations (not as commands or pressure).
6. Success: a vivid and concrete image of {{TRANSFORMACION}} achieved.
7. Failure avoided: what is at stake if they do not act, with dignity and without dramatizing.
8. Close: a one-line lighthouse slogan and a 4-to-6-sentence manifesto paragraph ready to head a page.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: validate that you have the brand, customer, problem, and transformation. If any of those four is missing, ask for it and stop; do not invent the business.
Phase 2 - Arc: draft the eight blocks in order, keeping the customer as hero and the brand as guide in each one.
Phase 3 - Problem layers: ensure the conflict is expressed at all three levels, not just the external; the philosophical must be a principle, not a repetition of the external.
Phase 4 - Reuse and voice: generate the reuse map and the evidence questions; apply {{TONO_VOZ}} if provided; use neutral professional Spanish, without emojis.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
Decisions and constraints: the hero's desire is one only (if there are several, prioritize and mark the rest as secondary); empathy and authority are never mixed in the same phrase; the failure avoided does not use exaggerated fear; all inferences are marked [ASSUMPTION]; without prices or free-of-charge offers.

Quality checklist:
- [ ] The customer is the hero and the brand is the guide in all eight blocks; the brand is never the protagonist.
- [ ] The hero has a single dominant desire, concrete and measurable or recognizable.
- [ ] The problem appears in all three layers and the philosophical is a principle, not an echo of the external.
- [ ] The guide balances two empathy phrases and two authority phrases, without inventing credentials or figures.
- [ ] The plan has exactly three clear and sequential steps.
- [ ] There is a direct call to action and a transitional one, both as invitations.

spec-marketing_topical_authority_hub:
[inputs]

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Building topical authority means covering a topic with such depth and cohesion that search engines and audiences recognize you as the reference source for the niche — not as just one more isolated piece. A well-designed hub (pillar-cluster architecture) concentrates relevance signals, captures search intent at each stage of the journey, and builds a defensible advantage: each article reinforces the others. What is unlocked is compounding organic traffic, reduced dependence on paid media, and a content strategy that scales by design, not by volume. The symmetrical risk is real: a poorly scoped universe or a mesh with cannibalization dilutes signals and competes against itself, so the plan must be as disciplined in what it excludes as in what it covers.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior SEO content strategist with a focus on topical authority and editorial information architecture.

Deliverable: complete content hub plan for {{TEMA_CENTRAL}}, directed at {{PUBLICO_OBJETIVO}} with angle {{ANGULO_DIFERENCIADOR}}. Produce:
1. Delimitation of the semantic universe: subtopics, key entities, and questions an expert in the niche must answer. Explicitly declare the scope limit (what stays out and why) to avoid dispersion.
2. Topical authority map in three layers: central pillar page, thematic clusters, and satellite articles per cluster, sized according to {{MADUREZ_SITIO}} (new site: focused minimum viable hub; scattered: consolidation and redirection; partial authority: expansion on strengths).
3. Hub master table: for each piece, working title, layer (pillar/cluster/satellite), dominant search intent (informational, commercial, transactional, navigational), journey stage (discovery, consideration, decision), differential angle, and role in the mesh (concentrates / distributes / captures).
4. Coverage gap detection compared to what already ranks; every unverifiable estimate marked as [ASSUMPTION] with its validation criterion (e.g. confirm with a keyword tool before producing).
5. Internal linking map: pillar-cluster, cluster-satellite, and satellite-satellite relationships, with entity-oriented anchor text (not repeated exact-match).

You are going to design the structure of a Meta Ads (Facebook and Instagram) campaign with Advantage Campaign Budget (CBO): a single budget lives at the campaign level and the algorithm distributes it in real time among ad sets toward the audience-and-creative combinations with the best performance. The real unit of learning is not the account but the ad set: each ad set needs enough signal density for the algorithm to model who to serve. A poorly assembled hierarchy (too many ad sets, overlapping audiences, budget that does not feed learning, unnecessary spend limits, edits that restart learning) fragments signals, keeps ad sets trapped in the learning phase, and drives up cost per result. A correct structure concentrates signals, exits learning, and lets the system invest where it performs. The goal is a campaign ready to build and read with judgment, not to improvise.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior paid media strategist specialized in Meta Ads, with experience managing campaign-level budget (CBO/Advantage) in performance accounts and mastery of the learning phase, attribution, and audience overlap.

1. Define the correct campaign objective and optimization event for META_NEGOCIO and EVENTO_CONVERSION, justifying the choice against the funnel (do not optimize a deeper event than the volume can sustain).
2. Determine the number of ad sets and the segmentation logic for each from AUDIENCIAS, avoiding overlap that would cannibalize delivery (audiences that intersect compete in the same auction and drive up cost). Start from a few broad ad sets; consolidating is preferable to multiplying. Flag where to activate Advantage+ Audience as a signal and where to restrict.
3. Recommend campaign-level budget using the 50x rule: each active ad set should be able to reach approximately 50 conversions of the event per week to exit the learning phase. If TICKET_PROMEDIO or NIVEL_INVERSION do not allow it, propose a higher-funnel event (e.g., initiate checkout or add to cart instead of purchase) and explain the proxy-vs.-final-event trade-off.
4. Indicate whether minimum/maximum spend limits per ad set are advisable and why; by default do not use them, because they restrict the algorithm and may prevent exiting learning. Valid exception: protecting a strategic audience (e.g., retargeting) from receiving no delivery.
5. Define 3 to 5 ads per ad set with distinct creative angles (not cosmetic variations of the same message) and a consistent naming convention (campaign | ad set | creative), traceable and filterable in reports.
6. Deliver a table with the final structure (campaign, ad sets, placements, attribution window, creatives) ready for Ads Manager.
7. Specify reading rules: duration and care of the learning phase, which edits restart it and which do not, the metric that defines the winner (aligned to META_NEGOCIO, not vanity metrics), when to consolidate, and when to turn off.

--- E | EXECUTION ---

If a critical piece of data is missing, ask for it before designing.

Phase 2 - Ad sets: define quantity, segmentation, and placements (default Advantage+ placements unless there is an explicit reason to restrict, e.g., a format that underperforms in a certain placement); eliminate overlaps and name the cannibalization risk.
Phase 3 - Budget: set the campaign budget coherent with learning (relative, no amounts); decide spend limits only if there is an explicit strategic reason.
Phase 4 - Creatives: 3 to 5 angles per ad set + naming convention; relate each angle to a pain point or motivator of the audience.
Phase 5 - Table and reading rules: assemble the buildable table and decision rules; close with two-week EstrategIA iteration plan (what to watch, what not to touch to avoid restarting learning, what to adjust).

The team needs to move from producing scattered creatives by intuition to a testing system where each piece validates an isolated hypothesis. A matrix that crosses message angles, formats, and hooks covers the message space with discipline, quickly identifies which angle and which hook move the needle, and reinvests the learning in the next batch. The risk to avoid: testing everything at once without isolating variables, which produces data but not learning.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior paid social strategist specialized in performance creative, with practice in Meta Ads, TikTok Ads, and LinkedIn Ads and in hypothesis-based angle testing frameworks.

spec-marketing_estructura_audiencias_pai:

--- S | SITUATION ---
Most paid social budget is burned showing the same ad and the same offer to people at opposing decision moments: the stranger who has just discovered the category receives the same thing as the customer ready to convert. This calls for an audience structure by temperature that assigns to each funnel level the message, offer, creative, and metric that correspond to it, for {{PRODUCTO_OFERTA}} targeting {{PUBLICO_OBJETIVO}} on {{PLATAFORMAS}}, with the objective of {{OBJETIVO_CONVERSION}}. Archetype: Senior paid media strategist (10+ years in Meta Ads, TikTok Ads, and LinkedIn Ads; full-funnel B2C and B2B acquisition funnels).

spec-marketing_estrategia_pujas_objetivo:
[inputs]

- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You are configuring or auditing the bid strategy for a paid media campaign and you need to align the bid model to the real KPI, not to the platform default. A correct choice unlocks the algorithm to optimize toward the business result (CPA, ROAS, or volume) rather than spending against a vanity metric; an incorrect one burns investment in a poorly calibrated learning period. The most expensive mistake is not choosing the wrong model, but activating target bidding without sufficient conversion signals: the algorithm does not learn, drives up CPA, and forces a restart of learning.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior paid media strategist (Google Ads and Meta) specialized in Smart Bidding and acquisition unit economics.
Deliver a bid model recommendation with an implementation plan:
1. Map KPI_PRIMARIO to the correct model: volume with no efficiency ceiling and budget to spend > Maximize conversions; controlled CPA > tCPA; profitability/ROAS with variable conversion values > tROAS; maximum value with fixed budget > Maximize value; FASE_FUNNEL awareness/consideration > CPM/CPV or Maximize clicks as a bridge.
2. Audit prerequisites against HISTORICO_CONVERSIONES: sufficient recent volume (indicative reference ~30 conv/30d for tCPA, ~50 for tROAS; mark [ASSUMPTION] if data is not confirmed) and instrumented and deduplicated conversion/value tracking.
3. Set the initial target from real history (real CPA for tCPA, real ROAS for tROAS) with a ramp; never aggressive targets on day one.
4. Define expected learning period and the rule of not moving target/budget by more than ~20% while it lasts.
5. Define guardrails tied to PRESUPUESTO and adjustment triggers.
Resolve these edge cases when applicable: (a) no history > start with volume/clicks and set the conversion threshold to migrate to target; (b) recent seasonality or promotion that inflates/deflates history > use a representative window or seasonal adjustment, not the peak; (c) conversion values not instrumented or not variable > discard tROAS and use tCPA or Maximize conversions; (d) insufficient budget for ~minimum conversion/day > warn about permanent learning risk before promising a target; (e) multiple funnel stages in one campaign > recommend separating or prioritizing the dominant stage.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Diagnosis: confirm KPI_PRIMARIO, PLATAFORMA, HISTORICO_CONVERSIONES, PRESUPUESTO, and FASE_FUNNEL; if any critical one is missing, ask before recommending (do not assume history).
Phase 2 - Selection: apply the KPI > model decision tree and resolve conflicts (fixed budget favors Maximize value/conversions with or without target; efficiency favors tCPA/tROAS). Explicitly state the chosen trade-off (efficiency vs. volume, control vs. learning speed).
Phase 3 - Prerequisites: validate volume and tracking; if not qualifying for Smart Bidding by value/CPA, recommend the bridge (Maximize conversions/clicks) and the quantitative threshold to migrate.
Phase 4 - Calibration: derive initial target and ramp from history; define learning window and exit condition.
Phase 5 - Guardrails: write limits, early alert signals, and review cadence by iterations (not by individual days within learning).
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The recommended model is explicitly derived from KPI_PRIMARIO and FASE_FUNNEL, with one-sentence justification.
- [ ] Volume and tracking prerequisites audited against HISTORICO_CONVERSIONES; assumptions marked [ASSUMPTION].
- [ ] Initial target anchored to real history with a ramp, not an arbitrary goal.
- [ ] Learning period defined, exit condition explicit, and <=20% change rule.
- [ ] Guardrails tied to PRESUPUESTO with actionable adjustment triggers.

spec-marketing_secuencia_retargeting_pai:
[inputs]
- OFERTA: {{OFERTA}} > Product or service being promoted and who it targets
- CICLO_COMPRA: {{CICLO_COMPRA}} > Typical duration from first contact to conversion and relative weight of the ticket
- PLATAFORMAS: {{PLATAFORMAS}} > Available advertising platforms (e.g., Meta, Google, LinkedIn) and, if known, their audience exclusion model
- EVENTOS_RASTREADOS: {{EVENTOS_RASTREADOS}} > Behavioral events that are actually tracked today (page view, scroll, product view, checkout start, abandonment, etc.)

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A digital campaign already generates traffic, but remarketing treats all visitors equally and wastes budget on people with very different intents: the one who barely scrolled a page receives the same push as the one who abandoned a checkout. The objective is to build a stepped retargeting sequence by intent level for {{OFERTA}}, delivering to each group the message, frequency, and investment proportional to their proximity to {{OBJETIVO_CONVERSION}}. This unlocks less advertising waste, more relevant messages per awareness level, control of ad fatigue, and a clear re-conversion route auditable by the team.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior paid media strategist specialized in performance retargeting and audience architecture, with the judgment to translate behavior into actionable intent levels.

Deliverable: stepped retargeting sequence by intent level, ready to configure. Steps:
1. Validate inputs: confirm OFERTA, CICLO_COMPRA, PLATAFORMAS, EVENTOS_RASTREADOS, and OBJETIVO_CONVERSION. If any is missing or ambiguous, ask before proceeding; do not invent events or figures. If an event is not in EVENTOS_RASTREADOS, do not use it as an audience and log it as a measurement gap.
2. Map EVENTOS_RASTREADOS to intent levels from lowest to highest (e.g., shallow visit, interest, consideration, high intent, hot abandonment). Each step is anchored to at least one real event.
3. Define each step with the seven elements: audience (exact behavioral condition plus retention window in days), message angle and promise based on awareness level, format and piece, call to action, frequency window plus impression cap per person, exclusion logic, and exit criterion.

Phase 2 - Intent ladder: order events in ascending levels and justify the cutoff for each retention window based on CICLO_COMPRA (shorter windows for low ticket or fast cycle; longer for extended cycle).
Phase 3 - Design per step: complete the seven-element card per level, maintaining coherence between angle, format, and CTA. Message commitment scales with intent: reminder at low levels, social proof and objection handling at mid levels, closing offer and legitimate urgency at hot abandonment.
Phase 4 - Exclusion architecture: trace the inclusion/exclusion matrix to guarantee mutual exclusivity and converter handling; note implementation differences between PLATAFORMAS if exclusions are not shared across them.
Phase 5 - Flow and control: draw the journey between steps and assign the reading metrics. Resolve edge cases: if an audience falls below the minimum to serve, propose step merger or window extension marked [ASSUMPTION]; if there is coverage overlap between PLATAFORMAS, define the serving priority.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
