spec-producto_metricas_contrapeso:
[inputs]
- PRODUCTO: {{PRODUCTO}} > Product or feature and its core value proposition
- METRICAS_OBJETIVO: {{METRICAS_OBJETIVO}} > List of target metrics or levers the team seeks to move (north star, activation, conversion, etc.)
- VALOR_A_PROTEGER: {{VALOR_A_PROTEGER}} > Dimensions that must not be sacrificed: experience, retention, quality, trust, margin
- ETAPA: {{ETAPA}} > Product stage (discovery, growth, maturity); calibrates optimization aggressiveness and threshold severity (optional)
- CADENCIA_REVISION: {{CADENCIA_REVISION}} > Dashboard review frequency (weekly, biweekly, monthly) (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
When optimizing a single target metric, teams and automated systems themselves tend to find shortcuts that raise the number without creating real value: this is Goodhart's Law in action ("when a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure"). The purpose is to build a counter-metric system for {{PRODUCTO}}: each lever of {{METRICAS_OBJETIVO}} is paired with a guardrail that detects damage before it erodes {{VALOR_A_PROTEGER}}. This enables fast and aggressive product decisions without fear of degrading the experience, and gives the product committee a shared language for stopping toxic optimizations in time. The {{ETAPA}} of the product modulates how aggressive optimization can be and how strict the thresholds should be: in discovery, more noise is tolerated; in maturity, the guardrails tighten.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior Head of Product Analytics who has designed gaming-resistant metric dashboards for digital products, fluent in objective/counter-metric frameworks (counter-metrics, guardrail metrics, HEART, North Star + inputs) and in detecting Goodharting in systems with automated optimization.

Deliverable: an actionable counter-metric system. Produce, in order:
1. Inventory of target metrics from {{METRICAS_OBJETIVO}}, with their declared intent (what value-creating behavior each one seeks to incentivize) and the metric type (north star, input, output, health).
2. Gaming model per metric: the shortcut or perverse behavior that would raise the number without real value, who benefits (team, adversarial user, automated system), and a probability × impact estimate to prioritize.
3. Objective <> counter-metric pairing table: for each objective, the counter-metric that monitors the damage to {{VALOR_A_PROTEGER}}, the expected relationship between both (healthy correlation vs. toxic divergence), and why the counter-metric is orthogonal: it cannot be inflated using the same move that raises the objective. Include at least one universal health counter-metric (retention or satisfaction) and, if applicable to the business model, a margin or unit cost guardrail.
4. Operational definitions: numerator, denominator, time window, segment, and source for each target metric and counter-metric, with no calculation ambiguity.
5. Guardrail thresholds: normal, alert, and blocking levels for each counter-metric; the concrete action triggered by each level and who executes it.
6. Instrumentation: events or fields to capture so that each counter-metric is measurable; mark [ASSUMPTION] when inferring unconfirmed instrumentation and flag counter-metrics that are not currently measurable (tracking gap).
7. Conflict-resolution rule: how to resolve the situation when the objective rises but the counter-metric enters alert or blocking, the priority hierarchy between objective and protected value, and who decides (role).
8. Review protocol for the {{CADENCIA_REVISION}} cadence: what is reviewed, in what order, the escalation criterion, and how the learning cycle on miscalibrated thresholds is closed.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Interpretation: restate the product, the received target metrics, and the value to protect; declare assumptions with [ASSUMPTION] and flag anything ambiguous as {to_confirm}. Use {{ADJUNTOS}} as evidence; do not fabricate absent data.
Phase 2 - Gaming modeling: for each objective, reason through the incentive and the most likely shortcut before proposing a counter-metric; prioritize by probability × impact and discard trivial shortcuts.
Phase 3 - Pairing: assign each objective one counter-metric that is orthogonal to the shortcut (cannot be inflated by the same move) and justify the orthogonality; verify that no counter-metric is in turn gameable by the same team.
Phase 4 - Operationalization: define metrics, thresholds, instrumentation, and conflict-resolution rules; verify that no pair is left without a threshold, an action, or a responsible party.
Phase 5 - Verification: review against the CRITERION checklist and correct before delivering.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Each metric in {{METRICAS_OBJETIVO}} has exactly one paired and justified counter-metric.
- [ ] Each pair explicitly states the concrete gaming shortcut, who benefits, and why the counter-metric detects it.
- [ ] The counter-metric is orthogonal: it cannot be inflated by the same move that raises the objective, and is not gameable by the same actor.
- [ ] At least one health counter-metric (retention or satisfaction) exists, and a margin or cost guardrail when the business model requires it.
- [ ] Each metric (target and counter-metric) has a complete operational definition: numerator, denominator, window, segment, source.
- [ ] Each counter-metric has normal / alert / blocking thresholds with an associated action and responsible party.
- [ ] Inferred instrumentation marked with [ASSUMPTION]; tracking gaps flagged; ambiguities as {to_confirm}.
- [ ] A conflict-resolution rule exists with a priority hierarchy and a responsible party for the objective vs. counter-metric conflict.
- [ ] The review protocol fits {{CADENCIA_REVISION}} and closes the learning cycle on thresholds.
- [ ] Thresholds calibrated according to {{ETAPA}}; no vanity metrics without a guardrail; no made-up numbers.
Expected deliverable: document with inventory, objective/counter-metric pairing table, operational definitions, threshold table with actions and responsible parties, instrumentation plan with gaps, conflict-resolution rule, and review protocol, ready to present to the product committee.

spec-producto_l28_engagement:
[inputs]
- PRODUCTO: {{PRODUCTO}} > Product or feature to measure and its user unit (account, device, workspace). The unit sets the denominator for the entire reading.
- PERIODO: {{PERIODO}} > Available data range; must cover >=28 days for a complete L28 window. If shorter, it is reported as a limitation and users without sufficient tenure are excluded.
- EVENTO_ACTIVO: {{EVENTO_ACTIVO}} > What counts as an active day: a value event (not just an open/login), e.g. create/complete/transact. Counted once per calendar day.
- UMBRAL_HABITO: {{UMBRAL_HABITO}} > Active days in L28 from which habit is considered established (optional; default >=14/28).
- OBJETIVO: {{OBJETIVO}} > Decision the reading enables: activation, retention, expansion, or churn reduction (optional; default: general adherence diagnostic).
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Volume metrics (sign-ups, MAU, sessions) conceal whether the product generates habit or just passing curiosity. The L7/L28 model counts active days within rolling windows of 7 and 28 days to separate occasional use from habitual use and reveal real adherence. A correct reading unlocks decisions about {{OBJETIVO}}: where to invest in activation, which segment is about to convert to habit and which is close to churn, and whether the product sustains recurring value or relies on acquisition. Applies to {{PRODUCTO}} over the period {{PERIODO}}.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior product analyst specializing in engagement and retention metrics, with judgment for translating activity counts into actionable habit readings.
Deliverable: L7/L28 engagement report with definitions, distribution by bands, adherence, habit threshold, levers by segment, and verdict.
1. Set definitions: active day = {{EVENTO_ACTIVO}} (value event, once per calendar day); rolling window (last 7 and 28 days up to the cutoff date), not a calendar month; user unit of {{PRODUCTO}}.
2. Calculate per user the L7 count (active days in 7 days) and L28 count (active days in 28 days). Distinguish total panel from cohort (users who entered within the window).
3. Build the L28 distribution by bands: 1, 2–7, 8–13, 14–20, 21–28 active days, labeled curious / casual / regular / power user, with count and percentage per band.
4. Calculate adherence: stickiness as average L7 / 7 and as DAU/MAU; provide the value and its reading (what range suggests healthy habit for this product category).
5. Apply the {{UMBRAL_HABITO}} habit threshold (default >=14/28), report the percentage of the base that crosses it, and justify the cutoff; flag the bridge segment (8–13 days) as the biggest lever for converting to habit.
6. Derive actionable segmentation: per band, the recommended lever to move it to the next one, prioritized according to {{OBJETIVO}}, with the signal that would confirm the lever is working.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Definition: close the active event, rolling window, and user unit; if {{EVENTO_ACTIVO}} or {{PERIODO}} is unclear, or if the data is not known to be per user or aggregate, ask before calculating.
Phase 2 - Count: derive L7 and L28 per user; verify that the window covers 28 complete days to avoid downward bias for new users; if the period is shorter, declare the limitation and restrict the calculation to users with sufficient tenure.
Phase 3 - Reading: distribution by bands, adherence (stickiness and DAU/MAU), and habit threshold crossing; contrast against any available internal benchmarks, not against unverified external figures.
Phase 4 - Action: translate each band into a prioritized lever with its success signal and synthesize the habit verdict. Do not fabricate figures: cite data from {{ADJUNTOS}} if available; mark any illustrative number as an example [ASSUMPTION].
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
- Active day defined as a value event (not mere app open) and counted once per calendar day.
- Rolling L7 and L28 windows explicitly defined, distinct from the calendar month; L28 covers 28 complete days or the limitation is declared and users without tenure are excluded.
- Total panel and cohort differentiated where applicable; user unit explicit as denominator.
- Distribution across the five L28 bands with segment label and count and percentage per band.
- Adherence reported as stickiness (L7/7) and as DAU/MAU, each with its reading.
- Explicit and justified habit threshold, with percentage of the base that crosses it and identification of the bridge segment (8–13 days).
