Phase 3 Insight labeling: name each cluster as an actionable statement that expresses the user's tension.
Phase 4 Meta-themes and prioritization: connect related clusters, order by evidence and impact, and explain the ordering criterion.
Integrity rules: distinguish signal (multiple participants) from noise (isolated case); mark every single-participant case as [HYPOTHESIS], never as a confirmed finding. Do not invent or infer absent data; mark anything ambiguous as [ASSUMPTION] rather than forcing it into a group. Respect {{NUM_PARTICIPANTES}} when reporting dispersion and never report more distinct participants than actually exist. Edge cases: if the material is insufficient to synthesize (too few notes or no variety), say so and propose what to collect; if {{IMPACTO_PRODUCTO}} is not provided, prioritize by evidence strength alone and note it; if all evidence comes from 1-2 participants, warn that the result is exploratory, not conclusive. Do not use prices or the term "free" in any example or evidence.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Every note is atomic and in the user's language, not interpreted.
- [ ] Clusters emerge from the material; none uses an imposed taxonomy.
- [ ] Every theme carries an insight name in the form of a tension-bearing statement — not a generic noun.
- [ ] Every theme reports number of observations AND number of distinct participants.
- [ ] Single-participant cases are marked [HYPOTHESIS], not as findings.
- [ ] Zero invented observations; anything ambiguous is marked [ASSUMPTION]; participant count respects {{NUM_PARTICIPANTES}}.
- [ ] Prioritization combines evidence strength and impact, not just frequency, and explains the order.
- [ ] If the material is insufficient or the impact dimension was not provided, this is stated explicitly.
Expected deliverable: table or list of prioritized themes (insight name, #observations, #participants, evidence, pattern), followed by 1-2 meta-themes and a prioritization note that justifies the order. If NIVEL_DETALLE requests a full map, include the note detail per cluster plus the "ungrouped" cluster if any.
spec-producto_research_repository:
[inputs]
- EQUIPO_Y_PRODUCTO: {{EQUIPO_Y_PRODUCTO}} > Product team and product/line on which research is centralized
- HERRAMIENTA_REPOSITORIO: {{HERRAMIENTA_REPOSITORIO}} > Tool where the repository will live (e.g., Dovetail, Notion, Airtable, Confluence) (optional)
- VOLUMEN_RESEARCH: {{VOLUMEN_RESEARCH}} > Approximate volume of existing research and cadence of new studies (optional)
- EQUIPOS_CONSUMIDORES: {{EQUIPOS_CONSUMIDORES}} > Teams that will query the repository cross-functionally (product, design, engineering, marketing, support)
- METRICA_DE_EXITO: {{METRICA_DE_EXITO}} > How the team will know the repository is working (e.g., insight reuse, time-to-answer, cited decisions) (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
The research for {{EQUIPO_Y_PRODUCTO}} accumulates in long reports, decks, and loose notes that no one reopens: knowledge gets repeated, contradicted, or lost, and every decision starts from scratch. Building an atomic research repository converts each finding into a minimal reusable, citable unit, queryable by {{EQUIPOS_CONSUMIDORES}} without depending on who did the study. It unlocks product decisions traceable to evidence, faster onboarding, and a research memory that compounds value over time instead of degrading. The risk to avoid is the opposite: a repository that becomes a graveyard of outdated, over-tagged, uncurated insights.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior Research Ops Lead specializing in designing and scaling atomic-insight repositories in cross-functional product teams.
Deliverable: the complete, actionable design of the atomic research repository, instrumentable in {{HERRAMIENTA_REPOSITORIO}} without rewriting. Produce:
1. Atomic insight unit schema: mandatory fields (actionable statement in one sentence, segment/persona, evidence cited with source and date, confidence level, originating method, tags) and optional fields (estimated impact, product area, lifecycle status, owner, links to decisions that cite it). Include a realistic populated example relevant to the topic and the definition of done that separates a valid insight from a raw observation.
2. Tag taxonomy in orthogonal facets (topic, journey stage, segment, need type) and anti-proliferation rules: maximum values per facet, criterion for creating a new tag, vocabulary owner, and process for merging redundant labels.
3. Evidence level scale (e.g., directly observed > reported > inferred > assumed) that unambiguously separates observed from inferred, with an operational definition for each level and each insight linked to its original source.
4. Operational workflow capture > curation > cross-team query, with roles (who captures, who curates, who approves the vocabulary), a concrete maintenance cadence, and a freshness mechanism that prevents an insight graveyard.
5. Governance: deduplication criterion, archiving policy for obsolete or invalidated insights (with traceability of why), and repository health metrics aligned to {{METRICA_DE_EXITO}}.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: confirm {{EQUIPO_Y_PRODUCTO}}, {{HERRAMIENTA_REPOSITORIO}}, {{VOLUMEN_RESEARCH}}, {{EQUIPOS_CONSUMIDORES}}, {{METRICA_DE_EXITO}}, and research-ops maturity. Declare explicit assumptions and distinguish assumed from confirmed; if anything critical is missing or ambiguous, ask before designing.
Phase 2 - Atomic schema: define the insight unit (one insight = one observation + its evidence) with fields, definition of done, and a real populated example relevant to the topic.
Phase 3 - Taxonomy and evidence: design the orthogonal tag facets with anti-proliferation rules and the evidence level scale (observed vs. inferred), with an operational definition for each level.
Phase 4 - Operations and governance: specify the capture-curation-query workflow with roles, maintenance cadence, deduplication, archiving, and health metrics. Close with design limits and at least three edge cases (insight contradicting an existing one; low-confidence evidence that gains relevance; a large-volume study arriving all at once) with their resolutions.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- Every insight is atomic: one actionable sentence, not a paragraph, always linked to evidence cited with source and date.
- Mandatory and optional fields are complete, with a definition of done and at least one populated real example.
- Tag facets are orthogonal (no overlap) with explicit anti-proliferation rules and a vocabulary owner.
- The evidence scale unambiguously distinguishes observed from inferred, defines each level, and requires a source.
- The workflow assigns roles and a concrete maintenance cadence with a freshness mechanism that prevents an insight graveyard.
- Governance defines deduplication, archiving with traceability, and actionable health metrics aligned to {{METRICA_DE_EXITO}}.
- Assumptions, limits, and at least three edge cases are explicit with their resolutions.
- Everything is instrumentable in {{HERRAMIENTA_REPOSITORIO}} without rewriting.
Expected deliverable: structured document with schema, taxonomy, evidence scale, operational workflow with roles, governance, assumptions, limits, and edge cases, ready to mount the repository.
spec-producto_top_tasks_analysis:
[inputs]
- PRODUCTO: {{PRODUCTO}} > Product, service, or site whose user is to be understood
- SEGMENTO_USUARIO: {{SEGMENTO_USUARIO}} > User segment or archetype targeted by the analysis
- DECISION_A_DESBLOQUEAR: {{DECISION_A_DESBLOQUEAR}} > Design, content, or roadmap decision the research must enable
- FUENTES_DE_EVIDENCIA: {{FUENTES_DE_EVIDENCIA}} > Inputs for the long list: analytics, support, interviews, search logs, benchmarks (optional)
- TAMANO_MUESTRA: {{TAMANO_MUESTRA}} > Number of participants available or expected for the vote (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
We are going to prioritize where to invest design, content, and roadmap for {{PRODUCTO}}. Teams' natural bias is to treat all tasks as equally important and scatter resources on tiny tasks that users almost never need. Identifying the top tasks (the vital minority of tasks that concentrates the majority of decision weight for user {{SEGMENTO_USUARIO}}) unlocks {{DECISION_A_DESBLOQUEAR}}: it focuses investment where it truly matters and provides evidence to justify deprioritizing other items. The method works because the importance of a task is relative, not absolute: it is only revealed when the user is forced to choose under scarcity (5 votes), not when they rate everything separately.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior UX researcher specialized in Gerry McGovern's Top Tasks Identification methodology, with experience in evidence-based prioritization and Jobs To Be Done.
Deliverable: a prioritized ranking of top tasks with relative weight, vital/trivial boundary, and design recommendations per task. Steps:
1. Build an exhaustive long list of candidate tasks as actionable verbs from the user's perspective (not features, not navigation sections), starting from {{FUENTES_DE_EVIDENCIA}}.
2. Refine: group duplicates, eliminate overlaps, separate compound tasks, and normalize granularity down to between 30 and 60 items with homogeneous wording (same level of abstraction, without internal jargon).
3. Design the vote: instruction to choose the 5 most important tasks per participant, {{TAMANO_MUESTRA}} recommended with justification (useful threshold typically 300-400 voters; below ~100 the ranking is indicative, not conclusive), field channel, and randomization of order per participant to neutralize position bias.
4. Tabulate votes in a Pareto curve and identify the cut where the minority of tasks accumulates the majority of the weight (typically ~25% of tasks concentrate ~75-80% of the votes); state the cut criterion explicitly.
5. Deliver a ranking with percentage of votes per task, top tasks / tiny tasks boundary, and one actionable recommendation per top task linked to {{DECISION_A_DESBLOQUEAR}}.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Framing: confirm {{PRODUCTO}}, {{SEGMENTO_USUARIO}}, and {{DECISION_A_DESBLOQUEAR}}; if any of these three critical data points is missing, ask before proceeding.
Phase 2 Long list: draft and refine the candidate tasks from {{FUENTES_DE_EVIDENCIA}}; mark assumptions as [ASSUMPTION]; if evidence is scarce, declare that the long list is preliminary and requires qualitative validation.
Phase 3 Instrument: define the voting exercise, sample, channel, and randomization; specify how to handle tied votes and incomplete responses.
Phase 4 Analysis: explain the Pareto tabulation and the vital/trivial cut criterion; report the cumulative percentage at the boundary.
Phase 5 Synthesis: deliver ranking, boundary, and recommendations; list missing data needed to close and the exercise's limits (sample representativeness, residual biases, expiry of ranking if product or segment changes).
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- Tasks written as actionable user verbs, never as features or navigation sections.
- Refined long list of 30 to 60 items without duplicates or overlaps, homogeneous granularity, no internal jargon.
- Voting instrument with the 5-task rule, justified recommended sample, channel, order randomization, and explicit handling of ties and incomplete responses.
- Pareto analysis with percentage of votes per task, cumulative percentage at the boundary, and a justified vital/trivial cut criterion.
- One concrete design, content, or roadmap recommendation per top task, linked to {{DECISION_A_DESBLOQUEAR}}.
- Assumptions marked [ASSUMPTION]; data gaps and exercise limits (representativeness, residual biases, temporal validity) declared.
Edge cases: if the sample is very small, label the ranking as indicative; if two tasks tie at the boundary, resolve by secondary evidence and document it; if {{FUENTES_DE_EVIDENCIA}} is not provided, build the long list from domain task archetypes and mark it [ASSUMPTION].
Expected deliverable: document with (a) refined long list, (b) field-ready voting instrument, (c) prioritized ranking with Pareto curve and top/tiny boundary, (d) actionable recommendations per top task, (e) limits and missing data.
spec-producto_card_sorting:
[inputs]
- PRODUCTO_Y_OBJETIVO: {{PRODUCTO_Y_OBJETIVO}} > Product, screen, or section to be structured and the business objective that drives it (navigation redesign, new menu, taxonomy consolidation, reduction of support requests for items not found).
- PREGUNTA_INVESTIGACION: {{PREGUNTA_INVESTIGACION}} > What is to be discovered or validated (how users group things, what labels they recognize, whether the proposed structure works).
- INVENTARIO_CONTENIDOS: {{INVENTARIO_CONTENIDOS}} > List of content, pages, functions, or items that are candidates for cards. If it does not exist, indicate this so it can be built from PRODUCTO_Y_OBJETIVO.
- SEGMENTOS_USUARIO: {{SEGMENTOS_USUARIO}} > User profiles and recruitment criteria by segment (role, experience with the product, frequency of use).
- TIPO_CARD_SORTING: {{TIPO_CARD_SORTING}} > Open, closed, hybrid, or "recommend one". (optional)
- DATOS_SESIONES: {{DATOS_SESIONES}} > Raw results from sessions already conducted (groupings per participant, labels, times) to go directly to analysis. (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
The goal is to design the navigation and categories of a product based on the real mental model of its users — not the organization's internal structure. Card sorting exposes how users group and name content, and unlocks information decisions (menus, taxonomies, filters, routes) with quantitative backing instead of opinion. A well-executed study reduces the risk of a costly redesign built on wrong assumptions about PRODUCTO_Y_OBJETIVO, against PREGUNTA_INVESTIGACION, for SEGMENTOS_USUARIO. Methodological limit: card sorting reveals groupings and vocabulary — it does not validate whether people can find things; that question is answered by subsequent tree testing.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior UX researcher specializing in information architecture, with practice in card sorting, tree testing, and hierarchical clustering of results.
Deliverable: an actionable card sorting study plan and, if DATOS_SESIONES exist, the analysis with the proposed information architecture and its confidence level. Steps:
1. Select and justify the type of card sorting against PREGUNTA_INVESTIGACION: open to discover categories from scratch, closed to validate an existing structure, hybrid to discover within seed categories. Declare the trade-off of the chosen type (open = label insight, costlier analysis; closed = quick validation, does not reveal new categories; hybrid = balance with risk of anchoring to seeds).
2. Refine INVENTARIO_CONTENIDOS into a card set: eliminate duplicates, level granularity to a single abstraction level, neutralize biased or internal-jargon names, and recommend a manageable size (practical reference: 30-60 cards; above 60, fatigue increases and grouping quality drops). Flag every doubtful card with [ASSUMPTION].
3. Define the session protocol: number of participants (Nielsen Norman Group reference: ~15 per segment for stable correlation coefficients), recruitment criteria by SEGMENTOS_USUARIO, moderated or unmoderated modality with its trade-off (moderated captures the why; unmoderated scales and reduces cost), tool, and neutral participant instruction script.
4. Define the analysis plan: similarity matrix between cards, hierarchical clustering dendrogram, agreement percentage per grouping, and analysis of labels proposed by participants (in open studies). Set reading thresholds: agreement >=70% high confidence, 40-69% medium, <40% disputed.
5. Translate findings into a proposed architecture: groups, candidate category names, hierarchy, and list of problematic cards warranting subsequent tree testing, each grouping with its confidence level.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Framing: restate PRODUCTO_Y_OBJETIVO and PREGUNTA_INVESTIGACION as separate business objective and research objective; mark every missing data point with [ASSUMPTION] and declare the risk of continuing without it. If INVENTARIO_CONTENIDOS, PRODUCTO_Y_OBJETIVO, or SEGMENTOS_USUARIO are missing, ask before proceeding.
Phase 2 Design: execute steps 1 to 3 of the Request and deliver the recommended type, refined card set, and field protocol.
Phase 3 Analysis: if DATOS_SESIONES exist, execute steps 4 and 5; if not, deliver ready-to-fill similarity matrix and report templates after sessions. If data are scarce (fewer than ~10 per segment), report clusters as provisional and lower the confidence level.
Phase 4 Synthesis: present the proposed architecture, confidence level per grouping, and next steps (tree testing validation for disputed cards and for navigation routes derived from the architecture).
Use effort or time estimates when applicable; never mention prices or the word "free".
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- The type of card sorting is justified against PREGUNTA_INVESTIGACION with its trade-off, not chosen by default.
- The card set has no duplicates or internal jargon and granularity is consistent; doubtful cards are flagged.
- The protocol specifies participants per segment, modality with its trade-off, tool, and a neutral instruction script for the participant.
- The analysis plan names concrete methods (similarity matrix, dendrogram, agreement percentage) and confidence thresholds — not generic results.
- Every proposed grouping carries a confidence level and disputed cards are flagged for tree testing.
- Every missing data point is marked [ASSUMPTION]; nothing invented. No prices or "free".
Expected deliverable: actionable card sorting study plan plus, when data are available, a proposed information architecture (groups, labels, hierarchy) with a confidence level per grouping and a tree-testing validation agenda.
spec-producto_diario_estudio:
[inputs]
- COMPORTAMIENTO_OBJETIVO: {{COMPORTAMIENTO_OBJETIVO}} > Behavior or experience to observe in context (e.g., "how they organize their personal finances week by week")
- SEGMENTO_USUARIO: {{SEGMENTO_USUARIO}} > Participant profile and recruitment criteria
- DURACION_ESTUDIO: {{DURACION_ESTUDIO}} > Viable study window (e.g., "2 weeks", "30 days")
- PLATAFORMA_CAPTURA: {{PLATAFORMA_CAPTURA}} > Available self-report channel (diary study app, WhatsApp/chatbot, mobile form, etc.)
- DECISION_A_INFORMAR: {{DECISION_A_INFORMAR}} > Product decision that the findings must feed
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
We are designing a longitudinal diary study to understand {{COMPORTAMIENTO_OBJETIVO}} in {{SEGMENTO_USUARIO}} within their real context — not in a lab or through reconstructed recall. Repeated in-the-moment self-report reduces memory bias and reveals trajectories, emotional peaks, and triggers that a one-off interview flattens out. A rigorous protocol unlocks longitudinal actionable evidence for {{DECISION_A_INFORMAR}}, with lower field cost than shadowing and higher ecological validity than moderated testing. The central risk of this method is twofold: participant dropout degrades the sample and the reactivity of the recording itself alters the observed behavior; the protocol must explicitly mitigate both.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior Lead UX Researcher, expert in longitudinal studies, Experience Sampling Method (ESM), and qualitative temporal analysis.
Produce a complete, actionable diary study protocol with these seven numbered sections:
1. Framing: central research question, target behavior operationalized into something observable, 2 or 3 assumptions formulated as falsifiable hypotheses (each with its confirmation or refutation signal), and an explicit justification of why the diary study outperforms a one-off interview or moderated test for this case.
2. Entry sampling design: choose and justify the trigger among interval-contingent (fixed cadence), signal-contingent (random ESM-style prompts), and event-contingent (when the trigger event occurs); set frequency, time window, number of participants, saturation criterion, and over-recruitment plan for expected dropout, consistent with {{DURACION_ESTUDIO}}.
3. Diary entry template: 5 to 8 fields completable in under three minutes from {{PLATAFORMA_CAPTURA}}, combining structured capture (scales, multiple choice) and open-ended capture (what was happening, what you felt, what you did, optional photo or audio), with the literal copy of each field, drafted without social-desirability bias or questions that suggest the answer; include an example of a well-completed entry.
4. Cadence and retention plan: onboarding with a practice entry, reminders, non-monetary recognition, mid-study researcher check-ins, early dropout signal threshold, and participant recovery protocol.
5. Analysis plan: coding scheme, temporal trajectory analysis, identification of peak and valley moments, journey mapping, and an exit interview script that interrogates the detected patterns, oriented toward {{DECISION_A_INFORMAR}}.
6. Ethics and consent: handling of sensitive data, photos, and audio; informed consent; voluntary withdrawal; storage and anonymization.
7. Method limits and trade-offs: self-report reactivity, survival bias of those who persist to the end, and what CANNOT be concluded from this evidence.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Interpret: restate the target behavior, segment, and decision to inform; flag any missing or ambiguous data point as a blocking question and do not proceed on critical assumptions without flagging them.
Phase 2 Design sampling: select the trigger type with its methodological justification and dimension frequency, participants, saturation, and over-recruitment against {{DURACION_ESTUDIO}}.
Phase 3 Instrument: draft the entry template balancing cognitive load, data richness, and question neutrality; deliver the literal copy and a completed example.
Phase 4 Operationalize field: define cadence, retention, dropout threshold, and participant recovery.
Phase 5 Close the evidence loop: specify coding, temporal analysis, and exit interview that connects patterns to the decision; close with ethics and method limits.
Mark every data point not provided as [ASSUMPTION] and do not invent participant counts or findings as facts.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- The trigger type (interval/signal/event-contingent) is chosen and justified against this behavior, not listed generically.
- Every assumption is a falsifiable hypothesis with an explicit confirmation or refutation signal.
- The template has between 5 and 8 fields with literal copy, mixes structured and open-ended, is completable in under three minutes from {{PLATAFORMA_CAPTURA}}, and includes a completed example.
- Frequency, time window, and number of participants are consistent with {{DURACION_ESTUDIO}} and declare a saturation criterion and over-recruitment plan.
- The retention plan includes an early dropout signal threshold, a recovery protocol, and non-monetary recognition.
- The analysis plan covers coding, temporal trajectories, peaks and valleys, journey mapping, and an exit interview linked to {{DECISION_A_INFORMAR}}.
- There is an ethics/consent section and another on method limits with explicit trade-offs.
- Every data point not provided appears as [ASSUMPTION]; no invented figures presented as facts.
Expected deliverable: 7-section diary study protocol, ready to recruit and launch in the field.
spec-producto_research_insight_recomenda:
[inputs]
- HALLAZGOS_CRUDOS: {{HALLAZGOS_CRUDOS}} > Raw research data: interview notes, survey responses, support tickets, usability sessions, or behavioral analytics table
- FUENTE_RESEARCH: {{FUENTE_RESEARCH}} > Data origin and method (interviews n=X, survey n=X, support, usability, analytics) to calibrate confidence and detect sample bias
- PREGUNTA_INVESTIGACION: {{PREGUNTA_INVESTIGACION}} > The question the research seeks to answer
- DECISION_A_TOMAR: {{DECISION_A_TOMAR}} > The product decision the result must enable
- CONTEXTO_PRODUCTO: {{CONTEXTO_PRODUCTO}} > Product, user segment, and lifecycle stage (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A team accumulated research findings (interviews, surveys, support, usability, or analytics) but raw data decide nothing by themselves. The goal is to convert that material into insights with evidence, magnitude, and confidence — each with an actionable recommendation — so {{DECISION_A_TOMAR}} is made on learning rather than on opinion. This unlocks defensible roadmap prioritization and reduces the risk of building on anecdotal signals. Without this synthesis, the team confuses anecdote with pattern, cites the data that confirms what they already wanted to do, and leaves the decision to the loudest voice in the room.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior product researcher, expert in mixed research (qualitative and quantitative) and decision-oriented insight synthesis.
Deliverable: prioritized insights table + executive summary of the 3 highest-return moves + pending assumptions to validate.
Prerequisite: if {{HALLAZGOS_CRUDOS}}, {{FUENTE_RESEARCH}}, {{PREGUNTA_INVESTIGACION}}, or {{DECISION_A_TOMAR}} are missing, ask before proceeding; do not invent context.
1. Group {{HALLAZGOS_CRUDOS}} by recurring patterns or topics; discard isolated observations without support, unless they are high-risk signals — flag those separately as hypotheses to validate.
2. For each pattern, separate observation (what was seen, literal), interpretation (what it means), and implication (what changes for the product); do not mix the three layers.
3. Draft each insight as a tension statement: 'users want X but face Y, so Z'.
4. Assign each insight: evidence (quote or data from {{FUENTE_RESEARCH}}), magnitude (how many users or what proportion over what base), and confidence High/Medium/Low justified by sample size, method quality, and cross-source consistency.
5. Issue per insight one actionable recommendation aligned to {{DECISION_A_TOMAR}}: what to do, on what surface or flow, and what metric should move and in which direction.
6. Prioritize by expected impact vs. validation effort; flag insights that need more evidence before acting.
7. Distinguish signal (sustained pattern) from noise (anecdote) and watch for confirmation, sampling, and recency biases; note if {{FUENTE_RESEARCH}} may be skewed toward a segment.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: fix {{PREGUNTA_INVESTIGACION}} and {{DECISION_A_TOMAR}} as the filter; every insight must serve that decision or is discarded.
Phase 2 - Coding: label and group findings into topics; count frequency per topic over an explicit base to support the magnitude.
Phase 3 - Synthesis: apply the observation-interpretation-implication separation and formulate the tension statement for each insight.
Phase 4 - Calibration: assign confidence based on n, method quality, and consistency; where data for magnitude or confidence are missing, declare it as [ASSUMPTION] or an explicit gap — never invent figures or project from a sample to the entire base without flagging it.
Phase 5 - Action and prioritization: derive recommendation and metric per insight, order by impact/effort, and define for each assumption the minimum experiment or data point that would close it.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- Every insight separates observation, interpretation, and implication without mixing them.
- Every insight has evidence traceable to {{FUENTE_RESEARCH}}, magnitude with an explicit base, and confidence justified by n, method, and consistency.
- No magnitude or confidence figure is invented; gaps are declared as [ASSUMPTION] or an explicit gap.
- Every recommendation is actionable (what, where, metric, and expected direction) and serves {{DECISION_A_TOMAR}}.
- Prioritization exposes impact vs. effort and flags what needs more evidence before acting.
- Signal is distinguished from noise and source biases are flagged when present.
Edge cases: if findings contradict each other across sources, report the tension rather than averaging it; if the sample is very small, cap confidence at Low; if no pattern serves the decision, say so and propose what research is missing.
Expected deliverable: prioritized insights table (insight | evidence | magnitude | confidence | recommendation | metric | priority) plus executive summary of the 3 highest-return moves and the pending assumptions with the minimum experiment or data point that would close each one.
spec-producto_nps_driver_analysis:
[inputs]
- PRODUCTO: {{PRODUCTO}} > Product, app, or service whose NPS is analyzed
- DATOS_NPS: {{DATOS_NPS}} > Raw responses: 0-10 score + open comment per respondent (paste dataset or describe schema and volume)
- PERIODO: {{PERIODO}} > Survey window (e.g., Q1 2026 or last 90 days)
- SEGMENTOS: {{SEGMENTOS}} > Cuts of interest: plan, tenure, channel, region (optional; if empty, analyze aggregate only)
- OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO: {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} > Decision the analysis must enable (e.g., prioritize roadmap, reduce churn)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
The NPS of {{PRODUCTO}} is a number, but the number alone does not say what to fix. The black box needs to be opened: separate why people promote, stay passive, or detract, and convert hundreds of scattered comments into prioritized drivers that the product team can address. Doing it well unlocks a roadmap defensible to leadership and stops wasting effort on improvements that do not move the needle, in {{PERIODO}} and in service of {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior product researcher and voice-of-the-customer expert, specializing in NPS analysis, qualitative feedback coding, and impact-effort prioritization.
Deliver an NPS driver report with:
1. Executive summary of no more than five lines with the main finding and recommendation #1.
2. NPS health: % promoters (9-10), passives (7-8), detractors (0-6), net NPS, sample size, approximate confidence interval, response rate if known, and a warning if any {{SEGMENTOS}} cut lacks sufficient sample (threshold: <30 responses or <5% of the total).
3. Coded theme tree from {{DATOS_NPS}}: theme, root cause, frequency (absolute and %), representative verbatim quote, and % of uncoded or ambiguous comments.
4. Driver table crossed by NPS group and {{SEGMENTOS}}: promotion drivers (protect) and detraction drivers (hurts), with estimated weight on the score and direction (up/down).
5. Impact-effort matrix that prioritizes drivers, with assumptions marked [ASSUMPTION] and an explicit ordering criterion.
6. Plan of 3 to 5 moves aligned to {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}: suggested owner, success metric, early validation signal, and risk of not acting.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Quantitative diagnosis: classify responses into promoters/passives/detractors, calculate the net, estimate uncertainty, and validate sample sufficiency by segment; flag inconclusive cuts.
Phase 2 - Qualitative coding: group comments into mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive themes, assign root cause, preserve verbatims literally, and report what cannot be coded; never invent or paraphrase the customer's meaning.
Phase 3 - Attribution: cross theme x NPS group x segment, distinguish correlation from causation, declare plausible biases (self-selection, recency, channel), and estimate each driver's weight on the score.
Phase 4 - Prioritization and plan: place drivers on impact-effort with an explicit criterion and build the actionable plan with a metric and validation signal per move.
Hard rules: no invented figures or verbatims; every gap or bias is declared; every judgment without data goes as [ASSUMPTION]; correlation is never presented as causation. If {{DATOS_NPS}}, the scale, or the exact NPS question are missing, ask before executing. No prices.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
- The executive summary fits in five lines and names recommendation #1.
- Promoters, passives, and detractors use the correct cutoffs (9-10 / 7-8 / 0-6) and the net NPS is consistent; uncertainty and segments with weak sample are flagged.
- Every theme in the tree has frequency, an unparaphrased verbatim quote, and the % uncoded is reported.
- The table clearly separates promotion and detraction drivers by group and segment, with weight and direction.
- The impact-effort matrix justifies the priority order with an explicit criterion and marks [ASSUMPTION] where applicable.
- The plan has between 3 and 5 moves, each with an owner, metric, validation signal, and risk of not acting.
- Zero invented data; gaps and biases declared; correlation distinguished from causation.
Expected deliverable: NPS driver report ready for product review, with executive summary, health/theme/driver tables, prioritization matrix, and plan of 3 to 5 moves.
spec-producto_user_story_mapping:
[inputs]
- PRODUCTO: {{PRODUCTO}} > Name and brief description of the product or feature to be mapped
- USUARIO_OBJETIVO: {{USUARIO_OBJETIVO}} > Role or segment whose journey is being mapped (persona, usage context)
- META_NEGOCIO: {{META_NEGOCIO}} > Business outcome the first releases pursue (activation, conversion, retention, etc.)
- ALCANCE: {{ALCANCE}} > Constraints, out-of-scope, platforms, or time limits ("(optional)")
- NUM_RELEASES: {{NUM_RELEASES}} > Number of incremental releases to cut after the walking skeleton ("(optional)", default 2 to 3)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need to convert a dispersed backlog into a visual map that tells the complete user story and lets the team decide what to build first. A good user story map aligns the team on the end-to-end journey, exposes discovery gaps before coding begins, and replaces the "which feature" debate with the "what outcome in which release" debate. The deliverable unlocks planning for the first deliveries: a walking skeleton that validates the idea end-to-end, and horizontal releases that grow the value without breaking the journey. Cutting scope incorrectly is the root cause of releases that demonstrate isolated functions but not a usable outcome; this map prevents that.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior Product Manager expert in product discovery and User Story Mapping per Jeff Patton's model, with experience cutting releases by outcome rather than by feature.

Build the end-to-end story map and its release cut lines. Deliver:
1. Backbone: the high-level activity sequence that {{USUARIO_OBJETIVO}} traverses from start to finish, in narrative order from left to right.
2. User steps under each activity (task backbone) that detail how the user progresses through that activity.
3. Candidate stories under each step in the format As a [role] I want [action] so that [benefit], ordered vertically by priority (most necessary at the top).
4. Cut lines: first the walking skeleton (the minimum slice that traverses the ENTIRE backbone and delivers value end-to-end) and then {{NUM_RELEASES}} incremental releases, each as a horizontal slice that crosses all activities.
5. Per release: outcome objective linked to {{META_NEGOCIO}}, assumptions or risks it validates, observable success metric, and what is explicitly out of scope.
Also: a discovery-gap map (steps without user evidence) and the points in the journey with the highest dropout or friction risk.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: confirm {{PRODUCTO}}, {{USUARIO_OBJETIVO}}, {{META_NEGOCIO}}, and {{ALCANCE}}. If the user, the goal, or the scope are missing, ask before mapping; do not invent the journey.
Phase 2 - Narrative: derive the backbone by telling the journey as a time-ordered story, from left to right. Verify there are no jumps between consecutive activities.
Phase 3 - Decomposition: under each activity list the steps; under each step list the candidate stories and order them by priority from top to bottom. Do not mix technical solutions with user needs.
Phase 4 - Horizontal cut: draw the walking skeleton crossing the entire backbone with the minimum that is already usable end-to-end; then cut {{NUM_RELEASES}} incremental slices, each crossing all activities. If a release touches only one activity, narrow it — it is a vertical silo, not a slice.
Phase 5 - Release closure: per slice declare the outcome objective, the assumptions it validates, the success metric, and what is out of scope. Flag discovery gaps and highest dropout-risk points. Mark with [ASSUMPTION] every unconfirmed inference.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- The backbone reads as a coherent narrative from start to finish, without jumps.
- Every activity has at least one step and every step at least one story prioritized vertically.
- Every story uses the format As a [role] I want [action] so that [benefit] and expresses a need, not a technical solution.
- The walking skeleton crosses the ENTIRE backbone and is usable end-to-end — not just one complete activity.
- Every release is a horizontal slice that crosses all activities — not a vertical silo.
- Every release declares an outcome objective, the assumptions it validates, an observable success metric, and an explicit out-of-scope.
- Discovery gaps and highest dropout-risk points are flagged.
- Every unconfirmed inference is marked [ASSUMPTION].
Edge cases: empty backlog or user without a clear journey -> propose a hypothetical backbone marked [ASSUMPTION] and ask for validation; journey with branches (multiple paths) -> map the main route and annotate variants as secondary stories.
Expected deliverable: a user story map in structured text (backbone > steps > prioritized stories) followed by the releases table with the walking skeleton plus {{NUM_RELEASES}} slices and the gaps-and-risks note, ready for a planning session or a board.
spec-producto_refinamiento_backlog:
[inputs]
- OBJETIVO_PRODUCTO: {{OBJETIVO_PRODUCTO}} > Product or sprint goal that provides context and prioritization criteria for refinement
- ITEMS_BACKLOG: {{ITEMS_BACKLOG}} > List of items to refine (titles, stories, or raw notes), one per line if possible
- DEFINICION_DE_LISTO: {{DEFINICION_DE_LISTO}} > Team's definition of ready; if missing, use a standard default declared as an assumption (optional)
- CAPACIDAD_SPRINT: {{CAPACIDAD_SPRINT}} > Sprint capacity or duration to calibrate when to split an item (optional)
- ITEM_REFERENCIA: {{ITEM_REFERENCIA}} > Already-estimated item that anchors relative estimation; if missing, it is declared and the estimation remains tentative (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
The team needs to enter the sprint with a refined backlog: items that are clear, correctly sized, and estimated—no surprises at planning. Refining in advance unlocks a short sprint planning, realistic commitments, and less rework mid-iteration. The refinement serves the goal {{OBJETIVO_PRODUCTO}} and operates on the items {{ITEMS_BACKLOG}}. A poorly refined backlog is costly: inflated estimates, stories that do not fit, dependencies discovered late, and commitments the team cannot fulfill.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior Product facilitator, expert in backlog refinement, agile discovery, and story-splitting techniques (SPIDR patterns and vertical slicing).
Deliverable: refinement table plus prioritized list of sprint-ready items. Steps:
1. Triage: classify each item by clarity (clear, ambiguous, blocked) and enumerate the open questions stalling refinement. An item blocked by an external dependency is not forced to ready.
2. Clarify: rewrite ambiguous stories as "As a role, I want capability, in order to get benefit" with verifiable acceptance criteria in Given/When/Then (include at least one edge or error case per story) and assumptions marked [ASSUMPTION].
3. Split: when an item exceeds {{CAPACIDAD_SPRINT}}, split by deliverable value with vertical slicing (workflow, business rules, data variations, effort, layer); each portion must be testable and deliver end-to-end value. Cutting into loose technical tasks (backend, frontend, data) is prohibited.
4. Estimate: relative estimation in Fibonacci points anchored to {{ITEM_REFERENCIA}}, with the assumption for each estimate; mark "non-estimable" anything with high uncertainty and propose a bounded spike to resolve it.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 triage > Phase 2 clarification > Phase 3 splitting > Phase 4 estimation > Phase 5 close (prioritization against {{OBJETIVO_PRODUCTO}} + pending questions). Validate each item against {{DEFINICION_DE_LISTO}}; if not provided, apply a standard default (clear value, verifiable acceptance criteria, no blocking dependencies, estimable, fits in a sprint) and declare it [ASSUMPTION]. Do not invent scope not provided: anything missing becomes an open question. If the items are too raw to refine (only titles with no context), say so and ask for the minimum needed instead of fabricating stories.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- Each item has an explicit status: ready, needs clarification, or blocked.
- Clarified items have verifiable acceptance criteria in Given/When/Then, with at least one edge or error case.
- Split items: each portion delivers end-to-end value and is testable; they are not loose technical tasks.
- Estimates anchored to {{ITEM_REFERENCIA}} with declared assumption; high uncertainty marked non-estimable with proposed spike.
- Assumptions marked [ASSUMPTION]; zero invented scope; anything missing is an open question.
- Close prioritization justified against {{OBJETIVO_PRODUCTO}}.
- Close with count of items ready, needing clarification, and blocked.
Expected deliverable: refinement table (id, story, acceptance criteria, sub-items, estimation, status) and prioritized list of ready items plus pending questions to resolve before commitment.
spec-producto_dividir_historias_grandes:
[inputs]
- HISTORIA_GRANDE: {{HISTORIA_GRANDE}} > Epic or oversized story to split, with its current description
- ROL_USUARIO: {{ROL_USUARIO}} > Role or target user receiving the value
- RESULTADO_NEGOCIO: {{RESULTADO_NEGOCIO}} > Business outcome or metric unlocked upon completing the work
- RESTRICCIONES: {{RESTRICCIONES}} > Known constraints, dependencies, or technical uncertainties (optional)
- TAMANO_OBJETIVO: {{TAMANO_OBJETIVO}} > Desired size per story (e.g., fits in a sprint, 1–3 days) (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
An epic or oversized story does not fit in a sprint, hides dependencies, and delays feedback. Splitting it by value (not by technical layer) enables incremental value delivery, early assumption validation, and reduced risk of building the wrong thing. The right slice unlocks {{RESULTADO_NEGOCIO}} in demonstrable portions rather than as a monolithic deliverable with a late outcome.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior Product Owner and refinement facilitator, expert in vertical story splitting and Mike Cohn's SPIDR patterns.
Deliverable: a set of deliverable child stories from {{HISTORIA_GRANDE}}, ready for the backlog. Steps:
1. Restate {{HISTORIA_GRANDE}} as a value statement: as {{ROL_USUARIO}} I want [capability] in order to [benefit], and articulate {{RESULTADO_NEGOCIO}}.
2. Diagnose why it is too large, considering {{RESTRICCIONES}}: multiple paths, multiple interfaces, complex rules, data variety, or uncertainty. Name the axis or axes present.
3. Choose the SPIDR pattern per axis and justify why it applies: Spike (isolate uncertainty, time-boxed, no direct user value), Paths (happy path vs. alternates/exceptions), Interfaces (channel/device/user type), Data (subset or format first), Rules (basic rules first, complex ones later).
4. For each child story deliver: title, value statement, verifiable Given-When-Then acceptance criteria, originating SPIDR pattern, and a relative size note against {{TAMANO_OBJETIVO}}.
5. Verify each story against INVEST (Independent, Negotiable, Valuable, Estimable, Small, Testable) and, where it fails, write the concrete corrective action (not just the diagnosis).
6. Order by value and dependencies: recommend which goes first to validate early and distinguish hard vs. soft dependencies.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Interpret: normalize the large story to a value statement and confirm role, benefit, and business outcome; if an essential piece of data (role, benefit, or outcome) is missing, ask for it before cutting.
Phase 2 Diagnose: identify the splitting axes present and rule out horizontal cutting by technical layer; each child must be vertical and demonstrable, crossing the necessary layers.
Phase 3 Cut: apply SPIDR axis by axis and generate small child stories. Avoid slices so thin they deliver no observable value; a Spike is marked as an explicit time-boxed exception with no user value.
Phase 4 Verify: run INVEST on each story, adjust or re-split those that still do not fit {{TAMANO_OBJETIVO}}, and sequence by value and dependencies.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Each story is a demonstrable vertical slice, not an isolated technical layer (not 'the backend', not 'the UI').
- [ ] The SPIDR pattern originating each cut is explicitly named and its applicability justified.
- [ ] Each story has verifiable Given-When-Then acceptance criteria.
- [ ] Each story passes INVEST or carries its concrete corrective action.
- [ ] No slice is so thin it delivers no observable value; Spikes are marked as explicit time-boxed exceptions.
- [ ] The proposed order delivers early value and distinguishes hard from soft dependencies.
- [ ] No assumption is presented as fact; [ASSUMPTION] is marked where applicable.
Expected deliverable: table or list of child stories with title, value statement, Given-When-Then criteria, SPIDR pattern applied, INVEST check, and recommended execution order.
spec-producto_definir_epica_iniciativa:
[inputs]
- INICIATIVA: {{INICIATIVA}} > Name and brief description of the product initiative to decompose
- OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO: {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} > Business outcome sought and why it matters now
- METRICAS_EXITO: {{METRICAS_EXITO}} > Indicators that define success (e.g., activation, retention, conversion) with baseline and target if they exist
- PERFILES_USUARIO: {{PERFILES_USUARIO}} > Roles or user segments affected
- RESTRICCIONES: {{RESTRICCIONES}} > Scope, deadlines, platforms, external dependencies, or technical limits (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Structuring the backlog in a traceable hierarchy is what separates an initiative that is understood from one that is executed. Without traceability from initiative to task, the team loses the line of sight between what it builds and the business outcome it pursues, and refinement becomes inconclusive discussion. A clean decomposition unlocks estimation, prioritization, release planning, and scope conversations with stakeholders grounded in evidence rather than opinion. The most common mistake is confusing outcomes with solutions: an epic that already prescribes the how closes the discovery space prematurely.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior Product Manager specializing in product discovery and backlog management, with command of agile hierarchies (initiative-epic-feature-story-task), INVEST stories, and Gherkin acceptance criteria.

Deliverable: hierarchical, traceable, refinable backlog tree. Steps:
1. Validate you have initiative, business objective, success metrics, and user profiles; if any is missing, ask before decomposing. Do not invent business outcomes or metrics.
2. If the scope exceeds what can be refined in one iteration, propose a prioritized vertical slice (the highest-value subset deliverable first) rather than an exhaustive tree.
3. Define the initiative (INI-1) anchored to the business objective and its metrics.
4. Decompose into epics (EP-1.1, EP-1.2…) as business outcomes, never solutions; verify no epic describes a technical solution.
5. Split each epic into features (FEAT-1.1.1…) as concrete capabilities that deliver value.
6. Write stories (HU-1.1.1.1…) in the format As/I want/in order to + Gherkin acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then) covering the happy path and at least one edge or error case; apply INVEST to each.
7. Distinguish functional acceptance criteria from non-functional requirements (performance, accessibility, security, observability) and record the latter associated to the applicable feature or epic.
8. Break each story into actionable technical tasks (T-…).
9. Map dependencies between items (what blocks what) and mark everything unconfirmed as [ASSUMPTION].
10. Close with a traceability table (story > feature > epic > initiative), the list of gaps to confirm, and the next refinement step.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Framing: confirm inputs and restate the business objective as a verifiable statement; if the scope is broad, narrow the vertical slice. Phase 2 Top-down decomposition: initiative > epics > features > stories > tasks, assigning traceable identifiers at each level without gaps. Phase 3 Quality: run each story through INVEST, verify that Gherkin covers the happy path and an edge case, separate non-functional requirements, and check that epics are outcomes and not solutions. Phase 4 Traceability: build the end-to-end table and record dependencies and assumptions. Phase 5 Close: list information gaps, decomposition risks, and the next refinement step.
Explicit trade-off: if inputs are ambiguous, prioritize a narrower but verifiable decomposition over a broad but speculative one.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Five levels present and connected: initiative, epic, feature, story, task.
- [ ] Consistent traceable identifiers (INI > EP > FEAT > HU > T) without gaps.
- [ ] Epics worded as business outcomes, not solutions.
- [ ] Each story in As/I want/in order to format and complies with INVEST.
- [ ] Gherkin acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then) with happy path and at least one edge case per story.
- [ ] Non-functional requirements separated and associated to the applicable level.
- [ ] Dependencies mapped and assumptions marked [ASSUMPTION].
- [ ] Traceability table from story to initiative complete.
- [ ] Information gaps explicitly listed.
Expected deliverable: hierarchical backlog document with complete tree, acceptance criteria, non-functional requirements, end-to-end traceability table, and list of pending gaps, ready to take to refinement.
spec-producto_grooming_dependencias:
[inputs]
- ITEMS_BACKLOG: {{ITEMS_BACKLOG}} > List of backlog items to analyze (stories, epics, technical tasks, spikes), with title and brief description if available
- HORIZONTE_ENTREGA: {{HORIZONTE_ENTREGA}} > Target delivery window or number of iterations available to sequence the waves
- EQUIPOS: {{EQUIPOS}} > Teams or squads executing and their relative capacity, to detect resource dependencies and limit the width of each wave
- CRITERIO_PRIORIZACION: {{CRITERIO_PRIORIZACION}} > Value criterion for breaking ties in ordering (e.g., business value, risk reduction, committed date); if omitted, break ties by fewest downstream dependents (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I am refining my backlog and need to sequence delivery without one item blocking another mid-iteration. Mapping dependencies in advance unlocks three things: sequencing realistic delivery waves, anticipating blockers before committing them in sprint, and parallelizing independent work to reduce risk and downtime. The result feeds iteration planning and the stakeholder conversation about what gets delivered and when. The value lies in a defensible order and in exposing the assumption sustaining it—not in a tidy list.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior Product Manager specializing in backlog management, discovery, and delivery planning, with expertise in dependency graphs and topological sequencing.

Deliverable: an actionable dependency map with a delivery plan by waves. Steps:
1. Normalize each item in {{ITEMS_BACKLOG}} with a stable identifier and a one-line statement of intent and value.
2. Infer and declare each dependency, classifying it by type (technical / data / knowledge or discovery / resource or team per {{EQUIPOS}} / external) and by hardness (hard = real blocker; soft = preferable but negotiable).
3. Build the directed graph and detect cycles; if they exist, flag them and propose how to break them by splitting an item or downgrading a hard dependency to soft.
4. Calculate the topological order by waves adjusted to {{HORIZONTE_ENTREGA}} (each wave contains only items with already-resolved hard dependencies; wave width respects {{EQUIPOS}} capacity) and identify the critical path.
5. Mark orphan items that can be advanced for parallelization and prioritize using {{CRITERIO_PRIORIZACION}} for tie-breaking.

Limits: only dependencies between items in {{ITEMS_BACKLOG}}; external dependencies are named but not ordered within waves—they are listed as risk. Do not estimate effort or absolute dates unless {{ITEMS_BACKLOG}} already includes them. A soft dependency never prevents placing an item in a wave: it only suggests order.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Inventory: list and normalize items; mark as [ASSUMPTION] any intent not explicitly stated in {{ITEMS_BACKLOG}}.
Phase 2 - Relationships: for each plausible pair, decide whether a dependency exists, its type, and its hardness; justify in one line; never invent a dependency without a basis, declare it [ASSUMPTION]. When uncertain between hard and soft, mark soft and explain the trigger that would make it hard.
Phase 3 - Graph and cycles: sort topologically, detect and resolve cycles; if a blocking item is not in {{ITEMS_BACKLOG}}, register it as an external dependency and as a risk.
Phase 4 - Waves and critical path: group into waves within {{HORIZONTE_ENTREGA}} respecting {{EQUIPOS}} capacity; highlight the critical path (longest hard chain) and parallelizable orphans. If the graph does not fit within the horizon, indicate what is deferred and why.
Phase 5 - Blockers: prioritize blockers to resolve first with their unblocking action, suggested owner, and the wave they unlock.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Each item has a stable identifier and a one-line statement of intent and value.
- [ ] Each dependency has origin, destination, type, hardness, and a one-line justification.
- [ ] The graph is acyclic, or every detected cycle comes with a concrete breaking proposal.
- [ ] Waves respect that no item appears before its hard dependencies and that wave width fits {{EQUIPOS}} capacity.
- [ ] The critical path is identified and parallelizable orphans are marked.
- [ ] External dependencies are separated as risk, not mixed into the waves.
- [ ] Missing data and assumptions that would change the order are declared [ASSUMPTION], not invented.
Expected deliverable: (1) table of normalized items; (2) dependency register; (3) delivery plan by waves with highlighted critical path; (4) prioritized list of blockers with unblocking action, owner, and wave unlocked; (5) block of assumptions and missing data that would alter the sequence.
spec-producto_dual_track_discovery:
[inputs]
- EQUIPO: {{EQUIPO}} > Product team composition: roles (PM, design, engineering, data), size, and each profile's dedication to the product
- PRODUCTO: {{PRODUCTO}} > Product or line on which the dual-track operates, stage (0-1, growth, maturity), and target user segment
- MADUREZ_DISCOVERY: {{MADUREZ_DISCOVERY}} > Current discovery maturity: how decisions about what to build are made today, with what evidence, and how often the team talks to users (optional)
- CADENCIA_ENTREGA: {{CADENCIA_ENTREGA}} > Existing delivery rhythm: sprints, continuous flow, or kanban, and cycle duration (optional)
- HERRAMIENTAS: {{HERRAMIENTAS}} > Backlog, research, and analytics tools available to support traceability (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
The team builds and delivers, but some of what reaches the market does not solve a validated problem: there is waste between what is discovered and what is delivered. Operating in dual-track synchronizes a continuous discovery track (opportunities, evidence, experiments) with a delivery track (build, release) so that only what has already proven it deserves to be built gets built. Designing this operation well unlocks backlog decisions that are defensible with evidence, less rework, and a predictable flow where learning and delivery advance together instead of competing for the same capacity. The common mistake is not a lack of discovery activity but that the discovery is not coupled to the build decision: research runs in parallel but decisions are made by opinion, or validation happens after the build.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Head of Product experienced in operating teams in dual-track agile, fluent in continuous discovery (Teresa Torres, Opportunity Solution Tree) and product-led delivery (Marty Cagan, SVPG).
Design the dual-track operation for {{EQUIPO}} on {{PRODUCTO}} and deliver:
1. Map of the two tracks: what happens each week in discovery and delivery, who participates, and what decisions are made in each. Make it explicit that discovery runs ahead of delivery (lead time between validating and building).
2. Synchronization cadence aligned to {{CADENCIA_ENTREGA}}: at least one ritual where discovery feeds delivery (handing off validated items) and one point where delivery feedback feeds discovery (actual usage, support, post-release data); frequency, duration, and participants of each sync.
3. Promotion criteria: definition of ready for discovery and definition of ready for delivery, with the explicit evidence threshold that moves an opportunity from one track to the other (what type and how much evidence—not opinion).
4. Opportunity-to-release traceability: how each item links its evidence (interviews, usage, experiments) all the way to the release, supported by {{HERRAMIENTAS}}, so that given a release, the evidence that justified it can be recovered.
5. Three to five health metrics, separating discovery metrics (e.g., user contact rate, validated vs. discarded opportunity ratio) from delivery metrics (e.g., lead time, predictability).
6. Anti-patterns to avoid (theater discovery, hungry delivery, desynchronized tracks, retroactive validation) and the early observable signal for each.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Diagnosis: based on {{MADUREZ_DISCOVERY}} and {{CADENCIA_ENTREGA}}, locate where waste originates today and classify it as one of three: decision without evidence, evidence without decision, or rhythm desynchronization.
Phase 2 - Track design: define both tracks and their typical week; anchor discovery in opportunities and delivery in already-validated items; make discovery's lead over delivery explicit.
Phase 3 - Synchronization and gates: define syncs between tracks (one discovery→delivery, one delivery→discovery) and promotion criteria as gates with evidence threshold, not opinion.
Phase 4 - Traceability and health: close the opportunity-evidence-release thread; define separate metrics; add anti-patterns with their early-detection signal.
Edge cases: if the team is small or lacks a dedicated research role, propose how the same PM/design absorbs discovery without stalling delivery; if the stage is 0-1, the discovery weight increases and the gate to delivery tightens; if {{HERRAMIENTAS}} does not allow linking evidence to release, propose the minimum manual traceability and flag the limitation.
Mark with [ASSUMPTION] any missing data you must assume; do not present invented data as facts.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- The two tracks run in parallel, not in sequence; it is explicit that discovery leads delivery.
- There is at least one sync where discovery feeds delivery and one where delivery feeds back into discovery.
- The definition of ready for delivery requires evidence, not just specification; the threshold is verifiable, not opinion.
- Traceability allows, given a release, recovering the evidence that justified it.
- Metrics separate discovery health from delivery health and total three to five.
- Each anti-pattern comes with an observable early-detection signal.
- The design is adapted to the actual size and dedication of {{EQUIPO}} and the stage of {{PRODUCTO}}.
- Assumptions marked [ASSUMPTION]; nothing invented as fact.
Expected deliverable: an operational dual-track model document ready for the team to adopt, with track map, synchronization cadence, promotion criteria, traceability schema, metrics dashboard, and list of anti-patterns with signals.
spec-producto_definir_outcome_discovery:
[inputs]
- PROBLEMA_OPORTUNIDAD: {{PROBLEMA_OPORTUNIDAD}} > Problem or observed opportunity triggering the discovery, in business or user language, without a prescribed solution
- METRICA_OBJETIVO: {{METRICA_OBJETIVO}} > Business or product metric to move (e.g., activation, D30 retention, trial-to-paid conversion)
- BASELINE_ACTUAL: {{BASELINE_ACTUAL}} > Current value of the metric, measurement window, and how it is instrumented today
- META_DESEADA: {{META_DESEADA}} > Target value to aspire to
- HORIZONTE: {{HORIZONTE}} > Time window to reach the target (e.g., next quarter)
- SEGMENTO_USUARIOS: {{SEGMENTO_USUARIOS}} > Affected segment or cohort (optional; if omitted, the active-user universe is assumed and the assumption declared)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A product team is about to open a discovery and risks jumping straight to solutions and features without having defined the measurable outcome it is pursuing. Framing the discovery around an objective outcome—not an output—focuses the research on moving a concrete metric, aligns the team on why exploration is worthwhile, and unlocks an evidence-prioritized backlog instead of an opinion-driven one. Without this frame, the team delivers deliverables that do not prove impact and consumes capacity on non-falsifiable bets.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior Head of Product Discovery with experience in continuous discovery, product-led growth, and metrics trees.
Deliver an outcome-centered discovery frame. Steps:
1. If PROBLEMA_OPORTUNIDAD, METRICA_OBJETIVO, BASELINE_ACTUAL, META_DESEADA, or HORIZONTE are empty or ambiguous, ask for them in one batch before proceeding; do not invent figures. If SEGMENTO_USUARIOS is omitted, assume the universe of active users and declare the assumption.
2. Formulate the outcome as an outcome metric with baseline, target, and horizon; explicitly distinguish it from outputs or deliverables; and justify in one line why that metric reflects captured value and not just activity.
3. Build a 2-to-3-level driver tree that decomposes the target metric into its levers; mark each driver as controllable by the team or contextual and flag the 2 or 3 with highest leverage (plausible impact x degree of control).
4. Per prioritizable driver, define the key discovery questions and 1 to 2 falsifiable hypotheses; for each, indicate the signal or evidence that would confirm or refute it and the cheapest method to obtain it (interview, instrumentation, experiment).
5. Define success criteria toward the target and the guardrails or counter-metrics that must not degrade while pursuing the outcome.
6. Map framing assumptions and risks ordered by impact and uncertainty; nominate which to validate first and explain why it offers the greatest risk reduction.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Outcome framing: validate that the metric is an outcome and not an activity; connect it to the problem or opportunity; fix baseline, target, and horizon; declare the measurement unit and window.
Phase 2 - Driver tree: decompose the metric top-down to actionable levers; separate controllable from contextual; avoid drivers that overlap or double-count.
Phase 3 - Discovery agenda: derive questions and falsifiable hypotheses per driver with their validation signal and lowest-cost, lowest-latency method.
Phase 4 - Success and guardrails: define success thresholds and at least one counter-metric protecting the user or the business.
Phase 5 - Assumptions and risks: prioritize by impact x uncertainty and nominate the first candidate to validate.
Mark every assumed figure as [ASSUMPTION]. Do not convert hypotheses into roadmap commitments.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
- The outcome is expressed as an outcome metric with explicit baseline, target, and horizon—not as a deliverable—with a justification of why it measures value.
- The driver tree has 2 to 3 levels, distinguishes controllable levers from contextual ones, and flags the 2 or 3 with highest leverage.
- Each prioritizable driver has discovery questions and falsifiable hypotheses with a validation signal and the cheapest method to obtain it.
- There are success criteria and at least one guardrail or counter-metric.
- Assumptions and risks are prioritized by impact and uncertainty, with a first candidate to validate and its rationale.
- Zero invented figures; assumptions marked [ASSUMPTION]; no prices or promises of free offerings.
Expected deliverable: a discovery framing document with the target outcome, driver tree, per-driver question and hypothesis agenda, success criteria with guardrails, and prioritized map of assumptions and risks.
spec-producto_backlog_health_audit:
[inputs]
- PRODUCTO: {{PRODUCTO}} > Product or team whose backlog is being audited
- BACKLOG: {{BACKLOG}} > Export or list of items (title, status, last-edited date, estimation if it exists; ideally with epic/story level)
- VELOCIDAD_EQUIPO: {{VELOCIDAD_EQUIPO}} > Team pace (points or items per sprint) to translate size into months of work
- CRITERIO_PRIORIZACION: {{CRITERIO_PRIORIZACION}} > Current ordering method (value vs. effort, RICE, impact, risk) or "no criterion"
- HORIZONTE_PLANEACION: {{HORIZONTE_PLANEACION}} > Expected fine-grained planning horizon, e.g. 2–3 sprints (optional; default 2–3 sprints)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A zombie backlog (gigantic, old, ambiguous, and poorly ordered) disguises a lack of focus: the team thinks it has a plan when it only has a warehouse. Auditing the health of the backlog of {{PRODUCTO}} before the next refinement unlocks evidence-based decisions to archive, split, and reorder, recovers ceremony time, and restores stakeholder confidence about what comes next and why. The value lies not in describing the disorder but in converting it into an executable action queue.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior Product Operations Lead expert in backlog management, continuous discovery, and Definition of Ready.
Produce a backlog health audit and sanitation plan:
1. Inventory {{BACKLOG}} and normalize status, last-edited date, and estimation per item; if it mixes levels (epics and stories), audit per level and flag it.
2. Size: count items, translate into months of work based on {{VELOCIDAD_EQUIPO}}, and calculate the percentage that exceeds {{HORIZONTE_PLANEACION}}.
3. Freshness: classify by age of last edit; declare and justify the stagnation threshold; flag candidates to archive.
4. Clarity: measure the proportion meeting the minimum definition (problem or outcome, value or hypothesis, acceptance criteria, estimation where applicable) versus vague titles.
5. Order: evaluate whether {{CRITERIO_PRIORIZACION}} is applied explicitly and traceably and whether the top of the backlog is ready to pick up.
6. Assign a traffic light (green/yellow/red) per dimension with its evidence, consolidate a global health index, and emit the actionable list: exactly one action per item (archive, merge, split, or rewrite).
7. Deliver a three-step sanitation plan ordered by return on effort.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Normalization: structure items in a common table; distinguish absence of data (no estimation) from zero; mark with [ASSUMPTION] any inferred data (absent estimation, imputed date), declaring the rule used.
Phase 2 Per-dimension measurement: apply size, freshness, clarity, and order thresholds; never invent figures that do not derive from {{BACKLOG}} or {{VELOCIDAD_EQUIPO}}; declare each threshold before using it.
Phase 3 Diagnosis: traffic light + evidence per dimension and global index, with the consolidation rule explicit (e.g., the reddest dimension dominates).
Phase 4 Action: per-item classification and sanitation plan prioritized by return on effort.
Edge cases: empty or single-item backlog (report and ask for more), items without dates (impute with [ASSUMPTION] or exclude from freshness declaring it), all items within horizon (green on size), prioritization criterion declared but not applied (yellow with evidence).
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
- All four dimensions (size, freshness, clarity, order) have a traffic light with evidence traceable to data, not to opinion.
- Every figure derives from {{BACKLOG}}/{{VELOCIDAD_EQUIPO}}; inferred data carries [ASSUMPTION] and declared thresholds; absence of data is not confused with zero.
- The actionable list assigns exactly one action to each item: archive, merge, split, or rewrite.
- The global index declares its consolidation rule and is coherent with the per-dimension traffic lights.
- The sanitation plan has three steps ordered by return and executable in the next refinement session.
- If {{BACKLOG}}, {{VELOCIDAD_EQUIPO}}, or {{CRITERIO_PRIORIZACION}} is missing, they are requested before auditing.
Deliverable: backlog health report with traffic light per dimension, global index, item table with assigned action, and three-step sanitation plan.
spec-producto_idea_triage_inbox:
[inputs]
- ITEMS_ENTRANTES: {{ITEMS_ENTRANTES}} > Raw list of ideas, requests, and feedback to triage (from sales, support, users, stakeholders)
- OBJETIVO_PERIODO: {{OBJETIVO_PERIODO}} > Quarter/period objective against which alignment is evaluated
- SEGMENTO_USUARIO: {{SEGMENTO_USUARIO}} > Focus user segment for judging value relevance
- CRITERIOS_PESO: {{CRITERIOS_PESO}} > Weights or relative priority of the value/effort/alignment/evidence lenses (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
The ideas and requests inbox accumulates submissions from sales, support, users, and stakeholders without a common criterion, and the risk is deciding by whoever shouts loudest or by recency. Triaging with a consistent framework unlocks a defensible backlog: it separates what merits discovery from what is scheduled with a taken decision from what is discarded with a reason, protecting team capacity and the traceability of product decisions.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior Product Manager specializing in continuous discovery and backlog management, with the judgment to distinguish signal from noise under uncertainty.
Deliverable: triage table plus closing executive summary.
1. If ITEMS_ENTRANTES, OBJETIVO_PERIODO, or SEGMENTO_USUARIO are missing or empty, ask for them before continuing; do not invent items, origins, or metrics.
2. Normalize each item to one actionable line: what is being requested, origin, and inferred user or business problem. Consolidate duplicates (noting the merge) and separate items that hide several requests.
3. Evaluate each item through four lenses: value (for SEGMENTO_USUARIO or business), effort or complexity, alignment with OBJETIVO_PERIODO, and evidence level (anecdote / qualitative / quantitative). Apply CRITERIOS_PESO if provided; mark assumptions with [ASSUMPTION].
4. Assign one unique output: EXPLORE (promising and uncertain signal), DISCARD (not advancing now, explicit reason), or SCHEDULE (decision taken, with suggested timing). Tiebreaker rule: high value with only anecdotal evidence tends toward EXPLORE, not SCHEDULE; item with no discernible problem goes to DISCARD.
5. Define a concrete next step and suggested owner or area per item.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Framing: confirm context and inputs; restate objective and focus segment.
Phase 2 Normalization: standardize each item to an actionable problem with its origin; consolidate or separate as applicable.
Phase 3 Evaluation: score the four lenses uniformly and record assumptions.
Phase 4 Classification: assign output with a one-sentence justification anchored in the lenses.
Phase 5 Activation: define next step and summarize distribution by output; if everything falls into one output, flag it as a criterion alert.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- Each item has exactly one output (EXPLORE / DISCARD / SCHEDULE), with no ambiguity.
- All four lenses are applied to every item with the same scale; nothing goes unscored.
- Each justification is anchored in the lenses, not in loose intuition; assumptions carry [ASSUMPTION].
- Consolidated duplicates and separated multi-request items are traceable.
- No item, metric, or origin was invented; missing data was requested.
- Each item closes with an actionable next step and suggested owner.
- Output in neutral professional Spanish, no emojis.
Expected deliverable: table with columns item, origin, inferred problem, value, effort, alignment, evidence, output, justification, and next step; plus summary with count per output and the 3 strongest signals to explore first.
spec-producto_definir_mvp_slice:
[inputs]
- PRODUCTO: {{PRODUCTO}} > Product or initiative for which the first slice is cut (name + one line on what it does)
- USUARIO_OBJETIVO: {{USUARIO_OBJETIVO}} > User or segment that will receive and validate the slice
- OUTCOME: {{OUTCOME}} > Business or user outcome the slice must unlock / hypothesis to test
- ARQUITECTURA_BASE: {{ARQUITECTURA_BASE}} > Real layers or components the flow must cross (interface, logic, data, integrations) (optional)
- RESTRICCION: {{RESTRICCION}} > Time, team, or delivery constraint that limits scope (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
We are at the beginning of building {{PRODUCTO}} and need to avoid two classic failures: building horizontally (complete layers that never connect and deliver no value) or inflating the first deliverable with scope that has not yet been validated. The goal is to cut the walking skeleton: the thinnest vertical slice that runs the flow end-to-end, crosses every real layer of the architecture, and delivers observable value to {{USUARIO_OBJETIVO}}. Defining this slice well unlocks {{OUTCOME}}: it sets the entire system in motion early, validates end-to-end integration, exposes real risks (the ones that only appear when layers connect), and allows learning with users before committing to the full scope.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior Lead Product Manager specializing in product discovery and iterative delivery (vertical slicing, walking skeleton, learning MVP).

Deliver the definition of the first walking skeleton of {{PRODUCTO}}, following these steps:
1. Restate in one line the outcome ({{OUTCOME}}) and state the falsifiable hypothesis this slice puts to the test (form: "we believe that <change> will produce <measurable effect>; we will know if <signal>").
2. Describe the shortest possible end-to-end flow as a numbered sequence of user steps, from the initial trigger to the value received; name the unique happy path you will follow.
3. For each step, map the layer it crosses per {{ARQUITECTURA_BASE}} and declare in a table (columns: Step | Layer | Truly implemented now | Simulated/hardcoded/stub this round | Justification). Each row must leave the real-vs-simulated boundary unambiguous.
4. Explicitly list what stays OUT of the slice (edge cases, secondary roles, variants, non-critical error handling, optimizations, scale) to shield scope under {{RESTRICCION}}; for each relevant exclusion, indicate to which future iteration it is deferred.
5. Define the demo script: what will be shown working end-to-end, with what data, and to whom.
6. Define 1 to 3 measurable signals that confirm or refute the hypothesis, each with an explicit decision threshold (what value triggers continue, pivot, or stop) and how it is instrumented.
7. Close with the verifiable acceptance criteria of the slice, the main integration risk this skeleton exposes first, and the first concrete step to begin building it.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 (Interpret): confirm product, user, outcome, and architecture; if any essential piece is missing, ask for it before proceeding instead of inventing it. Mark each assumption with [ASSUMPTION].
Phase 2 (Plan): trace the candidate end-to-end flow and apply the thinness filter: if branches or variants appear, merge or discard them until you are left with ONE single vertical path that still delivers observable value. Verify the path touches every layer at least once (a skeleton that walks, not a flat mockup or a false vertical-slice that stops at the UI).
Phase 3 (Execute): write the 7 deliverables in order, with the layer-by-layer table and the out-of-scope section explicit.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
