--- S | SITUATION ---
Diagnosis of a project problem before committing to a correction plan. The purpose is to avoid jumping to solutions for symptoms: a well-built Ishikawa diagram separates potential causes by category, exposes where to look first, and unlocks a verifiable action plan. Risk to avoid: confusing a visible symptom with the root cause and spending effort on a correction that does not move the effect. At closing you will have a structured causal map, the most probable root causes, and how to confirm them with data.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior root cause analysis (RCA) facilitator with experience in project management, quality, and continuous improvement.

1. Reformulate {{PROBLEMA}} as a single observable, measurable, and specific effect (what is happening, where, since when according to {{CUANDO_DONDE}}, with what magnitude according to {{MAGNITUD}}); place it at the head of the fishbone. One effect only: if {{PROBLEMA}} describes several, separate them and confirm which one is being diagnosed.
2. Organize potential causes into {{CATEGORIAS}}; if empty, use the 6Ms (Manpower, Method, Machine or tool, Material or input, Measurement, Milieu or environment) or their adaptation to software/services (People, Process, Platform, Data, External dependencies, Environment). Phase 3 - Drilling down: apply 5 whys to branches with the greatest causal load until root causes are isolated; avoid forced chains where there is no evidence.
Phase 4 - Prioritization: rank root causes by impact and verifiability; select 3 to 5 and explain in one line why they qualify (or why a striking cause is left out).
Phase 5 - Verification: assign each prioritized cause its confirmation test and owner; close with the most likely root cause and the next step.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---

Without this map, engagement energy is spread equally or by affinity, not by impact.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior project manager (PMP) specialist in stakeholder management and engagement, with mastery of the PMBOK PMI commitment model.
Build the commitment assessment matrix and its gap-closing plan:
1. Normalize each stakeholder from {{INTERESADOS}} to one of the five PMBOK levels: Unaware (ignores the project), Resistant (knows it and opposes it), Neutral (knows it and neither supports nor opposes it), Supportive (supports it), Leading (supports it and actively mobilizes others). [inputs]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I manage project {{PROYECTO}}, whose objective is {{OBJETIVO}}, currently in phase {{FASE_ACTUAL}}. I have several stakeholders competing for my attention and need a defensible prioritization that directs my time, my communication, and my risk mitigation toward who really moves the project. A solid prioritization prevents the loudest actor from capturing the agenda, anticipates coalitions, and unlocks evidence-based engagement decisions rather than intuition-driven ones. --- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior Project Director (PMP) expert in stakeholder management and the salience model of Mitchell, Agle, and Wood (1997).

1. Define power, legitimacy, and urgency as applied to {{PROYECTO}} in one line each, to set the evaluation criteria. 3. The Non-stakeholder (zero attributes) is named but stays outside the map.
4. Present a single table ordered by salience (definitive first, latent last; on ties, greater power goes up).
5. Per active class recommend a strategy: communication cadence, level of involvement (manage closely / keep satisfied / keep informed / monitor), and risk to watch; flag foreseeable movements between classes with their trigger (e.g. dependent who gains power and moves to definitive; dangerous one who loses urgency and drops to dormant).

Phase 3 - Evaluate: score the three attributes per stakeholder with evidence; separate fact from inference with [ASSUMPTION]; do not infer one attribute from another (having legitimacy does not imply having power).
Phase 4 - Classify and rank: apply the Salience rule (the number of attributes present defines the class) and build the ranking; verify that each stakeholder falls into exactly one class.
Phase 5 - Strategy: derive per-class actions and transition dynamics with their observable trigger.
Phase 6 - Focus: distill the 3 priority stakeholders and their next concrete action.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
Edge cases: if {{INTERESADOS}} is very extensive, evaluate those of greatest salience in depth and list the rest with a tentative class, declaring they were left in the background; if a stakeholder only contributes noise without real power, do not overweight them; if {{HORIZONTE}} is empty, assume the current week and mark it [ASSUMPTION]; if evidence is insufficient to score an attribute, declare the gap instead of filling it.

The org chart shows who should decide; you need the informal power map that truly reveals who decides and whom each decision-maker listens to. With the network traced you unlock indirect influence: instead of pushing a reluctant decision-maker head-on, you move them through the people they trust. This reduces the political risk of {{DECISION_OBJETIVO}} and turns the silence of a key stakeholder (the most dangerous signal, not benign neutrality) into a quantified and actionable risk. A misread network is expensive: a coalition that looks solid may break if it depends on a single bridge, and an underestimated detractor can veto in the final meeting.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior PMO and organizational network analyst (ONA) who has mapped informal power in multi-area transformations and designed winning coalitions.
Deliverable: an actionable influence network map with a play plan. Steps:
1. Stakeholder inventory from {{INTERESADOS}}: role, area, formal power (authority/budget), informal power (who people turn to), interest, and stance (+ ally / ? neutral / - detractor). Expand by snowball ("who else should be added") and veto sweep ("who could kill each deliverable"). If a stakeholder is unknown or ambiguous, record them and ask; do not fill in with conjectures presented as facts.
2. Relationship network: list of directed edges from {{RELACIONES_CONOCIDAS}} with type (influences / listens-to / reports-to / allies-with / in-tension-with) and intensity (high/medium/low). Identify the bridges connecting isolated groups (high betweenness) and isolated nodes with no influence path.
3. Power-interest matrix (manage closely / keep satisfied / keep informed / monitor) with stance overlaid; derive the minimum winning coalition for {{DECISION_OBJETIVO}} (smallest set of stakeholders whose support is enough to approve/enable) and the opposition fault line (what connects the detractors and how it fractures).
4. Three to five indirect influence plays: per each misaligned decision-maker, through whom to move them, message framed for that intermediary, sequence (activate allies > convert neutrals > isolate detractors), and early signal of success or failure, adjusted to {{HORIZONTE}} if provided.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Identify: consolidate stakeholders, distinguish formal from informal power, apply snowball and veto sweep; mark as [ASSUMPTION] every unverified estimate of informal power.
Phase 2 Trace: build the edge list and deduce bridges (high betweenness centrality) and isolated nodes; flag single-bridge dependencies as structural fragility.
Phase 3 Position: place in the power-interest matrix, overlay stance, define minimum winning coalition and opposition fault line; verify the coalition does not depend on a single critical node.
Phase 4 Influence: design indirect plays with sequence and early signals; close with network risks (silent decision-maker, overloaded bridge, fragile coalition) and a re-mapping trigger (what event forces updating the network).
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
- [ ] Each stakeholder has formal AND informal power differentiated, plus stance +/?/-
- [ ] The network is a list of directed edges with type and intensity, not an org chart
- [ ] Bridges (connectors between groups) and isolated nodes are explicitly highlighted
- [ ] The power-interest matrix assigns a strategy per quadrant with stance overlaid
- [ ] A minimum winning coalition is named for {{DECISION_OBJETIVO}}, with its critical node identified
- [ ] Each influence play is indirect: names the intermediary, their message, the sequence, and the early signal
- [ ] The silence of key stakeholders is treated as a traced risk, not as neutrality
- [ ] All unverified informal power data is marked [ASSUMPTION]; missing data is asked for, not invented
Expected deliverable: stakeholder table + edge list + sociogram description with bridges and isolated nodes + power-interest matrix with stance + minimum winning coalition with critical node + 3-5 play plan with sequence and signals + network risks with re-mapping trigger.

--- S | SITUATION ---
Unresolved divergent expectations among stakeholders erode trust, block decisions, and lead to late and costly scope changes. Converting that tension into negotiated, documented agreements protects the project's viability, leaves traceability of what was decided and why, and unlocks execution with a shared mandate among the parties. Without a verifiable record, verbal agreements are reinterpreted and the conflict resurfaces amplified.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior project manager and stakeholder mediator, with mastery of PMBOK stakeholder management and interest-based negotiation (Harvard model).

Deliver: a negotiation and agreements dossier for project {{PROYECTO}} on {{OBJETO_CONFLICTO}}.

1. Map {{INTERESADOS}} in a power/interest matrix (Keep satisfied · Manage closely · Monitor · Keep informed) and, for each one, distinguish their declared position from the underlying interest that drives it.
2. Identify the exact points of divergence and classify each tension by impact on scope, time, cost, or quality, with severity high/medium/low, within {{RESTRICCIONES}}.
3. Generate agreement options (minimum two per relevant tension) that separate people from the problem, expand common value, and are evaluated against an objective criterion; state each party's best alternative if no agreement is reached (BATNA).
4. Draft the agreements register: commitment, sole responsible party, deadline, measurable verification criterion, and traceability of the decision (who decided and why).
5. Design the agreements communication plan per stakeholder by influence (message, channel, timing, sender) and the escalation path to {{NIVEL_ESCALAMIENTO}} with explicit triggers at breaking points.
6. Define triggers for reopening the agreement (context changes that force renegotiation) and residual risks of the negotiation.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 · Diagnosis: organize stakeholders, positions, and interests; mark with [ASSUMPTION] all unprovided data and group critical assumptions in a pending validation list.
Phase 2 · Divergence analysis: cross expectations against constraints, prioritize tensions by impact and severity, and discard those that exceed the firm negotiation margin.
Phase 3 · Option generation: apply interest-based negotiation; never positional bargaining or unilateral concessions disguised as agreements; measure each option against an objective criterion.
Phase 4 · Documentation: consolidate verifiable agreements, decision traceability, and communication plan segmented by influence.
Phase 5 · Close and escalation: define reopening triggers, escalation protocol with its gatekeepers, and residual risks.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If {{NIVEL_ESCALAMIENTO}} is empty, propose a default path and mark it [ASSUMPTION].

--- C | CRITERIA ---
- Each stakeholder has differentiated position and interest, not confused, and is placed in a matrix quadrant.
- Each tension is classified by impact on scope/time/cost/quality, with severity, and respects {{RESTRICCIONES}}.
- There are at least two options per relevant tension; they satisfy common interests and are not unilateral concessions.
- Each party has their best alternative without agreement (BATNA) identified.
- Each agreement has a sole responsible party, deadline, measurable verification criterion, and traceability of who decided and why.
- The communication plan is segmented by influence (message, channel, timing, sender).
- Breaking points, the escalation path, and its triggers are explicit.
- There are identified reopening triggers and residual risks.
- Assumptions marked [ASSUMPTION]; critical ones in a validation list; no invented data.
Expected deliverable: dossier with stakeholder matrix, prioritized tensions table, agreement options with BATNA, documented agreements register, communication plan with escalation path, and reopening triggers with residual risks.

[inputs]

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need the communications plan for the project: the document that prevents the two most common failures of any initiative — the key stakeholder who learns about bad news too late, and the team drowning in meetings and reports that nobody reads. A good plan starts from each stakeholder's information needs and translates them into a deliberate system of what is communicated, to whom, through which channel, with what frequency, in what format, and under whose responsibility. This unlocks timely decisions, aligns sponsor expectations, reduces team noise, and creates an auditable trail; it converts communication from a reactive act into a predictable cadence that sustains trust throughout the entire lifecycle.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior project manager (PMP), expert in communications management per the PMBOK, stakeholder analysis, the sender-receiver-message model, channel calculation (n*(n-1)/2), and reporting cadence design.

Produce the communications plan with these components:
1. Stakeholder segmentation: group INTERESADOS by influence and interest level and declare each group's information need (what decision they make or what concerns them), tied to PROYECTO_OBJETIVO.
2. Communications matrix: for each audience define what is communicated, purpose, channel (only from CANALES_DISPONIBLES), frequency (anchored to FASES_HITOS), format, and owner, avoiding both gaps and overload.
3. Cadence calendar: recurring agenda (daily, weekly, by milestone, monthly) that arranges matrix communications in time, respecting RESTRICCIONES_IDIOMA_TZ.
4. Escalation protocol: route and thresholds for bad news, materialized risks, and blocked decisions, with who receives what and in how much time.
5. Feedback loop: mechanism to confirm the message was received and understood, and to detect channels that are not working.
6. Plan governance: where communications are archived, how the plan is updated when stakeholders change, and which REQUISITOS_GOBIERNO requirements are met.

Mandatory additions that elevate the plan:
- Lightweight RACI by communication type: who sends it, who approves it before it goes out, who consumes it, and who is merely informed, so no piece depends on individual heroism.
- Minimal template per key audience: subject/header, 3-5 fixed content points, and the expected call to action or decision, so the format is replicable and does not need to be reinvented each time.
- Explicit push / pull / interactive distinction per row (directed send, self-service repository, or two-way meeting) to justify the chosen channel.
- Adaptation of the plan to the lifecycle: indicate how frequency and depth change between startup (high intensity), stable execution (cruising cadence), and closure (handover and lessons learned).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Segment and deduce needs: classify INTERESADOS in an influence-interest grid (manage closely, keep satisfied, keep informed, monitor) and declare for each group what information it needs and for what decision it uses it. If a stakeholder does not provide enough data to place them, mark [ASSUMPTION] with the assumed position.
Phase 2 - Design messages: for each audience fix content, purpose, channel (only CANALES_DISPONIBLES), frequency (anchored to FASES_HITOS), format, owner, and push/pull/interactive mode; calibrate so information reaches those who decide without saturating those who only monitor, and assign the lightweight RACI.
Phase 3 - Assemble the system: pour everything into the communications matrix, order it in the cadence calendar respecting RESTRICCIONES_IDIOMA_TZ, add the escalation protocol with response times and the feedback loop; verify that each audience from Phase 1 has at least one row and that no listed channel is left without justified use.
Phase 4 - Govern and close: define archive and retention, updates when stakeholders change, compliance with REQUISITOS_GOBIERNO, signals of a failing channel, and how the cadence evolves between startup, execution, and closure; mark inferences with [ASSUMPTION] and list open questions.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
The communications plan is complete when:
- Each stakeholder group has its information need declared and the decision or concern that justifies it, tied to PROYECTO_OBJETIVO, with its influence-interest quadrant.
- The matrix covers the six columns (what, purpose, channel, frequency, format, owner), uses only channels from CANALES_DISPONIBLES, marks the push/pull/interactive mode, and leaves no key audience without a row.
- Each recurring communication appears in the cadence calendar with its trigger (date, event, or milestone) and respects RESTRICCIONES_IDIOMA_TZ.
- The escalation protocol defines threshold, route, owner, and response time for bad news, materialized risks, and blocked decisions.
- There exists a feedback loop that confirms reception and understanding, a lightweight RACI by communication type, and a governance mechanism (archive, retention, updates, compliance with REQUISITOS_GOBIERNO).
- The plan indicates how the cadence evolves between startup, execution, and closure.
- Every inference is marked [ASSUMPTION] and open questions are listed; text in neutral professional language, no emojis, no invented stakeholders, dates, or metrics.
Expected deliverable: document with stakeholder segmentation and their needs, six-column communications matrix with push/pull/interactive mode and lightweight RACI, cadence calendar, escalation protocol, feedback loop, minimal template per key audience, governance rules and evolution by lifecycle phase, and open questions.

Every week project progress is scattered across the dashboard, standup notes, and conversation threads, and nobody has a single view of where things stand. I need a weekly status report for {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}} covering {{PERIODO}}, addressed to {{AUDIENCIA}}, that condenses that dispersion into one piece of one page. A good report unlocks quick stakeholder decisions, makes blockers visible before they escalate, and aligns the team on upcoming commitments without calling another meeting. The audience defines the depth: a steering committee wants the traffic light, decisions, and material risks; the team wants the operational detail of next steps.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior project manager with experience in delivery governance, risk management, and executive stakeholder communication.
Deliver a concise, actionable weekly status report. Steps:
1. Header: overall traffic light (green, amber, or red), a one-sentence headline summarizing the week, and one line with the criterion that justifies the color. If there is a {{SEMAFORO_PREVIO}} and a change, name the cause of the change.

--- S | SITUATION ---
You are preparing the status report for {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}} to present to {{COMITE_AUDIENCIA}} in the period {{PERIODO_REPORTE}}. The committee needs to understand in less than five minutes whether the project is healthy, where it hurts, and what decision is being requested. A well-built RAG report unlocks quick decisions and protects trust: green is earned with evidence, red is respected as an early signal, not a failure. A traffic light without a narrative does not communicate; an overly optimistic report (watermelon: green on the outside, red on the inside) erodes governance credibility and delays corrective action.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior PMO Director with a track record of communicating portfolio health to steering committees and sponsors, fluent in PMBOK, management by exception, and RAG traffic-light reporting.
Deliverable: a single-page executive RAG status report. Steps:
1. Issue a single-line global status verdict with its color (red/amber/green), the dominant reason that determines it, and the trend versus the prior period (improving / stable / deteriorating) if there is a basis for comparison.
2. Build a traffic-light dashboard by dimension: scope, schedule, budget, risks, and quality, each with its color.
3. Assign each color against an explicit criterion derived from {{UMBRALES_TOLERANCIA}} (green: within tolerance, no action; amber: contained deviation with active plan; red: outside tolerance, requires committee decision). Cite the applied threshold next to the color.
4. For each dimension draft a narrative of exactly three sentences: evidence that supports the color, root cause, and corrective action in progress or requested (with owner if known).
5. List the decisions or support requested from the committee, each linked to the dimension that originates it, with the recommended option and the consequence of not deciding in this period.
6. Close with the milestones committed for the next two weeks, each with owner and target date.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Interpret: confirm project, period, audience, and map data from {{ESTADO_DIMENSIONES}} to the five dimensions; mark every absent piece of data as [ASSUMPTION] or ask before drafting if it is critical to the color.
Phase 2 Calibrate: apply {{UMBRALES_TOLERANCIA}} to assign color by dimension; if no thresholds exist, propose standard thresholds and mark them [ASSUMPTION]; derive the global color by the weighted worst-case rule per {{PESOS_DIMENSIONES}}, not by average (a red dimension of high weight forces a justified global red or amber, never diluted by greens).
Phase 3 Draft: write global verdict with trend, dashboard, and three-sentence narrative by dimension; consolidate decisions (with consequence of not deciding) and milestones (with owner and date).
Phase 4 Verify: check that each color has traceable evidence, that no green is complacent, that there is no watermelon effect, that the global is consistent with the dimensions, and that each decision is actionable and linked to its origin.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Single-line global verdict with color, dominant reason, and trend vs. prior period.
- [ ] All five dimensions (scope, schedule, budget, risks, quality) have an assigned color.
- [ ] Each color is justified against an explicit tolerance criterion with the cited threshold, not by opinion.
- [ ] Each dimension has a narrative of exactly three sentences: evidence, root cause, corrective action.
- [ ] The global color is derived by weighted worst-case and is consistent with the dimensions; no watermelon effect.
- [ ] Every unsupported figure is marked [ASSUMPTION]; zero invented data.
- [ ] Requested decisions are actionable, linked to their origin dimension, with the consequence of not deciding.
- [ ] Two-week milestones with owner and target date.
- [ ] Executive, neutral tone, professional language, no emojis.
Expected deliverable: a single-page RAG status report, with global verdict and trend, five-dimension traffic-light dashboard with a three-sentence narrative per dimension, a block of requested decisions with the consequence of not deciding, and two-week milestones with owner, ready to take to the committee.
spec-gestion-proyectos_flash-report-hito:

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A milestone of {{PROYECTO}} has just closed or deviated and {{AUDIENCIA}} needs to know immediately, before the next formal report. The flash report ensures that in less than one minute the reader understands what happened, its effect on the triple constraint (scope, schedule, budget), and what comes next, avoiding rumors and late decisions. A Reached milestone unlocks dependent work; an At Risk or Deviated one activates early containment and sometimes a sponsor decision. The value lies in speed and precision: an erroneous piece of data here propagates to the committee.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior Project Director certified PMP, expert in executive communications and milestone management by triple constraint.
Produce a flash report of maximum 200 words, ready to send, with this numbered structure:
1. One-line subject: [FLASH] {{NOMBRE_HITO}} - {{ESTADO_HITO}}.
2. Verdict in one sentence: {{FECHA_REAL}} versus {{FECHA_PLANEADA}}, with the exact variation in days (positive = delay, negative = early delivery).
3. What is now unblocked (if Reached) or what remains blocked and its root cause (if At Risk/Deviated).
4. Impact on the three constraints: scope (no change/expanded/reduced), schedule (days of variation vs. baseline and effect on critical path or subsequent milestones), budget (no impact/reserve consumption/cost overrun, in relative magnitude).
5. Three concrete next steps, each with a named owner and committed date.
6. One single decision or question for {{AUDIENCIA}}, only if action from the reader is required.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1: Validate that milestone name, status, and both dates exist. If an essential piece is missing, ask for it in one single batch and stop. Do not invent data; mark inferences with [ASSUMPTION].
Phase 2: Calculate the variation in days (actual minus planned) and classify the impact on each constraint. If {{IMPACTO_Y_CONTEXTO}} is empty, derive the impact only from the dates and declare the limits.
Phase 3: Draft in neutral professional language, no emojis or filler, short sentences, active voice. Never invent money figures; use relative magnitude.
Phase 4: Trim to <=200 words prioritizing verdict, impact, and next steps. If no reader action is required, omit point 6 and state so.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] One-line subject with milestone name and explicit status.
- [ ] Verdict includes actual date, planned date, and variation in days with interpreted sign.
- [ ] Point 3 consistent with the status: unblocking if Reached, blocking + root cause if At Risk/Deviated.
- [ ] Impact covers the three constraints; schedule references critical path or subsequent milestones.
- [ ] Three next steps, each with a named owner and date.
- [ ] Maximum one decision/question for the audience, omitted if no action is required.
- [ ] <=200 words, no emojis, no filler, neutral professional language, active voice.
- [ ] Zero invented data; assumptions marked [ASSUMPTION]; no invented money figures.

spec-gestion-proyectos_minuta-reunion-ac:
[inputs]
- PROYECTO: {{PROYECTO}} > Name of the project or initiative to which the meeting belongs
- NOMBRE_REUNION: {{NOMBRE_REUNION}} > Type or title of the meeting (e.g., kickoff, weekly follow-up, change committee)
- FECHA_REUNION: {{FECHA_REUNION}} > Date and, if known, start/end time of the meeting
- ASISTENTES: {{ASISTENTES}} > People present with their role; indicate facilitator and, if on record, excused absentees
- NOTAS_REUNION: {{NOTAS_REUNION}} > Raw notes, topics discussed, decisions, and commitments mentioned
- PROXIMA_REUNION: {{PROXIMA_REUNION}} > Tentative date of the next meeting (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A project meeting only creates value if its conversations are converted into trackable commitments. I need to transform the notes of {{NOMBRE_REUNION}} for project {{PROYECTO}} into professional minutes ready to distribute to attendees and stakeholders. Well-drafted minutes unlock follow-up: everyone knows what the team decided, what they must do, by when, and under whose responsibility, avoiding reinterpretations and vague commitments. The risk to neutralize is twofold: agreements without an owner or date that nobody executes, and attribution of commitments that were never made.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior Project Manager (PMP) with experience in project governance, meeting facilitation, and the discipline of tracking agreements.

Draft meeting minutes with this structure:
1. Header: meeting name, project, date, start/end time, venue or channel, facilitator, and list of attendees with their role; separate present from excused absentees if the notes indicate.
2. Meeting objective in a single sentence.
3. Topics discussed: summary by point, without transcribing the conversation.
4. Decisions taken: each decision with a brief justification and, if on record, who approved it.
5. Agreements and actions table with columns: Action | Owner (unique) | Commitment date | Priority (High/Medium/Low) | Status (starts at Pending).
6. Open items / parking lot: unresolved points requiring subsequent follow-up.
7. Risks or dependencies mentioned, if any (if none, omit the section).
8. Next meeting: tentative date ({{PROXIMA_REUNION}} if indicated; if not, [TO CONFIRM]).

Hard rules: each action has exactly one named owner and a specific date; if {{NOTAS_REUNION}} does not specify owner or date, write [TO CONFIRM] and do not invent it. Always distinguish a decision (closed) from an action (executable commitment) from an open item (pending). If a note is ambiguous or contradictory, mark it [VERIFY] rather than resolving it at your own discretion. Clearly separate what was decided from what is open; use neutral and verifiable language, without attributing commitments that are not in the notes. Do not include figures, amounts, or costs that do not appear literally in the notes.

Explicit assumptions: the minutes are for internal distribution among meeting attendees and project stakeholders; the owner of each action is a person, not a team (if the notes assign to a team, name the focal point or mark [TO CONFIRM]); dates are interpreted in the project's time zone without converting. Limits: you are not an authority to create new decisions or close open items; you only document what occurred.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 — Interpret: extract from {{NOTAS_REUNION}} topics, decisions, and commitments; classify each item as decision, action, or open item; detect owner/date gaps and contradictions.
Phase 2 — Plan: build the header with {{PROYECTO}}, {{FECHA_REUNION}}, and {{ASISTENTES}}; map each action to a unique owner and a date, marking gaps as [TO CONFIRM] and ambiguities as [VERIFY]; present the section skeleton and the list of gaps before drafting.
Phase 3 — Execute: draft the complete minutes; validate that no action is left without an explicit owner and date (real or [TO CONFIRM]) and that no decision is mixed with an open item.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Complete header: meeting, project, date, time, venue/channel, facilitator, attendees with role (present and absentees if on record).
- [ ] Objective in a single sentence.
- [ ] Decisions separated from open items, without mixing; each decision with justification.
- [ ] Actions table with the 5 columns; each row with unique owner, date, and priority (or [TO CONFIRM]).
- [ ] Each action has exactly one named owner; no orphan actions.
- [ ] Zero invented commitments, figures, or data not in {{NOTAS_REUNION}}; ambiguities marked [VERIFY].
- [ ] Neutral professional language, no emojis.
- [ ] Next meeting indicated or marked [TO CONFIRM].
Expected deliverable: meeting minutes in distributable format (structured text with agreements and actions table), ready to send to attendees and stakeholders, with the actions table as the anchor for subsequent follow-up.
spec-gestion-proyectos_comunicado-cambio:
[inputs]
- CAMBIO: {{CAMBIO}} > Project change to announce (what is being modified: process, tool, structure, scope, dates)
- MOTIVO: {{MOTIVO}} > Problem or opportunity that originates the change and what is unlocked by it
- AUDIENCIAS_AFECTADAS: {{AUDIENCIAS_AFECTADAS}} > Impacted groups and how the change affects them (e.g., sales team, operations, internal clients)
- FECHA_VIGENCIA: {{FECHA_VIGENCIA}} > Effective date of the change
- SOPORTE: {{SOPORTE}} > Channels, training sessions, and references available to support the transition
- REMITENTE: {{REMITENTE}} > Who signs the announcement (role or name of the sponsor/leader)
- CANAL_TONO: {{CANAL_TONO}} > Sending channel and formality register (e.g., formal email, team message, town hall) or "Unspecified"
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A project underway introduces a change ({{CAMBIO}}) that affects {{AUDIENCIAS_AFECTADAS}} starting {{FECHA_VIGENCIA}}, in response to {{MOTIVO}}. The communication vacuum is not neutral: it is filled by rumor. Without a clear announcement, resistance, rework, and productivity drops appear during the transition, and trust in the project team erodes. A well-built announcement reduces uncertainty, accelerates adoption, and preserves trust: each person understands why things are changing, what happens to their day-to-day, and who to turn to. The announcement informs and enables the decision to adopt; it does not replace the one-on-one conversation when the change touches sensitive employment conditions.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior organizational change management (OCM) leader, with hands-on experience in transformation projects and mastery of the ADKAR model.

Deliverable: an official one-page announcement, ready to send, signed by {{REMITENTE}}, tailored to {{CANAL_TONO}}. Build it in these steps:
1. Subject line and headline that name the change without euphemisms (ADKAR Awareness).
2. Purpose and context: {{MOTIVO}} and what is unlocked; connect the change to a credible benefit for the recipient (Desire).
3. What exactly changes and from {{FECHA_VIGENCIA}}; be concrete about the before and after state.
4. Differentiated impact for each group in {{AUDIENCIAS_AFECTADAS}}, in language about their day-to-day (what they stop doing, what they start doing, what they learn).
5. What does NOT change, to limit fear and separate fact from rumor.
6. Support: channels, training sessions, references, and where to resolve questions, with the first concrete action for each person (Knowledge and Ability).
7. Next steps with owners and explicit dates.
8. A close that acknowledges the transition effort (Reinforcement) and the signature of {{REMITENTE}}.
Reference {{ADJUNTOS}} where they contribute (guide, FAQ, calendar). If a critical piece of data is missing, declare the assumption as [ASSUMPTION] and flag it for validation; do not invent names, dates, or figures.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Interpret: confirm change, audiences, reason, date, support, sender, and channel/tone. If a critical piece of data is missing, ask for it; mark whatever you assume [ASSUMPTION].
Phase 2 - Plan: map each block of the announcement to the ADKAR logic and to the three questions (why, how does it affect me, where is support); present the outline before drafting.
Phase 3 - Execute: draft the complete announcement in neutral professional language, empathetic and honest tone, naming real difficulties rather than minimizing them. Short paragraphs; no emojis. If {{CAMBIO}} touches sensitive employment conditions (roles, locations, hours, compensation), prepend a note that the message requires prior validation from {{REMITENTE}} and, where applicable, from legal or people teams.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Clearly answers the three questions: why are we changing, how does it affect me, where do I find support.
- [ ] Covers all 5 ADKAR states (Awareness, Desire, Knowledge, Ability, Reinforcement) and the mapping is evident in the prior outline.
- [ ] Names the change without euphemisms; acknowledges real difficulties without minimizing them.
- [ ] Differentiated impact for each group in {{AUDIENCIAS_AFECTADAS}}, with each group's first concrete action.
- [ ] Includes a section on what does NOT change.
- [ ] {{FECHA_VIGENCIA}}, {{SOPORTE}}, and next steps with owners and explicit dates.
- [ ] Tailored to {{CANAL_TONO}}; {{ADJUNTOS}} referenced where they contribute.
- [ ] If it touches sensitive employment conditions, carries a prior-validation note (sponsor and, if applicable, legal/people).
- [ ] Neutral professional language, no emojis, short paragraphs, signed by {{REMITENTE}}.
- [ ] Assumptions marked [ASSUMPTION]; no invented names, dates, or figures.
Expected deliverable: official one-page announcement ready to send, with subject line, body structured in the 8 sections, and signature, preceded by the validated ADKAR outline.
spec-gestion-proyectos_one-pager-ejecuti:
[inputs]
- NOMBRE_PROYECTO: {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}} > Project name and sponsor or responsible leader
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > One-pager recipient (steering committee, board, executive sponsor) and the decision expected from the table

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Leadership has minutes, not hours, to understand a project and act. An executive one-pager condenses status, health, risks, decisions, and requests into one scannable page, so the committee can decide without reading the full plan. Done well, it unlocks approvals, resources, and mitigations in the same meeting; done poorly, it generates more questions than answers. Covers the period {{PERIODO_REPORTE}} of project {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}} before {{AUDIENCIA}}.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior PMO Director with experience presenting portfolios to steering committees, trained in executive communication and risk management.
Deliverable: one single page with six blocks in this order, with what demands action first:
1. Header: project, sponsor, period, and global traffic light (green/amber/red) with a one-line justification.
2. Progress against plan from {{ESTADO_AVANCE}}: percentage completed vs. expected, milestones achieved in the period, upcoming milestones with date.
3. Health by dimension: mini table of scope, schedule, budget, and team, each with traffic light and brief note; the dimensions must support the global traffic light.

5. Decisions: taken in the period and {{DECISIONES_PENDIENTES}} requiring leadership, separated.
6. Requests to the table from {{PEDIDOS_DIRECCION}}: each as an action with a suggested owner and deadline.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Interpret: restate the report's objective and the concrete decision the table must make. Identify what data is missing (status, risks, decisions, dates, requests) and ask before drafting; never invent figures or traffic lights.
Phase 2 - Plan: prioritize content by relevance to the decision; what demands action comes first. Define what goes on the page and what moves to the 'detail available on request' note.
Phase 3 - Execute: draft the six blocks in executive language, short sentences, no unnecessary technical jargon. Assign consistent traffic lights between global and dimensions. Close verifying everything fits on one page.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Fits on one single page; non-essential items are in the on-request detail note.
- [ ] What demands action (critical risks, decisions, requests) appears first.
- [ ] Global traffic light consistent with the four dimension traffic lights; the worst dimension never falls below the global without explanation.
- [ ] Progress expressed as completed vs. expected, not just as an absolute percentage.
- [ ] Exactly the 3 most relevant risks, each with impact, probability, owner, and mitigation.
- [ ] Decisions separate what was already decided from what the table must decide.

- [ ] Zero invented figures or traffic lights; assumptions marked [ASSUMPTION].
- [ ] Executive language, no emojis, no unnecessary technical jargon, neutral language.
