[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need the system prompt that will govern a custom programming agent for the project {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}}, targeting {{HERRAMIENTA_DESTINO}}. A code agent without a behavioral contract improvises: it invents APIs, rewrites things it should not, and delivers changes that are impossible to review. A well-designed system prompt turns it into a predictable and auditable collaborator: it respects the stack, knows its hard limits, follows a fixed workflow, and always delivers in the same reviewable format. This unlocks delegating real coding work with confidence and fast reviews.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior prompt engineer specializing in the design of system prompts for code agents, with experience operating programming assistants in production repos and adapting contracts to different IDEs/agents.
Deliverable: the complete agent system prompt, in a single pasteable block, plus (a) a short list of [ASSUMPTION] tags and (b) a mini acceptance checklist for the user to validate. Build the system prompt with these five explicitly numbered sections inside the prompt:
1. Role and identity: define who the agent is, its seniority, and its mission in {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}}; establish that it prioritizes correctness and reviewability over speed.
2. Stack and conventions: fix the stack {{STACK_TECNICO}} and conventions {{CONVENCIONES}} as mandatory (language, framework, package manager, runtime, linter/formatter, folder structure, patterns). Golden rule: when in doubt about a convention, mimic the existing neighboring code before introducing a new style.
3. Hard constraints: translate {{RESTRICCIONES_DURAS}} into explicit, verifiable NEVER rules; include by default: do not invent APIs or signatures (if not present in the code or docs, declare it and ask for confirmation), do not delete or move files without confirming, do not add dependencies without justifying a native alternative, do not expose or assume secrets (use placeholders), do not touch CI/CD configuration or data migrations without explicit approval, do not reformat entire files when the change is a single point.
4. Workflow: numbered steps the agent follows for each task (1-read the relevant code before writing; 2-restate the task in one line; 3-present a short plan; 4-execute the minimum change; 5-self-verify: lint, build/tests, or manual review when there is no runtime) bounded by {{NIVEL_AUTONOMIA}}. Define the behavior at each level: propose only / edit with confirmation / autonomous within scope.
5. Output format and clarifications: define exactly what it returns per {{FORMATO_SALIDA}} (diff, full file, explanation, test commands) and the protocol for requesting data when something is ambiguous instead of assuming (ask for at most the essential and propose a reasonable tagged default).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 – Interpretation: read the seven inputs; if {{NIVEL_AUTONOMIA}}, {{STACK_TECNICO}}, or {{RESTRICCIONES_DURAS}} are empty or ambiguous, ask before drafting. If {{HERRAMIENTA_DESTINO}} imposes limits (no command execution, short context window, no access to the full repo), adapt the workflow and state it inside the system prompt.
Phase 2 – Design: draft the five sections in the imperative second person directed at the agent, with verifiable rules and no filler; resolve the edge case of conflict between {{NIVEL_AUTONOMIA}} and a hard constraint (the constraint wins) and the case of a missing convention (mimic neighboring code). Make the workflow always end in verification.
Phase 3 – Packaging: deliver the prompt in a single pasteable block; below it the list of [ASSUMPTION] tags and a mini acceptance checklist (3–5 items). Do not include prices or the word free.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- The five sections (role, stack/conventions, hard constraints, workflow, output format) are present and numbered inside the system prompt.
- The constraints are in NEVER form, are verifiable, and are project-specific, not generic.
- The workflow explicitly includes read-before-write and verify-before-close, defines the three {{NIVEL_AUTONOMIA}} levels, and resolves the constraint-vs-autonomy conflict in favor of the constraint.
- The output format is unambiguous: it defines what the agent returns and how it requests clarifications with a reasonable default.
- The system prompt is adapted to {{HERRAMIENTA_DESTINO}} and is self-contained and pasteable without editing.
- The delivery includes a list of [ASSUMPTION] tags and a mini acceptance checklist.
Expected deliverable: a system prompt block ready to paste into the code agent configuration, plus a brief list of [ASSUMPTION] tags and a mini acceptance checklist.
spec-vibe-coding_contexto-empaquetado-pa:
[inputs]
- REPOSITORIO: {{REPOSITORIO}} > Repo or path/URL to package, with access to the file tree (name, stack if known)
- TAREA_AGENTE: {{TAREA_AGENTE}} > Specific task the agent must execute with this context (e.g. "add pagination to the orders endpoint", "migrate the auth module to OAuth2")
- LIMITE_TOKENS: {{LIMITE_TOKENS}} > Available context budget for the agent, e.g. 8k tokens (optional; if missing, optimize by density with no hard cap and declare it)
- ARCHIVOS_PRIORITARIOS: {{ARCHIVOS_PRIORITARIOS}} > Files you already know are relevant, to bias the curation (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A code agent is only as good as the context it receives: too much and the signal is diluted and budget burned; too little and it hallucinates the architecture. You need to package {{REPOSITORIO}} so the agent executes {{TAREA_AGENTE}} with just the right and sufficient context, within {{LIMITE_TOKENS}}. A good package unlocks the agent starting by hitting the right code on the first attempt, without asking avoidable questions or breaking repo conventions. This is context engineering: the signal-to-token ratio, not the volume, is what determines whether the agent succeeds.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior context engineer specializing in code agents, with software architecture judgment and strict token-budget discipline.

Deliverable: a packed context document in Markdown, ready to paste as the agent's initial instruction. Steps:
1. Map {{REPOSITORIO}}: folder structure, dominant language and framework, entry point, dependency manifests, configuration, and conventions; integrate {{ARCHIVOS_PRIORITARIOS}} as an initial signal.
2. Classify files by their relevance to {{TAREA_AGENTE}} into three levels: CRITICAL (read in full), REFERENCE (signatures/interfaces/schemas/load-bearing fragments only), and CONTEXT (one line of existence and purpose).
3. For each CRITICAL file extract the essentials: public contract, invariants, side effects, and extension points; discard dispensable internal implementation.
4. Assemble the package: repo map, rules/conventions to respect, files by level, and explicit list of omissions with their reason.
5. Adjust the volume to fit within {{LIMITE_TOKENS}}, downgrading files from a higher level to a lower one before cutting critical content.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 – Mapping: reconstruct the repo topology and detect real conventions (not assumed: derived from observed code and config). Tag any unverifiable data as [ASSUMPTION]. If the repo exceeds what can be inspected, declare the limit and propose task-directed sampling.
Phase 2 – Curation: score each file by relevance to {{TAREA_AGENTE}} and assign a level; the rule is maximum signal per token. A file is CRITICAL only if the agent needs to read it in full to not err on the task.
Phase 3 – Distillation: summarize each critical file to its contract and risks (invariants, side effects, extension points); preserve literal text only when load-bearing (signatures, schemas, invariants).
Phase 4 – Sanitization: remove or replace with placeholders every secret, credential, token, or PII before including any fragment.
Phase 5 – Assembly and budget: build the document and verify it fits within {{LIMITE_TOKENS}}; if not, downgrade levels (CRITICAL->REFERENCE, REFERENCE->CONTEXT) before cutting critical content, and document each cut with its reason.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Every CRITICAL file is justified by {{TAREA_AGENTE}}; none is superfluous.
- [ ] Levels properly applied: nothing critical was left as context, nor vice versa.
- [ ] Every critical file exposes contract, invariants, side effects, and extension points; without superfluous internal implementation.
- [ ] Conventions are derived from observed code; anything unverifiable is tagged [ASSUMPTION].
- [ ] Zero secrets, credentials, tokens, or PII in the package.
- [ ] The document fits within {{LIMITE_TOKENS}}; downgrades and omissions are listed with their reason.
- [ ] An agent that reads only this document could locate where to touch the code without requesting the repo again.
Expected deliverable: Markdown document with sections Repo map, Rules and conventions, CRITICAL files (distilled), REFERENCE files, CONTEXT files, and Omitted (with reason), ready to paste as the agent's initial instruction.
spec-vibe-coding_generar-componente-ui-d:
[inputs]
- DESCRIPCION_COMPONENTE: {{DESCRIPCION_COMPONENTE}} > What the component does, what it shows, and how it behaves (e.g. "notification card with title, message, icon by type, and optional close button with configurable auto-close")
- PROPS_ESPERADAS: {{PROPS_ESPERADAS}} > Input data and component events with their type, required/optional, and default value if applicable (e.g. "title:text required, message:text required, type:info|success|warning|error = info, onClose:function optional, autoCloseMs:number optional")

- SISTEMA_DISENO: {{SISTEMA_DISENO}} > Token source and names: colors, spacing, typography, radii, shadows, breakpoints (e.g. "Tailwind with theme tokens", "CSS variables --color-* / --space-*", "undefined: ask")
- CONVENCIONES_REPO: {{CONVENCIONES_REPO}} > Destination repo rules: token import path, file naming, reusable base primitives or components, or "No conventions: ask"
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, screenshots, Figma, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You are translating the functional description of an interface component into production code. The goal is to eliminate the bottleneck between what is imagined and what is integrated: a component that not only looks right in the happy path, but is born accessible, typed, and with all its states resolved. Delivering it unlocks immediate integration into the design system without rework from forgotten states, untyped props, or accessibility failures caught too late — which are the most expensive to fix.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior front-end engineer specializing in design systems and accessibility (WAI-ARIA / WCAG 2.1 AA).

Generate the component described in DESCRIPCION_COMPONENTE for the stack FRAMEWORK_LENGUAJE, following these steps:
1. Define the props signature from PROPS_ESPERADAS with strict typing: exact types, required vs. optional props, default values where applicable, and closed union types for enumerations (variants, sizes, types).
2. Implement the semantic structure with the correct HTML elements and roles; apply ARIA attributes only where native semantics fall short, without redundancies or invalid roles.
3. Implement every state in ESTADOS_REQUERIDOS in a visually distinguishable way: visible focus, logical tab order, keyboard navigation for every interactive element, screen reader announcement in dynamic states (loading, error), and respect for prefers-reduced-motion in animations.
4. Apply styles consuming exclusively tokens from SISTEMA_DISENO (colors, spacing, typography, radii, shadows); zero arbitrary fixed values. Respect CONVENCIONES_REPO for imports, naming, and reuse of primitives; do not duplicate what already exists.
5. Keep the component self-contained (without business logic or network unless requested) and externalize visible and screen reader support text via props to enable i18n. Do not add new dependencies without justifying them and offering a dependency-free alternative.
6. Comment only where the intent is not obvious and document the props signature.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 – Interpretation: restate what component you understood, its props with type, the states to cover, the destination stack, and the token source. If DESCRIPCION_COMPONENTE, PROPS_ESPERADAS, FRAMEWORK_LENGUAJE, or SISTEMA_DISENO are missing or ambiguous, ask the minimum necessary questions and stop; do not assume the stack or invent token names, breakpoints, or import paths.
Phase 2 – Plan: list the props signature, the states to implement, and the accessibility strategy (semantics, roles, ARIA, focus, tab order, keyboard, screen readers, reduced motion) before writing code.
Phase 3 – Execution: deliver the component code and, at the close, the list of covered states with how to trigger each one and a note on relevant trade-offs (e.g. ARIA chosen, focus decision).
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] All props from PROPS_ESPERADAS are typed with their exact type; required and optional differentiated; default values where applicable; enumerations as closed unions.
- [ ] Every state in ESTADOS_REQUERIDOS is implemented and visually distinguishable; dynamic states are announced to screen readers.
- [ ] Every interactive element is keyboard-operable, with visible focus, logical tab order, and correct role/ARIA; the happy path introduces no focus traps.
- [ ] Styles consume tokens from SISTEMA_DISENO; zero arbitrary fixed values of color, spacing, or typography; sufficient contrast for WCAG 2.1 AA; animations respect prefers-reduced-motion.
- [ ] The component respects CONVENCIONES_REPO (imports, naming, reuse) and introduces no new dependencies without justification; texts externalizable for i18n.
- [ ] The code compiles/validates in FRAMEWORK_LENGUAJE and comments exist only where the intent is not obvious.
- [ ] No missing data was invented: anything ambiguous was asked about in Phase 1.
Expected deliverable: integration-ready component code + documented props signature + list of covered states with their trigger + brief note on accessibility trade-offs.
spec-vibe-coding_clonar-ui-desde-screens:
[inputs]
- SCREENSHOT: {{SCREENSHOT}} > Image of the screen to clone (attached or referenced); indicate whether it is the full screen or a crop and the width/device it corresponds to
- STACK_OBJETIVO: {{STACK_OBJETIVO}} > Output technology: HTML+CSS, React, Vue, Svelte, Flutter, SwiftUI, etc.
- SISTEMA_ESTILOS: {{SISTEMA_ESTILOS}} > Style system or library: plain CSS, Tailwind, CSS Modules, styled-components, or a specific component library (optional)

- RESPONSIVE: {{RESPONSIVE}} > Whether it should adapt to other sizes and which breakpoints, or if only the screenshot width is needed (optional, default: visible width only)
- RESTRICCIONES_TECNICAS: {{RESTRICCIONES_TECNICAS}} > Limits to respect: framework version, browser support, no new dependencies, dark mode, i18n, etc. (optional, default: no additional constraints)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I have the screenshot {{SCREENSHOT}} of an existing screen and I need to reproduce it as code in {{STACK_OBJETIVO}} with fidelity {{NIVEL_FIDELIDAD}}, respecting {{RESTRICCIONES_TECNICAS}}. An image is a partial source: it reveals the static composition of a single state and a single size, but not interactive states, breakpoints, real text, vector assets, or the logic behind it. Cloning a UI well from a screenshot unlocks rapid prototyping, migration of legacy screens, replicating a pattern that works, and starting from a clean code base instead of a blank canvas; cloning it poorly delivers pixels that do not scale, scattered magic values, and invisible assumptions that break later. The value is not in copying pixels but in reconstructing the implicit system (tokens, hierarchy, layout) that generates them.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior frontend engineer specializing in translating visual designs into code, with mastery of design systems, tokens, responsive layout, and accessibility.

Deliverable: the screenshot screen reproduced as componentized code in {{STACK_OBJETIVO}}, accompanied by the visual tree, inferred tokens, state handling, and a fidelity checklist. Steps:
1. Screenshot reading: describe what you see in {{SCREENSHOT}} (screen type, apparent purpose, breakpoint it represents) before coding, to confirm a shared interpretation.
2. Visual tree: decompose the image into a hierarchy of regions and components (header, nav, hero, cards, lists, forms, footer) with nesting and layout model per region (flex, grid, stack, absolute position). Identify the repeatable pattern: if there are 5 identical cards, there is one component, not five blocks.
3. Inferred design tokens: extract color (approximate hex), typography (family, sizes, weights, line height), spacing scale, radii, shadows, and borders; infer the system (e.g. spacing in multiples of 4/8). Values not distinguishable with certainty are given as a range and tagged [ASSUMPTION].
4. Code: generate the componentized interface in {{STACK_OBJETIVO}} using {{SISTEMA_ESTILOS}}, with centralized tokens (CSS variables, theme, or constants), semantic, accessible markup (ARIA roles, labels, heading hierarchy, contrast, focus order), and example data as placeholder; no scattered magic values. Respect {{RESTRICCIONES_TECNICAS}}.
5. States and responsive: declare states (hover, focus, active, disabled, empty, loading, error) and breakpoints NOT visible in a single image; respect {{RESPONSIVE}}, propose reasonable behavior, and tag it as a decision to validate.
6. Fidelity checklist: table comparing region by region the observed against the implemented at the {{NIVEL_FIDELIDAD}} level, plus the list of gaps the image does not resolve (real text, microcopy, interactions, dynamic data, brand assets, vector icons, licensed fonts).
Constraint: do not invent business logic, endpoints, or real data; the output is the presentation layer only. Do not use proprietary brand fonts or assets without flagging their substitute/placeholder.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 – Interpretation: confirm stack, fidelity, responsive scope, and constraints; if {{SCREENSHOT}} is missing, clipped, low-resolution, or the stack is undefined, ask before proceeding. Phase 2 – Dissection: produce the visual tree and the inferred token table, separating observed from assumed and inferring the underlying system. Phase 3 – Implementation: code from the outside in (region layout, then reusable components, then token detail), centralizing styles. Phase 4 – Verification: walk through the fidelity checklist region by region, list gaps and assumptions, and deliver minimal instructions to run or preview the result.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Screenshot reading confirmed before writing code.
- [ ] Complete visual tree: every region with its nesting, layout model, and repeatable patterns identified as components.
- [ ] Inferred tokens centralized (color, typography, spacing, radii, shadows) with inferred system; uncertain values tagged [ASSUMPTION].
- [ ] Code in {{STACK_OBJETIVO}} componentized, semantic, accessible (ARIA, focus, contrast, headings), and without scattered magic values.
- [ ] {{RESTRICCIONES_TECNICAS}} respected; no unflagged proprietary dependencies or assets.
- [ ] Non-visible states and breakpoints explicitly declared as decisions to validate, per {{RESPONSIVE}}.
- [ ] Region-by-region fidelity checklist at the {{NIVEL_FIDELIDAD}} level and list of information gaps.
- [ ] No invented business logic, endpoints, or real data.
- [ ] Minimal run/preview instructions included.
Expected deliverable: screen code ready to render, plus visual tree, token table, state/responsive handling, fidelity checklist, gap list, and consolidated assumptions.
spec-vibe-coding_landing-page-de-convers:
[inputs]
- PRODUCTO: {{PRODUCTO}} > Product or service the landing page promotes and its central value
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Who it targets: role, sector, or profile of the target visitor
- ACCION_CONVERSION: {{ACCION_CONVERSION}} > Single desired action: sign up, schedule a demo, leave an email, buy
- PRUEBA_SOCIAL: {{PRUEBA_SOCIAL}} > Available real testimonials, logos, metrics, or number of clients (if missing, markers are used)
- TONO_ESTILO: {{TONO_ESTILO}} > Desired tone of voice and visual style: sober, energetic, corporate, minimalist (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
The team needs to convert visits into a concrete action and for that it needs a landing page for {{PRODUCTO}} targeting {{AUDIENCIA}} — not a decorative page. The purpose is to transform a diffuse value proposition into a page that guides the eye through a clear hierarchy all the way to {{ACCION_CONVERSION}}: a hero that promises a result, scannable benefits, social proof that builds trust, and a CTA repeated without distractions. A well-built landing page is published and measured immediately, and is ready to iterate on real data. EstrategIA contributes the rigor of persuasive copy applied to an interface that runs without dependencies.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior product designer and conversion copywriter, expert in single-page landing pages, AIDA model, unique value proposition, social proof, and accessible visual hierarchy.
Deliver the following, in this order:
1. Restate the objective in one sentence: "Convince {{AUDIENCIA}} to {{ACCION_CONVERSION}} by showing the value of {{PRODUCTO}}".
2. If {{PRODUCTO}}, {{AUDIENCIA}}, {{ACCION_CONVERSION}}, or {{PRUEBA_SOCIAL}} are missing or ambiguous, ask for exactly that data before writing code. Do not invent testimonials, figures, or logos: if {{PRUEBA_SOCIAL}} is missing, use visible [REPLACE: ...] markers and indicate what to substitute. If there are multiple audiences, prioritize a single one per landing and declare the rest as [ASSUMPTION] discarded.
3. Define the structure in hierarchy order: hero (benefit headline + subtitle + CTA visible without scrolling), block of three benefits or problem-solution, social proof section from {{PRUEBA_SOCIAL}}, and close with repeated CTA and micro-copy that reduces friction (what happens on click, how long it takes, no commitment).
4. Write the copy with AIDA in the tone {{TONO_ESTILO}}: headline with a concrete, measurable result, body of benefits over features, a single primary CTA with an action verb; a secondary CTA only if it does not compete with the primary.
5. Deliver a single self-contained index.html with embedded CSS, responsive, accessible, and semantic.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 – Interpretation: restate objective, audience, and action; list what data is missing and tag assumptions with [ASSUMPTION]. Decision: if {{PRODUCTO}} is abstract, translate it into an observable result for the visitor.
Phase 2 – Architecture: define the 4 sections, the single H1, the message of each block, and where the CTA is repeated (at minimum hero and close). Trade-off: prioritize clarity over density; if content is excessive, cut it instead of adding sections.
Phase 3 – Copy: draft headline, subtitle, three benefits, social proof, and CTA micro-copy applying AIDA; no prices or the word free; neutral and professional English.

Modeling it as an explicit finite state machine shifts that guarantee to the type system: instead of prohibiting the impossible state by convention, it becomes impossible to represent (make illegal states unrepresentable). The compiler or type constructor rejects invalid combinations outright, entire classes of bugs are eliminated, the domain is documented in the code, and future features start from a verifiable foundation.

6. Deliver a state diagram in Mermaid stateDiagram-v2 consistent cell by cell with the table, marking the initial state and terminal states.

Phase 5 Close: draft the invariants now guaranteed by the type and the limits of the model (which still requires runtime logic: persistence, real concurrency, external payload validation).

spec-vibe-coding_logica-offline-y-sincro:
[inputs]
- APP_AND_ENTITIES: {{APP_AND_ENTITIES}} > What app and which entities must work offline (e.g. notes app: notes, tags, attachments)
- STACK: {{STACK}} > Target stack and local storage (e.g. React Native + SQLite/WatermelonDB; Flutter + Isar/Drift; web + IndexedDB)
- CONFLICT_STRATEGY: {{CONFLICT_STRATEGY}} > Preferred conflict strategy: last-write-wins, field-level merge, or manual review (optional; if omitted, recommend and justify based on LOSS_TOLERANCE)
- LOSS_TOLERANCE: {{LOSS_TOLERANCE}} > How much data loss is acceptable and which data is critical vs. discardable (optional)
- ATTACHMENTS: {{ATTACHMENTS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
The app must remain usable without network connectivity and must not lose the user's work on reconnection. A well-designed offline-first layer unlocks use in coverage-dead zones, resilience on outages, and a UX without blocking spinners, avoiding the most expensive bug in these apps: duplicated or overwritten data on sync. The design produced is the foundation on which cache, outbox, and reconciliation of {{APP_AND_ENTITIES}} are implemented. Getting the versioning or idempotency wrong is paid for in silent data corruption, not in a visible crash: this is why the design is validated with acceptance criteria, not just with code that compiles.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior offline-first application engineer, with proven experience in data synchronization, conflict resolution, and outbox/mutation queue design.
Design the local and synchronization layer for {{APP_AND_ENTITIES}} in {{STACK}}, delivering actionable code or pseudocode. First declare the assumptions you adopt and the limits of the solution (what it does NOT cover). Then:
1. Local cache model: persisted entities, primary key, per-record version (monotonic counter or Lamport-style logical timestamp, NEVER the client's wall clock), and status flags: dirty (pending local change), synced, and base_version (version of the last confirmed sync, the anchor for detecting conflict).
2. Mutation queue (outbox): per-operation schema (local id, type create/update/delete, entity, payload, base_version, timestamp, status pending/sending/confirmed/failed, attempts, idempotency_key); deterministic drain order (FIFO per entity respecting parent-child dependencies), and retry policy with exponential backoff + jitter and attempt ceiling before marking failed and notifying.
3. Reconciliation engine: applying the server delta onto the cache, detecting conflict (dirty local record whose base_version differs from the server's version), and applying {{CONFLICT_STRATEGY}} with trade-off justification; if omitted, recommend one based on {{LOSS_TOLERANCE}} (LWW if loss is tolerable, field-level merge if entities have independent fields, manual review if data is critical).
4. Sync state machine: offline, queuing, syncing, synced, conflict; named events and transitions (reconnect, network error, conflict detected, resolution applied, retry exhaustion).
5. Temporary IDs: local id generation on offline create and reconciliation with the server's definitive id (remapping of references in still-queued child mutations).
6. Idempotency: stable idempotency_key per mutation so that a resend after timeout does not duplicate on the server.
Also deliver a textual flow diagram of reconnect -> queue drain -> reconciliation -> conflict resolution, and a verifiable acceptance criterion for each point 1-6.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Interpretation: confirm {{APP_AND_ENTITIES}}, {{STACK}}, {{CONFLICT_STRATEGY}}, and {{LOSS_TOLERANCE}}; if anything critical is missing, ask before coding; declare assumptions and limits.
Phase 2 - Modeling: define cache schema, outbox schema, and state machine.
Phase 3 - Synchronization: specify queue drain, retries, server delta reconciliation, and conflict detection.
Phase 4 - Robustness: resolve temporary IDs and idempotency and enumerate edge cases: update on already-deleted server record (tombstone), delete-vs-update conflict, stale payload, resend after timeout with no confirmation, parent-create before child-create order.
Phase 5 - Delivery: code/pseudocode + textual flow diagram + acceptance criteria.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Assumptions and limits declared before the code.
- [ ] Local cache with key, logical version (not wall clock), and base_version that allows detecting conflict, not just pending changes.
- [ ] Outbox with explicit states, deterministic drain order respecting parent-child dependencies, and exponential backoff with jitter and ceiling.
- [ ] Conflict strategy declared and justified; coherent with {{LOSS_TOLERANCE}}.
- [ ] Complete state machine with all named transitions, including retry exhaustion.
- [ ] Temporary IDs remapped to server IDs without breaking still-queued child references.
- [ ] Idempotency preventing duplicates on resend after timeout.
- [ ] Edge cases covered: tombstone, delete-vs-update, stale payload, resend with no confirmation, parent-child order.
- [ ] Executable/actionable code or pseudocode in {{STACK}} + textual flow diagram + verifiable acceptance criterion per point 1-6.
Expected deliverable: technical design of the offline-first layer with assumptions and limits, cache and outbox schemas, reconciliation engine, state machine, flow diagram, and acceptance criteria, ready to implement.
spec-vibe-coding_diagnostico-de-error-de:
[inputs]
- STACKTRACE: {{STACKTRACE}} > Complete error stacktrace or traceback, copied exactly as the runtime emits it (header, frames, and Caused by blocks if they exist)
- LANGUAGE_RUNTIME: {{LANGUAGE_RUNTIME}} > Language, version, and runtime/framework where it occurs (e.g. Python 3.12, Node 20, Java 17/Spring, .NET 8) (optional)
- RELEVANT_CODE: {{RELEVANT_CODE}} > Code fragment of the line or function appearing in the topmost frame of your code (optional)
- REPRODUCTION_CONTEXT: {{REPRODUCTION_CONTEXT}} > What was running, with what input, and steps to reproduce the error (optional)
- PRIOR_ATTEMPTS: {{PRIOR_ATTEMPTS}} > What has already been tried or ruled out, to avoid repeating paths (optional)
- ATTACHMENTS: {{ATTACHMENTS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A stacktrace is the error's black box: it contains the exact call path to the failure point, but reading it incorrectly leads to patching the symptom (the last frame, almost always from a library) instead of the root cause (the first frame of your code that broke the invariant). I need to interpret this stacktrace to locate the root cause and apply the minimal fix, without unnecessary refactors or scope changes. A rigorous diagnosis unlocks three things: a bounded and verifiable fix, an explanation of the failure mechanism that prevents its recurrence, and the informed decision of whether an additional defensive guard is needed. The anti-pattern to avoid: speculative changes — touching multiple things at once without knowing which fix worked.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior software engineer expert in debugging, stacktrace reading, and root-cause analysis in multiple languages and runtimes.

Deliverable: a root-cause diagnosis with the minimal fix and its verification. Steps:
1. Read the header of {{STACKTRACE}}: identify the exception type and transcribe literally what the message asserts (do not paraphrase it: the exact text often contains the discriminating data).
2. Traverse the frames from inside out: locate where the exception was thrown, trace toward the root cause, and separate the frames of your own code from those of libraries and runtime (using {{LANGUAGE_RUNTIME}} to recognize project paths vs. environment paths). Mark the first frame of your own code in the failure path.
3. If there is chaining (Caused by / during handling of / the above exception was the direct cause), follow the chain to the originating exception and explicitly separate symptom from cause.
4. Formulate 2 or 3 root-cause hypotheses ordered by probability; for each one declare the stack evidence in favor, the evidence against, and how to confirm or discard it quickly. Cross with {{RELEVANT_CODE}}, {{REPRODUCTION_CONTEXT}}, and {{PRIOR_ATTEMPTS}}; do not propose a path that {{PRIOR_ATTEMPTS}} already discarded without justifying why it is worth revisiting.
5. Select the most probable hypothesis and explain the failure mechanism (why it occurs, not just where) in one or two sentences.
6. Propose the minimal fix as a diff or before/after, attacking only the root cause; all defensive guards (null validation, edge handling, retries, logging) go separately and marked as optional, with their adoption criterion.
7. Indicate how to verify: the specific test case or reproduction step that goes from failing to working, and what regression to watch for.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Stack reading: parse header (type + message) and frames; identify language/runtime from {{LANGUAGE_RUNTIME}} or from the shape of the trace itself if not provided.
Phase 2 - Frame triage: from inside out, classify each frame as own code, library, or runtime; isolate the first own-code frame in the failure path and the Caused by chain to the originating cause.
Phase 3 - Hypotheses: generate 2 or 3 candidate causes with evidence for/against and a cheap check to confirm or discard each; do not choose without contrasting.
Phase 4 - Minimal fix and verification: explain the mechanism, deliver the bounded patch (diff or before/after), separate the optional parts, and define the test or reproduction that validates the fix.
Evidence rule: do not invent code, file names, line numbers, or values not in the inputs; inferences are marked [ASSUMPTION]. If the code of a frame, the runtime, a library version, or the reproduction steps are missing, ask for them before concluding.
Edge cases: if {{STACKTRACE}} is truncated, minified/obfuscated, mixes several errors, or the message does not correspond to the described failure, flag it and say what is missing to close the diagnosis. If the root frame falls entirely in third-party code, locate the last own-code frame that invoked that path and treat the case as library misuse unless there is evidence of a third-party bug. If the stack points to a generic wrapper, do not stop there: pursue the originating cause in the chain.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Exception type and message identified literally from the header.
- [ ] Stack read from inside out, with the first own-code frame marked and library/runtime frames separated.
- [ ] Caused by chain followed to the originating cause; symptom and cause explicitly distinguished.
- [ ] 2 or 3 hypotheses ordered by probability, each with evidence for, against, and a cheap confirmation check; none repeats a path already discarded in {{PRIOR_ATTEMPTS}} without justifying it.
- [ ] Minimal fix bounded to the root cause, shown as diff or before/after; defensive guards separated and marked optional with their adoption criterion.
- [ ] Concrete verification: test case or reproduction step that goes from failing to working, plus the regression to watch for.
- [ ] Zero invented code, files, or values; inferences marked [ASSUMPTION]; missing information requested, not assumed; truncated or inconsistent stack flagged.
Expected deliverable: a diagnosis containing (1) exception and message, (2) stack reading with the root frame marked, (3) table or list of hypotheses with evidence and check, (4) chosen root cause with its mechanism, (5) minimal patch in diff/before-after with optional guards separately, (6) verification plan.
spec-vibe-coding_reproducir-bug-con-caso:
[inputs]
- SYMPTOM_OR_STACKTRACE: {{SYMPTOM_OR_STACKTRACE}} > Description of the failure or complete stack trace: what fails, error message, reported line, exception type
- SUSPECT_CODE: {{SUSPECT_CODE}} > Code fragment or module path where the failure originates; include collaborating functions if the origin is not obvious
- ENVIRONMENT_AND_FREQUENCY: {{ENVIRONMENT_AND_FREQUENCY}} > Where it appears (CI, local, production, container) and with what frequency (1 in every N runs, only under load, only in parallel, only after a certain test)
- TECHNICAL_STACK: {{TECHNICAL_STACK}} > Language, runtime version, test framework, concurrency manager, and relevant versioned dependencies
- PRIOR_ATTEMPTS: {{PRIOR_ATTEMPTS}} > What has already been tried to reproduce or fix, and what was ruled out (optional)
- ATTACHMENTS: {{ATTACHMENTS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
An intermittent or non-deterministic failure is blocking progress: it appears in some runs and disappears in others, which prevents debugging it, fixing it with confidence, and closing the bug. The goal is to transform that ghost symptom into a minimal, deterministic, and self-contained reproducer (MCVE) that reliably triggers the failure. A minimal case unlocks the fix, serves as a permanent regression test, and allows sharing the problem without exposing the entire system or sensitive data.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior software engineer specialized in debugging non-deterministic systems and case reduction (MCVE), with mastery of race conditions, control of randomness sources, variable isolation, and delta bisection.

Deliverable: a minimal executable reproducer of the failure, plus the diagnosis of the condition that triggers it and the path to convert it into a regression test.

Concrete steps:
1. Validate inputs. If SYMPTOM_OR_STACKTRACE, SUSPECT_CODE, ENVIRONMENT_AND_FREQUENCY, or TECHNICAL_STACK is missing, ask for it before continuing.
2. Formulate 2 or 3 hypotheses about the non-determinism source: race condition, mutable shared state, execution or test order dependency, time or clock dependency, unfixed input data, external resource, random seed, data structure iteration order, locale or timezone, core count.
3. Design the isolation experiment: fix all variables except the suspect one (a single free variable per iteration).
4. Reduce by bisection down to the minimum code that still fails.
5. Deliver the final self-contained reproducer with run instruction, diagnosis, and conversion to regression test.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: reconstruct the observable symptom and its appearance rate from the inputs; mark as [ASSUMPTION] every code behavior not verifiable.
Phase 2 - Hypotheses: list the 2 or 3 most probable non-determinism sources, ordered by evidence, with the signal that would confirm or refute each one.
Phase 3 - Variable control: freeze randomness seeds, clock, and timezone; fix execution and iteration order; replace network, disk, and services with doubles or in-memory data; force concurrency or a stress loop to raise the appearance probability until it becomes observable.
Phase 4 - Bisection: remove dependencies, layers, and lines one by one, verifying after each trim that the failure persists; stop at the minimal irreducible.
Phase 5 - Confirmation: explicitly discard each unsupported hypothesis and identify the exact condition that triggers the failure; if after control determinism is not achieved, declare the residual non-determinism and the next hypothesis to try.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The reproducer is a single self-contained and executable file or test, with no dependencies on the full system or sensitive data.
- [ ] Every source of non-determinism is controlled (seed, clock, timezone, locale, execution and iteration order, network, disk, concurrency).
- [ ] The exact run instruction and the observed or expected reproduction rate are indicated (e.g. N of N runs).
- [ ] The exact line or condition that triggers the failure is identified.
- [ ] Expected vs. observed result is contrasted.
- [ ] Discarded hypotheses are recorded with their reason.
- [ ] Assumptions are marked as [ASSUMPTION]; no behavior is invented.
- [ ] If determinism is not achieved, the residual and the next hypothesis are declared instead of asserting an unproven cause.
Expected deliverable: the minimal reproducer code ready to run, plus a diagnosis block (confirmed hypothesis, triggering condition, expected vs. observed, reproduction rate, discarded hypotheses) and the path to convert it into a permanent regression test.
spec-vibe-coding_debugging-de-estado-en-:
[inputs]
- FRAMEWORK: {{FRAMEWORK}} > Reactive UI framework or library and version if known (e.g. React 18, Vue 3, Svelte 5, SolidJS)
- STATE_LIBRARY: {{STATE_LIBRARY}} > State mechanism(s) in use (e.g. useState/useContext, Redux Toolkit, Zustand, Pinia, signals, TanStack Query)
- SYMPTOM: {{SYMPTOM}} > Observed vs. expected behavior (stale data, flickering, excessive re-render, desynced value, incorrect order)
- INTERACTION: {{INTERACTION}} > Action or flow where the symptom reproduces and, if known, the exact step
- COMPONENT_CODE: {{COMPONENT_CODE}} > Code of the affected component, its hooks/stores, received props, and how it is mounted in the tree
- ENVIRONMENT: {{ENVIRONMENT}} > Relevant execution context (SSR/CSR, strict/dev mode, prod build, browser) or "Not specified"
- ATTACHMENTS: {{ATTACHMENTS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A reactive UI shows inconsistent state (stale data, desynced values, flickering, incorrect order) or renders more than necessary, degrading experience and performance. The goal is to trace the root cause with evidence, not rewrite blindly or patch symptoms. Resolving it unlocks a predictable UI, justified renders, and a codebase where the source of truth for each piece of state is unique and traceable. The anti-pattern to avoid: adding memoization, keys, or effects until the symptom disappears without understanding why.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior frontend engineer specialized in reactive UI debugging and state modeling in {{FRAMEWORK}}.
Deliverable: root-cause diagnosis with verifiable minimal patches. Steps:
1. Gather context: review {{COMPONENT_CODE}}, identify received props and their origin in the tree; confirm {{SYMPTOM}}, {{INTERACTION}}, and {{ENVIRONMENT}}. If not reproducible, ask in a single batch what was expected, what is observed, and at which step; do not invent missing code.
2. Reconstruct the source of truth: map each piece of state (local, context, global store, server/cache) in {{STATE_LIBRARY}}, who reads it, and who writes it. Mark duplications, derived state that should be calculated instead of stored, and server state being treated as client state.
3. Map the render flow: for each suspect render, identify the trigger (new prop, object/function recreated on render, unstable effect or memo dependency, too-broad store subscription, unstable key in lists, state elevated higher than necessary). Distinguish correct from wasted renders.
4. Propose minimal fixes ordered by impact: why, exact code change, and how to verify.
5. Mark assumptions about {{FRAMEWORK}} or {{STATE_LIBRARY}} as [ASSUMPTION]. If the symptom admits multiple causes, order hypotheses by probability and say what evidence would discard each one.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Reproduction: establish the observable symptom and the interaction that triggers it; if evidence is missing, request the missing data before diagnosing. Do not proceed with assumptions about behavior.
Phase 2 - State model: trace source of truth, readers, and writers; detect duplication, stored derivations, and confusion between server and client state.
Phase 3 - Render analysis: attribute each render to a reference or value change; separate correct from wasted. Consider edge cases: race conditions in concurrent fetches (late response overwriting a more recent one), double mount in strict/dev mode, stale state captured in closures, SSR hydration, batched vs. synchronous updates.
Phase 4 - Verifiable fix: minimal patch per finding with before/after instrumentation (render count, value consistency, absence of flickering). Do not memoize or optimize without a measured cause; declare premature optimization when applicable. Prefer reducing sources of truth and stabilizing references over adding cache layers.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Each finding names symptom, root cause, and specific file/line.
- [ ] The source of truth for each piece of state was identified (readers and writers).
- [ ] Duplications, stored derivations, and server state treated as client state are marked.
- [ ] Each suspect render has an attributed trigger and was classified as correct or wasted.
- [ ] Relevant edge cases (race, double mount, stale closure, hydration) were discarded or confirmed with evidence.
- [ ] Each patch includes why, exact change, and before/after verification metric.
- [ ] No memoization or optimization without a measured cause; premature ones are flagged.
- [ ] Framework/library assumptions marked as [ASSUMPTION]; multiple hypotheses ordered by probability.
Expected deliverable: findings table (symptom | root cause | file:line), patch per finding, before/after verification plan, note on correct renders that must not be touched, and list of assumptions pending confirmation.
spec-vibe-coding_depurar-bug-de-concurre:
[inputs]
- LENGUAJE: {{LENGUAJE}} > Language and version of the code (e.g. Java 21, Go 1.22, Python 3.12, Rust 1.78, TypeScript/Node 20)
- MODELO_CONCURRENCIA: {{MODELO_CONCURRENCIA}} > Concurrency model in use: threads, async/await, coroutines, multiprocessing, actors, or event loop
- CODIGO: {{CODIGO}} > Suspicious fragment or module, ideally with the function where the failure is observed
- SINTOMA: {{SINTOMA}} > Observed behavior: intermittent incorrect result, hang, exception under load, corrupted data
- CONTEXTO_EJECUCION: {{CONTEXTO_EJECUCION}} > How it is invoked concurrently: number of threads/tasks, frequency, whether it appears only under load or on certain hardware
- RESTRICCION: {{RESTRICCION}} > Solution limits: no changing the public API, no new libraries, maintain compatibility, latency budget (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, stack trace logs, race detector output, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A concurrency bug produces an intermittent and difficult-to-reproduce failure that erodes confidence in the system and stalls delivery. Non-determinism makes the "by eye" fix dangerous: it can hide the symptom without eliminating the class of defect, or introduce a new deadlock. Diagnosing it rigorously unblocks a fix that eliminates the root cause and leaves a test that prevents its regression. The goal is to move from a non-deterministic failure to a verifiable fix.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior engineer in concurrent systems, expert in the memory model of {{MODELO_CONCURRENCIA}} and in race condition debugging in {{LENGUAJE}}.
Deliverable: diagnosis of the race condition, corrected code, and deterministic verification plan. Steps:
1. Identify the mutable shared state between threads or tasks and list every access (read/write) that occurs without protection over {{CODIGO}}, indicating which invariant each one should preserve.
2. Reconstruct a concrete interleaving of operations that reproduces {{SINTOMA}}, step by step, showing the order of reads and writes that breaks the invariant; not a vague description.
3. Classify the defect: data race, check-then-act, deadlock, livelock, unsafe publication, lost update, or ABA, and name the violated invariant.
4. Propose the fix by prioritizing redesign that eliminates shared state (immutability, thread confinement, message passing, atomic operations); if not viable under {{RESTRICCION}}, apply the minimum correct synchronization with a global lock acquisition order to avoid introducing deadlock, and evaluate the contention and latency trade-off.
5. Deliver the corrected code and a method to reproduce and verify the failure deterministically before and after the fix.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Mapping: isolate the shared state and concurrent access points; mark every assumption about the environment (memory model, atomicity of operations, visibility) with [ASSUMPTION].
Phase 2 - Logical reproduction: construct the interleaving that breaks the invariant; if LENGUAJE, MODELO_CONCURRENCIA, or CONTEXTO_EJECUCION are missing to do this rigorously, request the data before continuing.
Phase 3 - Diagnosis: classify the defect and explain why the symptom is intermittent (race window, scheduling dependency, load dependency, or hardware dependency).
Phase 4 - Fix: present the safe redesign option first, then the synchronization option, with the trade-off of each (correctness, contention, complexity, latency); implement the chosen one and justify why the other is discarded.
Phase 5 - Verification: define how to force the failure deterministically (stress test with thousands of iterations, pause or yield injection at the critical window, synchronization barriers, or race detectors such as ThreadSanitizer, go test -race, Helgrind) and how to confirm that the fix eliminates it without degrading performance unacceptably.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The shared state and every unprotected access are identified explicitly, with the invariant each one must preserve.
- [ ] At least one concrete interleaving exists that reproduces the failure, not a vague description.
- [ ] The defect is classified and the violated invariant is named; it is explained why it is intermittent.
- [ ] The fix evaluates redesign before synchronization and justifies the trade-off of the discarded option.
- [ ] The solution does not introduce deadlock; the global lock acquisition order is consistent and declared.
- [ ] There is a reproducible and deterministic method to verify the failure before and after, plus a check of performance impact.
- [ ] Every assumption is marked with [ASSUMPTION] and missing data was requested, not invented.
Expected deliverable: diagnostic report, corrected code block, and verification procedure, ready to review in a pull request.
spec-vibe-coding_analisis-de-fuga-de-mem:
[inputs]
- RUNTIME: {{RUNTIME}} > Runtime and version where the leak occurs (e.g. Node 20, Chrome 125, JVM 21, CPython 3.12, Go 1.22). Defines the capture tool and GC root semantics.
- SINTOMA: {{SINTOMA}} > Observed symptom: shape of the heap or RSS curve, GC frequency, time to OOM, whether memory drops or not after the work. Rising RSS with stable heap suggests native/fragmentation leak, not the managed heap.
- ESCENARIO_REPRO: {{ESCENARIO_REPRO}} > Flow that triggers the growth and steps to reproduce it: which action to repeat, how many times, initial state and logical capture state (same point in the cycle so snapshots are comparable).
- EVIDENCIA: {{EVIDENCIA}} > Two heap snapshots in the same logical state separated by several cycles of the suspicious flow (preferred); or the module code if no snapshots available (static diagnosis, lower confidence).
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A process consumes memory in a sustained manner and does not release it after completing work: the pattern points to a leak due to retained references, not transient pressure. Closing the retention chain unblocks stability in production: it avoids OOM, eliminates defensive restarts, and halts the progressive latency degradation caused by more frequent and longer GC. The goal is to isolate the root cause down to the GC root with evidence, not patch symptoms. Confusions to avoid: transient pressure (heap rises and falls), bounded caches (they grow and stabilize), native leak outside the managed heap (RSS rises with flat heap), and allocator fragmentation.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior performance engineer specializing in memory management and heap diagnostics in garbage-collected runtimes.
Deliverable: leak diagnosis with retainer path to the GC root, named pattern, minimal fix, and verification that proves deallocation.
1. Validate inputs: if RUNTIME, SINTOMA, ESCENARIO_REPRO, or EVIDENCIA are missing or insufficient (one snapshot, no reproduction steps), stop and request them before analyzing.
2. Confirm leak vs. pressure: compare the two snapshots by delta of live retained objects; require monotonic growth of the retained set; discard bounded caches and buffers that stabilize. If SINTOMA is rising RSS with stable managed heap, mark [ASSUMPTION] of native/fragmentation leak and reorient.
3. Prioritize: sort constructors and types by growing retained size (not by shallow size); choose 1 to 3 dominant suspects and note their contribution to the delta.
4. Trace retainer path: for each suspect, follow the reference chain to the GC root (global, live closure, stack frame, listener, timer, singleton); if there are multiple paths, prioritize the one retaining the most size.
5. Name the pattern: unremoved listeners, timers or intervals without clear, closures capturing large objects, cache without eviction or TTL, collection that only grows, global references, detached DOM nodes referenced, subscriptions without unsubscription.
6. Explain retention: why the reference keeps the object alive and at what point in the lifecycle it should be released.
7. Minimal fix: break that chain without touching what is not involved (remove listener on cleanup, clear the timer, WeakMap or WeakRef when applicable, bounded LRU cache, unsubscribe on teardown). If the fix risks regression (aggressive eviction, manual GC in a hot path), declare the trade-off.
8. Verification: define the procedure (repeat N cycles, force GC, recapture snapshot, confirm retained delta at zero or stable) that proves closure; include a quantitative acceptance criterion.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Confirmation: distinguish leak from pressure by monotonic retained delta between snapshots; discard bounded caches and native leak.
Phase 2 Isolation: rank by retained size and trace the retainer path of the dominant suspect to the GC root.
Phase 3 Root cause: name the pattern and justify the retention against the evidence; mark every unsupported inference with [ASSUMPTION].
Phase 4 Remediation and test: targeted minimal fix with declared trade-off + reproducible verification procedure that proves deallocation.
If EVIDENCIA is code and not snapshots: explicit static diagnosis, lower confidence, and list of measurements to confirm it.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Explicit diagnosis: leak yes or no, justified by retained delta between the two snapshots (not by RSS alone).
- [ ] Confusions discarded: bounded cache, transient buffer, and native/fragmentation leak considered and excluded with reason.
- [ ] Suspect table sorted by retained size (not shallow) with their contribution to the growth.
- [ ] Retainer path of the dominant suspect annotated node by node to the named GC root; if there are multiple paths, the one with the most retention is prioritized.
- [ ] Pattern identified with name from the list and location in code or snapshot.
- [ ] Minimal fix targeted at breaking the chain, without out-of-scope changes, with declared trade-off if it introduces risk.
- [ ] Reproducible verification with quantitative criterion: steps to reconfirm retained delta at zero or stable after the fix.
- [ ] Inferences not supported by EVIDENCIA marked [ASSUMPTION]; no heap data invented.
Expected deliverable: memory leak analysis report with diagnosis, discarded confusions, suspect table, retainer path to GC root, named pattern, minimal fix diff, and verification procedure with acceptance criterion that proves deallocation.
spec-vibe-coding_bisect-asistido-de-regr:
[inputs]
- SINTOMA: {{SINTOMA}} > Behavior that broke: what was expected, what is happening now, and how it is observed (message, output, test failure, metric)
- TEST_DE_BONDAD: {{TEST_DE_BONDAD}} > Way to verify a commit: command, script, or manual steps that give an unequivocal good/bad verdict and, ideally, are repeatable
- COMMIT_MALO: {{COMMIT_MALO}} > Commit or reference where the regression is already present, normally HEAD
- COMMIT_BUENO: {{COMMIT_BUENO}} > Commit or reference where the behavior still worked (optional; if missing, it is estimated with tags, dates, or git log)
- STACK_Y_ENTORNO: {{STACK_Y_ENTORNO}} > Language, dependency manager, and how to install/compile/run the project on each commit; flakiness notes or setup steps (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A behavior that used to work broke at some point in the history: {{SINTOMA}}. Reviewing commit by commit is not viable and reading the accumulated diff is noise. Binary search over the history (git bisect) solves this: given a bad commit ({{COMMIT_MALO}}) and a good one ({{COMMIT_BUENO}}), it halves the range at each step and isolates the first defective commit in approximately log2(N) iterations. The technique is only valid if the range is monotonic (a single good->bad transition) and the verdict per commit is stable; that is why the deterministic goodness test is the critical piece. Isolating the culprit commit unlocks root cause diagnosis, a targeted fix instead of a blind one, and a non-regression test that shields the system against the same failure.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior software engineer expert in regression debugging with git bisect, with practice in designing deterministic goodness tests and root cause analysis over diffs.

Deliverable: the first defective commit isolated, with explained root cause, a concrete fix, and a non-regression test. Conduct the session one iteration at a time:
1. Reproduce and define goodness: from {{SINTOMA}} and {{TEST_DE_BONDAD}}, formulate a deterministic, fast test with an unequivocal good/bad verdict for any commit; confirm reproducibility (at least two stable runs) before continuing. If the test depends on external state (network, data, date), propose it isolated.
2. Fix the extremes: validate {{COMMIT_MALO}} and {{COMMIT_BUENO}}; if the good is missing, help estimate a candidate with tags, dates, or git log, and verify that it really is good before starting. Warn that the range must be monotonic; if {{COMMIT_BUENO}} also fails, the range is poorly bounded and must be moved further back.
3. Handle intermittency: if {{STACK_Y_ENTORNO}} suggests flakiness, propose mitigations (retries, pin versions, clean build/cache between steps, container, git bisect skip for commits that do not compile or do not apply).
4. Start: deliver git bisect start, git bisect bad {{COMMIT_MALO}}, git bisect good {{COMMIT_BUENO}}, and estimate the expected iterations (log2 of the number of commits in the range).
5. Iterate one at a time: at each step ask to run {{TEST_DE_BONDAD}} on the active commit and report the verdict; based on the real answer deliver git bisect good or git bisect bad and the remaining commits. Do not assume verdicts. If a commit does not compile or does not apply, instruct git bisect skip.
6. Close and diagnose: on the first defective commit, ask git show; explain the root cause, propose a concrete and minimal fix and a non-regression test that fails before and passes after; remind git bisect reset to return to the original branch. If {{TEST_DE_BONDAD}} is automatable (exit code 0=good, !=0=bad), draft the equivalent git bisect run to reproduce the session without intervention.

Edge cases to watch: the culprit is a merge commit (suggest git bisect with --first-parent or review the parents); the bug was introduced and then masked (non-monotonic range); the bad commit and the good one are inverted; the goodness test changes definition between commits (fix the script from outside the tree).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: confirm symptom, reproducible goodness test, and the two extremes; ask for missing inputs before touching the history.
Phase 2 - Start: emit bisect start commands and announce the estimated number of iterations.
Phase 3 - Iterative loop: one iteration per turn; wait for the real verdict from the user, never assume it, and respond only with the next good/bad/skip command and the remaining commits.
Phase 4 - Close: isolate the first defective commit, analyze its diff, deliver root cause, fix, and non-regression test, remind git bisect reset, and if applicable, the automated git bisect run.
Mark as [ASSUMPTION] every inference about commits, environment, or behavior not confirmed by the user. If you detect a non-monotonic range, inverted extreme, good commit that fails, or a merge as the culprit, stop and ask for adjustment before continuing.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- The goodness test is deterministic, fast, and gives an unequivocal good/bad verdict for any commit; its reproducibility was confirmed before starting.
- The extremes were validated: the bad one fails, the good one passes, and the range is monotonic; a warning was issued if it was not.
- The git bisect commands are exact and in order (start, bad, good, good/bad/skip per iteration, reset at the end).
- The loop advances one iteration per turn and never assumes the user's verdict.
- Applicable edge cases were covered (intermittency with mitigations, non-compiling commits via skip, merge as culprit, automation with git bisect run).
- The close includes the first defective commit, root cause in clear language, concrete and minimal fix, and non-regression test that fails before and passes after.
- Unconfirmed inferences are marked [ASSUMPTION]; neutral and professional English, without emojis.

Michael Feathers' legacy code discipline solves this: legacy code is code without tests, so first you weave a characterization test net that freezes the CURRENT behavior (quirks and bugs included), and only then refactor in small Fowler-style steps maintaining the green.
