[inputs]
- FUENTE: {{FUENTE}} > Source system or table whose schema is evolving (e.g., "checkout events, Kafka topic orders.v1")
- MOTOR_INGESTION: {{MOTOR_INGESTION}} > Pipeline engine (e.g., Spark Structured Streaming, dbt, Fivetran, Flink, Kafka Connect)
- FORMATO_DATOS: {{FORMATO_DATOS}} > Serialized format at source and destination (e.g., Avro at source, Parquet/Iceberg at destination)
- DESTINO: {{DESTINO}} > Target layer and technology (e.g., Iceberg lakehouse, Snowflake warehouse, bronze/silver layer)
- POLITICA_COMPATIBILIDAD: {{POLITICA_COMPATIBILIDAD}} > Desired policy (backward, forward, full, or transitive) and critical consumers to protect
- CAMBIOS_PROPUESTOS: {{CAMBIOS_PROPUESTOS}} > List of changes to evaluate: new columns, renames, type changes (optional; if missing, the AI asks for the schema diff before classifying)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A source feeding an ingestion pipeline is going to change its schema and the team needs to absorb new columns, renames, and type changes without breaking downstream consumers or blindly reprocessing history. The goal is to unblock continuous source changes with a data-contract discipline that makes evolution predictable, versioned, and auditable, avoiding silently corrupt load incidents and accumulated schema debt.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior data engineer specializing in ingestion platforms and data contracts, with expertise in Avro/Protobuf schema evolution rules, schema registry, and bronze/silver/gold modeling.
Deliverable: an actionable and versioned schema evolution strategy for {{FUENTE}} on {{MOTOR_INGESTION}} ({{FORMATO_DATOS}} toward {{DESTINO}}), under policy {{POLITICA_COMPATIBILIDAD}}. Steps:
1. Classify each change in {{CAMBIOS_PROPUESTOS}} as backward-compatible, forward-compatible, or breaking applying Avro/Protobuf rules; declare for each one what breaks and which consumer is affected. Mark with [ASSUMPTION] any inference about consumers, volumes, or undeclared environments.
2. Define handling rules by type: new columns with explicit default and tolerance for absence; renames via alias/field mapping instead of DROP+ADD (which loses data and resets lineage); type changes distinguishing safe promotions (int to long, int to string, adding a union member) from unsafe conversions (string to int, narrowing, precision change) that require a shadow column and controlled backfill.
3. Draft the versioned data contract: a concrete example schema, responsible owner, semantic version MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH (MAJOR=breaking, MINOR=additive compatible, PATCH=metadata), compatibility policy, and a dated deprecation window for retired fields.
4. Design verifiable enforcement: validation against the schema registry in CI and at runtime, dead-letter quarantine for records that violate the contract with their reprocessing criterion, and drift detection between the actual source schema and the declared contract.
5. Deliver the version promotion runbook and the reversible rollback plan, with intermediate dual-write/dual-read states and the cutover criterion when applicable.
Edge cases to cover: field from nullable to required; field reordering in positional formats; enum with a new value that an old consumer does not recognize; change of timezone or unit in a field without renaming it (semantically invisible change to the schema). State the trade-off between adoption speed and safety for each relevant decision (e.g., dual-write doubles temporary storage but eliminates the inconsistency window).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Interpret: restate source, engine, format, destination, policy, and consumers to protect; list what is missing. If {{CAMBIOS_PROPUESTOS}} is empty or there is no schema diff, ask for it before classifying; do not invent the content of the change.
Phase 2 - Plan: present the plan (classification > rules > contract > enforcement > runbook) and assumptions before generating artifacts.
Phase 3 - Execute: produce the classification tables, the versioned data contract (with concrete schema), the enforcement design, and the runbook with rollback.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The three change types (new columns, renames, type changes) each have an explicit rule and a concrete schema example.
- [ ] Each change is classified as backward/forward/breaking with justification per Avro/Protobuf rules and which consumer it breaks.
- [ ] Renames are resolved with alias/mapping, never DROP+ADD that loses data or lineage.
- [ ] Type changes distinguish safe promotion from unsafe conversion (shadow column/backfill).
- [ ] The contract declares schema, owner, semantic version with its bump rule, compatibility policy, and a dated deprecation window.
- [ ] Verifiable enforcement exists: schema registry (CI and runtime), dead-letter quarantine with reprocessing criterion, and drift detection.
- [ ] The runbook includes promotion steps and a reversible rollback plan with dual-write/dual-read states and cutover criterion.
- [ ] Applicable edge cases (nullable to required, positional reordering, new enum, semantic unit/TZ change) are addressed or discarded with a reason.
- [ ] All inferences about consumers or undeclared environments are marked [ASSUMPTION], and speed-vs-safety trade-offs are explicit.
Expected deliverable: a document with classification and rules tables, an example versioned data contract, the enforcement design, and a promotion + rollback runbook, ready for review by the contract owner.
spec-datos_etl_normalizar_json_anidado:
[inputs]
- JSON_FUENTE: {{JSON_FUENTE}} > JSON document to normalize: a representative sample or schema, with enough records to detect structural variations (optional fields, mixed types, empty vs. absent arrays)
- MOTOR_DESTINO: {{MOTOR_DESTINO}} > Target engine or dialect that determines the DDL, the flattening function, and the UPSERT options (PostgreSQL, BigQuery, Snowflake, SQL Server, SQLite) (optional, default: portable ANSI SQL with per-engine notes)
- CLAVE_PRIMARIA: {{CLAVE_PRIMARIA}} > Field or combination from the JSON that stably identifies each root record; if it does not exist or is not unique/non-null, a deterministic surrogate key is generated (optional)
- ESTRATEGIA_ARRAYS: {{ESTRATEGIA_ARRAYS}} > How to handle arrays: normalized child table (default), bridge table for scalar arrays, or denormalize to columns only if cardinality is fixed and low (optional, default: normalized child table)
- CONVENCION_NOMBRES: {{CONVENCION_NOMBRES}} > Table and column naming convention: snake_case with path separator, entity prefix, singular/plural, engine identifier length limit (optional, default: snake_case with underscore as path separator)
- MODO_CARGA: {{MODO_CARGA}} > Load strategy: full reload, incremental by UPSERT (merge key), or append-only with batch marker; determines idempotency and reconciliation (optional, default: incremental by UPSERT)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I have data in {{JSON_FUENTE}} with nested objects and arrays that a relational engine cannot query directly with plain SQL. I need to unpack it into a relational tabular model, normalized, traceable, and repeatably loadable, for {{MOTOR_DESTINO}}. Flattening and normalization (Codd's normal forms, up to 3NF) convert nested paths into columns, arrays into 1:N parent-child relationships governed by primary and foreign keys, and produce a schema that is indexable and queryable. A good model unlocks analytical queries without parse-at-read-time, reliable joins, referential integrity, efficient partitioning, idempotent loads, and an auditable lineage between source and store. The real challenge is not just flattening: it is handling schema variability across records, type ambiguities, and load repeatability without duplicating or losing rows.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior data engineer specializing in relational modeling and semi-structured data transformation, with practice in JSON flattening, normalization (Codd's normal forms), and each engine's native functions (JSON_TABLE, lateral flatten, UNNEST, OPENJSON).

Deliverable: a complete relational tabular model derived from {{JSON_FUENTE}}, with its DDL, transformation logic, lineage, and load plan. Steps:
1. Profile the structure: traverse {{JSON_FUENTE}} and build a path tree; for each node declare type (object, array of objects, array of scalars, array of arrays, scalar), cardinality, nullability, and depth; report schema inconsistencies across records: optional fields, mixed types at the same path, JSON null vs. absent key, empty arrays vs. absent arrays, numbers encoded as strings, booleans as 0/1/"true", and dates with heterogeneous formats or timezones.
2. Partition into tables: flatten each 1:1 object into columns of the same table using path notation and {{CONVENCION_NOMBRES}}; convert each array of objects into a 1:N child table; resolve arrays of scalars per {{ESTRATEGIA_ARRAYS}}; decompose each array of arrays into successive levels of child tables. Respect the engine's identifier length limit.
3. Define keys: use {{CLAVE_PRIMARIA}} as the root entity key only if it is stable, non-null, and unique in the sample; if not, generate a deterministic surrogate derived from the business identity (not the entire document, so that reprocessing does not change it); propagate the parent foreign key to each child; retain the array position index as part of the child key when order matters; declare the merge key that will make the load idempotent.
4. Normalize to 3NF: eliminate repeating groups (1NF), partial dependencies (2NF), and transitive dependencies (3NF); flag points where denormalization is advisable by query pattern and justify it with the trade-off (faster reads vs. risk of update anomaly).
5. Map types: infer the SQL type of each column (integer, decimal with precision and scale, text, boolean, date/time with or without timezone in ISO 8601, native JSON for irreducible residuals) according to {{MOTOR_DESTINO}}; define the NULL policy (absent key and JSON null map to NULL unless otherwise specified); flag ambiguous ones.
6. Deliver: CREATE TABLE DDL per table with PK, FK, UNIQUE, NOT NULL, and CHECK; transformation logic to populate it (native SQL for {{MOTOR_DESTINO}} or pseudocode if portable) consistent with {{MODO_CARGA}} and idempotent; a textual entity-relationship diagram; a lineage map linking each {{JSON_FUENTE}} path to its destination column; and reconciliation queries that compare row counts and control sums between source and destination to detect losses or duplicates.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Profiling: path inventory, types, cardinalities, depth, and schema anomalies over the sample.
Phase 2 Logical design: entity tree, table decisions, and identification of 1:1, 1:N, and N:N (bridge) relationships.
Phase 3 Physical design: keys (natural or deterministic surrogate), merge keys, types, constraints, and 3NF normalization with notes on deliberate denormalization.
Phase 4 Materialization: DDL, idempotent transformation logic per {{MODO_CARGA}}, entity-relationship diagram, lineage map, and reconciliation queries. All type, cardinality, or key inferences not confirmed by {{JSON_FUENTE}} are marked [ASSUMPTION].
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- Every path in the JSON appears exactly once in the lineage map, mapped to a column or explicitly discarded with a reason.
- Every table has a primary key; every child table has the parent's foreign key and retains array order when applicable; each child has its merge key declared.
- No array of objects was flattened into columns (avoids repeating groups); no repeated entity was left duplicated without separating; arrays of arrays are decomposed, not collapsed.
- The model meets 3NF or documents and justifies each deliberate deviation by query with its trade-off.
- Each column has a valid SQL type in {{MOTOR_DESTINO}} and a defined NULL policy; absent key and JSON null are distinguished if the business requires it; inferences without evidence are marked [ASSUMPTION].
- The DDL is executable in {{MOTOR_DESTINO}}; the transformation logic is idempotent per {{MODO_CARGA}} (re-executing does not duplicate or lose rows) and produces the expected rows from {{JSON_FUENTE}}.
- The reconciliation queries match counts and control sums source vs. destination.
Expected deliverable: profiling tree with anomalies, set of tables with DDL (PK/FK/UNIQUE/CHECK), idempotent transformation logic populating each table, textual entity-relationship diagram, path-to-column lineage map, reconciliation queries, and list of assumptions.
spec-datos_etl_arquitectura_medallion:
[inputs]
- MOTOR_LAKEHOUSE: {{MOTOR_LAKEHOUSE}} > Lakehouse engine and table format (e.g., Databricks Delta Lake, Apache Iceberg on Spark, Snowflake, BigQuery)
- DOMINIOS_DATOS: {{DOMINIOS_DATOS}} > Domains or sources to model and their load type: batch, CDC, or streaming (e.g., daily batch sales, CDC customers, streaming web events)
- SLA_FRESCURA: {{SLA_FRESCURA}} > Maximum acceptable latency per layer (e.g., bronze near real-time, silver 1h, gold daily)
- HERRAMIENTA_ORQUESTACION: {{HERRAMIENTA_ORQUESTACION}} > Orchestrator and quality tool (e.g., Airflow + dbt + Great Expectations) (optional)
- POLITICA_CALIDAD: {{POLITICA_CALIDAD}} > How to handle records that fail a gate: quarantine, hard reject, or alert and continue; with who receives the alert if applicable (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Structuring the medallion architecture of a lakehouse so that each layer has unambiguous responsibilities and the promotion of data between bronze, silver, and gold is predictable, auditable, and reproducible. Purpose: unlock reliable analytical consumption by avoiding three costly anti-patterns: business logic leaking into bronze (breaks reprocessing), silver accumulating duplicates (corrupts metrics), gold serving data without quality guarantees (erodes trust). The result is an architecture contract that a data team implements directly on {{MOTOR_LAKEHOUSE}} for domains {{DOMINIOS_DATOS}}, with freshness {{SLA_FRESCURA}}.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior data engineer specializing in lakehouse architectures and the medallion pattern, with experience in data quality contracts and data governance.
Deliverable: an actionable medallion architecture contract. Components:
1. Table per layer (bronze, silver, gold): purpose, owner, physical format, granularity, retention, and schema policy (schema-on-read vs. enforced). No overlap of responsibilities.
2. Promotion rules bronze->silver and silver->gold: transformations applied, deduplication, conforming of dimensions and facts, null handling, and business rules per hop. Declare what does NOT happen in each layer (no business logic in bronze; no presentation-level aggregation in silver).
3. Quality gate matrix per layer: schema validations, referential integrity, freshness (per SLA_FRESCURA), completeness, and uniqueness; each gate with its trigger threshold and action on failure per POLITICA_CALIDAD (quarantine / reject / alert). If HERRAMIENTA_ORQUESTACION is provided, express each gate as an assertion implementable in it.
4. Engineering guarantees per layer: load idempotency, reprocessing and backfill strategy, schema evolution handling (new column, type change, rename), partitioning and ordering, anchored to real mechanisms of MOTOR_LAKEHOUSE (MERGE, time travel, OPTIMIZE).
5. Lineage model: traceability between layers and minimum metadata per table (source, ingestion timestamp, schema version, run id, control hash) that allows a gold record to be traced back to bronze.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Interpret: confirm MOTOR_LAKEHOUSE, DOMINIOS_DATOS (with load type: batch/CDC/streaming), SLA_FRESCURA, HERRAMIENTA_ORQUESTACION, and POLITICA_CALIDAD. If a key piece of data is missing, request it; anything unconfirmed is marked [ASSUMPTION]. Do not assert engine capabilities (MERGE, time travel, schema enforcement) without certainty: declare them [ASSUMPTION] to validate.
Phase 2 - Design layers: define the table per layer anchored to the real engine capabilities.
Phase 3 - Define promotions and gates: specify transformations, deduplication, and validations per hop, mapping each gate to its threshold and action on failure.
Phase 4 - Close engineering and lineage: idempotency, reprocessing, schema evolution, partitioning, metadata, and traceability.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- The three layers have purpose, owner, format, granularity, retention, and schema policy, with no overlap of responsibilities.
- Each promotion rule explicitly declares what is done and what is NOT done in that layer.
- Bronze preserves immutable raw data; no business rule is applied before silver.
- Each quality gate has a trigger threshold and a concrete action on failure consistent with POLITICA_CALIDAD; if HERRAMIENTA_ORQUESTACION was provided, the gate is expressible as an assertion in it.
- Idempotency, reprocessing, and schema evolution are resolved with engine mechanisms (MERGE, time travel, OPTIMIZE), not generic ones.
- Lineage allows tracing a gold record back to its origin in bronze.
- Handling declared for late-arriving data and historical partition reprocessing without duplication.
- Unverified engine capabilities marked [ASSUMPTION]; no prices or invented data.
Expected deliverable: medallion architecture contract document with layer table, promotion rules table, quality gate matrix with thresholds and actions, engineering guarantees per layer, and lineage model, ready to implement on {{MOTOR_LAKEHOUSE}}.
spec-datos_etl_costo_optimizacion:
[inputs]
- PIPELINE: {{PIPELINE}} > Name and one-line description of the pipeline to optimize (purpose, layers, consumption outputs)
- PLATAFORMA_MOTOR: {{PLATAFORMA_MOTOR}} > Cloud and query/transformation engine (columnar warehouse, engine on data lake, orchestrator) and billing model if known (by bytes scanned, by slots/compute-hours, by storage and tier)
- VOLUMEN_DATOS: {{VOLUMEN_DATOS}} > Total volume and per critical table, growth, and current partition/storage format
- PATRONES_CONSULTA: {{PATRONES_CONSULTA}} > Most frequent or costly queries and jobs, dominant filter columns, and consumption SLAs
- COSTO_ACTUAL: {{COSTO_ACTUAL}} > Known cost breakdown by stage or service (compute vs. storage), or top queries/jobs by spend (optional)
- FRESCURA_REQUERIDA: {{FRESCURA_REQUERIDA}} > Data latency tolerated per table or layer (real-time, hourly, daily) (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
The compute and storage cost of {{PIPELINE}} on {{PLATAFORMA_MOTOR}} is growing faster than the value it delivers, and I need to cut it without degrading freshness or correctness. In analytical platforms, spend concentrates in a few high-leverage vectors: bytes scanned per query, recomputation of data that has not changed, and poorly structured storage. Tackling them with FinOps discipline (partition pruning and predicate pushdown, compressed columnar format with compaction, and incremental materialization) unlocks sustained savings, faster jobs, a predictable cost base, and freed capacity for new workloads, without rewriting the platform.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior data engineer with practice in FinOps and optimization of analytical cloud platforms (columnar warehouses and data lakes on object storage), who separates compute and storage drivers before touching anything and declares the assumed billing model.

Deliverable: an actionable and validatable cost optimization plan for {{PIPELINE}}. Steps:
1. Diagnosis per stage: map ingestion, transformation, materialization, and consumption; for each one identify the dominant cost driver from {{COSTO_ACTUAL}} (bytes scanned, compute-hours or slots, storage volume and tier, reprocessing of unchanged data) and explicitly separate compute from storage. Apply 80/20 to isolate the few vectors that concentrate spend.
2. Partition pruning and predicate pushdown: against {{PATRONES_CONSULTA}}, verify that critical tables are partitioned by the dominant filter column (typically event date) with the appropriate granularity, without over-partitioning that generates too many small files; confirm that filters land on the partition column (not on an expression or function that disables it) so the engine discards partitions and scans fewer bytes.
3. Columnar format and compaction: if there is CSV/JSON or poorly organized Parquet in {{VOLUMEN_DATOS}}, convert to compressed columnar (Parquet or ORC) to read only the necessary columns; compact small files to a target size (order of hundreds of MB) and apply clustering or sort by frequent filter columns to maximize data skipping.
4. Selective materialization: per table, decide between view, incremental materialization (only the new/modified delta), or full-refresh based on change frequency, recomputation cost, and {{FRESCURA_REQUERIDA}}; eliminate intermediate materializations that no consumer uses. Define the delta key (update timestamp or version) and how to handle late-arriving data and backfills.
5. Storage and retention: move cold or historical data to lower-cost tiers in {{PLATAFORMA_MOTOR}} and define expiration/retention of temporary and staging tables.
6. Prioritize levers in a table (estimated savings vs. effort vs. impact on freshness/risk) and deliver the concrete changes: partitioning DDL, query rewrites, materialization configuration, and tiering policies. Mark [ASSUMPTION] on all unconfirmed data.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Framing: confirm engine, volume, query patterns, cost breakdown, and freshness; declare the billing model you assume; if an input is missing that would change the recommendation, ask for it before proposing; do not invent billing figures or assume an engine.
Phase 2 Diagnosis: attribute cost per stage separating compute from storage and flag the few vectors that concentrate spend (80/20 rule).
Phase 3 Lever design: apply in order partition pruning/pushdown, columnar format/compaction, selective materialization, and tiering; for each lever estimate savings relatively or per bytes/time (not in currency unless {{COSTO_ACTUAL}} allows it), declare its impact on freshness and risk, and name the metric that would confirm the savings (bytes scanned, files per partition, job time).
Phase 4 Plan and validation: prioritize by savings-effort-risk, specify concrete changes, and define how to validate result parity (counts, control sums, before/after output comparison) and the measured cost regression; include a rollback plan per lever.
Edge cases: if {{COSTO_ACTUAL}} is not broken down, infer the driver from {{PATRONES_CONSULTA}} and {{VOLUMEN_DATOS}} and mark it [ASSUMPTION]; if a cost lever conflicts with {{FRESCURA_REQUERIDA}} (e.g., incremental that delays real-time data), declare the trade-off and propose the alternative that respects the SLA; if the engine charges more for storage than compute, prioritize compaction, format, and tiering over pushdown.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- The diagnosis separates compute from storage, declares the assumed billing model, and attributes cost to specific stages and vectors (80/20), not to generalities.
- Each partitioning recommendation names the column and granularity, and verifies that {{PATRONES_CONSULTA}} filters activate it (no over-partitioning or small files).
- The format/compaction decision declares the target file size and clustering/sort columns.
- Materialization is decided table by table (view / incremental / full-refresh) justified against {{FRESCURA_REQUERIDA}} and recomputation cost, with a delta key and handling of late-arriving data/backfills; intermediates with no consumer are eliminated.
- Levers are prioritized by estimated savings vs. effort vs. impact on freshness/risk, each with the metric that would confirm the savings.
- There is a validation plan that checks result parity, measures cost regression, and defines rollback per lever; unconfirmed data is marked [ASSUMPTION] and no billing figures are invented.
Expected deliverable: a cost optimization plan with quantified diagnosis per stage, a prioritized lever table, concrete changes (partitioning DDL, query rewrites, materialization configuration, tiering policies), and a before/after validation protocol with rollback, ready to execute by sprints.
spec-datos_dashboard_diseno_ejecutivo:
[inputs]
- DECISION_NEGOCIO: {{DECISION_NEGOCIO}} > Business decision or question the dashboard must enable (e.g., "decide where to reallocate commercial budget each month")
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Who reads the dashboard and their expected level of detail (e.g., steering committee, middle management)
- FUENTE_DATOS: {{FUENTE_DATOS}} > Data origin and available metrics (e.g., CRM, ERP, consolidated spreadsheet; existing columns or KPIs)
- PERIODICIDAD: {{PERIODICIDAD}} > Dashboard review frequency (e.g., weekly in WBR, monthly in MBR)
- HERRAMIENTA: {{HERRAMIENTA}} > Target BI tool (e.g., Power BI, Looker Studio, Tableau, Metabase)
- RESTRICCIONES: {{RESTRICCIONES}} > (optional) Sensitive data, tool limits, or governance rules
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
An executive dashboard is not a report: it is a decision instrument. When a dashboard forces the reader to search for the answer, it fails. The goal is for {{AUDIENCIA}} to look at the screen and, in seconds, know the status, the cause, and the action linked to {{DECISION_NEGOCIO}}. Designing the hierarchy of 5-7 metrics and the layout well unlocks shorter meetings, faster decisions, and fewer disputes about which number is correct. This applies to the {{PERIODICIDAD}} cycle and will be implemented in {{HERRAMIENTA}}. The risk to avoid is the warehouse-dashboard: many charts, no decision.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior Business Intelligence and executive information design architect, with experience building dashboards for steering committees.
Deliverable: a dashboard specification ready to implement. Steps:
1. Translate {{DECISION_NEGOCIO}} into 3-5 business questions the dashboard answers in under 10 seconds, each with the action it unlocks for {{AUDIENCIA}} and the threshold that triggers that action.
2. Derive from those questions between 5 and 7 key metrics from {{FUENTE_DATOS}}. Per metric: name, exact formula, unit, frequency aligned to {{PERIODICIDAD}}, granularity and cut dimension, data owner, exact source, leading/lagging type, and numeric green/amber/red threshold. If you exceed 7, justify or cut. If a metric cannot be calculated from {{FUENTE_DATOS}}, mark it as a data gap and name a temporary proxy.
3. Design the visual hierarchy in three levels: BLUF headline at the top (status in one sentence + 1-3 critical KPIs), trends in the middle band, actionable detail and breakdowns at the bottom; apply Z or F reading pattern and justify which one based on the number of blocks.
4. Assign the correct chart type to each metric (KPI with delta vs. target, line for trend, bars for comparison, table for detail) and justify briefly; avoid pie charts with more than three categories and misleading dual axes.
5. Define the semantic palette (green/amber/red with numeric thresholds), a brand color for accents, and accessible contrast rules: minimum WCAG AA and state never encoded by color alone (add icon or label).
6. Deliver a wireframe in ASCII blocks or table with the position of each element, global filters, drill-down paths, and implementation notes for {{HERRAMIENTA}} respecting {{RESTRICCIONES}} (include refresh latency and sensitive data handling).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Decision: start from the business question, never from the available data; discard any metric that does not move a decision.
Phase 2 - Metrics: apply the 5-7 element principle (cognitive load limit); prioritize actionable over vanity metrics; pair each leading indicator with its lagging counterpart when applicable; explicitly declare data gaps.
Phase 3 - Hierarchy and layout: order by descending importance per Z/F pattern; critical items top-left; group by affinity; define how the dashboard looks with no data and in case of source error.
Phase 4 - Visual encoding: choose encoding by data type (trend=line, comparison=bar, limited part-to-whole, status=KPI with delta); minimize non-data ink; fix axis scales from zero unless justified.
Phase 5 - Validation: test the dashboard against the Phase 1 questions, against accessibility, and against governance; confirm each KPI has an owner and that no sensitive data is exposed outside {{RESTRICCIONES}}.
If {{DECISION_NEGOCIO}}, {{AUDIENCIA}}, {{FUENTE_DATOS}}, {{PERIODICIDAD}}, or {{HERRAMIENTA}} are missing, ask for them before designing. Mark assumptions with [ASSUMPTION].
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Each metric traces to a business question and to an action with its trigger threshold; zero vanity metrics.
- [ ] Total KPIs between 5 and 7; if more, it is justified.
- [ ] Each metric has an exact formula, unit, frequency, granularity, owner, source, leading/lagging type, and numeric green/amber/red threshold.
- [ ] Data gaps declared with a temporary proxy when a metric cannot be derived from {{FUENTE_DATOS}}.
- [ ] The BLUF headline answers the main question without scrolling or interaction.
- [ ] Chart type justified by data type; no pie with more than three categories or misleading dual axis; axes from zero unless noted.
- [ ] Semantic palette with thresholds and WCAG AA contrast; state does not depend on color alone.
- [ ] Wireframe with position, global filters, drill-down, no-data/error states, and notes for {{HERRAMIENTA}}; {{RESTRICCIONES}} respected.
- [ ] Assumptions marked [ASSUMPTION].
Expected deliverable: table of 5-7 metrics (formula, unit, frequency, granularity, owner, source, threshold) + questions-to-metrics-to-actions map + wireframe in blocks with hierarchy, filters, and drill-down paths + semantic palette + validation checklist, all ready to build in {{HERRAMIENTA}}.
spec-datos_dashboard_seleccion_grafico:
[inputs]
- MENSAJE: {{MENSAJE}} > Main message in one sentence, the insight the audience must understand (e.g., "northern region sales are triple the rest", "churn rises every quarter")
- DATOS: {{DATOS}} > Data structure: variables, number of categories or data points, whether there is a temporal dimension, whether the parts sum to a total
- AUDIENCIA_MEDIO: {{AUDIENCIA_MEDIO}} > Who reads it and where it will be seen (executive report, live dashboard, slide, mobile, printed)
- RESTRICCIONES: {{RESTRICCIONES}} > Tool limits, space, accessibility (color blindness, black and white), or others (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need to choose the correct chart type to communicate {{MENSAJE}} to {{AUDIENCIA_MEDIO}}, so that the reader understands the insight at a glance and without being led to a false conclusion. The purpose is for the visual form to serve the message, not to distort it: a good chart unlocks fast decisions and trust in the data; a poorly chosen or misleading one erodes both. The result is a justified chart recommendation ready to build. Value at risk: a wrong choice not only looks bad, it leads to decisions based on a false perception of the data.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: senior data visualization specialist, trained in Andrew Abela's chart selection framework (Chart Suggestions / Extreme Presentation, 2006), the Cleveland-McGill perceptual hierarchy (1984), and Edward Tufte's graphic integrity principles (lie-factor and data-ink ratio).

Deliverable: a chart recommendation for {{MENSAJE}} about {{DATOS}}, structured as follows:
1. Framing: restate the message, confirm data structure, audience/medium, and constraints; mark as [ASSUMPTION] what you infer and as [TO_CONFIRM] what blocks the decision.
2. Intent: classify the message into one of the five families — compare across categories, compare over time/trend, distribution, relationship or correlation, composition (part-to-whole) — and justify the choice by dismissing the others in one line each. If the message mixes two intents, prioritize the dominant one and name the secondary as a complementary view.
3. Recommendation: a primary chart and an alternative, justified with the Cleveland-McGill perceptual hierarchy (position on common axis > length > angle/area > color/volume): prioritize the encoding with the lowest read error for this intent. Explicitly dismiss the tempting but inferior option (e.g., pie when bars read better) and say why.
4. Encoding: define what variable goes on each axis, the order of categories (by value, alphabetical, or natural, and why), what to highlight, linear or logarithmic scale, and whether the magnitude axis starts at zero (mandatory in bars; optional with justification in lines).
5. Anti-patterns: list the misleading pitfalls to avoid in this case (truncated Y axis in bars, dual Y axis, 3D, pie with more than five slices or not summing to 100%, heat map with non-perceptually-uniform scale, stacked area with many series, excess non-data ink) and the specific distortion they would cause here.
6. Accessibility: note adjusted to {{AUDIENCIA_MEDIO}} and {{RESTRICCIONES}} (sufficient contrast, direct labels vs. distant legend, not depending on color alone, legibility at the real size/medium, palette safe for color blindness).
7. Close: the recommendation in one actionable sentence, ready to build, with the key highlight of the message.

Brand rules: neutral professional English, no emojis; never prices or the word "free".

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: extract the intent from {{MENSAJE}} and the nature of {{DATOS}} (categorical, temporal, continuous quantitative, part-to-whole). If message, data structure, or medium are missing, ask for them before continuing; do not invent numbers or figures not provided.
Phase 2 - Classification: assign one intent family and dismiss the rest with a brief reason.
Phase 3 - Perceptual selection: map the family to chart candidates and choose primary + alternative applying Cleveland-McGill; explicitly dismiss the tempting but inferior option.
Phase 4 - Specification: detail encoding, scale, and the zero rule per the chosen type.
Phase 5 - Integrity audit: review against the misleading anti-patterns and accessibility; correct before delivering and verify the highlight reinforces the message, not another point.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- The intent is classified into one of the five families and justified, with the others dismissed.
- There is a primary chart and an alternative, both justified with the Cleveland-McGill hierarchy, not by preference; the inferior option is dismissed with a reason.
- The encoding specifies axes, category order with criterion, scale, and the zero rule.
- The anti-patterns relevant to the case are named with the specific distortion they produce here.
- There is an accessibility note adjusted to the real audience, medium, and constraints.
- The close highlight reinforces the declared message, not a secondary point.
- No invented data; what is assumed is marked [ASSUMPTION]; blockers as [TO_CONFIRM]; no figures not provided.
- Neutral professional English, no emojis; no prices or "free".
Expected deliverable: a 7-block chart recommendation with primary chart, alternative, full encoding, list of anti-patterns to avoid, accessibility note, and one closing sentence ready to build.
spec-datos_dashboard_kpi_jerarquia:
[inputs]
- MODELO_NEGOCIO: {{MODELO_NEGOCIO}} > Product or business line, how it generates value and how it monetizes
- OBJETIVO_ESTRATEGICO: {{OBJETIVO_ESTRATEGICO}} > Outcome the dashboard should help move in the defined horizon
- AUDIENCIA_DECISIONES: {{AUDIENCIA_DECISIONES}} > Who consumes the dashboard and what decisions they will make with it
- METRICAS_DISPONIBLES: {{METRICAS_DISPONIBLES}} > Metrics and data sources available today ("(optional)": if omitted, the ideal set is proposed and unavailable items are flagged)
- GRANULARIDAD_TEMPORAL: {{GRANULARIDAD_TEMPORAL}} > Update frequency and analysis horizon (daily, weekly, monthly) (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A dashboard that shows a flat list of metrics forces every reader to mentally reconstruct what matters, what moves what, and where to look when something fails. Structuring KPIs in a hierarchy with drill-down turns the dashboard into a story: a north-star metric that says whether we are on track, levers that say why, and diagnostics that say where to act. This unlocks faster decisions, aligned conversations between business and data, and a dashboard that is navigated from general to detail without losing the causal thread. The risk to avoid is optimizing the north-star while degrading another dimension (quality, cost, retention), which is why the hierarchy includes guardrails.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior product analytics and Business Intelligence architect, specializing in actionable metric systems (North Star Framework, metric trees, and data storytelling).

Deliverable: a KPI hierarchy in three levels with a designed drill-down path, plus a tree map, a master table, and an instrumentation contract. Steps:
1. Define the single north-star metric: the indicator that captures the value delivered to the user and that the business seeks to grow. Justify the choice and explicitly discard at least one candidate for being a vanity metric.
2. Decompose the north-star into secondary metrics (actionable levers or drivers). For each lever explicitly state its relationship with the north-star: if arithmetic (sum, product, rate), write the formula; if causal, declare it as a hypothesis with its expected signal.
3. For each lever, define third-level diagnostic metrics that explain the why, with suggested cut dimensions (segment, channel, geography, cohort, device).
4. Design the drill-down path in three planes: what is seen in the summary view, what expands on interaction, what detail appears at the bottom (summary first > zoom and filter > detail on demand).
5. For each metric specify: name, exact calculation definition, unit, temporal granularity, desired direction, and goal or alert threshold when applicable. Flag as guardrail any metric that must not degrade when moving the north-star.
6. Deliver a visual map of the tree in text, a master KPI table ready for the data team, and an instrumentation contract that, per metric, lists source, origin event or table, and whether the data exists today or requires instrumentation.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: confirm business model, objective, audience, and available data. If anything is missing or ambiguous, ask before assuming; mark any unavoidable assumption with [ASSUMPTION].
Phase 2 - North-star: select and justify the north-star metric; list at least one discarded candidate with its vanity reason.
Phase 3 - Tree: derive levers (level 2) with formula or causal hypothesis, then diagnostics (level 3) with cut dimensions; identify guardrails.
Phase 4 - Navigation: map each level to a drill-down plane and define the interactions (what filters, what expands, what links to detail).
Phase 5 - Packaging: build the tree map, the master table, and the instrumentation contract; validate against the checklist and report every metric not measurable today.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- There is one and only one north-star metric, actionable and not a vanity metric, with justification and at least one discarded candidate.
- Each level-2 lever has an explicit relationship with the north-star: arithmetic formula or causal hypothesis with expected signal.
- Each lever has at least one level-3 diagnostic metric with cut dimensions.
- Every metric defines name, exact calculation, unit, granularity, desired direction, and goal or threshold when applicable.
- Guardrails are identified that must not degrade when optimizing the north-star.
- The drill-down path respects summary first > zoom and filter > detail on demand, and each level is mapped to a navigation plane.
- The instrumentation contract marks, per metric, source, origin, and availability today; what is not measurable is declared, not invented.
- All assumptions are marked [ASSUMPTION]; no data or goals are invented without a basis.
Expected deliverable: (a) visual map of the tree in text with north-star at the top and diagnostics at the bottom; (b) master KPI table with one row per metric and the checklist columns; (c) description of the drill-down path in three planes; (d) instrumentation contract with availability of each metric.
spec-datos_dashboard_critica_rediseno:
[inputs]
- PROPOSITO_DASHBOARD: {{PROPOSITO_DASHBOARD}} > Purpose of the dashboard and the concrete decision it must enable
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Who uses it, their level (executive, operational, analyst), and consumption context (large screen, mobile, meeting)
- KPIS_PRIORITARIOS: {{KPIS_PRIORITARIOS}} > 3 to 5 KPIs or key questions the dashboard must answer, ideally with their goal or threshold
- HERRAMIENTA_Y_RESTRICCIONES: {{HERRAMIENTA_Y_RESTRICCIONES}} > Tool (Power BI, Tableau, Looker, or other) and space, brand, or technical constraints (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Dashboard screenshot, panel-by-panel description, dashboard file, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
An overloaded dashboard costs time and decisions: the reader cannot find the signal through the noise, distrusts the numbers, or ignores the dashboard altogether. The purpose of this prompt is to audit the cognitive load, data-ink ratio, and actionable clarity of an existing dashboard, and to propose a redesign that is readable at a glance. What is unlocked: faster decisions, a dashboard that people actually use, and explicit criteria to defend each change to whoever designed the original. Scope limit: this prompt critiques design and visual narrative; it does not audit query correctness or source data quality except where the design leads to misreading.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior data visualization designer and BI analyst, trained in Tufte's principles (data-ink ratio, chartjunk) and Few's principles (at-a-glance dashboards, semantic color use, pre-attentive encoding), with experience in executive and operational dashboards.

Deliverable: a structured critique of the current dashboard plus a justified redesign. Steps:
1. Confirm purpose, audience, priority KPIs, and tool. If {{PROPOSITO_DASHBOARD}}, {{AUDIENCIA}}, or {{KPIS_PRIORITARIOS}} are missing, ask for them before auditing (without them there is no relevance criterion). If {{ADJUNTOS}} is "No attachments", work with an explicit dashboard placeholder and flag it.
2. Inventory of the current state: list each panel, its chart type, the question it attempts to answer, the visual elements it contains, and, if deducible, the frequency of use or actual relevance.
3. Audit in three dimensions, with high/medium/low severity and the principle supporting each finding:
   a. Cognitive load: count of panels, colors, chart types, and competing text blocks; saturation and working memory demanded vs. the practical limit of 5 to 9 simultaneous elements.
   b. Data-ink ratio: non-informative ink (dense grids, 3D, shadows, gradients, redundant borders and legends, decoration, duplicate axes, labels repeating the axis).
   c. Clarity and actionability: one panel = one question; hierarchy from main KPI to detail; scales and labels without deception (truncated axes, dual axes, improperly compared areas, pie with many slices); presence of comparative context (goal, prior period, normal band); and whether the user knows what action to take.
4. Proposed redesign: panel-by-panel grid ordered by reading hierarchy (top-left = most important); which charts to remove, merge, or change type and why; reduced palette to semantic color with accessible contrast; typographic hierarchy; and the 3 to 5 KPIs that must dominate the view.
5. Before/after table: each change, its justification (named principle), and the expected impact on readability or decision speed.
6. Operational close: minimum data contract per panel (granularity, freshness, filters) and a lightweight validation plan with 2 or 3 real users (five-second test: what do they see and what would they do).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: restate purpose, audience, and KPIs; if there are critical gaps, ask before proceeding.
Phase 2 - Inventory and diagnosis: document the current state and run the three-dimension audit; cite the principle of each finding and assign severity.
Phase 3 - Redesign: propose grid, hierarchy, color, and typography; resolve high-severity findings first and declare trade-offs (density vs. simplicity, completeness vs. focus).
Phase 4 - Close and verification: define data contract and validation plan; verify that each priority KPI has its panel, that no chart deceives, and that the element count is lower than the original. Do not invent business figures: mark what is absent as [ASSUMPTION].
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Purpose, audience, and KPIs confirmed or requested before auditing.
- [ ] Complete inventory: each panel with type, question, elements, and deduced relevance.
- [ ] Three dimensions covered (cognitive load, data-ink ratio, clarity) with severity and principle per finding.
- [ ] Redesign with grid, visual hierarchy, accessible semantic color, and typography; 3 to 5 dominant KPIs.
- [ ] Each redesign decision justified by a named principle (Tufte/Few or other) with its trade-offs.
- [ ] Before/after table with change, justification, and expected impact.
- [ ] Verifiable reduction in non-informative elements/ink vs. the original.
- [ ] Data contract per panel and user validation plan included.
- [ ] Tool constraints respected or flagged as unfeasible.
- [ ] Business figures not invented; assumptions marked [ASSUMPTION]; neutral professional English, no emojis.
Expected deliverable: document with (1) inventory, (2) three-dimension audit prioritized by severity, (3) panel-by-panel redesign specification, (4) before/after table with justification and impact, and (5) data contract + validation plan.
spec-datos_dashboard_layout_mobile:
[inputs]
- DASHBOARD: {{DASHBOARD}} > What the dashboard measures and how it is used (its business purpose and the question it answers)
- VISUALES: {{VISUALES}} > Inventory of current visuals: cards, charts, tables, and filters it currently contains, with their type and the metric they show
- MENSAJE_PRINCIPAL: {{MENSAJE_PRINCIPAL}} > Conclusion or decision the user must be able to read first, in seconds
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Who consults it on mobile and in what context (standing, in a meeting, in the field, with one hand)
- RESTRICCIONES: {{RESTRICCIONES}} > Technical constraints: BI tool, available breakpoints, supported interactions, data per screen (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A dashboard designed for a large screen does not translate well to mobile: multi-column grids break, tables require horizontal scrolling, text forces zooming, and the main message is buried under controls and legends. The purpose of this task is to reorganize the visuals of {{DASHBOARD}} into a mobile-first responsive layout where {{MENSAJE_PRINCIPAL}} is read in the first seconds without scrolling, and the rest of the detail is revealed progressively. By achieving this, {{AUDIENCIA}} can decide or act from the phone with the same confidence as on desktop, and the dashboard stops losing users due to reading friction. The framework contributes information hierarchy applied to data visualization on a small screen: a single dominant question, a single answer at the top, and everything else subordinated.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior dashboard designer and responsive data visualization specialist, with expertise in mobile-first, progressive disclosure, inverted data pyramid, KPI visual hierarchy, and tactile interaction patterns.
Deliver the following, in this order:
1. Restate what {{DASHBOARD}} is for and who consults it on mobile in one sentence: "[role] reviews [decision] in [use context]". If {{VISUALES}}, {{MENSAJE_PRINCIPAL}}, or {{AUDIENCIA}} are missing or ambiguous, ask for them before continuing; do not invent metrics or visuals.
2. Fix the main message from {{MENSAJE_PRINCIPAL}}: the single conclusion readable in ~3 seconds without scrolling. Subordinate everything else to it. If {{MENSAJE_PRINCIPAL}} contains several ideas, choose the dominant one and leave the others as Level 2.
3. Classify each visual from {{VISUALES}} into Level 1 (answers the question, always visible), Level 2 (context, below or behind a tap), or Level 3 (detail, drill-down or filter), with a one-line justification per visual and an explicit criterion for why that level and not another.
4. Define the vertical order in a single column applying the inverted pyramid: main KPI and its delta at the top, trend next, breakdown and table at the bottom, adjusted to {{AUDIENCIA}} and their context. Indicate the expected scroll length and where the first fold cuts (what is visible without scrolling).
5. Reassign each chart type to its narrow-screen-readable equivalent (wide table to cards or list; many categories to top-N plus "others"; dual axis to sparkline or number with delta; pie with many slices to horizontal bars or single number; dense heat map to ranking or traffic light), respecting {{RESTRICCIONES}}; for each change indicate before, after, and reason. If {{RESTRICCIONES}} does not support a format, offer the best native alternative.
6. Specify responsive rules: collapse breakpoint per block, what is hidden or moved to a menu, how filters mutate (side panel to bottom sheet or accordion), default filter values on mobile, and the minimum tap area (>=44 px) for thumb use, within what {{RESTRICCIONES}} allows.
7. Declare what is NOT shown on mobile and why (redundant legends, axes with too many ticks, unnecessary decimals, competing KPIs, secondary table columns) and where the omitted content moves to (desktop, export, drill).
8. Close with a resolved mobile validation checklist and a note on perceived performance (how many visuals above the fold, risk of slow load) and accessibility (contrast and minimum text size).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Framing: confirm purpose, main message, and audience; list gaps and assumptions before designing.
Phase 2 Prioritization: assign the three levels to each visual based on how much they serve the main message; resolve ties by favoring what answers the dominant question.
Phase 3 Vertical layout: order Level 1 in one column by inverted pyramid; place Level 2 and 3 in progressive disclosure (accordion, tab, drill-down); mark the first fold.
Phase 4 Visual reassignment: translate each chart to the format readable on narrow screens with its before/after/reason justification.
Phase 5 Responsive rules: define breakpoints, collapses, filter behavior and defaults, and tap area.
Phase 6 Validation: run the mobile checklist, review performance and accessibility, and mark [ASSUMPTION] on every decision without confirmed data.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The main message is understood in ~3 seconds without scrolling or zooming and is above the first fold.
- [ ] Each visual from {{VISUALES}} has been assigned a level, an order, and a concrete responsive rule, with justification.
- [ ] Layout in a single column: zero multi-column grids and zero horizontal scrolling on mobile.
- [ ] Each chart reassignment declares before, after, and reason, and respects {{RESTRICCIONES}} or proposes a native alternative.
- [ ] Filters and controls have a usable tap area for the thumb (>=44 px) and a defined default state.
- [ ] What is hidden or deferred on mobile is explicitly declared, why, and where it moves.
- [ ] A perceived performance note and an accessibility note (contrast, minimum text) are included.
- [ ] Every decision without confirmed data marked [ASSUMPTION]; no invented metrics.
Expected deliverable: a responsive reorganization plan with the purpose sentence, the main message, the level-prioritization table, the mobile vertical order with fold marker, the visual reassignment table (before/after/reason), the breakpoint and filter rules, the list of omissions, the performance and accessibility notes, and the resolved validation checklist.
spec-datos_dashboard_filtros_interactivi:
[inputs]
- DASHBOARD: {{DASHBOARD}} > Name and purpose of the dashboard, audience, and the decision it enables
- HERRAMIENTA_BI: {{HERRAMIENTA_BI}} > BI engine or stack (e.g. Power BI, Tableau, Looker, Metabase, Superset) and connection mode (import / DirectQuery / live)
- MODELO_DATOS: {{MODELO_DATOS}} > Tables, relationships, granularity, approximate row volume, and source (DWH / lake / extract)
- VISTAS_Y_VISUALES: {{VISTAS_Y_VISUALES}} > Pages or tabs and visuals per page that must interact
- ROLES_USUARIO: {{ROLES_USUARIO}} > User profiles, filter control level, and row-level security (RLS) rules if applicable
- METRICAS_CLAVE: {{METRICAS_CLAVE}} > Key metrics and dimensions driving the analysis and the unit/aggregation of each
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A dashboard only delivers value if its interactivity is coherent: when the user filters in one view, all others must respond predictably, without contradictions between cards or slow queries. Designing filters, cross-filtering, and parameters before building avoids the most costly BI rework: rebuilding relationships, breaking user trust with figures that don't reconcile across visuals, and degrading performance with poorly handled high-cardinality filters. This design unlocks a self-explanatory, navigable dashboard with acceptable response times.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior BI architect and analytics experience specialist, focused on interactivity design and modeling for production dashboards.
Deliver the complete interactivity system design in these steps:
1. Filter inventory: table with filter, scope (global / page / visual), control type, dimension or field, expected cardinality, selection mode (single / multiple), default value, and the role that controls it.
2. Cross-filtering map: source > destination table with direction (one-way / two-way), exempt visuals and note explaining why, avoiding circular filtering and double-counts; declare model relationships that enable or block each propagation.
3. Parameters and advanced interactivity: what-if, metric or scenario selectors, drill-through, and bookmarks; define range, step, default, and expected effect.
4. Precedence and reset: application hierarchy when filters coincide (global > page > visual or other), reset button behavior, and selection persistence between pages.
5. States: default on opening, empty or no-data state with associated message per sensitive visual; synchronization with row-level security if applicable.
6. Performance: handling of high cardinality, lazy loading of lists, pre-aggregations, indexing or partitioning, multiple-selection limits, and impact of connection mode (import / DirectQuery / live) on each filter.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: confirm BI tool, connection mode, data model, views, roles, and metrics; if an essential piece of information is missing, ask before designing — do not invent the model or relationships.
Phase 2 - Inventory and scope: classify each filter by scope and control according to the decision it enables, not by habit; flag high-cardinality filters as edge cases to address in Phase 5.
Phase 3 - Propagation rules: trace cross-filtering as a directed graph, detect cycles and double-counts (many-to-many relationships, bridge tables, mixed granularities), and declare exemptions.
Phase 4 - Parameters and precedence: define advanced interactivity and resolve conflicts with an explicit precedence rule; document the trade-off when an option improves coherence at the cost of performance or vice versa.
Phase 5 - States and performance: close with defaults, empty states, RLS synchronization, and performance tactics suited to the cardinality and the engine.
Mark with [ASSUMPTION] everything assumed and justify each decision in one line.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Each filter has explicit scope, control, cardinality, selection mode, default, and controlling role.
- [ ] The cross-filtering map is cycle-free and declares exempt visuals with their reason and the model relationship that supports it.
- [ ] There is no risk of double-counting or contradictory figures across visuals (many-to-many, mixed granularities, and bridge tables reviewed).
- [ ] What-if parameters have defined range, step, default, and effect.
- [ ] An unambiguous precedence rule exists and reset behavior and persistence are clear.
- [ ] Default states and empty/no-data states are defined with their message, synchronized with RLS if applicable.
- [ ] Performance tactics address high cardinality, lazy loading, selection limits, and the connection mode of the indicated engine.
- [ ] Every assumption is marked [ASSUMPTION] and every decision and trade-off has its rationale in one line.
Expected deliverable: interactivity design document with six tables (filters, cross-filtering, parameters, precedence/reset, states, performance) and a final summary of coherence and performance risks prioritized by impact and probability, each with its mitigation.
spec-datos_dashboard_accesibilidad_color:
[inputs]
- TIPO_GRAFICO: {{TIPO_GRAFICO}} > Visualization type (bar, line, heat map, scatter, stacked area, donut)
- SERIES_CATEGORIAS: {{SERIES_CATEGORIAS}} > Series or categories that must be distinguishable from each other and how many there are
- PALETA_ACTUAL: {{PALETA_ACTUAL}} > Colors currently in use as hex codes (or "no defined palette")
- NIVEL_WCAG: {{NIVEL_WCAG}} > Target conformance level: AA or AAA per WCAG 2.1
- CONTEXTO_USO: {{CONTEXTO_USO}} > Medium and background where it will be displayed (light web, dark mode, print, projection) in hex if known
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A visualization is going to be published on a dashboard that will be read by people with different color vision and on screens of unequal quality. Approximately one in twelve men has some form of color vision deficiency, almost always red-green, and a dashboard that distinguishes series only by hue leaves those people unable to read it. Resolving color, contrast, and labeling before publishing unlocks defensible WCAG compliance, reduces accessibility complaints, and improves readability for everyone. This redesign feeds the dashboard style guide and the visualization component library, so decisions must be reusable, not one-off patches.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: senior accessible data visualization specialist, experienced in applying WCAG 2.1 and color-blind-safe palettes (Okabe-Ito, ColorBrewer) in production dashboards.
Deliverable: a color accessibility audit plus a redesigned hex palette with redundant encoding, a verification checklist, and a compliance verdict. Steps:
1. Validate inputs; if TIPO_GRAFICO, SERIES_CATEGORIAS, PALETA_ACTUAL, NIVEL_WCAG, or CONTEXTO_USO are missing or ambiguous, ask for all of them in one single round before continuing. If the background is not provided in hex, assume white #FFFFFF (light) or #1A1A1A (dark) and mark it [ASSUMPTION].
2. Diagnose the current palette on three axes: color-blindness safety (simulate deuteranopia, protanopia, tritanopia and mark pairs that collapse); contrast (ratio of each color against the background and between adjacent series; thresholds 3:1 non-text and borders, 4.5:1 normal text, 3:1 large text); and exclusive dependence on color.
3. Redesign the palette: assign each series a hex from a validated system, ordered by maximum perceptual distance; use a single-hue sequential scale for magnitude and a diverging scale with a neutral center for deviation from a baseline. Report hex, contrast against background, and assigned series.
4. Add at least one redundant encoding layer appropriate to the chart type (marker shape, fill pattern, direct label, line weight or style, order or position).
5. Deliver a verification checklist with status per criterion and instructions for validating with a color blindness simulator and contrast checker.
6. Close with a recommendation: the target NIVEL_WCAG level is met, or list the prioritized pending adjustments (blocking / recommended).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Framing: confirm inputs; do not invent brand values or assume the BI tool.
Phase 2 Diagnosis: evaluate color blindness, contrast, and color dependence; report each non-compliant pair with its numerical contrast ratio.
Phase 3 Redesign: derive the palette from Okabe-Ito or ColorBrewer depending on whether the categories are qualitative, sequential, or diverging; deliver hex + contrast + series and add the redundant layer. If CONTEXTO_USO includes print or projection, declare the contrast-degradation adjustment separately.
Phase 4 Verification: assemble the checklist, mark every unconfirmed piece of data as [ASSUMPTION], and declare final compliance.
Edge cases: if SERIES_CATEGORIAS exceeds 8, warn that no qualitative system guarantees safe distinction and propose grouping, pagination, or reinforced redundant encoding. If the brand palette is non-negotiable, preserve hue and resolve via contrast, value, and redundant layer, making the conflict explicit. If the medium is dark mode, recalculate against the dark background and do not reuse ratios from the light background.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- Every series in SERIES_CATEGORIAS has an assigned hex and remains distinguishable under deuteranopia, protanopia, and tritanopia.
- Every reported contrast ratio is numerical and meets the applicable threshold (3:1 graphic/border, 4.5:1 normal text, 3:1 large text) for the target NIVEL_WCAG level, against the actual background of CONTEXTO_USO.
- No meaning depends on color alone: there is at least one redundant layer (shape, pattern, direct label, weight, position).
- The palette comes from a named validated system (Okabe-Ito or ColorBrewer) and is justified as qualitative, sequential, or diverging.
- Every unconfirmed piece of data is marked [ASSUMPTION]; no brand colors are invented; the BI tool is not assumed.
Expected deliverable: palette table (series, hex, contrast against background, redundant layer), report of non-compliant pairs with their numerical ratio, verification checklist with validation instructions, and WCAG compliance verdict with prioritized pending adjustments.
spec-datos_dashboard_alertas_umbral:
[inputs]
- METRICAS_CLAVE: {{METRICAS_CLAVE}} > Metrics or KPIs to monitor and the unit of each (e.g. conversion rate in %, backlog in tickets, margin in points, latency in ms)
- METAS_Y_TOLERANCIAS: {{METAS_Y_TOLERANCIAS}} > Target or objective value for each metric and how much deviation is tolerated before amber and before red; include whether the target is a contractual/SLA commitment or aspirational
- ORIGEN_DE_DATOS: {{ORIGEN_DE_DATOS}} > Source and granularity (table, refresh frequency, daily/weekly level); include whether a historical series is available and its age
- DUENOS_Y_CANALES: {{DUENOS_Y_CANALES}} > Who receives each alert and via which channel (email, Slack, panel), and the escalation path if it persists
- CONTEXTO_DE_RUIDO: {{CONTEXTO_DE_RUIDO}} > (optional) Seasonality, low-volume periods, maintenance windows, or expected events that should not trigger false alerts
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A report only creates value when it signals by itself what demands action. Without explicit threshold rules, the reader interprets numbers by eye, deviations are detected late, and nobody knows who is responsible. The goal is to transform metrics into a traffic-light and alert system with defensible cut-offs, anti-noise measures, and owner-assigned notifications, so that the report governs attention instead of competing for it. This unlocks early detection, consistent response, and less alert fatigue.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior Business Intelligence analyst specialized in operational alert design and business observability.
Deliver the following, in this order:
1. Threshold rule table per metric: desired direction (higher is better / lower is better / range), threshold type (fixed vs. target; relative to period or budget; statistical by deviation from the mean), and the resulting numerical rule with its unit.
2. Traffic-light band matrix: green / amber / red cut-offs per metric with the numerical justification for each cut-off traced to METAS_Y_TOLERANCIAS. Declare the boundary convention (what happens exactly at the cut-off value) and full coverage with no gaps or overlaps between bands.
3. Anti-noise rules: minimum persistence window before triggering, debounce or grace period to resume (hysteresis to avoid oscillating at the boundary), and suppression of false positives per CONTEXTO_DE_RUIDO (seasonality, low volume, maintenance).
4. Accessible conditional formatting: an icon or text label in addition to color in each band (never color alone), suitable for color blindness; declare the missing or stale data state as a distinct band (grey/no data), not as green.
5. Notification matrix per amber and red band: channel, owner (from DUENOS_Y_CANALES), message with metric, current value, crossed threshold, and suggested action, plus the escalation path if it persists and the alert's close/recovery condition.
6. Assumptions log with the [ASSUMPTION] label for all inferred data (target, tolerance, history, owner) and why it was assumed.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Framing: confirm metrics, unit, desired direction, and availability of historical series; if a target, tolerance, source, or owner is missing, ask before proposing cut-offs.
Phase 2 Threshold design: choose the threshold type per metric and justify it (fixed target for contractual/SLA commitments; relative for trends and period-on-period comparison; statistical only when stable and sufficient history exists). Declare the chosen trade-off.
Phase 3 Bands and anti-noise: derive green/amber/red cut-offs, verify complete coverage, and apply persistence, debounce, and hysteresis to avoid alert fatigue.
Phase 4 Activation: define accessible conditional formatting, the no-data state, and the actionable notification per band with owner, escalation, and close condition.
Phase 5 Verification: review each band against the checklist and mark [ASSUMPTION] on what was inferred.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Every metric declares its desired direction and unit.
- [ ] Every band cut-off has numerical justification traceable to the target or tolerance, not an arbitrary value.
- [ ] Bands cover the full range with no gaps or overlaps and the boundary convention is declared.
- [ ] Anti-noise rules exist (persistence, debounce, hysteresis) to prevent alert fatigue.
- [ ] Conditional formatting combines color with an icon or text, is readable for color blindness, and treats missing/stale data as a distinct state.
- [ ] Every amber and red alert has an owner, channel, actionable message, escalation path, and close condition.
- [ ] All inferred data is marked [ASSUMPTION]; no threshold was invented without basis.
Expected deliverable: a ready-to-implement specification with the threshold rule table, the traffic-light band matrix with cut-offs and justification, the anti-noise rules, the accessible conditional formatting, the notification matrix by owner, and the assumptions log.
spec-datos_dashboard_narrativa_anotacion:
[inputs]
- DASHBOARD: {{DASHBOARD}} > Description or screenshot of the current dashboard: which charts it contains, their current titles, chart type (line, bar, KPI, table), and the tool used (Power BI, Tableau, Looker, spreadsheet)
- METRICAS_CLAVE: {{METRICAS_CLAVE}} > List of displayed metrics with their period values and, if available, the prior-period comparison or target; indicate unit and whether it is cumulative or a rate
- PERIODO: {{PERIODO}} > Time range covered by the dashboard (e.g. April 2026, Q1, last 30 days) and, if applicable, the granularity (daily, weekly, monthly)
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Who reads it: executive committee, operational team, external client; defines level of detail, tone, and the decision that audience must make
- EVENTOS_CONTEXTO: {{EVENTOS_CONTEXTO}} > Events during the period that explain movements: launches, campaigns, price changes, incidents, seasonality, with their date (optional)
- UMBRALES: {{UMBRALES}} > Current targets, SLAs, budgets, or break-even points against which metrics are evaluated, or "No thresholds defined" (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A dashboard with raw metrics forces every reader to interpret on their own: neutral titles like "Revenue" or "Conversion" don't say what changed or what to do, and without visual guidance attention scatters across charts competing for it. The goal is to convert the dashboard {{DASHBOARD}} for the period {{PERIODO}} into a decision-making tool for {{AUDIENCIA}}, where the finding reads in seconds and the suggested action is explicit. This unlocks shorter meetings, faster decisions, and a dashboard that explains itself when the author is not present. The risk to avoid: narrative that decorates instead of informs, or causes stated without support in the data.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior Business Intelligence analyst specialized in data storytelling, with mastery of visual hierarchy, pre-attentive principles, and executive dashboard design.
Deliverable: four narrative layers for {{DASHBOARD}}, ready to apply.
1. Actionable titles: rewrite each chart title to communicate the finding, not the metric. Format: subject + figure + direction + cause when known (e.g. "Revenue fell 12% in April due to the drop in new subscriptions"). If the cause is not in the inputs, omit it or mark it [ASSUMPTION]; never invent it. Deliver table: current title > proposed actionable title > finding it communicates.
2. Contextual annotations: for each relevant series, define one annotation anchored to a specific point using {{EVENTOS_CONTEXTO}} and {{UMBRALES}}. Classify each as event, anomaly, or critical threshold (target, SLA, break-even) and include a brief label (<= 12 words) explaining the why. Limit to the 5–7 highest-value annotations to avoid saturating the canvas. Deliver table: chart | point/date | type | label.
3. Automated executive summary: write 3 to 5 sentences to place above the dashboard answering what happened, why it matters, and what decision is suggested, in descending order of relevance. Deliver the version with data from {{METRICAS_CLAVE}} and a template version with placeholders ({{metrica}}, {{valor}}, {{delta}}, {{causa}}) so it regenerates when the data changes.
4. Reading order: order the recommendations using visual hierarchy in F or Z, placing the critical content at the top left. Justify the chosen pattern based on dashboard density (Z for few blocks, F for dense lists) and indicate which chart occupies the highest-weight position.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Interpret: confirm metrics, period, audience, events, and thresholds; identify the 2–3 dominant findings of the period (greatest magnitude of change or greatest deviation from target). If an essential input is missing or ambiguous, ask for it before proceeding.
Phase 2 - Plan: define the reading order and map each finding to its chart, title, and annotations; discard those that would not move a decision.
Phase 3 - Execute: produce the four layers. Mark with [ASSUMPTION] any unconfirmed cause or figure; never invent data or attribute causality without evidence (a coincident event does not prove the cause: declare it as a correlation).
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
- Every actionable title carries a figure and direction; the cause only appears if it is in the inputs or marked [ASSUMPTION].
- Every annotation is anchored to a specific point (date or value) and classified as event, anomaly, or threshold; maximum 5–7 annotations.
- Stated causality has support in the inputs; every temporal coincidence is declared as correlation, not cause.
- The executive summary does not exceed 5 sentences and exists in a data version and a template version with placeholders.
- The reading order follows an explicit F or Z pattern and justifies what goes at the top left.
- Tone and level of detail are adjusted to {{AUDIENCIA}}.
- Zero invented metrics; assumptions labeled.
Expected deliverable: three tables (titles, annotations, reading order) plus the executive summary block in both versions, ready to paste into {{DASHBOARD}}.
spec-datos_dashboard_self_service:
[inputs]
- SECTOR: {{SECTOR}} > Industry or business area (banking, retail, health, manufacturing, SaaS)
- HERRAMIENTA_BI: {{HERRAMIENTA_BI}} > Available BI platform (Power BI, Tableau, Looker, Metabase, Qlik)
- DOMINIOS_DATOS: {{DOMINIOS_DATOS}} > Priority data domains to enable (sales, customers, operations, finance)
- MADUREZ_ANALITICA: {{MADUREZ_ANALITICA}} > Current level of analytical maturity of business users (initial, intermediate, advanced)
- OBJETIVO_ADOPCION: {{OBJETIVO_ADOPCION}} > Expected outcome of the initiative (optional: reduce requests to the data team, increase autonomy, improve confidence in figures)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Business users in {{SECTOR}} depend on the data team for every question, creating bottlenecks, decision delays, and parallel reports with contradictory figures. The goal is to design a self-service analytics experience on {{HERRAMIENTA_BI}} that allows them to explore the domains {{DOMINIOS_DATOS}} autonomously, starting from an analytical maturity of {{MADUREZ_ANALITICA}}, without risk of misinterpretation or of making decisions on uncertified figures. The central challenge is to enable autonomy while preserving a single governed source of truth: more freedom without governance produces a figures mess; more governance without freedom recreates the bottleneck. A well-designed experience unlocks faster decisions, frees the data team for higher-value work, and consolidates confidence in the numbers.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior self-service analytics and BI architect, with experience in semantic layer modeling, data governance, and adoption programs in data organizations.
Deliver a self-service experience design document that contains:
1. Curated dataset semantic layer: 2 to 4 domain datasets with declared grain, dimensions, certified metrics (each with its business formula in plain language), and field source, separating certified from experimental. Include one explicit anti-pattern to avoid: two metrics with the same label but different formulas.
2. Library of reusable visualization templates for frequent use cases (KPI tracking, time comparison, ranking, distribution, funnel), each with the business question it answers, when to use it, and when NOT to use it.
3. Governance guardrail matrix: row-level and domain permissions, handling of PII and sensitive data, freshness and quality validation, visible certified vs. uncertified label, and limits to prevent queries that degrade performance. Indicate the action for each control violation.
4. Enablement model: user levels (consumer, explorer, author), learning path per level, promotion criteria between levels, and a process — with a responsible party — for promoting an ad hoc analysis to certified content.
5. Success metrics dashboard aligned with {{OBJETIVO_ADOPCION}}: adoption, autonomy, reduction of requests to the data team, and confidence in figures, each with definition, measurement method, and starting baseline. Add one common adoption risk (e.g. users keep requesting reports from the data team) with its mitigation.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: confirm sector, BI tool, priority domains, analytical maturity, and objective; mark assumptions as [ASSUMPTION] if not provided; integrate {{ADJUNTOS}} when available.
Phase 2 - Semantic layer: model the domain datasets and their certified definitions before thinking about visualizations; adjust the detail of definitions to the maturity level {{MADUREZ_ANALITICA}}.
Phase 3 - Templates: derive the visualization library from real business questions, not from chart types.
Phase 4 - Guardrails: define access, quality, certification, and performance controls as an applicable matrix, with action for each violation.
Phase 5 - Enablement and metrics: design user levels, their learning path, the content certification flow, and the success dashboard with baselines and one mitigated adoption risk.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- Every dataset declares grain, certified metrics with their business formula and field source; certified is separated from experimental and the homonymous-metric anti-pattern is named.
- Every visualization template indicates the business question it answers, when to use it, and when NOT to.
- Guardrails cover row-level and domain access, PII, freshness, quality, visible certification, and performance, expressed as a matrix with action for each violation.
- The three user levels have a learning path, promotion criteria, and an explicit process — with a responsible party — for certifying ad hoc content.
