--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Framing: validate columns, types, and size of each segment; declare assumptions and unit of analysis.
Phase 2 Sanitation: report nulls and outliers, apply TRATAMIENTO_OUTLIERS, fix the comparable base, and record excluded rows.
Phase 3 Summary and shape: table of statistics per segment + shape description with histograms and comparative boxplot (or data ready to plot).
Phase 4 Contrast: compare segments with effect size and warn where the sample (n < N_MINIMO) or imbalance prevents concluding.
Phase 5 Synthesis: prioritized findings with evidence, magnitude, and action; inferences not supported by data tagged [ASSUMPTION].
Edge cases: segment with very low n = inconclusive; long tail of segments = group into Others with justification; zeros or negatives that are relevant = flag; do not assert significance without n and explicit assumptions.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- METRICA and VARIABLE_SEGMENTO confirmed; ambiguous columns are asked, not assumed.
- Coverage per segment reported (n, nulls, proportion of missing values) and comparable base fixed.
- Missing value and outlier treatment explicit, consistent, and traced (affected rows).
- Each segment shows n, mean, median, standard deviation, coefficient of variation, min, P25/P50/P75, P90, max, and interquartile range.
- Shape of each distribution described (skewness, tails, multimodality) with histograms and comparative boxplot, or data ready to plot if not possible.
- Differences quantified with effect size; comparisons with n < N_MINIMO or strong imbalance flagged as inconclusive.
- No invented values; every inference not supported by data tagged [ASSUMPTION].
Expected deliverable: comparative table of statistics per segment + shape descriptions (with histograms/boxplot or data to plot them) + 2-3 prioritized findings with numerical evidence, segment, magnitude, and suggested action linked to the decision.
spec-datos_eda_serie_temporal_descomposi:
[inputs]
- SERIE: {{SERIE}} > Data with a date/time column and a numeric value column (sales, sessions, demand, etc.)
- FRECUENCIA: {{FRECUENCIA}} > Temporal granularity of the observations (daily, weekly, monthly, hourly)
- PERIODO_ESTACIONAL: {{PERIODO_ESTACIONAL}} > Number of observations per cycle (7 daily-weekly, 12 monthly-annual, 24 hourly-daily) (optional)
- OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO: {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} > Decision or question that the decomposition must inform
- UMBRAL_ANOMALIA: {{UMBRAL_ANOMALIA}} > Criterion for flagging anomalous residuals, e.g. more than 3 standard deviations or interquartile range (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Before forecasting or making decisions about temporal data, it is necessary to understand what drives them. A raw series mixes three signals: an underlying trend, a recurring seasonal pattern, and a residual that contains both noise and the true anomalies. Decomposing {{SERIE}} separates those signals: it unlocks an honest reading of the real level (without the effect of the day of the week or month), detection of anomalies that would otherwise remain hidden within the cycle, and a clean base for modeling. The result feeds directly into {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}. Risk to avoid: a poor decomposition contaminates every downstream decision, because trend and seasonality that are poorly separated inflate or hide real signals.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior data analyst specializing in time series, with mastery of classical decomposition and STL, exploratory diagnosis, and business reading.
Deliverable: decomposition report for {{SERIE}} with component summary table, prioritized anomaly list, and monitoring strategy. Steps:
1. Audit temporal quality: confirm that {{FRECUENCIA}} matches the timestamps; verify chronological order, gaps, duplicate dates, missing values, and history sufficiency (recommended minimum: 2 complete seasonal cycles, ideal 3+). Report each incident and propose treatment (interpolation, imputation, exclusion) without altering data silently.
2. Choose additive vs. multiplicative model based on whether the seasonal amplitude is constant (additive) or grows with the level (multiplicative); justify with the variance-magnitude relationship. If there are zeros or negatives, direct multiplicative does not apply: declare it and opt for additive or transformation.
3. Confirm or adjust {{PERIODO_ESTACIONAL}}; evaluate multiple seasonality (e.g. intraday + intraweek) and prefer STL when seasonality evolves or outliers are present, given its robustness.
4. Separate trend, seasonality, and residual: describe direction and breaks of the trend, profile of the seasonal pattern (peaks and troughs), and strength of each component (explained variance). Verify that the residual retains no structure (autocorrelation or residual seasonality); if it does, declare incomplete decomposition.
5. Detect anomalies in the residual according to {{UMBRAL_ANOMALIA}}; for each report the date, magnitude, sign, and a verifiable causal hypothesis, distinguishing a point anomaly from a sustained level change.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Diagnosis: profile the series and its temporal integrity before touching components.
Phase 2 - Model: fix additive/multiplicative or STL and seasonal period with observed evidence.
Phase 3 - Decomposition: isolate the three components, interpret each in business language, and validate that the residual is clean.
Phase 4 - Anomalies and close: flag extreme residuals, formulate hypotheses, distinguish point vs. level change, and consolidate summary table plus monitoring.
Tag each assumption as [ASSUMPTION]; do not impute absent values or choose a model without declaring it. If {{FRECUENCIA}}, {{PERIODO_ESTACIONAL}}, or {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} are missing or clash with the data, or if history is insufficient to estimate seasonality, ask before continuing instead of forcing the analysis.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Temporal integrity audited: order, gaps, duplicates, missing values, and history sufficiency reported with proposed treatment.
- [ ] Additive vs. multiplicative vs. STL choice justified with the variance-magnitude relationship and data constraints (zeros/negatives).
- [ ] Seasonal period confirmed and multiple seasonality evaluated.
- [ ] Three components described with direction, breaks, seasonal profile, and strength (explained variance).
- [ ] Residual verified without remaining structure; if it retains structure, declared.
- [ ] Anomalies with date, magnitude, sign, and verifiable hypothesis, distinguishing point vs. level change, according to the declared threshold.
- [ ] Assumptions tagged [ASSUMPTION]; no value invented or imputed silently.
- [ ] Findings tied to {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}.
Expected deliverable: report with component summary table (strength and reading of each), prioritized anomaly list, and an actionable monitoring strategy.
spec-datos_eda_hipotesis_a_preguntas:
[inputs]
- PREGUNTA_NEGOCIO: {{PREGUNTA_NEGOCIO}} > Business question as it arrives, even if vague (e.g. "why did sales fall")
- DECISION_A_TOMAR: {{DECISION_A_TOMAR}} > Decision or action that depends on the answer; orients scope and prioritization
- FUENTES_DISPONIBLES: {{FUENTES_DISPONIBLES}} > Tables, systems, or accessible datasets and their known state (optional)
- VENTANA_Y_POBLACION: {{VENTANA_Y_POBLACION}} > Time period and segment/population of interest (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A vague business question consumes weeks of analysis without converging because no one defined what is being tested or what evidence would be sufficient to decide; the ultimate risk is data-dredging — finding spurious patterns that do not withstand replication. Converting it into an explicit analysis plan (falsifiable hypotheses + data required + verification method + threshold) before querying a single table unlocks {{DECISION_A_TOMAR}}: it focuses effort, bounds the search space, and produces conclusions that are defensible before management. A plan published in advance also prevents moving the threshold after seeing the data.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior data scientist with experience in product analytics, experimental design, and translation of business questions into exploratory analysis plans.
Deliverable: a structured analysis plan that transforms {{PREGUNTA_NEGOCIO}} into executable work using {{FUENTES_DISPONIBLES}} over {{VENTANA_Y_POBLACION}}. Produce in this order:
1. Question rewritten precisely: what is measured, the unit of analysis, and the decision it unlocks.
2. Three to five falsifiable hypotheses: each as a testable statement with a directional prediction and the exact condition that would refute it.
3. Data required per hypothesis: sources/tables, fields, granularity, temporal window, and population.
4. Verification method per hypothesis: technique (cohort comparison, metric decomposition, correlation, mean difference test, time series), decision metric, and signal/noise threshold.
5. Confounders and biases: seasonality, segment mixing (Simpson's paradox), missing data, reverse causality, and how to control for each.
6. Execution order prioritized by decision value over data cost, with a stopping rule (which result closes the analysis or invalidates a hypothesis).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Interpret: rewrite the question, fix the unit of analysis and the dependent decision; declare each assumption as [ASSUMPTION]. If the decision, sources, or window/population are missing, ask before proceeding.
Phase 2 - Structure hypotheses: derive candidate causes (non-overlapping and, jointly, exhaustive); formulate each as a falsifiable statement with its directional prediction and its refutation test. Include at least one measurement hypothesis (the data changed, not the phenomenon) and one external/market hypothesis.
Phase 3 - Map evidence: per hypothesis link required data + method + metric + signal/noise threshold; discard hypotheses that are not testable with the available data or explicitly flag the missing data. Distinguish signal from normal variation: define what magnitude and persistence count as a finding.
Phase 4 - Harden and prioritize: list confounders/biases with their concrete control (segment, normalize by exposure, comparable window, placebo test), order execution by decision value over data cost, fix the stopping rule, and close with the open questions you need resolved.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
- Each hypothesis is falsifiable: it explicitly states what result would refute it, not just what would confirm it.
- Each hypothesis has data required with granularity and window, plus a method with metric and signal/noise threshold; nothing is left without a verification path.
- The hypotheses do not overlap and cover the plausible space of causes; at least one measurement hypothesis and one external one are included, and seasonality, segment mixing, and reverse causality are named as risks with their control.
- Every unconfirmed business data point appears as [ASSUMPTION]; missing data is asked for, not invented.
- The prioritization justifies the order by decision value over {{DECISION_A_TOMAR}} and data cost, and includes a stopping rule.
Expected deliverable: a 1-2 page analysis plan, ready for an analyst to execute query by query, with a final section of open questions.
spec-datos_eda_test_significancia:
[inputs]
- PREGUNTA_NEGOCIO: {{PREGUNTA_NEGOCIO}} > Decision question motivating the test (e.g. "did the redesign increase conversion?")
- VARIABLES_Y_TIPOS: {{VARIABLES_Y_TIPOS}} > Variables involved and their type/scale (continuous, ordinal, nominal, count)
- NUM_GRUPOS: {{NUM_GRUPOS}} > Number of groups or categories to compare
- DISENO_MUESTRAL: {{DISENO_MUESTRAL}} > Independent observations or paired/repeated measures
- TAMANO_MUESTRA: {{TAMANO_MUESTRA}} > Total and per-group sample size
- ALFA: {{ALFA}} > Significance level and directionality (optional; default 0.05 two-tailed)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
An observed difference or association in the data may be real or sampling noise. Choosing the wrong test, ignoring its assumptions, or reading a p-value as if it were a magnitude produces invalid conclusions that propagate into costly business decisions. Resolving {{PREGUNTA_NEGOCIO}} with the correct test, its verified assumptions, and a quantified effect size unlocks a defensible and auditable decision, and avoids confusing significance with impact.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior applied statistician with experience in exploratory analysis, experimental design, and product inference.
Deliverable: a reproducible hypothesis-contrast report. Steps:
1. Classify each variable from {{VARIABLES_Y_TIPOS}} by type and scale (continuous, ordinal, nominal, count).
2. Formulate null and alternative hypotheses in plain language, declare one- or two-tailed directionality and fix {{ALFA}} (default 0.05).
3. Verify the assumptions of the candidate family and document each check: normality (Shapiro-Wilk or Q-Q), homogeneity of variances (Levene), independence, minimum expected frequencies in contingency, influential outliers.
4. Select the test using an explicit decision tree for {{NUM_GRUPOS}} and {{DISENO_MUESTRAL}}: Student's or Welch's t (two independent means), paired t (repeated measures), one-way ANOVA (three or more groups), chi-square of independence or Fisher's exact (two categoricals), or the non-parametric Mann-Whitney, Wilcoxon or Kruskal-Wallis when assumptions are violated.
5. Run the test and report the statistic, degrees of freedom, exact p-value, appropriate effect size (Cohen's d, eta squared, Cramér's V, or rank-biserial r), and the 95% confidence interval.
6. Interpret in business language separating statistical significance from practical relevance; correct for multiple comparisons (Bonferroni or Holm) if more than one contrast; indicate a post-hoc test after a significant global result; warn about low power and small {{TAMANO_MUESTRA}}.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 – Framing: tabulate variables and types, set hypotheses, directionality, and {{ALFA}}.
Phase 2 – Diagnosis: run assumption checks and log each result (verified, not assumed).
Phase 3 – Selection: apply the decision tree and justify the chosen test against the discarded alternatives.
Phase 4 – Calculation: run the test, the effect size, and its confidence interval; apply multiple correction and post-hoc if applicable.
Phase 5 – Interpretation: translate to business decision, separate significance from relevance, declare limitations and next step.
Mark any assumed data as [ASSUMPTION]; if a critical input is missing, ask for it before calculating rather than inventing it.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Each variable classified by type and scale.
- [ ] Explicit null and alternative hypotheses, with directionality and {{ALFA}} declared.
- [ ] Log with the result of each verified assumption (not assumed).
- [ ] Visible decision tree justifying the chosen test and the discarded alternatives.
- [ ] Complete results: statistic, df, exact p-value, effect size, and 95% CI.
- [ ] Explicit distinction between statistical significance and practical relevance.
- [ ] Multiple comparison correction and post-hoc when applicable.
- [ ] Power/small-sample warning and assumed data marked [ASSUMPTION].
Expected deliverable: report with variable table, hypotheses, assumption log, chosen and justified test, numerical results, actionable interpretation, and recommendation of the next analytical step.
spec-datos_eda_segmentacion_clustering:
[inputs]
- TIPO_ENTIDAD: {{TIPO_ENTIDAD}} > What is being segmented: customers, products, users, transactions, branches
- GRANO_FILA: {{GRANO_FILA}} > What a row in the dataset represents (one row = a unique entity or an aggregated event)
- OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO: {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} > Decision unlocked with the segments (prioritize campaigns, design pricing, reduce churn)
- ALGORITMO: {{ALGORITMO}} > Preferred clustering method: K-Means, K-Medoids, agglomerative hierarchical, or DBSCAN
- FEATURES_CANDIDATAS: {{FEATURES_CANDIDATAS}} > List of candidate feature columns, separating numerical from categorical
- RANGO_K: {{RANGO_K}} > Range of clusters to evaluate (e.g. 2 to 10) (optional; ignore if ALGORITMO is DBSCAN, which does not receive k)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
An analyst or business leader has a dataset of {{TIPO_ENTIDAD}} and needs to discover natural segments currently hidden in order to make the decision of {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}. The recurring risk is producing meaningless cluster labels: numbers without names, sizes, or levers. This prompt unlocks a reproducible workflow that converts raw data into actionable segments, with the strategy of delivering decisions, not partitions. Risks to avoid upfront: data-leakage features that inflate artificial separation, uncontrolled scale that biases distance, and k chosen solely by a mathematical metric without a business reading.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior data scientist specializing in unsupervised segmentation and entity analytics, with expertise in scikit-learn and business translation.
Deliverable: a reproducible clustering workflow plus a segment profiling table, Python code, and recommendations. Steps:
1. Confirm {{TIPO_ENTIDAD}}, {{GRANO_FILA}}, {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}, and {{ALGORITMO}}; if data is missing, ask for it before continuing. Declare whether a row is a unique entity or an aggregated event (a mixed grain invalidates the clustering).
2. Select and justify features from {{FEATURES_CANDIDATAS}}: separate numerical from categorical, discard identifiers and leakage variables (those that only exist after the decision or encode the outcome), define treatment of nulls and outliers. Flag redundant or collinear features that distort distance.
3. Scale numerical features (StandardScaler by default, RobustScaler if strong outliers) and encode categoricals (one-hot for low cardinality, frequency or grouping for high cardinality), justifying why distance is sensitive to scale. If categoricals dominate, consider K-Medoids with mixed distance instead of K-Means.
4. Choose k from {{RANGO_K}}: report the elbow method (inertia), silhouette coefficient, and Davies-Bouldin index, and recommend a justified k that balances metric and actionability (an actionable k beats a purely mathematical optimum). If {{ALGORITMO}} is DBSCAN, replace the k search with eps and min_samples calibration via k-distance plot.
5. Fit the final model with a fixed seed (random_state), assign each entity to its cluster, and validate stability through resampling or re-initialization. Report residual, tiny, or noise clusters (DBSCAN: label -1).
6. Profile each cluster: absolute and percentage size, means or medians of key features, 2–3 differentiating traits, a descriptive name, and a lever aligned to {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 – Framing: validate entity, grain, and objective; mark with [ASSUMPTION] any unconfirmed data.
Phase 2 – Preparation: clean features, treat nulls and outliers, scale and encode reproducibly (scikit-learn pipeline); exclude identifiers and leakage.
Phase 3 – k Selection: sweep {{RANGO_K}}, tabulate inertia, silhouette, and Davies-Bouldin, converge on a k with explicit justification and business reading.
Phase 4 – Modeling: fit the final algorithm with a fixed random_state, assign labels, verify stability, and report noise or degenerate clusters.
Phase 5 – Profiling and translation: describe each cluster quantitatively and qualitatively, name it, and associate a business lever.
Edge case: if the dataset does not support meaningful clustering (insufficient features, silhouette < 0.1 across the whole range, one dominant cluster), declare it and recommend reformulating features or grain instead of forcing segments.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Row grain declared (unique entity vs. aggregated event) and consistent.
- [ ] Every feature used is justified; identifiers, leakage, and collinears excluded.
- [ ] Explicit and reproducible scaling and encoding (pipeline + fixed seed).
- [ ] k choice supported by at least two internal metrics plus an actionability reading (or eps/min_samples calibration if DBSCAN).
- [ ] Model stability validated; noise or residual clusters reported.
- [ ] Each cluster has absolute and percentage size, differentiating traits, a name, and a business lever.
- [ ] Assumptions marked [ASSUMPTION]; no invented numbers or metrics.
- [ ] Executable Python code (pandas + scikit-learn) consistent with the described workflow.
- [ ] If the dataset does not support segments, it is declared rather than forced.
Expected deliverable: segment profiling table, reproducible code block, and paragraph of actionable recommendations for {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}.
spec-datos_eda_analisis_causa_raiz:
[inputs]
- METRICA: {{METRICA}} > Metric that dropped and its exact definition; if it is a rate or average, specify numerator and denominator (e.g. conversion = orders/sessions, average ticket, monthly churn)
- PERIODOS: {{PERIODOS}} > Base period and comparison period with their values; indicate the length of each to verify comparability (e.g. April 3.8% vs May 3.1%, both full months)
- DIMENSIONES: {{DIMENSIONES}} > Dimensions available to slice the metric: segment, product, channel, region, device, cohort
- DATOS: {{DATOS}} > Whether disaggregated data by dimension is available or only the aggregate; volume/rate by segment in both periods; reference to attachments if applicable
- DECISION: {{DECISION}} > What decision or action depends on isolating the cause (stop, revert, reallocate, communicate) and its horizon
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A metric dropped and the organization reacts with cross-hypotheses and no evidence to order them. The risk is not only not knowing why: it is acting on the wrong symptom — increasing investment in a channel that actually improved, or blaming a product that merely lost weight in the mix. The purpose of this analysis is to transform a diffuse drop into a quantified bridge that decomposes the variation in {{METRICA}} between {{PERIODOS}} into its volume, mix, and rate effects, and that isolates the real driver with its exact magnitude. What is unlocked: {{DECISION}} is made on the correct cause, not on the average that hides it. MetodologIA contributes here the rigor of variance decomposition applied to a real business problem.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior data analyst specializing in metric root-cause analysis, expert in variance bridge (mix/rate/volume), cohort analysis, and Simpson's paradox.
Deliver, in this order:
1. Restate the question: "Explain the variation in {{METRICA}} between {{PERIODOS}} (Δ = X), isolating its cause".
2. Classify {{METRICA}} as an additive total, rate/ratio, or average, and declare which decomposition applies (additive bridge for totals; mix/rate separation for ratios; weight-based averaging for averages).
3. Decompose Δ into a volume effect (change in total size), a mix/composition effect (change in mix between segments with different rates), and a rate/performance effect (change within each segment), using {{DIMENSIONES}} and isolating each term with the others held constant (one-factor-at-a-time).
4. Build the bridge from the base to the current value in a table and verify that the sum of effects closes with residual ≈ 0; if it does not close, declare and explain the cross term (mix×rate interaction).
5. Apply the Simpson test: check whether the aggregate contradicts the majority of segments and, if so, declare it as the central finding.
6. Isolate the 2–3 segments that concentrate the drop (Pareto) and quantify each one's contribution to Δ in points and as a percentage of the change.
7. Name the dominant driver unambiguously (which effect and in which segment) and formulate 2–3 falsifiable business-cause hypotheses, marking [ASSUMPTION] for those not backed by data, each with the cut that would confirm it.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 · Framing and comparability: confirm the metric and its definition, the periods with their values and length, the dimensions, data granularity, and the decision at stake. Verify that the periods are comparable (same length, same seasonality, no missing days or change in the metric's definition); if they are not, normalize or declare it as a limitation. If a critical piece of data is missing or only the aggregate is available, ask for it in a single batch before calculating and do not invent figures.
Phase 2 · Classification: classify the metric (total / rate / average) to choose the correct decomposition; an aggregate rate requires separating mix from rate, a total admits an additive bridge, an average is weighted by segment weight.
Phase 3 · Decomposition: calculate the volume effect, mix effect, and rate effect by segment, isolating each term with the others held constant; document the isolation order because it can generate cross terms.
Phase 4 · Bridge and closure: build the base-to-current bridge table, verify residual ≈ 0, and explain any cross term that does not close; report the interaction if material.
Phase 5 · Simpson and Pareto: detect aggregate-vs-segment reversal and concentrate the explanation on the 2–3 segments that move Δ; discard confounders before attributing (seasonality, campaign mix, data quality).
Phase 6 · Cause and hypotheses: translate the dominant driver into falsifiable business hypotheses; explicitly distinguish correlation from causality and name the data cut or experiment that would confirm each hypothesis.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
- Periods verified as comparable (length, seasonality, stable definition); any adjustment or limitation declared.
- The metric was classified (total / rate / average) and the chosen decomposition corresponds to that type.
- The total Δ is calculated and the question restated before decomposing.
- The bridge separates the volume effect, mix effect, and rate effect, and the sum of effects reconstructs the current value with residual ≈ 0 (or the residual/cross term is declared and explained).
- The Simpson test was applied explicitly; if there is an aggregate-vs-segment reversal, it is named as the central finding.
- The 2–3 segments that concentrate the drop are isolated, with their contribution to Δ quantified in points and as a % of the change.
- The dominant driver is named unambiguously (mix, rate, or volume, and in which segment), without diluting it into "several reasons".
- Causality and correlation were distinguished; plausible confounders were flagged.
- No figure was invented; missing data and assumptions are marked [ASSUMPTION], with the cut that would resolve them.
Expected deliverable: variance bridge table (effect by effect summing to Δ) + dominant driver named with its magnitude + 2–3 falsifiable cause hypotheses with the data query that confirms each, in neutral Spanish and professional tone.
spec-datos_eda_muestreo_representativo:
[inputs]
- POBLACION_OBJETIVO: {{POBLACION_OBJETIVO}} > Universe to study and unit of analysis (e.g. active customers, transactions, sensors)
- TAMANO_POBLACION: {{TAMANO_POBLACION}} > Known or estimated population size N; "unknown" if there is no closed sampling frame
- VARIABLE_CLAVE: {{VARIABLE_CLAVE}} > Main analysis variable and its scale (proportion, continuous mean, count)
- NIVEL_CONFIANZA: {{NIVEL_CONFIANZA}} > Target confidence level (optional; default 95%, z=1.96)
- MARGEN_ERROR: {{MARGEN_ERROR}} > Admissible margin of error e in the estimate (optional; default 5%)
- TAMANO_EFECTO_MINIMO: {{TAMANO_EFECTO_MINIMO}} > Minimum effect to detect for the power verification (optional)
- VARIABLES_ESTRATIFICACION: {{VARIABLES_ESTRATIFICACION}} > Candidate variables for strata or clusters (optional; e.g. region, segment, period)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A reliable exploratory analysis starts with a sample that faithfully represents the target population: a poorly designed sample contaminates every subsequent conclusion, while a solid one enables valid estimates at a fraction of the cost of processing the entire universe. Designing the sampling before touching the data unlocks defensible inferences, sufficient power, and methodological traceability for audit. The goal is to produce an applicable scheme for POBLACION_OBJETIVO that preserves representativeness with respect to VARIABLE_CLAVE and honestly declares the biases the design cannot control.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior statistician specializing in sampling design and inference, with experience in surveys and in sampling from operational databases.
Deliverable: an actionable sampling design sheet. Steps:
1. Characterize the population: N (TAMANO_POBLACION), available sampling frame and its coverage, unit of analysis, VARIABLE_CLAVE and its scale, and the inferential objective (estimate, compare, or detect a difference). Declare as [ASSUMPTION] any data not provided; if information is missing that would change the technique or make the calculation infeasible, ask for it before proceeding.
2. Recommend the technique among simple random, systematic, stratified, cluster, or multi-stage. Justify against the population structure and the objective; explicitly discard non-chosen alternatives with their reason and name the main risk of the chosen one (e.g. hidden periodicity in systematic, inflated variance in clusters).
3. Calculate sample size n step by step. Proportions: n0 = z² × p × (1-p) / e² (use p=0.5 as the worst case if no prior estimate). Means: n0 = z² × sigma² / e². Apply the finite-population correction n = n0 / (1 + (n0-1)/N) when N is known and the fraction n0/N exceeds 5%. Adjust for design effect (n_final = n × deff) if there are clusters or strata, and for expected non-response or eligibility rate (n_to_issue = n_final / rate). Use NIVEL_CONFIANZA and MARGEN_ERROR; declare p, sigma, and deff.
4. Verify power to detect TAMANO_EFECTO_MINIMO: declare alpha, target power (typically 0.80), and the implied test; if power is insufficient, increase n and take the larger of the margin-of-error n and the power n.
5. If stratifying according to VARIABLES_ESTRATIFICACION: define strata, allocation (proportional, or Neyman when variance differs between strata or sampling cost varies), and distribution of n by stratum in a table.
6. Representativeness validation plan: variables to compare sample vs. population, goodness-of-fit test (chi-square for categoricals, Kolmogorov-Smirnov for continuous), and weighting or post-stratification plan for coverage bias or non-response.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 – Diagnosis: consolidate inputs and assumptions; classify the objective (estimate proportion, mean, or detect a difference) and evaluate the sampling frame coverage (undercoverage, duplicates, outdated frame).
Phase 2 – Design: select and justify the technique; instantiate the formulas with the declared parameters, showing each substitution and intermediate result.
Phase 3 – Verification: compare the margin-of-error n against the power n and against the operational budget; reconcile discrepancies, apply corrections (finite, deff, non-response), and leave the final n and the n-to-issue.
Phase 4 – Validation: deliver the representativeness control plan, the weighting procedure, and the residual limitations of the design.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Inferential objective declared (estimate / compare / detect) and frame coverage evaluated.
- [ ] Technique justified against the population structure, with discarded alternatives and main risk named.
- [ ] Explicit n formula with z, e, and p/sigma declared; finite-population correction applied when applicable.
- [ ] Adjustments for design effect and non-response applied or marked as not applicable with reason.
- [ ] Power verified (alpha, power, effect, test); final n = larger of margin-of-error n and power n.
- [ ] Stratum allocation defined if stratifying (proportional or Neyman, with justification).
- [ ] Representativeness validation and weighting plan included.
- [ ] Limitations and residual biases declared; all assumed numbers marked [ASSUMPTION]; no invented data.
Expected deliverable: sampling design sheet with recommended technique and discarded alternatives, final n and n-to-issue with visible numerical derivation, assumptions table, stratum allocation if applicable, validation and weighting plan, and explicit limitations; ready to execute.
spec-datos_eda_analisis_pareto:
[inputs]
- DIMENSION_ANALISIS: {{DIMENSION_ANALISIS}} > What is being ranked and prioritized (customers, products, defect causes, ticket reasons, regions)
- COLUMNA_CATEGORIA: {{COLUMNA_CATEGORIA}} > Name of the column that identifies each category to accumulate (the granularity of the Pareto axis)
- COLUMNA_VALOR: {{COLUMNA_VALOR}} > Name of the column with the effect metric to sum; MUST be additive (summable without losing meaning) and comparable across categories
- EFECTO_OBJETIVO: {{EFECTO_OBJETIVO}} > Which effect is to be concentrated and understood (revenue, cost, defects, tickets, hours, churn)
- ACCION_PRIORIZADA: {{ACCION_PRIORIZADA}} > Decision the analysis must enable (where to focus improvement, retention, quality control, cost reduction)
- UMBRAL_CORTE: {{UMBRAL_CORTE}} > Cumulative percentage defining the vital few (default 80%); adjustable to 70 or 90 depending on focus appetite (optional)
- RESTRICCIONES_CONOCIDAS: {{RESTRICCIONES_CONOCIDAS}} > Period, segment, exclusions, or data limits to consider (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Effort and attention are spread equally across too many categories, when almost always a minority concentrates the majority of the effect. Applying Pareto before acting unlocks a defensible prioritization: it concentrates resources where they move the result and frees focus from the tail that contributes little. The finding directly feeds the ACCION_PRIORIZADA decision and the period's effort allocation. Risk to avoid: forcing the 80/20 narrative onto a flat distribution, where cutting the tail would destroy value without concentrating anything.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior data analyst, fifteen years applying Pareto analysis and distribution reading to prioritize operational and commercial decisions.
Deliverable: a Pareto analysis over DIMENSION_ANALISIS plus an actionable prioritization recommendation. Steps:
1. Validate inputs; if DIMENSION_ANALISIS, COLUMNA_CATEGORIA, COLUMNA_VALOR, or EFECTO_OBJETIVO are missing or ambiguous, ask for them in a single batch before continuing. Confirm that COLUMNA_VALOR is additive (summable); if it is an average, ratio, percentage, or count of distinct items, warn that summing it is meaningless and ask for the base metric.
2. Aggregate COLUMNA_VALOR by COLUMNA_CATEGORIA, sort in descending order, and build the table with value, percentage of total, and cumulative percentage by category. Handle nulls, negative signs, and duplicates explicitly (do not discard them silently).
3. Identify the cut per UMBRAL_CORTE (default 80%): the categories whose cumulative total reaches it; report how many there are and what fraction of the universe of categories they represent (e.g. 6 out of 40 = 15%).
4. Name the vital few against the trivial many and declare the shape of the distribution with a simple metric: what % of the effect the top 20% of categories concentrates.
5. For each vital category, propose a concrete action linked to ACCION_PRIORIZADA, ordered by expected impact, and close with what to attack first and what to leave in the tail.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 – Framing: confirm dimension, columns, effect, threshold, and action; do not invent data or assume the shape of the distribution.
Phase 2 – Calculation: aggregate and sort in descending order; calculate value, percentage, and cumulative percentage; apply the UMBRAL_CORTE cut and quantify the vital group (how many categories and what fraction of the universe).
Phase 3 – Critical reading: issue an explicit verdict on whether the distribution is concentrated (Pareto applies) or flat (it does not apply and prioritizing by volume would be misleading); re-verify that COLUMNA_VALOR is additive and comparable; flag biases of period, seasonality, coarse grouping, or inconsistent granularity; treat any residual 'Other' category separately because it would inflate a false vital; mark anything unsupported as [ASSUMPTION].
Phase 4 – Decision: translate each vital category into an action linked to ACCION_PRIORIZADA, order by expected impact considering effort and feasibility, and resolve what to prioritize and what to defer.
Edge case: if two or three categories capture almost all the effect, flag the concentration and dependency risk, not just the focus opportunity.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist: table sorted in descending order with value, percentage of total, and cumulative percentage; UMBRAL_CORTE cut quantified (how many categories and what fraction of the universe); vital few named one by one; concentration metric reported (% of effect in the top 20%); explicit verdict concentrated vs. flat; COLUMNA_VALOR validated as additive and comparable; nulls, negatives, and 'Other' residual treated without hiding them; biases declared; assumptions marked [ASSUMPTION]; zero invented figures. Expected deliverable: Pareto table + named list of the vital group + decision paragraph indicating what to attack first, what to leave in the tail and why, ready for period effort assignment.
spec-datos_eda_funnel_dropoff:
[inputs]
- ETAPAS_FUNNEL: {{ETAPAS_FUNNEL}} > Funnel stages in order (e.g.: visit > registration > cart > checkout > purchase)
- VOLUMENES_POR_ETAPA: {{VOLUMENES_POR_ETAPA}} > Unique users or events reaching each stage, aligned to the order above
- PERIODO_Y_SEGMENTO: {{PERIODO_Y_SEGMENTO}} > Date range and segment (channel, device, geography) the data covers
- OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO: {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} > North metric or result to be improved (e.g.: increase purchases, reduce checkout abandonment)
- BENCHMARK_CONVERSION: {{BENCHMARK_CONVERSION}} > Target or reference conversion for comparison (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need to decide where to concentrate the optimization effort in my conversion funnel. Without a clear diagnosis, the team invests in low-impact improvements on stages that are not the real bottleneck. A rigorous stage-by-stage analysis unlocks a decision: which is the single transition that, if improved, moves the north metric the most, and what to test first. The business objective is {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} over the period and segment {{PERIODO_Y_SEGMENTO}}.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior product and data analyst, specializing in conversion rate optimization (CRO) and funnel analysis, with the judgment to distinguish correlation from cause and to prioritize by impact over effort.

Deliverable: a funnel diagnosis with prioritized hypotheses. Steps:
1. Build the funnel table over {{ETAPAS_FUNNEL}} and {{VOLUMENES_POR_ETAPA}}: for each stage show users entering, stage-to-stage conversion (step N+1 / step N), cumulative conversion (step N / first stage), and absolute users lost in each transition.
2. Identify the largest drop-off point. Explicitly declare whether you are prioritizing it by the highest drop-off percentage or by the highest absolute volume of lost users, and why; when both criteria diverge, show both readings and recommend based on {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}.
3. Compare against {{BENCHMARK_CONVERSION}} if provided, marking the stages below the reference; if no benchmark is available, say so and do not invent a target.
4. Formulate 3 to 5 improvement hypotheses for the critical drop-off, ordered by impact-to-effort ratio. For each one: probable causal mechanism, validation method (A/B test, cohort analysis, segmentation, instrumentation review), and expected impact on conversion (range, not exact figure).
5. Close with a data-quality note: measurement risks (double-counting, unfired events, attribution window, bot traffic, mixed segments, non-representative period) that qualify the conclusions.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 – Input validation: confirm that each stage in {{ETAPAS_FUNNEL}} has its volume in {{VOLUMENES_POR_ETAPA}} and that the sequence is monotonically decreasing. If a stage, its volume, or the period is not clear, do not invent figures: ask for them before calculating. If a stage grows relative to the previous one, stop and flag possible double-counting, an out-of-order stage, or user re-entry before continuing. Mark any assumption with [ASSUMPTION].
Phase 2 – Quantification: calculate conversions and absolute losses; show each column's formula once only. Round with judgment and keep the unit (users vs. events) consistent.
Phase 3 – Diagnosis: locate the critical drop-off and justify the prioritization criterion; name explicitly the winning transition (the one that most moves the north metric if improved).
Phase 4 – Hypotheses and validation: derive hypotheses treated as explanations to falsify, never as confirmed causes; for each one define what evidence would confirm or refute it.
Phase 5 – Safeguard: issue the data-quality note before closing.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Complete funnel table: entries, stage-to-stage conversion, cumulative conversion, and absolute lost users per transition.
- [ ] Formulas for each column stated and arithmetic consistent with {{VOLUMENES_POR_ETAPA}}; unit (users vs. events) uniform.
- [ ] Coherence validated: decreasing sequence; any growth or jump flagged as anomaly before diagnosing.
- [ ] Largest drop-off identified with declared criterion (percentage vs. volume), discrepancies shown, and winning transition named.
- [ ] 3 to 5 hypotheses, each with causal mechanism, validation method, and expected impact, ordered by impact/effort.
- [ ] Hypotheses presented as explanations to validate with their falsification criterion; correlation not presented as cause.
- [ ] Missing figures requested, never invented; assumptions marked [ASSUMPTION]; non-existent benchmark not invented.
- [ ] Data-quality note with at least three measurement risks and their effect on the conclusions.
Expected deliverable: funnel table + critical drop-off diagnostic paragraph with the winning transition + prioritized list of 3 to 5 hypotheses + data-quality note.
spec-datos_storytelling_pregunta_a_insig:
[inputs]
- ANALISIS_FUENTE: {{ANALISIS_FUENTE}} > Table, chart, resolved query, or list of already-calculated findings to be distilled
- DECISION_A_HABILITAR: {{DECISION_A_HABILITAR}} > The concrete decision the insight must allow to be taken (e.g. where to invest the quarter's budget)
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Who receives the insight and their level (e.g. executive committee, product leader, commercial team)
- METRICA_CLAVE: {{METRICA_CLAVE}} > The business metric at stake (e.g. cancellation rate, margin per order, conversion)
- LINEA_BASE: {{LINEA_BASE}} > Reference against which the finding is compared (prior period, target, control segment) (optional)
- HORIZONTE_DECISION: {{HORIZONTE_DECISION}} > When the decision must be made (e.g. this week, before end of quarter); calibrates urgency of the recommendation (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A finished analysis does not move anyone on its own: a table or a chart is raw material, not a decision. The recipient ({{AUDIENCIA}}) does not need to see all the figures — it needs to know what to do with them. This prompt converts {{ANALISIS_FUENTE}} into an actionable insight that enables {{DECISION_A_HABILITAR}} and holds up when someone in the room asks "so what". It unlocks the shift from reporting data to directing decisions, which is where analytics generates value. The risk to neutralize is twofold: the inflated insight (claims more than the source supports) and the inert insight (true but without an actionable consequence).

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior data analyst and business storyteller, with experience presenting findings to executive committees and translating metrics into defensible decisions.

Deliverable: an actionable insight structured from {{ANALISIS_FUENTE}}, ready to open a meeting or an email. Produce, in this order:
1. Central claim: a single sentence with the main finding in business language, not metric language: what changed in {{METRICA_CLAVE}}, by how much, against {{LINEA_BASE}}, and in which period.
2. The 'so what': why that statement matters to {{AUDIENCIA}}; what is gained or lost if no one acts.
3. Business implication: the chained effect on revenue, cost, risk, customer experience, or operational capacity, with approximate magnitude only when the data supports it.
4. Recommendation: one concrete and prioritized action in service of {{DECISION_A_HABILITAR}}, with a suggested owner, horizon (aligned to {{HORIZONTE_DECISION}} when provided), and a verifiable first step.
5. Confidence and monitoring: confidence level (high/medium/low) with its reason (sample size, data quality, presence of {{LINEA_BASE}}, possible causality vs. correlation), key assumptions marked [ASSUMPTION], and the single metric to monitor in order to confirm or refute the decision with its alarm threshold.
6. One-sentence headline: condensed version ready to head a slide or a subject line.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 – Interpret: identify in {{ANALISIS_FUENTE}} the dominant finding (highest magnitude, most relevant to {{DECISION_A_HABILITAR}}) and separate observed fact from interpretation. Discard secondary findings that do not move the decision. If {{ANALISIS_FUENTE}}, {{DECISION_A_HABILITAR}}, or {{AUDIENCIA}} is missing, ask for them before continuing.
Phase 2 – Structure with pyramid: apply the Minto principle (conclusion first, evidence after). The central claim leads; the so-what, the implication, and the recommendation support it. Every comparison declares its {{LINEA_BASE}}; if there is no baseline, say so and lower the confidence.
Phase 3 – Test the 'so what': subject the statement to the so-what test. If it does not produce a real business consequence, reformulate it or downgrade it to contextual data. Mark every estimated figure or assumption with [ASSUMPTION]; never invent numbers not in the source. Distinguish correlation from causality and do not present one as the other.
Phase 4 – Act and calibrate: derive the prioritized recommendation, assign an honest confidence level, and define the single monitoring metric with its threshold. Condense everything in the one-sentence headline.
Edge case: if {{ANALISIS_FUENTE}} only allows description and not decision-making (ambiguous data, no baseline, insufficient sample), declare it explicitly instead of forcing an insight, and indicate what missing piece of data would close {{DECISION_A_HABILITAR}}.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
- The central claim is a single sentence, in business language, and declares magnitude, period, and {{LINEA_BASE}}.
- The 'so what' expresses a real consequence for {{AUDIENCIA}}, not a restatement of the data.
- The recommendation is concrete, prioritized, with owner, horizon, and verifiable first step, and serves {{DECISION_A_HABILITAR}}.
- Fact and interpretation are separated; correlation and causality are not confused; every estimate carries [ASSUMPTION]; no figures absent from {{ANALISIS_FUENTE}}.
- The confidence level has an explicit reason and there is exactly one monitoring metric with a threshold.
- The one-sentence headline is self-sufficient and defensible.
- If the source does not allow decision-making, the output declares it and names the missing piece of data instead of inflating the insight.
Expected deliverable: actionable 6-block insight, dense and without filler, that passes the so-what test and allows {{AUDIENCIA}} to take {{DECISION_A_HABILITAR}} with evidence.
spec-datos_storytelling_estructura_scqa:
[inputs]
- TEMA_REPORTE: {{TEMA_REPORTE}} > Topic and scope of the data report (e.g. quarterly churn, acquisition funnel, campaign performance)
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Who makes the decision upon reading (role and level: board of directors, VP of Product, board) and what they care about
- HALLAZGOS_DATOS: {{HALLAZGOS_DATOS}} > Available results, metrics, and figures (numbers, periods, segments, comparisons, source)
- DECISION_O_ACCION: {{DECISION_O_ACCION}} > Decision or action the report must enable or unlock
- FORMATO_SALIDA: {{FORMATO_SALIDA}} > (optional) Expected final format (one-page memo, slide script, executive summary); default one-page executive memo
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need to convert the findings of {{TEMA_REPORTE}} into a narrative that {{AUDIENCIA}} understands in minutes and uses for {{DECISION_O_ACCION}}. Today the data arrives as tables and charts with no narrative thread: the risk is that the conclusion gets buried under figures, the committee does not see why to act, or the decision is made on the wrong metric. Structuring the report with the SCQA framework of Barbara Minto's Pyramid Principle unlocks a narrative where the thesis comes first, the evidence supports it in an orderly way, and every visual pushes toward the decision rather than merely describing the variable.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior data and executive-communication analyst with fifteen years translating analytical results into committee decisions, expert in the SCQA framework of Barbara Minto's Pyramid Principle.
Deliverable: an executive report in {{FORMATO_SALIDA}} with a thesis title, SCQA opening, pyramid body, actionable recommendation, and decision-oriented visual titles. Steps:
1. SITUATION: one or two sentences of the stable context that {{AUDIENCIA}} already accepts about {{TEMA_REPORTE}} (baseline, current target, status quo), neutral and consensual.
2. COMPLICATION: the change, tension, or anomaly that breaks that stability, anchored in a concrete piece of data from {{HALLAZGOS_DATOS}}; this is where the urgency originates.
3. QUESTION: the single question that complication triggers in {{AUDIENCIA}}, specific and answerable with the data.
4. ANSWER: the thesis that answers the question as the main idea, stated first; below it, in a pyramid, the arguments that support it.
5. PYRAMID: MECE arguments (mutually exclusive, collectively exhaustive), ordered by relevance to {{DECISION_O_ACCION}}, each with its quantified finding.
6. CLOSE: one actionable recommendation with suggested owner and horizon, and one decision-oriented title for each chart or table (say the insight, not the variable).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 – Framing: confirm TEMA_REPORTE, AUDIENCIA, HALLAZGOS_DATOS, and DECISION_O_ACCION; if a key figure or the baseline context is missing, ask for it before continuing (one variable at a time).
Phase 2 – SCQA skeleton: draft S, C, Q, and the R-thesis in a single line each; validate that C quantifies the tension and that Q has a unique answer.
Phase 3 – Evidence pyramid: group HALLAZGOS_DATOS under the thesis in MECE arguments ordered by weight; mark every inference as [ASSUMPTION], separate correlation from cause, and name the source of each figure.
Phase 4 – Executive writing: build thesis title, opening, body, recommendation, and visual titles in {{FORMATO_SALIDA}}; quantify the impact in the unit that matters to AUDIENCIA.
Phase 5 – Verification: check for a single main message, zero invented figures, overlaps or gaps in the pyramid resolved, and every visual pushing toward {{DECISION_O_ACCION}}.
Edge cases: if the data does not support a single thesis, declare the uncertainty and propose the missing piece of data; if the complication does not yet have a solid figure, mark it [ASSUMPTION] and try to confirm it; if AUDIENCIA mixes levels, prioritize the highest-ranking decision-maker.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] SITUATION states stable and consensual context, with no thesis or judgment.
- [ ] COMPLICATION breaks stability and is anchored in a real quantified piece of data from HALLAZGOS_DATOS (or marked [ASSUMPTION] if not).
- [ ] QUESTION is unique, specific, and answerable with the available data.
- [ ] ANSWER is the thesis and comes first (top-down), not at the end.
- [ ] Pyramid arguments are MECE and ordered by relevance to DECISION_O_ACCION.
- [ ] Each argument has a quantified finding with its source; every inference is marked [ASSUMPTION]; no causality confused with correlation.
- [ ] There is a single main message; no figure was invented.
- [ ] Each visual title communicates the decision-oriented insight, not the variable.
- [ ] The recommendation has an owner and a horizon; no prices; neutral Spanish and professional, no emojis.
Expected deliverable: executive report in {{FORMATO_SALIDA}} with thesis title, one-paragraph SCQA opening, pyramid body (2–4 arguments with data and source), actionable recommendation with owner and horizon, and one decision-oriented title per visual.
spec-datos_storytelling_piramide_minto:
[inputs]
- HALLAZGOS_Y_DATOS: {{HALLAZGOS_Y_DATOS}} > Key findings and figures from the analysis (metrics, variations, periods, sources)
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Who receives the narrative and their level (executive committee, area leader, board)
- DECISION_OBJETIVO: {{DECISION_OBJETIVO}} > Concrete decision the narrative must enable
- LOGICA_AGRUPACION: {{LOGICA_AGRUPACION}} > (optional) Argument-ordering logic: deductive, inductive, or by relevance. If omitted, choose based on the audience and justify
- ACCION_Y_HORIZONTE: {{ACCION_Y_HORIZONTE}} > (optional) Recommended action, owner, and time horizon
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A data analysis only generates a decision when it is told top-down: conclusion first, evidence after. Building the narrative with the Minto Pyramid and SCQA achieves that {{AUDIENCIA}} understands the what-to-do in the first 30 seconds and takes {{DECISION_OBJETIVO}} without having to traverse the data in reverse order. This reduces clarification meetings and turns the finding into action. The frequent mistake this prompt avoids: burying the conclusion under the method, opening with the methodology, or presenting data lists with no single idea to govern them.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior data analyst and executive storyteller, expert in the Minto Pyramid (Barbara Minto), MECE principle, and SCQA structure, with practice communicating to decision committees.
Deliverable: a data-based top-down narrative. Steps:
1. Formulate the SCQA: Situation (known stable context), Complication (what breaks it), Question (the one that triggers the analysis), Answer (the conclusion).
2. Distill ONE governing idea (governing thought): actionable, measurable, answering the Question in a single sentence.
3. Group 2 to 4 supporting arguments that satisfy MECE: mutually exclusive (no overlap) and collectively exhaustive (no gaps relative to the governing idea).
4. Order the arguments according to {{LOGICA_AGRUPACION}} (deductive, inductive, or by relevance) and declare the logic used and why it fits {{AUDIENCIA}}.
5. Under each argument, anchor evidence from {{HALLAZGOS_Y_DATOS}} with figure, unit, period, and source. If a piece of data does not exist, mark it [ASSUMPTION] or ask for it; never invent it. If two figures contradict each other, expose the tension instead of averaging.
6. Close with the implication ("and therefore") and the action according to {{ACCION_Y_HORIZONTE}}, with owner and horizon. Use {{ADJUNTOS}} as the primary source of figures when available.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 – Framing: draft the SCQA and validate that the Question and Answer are coherent with {{DECISION_OBJETIVO}}.
Phase 2 – Summit: formulate the governing idea and discard it if it is not actionable or measurable.
Phase 3 – MECE structure: define the arguments, test for absence of overlap and gaps, order them by {{LOGICA_AGRUPACION}}.
Phase 4 – Evidence: anchor each figure to its argument with traceability (figure/unit/period/source); mark gaps [ASSUMPTION] and data conflicts as open tensions.
Phase 5 – Narrative: draft the 5–7 sentence opening script and the MECE test per argument.
Phase 6 – Critical close: declare what decision is enabled and the main risk of acting on the narrative as it stands.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] SCQA in 4 lines, with Question and Answer aligned to {{DECISION_OBJETIVO}}.
- [ ] A single governing idea, actionable and measurable (not descriptive or multi-topic).
- [ ] 2–4 arguments that pass the double MECE test (exclusive and exhaustive), with the ordering logic declared and justified.
- [ ] Each piece of evidence has figure, unit, period, and source; gaps marked [ASSUMPTION]; conflicts exposed as tensions; zero invented numbers.
- [ ] Close with implication, action (owner + horizon), decision enabled, and main risk.
Edge cases: insufficient data for a MECE branch → declare the gap and ask for it; mixed audience → prioritize the highest-ranking decision-maker; if {{LOGICA_AGRUPACION}} is not provided → choose one and justify.
Expected deliverable: (1) SCQA in 4 lines; (2) pyramid in indented text (governing idea > arguments > evidence); (3) narrative script of 5–7 sentences for the opening; (4) MECE test in one line per argument; (5) line of enabled decision + main risk.
spec-datos_storytelling_audiencia_ejecut:
[inputs]
- ANALISIS_TECNICO: {{ANALISIS_TECNICO}} > Technical source result: model output, dashboard, query, study, or report to translate
- DECISION_EN_JUEGO: {{DECISION_EN_JUEGO}} > Concrete decision this message must enable or unlock at the committee
- AUDIENCIA_C_LEVEL: {{AUDIENCIA_C_LEVEL}} > Roles present and their dominant priority (CEO/growth, CFO/cost-risk, COO/operations)

- CIFRAS_REFERENCIA: {{CIFRAS_REFERENCIA}} > Base figures for quantifying the impact (optional; anything not provided is marked [ASSUMPTION])
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A solid technical analysis loses its value when it reaches the executive committee in the language of the method rather than the language of the decision. C-level leaders have minutes, not pages, and they act on impact in {{METRICA_NEGOCIO}}, not on confidence intervals or model metrics. Translating ANALISIS_TECNICO into a narrative that enables DECISION_EN_JUEGO unlocks approval, aligns the committee, and turns the data into action. A poor translation buries months of analytical work or, worse, induces a decision based on misunderstood figures.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Lead data analyst and executive communication consultant, with a track record presenting quantitative findings to boards of directors and translating statistical complexity into business decisions.
Deliverable: a complete, presentation-ready executive message. Steps:
1. Isolate the single decision DECISION_EN_JUEGO must unlock; if it is ambiguous or missing, ask before continuing. Do not proceed with multiple mixed decisions.
2. Draft a one-sentence headline that expresses the finding in terms of METRICA_NEGOCIO, never in statistical language.
3. Translate each metric from ANALISIS_TECNICO to its executive equivalent using CIFRAS_REFERENCIA; declare the conversion formula in half a line and mark [ASSUMPTION] on any figure not provided. Provide a range (floor-ceiling) when uncertainty is material.

6. Close with an actionable recommendation and the concrete next step requested from the committee, with owner and timeline when the information allows.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 – Interpret: extract from ANALISIS_TECNICO the dominant finding and link it to DECISION_EN_JUEGO; discard anything that does not move the decision.
Phase 2 – Translate: apply the "metric-to-impact" principle; every unavoidable technical term is explained in half a line. Quantify with CIFRAS_REFERENCIA, declare the conversion, and flag assumptions.
Phase 3 – Structure: organize in an inverted pyramid according to the priority of AUDIENCIA_C_LEVEL (growth, cost-risk, or operations lead the angle).
Phase 4 – Defend: build the anticipated-questions block with defensible answers; never defend a figure you cannot sustain.
Phase 5 – Close: formulate the recommendation and next step with owner and timeline when applicable.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The headline is in terms of METRICA_NEGOCIO, without statistical jargon.
- [ ] The conclusion and recommendation appear before any methodological detail.
- [ ] Each technical finding has its quantified equivalent in business impact, with the conversion declared.
- [ ] Any figure not provided in CIFRAS_REFERENCIA is marked [ASSUMPTION] and verified data is distinguished from assumptions.
- [ ] The block anticipates 3 to 5 real committee questions with a brief and defensible answer.
- [ ] The methodological detail does not exceed one supporting line.
- [ ] Closes with an actionable recommendation and one concrete next step (owner/timeline when applicable).
- [ ] The angle of the message reflects the dominant priority of AUDIENCIA_C_LEVEL.

spec-datos_storytelling_titulo_accionabl:
[inputs]
- GRAFICO: {{GRAFICO}} > Chart type and variables displayed (e.g. bar chart of sales by quarter, monthly churn line chart, price-volume scatter plot)
- INSIGHT: {{INSIGHT}} > Pattern, contrast, change, or anomaly that matters to communicate (optional; if missing, the model infers it and marks it as proposed)
- DATOS_CLAVE: {{DATOS_CLAVE}} > Actual figures, direction, or magnitude from the chart to support the title (without this, the model does not invent numbers; include period and unit when applicable)

- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A chart title is the most-read element and often the only thing the audience processes, yet it is usually wasted on a descriptive label ("Sales by Quarter") that only names the axes and forces the reader to figure out alone what to think. The goal is to convert the title of {{GRAFICO}} into an actionable statement that communicates {{INSIGHT}} directly and pushes {{AUDIENCIA}} toward {{ACCION}}, adapted for {{CANAL}}. This enables faster reading, a shorter meeting, and a better-framed decision, because the message travels with the chart even when it is shared without context. EstrategIA contributes the rigor of one chart = one idea, asserting only what {{DATOS_CLAVE}} supports.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior data analyst and data storytelling expert, trained in the Cole Nussbaumer Knaflic approach (Storytelling with Data), the one chart = one idea principle, and title-as-takeaway design.
Deliver, in this order:
1. One-sentence reframing of {{GRAFICO}} + main idea from {{INSIGHT}}; if any essential piece is missing (chart, insight, key data, audience, or action), ask before continuing and do not invent figures.
2. Diagnosis of the current title if one was provided: classify it as descriptive, neutral, or actionable and explain in one line the cost of a descriptive title (cognitive load, risk of misinterpretation).
3. Isolation of the single insight relevant to {{AUDIENCIA}} and {{ACCION}}; if there are multiple ideas, choose one and set the rest aside (one chart = one idea), suggesting whether the others deserve their own chart.

5. For each title: angle (urgency, opportunity, reassurance, alert), assertion level (describes the change vs. explicit recommendation), and when to use it.
6. Recommended winning title with a one-line justification + suggested subtitle or annotation to hold the remaining context (period, source, assumption) without overloading the title.

Phase 1 – Framing: identify the single idea that serves the decision of {{AUDIENCIA}} and discard secondary ones.
Phase 2 – Extraction: derive from {{DATOS_CLAVE}} the magnitude, direction, and comparison that will give the title force, without adding data not provided; separate observed from inferred.
Phase 3 – Writing: write subject-verb-finding statements, testing different angles and verifying that each passes the "so what" test (answers why it matters and to which decision it leads).
Phase 4 – Curation: choose the winner based on fit with {{AUDIENCIA}}, {{ACCION}}, and {{CANAL}}; refine against anti-patterns and confirm that no figure lacks support.
Edge cases: if {{INSIGHT}} contradicts a prior title, flag it; if {{DATOS_CLAVE}} does not support any strong statement, offer the most honest title available and declare the limit; if there are multiple insights of equal weight, recommend splitting into separate charts.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Each title is a complete statement (subject + verb + finding), not an axis label.
- [ ] The title communicates a single idea, aligned with {{ACCION}} and {{AUDIENCIA}}.
- [ ] Every figure comes from {{DATOS_CLAVE}}; anything inferred carries [ASSUMPTION]; no numbers or causality are invented.
- [ ] Each title passes the "so what" test and fits the length of {{CANAL}}.
- [ ] No prices, no use of the word free, no emojis; neutral and professional English.
- [ ] Diagnosis of the prior title was delivered (if one existed), 3 alternatives with angle and assertion level, 1 justified winner, suggested subtitle/annotation, and list of anti-patterns.
