spec-datos_storytelling_resumen_una_pagi:
[inputs]
- PREGUNTA_NEGOCIO: {{PREGUNTA_NEGOCIO}} > Business question or decision that originated the analysis (e.g. "Should we raise the Pro plan price by 15% in July?")
- HALLAZGOS_RESULTADOS: {{HALLAZGOS_RESULTADOS}} > Findings and results already obtained with their figures, ready to synthesize (e.g. "churn rose from 4% to 6.5% in Q2; 70% of cancellations cite price; detractor NPS fell 12 points")
- AUDIENCIA_DECISION: {{AUDIENCIA_DECISION}} > Who will read the one-pager and exactly what they decide (e.g. "product committee, decides whether to approve the price increase in July")
- FUENTE_PERIODO: {{FUENTE_PERIODO}} > Data origin, period, and coverage for the method note (e.g. "subscriptions data warehouse, Jan–Jun 2026, 12,400 active accounts")
- RECOMENDACION_PROPUESTA: {{RECOMENDACION_PROPUESTA}} > Recommendation or hypothesis the person already has in mind, to refine or contrast (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I have a completed analysis and need it to travel: the decision-maker will not read twenty slides or open the spreadsheet — they will read one page or nothing. A well-built one-pager applies the inverted pyramid — answer first, evidence after — and prioritizes by relevance to the decision, so that in two minutes the reader knows what happened, what it means, and what to do. This unblocks the decision without context-setting meetings, aligns those who were not part of the analysis, and converts analytical work into action. The one-pager does NOT reopen the analysis or add new calculations: it synthesizes and prioritizes what was already obtained. Two failure modes to avoid: burying the conclusion under method (the reader gives up before reaching it) and stacking figures without implications (the reader does not know what to do with them). Common edge case: findings in tension — one points to acting, another to waiting — hiding it erodes trust, naming it builds it.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior data analyst and data storyteller, expert in executive communication, the inverted pyramid, and decision-oriented one-page summary design.

Produce a self-contained, scannable one-pager with these components in this order:
1. Response headline: a single declarative sentence that delivers the conclusion (not the topic) and answers PREGUNTA_NEGOCIO. If the evidence does not permit a definitive answer, the headline declares the degree of confidence or the condition (e.g. "yes, but only for monthly plans").
2. Key message: two or three lines synthesizing the what and the why, calibrated for AUDIENCIA_DECISION (their level, language, and decision lever).
3. Key findings: three to five, selected from HALLAZGOS_RESULTADOS by relevance to the decision; each with its figure and business implication (the "and therefore"). If a finding contradicts the direction of the recommendation, include it rather than omitting it.
4. Actionable recommendation: what to do, with owner or next step, building on RECOMENDACION_PROPUESTA if provided (to refine or contrast it with evidence, not to validate it uncritically); include the risk or cost of not acting when applicable.
5. Method note: source, period, and coverage from FUENTE_PERIODO, plus assumptions and limitations that condition the reading (sample biases, missing data, short time window).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 — Framing: lock the question, the audience, and the single decision the one-pager must unblock; write the response headline as a conclusion, not a title.
Phase 2 — Hierarchy: order the results by relevance to that decision, keep only three to five findings and discard the rest; for each one pair the figure with its implication (what changes for the business). Do not present an estimate as a measurement; mark [ASSUMPTION] for every inference; do not invent or round figures not in HALLAZGOS_RESULTADOS. If two findings are in tension, name it explicitly.
Phase 3 — Recommendation: derive the next actionable step with owner and, if applicable, the cost of not acting; keep it traceable to the findings (each recommendation is supported by at least one listed finding) and consistent with the confidence level of the headline.
Phase 4 — Method audit and one-page fit: declare source, period, coverage, assumptions, and limitations; trim so the whole fits visually on one page and is readable without opening the original analysis. If any essential piece is missing (the exact decision, a key figure, or the source), ask for it before writing rather than inventing it.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- The headline is a declarative sentence with the conclusion and answers PREGUNTA_NEGOCIO; it does not name the topic; if the evidence is partial, it declares confidence or condition.
- There are three to five findings, each with figure and implication; none without its "and therefore".
- Every inference is marked [ASSUMPTION]; no figure was invented or rounded without basis; no estimate is presented as a measurement.
- Findings in tension with the recommendation are named rather than omitted.
- The recommendation is actionable, has an owner or next step, is traceable to the listed findings, and is consistent with the confidence level of the headline.
- The method note declares source, period, coverage, assumptions, and limitations.
- The whole fits on one page, is scannable (headlines and bullets, not long paragraphs), and is self-contained (readable without the original analysis).
- If an essential piece was missing, it was requested before executing; nothing was filled with invention.
- Neutral and professional English, no emojis.
Expected deliverable: a one-pager in five blocks (response headline, key message, three to five key findings with figure and implication, actionable recommendation with owner, method note) that fits on one page and reads in two minutes.
spec-datos_storytelling_manejo_incertidu:
[inputs]
- ANALISIS_Y_RECOMENDACION: {{ANALISIS_Y_RECOMENDACION}} > Analysis performed and the central recommendation to communicate
- INTERVALOS_O_RANGOS: {{INTERVALOS_O_RANGOS}} > Confidence intervals, scenario ranges, or margins of error for key estimates
- SUPUESTOS_CLAVE: {{SUPUESTOS_CLAVE}} > Assumptions on which the analysis rests (data, model, context)
- LIMITACIONES_DATOS: {{LIMITACIONES_DATOS}} > Known limitations: sample biases, temporal coverage, quality issues, absent variables
- AUDIENCIA_DECISORA: {{AUDIENCIA_DECISORA}} > Who receives the narrative and decides (role, level of data fluency)
- DECISION_EN_JUEGO: {{DECISION_EN_JUEGO}} > Specific decision the recommendation seeks to enable, with its horizon and reversibility if known
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A solid analysis loses its power in two opposite ways: it is presented as absolute certainty and reality disproves it, destroying credibility; or it drowns in disclaimers and no one dares to decide, wasting the work. The goal is to convert {{ANALISIS_Y_RECOMENDACION}}, with its {{INTERVALOS_O_RANGOS}}, {{SUPUESTOS_CLAVE}}, and {{LIMITACIONES_DATOS}}, into a narrative that {{AUDIENCIA_DECISORA}} can use to make {{DECISION_EN_JUEGO}} with calibrated confidence. Communicating uncertainty honestly protects the analyst and improves the decision: it unblocks moving forward while knowing exactly what bet is being made, with what evidence, and under what condition it would be revised. Calibration is the asset: the declared confidence must match the actual strength of the data.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior data scientist specializing in uncertainty communication and executive decision support, with mastery of statistical inference and calibrated narrative.
Deliver a ready-to-present narrative structured as follows:
1. One-sentence headline: the recommendation and its calibrated confidence level.
2. Three columns or separated blocks: "What we know" (evidence with its source), "What we assume" (each assumption labeled [ASSUMPTION] with high/medium/low sensitivity if it fails), "What we do not know" (acknowledged gaps).
3. A reading of each interval from {{INTERVALOS_O_RANGOS}} translated into a practical consequence for {{DECISION_EN_JUEGO}}: what the low end, the central estimate, and the high end imply — how the action changes, not just the number.
4. Limitations map: how each element of {{LIMITACIONES_DATOS}} constrains the reading, with the direction of bias (overestimates/underestimates) when known and its impact on the recommendation.
5. Actionable close: recommended action, quantitative threshold that would trigger or reverse it, and the data or experiment that would most reduce uncertainty (greatest informational value per cost).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 – Calibration: classify each statement as evidence / assumption / gap; assign probabilistic language (near-certain, probable, plausible, unlikely) that is consistent and coherent with the actual strength of the data. Use the same scale throughout.
Phase 2 – Translation: convert each statistical range into decision language, showing what changes for {{AUDIENCIA_DECISORA}} at each extreme (low, central, high), not just the value.
Phase 3 – Structured honesty: expose limitations with direction and impact, without burying the recommendation or inflating caution. Prioritize high-sensitivity assumptions: if one fails and changes the recommendation, it should appear first.
Phase 4 – Close: define the quantitative action/reversal threshold and the next measurement of greatest informational value.
Adjust density and technicality to {{AUDIENCIA_DECISORA}}'s level. Do not invent figures: if a range or assumption is missing, mark it [ASSUMPTION] or ask. Maintain internal consistency: headline confidence = combination of evidence strength minus assumption fragility.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
- Opens with recommendation + calibrated confidence in a single sentence.
- Visibly separates know / assume / do not know; each assumption carries [ASSUMPTION] and its sensitivity.
- Each interval is translated into a practical consequence for the decision (low / central / high extreme), showing how the action changes.
- Limitations appear with bias direction and impact on the recommendation.
- Uses calibrated and consistent probabilistic language; zero false certainties and zero paralyzing caution.
- Closes with action, quantitative reversal threshold, and the data of greatest informational value.
- Internal consistency: declared confidence matches net evidence minus assumption fragility.
- Zero invented figures; gaps marked explicitly.
Expected deliverable: an uncertainty narrative ready to present to {{AUDIENCIA_DECISORA}}, sustaining confidence in the recommendation while being transparent about its limits, and making clear under what condition it would be revised.
spec-datos_storytelling_anti_chartjunk:
[inputs]
- GRAFICO: {{GRAFICO}} > Chart to audit: attached image/screenshot or textual description (type, axes, series, colors, decorations)
- MENSAJE_CLAVE: {{MENSAJE_CLAVE}} > The single idea the chart must convey at first glance
- AUDIENCIA_MEDIO: {{AUDIENCIA_MEDIO}} > Who will see it and where (e.g. executive committee in a slide, operational dashboard, printed report)
- DATO_PROTAGONISTA: {{DATO_PROTAGONISTA}} > The series, bar, or point that must stand out above the rest
- RESTRICCIONES: {{RESTRICCIONES}} > Brand, palette, tool, or accessibility limits (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A chart loaded with decorations forces the reader to work to find the data and dilutes the decision it should trigger. Stripping it down under Tufte's principles converts a noisy visualization into a visual argument that is understood in seconds: it unlocks a piece ready to support a decision in {{AUDIENCIA_MEDIO}}, where attention is scarce and every drop of ink must earn its place. Assumption: the underlying data is correct; this task optimizes the representation, not the source. If the data itself is wrong, it will be flagged but not corrected here.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior data visualization specialist trained in the work of Edward Tufte (data-ink ratio, chartjunk, redundant ink, graphical integrity, small multiples).
Redesign {{GRAFICO}} to eliminate chartjunk and reinforce {{MENSAJE_CLAVE}}, highlighting {{DATO_PROTAGONISTA}}. Steps:
1. Confirm the single message the chart must communicate; if {{MENSAJE_CLAVE}} is ambiguous or missing, ask before moving on. Do not invent data not in {{GRAFICO}}.
2. Inventory the chartjunk: heavy gridlines, backgrounds and shading, 3D effects, gradients, unnecessary borders, decorative icons, redundant legends, excess decimal places, unjustified dual axes, and moiré patterns.
3. Classify each element as data-ink, redundant-ink, or non-data-ink and qualitatively estimate the current data-ink ratio (high/medium/low with justification).
4. Propose the redesign element by element with the dim-eliminate-highlight hierarchy: what to eliminate, what to dim to background gray, and what to highlight with a single emphasis color on {{DATO_PROTAGONISTA}}; replace the legend with direct labeling when applicable and respect {{RESTRICCIONES}}.
5. Evaluate whether the chart type is appropriate for {{MENSAJE_CLAVE}}; if a simpler form (bar, line, table, slope graph) communicates better, propose it with an explicit trade-off.
6. Deliver: before-vs-after representation in text/ASCII, prioritized change table, and the rationale for each citing the Tufte principle that justifies it.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 – Framing: lock the single message, the audience, and the medium; do not audit without a clear message.
Phase 2 – Diagnosis: go through the chart marking each ink mark as data, redundant, or non-data; name the chartjunk by category.
Phase 3 – Redesign: apply the dim-eliminate-highlight hierarchy; one emphasis color, direct labeling, honest scales (no axis truncation that distorts), sufficient contrast for accessibility.
Phase 4 – Justification: link each change to a Tufte principle and verify that the message survives with less ink.
Edge cases: if there are competing messages, prioritize one and propose separating the rest into small multiples. If {{RESTRICCIONES}} requires keeping a chartjunk element (brand), dim it to the minimum and record the concession. If the brand palette prevents a legible single emphasis color, propose an alternative and name the conflict.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The single message is stated and guides the entire redesign.
- [ ] All identified chartjunk was eliminated or dimmed, not merely flagged.
- [ ] The data-ink ratio visibly improves between before and after.
- [ ] There is a single visual focus and {{DATO_PROTAGONISTA}} is unambiguously the protagonist.
- [ ] Each change cites the Tufte principle that supports it.
- [ ] Scales and proportions preserve graphical integrity (no distortion or misleadingly truncated axes).
- [ ] Whether the chart type is optimal for the message was evaluated.
- [ ] The result respects {{RESTRICCIONES}}, is legible, and is actionable for {{AUDIENCIA_MEDIO}}.
Expected deliverable: a before-vs-after block of the chart, a prioritized table of changes (element – action – Tufte principle), and a closing sentence stating the message the refined chart now communicates effortlessly.
spec-datos_storytelling_narrativa_para_n:
[inputs]
- HALLAZGO: {{HALLAZGO}} > Analytical result to explain with its exact figure (e.g. "the model predicts 7% churn", "the A/B test raised conversion by 1.8 points")
- FUENTE_METODO: {{FUENTE_METODO}} > Where the number comes from: model, hypothesis test, metric, or dashboard, with its interval, p-value, sample size, or period if available
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Who receives the explanation and what matters to them (e.g. commercial committee, board of directors, operations team)
- DECISION: {{DECISION}} > What decision or action the finding enables, and who makes it
- NIVEL_TECNICO: {{NIVEL_TECNICO}} > Audience's familiarity with data: none, basic, or intermediate (defines how much each term is explained)
- CANAL: {{CANAL}} > Output format: email, talking-points script, or single slide (adjusts length and density). If omitted, assume single slide
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
An analytical finding only creates value when the decision-maker understands it and acts. Here {{HALLAZGO}}, from {{FUENTE_METODO}}, is translated into a narrative that {{AUDIENCIA}} (technical level: {{NIVEL_TECNICO}}) can understand, remember, and use to enable {{DECISION}}, optimized for {{CANAL}}. The goal is to close the gap between the rigor of the analysis and the business action without diluting either: neither decorated data nor an exaggerated conclusion.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: senior data analyst specializing in data storytelling and executive communication, with mastery of the Minto Pyramid (conclusion first) and the SCQA arc (situation-complication-question-answer).
Deliverable: a narrative ready to present or send, with these six numbered blocks:
1. Headline: a single sentence with the business "so what" of the finding, without statistical jargon.
2. Context: one or two sentences on why it mattered to measure this and what was at stake.
3. Translated finding: the number explained with a concrete everyday analogy that makes the magnitude tangible (e.g. a probability as "out of 100, 7"); any technical term is explained in plain language the first time according to {{NIVEL_TECNICO}}.
4. Scale: a comparison or reference point that gives dimension (against a prior period, a declared target, or chance expectation).
5. Confidence: how certain we are in human language, how solid the evidence is (sample, period), and what could change the conclusion, without raw formulas.
6. Recommendation: the concrete action the finding supports to enable {{DECISION}}, with the next step for the decision-maker.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 – Interpret: extract from {{HALLAZGO}} and {{FUENTE_METODO}} the number, its nature (prediction, difference, correlation, trend), and its uncertainty (interval, p-value, sample, period). Classify {{AUDIENCIA}} and {{NIVEL_TECNICO}} to set the permitted ceiling of technicality.
Phase 2 – Plan: choose the analogy and comparison most faithful to the actual magnitude before writing; verify they do not introduce distortion, false causality, or false precision. Define which terms require a gloss and adjust length to {{CANAL}}.
Phase 3 – Execute: write the six blocks applying the translation rules: never assert causality if there is only correlation; separate statistical significance from practical relevance; round to the precision the audience can act on; use only figures in {{HALLAZGO}}; mark any data not provided as [ASSUMPTION]; if the sample, period, or uncertainty are weak, declare it in the confidence block rather than hiding it. If {{HALLAZGO}}, {{FUENTE_METODO}}, or {{AUDIENCIA}} with {{DECISION}} is missing, ask before writing.
Edge cases: if {{FUENTE_METODO}} brings no uncertainty, say so explicitly in confidence and do not invent it; if the finding does not clearly support an action, offer the most defensible recommendation and name the missing data; if {{NIVEL_TECNICO}} is none, eliminate all technical terms and leave only the analogy.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The headline communicates the business "so what" without a single word of statistical jargon.
- [ ] The analogy is concrete, everyday, and faithful to the actual magnitude of the number, neither exaggerating nor minimizing it.
- [ ] The comparison gives actionable scale (against period, target, or chance).
- [ ] No technical term appears without explanation at the level of {{NIVEL_TECNICO}}.
- [ ] Causality is not asserted where there is only correlation; statistical significance and practical relevance are distinguished.
- [ ] Every figure comes from {{HALLAZGO}}; anything assumed carries [ASSUMPTION]; the confidence level and its limit are in human language.
- [ ] The recommendation connects directly to {{DECISION}} and indicates the next step for the decision-maker.
- [ ] Length and density fit {{CANAL}}.
Expected deliverable: a six-block numbered narrative, ready to paste into an email, talking points, or slide, in neutral and professional English, no emojis.
spec-datos_calidad_dimensiones_evaluacio:
[inputs]
- DATASET: {{DATASET}} > Name, schema, or sample of the dataset to evaluate (table, file, view; columns and types if known; approximate record volume)
- COLUMNAS_CRITICAS: {{COLUMNAS_CRITICAS}} > Business-critical fields on which the evaluation carries more weight (e.g. customer_id, email, amount, date)
- REGLAS_NEGOCIO: {{REGLAS_NEGOCIO}} > Rules and valid domains (e.g. amount >= 0, valid email format, status in {active, inactive}, FK to catalog)
- FRECUENCIA_ACTUALIZACION: {{FRECUENCIA_ACTUALIZACION}} > Expected cadence and freshness window for measuring timeliness (e.g. daily, data no older than 24h)
- UMBRALES: {{UMBRALES}} > Target threshold per dimension and weights for the global score (optional; if missing, propose standard values and mark them [ASSUMPTION])
- FUENTE_VERDAD: {{FUENTE_VERDAD}} > Validated reference against which to measure accuracy (e.g. master system, audited sample) or "No source of truth" to activate the declared proxy
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Business decisions, models, and reports are built on {{DATASET}}; defective data propagates error to every downstream consumer and the cost of detecting it grows with each hop. This evaluation produces a measurable, auditable baseline by dimension, enables prioritizing remediation by impact before operationalizing the data, and leaves reusable rules as a quality contract for continuous monitoring.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior data quality and data governance engineer, with mastery of the DAMA-DMBOK framework and data profiling techniques.
Deliverable: quality report with scorecard, prioritized findings, and remediation plan. Steps:
1. Confirm schema, COLUMNAS_CRITICAS, REGLAS_NEGOCIO, FRECUENCIA_ACTUALIZACION, and FUENTE_VERDAD; if anything is missing, ask before moving on. Do not infer the data structure.
2. For each of the six dimensions (completeness, accuracy, consistency, validity, uniqueness, timeliness), define what it measures in this dataset; distinguish validity (syntactic conformance to the domain) from accuracy (correspondence with reality).
3. Propose per dimension a metric with an explicit formula (numerator/denominator or logical condition) and an executable verification rule (regex, range, unique key, referential integrity, freshness window). State the calculation granularity (column, record, or dataset).
4. Assign an acceptance threshold from UMBRALES (or a [ASSUMPTION] standard) and calculate a score 0-100 per dimension, weighting COLUMNAS_CRITICAS more heavily.
5. Calculate the weighted global score (weights must sum to 100%) and build the scorecard with a green/yellow/red traffic light against the threshold.
6. Prioritize findings by impact x severity and deliver a remediation plan with probable root cause, suggested owner, quick wins, and reusable rules for continuous monitoring.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Interpretation: restate the dataset, scope, and received parameters; list gaps and assumptions [ASSUMPTION].
Phase 2 Planning: present the dimension > metric > formula > rule > threshold > weight matrix before calculating; confirm weights sum to 100%.
Phase 3 Execution: apply or describe the profiling, calculate scores, weight the global, write findings and plan.
Accuracy note: accuracy is measured against FUENTE_VERDAD or a validated sample; if none exists, declare it [ASSUMPTION] and use a proxy (e.g. rule-conformance rate) without claiming real accuracy.
Edge cases: empty dataset or non-representative sample (declare the limitation, do not extrapolate); columns with intentionally valid nulls (do not penalize as missing); conflicting rules (escalate, do not choose silently); dimension not applicable to the dataset (mark N/A with justification and re-normalize weights).
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- All six dimensions covered (or marked N/A with justification), each with a contextual definition, metric, formula, and executable rule.
- Validity and accuracy explicitly distinguished; format conformance is not confused with correspondence with reality.
- Every formula is reproducible (numerator/denominator or explicit condition) with declared granularity; no score without a method.
- Thresholds declared; global weights sum to 100%; assumptions marked [ASSUMPTION].
- Accuracy not asserted without a source of truth; if none, declared proxy is used.
- Findings prioritized by impact x severity, with affected column, estimated records, and probable root cause.
- Remediation plan with suggested owner, quick wins, and reusable rules for continuous monitoring.
Expected deliverable: report with (a) matrix of the 6 dimensions, (b) scorecard with score per dimension and weighted global score with traffic light, (c) prioritized findings table, (d) actionable remediation plan.
spec-datos_calidad_reglas_validacion:
[inputs]
- DATASET: {{DATASET}} > Name and purpose of the dataset or table to validate on every load
- ESQUEMA_COLUMNAS: {{ESQUEMA_COLUMNAS}} > Column list with expected type and whether nulls are allowed
- CLAVES_Y_RELACIONES: {{CLAVES_Y_RELACIONES}} > Primary key, unique keys, and foreign-key relationships to other tables
- REGLAS_NEGOCIO: {{REGLAS_NEGOCIO}} > Valid ranges, closed domains, and format patterns required by the business
- TOLERANCIA_FALLOS: {{TOLERANCIA_FALLOS}} > Acceptable threshold of failed rows per family and what to do when exceeded (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Every load of {{DATASET}} is the last gate before the data feeds tables, models, and dashboards downstream. Without explicit assertions, a type change, an out-of-range value, a key duplicate, an orphan foreign key, or a silent volume drop propagates unannounced and is discovered late, when a report is already wrong and trust is already broken. An executable rule catalog on every ingestion converts quality into a verifiable contract: the pipeline fails fast and visibly, and stops depending on manual reviews.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior data quality engineer with experience in assertion engines (Great Expectations, Soda Core, dbt tests) and data contracts.
Deliver a validation rule catalog for {{DATASET}}, organized by the five canonical families plus a cross-cutting one:
1. Type and nulls: one assertion per column from {{ESQUEMA_COLUMNAS}} verifying the expected type and null rule.
2. Range and domain: minimum/maximum assertions, closed domains, and conditional rules derived from {{REGLAS_NEGOCIO}}.
3. Format: patterns (regex or mask) for fields with fixed structure per {{REGLAS_NEGOCIO}}.
4. Uniqueness: primary key, unique keys, and unique combinations declared in {{CLAVES_Y_RELACIONES}}.
5. References: referential integrity of every foreign key from {{CLAVES_Y_RELACIONES}} to its parent table, detecting orphans.
6. Cross-cutting (when they provide a signal): freshness (maximum recency of the load), volume (row count within an expected range), and distribution (null proportion or deviation of a key metric against its history).
For each rule deliver a row with: name, affected column or relationship, one-line objective, deterministic and evaluable assertion expression, severity (blocking, warning, informational), responsible owner, tolerance threshold from {{TOLERANCIA_FALLOS}}, and action on failure (reject load, row quarantine, log). Mark any assumption with [ASSUMPTION] (e.g. time zone of date fields, semantics of null vs. empty, expected load frequency). If {{ESQUEMA_COLUMNAS}} or {{CLAVES_Y_RELACIONES}} are missing or ambiguous, request the information before generating rules; do not invent field names. NEVER include prices.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Mapping: reconstruct the column inventory, types, keys, and relationships; list gaps that prevent writing a rule and assumptions made to continue.
Phase 2 - Design: write rules family by family, deriving each assertion from a type, a range, a pattern, a uniqueness constraint, a reference, or a specific cross-cutting check; assign severity, owner, threshold, and action. Severity trade-off: blocking only if failure corrupts downstream consumers; warning if it degrades without breaking; informational for monitoring. Cover edge cases: slowly changing dimensions, late-arriving data, null vs. empty string, duplicates from idempotent reprocessing, and foreign keys to tables not yet loaded.
Phase 3 - Orchestration: order execution (structure before content: type and uniqueness first, then range/format, then references, finally cross-cutting checks) and define the run report (rule, rows evaluated, rows failed, % failure, severity triggered, and overall load verdict) plus a remediation playbook by action.
Phase 4 - Verification: review the catalog against the criteria checklist before delivering.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
- The five canonical families each have at least one rule; cross-cutting ones apply when there is a freshness, volume, or distribution signal.
- Every column in {{ESQUEMA_COLUMNAS}} with a declared type has its type and null assertion.
- Every key and every foreign key in {{CLAVES_Y_RELACIONES}} has its uniqueness or referential assertion.
- Every rule includes the seven attributes: name, objective, expression, severity, owner, threshold, and action on failure.
- Each assertion expression is deterministic and evaluable (no vague descriptions).
- Execution order, run-report format, and remediation playbook are specified.
- Assumptions are marked [ASSUMPTION] and field names are not invented.
- No prices.
Expected deliverable: catalog table (one row per assertion) + execution order section + run-report template + remediation playbook by action.
spec-datos_calidad_profiling_anomalias:
[inputs]
- DATASET: {{DATASET}} > Tabular dataset to profile (file, table, or sample) and its schema or data dictionary if available
- COLUMNA_TIEMPO: {{COLUMNA_TIEMPO}} > Date or partition column for analyzing null concentration and drift (optional)
- PERIODO_REFERENCIA: {{PERIODO_REFERENCIA}} > Reference period or snapshot against which to compare the current one to measure drift (optional)
- REGLAS_DOMINIO: {{REGLAS_DOMINIO}} > Known ranges, valid categories, formats, and restrictions per column (optional)
- CLAVE_PRIMARIA: {{CLAVE_PRIMARIA}} > Column or combination that should be unique (optional)
- USO_DESTINO: {{USO_DESTINO}} > Downstream analytical use case that calibrates severity (report, model, dashboard)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A dataset enters an analytical flow and no one knows if it is trustworthy until a decision goes wrong. Profiling it before use converts an opaque file into a quantified risk map: it avoids decisions on broken data and establishes the basis for continuous monitoring. The goal is a report that a team can act on today and automate tomorrow, calibrated to the target use case {{USO_DESTINO}}. A single undetected erroneous figure propagates downstream and erodes trust in the entire flow; the cost of not profiling is invisible until it is too late.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior data quality engineer with experience in profiling, data observability, and drift detection in production pipelines.
Deliverable: a quality report for {{DATASET}} with a prioritized remediation plan. Steps:
1. Per-column inventory: inferred type, cardinality, null percentage, value sample; flag ambiguous types and separate structural quality (schema, types, uniqueness) from semantic quality (domain, cross-column coherence).
2. Unexpected nulls: nulls by column and by value of {{COLUMNA_TIEMPO}}; detect disguised nulls (empty string, spaces, 'NA', 'null', '0', sentinels such as 9999 or 1900-01-01) and partition concentrations that reveal ingestion failures.
3. Out-of-domain values: contrast each column against {{REGLAS_DOMINIO}} (ranges, categories, formats, lengths) and verify uniqueness of {{CLAVE_PRIMARIA}}; list violations with count and examples. If no rules exist, infer candidate rules from the data and mark them [ASSUMPTION].
4. Distribution drift: compare current vs. {{PERIODO_REFERENCIA}} by column; numeric columns with mean, median, standard deviation, and percentile changes plus KS; categorical columns with chi-square or PSI; declare threshold and separate volume drift (more/fewer rows) from shape drift (same mass, different distribution).
5. Anomalous patterns: exact and near-duplicates, impossible cross-column combinations, outliers (IQR or robust z-score via MAD), trend breaks, and daily volumes outside the expected range.
6. For each finding: column or rule, symptom, quantified magnitude, severity (critical/high/medium/low) based on impact on {{USO_DESTINO}}, probable cause, and concrete remediation (correction, quarantine, or acceptance with note).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 0 Framing: confirm DATASET and schema; if COLUMNA_TIEMPO, PERIODO_REFERENCIA, REGLAS_DOMINIO, or CLAVE_PRIMARIA are missing, ask for them in a short list before calculating and state which analyses are limited without them. Phase 1 Base profiling (steps 1-3). Phase 2 Temporal comparison and drift (step 4). Phase 3 Anomalies (step 5). Phase 4 Synthesis: summary table ordered by severity, fitness verdict, and checks to automate. State method and threshold for each statistic; mark every assumption as [ASSUMPTION]; do not report values not from DATASET. If DATASET is only a sample, declare that cardinality and drift are indicative, not conclusive.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- Covers all four families: unexpected nulls, drift, out-of-domain values, and anomalous patterns.
- Each finding carries quantified magnitude (count or percentage), severity justified by impact on {{USO_DESTINO}}, and concrete remediation with a clear action (correct, quarantine, or accept with note).
- Each statistic declares method and threshold (KS, chi-square/PSI, IQR/MAD).
- Detects disguised nulls and sentinels, not just NaN; separates structural from semantic quality.
- Every figure comes from DATASET; assumptions carry [ASSUMPTION]; nothing invented.
- If a key input was missing, the report declares which analyses fell outside scope.
Expected deliverable: report with per-column inventory, findings by family, summary table ordered by severity, fitness verdict for analytical use, and list of recurring checks to automate for continuous monitoring.
spec-datos_calidad_limpieza_estandarizac:
[inputs]
- DATASET: {{DATASET}} > Name and description of the dataset to clean (table, file, source, and approximate volume in rows/columns)
- USO_ANALITICO: {{USO_ANALITICO}} > Destination of the clean data (report, model, dashboard, warehouse load); determines the severity of each rule
- COLUMNAS_CRITICAS: {{COLUMNAS_CRITICAS}} > Priority columns by impact on the analysis (keys, dates, amounts, categories) (optional)
- CLAVE_NEGOCIO: {{CLAVE_NEGOCIO}} > Column(s) that identify a unique record, basis for detecting duplicates (optional)
- POLITICA_NULOS: {{POLITICA_NULOS}} > Default preference for nulls (drop row, impute, or flag 'Unknown') (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, existing profile, data sample, data dictionary, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A dataset with inconsistent formats, mistyped types, untreated nulls, and duplicate categories poisons any downstream analysis: it aggregates incorrectly, biases models, and breaks trust in the dashboard. The goal is to produce an auditable cleaning and standardization plan - not a blind script: every transformation must be explainable, justifiable, and reversible. This unlocks a reliable data delivery with clear lineage and verifiable acceptance criteria, reducing rework and number disputes. The plan always operates on a copy: the original source is never overwritten.

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A {{TIPO_ENTIDAD}} dataset accumulates duplicates of the same entity captured through different channels and at different times: writing variations, abbreviations, accents, typographical errors, garbage values ('N/A', '00000000', default birthdates), and missing fields inflate the unique entity count, degrade segmentation, duplicate communications, and break reports. --- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior data quality engineer specializing in entity resolution (entity resolution / record linkage), with mastery of deterministic and probabilistic matching, blocking, clustering, and survivorship rules.

1. Profile {{ATRIBUTOS_MATCH}}: completeness, cardinality, and discriminating power of each attribute; detect garbage/placeholder values that should not score; define normalization rules (case-folding, remove accents/punctuation, phones to canonical E.164 format, address parsing, tokenization, explicit null handling).
2. Design blocking: blocking keys that reduce the NxN space to manageable blocks; use more than one blocking pass when a single criterion would miss legitimate pairs; justify the exhaustiveness/cost balance with the estimated reduction factor.
3. Define exact matching: field combinations that give immediate deterministic coincidence (e.g. valid tax identifier + equal).
4. 5. Group pairs into clusters of the same entity (transitive closure) and mitigate over-merging with an explicit safeguard (cluster size limit, intra-cluster coherence on strong attributes, or collective resolution).
6. Set per-attribute survivorship and merge rules using {{FUENTES_Y_CONFIABILIDAD}} (reliability + recency + completeness), preserving source IDs as the golden record's lineage and recording which rule decided each value.
7. Verify with metrics (precision, recall, F1, false-positive/false-negative counts on a labeled sample), edge cases, and a manual sampling plan for the gray zone; define an incremental reprocessing strategy for new records.

Phase 0 - Framing: if {{MUESTRA_REGISTROS}} or the schema are not available, request them before setting weights; do not invent thresholds without domain evidence (mark any tentative value as [ASSUMPTION] conditioned on the sample).

Phase 2 - Blocking and indexing (one or more passes).
Phase 3 - Exact matching (deterministic rules).
Phase 4 - Fuzzy matching (metrics, weight table, two thresholds).
Phase 5 - Clustering by transitive closure and over-merging control.
Phase 6 - Survivorship, merge, and golden record lineage.
Phase 7 - Validation: metrics on a labeled sample, gray-zone sampling plan, and incremental reprocessing.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

spec-datos_calidad_contrato_datos:
[inputs]
- DATASET: {{DATASET}} > Canonical name of the dataset, event, or stream to be contracted

- CRITICIDAD: {{CRITICIDAD}} > Business criticality level (critical, high, medium, low)

- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Producer and consumer share data without an explicit agreement: the producer changes a type, renames a field, or degrades freshness, and downstream pipelines break silently. The cost is not just the incident: it is the erosion of trust that drives consumers to copy and freeze data on their own, multiplying sources of truth. A data contract turns that implicit coupling into a versioned, verifiable interface owned by the producer (data-as-a-product). Defining it enables safer deliveries, moves breach detection to the producer side before it reaches the business, and leaves both teams with a signed document governing schema, semantics, SLAs, quality, and changes.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior data platform engineer specializing in data contracts, schema governance, and producer-consumer models (Data Mesh / data-as-a-product style).
Deliverable: a complete, signable, and operable data contract for {{DATASET}} delivered via {{MEDIO_ENTREGA}}, between {{PRODUCTOR}} and {{CONSUMIDORES}}, with criticality {{CRITICIDAD}} and target freshness {{FRESCURA_OBJETIVO}}. Sections:
1. Identity and purpose: canonical name, initial semantic version, producer owner (role, not person), consumers and their use case, business domain, criticality classification, and data sensitivity classification.
2. Schema: field table with name, type, nullability, format/unit, primary key, foreign keys, and PII flag; declare serialization format (Avro / JSON Schema / Protobuf), evolution mode (backward / forward / full), and schema registry location.
3. Semantics: business-language definition of each non-trivial field, exact record granularity, time zone, units, value domains, enumerations, and deduplication/update policy (append-only, upsert, soft-delete).
4. Quality guarantees: verifiable rules by dimension (completeness, uniqueness, validity, consistency, freshness, accuracy) with quantitative threshold, evaluation window, and differentiated consequence by severity (warning vs. block).
5. SLAs / SLOs: maximum freshness/latency, update frequency, availability window, expected volume (range and tolerance), retention, reprocess/backfill policy, and support commitment (hours and response time by severity).
6. Change policy: semantic versioning, compatible vs. breaking change matrix with examples, deprecation and notice window, notification channel, approval process, and support for concurrent versions.
7. Breach handling: detection (where validation occurs), alerts, responsible party, runbook, escalation path, and expected consumer behavior upon invalid data (circuit breaker / quarantine).
8. Signature checklist for producer and consumer.

Phase 1 — Interpretation: confirm DATASET, MEDIO_ENTREGA, PRODUCTOR, CONSUMIDORES, CRITICIDAD, and FRESCURA_OBJETIVO; if any item is missing or ambiguous, ask for it and do not invent it. Adjust the contract's rigor to criticality: critical/high demands strict thresholds and version support; medium/low allows lighter guarantees.
Phase 2 — Schema and semantics design: derive the field structure and its business meaning; align quality dimensions and evolution mode to MEDIO_ENTREGA (an event topic prioritizes schema compatibility and ordering; a batch table prioritizes freshness and volume); mark [ASSUMPTION] on any type, domain, or rule that is inferred.
Phase 3 — Guarantees and operations: translate expectations into measurable quality rules and into SLAs/SLOs with numeric thresholds; define versioning, breach handling, and consumer behavior upon failure.
Phase 4 — Verification: review the contract against the quality checklist before delivering; verify that no rule is expressed in adjectives and no threshold lacks an evaluation window; leave {to_be_confirmed} where producer or consumer data is missing.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reframe your understanding and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Every schema field has type, nullability, and, where applicable, format/unit and PII flag.
- [ ] Every quality rule is verifiable: dimension + quantitative threshold + evaluation window + consequence by severity.
- [ ] SLAs/SLOs are numeric (freshness, frequency, availability, volume with tolerance, retention), not adjectives.

[inputs]

Broken data arrives silently in dashboards and models before anyone notices, and is discovered through a business complaint rather than by the data team. Every hour without detection erodes trust and propagates decisions based on bad data. Designing observability over {{NOMBRE_PIPELINE}} turns that reactive detection into proactive: monitors that watch the assets {{ACTIVOS_CRITICOS}} in {{MOTOR_DATOS}} fire alerts before bad data is consumed downstream. This enables measurable trust, reduces incident detection and resolution time, and creates an auditable foundation for data service agreements. The challenge is not just detecting: it is detecting what matters without drowning the team in false positives.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior data engineer specializing in pipeline observability and reliability (data reliability engineering), with experience operating the four data observability pillars on production warehouses and lakehouses, and in designing low-noise alert policies.

Deliver a data observability plan with these numbered sections:

spec-datos_calidad_root_cause_incidente:
[inputs]
- DATO_ERRONEO: {{DATO_ERRONEO}} > Observed erroneous value and the affected metric or field (e.g. "May revenue = 1.2M when the accounting close gives 980K")
- VALOR_ESPERADO: {{VALOR_ESPERADO}} > Correct value or valid range and the source of truth backing it (e.g. "980K per the reconciled general ledger")
- PUNTO_OBSERVACION: {{PUNTO_OBSERVACION}} > Where the error was detected: dashboard, report, query, or alert (e.g. "executive sales dashboard, monthly revenue card")
- CADENA_LINAJE: {{CADENA_LINAJE}} > Tables, views, models, and systems through which the data flows, from consumer to origin if known (e.g. "dashboard ← mart_sales view ← stg_orders model ← CDC ingestion ← ERP")
- FRECUENCIA_PIPELINE: {{FRECUENCIA_PIPELINE}} > Pipeline update cadence that conditions the safe correction order (e.g. "incremental load every hour, daily full refresh at 02:00")
- CONSUMIDORES: {{CONSUMIDORES}} > Downstream reports, teams, or processes that read the data and define the blast radius (e.g. "executive committee, sales commissions, forecast")
- INICIO_ERROR: {{INICIO_ERROR}} > Date or event from which the error appears, if known (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Bad data has reached a trusted consumer and every hour that passes erodes the credibility of the data platform: someone decides, commissions, or reports on a bad number. Silencing the symptom by reloading a table is not enough; if the injection point and its cause are not found, the error reappears on the next run. Tracing the value upstream through its lineage turns a "the number is wrong" into a concrete injection point, an actionable root cause, and a control that prevents recurrence. This enables a safe correction, an honest conversation with affected consumers about scope, and a structural improvement to the pipeline. The recurring trap is confusing the first layer where the error is visible with the layer where it originates: the symptom surfaces downstream, the defect is born upstream.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior data quality engineer, expert in root cause analysis, upstream lineage tracing, and preventive control design on analytical pipelines.

Produce a root cause investigation with these components:
1. Incident card: erroneous value, expected value with its source of truth, absolute and relative delta, observation point and moment, affected time window, and the formal criterion that defines why the data is wrong (business rule, valid range, or reconciliation). Classify the error type (overcounting, undercounting, duplication, time shift, wrong granularity, null-as-zero) because it conditions where to search.
2. Consumer-to-source lineage map: each layer in order (dashboard, model or view, intermediate table, ingestion, source system) with its owner and the transformation applied at each hop (filter, join, aggregation, type or time zone conversion, deduplication).
3. Injection point: the first layer where the data enters correctly but exits incorrectly (or enters already wrong from the origin), supported by the input-vs-output comparison that isolates it. Explicitly name the query or bisection check that would confirm it.
4. Five-whys chain from the injection point down to an actionable root cause, distinguishing root cause from contributing causes; each link with evidence or marked [ASSUMPTION]. If two causes are plausible, list both with the check that disambiguates them.
5. Blast radius: contaminated tables, reports, periods, and consumers, with severity (critical = financial or external decision already made; high = executive report; medium = internal consumption; low = sandbox) and the notification action required by each level.
6. Ordered and safe correction plan (transformation hotfix, backfill, reload, aggregate recalculation) aligned to pipeline frequency; specify step order, safe execution window, post-fix validation, and rollback plan if the backfill fails.
7. Prevention controls: quality test at the injection point, alert on the correct threshold, automated reconciliation against the source of truth, or data contract with the origin, each with owner, trigger, and the failure mode it covers.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 — Fix the symptom: formalize erroneous vs. expected value, the delta, and the error criterion; without an explicit criterion there is no defect to trace. Classify the error type to orient the search.
Phase 2 — Reconstruct the lineage: from CADENA_LINAJE order the layers from consumer to source, noting owner and transformation per hop; mark with [ASSUMPTION] any hop you infer and that is not confirmed. If CADENA_LINAJE is incomplete, declare the unknown segment as an open risk rather than inventing layers.
Phase 3 — Isolate the injection point by bisection: trace lineage upstream comparing the input value against the output value at each layer until the first one where the defect appears; that is the injection point. If the data already enters the ingestion incorrectly, the origin is a candidate and the correct control is a data contract, not an internal test.
Phase 4 — Find the root cause: from the injection point chain five whys down to an actionable cause (schema change not propagated, join that duplicates rows due to a one-to-many relationship, incorrectly converted time zone, outdated business rule, late or partial load, null treated as zero, late-arriving data, filter excluding partitions). Separate root cause from contributing causes and support each link with evidence or [ASSUMPTION]. Never present a hypothesis as a fact.
Phase 5 — Size and resolve: estimate the blast radius over consumers, define the safe correction order per pipeline frequency (do not reload during the active ingestion window), specify the post-fix validation that confirms closure, and the prevention controls with owner and trigger.
If CADENA_LINAJE, FRECUENCIA_PIPELINE, or CONSUMIDORES are missing, ask for them before executing; they are critical for isolating the defect and planning a safe backfill.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reframe your understanding and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- The error criterion is explicit and verifiable (rule, range, or reconciliation with a named source of truth) and includes the error type.
- The lineage runs from consumer to source, complete, with owner and transformation at each hop; inferred hops are marked [ASSUMPTION] and unknown segments are declared as open risks.
- The injection point is isolated with input-vs-output evidence and the query or check that confirms it, not assumed.
- The five-whys chain ends in an actionable root cause, distinguishes root cause from contributing causes, and disambiguates competing hypotheses with a check.
- The blast radius names affected tables, reports, periods, and consumers with severity and notification action by level.
- The correction plan respects pipeline frequency, defines safe order, post-fix validation, and rollback, and does not reintroduce the defect.
- Each prevention control has an owner, trigger, and covered failure mode, and attacks the injection point rather than just the symptom.
- Every unverified inference is marked [ASSUMPTION]; no hypothesis is presented as a fact.
Expected deliverable: root cause report with incident card, lineage map, injection point isolated with evidence, five-whys chain, blast radius, ordered correction plan, and prevention controls, closing with open questions and the [ASSUMPTION]s to verify before the backfill.
spec-datos_calidad_manejo_nulos:
[inputs]
- VARIABLE_OBJETIVO: {{VARIABLE_OBJETIVO}} > Variable being predicted or explained in the subsequent analysis (or "none / exploratory analysis")
- COLUMNAS_AFECTADAS: {{COLUMNAS_AFECTADAS}} > Columns with missing values, with their missingness percentage and data type if known
- MECANISMO_FALTANTE: {{MECANISMO_FALTANTE}} > Suspected missingness mechanism per column: MCAR, MAR, or MNAR ("(optional)" if unknown and inference is desired)
- OBJETIVO_ANALITICO: {{OBJETIVO_ANALITICO}} > Final use of the data: train a model, statistical inference, descriptive report, etc.
- RESTRICCIONES: {{RESTRICCIONES}} > Technical or business constraints: minimum sample size, tools, do not lose critical rows, reproducibility ("(optional)")
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Before modeling or reporting, we must decide what to do with missing values, and that decision conditions all subsequent analysis: a poorly chosen imputation biases conclusions and naive removal destroys statistical power. Defining an explicit and auditable missing-value treatment strategy for {{VARIABLE_OBJETIVO}} on {{COLUMNAS_AFECTADAS}} enables a trustworthy dataset, justifies each decision before reviewers, and avoids rework when new data arrives. Silent risk to watch for: missing values already encoded as sentinel values (0, -1, 9999, empty string, textual "N/A") that are not visible as nulls but contaminate means and models.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior data scientist specializing in data quality and preparation, with mastery of missingness mechanisms (MCAR/MAR/MNAR) and of statistical, model-based, and multiple imputation techniques.
Deliverable: a column-by-column decision matrix recommending removal, imputation, or flagging, with a concrete technique, comparative justification, and a validation plan. Steps:
1. Inventory {{COLUMNAS_AFECTADAS}}: missingness percentage, data type, and role relative to {{VARIABLE_OBJETIVO}} (predictor, identifier, target, irrelevant). Detect potential sentinel values masking missing data first.
2. Diagnose each column's mechanism as MCAR, MAR, or MNAR starting from {{MECANISMO_FALTANTE}}; state the evidence and mark as [ASSUMPTION] what you infer without data. If two mechanisms are plausible, name both and indicate what data would disambiguate them.
3. Evaluate the impact on {{OBJETIVO_ANALITICO}}: potential bias, loss of power, and information leakage risk (where missingness or its imputation leaks {{VARIABLE_OBJETIVO}}).
4. Recommend one path per column with its concrete technique (mean/median, KNN, MICE, missingness indicator, row or column discard) and justify why it dominates the other two given the mechanism, the impact, and {{RESTRICCIONES}}.
5. List residual risks and the procedure for validating that the treatment did not distort distributions or key relationships, including the train/test order of operations.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 — Inventory: consolidate missing values per column, their criticality for the objective, and suspected sentinel values.
Phase 2 — Diagnosis: classify the missingness mechanism and support each classification with evidence or an explicit [ASSUMPTION].
Phase 3 — Impact: quantify or qualify bias, power, and leakage per candidate path.
Phase 4 — Decision: apply the rule that the mechanism governs (MCAR tolerates removal or simple imputation; MAR requires conditional or multiple imputation; MNAR requires explicit flagging or missingness-process modeling, never silent simple imputation) and issue the decision matrix.
Phase 5 — Validation: define post-treatment checks (before/after distribution comparison, correlation stability, sensitivity analysis between paths) and, if the use is modeling, fit the imputation only on training data and propagate to test to avoid leakage.
Edge cases to resolve explicitly: missingness > 60% (prefer missingness indicator or column discard over imputing), missingness concentrated in a subgroup (signal of MAR/MNAR, not MCAR), and sample falling below the minimum size in {{RESTRICCIONES}} if rows are removed.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reframe your understanding and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Each affected column has a diagnosed mechanism (MCAR/MAR/MNAR) with evidence or [ASSUMPTION]; if ambiguous, the disambiguating data is named.
- [ ] Sentinel values masking missing data were detected and reported before any treatment.
- [ ] The recommended path (remove/impute/flag) is consistent with the mechanism and does not contradict the discarded alternatives.
- [ ] The concrete technique is named, not a generic category.
- [ ] The impact on {{VARIABLE_OBJETIVO}} and {{OBJETIVO_ANALITICO}} is explicit (bias, power, leakage) and, if modeling, the train/test order of imputation is fixed.
- [ ] {{RESTRICCIONES}} are respected (including minimum sample size) and residual risks are noted.
- [ ] Applicable edge cases (>60%, subgroup, minimum sample) are resolved.
- [ ] There is a verifiable validation plan.
Expected deliverable: column-by-column decision matrix (mechanism, path, technique, justification, residual risk) plus a post-treatment validation plan, ready to implement and audit.
spec-datos_gobierno_politica_marco:
[inputs]
- ORGANIZACION_Y_SECTOR: {{ORGANIZACION_Y_SECTOR}} > Organization name or type and its sector (e.g. mid-size insurer, retail, fintech)
- MARCO_REGULATORIO: {{MARCO_REGULATORIO}} > Applicable privacy/data frameworks (e.g. GDPR, CCPA, LGPD, local regulation) (optional)
- DOMINIOS_DE_DATOS: {{DOMINIOS_DE_DATOS}} > Priority data domains or areas (e.g. customer, product, finance, HR)
