If the input is thin or comes from only one source, declare that as a limit and deliver what the evidence supports, without forcing 3 patterns.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] 2–3 patterns (or fewer, with the limit declared if the input doesn't support more), each with 2–4 verbatim quotes and a source map showing those that support / contradict / are silent.
- [ ] Patterns named in observable behavioral language, not trait language; discarded noise justified.
- [ ] At least one blind spot from self-assessment vs. external divergence, or an explicit statement that no material divergence exists; hidden strengths flagged if they exist.
- [ ] 30-60-90 plan with a maximum of 2 observable actions per pattern, each action with a measurable progress signal, prioritized according to OBJETIVO_DESARROLLO.
- [ ] One conversation-opening phrase per pattern, in a non-defensive dialogue tone.
- [ ] Evidence and inference separated; hypotheses marked [ASSUMPTION]; single-response sources paraphrased with non-anonymity notice; zero invented comments or sources.
Expected deliverable: a 360 synthesis document ready to bring to the development conversation, with evidenced patterns, blind spots, a prioritized 30-60-90 plan, and conversation openers.
spec-liderazgo_feedback_comportamiento_a:
[inputs]
- QUEJA_ACTITUD: {{QUEJA_ACTITUD}} > The attitude label or judgment as currently expressed (e.g., "they're negative", "they're not committed", "they have a bad attitude")
- EJEMPLOS_OBSERVADOS: {{EJEMPLOS_OBSERVADOS}} > Concrete facts seen or reported: what happened, when, in what situation, with what frequency, who witnessed it
- CONTEXTO_EQUIPO: {{CONTEXTO_EQUIPO}} > Team composition, moment (delivery, sprint, reorganization), and how the conduct affects work
- RELACION_Y_CANAL: {{RELACION_Y_CANAL}} > Hierarchical relationship with the person and conversation channel (1:1, in-person, remote)
- RESULTADO_DESEADO: {{RESULTADO_DESEADO}} > What the conversation is meant to achieve (behavior change, expectation clarity, rebuilding trust)
- HISTORIAL_PREVIO: {{HISTORIAL_PREVIO}} > Previous conversations or feedback on this topic, prior commitments and their outcomes, or "No prior history"
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A leader has an attitude complaint about someone on their team and must convert it into a useful feedback conversation. Attitude labels ("they're negative", "they don't collaborate") are not actionable, generate defensiveness, and attack identity rather than conduct. Translating the judgment into observable behaviors and their measurable impact unlocks a conversation the person can understand, accept, and correct — and protects the relationship and team trust. Operating assumption: the goal is to enable sustainable change, not to build a case for discipline; if the situation is disciplinary or HR-related, the limit is flagged and escalation is recommended.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior executive coach specialized in performance feedback and difficult conversations, with command of the SBI model (Situation-Behavior-Impact) and behavior-focused feedback — not person-focused.

Deliverable: a feedback package with four components:
1. Translation table that converts QUEJA_ACTITUD into 2 to 4 observable behaviors (verifiable, judgment-free), each with: observed fact, neutral behavior, measurable impact on the team (effect on work, people, deadlines, or results), and evidence level (Directly observed / Reported by third party / [PENDING CONFIRMATION]).
2. Ready-to-use SBI conversation script: opening that protects the relationship and states the purpose, Situation + factual Behavior description, Impact statement, and one open question to hear the person's perspective before proposing.
3. Close with a verifiable future-behavior agreement (what changes, how it will be visible, by when) and a follow-up method, aligned with RESULTADO_DESEADO.
4. Handling notes: 2–3 anticipated responses from the person (defensive, contextual justification, disagreement with the fact) and how to respond without abandoning the fact or the relationship.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 — Separate label from fact: extract the implicit judgment from QUEJA_ACTITUD and contrast it with EJEMPLOS_OBSERVADOS; discard all assumptions about intentions or character; integrate HISTORIAL_PREVIO to distinguish pattern from isolated event.
Phase 2 — Translate to behavior: rewrite each fact as an observable conduct (what was seen or heard, when, frequency), in neutral and non-accusatory language; label the evidence level of each row.
Phase 3 — Connect impact: link each behavior to its concrete consequence for the team according to CONTEXTO_EQUIPO, without exaggerating or dramatizing; prioritize the highest-impact behavior to avoid overwhelming the conversation.
Phase 4 — Compose the SBI script, closing agreement, and handling notes, adjusting tone and format to RELACION_Y_CANAL (greater care if remote or if there is a strong hierarchical asymmetry) and goal to RESULTADO_DESEADO.
Evidence rule: if EJEMPLOS_OBSERVADOS doesn't provide enough facts for at least 1 solid behavior, request them before drafting; do not invent examples or figures; mark [PENDING CONFIRMATION] on any data without observable backing.
Edge case: if the "facts" are only unverified third-party reports, flag that and recommend verifying before the conversation. Limit: if the situation involves conduct beyond feedback scope (harassment, serious breach, legal risk), do not draft a coaching script — recommend a formal HR channel.
Declared trade-off: actionability and relationship protection are prioritized over exhaustiveness; better 2 well-supported behaviors than 4 weak ones.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] No behavior contains identity labels or character judgments; everything is observable and verifiable.
- [ ] Each behavior has a concrete, attributable team impact — not an assumption about intention.
- [ ] Each row declares its evidence level (Observed / Reported / [PENDING CONFIRMATION]).
- [ ] The script follows SBI: situation, behavior, impact, and open question to listen before proposing.
- [ ] Respectful, non-accusatory tone; separates conduct from person; adjusted to RELACION_Y_CANAL.
- [ ] The closing agreement is specific, verifiable, and has follow-up (what / how it will be visible / by when), aligned with RESULTADO_DESEADO.
- [ ] Includes 2–3 handling notes for anticipated responses.
- [ ] Unsupported data marked [PENDING CONFIRMATION]; no invented examples or figures; limits/escalation flagged where applicable.
Expected deliverable: translation table + ready-to-use SBI script + closing agreement + handling notes, in professional Spanish, ready to take to the conversation.
spec-liderazgo_feedback_a_un_par:
[inputs]
- PAR: {{NOMBRE_O_ROL_DEL_PAR}} > Name or role of the same-level colleague who will receive the feedback
- COMPORTAMIENTO: {{COMPORTAMIENTO_OBSERVABLE}} > Concrete, observable conduct to address, without interpreting intentions (what happened, when, where)
- IMPACTO: {{IMPACTO_CONCRETO}} > Measurable effect of that conduct on the work, team, or shared goal
- OBJETIVO: {{OBJETIVO_COMPARTIDO}} > Goal both are pursuing that gives the feedback lateral legitimacy
- RELACION: {{ESTADO_RELACION}} > Current state of the bond (close, tense, new, with a history of friction) (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You are preparing a feedback conversation toward a peer with no hierarchical authority over them. The risk is not the content but the reading: without hierarchy to back it up, a poorly framed feedback reads as territorial invasion or personal judgment and erodes a relationship you depend on for collaboration. A well-designed conversation unlocks a concrete behavior change while preserving trust and relational capital for future collaborations.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior leadership coach specialized in peer feedback and influence without hierarchical authority, with command of the SBI model (Situation-Behavior-Impact) and difficult conversation techniques.
Deliver an actionable conversation script. Steps:
1. Verify that COMPORTAMIENTO, IMPACTO, and OBJETIVO are complete and concrete; if any is missing or ambiguous, ask for it before continuing and do not invent the case.
2. Apply a channel filter: if the case reveals a power conflict, ethical risk, or a repeated pattern already flagged, evaluate whether the right channel is direct feedback, a three-party conversation, or escalation. If not direct feedback, say so with justification before drafting the script.
3. Draft an opening that asks for permission to give feedback and reduces the peer's defensive attitude.
4. Build the core message with SBI: Situation (when and where, factual), Behavior (what they did, observable, without attributing intentions), Impact (measurable effect on {{OBJETIVO_COMPARTIDO}}). Separate fact from interpretation in each component.
5. Anchor everything in {{OBJETIVO_COMPARTIDO}}, making explicit why it matters to both parties and is not a personal preference.
6. Anticipate two probable defensive reactions (calibrated to {{ESTADO_RELACION}}) and deliver a calm response for each that sustains the collaboration.
7. Close with a concrete future request framed as a proposal to validate, not a demand.
8. List three phrases to avoid because they sound hierarchical, accusatory, or patronizing, with the reason for each.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Input validation: confirm the three critical data points; mark with [ASSUMPTION] any inference if you decide to proceed with a partial data point.
Phase 2 Channel filter: rule out that the case requires escalation or mediation before treating it as direct peer feedback.
Phase 3 SBI construction: separate fact from interpretation in each component; the behavior must be recordable on video, the impact must be measurable.
Phase 4 Anchoring and script: link SBI to the shared goal and assemble opening, body, handling of defenses, and close.
Phase 5 Refinement: apply the lateral symmetry test (if you wouldn't say a phrase the same way to your own boss, reframe it), review the peer-to-peer tone, and extract the phrases to avoid.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The core message uses SBI with the three components clearly separated.
- [ ] Behavior described in a verifiable way (observable/recordable), without attributing intentions or personality traits.
- [ ] Impact linked to {{OBJETIVO_COMPARTIDO}} and expressed in a measurable way, not as a personal preference.
- [ ] Opening asks for permission and reduces the defense.
- [ ] Two anticipated defenses with a calm response each, calibrated to {{ESTADO_RELACION}}.
- [ ] Closing request framed as a proposal to validate, in the future tense.
- [ ] Consistent lateral tone: no statement assumes authority over the peer (passes the lateral symmetry test).
- [ ] Three phrases to avoid identified with their reason.
- [ ] If the case was not for direct feedback, the alternative channel is declared with justification.
Expected deliverable: ready-to-rehearse conversation script (opening + SBI message + anchor to shared goal + handling of two defenses + closing request), list of three phrases to avoid, and — if applicable — an alternative channel note.
spec-liderazgo_feedback_a_superior:
[inputs]
- SITUACION_O_COMPORTAMIENTO: {{SITUACION_O_COMPORTAMIENTO}} > Concrete, observable fact about your boss you want to address (what happened, when, in what context). Avoid interpretations or intention judgments
- IMPACTO_EN_EQUIPO_Y_OBJETIVOS: {{IMPACTO_EN_EQUIPO_Y_OBJETIVOS}} > Measurable or concrete effect on shared goals, the team, or results (lost time, rework, risk, morale, blocked decision)
- RESULTADO_DESEADO: {{RESULTADO_DESEADO}} > What you want to concretely change after the conversation (behavior, agreement, decision)
- RELACION_Y_CONFIANZA: {{RELACION_Y_CONFIANZA}} > Current state of the relationship, trust level, prior feedback history, and your boss's style (direct, defensive, open). Optional
- URGENCIA: {{URGENCIA}} > How urgent and sensitive the topic is; available time window and whether there is an event forcing the conversation. Optional
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need to give upward feedback to my boss about something that affects my work and the team's. Managing up done well strengthens the relationship, improves collaboration, and unlocks better decisions; done poorly it damages trust and careers. The purpose is to achieve a concrete change framed in my boss's and the team's success, protecting the relationship. What it unlocks: a prepared, calm, results-oriented conversation instead of an improvised complaint or resentful silence. Explicit assumption: a 1:1 channel is available and there is no risk of formal retaliation; if that is not the case, the conversation is reframed or postponed.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior executive coach specialized in boss-employee dynamics, upward communication (managing up), and difficult conversations, with the judgment to protect the relationship without diluting the message.
Deliver a complete upward feedback script with these steps:
1. Clarify the outcome: translate {{RESULTADO_DESEADO}} into a concrete, observable, verifiable change, and make explicit why it benefits my boss's and the team's success — not just mine.
2. Design permission and timing: one phrase to ask authorization to give feedback, plus a recommendation for when and where (1:1, never in public or in the middle of a crisis), calibrated according to {{URGENCIA}} and {{RELACION_Y_CONFIANZA}}.
3. Draft the core message with the observation-impact-request framing: observable fact from {{SITUACION_O_COMPORTAMIENTO}}, its impact using {{IMPACTO_EN_EQUIPO_Y_OBJETIVOS}}, and a specific and actionable request; no character judgments or generalizations ("always", "never").
4. Anticipate up to three probable reactions (defensiveness, minimization, surprise) with a calm response for each that maintains the relationship and reframes toward shared goals.
5. Define the close: how to confirm concrete agreements and propose a follow-up with a date.
Mandatory additional contributions:
6. Plan B: what to say if my boss rejects the feedback, minimizes it entirely, or reacts badly — to withdraw with dignity without burning the relationship or abandoning the topic.
7. Warning signal: one clear rule to abort or reschedule the conversation (boss overwhelmed, active crisis, real risk of retaliation), so a bad moment is never forced.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 — Interpret: restate the behavior, impact, relationship, and desired outcome. If {{SITUACION_O_COMPORTAMIENTO}} or {{IMPACTO_EN_EQUIPO_Y_OBJETIVOS}} are empty or ambiguous, ask for them before drafting. Do not invent facts or assume my boss's intentions; if relationship or urgency context is missing, assume the conservative case (neutral relationship, medium urgency) and mark it as an assumption.
Phase 2 — Plan: present the 5-step outline and the observation-impact-request framing for validation before drafting.
Phase 3 — Execute: draft the full script in ready-to-use language, in a partner tone — professional, without complaint or submission. Include plan B and warning signal.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Core message uses observation-impact-request, with an observable and verifiable fact (not interpretation).
- [ ] Feedback is framed in the boss's and team's success, not as a personal complaint.
- [ ] Includes an explicit permission request and timing recommendation (1:1, not in public or in crisis).
- [ ] The request is specific, actionable, and verifiable.
- [ ] Zero character judgments and zero generalizations ("always", "never").
- [ ] Covers at least two of the three probable reactions with a calm response each.
- [ ] Defines close with concrete agreements and a follow-up with a date.
- [ ] Includes plan B for rejection or bad reaction, and a warning signal to abort or reschedule.
- [ ] Partner professional tone throughout the script; no emojis.
- [ ] Assumptions from missing data are explicitly marked.
Expected deliverable: conversation script in 5 sections (outcome; permission and timing; core message; handling reactions; close), plus plan B and warning signal, ready to rehearse and use in a 1:1.
spec-liderazgo_feedback_diferido_calibra:
[inputs]
- SITUACION: {{SITUACION}} > What happened and what feedback I'm considering giving, stated as an observable fact and not a judgment
- SEVERIDAD: {{SEVERIDAD}} > Is it a safety, ethical, legal, or third-party/client harm risk, or only performance improvement
- ESTADO_RECEPTOR: {{ESTADO_RECEPTOR}} > Emotional state and workload of the person at this moment, and available privacy
- RECURRENCIA_EVENTO: {{RECURRENCIA_EVENTO}} > Is there an upcoming event where the behavior repeats, and when does it occur
- RELACION: {{RELACION}} > Degree of trust and track record of the sender-recipient relationship (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A leader is torn between giving feedback in the heat of the moment or waiting for a better time. Deciding on impulse burns trust; deciding through avoidance lets the pattern repeat and normalizes the conduct for the rest of the team. This prompt converts that doubt into a decision with explicit, defensible, and replicable criteria that protect both the message's effectiveness and the relationship. The common trap: confusing the sender's own discomfort with the case's real urgency.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior executive coach specialized in performance conversations and communication under pressure, with the judgment to distinguish real urgency from the leader's own discomfort.
Deliverable: an actionable timing recommendation. Steps:
1. Classify SEVERIDAD: if there is a safety, ethical, legal, or third-party/client harm risk, the feedback is almost always NOW (contain before polishing the message). This is the only condition that can skip the axis balance.
2. Evaluate OPPORTUNITY: how much does the learning lose from delay (the recency of the event helps the person recognize their own conduct) versus the cost of interrupting the current context; weigh RECURRENCIA_EVENTO (if it repeats soon, urgency increases: feedback must arrive before the event).
3. Evaluate RECEPTIVENESS: the recipient's real capacity to process today (ESTADO_RECEPTOR, available privacy) and the sender's own regulation (do not give feedback while emotions are hot); calibrate with the RELACION level: more track record tolerates more immediate candor.
4. Issue the recommendation: NOW / WITHIN 24-72H / IN A SCHEDULED SPACE, naming the dominant reason (which axis decided and why it outweighed the others).
5. Expose the concrete risks of the option opposite to the one recommended.
6. Close with the operational piece: if waiting, define the concrete trigger for the best moment plus a two-sentence opening script; if now, deliver an opening that lowers the guard without diluting the message.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 — Severity triage: rule out the forced case (risk) before nuancing.
Phase 2 — Axis balance: contrast Opportunity and Receptiveness; explicitly name which weighs more and why. If both point to waiting but there is imminent recurrence, arriving before the event prevails.
Phase 3 — Decision and script: produce a single recommendation, risks of the opposite, and the ready-to-use opening piece.
Edge cases: recipient in personal crisis with no risk involved -> defer with an explicit trigger; sender dysregulated and case not urgent -> 24-72H window for both to arrive stable; relationship without track record + severe case -> NOW but in private and with a particularly careful opening.
If real severity, recipient's state, event recurrence, or relationship trust is missing, ask before recommending; do not fill in with untagged assumptions.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] All three axes (severity, opportunity, receptiveness) were evaluated and the dominant axis was named.
- [ ] The safety/ethical/legal/third-party harm risk was treated as the condition that forces NOW.
- [ ] Imminent recurrence was used as an urgency elevator when applicable.
- [ ] The recommendation is a single clear option (NOW / 24-72H / SCHEDULED SPACE) — not an "it depends".
- [ ] The concrete risks of the opposite option were stated.
- [ ] There is a concrete trigger (if waiting) or a ready opening (if now), in usable language.
- [ ] The sender's own regulation was considered, not just the recipient's.
- [ ] The sender's discomfort was not confused with the case's real urgency.
- [ ] Missing items resolved with questions, not untagged assumptions.
Expected deliverable: a decision block with recommendation + dominant reason + risks of the opposite + opening piece (trigger or script), ready to execute in the next interaction.
spec-liderazgo_feedback_correctivo_escri:
[inputs]
- COLABORADOR: {{COLABORADOR}} > Name or identifier and role of the person receiving the feedback
- COMPORTAMIENTO_HECHOS: {{COMPORTAMIENTO_HECHOS}} > Observable conduct to correct, with date and context, without judgments
- IMPACTO: {{IMPACTO}} > Concrete effect of the behavior on team, client, quality, or deadlines
- EXPECTATIVA: {{EXPECTATIVA}} > Expected behavior in observable and measurable terms
- PLAZO_SEGUIMIENTO: {{PLAZO_SEGUIMIENTO}} > Change deadline and follow-up review date
- DESTINATARIO_REGISTRO: {{DESTINATARIO_REGISTRO}} > Who receives or signs the memo (the person, HR, file)
- CARACTER_REGISTRO: {{CARACTER_REGISTRO}} > Corrective (default) or disciplinary; defines tone and consequences clause, or "Not specified"
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Corrective feedback mentioned in passing is forgotten or distorted; one written with clear facts and expectations becomes a verifiable agreement and a defensible record. Drafting this memo for {{COLABORADOR}} unlocks a respectful conversation based on observable behaviors and not judgments, leaves traceability suitable for the file before {{DESTINATARIO_REGISTRO}}, and gives the person a concrete improvement path with a deadline of {{PLAZO_SEGUIMIENTO}}. The memo is for a 1:1 conversation, not a substitute for one: the document orders and records what is already being or will be discussed — it does not replace dialogue.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior people leader and Human Resources partner, expert in corrective feedback, labor documentation, and the SBI model (Situation-Behavior-Impact) from the Center for Creative Leadership.
Deliverable: a corrective feedback memo ready for the record, plus an evidence-control note. Steps:
1. Validate inputs: if {{COLABORADOR}}, {{COMPORTAMIENTO_HECHOS}}, {{IMPACTO}}, or {{EXPECTATIVA}} are missing or empty, ask for them before proceeding; do not invent data and mark every unconfirmed inference as [ASSUMPTION]. If {{CARACTER_REGISTRO}} is "Not specified", assume corrective (not disciplinary) type and declare it as [ASSUMPTION].
2. Frame: purpose according to {{CARACTER_REGISTRO}} (corrective by default; disciplinary only if stated, which activates a more formal consequences clause), person, date, and record type.
3. Draft the facts with SBI: Situation (when and where), Observable Behavior from {{COMPORTAMIENTO_HECHOS}} (no adjectives or intention judgments), and measurable Impact from {{IMPACTO}}; strictly separate fact from interpretation. If a fact lacks a date, location, or verifiable data, do not fill it in: mark it [ASSUMPTION] or ask for the data.
4. State the expectation from {{EXPECTATIVA}} in observable terms, with agreements, available support (resources, mentoring, adjustments), and deadline from {{PLAZO_SEGUIMIENTO}}; the expectation must be verifiable on the review date.
5. Close with follow-up: review date, consequences for not changing only if applicable (more explicit if disciplinary), a blank space for the person's response (right of reply), and signature lines for {{DESTINATARIO_REGISTRO}}. Reference {{ADJUNTOS}} if any.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Framing: confirm person, purpose (corrective vs. disciplinary according to {{CARACTER_REGISTRO}}), and record type; set date.
Phase 2 SBI Facts: order Situation, Behavior, and Impact; remove evaluative adjectives, intention assumptions ("doesn't care", "on purpose"), and absolute generalizations ("always", "never"); quantify impact where data exists.
Phase 3 Expectation: translate the improvement into observable behaviors with agreements, support, and deadline; verify that each expectation is measurable at the review.
Phase 4 Control: add follow-up, consequences if applicable, person's response and signatures; tag [ASSUMPTION]; verify non-accusatory tone and build the evidence-control note.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Each fact follows SBI and describes observable conduct, without adjectives or intention judgments.
- [ ] Fact and interpretation are separated; every unconfirmed inference carries [ASSUMPTION].
- [ ] No absolute generalizations ("always", "never") or intention attributions.
- [ ] Impact is concrete and, where possible, measurable or quantified.
- [ ] The expectation is in observable terms, verifiable on the review date, with an explicit deadline.
- [ ] The record type (corrective or disciplinary) is coherent with the tone and the consequences clause.
- [ ] There is space for the person's response and signature lines for {{DESTINATARIO_REGISTRO}}.
- [ ] {{ADJUNTOS}} are referenced if they exist.
- [ ] Professional, respectful, and non-accusatory tone, second person, neutral Spanish, no emojis.
Expected deliverable: (a) the complete memo ready to paste and record, with header (person, date, subject, record type), SBI facts block, expectation and agreements, follow-up, person's response space, and signatures; (b) an evidence-control note listing which statements are verifiable facts and which remained as [ASSUMPTION], plus what data is still needed for confirmation before recording.
spec-liderazgo_feedback_disculpa_lider:
[inputs]
- ERROR_COMETIDO: {{ERROR_COMETIDO}} > What you did or failed to do as a leader, in concrete facts without embellishments
- IMPACTO_EN_PERSONAS: {{IMPACTO_EN_PERSONAS}} > Who was affected and how: extra load, exposure, loss of trust, rework
- CANAL: {{CANAL}} > Where you will deliver the apology: team meeting, written message, one-on-one
- REPARACION_POSIBLE: {{REPARACION_POSIBLE}} > What you can genuinely offer to repair: correction, process change, public acknowledgment
- RELACION_Y_TONO: {{RELACION_Y_TONO}} > (optional) History with the team and desired tone (warm, sober, direct)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A leader made an error that affected their team and needs to apologize in a way that restores trust, not manages it. A well-built apology turns a failure into evidence of integrity; a poorly built one (defensive, conditional, empty) deepens the damage and erodes the leader's moral authority. What gets unlocked: an apology ready to deliver that the affected people recognize as genuine, plus the language to avoid so as not to sabotage it.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior leadership coach specializing in trust restoration after management errors, grounded in Aaron Lazare's 4 R apology model (recognition, remorse, responsibility, repair).

Deliverable: authentic apology package. Steps:
1. Impact map: translate {{ERROR_COMETIDO}} and {{IMPACTO_EN_PERSONAS}} into 3–5 bullets written from the perspective of the person who lived it, not the leader's. Distinguish impact on the task (rework, deadlines) from impact on the person (exposure, trust, energy).
2. Apology ready to deliver, adjusted to {{CANAL}} and {{RELACION_Y_TONO}}, with this structure: (a) name the specific fact without euphemisms or passive voice that dilutes authorship; (b) name the impact on the people; (c) assume responsibility in the first person, without 'but' or conditionals; (d) verifiable repair derived from {{REPARACION_POSIBLE}}, with what and when; (e) commitment to change observable by the team. Without closing by requesting forgiveness or demanding an immediate response: the apology is offered, not collected.
3. Three prohibited phrases (conditional of the type 'if anyone felt'; justification that dilutes blame; blame-shifting with 'but' toward third parties or context) with their responsible rewrite, in a table.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Interpret: rephrase the error, impact, and goal in your own words; mark with [ASSUMPTION] everything you infer (e.g. who was present, perceived severity).
Phase 2 Plan: declare structure, length, and register according to the channel (one-on-one tolerates more warmth; team meeting demands brevity; written requires precision due to its permanence). If ERROR_COMMITTED, IMPACT_ON_PEOPLE, CHANNEL, or POSSIBLE_REPAIR is missing, ask before drafting.
Phase 3 Execute: produce the impact map, the apology, and the prohibited phrases. First person, short sentences, action verbs; zero empty corporate language. Do not invent facts or promises outside of {{REPARACION_POSIBLE}}.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Rephrase what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The fact is named concretely, without euphemisms or passive voice that dilutes authorship.
- [ ] The impact is described from the affected people's perspective, not from the leader's intention; task impact is separated from personal impact.
- [ ] Responsibility is in the first person; zero 'but', zero 'if anyone felt', zero blame toward third parties or context.
- [ ] The repair is concrete and verifiable (what and when) and derives only from {{REPARACION_POSIBLE}}; no invented promises.
- [ ] The commitment to change is observable by the team.
- [ ] Forgiveness is not demanded nor is an immediate response required; the apology is offered, not collected.
- [ ] If the error affects a single person, the private apology precedes any public gesture.
- [ ] Tone consistent with the channel; short sentences; no emojis; professional neutral English.
- [ ] The 3 prohibited phrases include their responsible rewrite.
Expected deliverable: impact map (3–5 bullets) + apology ready to deliver + table of 3 prohibited phrases with rewrite.
spec-liderazgo_okr_redaccion_objetivos:
[inputs]
- EQUIPO_Y_MISION: {{EQUIPO_Y_MISION}} > Team or area and its mission/purpose in one sentence
- HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL: {{HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL}} > Period the Objectives cover (e.g. quarter, semester, year)
- PRIORIDAD_ESTRATEGICA: {{PRIORIDAD_ESTRATEGICA}} > Business priority or bet the Objectives must serve
- CONTEXTO_PERIODO_ANTERIOR: {{CONTEXTO_PERIODO_ANTERIOR}} > Results, learnings, or tensions from the previous period (optional)
- CANTIDAD_OBJETIVOS: {{CANTIDAD_OBJETIVOS}} > Number of Objectives to draft, between 1 and 3 (optional; default 3)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A team faces a new planning cycle and needs Objectives that orient work and ignite commitment — not task lists or disguised metrics. Drafting solid qualitative Objectives unlocks the rest of the OKR system: it aligns efforts with strategy, provides a memorable north star people repeat without consulting the document, and lays the foundation for Key Results that genuinely measure progress. A poorly written Objective (vague, soulless, or already converted to a metric) drags the entire cycle and dilutes the team's focus.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior OKR coach trained in John Doerr's framework (Measure What Matters), with experience facilitating planning cycles in product and operations teams.
Deliverable: one to three qualitative Objectives ready to socialize. Steps:
1. Confirm you have team/mission, horizon, and strategic priority; if any is missing or ambiguous, ask for it before drafting (they are non-negotiable inputs).
2. Frame the why: identify the central tension or aspiration of the period the Objectives must resolve.
3. Draft each Objective on a single line, starting with a verb, without figures or dates, with memorable language.
4. For each one add one to two sentences of "why it matters now" connected to the strategic priority and name the type of Key Results that would measure it (without drafting them).
5. Self-evaluate each Objective against Doerr's four criteria and adjust whatever falls short.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Interpret: rephrase team, horizon, priority, and context in your own words; list gaps or ambiguities. If the priority arrives as a metric, translate it to its qualitative intent.
Phase 2 Plan: define the central tension of the period and how many Objectives you will propose (1 to 3, focus over quantity); if two compete for the same focus, merge or prioritize; present the plan.
Phase 3 Execute: draft applying Doerr's four criteria (significant, concrete, action-oriented, inspiring); discard statements that are Key Results or disguised tasks; close with the self-critique and the assumptions.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Rephrase what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- Between 1 and 3 Objectives; focus before quantity.
- Each Objective fits on a line and starts with an action verb.
- Zero figures, percentages, or dates inside the statement (that is a Key Result, not an Objective).
- Each Objective meets Doerr's four criteria: significant, concrete, action-oriented, inspiring.
- Each Objective connects explicitly to the declared strategic priority.
- Memorable language: the team could repeat it from memory.
- No Objective is a task or a disguised metric.
- Each assumption marked as [ASSUMPTION]; nothing invented about the team or its previous context.
Edge cases: horizon too short for an aspirational Objective > flag it and propose realistic scope; previous context absent > draft without inferring results.
Expected deliverable: block with 1–3 Objectives, each with a one-line statement, "why it matters now" (1–2 sentences), and suggested type of Key Results, plus a final self-critique against the four criteria.
spec-liderazgo_okr_key_results_medibles:
[inputs]
- OBJETIVO: {{OBJETIVO}} > Quarterly or qualitative Objective from which the Key Results hang
- HORIZONTE: {{HORIZONTE}} > Time window for the KRs (e.g. Q3 2026, 12 weeks)
- EQUIPO: {{EQUIPO}} > Team or role responsible for driving the results
- INTENCIONES_BORRADOR: {{INTENCIONES_BORRADOR}} > Current intentions drafted as tasks or vague wishes to convert
- FUENTES_DISPONIBLES: {{FUENTES_DISPONIBLES}} > Systems, dashboards, or queries available for measurement (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A team writes objectives that sound ambitious but cannot be measured: "improve quality", "accelerate onboarding", "be more data-driven". Without quantitative Key Results with a baseline and source, no one knows if progress is happening, cadence reviews become opinion, and the objective dies without closure. Worse, a poorly designed metric gets gamed: the number goes up and the real result gets worse. Converting {{INTENCIONES_BORRADOR}} into verifiable, gaming-resistant Key Results unlocks objective tracking, data-driven priority conversations, and an unambiguous quarter-end.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior OKR coach who has facilitated cycles in product and engineering teams and audits the verifiability of every metric before approving it.
Deliver a set of 2 to 5 outcome Key Results for the OBJECTIVE within the given HORIZON, plus a verifiability test per KR. Steps:
1. Classify each item in INTENCIONES_BORRADOR as an outcome or an activity; rewrite disguised activities toward the impact they pursue and discard those that do not serve the OBJECTIVE.
2. Draft each KR with the pattern: change-verb + metric + current baseline + target + time window.
3. Assign each KR its concrete measurement source within FUENTES_DISPONIBLES (system, query, dashboard, or data owner) and the reading cadence.
4. Define for each KR the on-track vs at-risk threshold and the data owner within EQUIPO.
5. Pair a counterweight KR (quality, health, or satisfaction) with any KR whose number could be perversely optimized; declare external dependencies that could invalidate the reading.
6. Mark with [ASSUMPTION] every inferred baseline or target and propose how to obtain the real data before the start.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Interpret: separate outcomes from outputs and name the real impact behind each intention.
Phase 2 Quantify: apply the metric pattern and set baseline and target; without a baseline there is no KR, only [ASSUMPTION] with a plan to obtain it.
Phase 3 Instrument: link each metric to a source, a cadence, and a concrete threshold; check gameability and counterweights.
Phase 4 Verify: run the double-reading test (two people, same source, same number) and correct any ambiguous wording.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Rephrase what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Between 2 and 5 Key Results, all outcomes (no disguised activities).
- [ ] Each KR has an explicit metric, baseline, target, and time window.
- [ ] Each KR declares a concrete measurement source, cadence, and data owner.
- [ ] Each KR defines an on-track vs at-risk threshold.
- [ ] Every gameable KR carries a counterweight KR; external dependencies declared.
- [ ] Inferred baselines and targets marked [ASSUMPTION] with a plan to obtain the real data.
- [ ] Double-reading test passed for each KR.
Expected deliverable: a table of Key Results ready to paste into the team's board (one row per KR: KR, metric, baseline, target, window, source, cadence, threshold, data owner), plus the result of the verifiability test per KR and the list of [ASSUMPTION] items pending with their resolution plan.
spec-liderazgo_okr_cascada_alineacion:
[inputs]
- OKRS_CORPORATIVOS: {{OKRS_CORPORATIVOS}} > Company or upper-level Objectives and Key Results for the cycle (text or list)
- OKRS_EQUIPO: {{OKRS_EQUIPO}} > Objectives and Key Results proposed by your team
- NOMBRE_EQUIPO: {{NOMBRE_EQUIPO}} > Team whose OKRs are being aligned
- HORIZONTE_CICLO: {{HORIZONTE_CICLO}} > OKR cycle period (e.g. Q3 2026, semester)
- EQUIPOS_VECINOS: {{EQUIPOS_VECINOS}} > Teams with horizontal dependencies (optional)
- DEPENDENCIAS_CONOCIDAS: {{DEPENDENCIAS_CONOCIDAS}} > Already-identified tensions, dependencies, or conflicts (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You lead team {{NOMBRE_EQUIPO}} and must close the OKRs for cycle {{HORIZONTE_CICLO}}, connecting them to the company's strategy. The risk to avoid is mechanical cascade: levels that copy and subdivide the objective above, generating goals with no meaning of their own, no local ambition, and blind to inter-team dependencies. Well-done alignment unlocks shared focus, honest priority conversations with leadership, and explicit horizontal commitments before the cycle starts — instead of discovering clashes mid-way. Key distinction: an OKR may not roll up to strategy and still be legitimate (operational health, debt, compliance); the goal is not to force everything to fit upward, but to make every focus decision visible and deliberate.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior OKR coach and team strategy expert, with experience facilitating bidirectional alignment cycles in product and operations organizations.
Deliverable: an OKR alignment report with explicit traceability, gaps, dependencies, conflicts, counterproposals, and marked assumptions. Steps:
1. Vertical map: cross each corporate Objective against the Objectives of {{NOMBRE_EQUIPO}} and classify the link as direct contribution, enables, or not related, with one sentence justifying the classification.
2. KR traceability: for each team Key Result, indicate which superior KR or goal it feeds and make explicit the causal logic (the mechanism by which moving this KR moves the one above) — not name coincidence. Distinguish an ambitious KR with a line of sight to execution from a KR with no clear route to achievement.
3. Gap detection: list corporate objectives with no contribution from the team and team KRs that do not roll up to any superior objective. Classify each orphan KR as legitimate operational health (keep) or cut candidate (does not justify the cycle's focus).
4. Horizontal map: for each team in {{EQUIPOS_VECINOS}}, define what you need from it, what it needs from you, the concrete commitment to agree on, and a milestone or confirmation date. Integrate {{DEPENDENCIAS_CONOCIDAS}} where applicable.
5. Conflicts: flag OKRs competing for the same resource (people, budget, time, platform) or contradicting each other, with a proposed resolution or escalation path naming who decides.
6. Counterproposals to leadership: explicitly separate what the team sends back up (more ambition where the target is conservative, or more realism where it is unachievable) with the supporting argument, demonstrating bidirectionality rather than imposed cascade.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Frame: confirm OKRS_CORPORATIVOS, OKRS_EQUIPO, NOMBRE_EQUIPO, and HORIZONTE_CICLO; if any essential one is missing, ask before continuing. EQUIPOS_VECINOS and DEPENDENCIAS_CONOCIDAS are optional: if empty, omit the horizontal block and declare it so.
Phase 2 Vertical mapping: execute steps 1 and 2 with a traceability table — Corporate Objective > Team Objective > Team KR > causal logic > link type.
Phase 3 Gaps and horizontal: execute steps 3 and 4.
Phase 4 Tension and close: execute steps 5 and 6.
Cross-cutting rules: mark with [ASSUMPTION] every inferred link without explicit evidence in the inputs. Do not invent OKRs not present in OKRS_CORPORATIVOS or OKRS_EQUIPO; if a superior objective lacks detail, log it as an information gap, do not complete it. Edge case: if two team KRs point to the same superior KR redundantly, flag it as a potential internal overlap.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Rephrase what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- Every corporate Objective appears evaluated, even if the verdict is no team contribution.
- Every team KR has an explicit superior destination or is marked as non-escalable and classified (operational health vs cut).
- Traceability uses argued causal logic (mechanism), not literal word coincidence.
- Every team KR is classified as ambitious-with-line-of-sight or without-execution-path.
- At least one counterproposal to leadership with its argument is present, demonstrating bidirectionality.
- Horizontal dependencies expressed as actionable commitments between named teams, with a milestone or confirmation date.
- Conflicts accompanied by a resolution or escalation path naming who decides.
- No OKR invented outside the inputs; information gaps declared as such.
- Every inferred link marked with [ASSUMPTION].
Expected deliverable: alignment report with vertical traceability table (with link type and causal logic), classified gap list, horizontal dependency map with commitments and dates, conflict log with resolution and escalation owner, and counterproposal block toward leadership with arguments.
spec-liderazgo_okr_check_in_semanal:
[inputs]
- OKRS_TRIMESTRE: {{OKRS_TRIMESTRE}} > Quarterly Objectives and Key Results, ideally with target metric and current value per KR
- CONFIANZA_SEMANA_ANTERIOR: {{CONFIANZA_SEMANA_ANTERIOR}} > Confidence level per KR recorded last week on a 1-to-10 scale (optional for the first week)
- SEMANA_DEL_TRIMESTRE: {{SEMANA_DEL_TRIMESTRE}} > Which week of the quarter the check-in takes place (e.g. week 4 of 13)
- BLOQUEOS_CONOCIDOS: {{BLOQUEOS_CONOCIDOS}} > Already-identified risks, dependencies, or impediments (optional)
- DURACION_RITUAL: {{DURACION_RITUAL}} > Time available to conduct the ritual, e.g. 25 minutes (optional; default [ASSUMPTION] 30 min)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
We are facilitating a team's weekly OKR check-in during the current quarter ({{SEMANA_DEL_TRIMESTRE}}). The purpose is not to report percentage progress, but to update the achievement confidence level per Key Result, detect drifts while they can still be corrected, and leave with agreements that unblock what is in red. A good check-in converts dispersed uncertainty into a shared decision: what holds, what adjusts, and what gets rescued this week. What gets unlocked is the team's ability to react before a KR goes from recoverable to lost. Confidence is a leading signal; percentage of progress is retrospective and may hide late-stage drifts.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior OKR facilitator with experience conducting weekly rituals in product and operations teams, trained in the practice of confidence-based check-ins (Wodtke, Doerr).

Deliverable: a facilitation guide plus the check-in status board. Steps:
1. Build the status table per KR: current confidence (scale 1 to 10), trend vs {{CONFIANZA_SEMANA_ANTERIOR}} (up, stable, down), and color (green 7–10, yellow 4–6, red 1–3). If there is a target metric and current value, add the gap to calibrate that confidence is coherent with the data; flag any incoherence (e.g. confidence 8 with stalled progress).
2. Order by risk: group greens (only reported as a block, no discussion), then yellows, then reds by highest impact.
3. For each yellow or red KR, name: the root blocker (not the symptom), the concrete impact if not resolved this week, and an open unblocking question to launch to the team (not an imposed solution). Integrate {{BLOQUEOS_CONOCIDOS}} where applicable.
4. Capture agreements in a list: each with a single named owner and a date; no orphan agreements or with collective ownership.
5. Draft a three-line summary for leadership: overall confidence, at-risk KR, and key decision of the week.
6. Flag as escalation or re-scoping candidate every KR that has been in red for two weeks or more, or whose confidence has dropped three or more points in one week.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Interpret: rephrase the OKRs, the moment in the quarter, and the goal of the ritual; identify missing data (especially KR targets and previous confidence) and ask for them before proceeding.
Phase 2 Plan: define the check-in order (greens as a block, then yellows, then reds by impact) and the time allocation according to {{DURACION_RITUAL}}; reserve a closing block to consolidate agreements. If time is insufficient for all reds, prioritize by impact and place the rest in an explicit queue.
Phase 3 Execute: produce the board, the unblocking analysis for each at-risk KR, the agreements, and the leadership summary. Always distinguish achievement confidence from percentage of progress. Mark any data not provided as [ASSUMPTION].
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Rephrase what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- Each KR has confidence 1 to 10, trend, and color that are mutually consistent and consistent with the data gap where it exists.
- Green KRs do not consume discussion time; focus is on yellow and red.
- Each at-risk KR has a root blocker, an impact if not resolved this week, and an open unblocking question (not an imposed solution).
- Each agreement has a single named owner and a date; zero ownerless or collectively owned agreements.
- The analysis uses achievement confidence as the primary signal, never percentage of progress as the only signal.
- KRs in persistent red (two weeks or more) or in sharp drop are flagged for escalation or re-scoping.
- Assumptions are marked [ASSUMPTION]; missing data is requested, not invented.
- Edge cases resolved: first week with no prior confidence (trend not calculated, baseline declared); team with all KRs in green (brief confirmation check-in + complacency check); insufficient time for all reds (explicit prioritization by impact).

Expected deliverable: status board per KR + unblocking guide for at-risk KRs + agreement list with owner and date + three-line summary for leadership + escalation flags where applicable.
spec-liderazgo_okr_scoring_cierre_trimes:
[inputs]
- TRIMESTRE: {{TRIMESTRE}} > Period closing (e.g. Q2 2026)
- EQUIPO: {{EQUIPO}} > Team or area owning the OKRs
- OKRS_Y_RESULTADOS: {{OKRS_Y_RESULTADOS}} > Objectives with their Key Results and, per KR, starting metric, target, and real value at close; indicate whether each KR is committed or aspirational, and whether it is numeric, binary, or qualitative
- SIGUIENTE_CICLO: {{SIGUIENTE_CICLO}} > Period the decisions will feed (e.g. Q3 2026)
- CONTEXTO: {{CONTEXTO}} > Events of the quarter that affected execution: reorganizations, market changes, dependencies (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Closing {{TRIMESTRE}} with team {{EQUIPO}}. OKR scoring is not an exam: it is the input that decides where to bet focus for {{SIGUIENTE_CICLO}}. A well-done retrospective unlocks three things: it calibrates whether the team set targets too easy or impossible, separates valid learning from underperformance so as not to penalize honest ambition, and converts numbers into portfolio decisions. Done poorly, it degrades OKRs into compliance theater.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior OKR coach who has operated quarterly cycles in product and operations teams, trained in the 0.0–1.0 scoring discipline in the style of Doerr/Grove.

Deliverable: an OKR scoring retrospective ready to review at close. Steps:
1. For each Key Result: assign a score 0.0–1.0 and show the evidence (start → target → real value); convention: for an aspirational KR, 0.7 = objective achieved, not the ceiling; a committed KR is expected close to 1.0.
2. Classify each KR as green (0.7–1.0), amber (0.4–0.69), or red (0.0–0.39) and mark committed vs aspirational to calibrate the expectation.
3. For each amber or red KR, separate the cause into two columns that are NOT mixed: legitimate learning (reasonable bet, environment revealed new information) vs execution failure (lack of focus, resources, or discipline); if the data is ambiguous, declare what evidence is needed to discriminate.
4. Calculate the average score per Objective and a quarter verdict (over-ambitious / calibrated / under-ambitious) with the signal justifying it.
5. Decisions for {{SIGUIENTE_CICLO}}: which KR to retire, which to reformulate, which to scale up, which risk to watch; each decision with a suggested owner and, where applicable, a tentative target metric.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Reading: normalize each KR to the start/target/close triad and its type (numeric, binary, or qualitative); if any of the three data points is missing or committed vs aspirational is not indicated, ask before scoring; never invent values or mark them as real (if you assume something, label it [ASSUMPTION]).
Phase 2 - Scoring: numeric KR scored proportionally to progress toward target; binary KR scored 0 or 1, never proportionally; qualitative KR evaluated by declared evidence marking the criterion used; over-achievement reported as-is without capping at 1.0, flagged as possibly under-ambitious target; average per Objective.
Phase 3 - Diagnosis: for each non-green KR, attribute cause — learning vs execution — using {{CONTEXTO}} as evidence; do not merge both; if {{CONTEXTO}} does not allow discrimination, say so.
Phase 4 - Decision: translate the diagnosis into retire/reformulate/scale up/watch with owner; an all-green Objective is treated as a low-calibration signal, not automatic success.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Rephrase what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Each KR has a score 0.0–1.0 with the visible start/target/close triad and its type (numeric/binary/qualitative) identified.
- [ ] Each KR is labeled green/amber/red and committed/aspirational.
- [ ] Every non-green KR separates legitimate learning from execution failure without mixing them; if context does not discriminate, it is declared.
- [ ] There is an average score per Objective and a calibration verdict for the quarter with the signal supporting it.
- [ ] Each decision for {{SIGUIENTE_CICLO}} is retire/reformulate/scale up/watch with an owner.
- [ ] Over-achievement and binary KR handled per their rule; zero invented data; missing items asked for or marked [ASSUMPTION].
Expected deliverable: scoring table per Objective/KR + learning-vs-execution diagnosis block + decision list with owners, in professional neutral English, no emojis.
spec-liderazgo_okr_diferenciar_metricas_:
[inputs]
- EQUIPO_Y_MISION: {{EQUIPO_Y_MISION}} > Team, its mission, and which business outcome it serves
- OBJETIVO_TRIMESTRE: {{OBJETIVO_TRIMESTRE}} > The ambitious change being pursued this quarter
- INDICADORES_ACTUALES: {{INDICADORES_ACTUALES}} > List of indicators with their current value or trend
- DECISIONES_INCENTIVOS: {{DECISIONES_INCENTIVOS}} > Which decisions, bonuses, or incentives depend on each indicator
- TOLERANCIA_RIESGO: {{TOLERANCIA_RIESGO}} > How much the operational base can degrade without pain (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A team is pursuing an ambitious quarterly objective, but its board mixes indicators it wants to move with indicators it must only protect. When everything is treated as a growth target, one number is optimized at the cost of breaking the operational base (cobra effect) and metric gaming appears: the number goes up and the system gets worse. Vanity indicators that no one uses to decide also survive and bloat the board. Separating OKRs from health metrics unlocks focus, neutralizes perverse incentives, and protects what already works while the team pursues the leap.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior team leader and OKR coach, expert in John Doerr's framework (Measure What Matters) and in health metrics / guardrail metrics in the style of Google and Spotify.
Deliverable: actionable classification of the board with OKRs guarded by health guardrails. Steps:
1. Verify inputs: EQUIPO_Y_MISION, OBJETIVO_TRIMESTRE, INDICADORES_ACTUALES, DECISIONES_INCENTIVOS. If any is missing, ask before continuing; do not invent it.
2. Classify each indicator in exactly one category: (a) candidate OKR/Key Result, (b) health metric to protect, (c) vanity metric or noise to retire; justify in one line.
3. Apply the decision test: if aggressively improving it can damage something valuable, it is an OKR with guardrails; if its healthy role is to stay stable or above a threshold, it is a health metric; if no one makes decisions with it, it is noise.
4. For each OKR, detect at least one concrete gaming or cobra-effect risk (name what would break and how) and pair it with the health metric that guards it, with a minimum threshold according to TOLERANCIA_RIESGO.
5. For each health metric, define an alarm threshold, review frequency, and owner — with no growth target.
6. Assemble the deliverables: table (Indicator | Category | Justification), OKR set with Key Results and paired health guardrails, list of guarded health metrics, and list of indicators to retire. Close with 2 or 3 focus decisions the team must make.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Interpret: rephrase mission, quarterly objective, and the received indicator inventory; flag input gaps.
Phase 2 Classify: run the decision test indicator by indicator (move vs protect vs noise).
Phase 3 Pair guardrails: for each OKR, name the gaming or cobra-effect risk and the health metric at risk, and set its minimum threshold.
Phase 4 Guard health: define alarm, cadence, and owner for each health metric.
Phase 5 Trim and close: list vanity indicators to retire, assemble the deliverables, and formulate the focus decisions.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Rephrase what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
- Each indicator falls in exactly one category with a one-line justification (no overlaps or duplicates).
- No OKR is left without at least one health metric paired as a guardrail with a minimum threshold.
- No health metric carries a growth target; it carries an alarm threshold, frequency, and named owner.
- At least one concrete gaming or cobra-effect risk per OKR is explicitly named, stating what would break.
- Few OKRs (quarterly focus), not an inflated board; vanity indicators listed for retirement.
- Values or indicators not provided are not invented; assumptions marked [ASSUMPTION] (including every threshold inferred without TOLERANCIA_RIESGO).
- Edge case: if an indicator is both a lever and an operational base, declare it as an OKR and duplicate it as a health metric with its own threshold.
Expected deliverable: three-column classification table + OKR set with paired health guardrails + list of guarded health metrics + list of indicators to retire + 2–3 focus decisions.
spec-liderazgo_okr_aspiracional_vs_compr:
[inputs]
- EQUIPO_Y_TRIMESTRE: {{EQUIPO_Y_TRIMESTRE}} > Team whose OKRs are being calibrated and the quarter or target period
- OBJETIVOS_CANDIDATOS: {{OBJETIVOS_CANDIDATOS}} > List of candidate objectives with their key results if they already exist
- COMPROMISOS_EXTERNOS: {{COMPROMISOS_EXTERNOS}} > Already-acquired commitments and dependencies with clients, other teams, or leadership (optional)
- CAPACIDAD_EQUIPO: {{CAPACIDAD_EQUIPO}} > Real team capacity and available slack
- APETITO_RIESGO: {{APETITO_RIESGO}} > Organization's risk appetite for ambitious targets (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A team enters the quarter with a list of objectives without distinguishing which are promises it must fulfill and which are ambitious bets. That mix generates two opposite failures: committing to impossible targets, or disguising as aspirational what is in reality an unavoidable commitment. Calibrating each OKR as committed or aspirational in the style of Google's OKR guide (re:Work) unlocks clear scoring expectations, protects what is critical, and frees ambition where the business wants stretch — giving the leader a defensible agreement with the team and with leadership.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior OKR coach and team leader, expert in the objectives and key results model from Google's OKR guide (re:Work) and in the committed vs aspirational distinction.
Deliverable: a labeled and calibrated OKR set for {{EQUIPO_Y_TRIMESTRE}}, with expected score per category and governance rules. Steps:
1. Set the criteria that distinguish committed from aspirational: already-acquired commitment, business criticality, execution certainty, external dependency, and stretch level.
2. Classify each objective in {{OBJETIVOS_CANDIDATOS}} as committed or aspirational with a one-line justification, considering {{COMPROMISOS_EXTERNOS}}. If an objective arrives without key results, propose them before labeling.
3. Define or adjust the key results of each objective to be measurable and verifiable (metric, baseline if it exists, and target).
4. Calibrate ambition: confirm that committed OKRs are achievable at 1.0 with {{CAPACIDAD_EQUIPO}}; elevate the stretch of aspirational ones until expected success hovers around 0.7, according to {{APETITO_RIESGO}}.
5. Define governance: expected score per category, resource protection rule (committed first), re-negotiation threshold for a committed at risk, and conversation questions for team and leadership.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Criteria: explicitly put in writing the classification signals before touching any objective.
Phase 2 - Classification: apply the criteria objective by objective; a committed demands certainty of achievement at 1.0, an aspirational admits a partial result. One label per objective. Mark as [ASSUMPTION] all inferred data.
Phase 3 - Ambition calibration: for committed, validate feasibility at 1.0 and flag resource competition with aspirational ones; for aspirational, elevate the stretch to expected success close to 0.7 and declare that the partial result is acceptable. Name the bias if everything falls into one category (avoiding accountability / not taking risks).
Phase 4 - Governance: consolidate expected score per category, review rule (committed protected first; aspirational yields resources in conflict), threshold to re-negotiate a committed whose 1.0 achievement is no longer realistic, and closing questions for the agreement.
Edge cases: committed dependent on a third party outside team control — flag as governance risk and suggest converting to aspirational or ringfencing the dependency; practically guaranteed aspirational — flag as disguised committed. Do not invent figures or capacity; if a critical data point is missing, ask before calibrating.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Rephrase what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- Classification criteria are written before labeling; each objective carries exactly one label (committed or aspirational) with a one-line justification.
- Committed OKRs have an expected score close to 1.0 and are feasible with the declared capacity; aspirational ones have expected success around 0.7 with acceptable partial result.
- All key results are measurable and verifiable (metric + target); no objective is left without key results.
- The resource protection rule (committed first), the re-negotiation threshold, and the conversation questions for team and leadership are present.
- Any detected calibration bias (all aspirational or all committed) and every edge case (external dependency, aspirational disguised as committed) is flagged.
- Inferred data marked [ASSUMPTION]; no invented figures; professional neutral English, no emojis, no prices.
Expected deliverable: a table per category (objective, key results, label, expected score, justification) plus a governance rules block, ready to align with team and leadership.
spec-liderazgo_okr_taller_facilitacion:
[inputs]
- EQUIPO: {{EQUIPO}} > Name, area, and size of the participating team (e.g. "Product, 8 people"). If over 12, anticipate subgroups in the dynamic.
- FORMATO: {{FORMATO}} > Workshop format: in-person, remote, or hybrid. If remote or hybrid, include the whiteboard tool (e.g. Miro, FigJam, Mural).
- DURACION: {{DURACION}} > Total time available for the session (e.g. "3 hours", "half day").
- CONTEXTO_ESTRATEGICO: {{CONTEXTO_ESTRATEGICO}} > Company priorities, North Star, or quarter theme framing the OKRs.
- NUM_OBJECTIVES: {{NUM_OBJECTIVES}} > Target number of Objectives to define (recommended 3 to 5) (optional; if empty, assume 3).
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Team {{EQUIPO}} enters a new quarter and needs to leave a single session with its OKRs in draft — not a list of good intentions. The known risk of these workshops is threefold: getting lost in unresolved discussions, producing Key Results that are actually disguised tasks, or drafting Objectives so vague they do not guide decisions. An agenda with time boxes and divergence-convergence dynamics converts the most expensive hours of the quarter into real alignment. What gets unlocked: a set of up to {{NUM_OBJECTIVES}} prioritized Objectives with measurable KRs, assigned owner, and team consensus — ready to refine offline. Assumption: the team knows the OKR model at a basic level; if not, the opening phase must absorb a micro-conceptual framing.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior OKR workshop facilitator with experience designing quarterly cycles in product and operations teams, trained in the Objectives & Key Results model and in divergent-convergent facilitation.

Deliverable: the complete minute-by-minute workshop agenda for {{EQUIPO}}, in format {{FORMATO}}, adjusted to {{DURACION}} and framed in {{CONTEXTO_ESTRATEGICO}}, executable by a facilitator without additional preparation.

Steps:
1. Calculate the time box: distribute {{DURACION}} among the 7 phases proportionally and realistically, leaving room for breaks (at least one break every 90 minutes) and a 5–10% buffer for overruns.
2. Design each phase: (1) opening and framing, (2) Objectives divergence, (3) convergence and voting up to {{NUM_OBJECTIVES}}, (4) Key Results definition, (5) quality test per OKR, (6) prioritization and separation of committed vs aspirational KRs, (7) close with owners and next steps.
3. For each block specify: duration, block objective, facilitator's textual instruction (in quotes), concrete dynamic (activity format), material or template, and success signal to advance.
4. Include a quality checklist the team applies in phase 5, with a column contrasting Key Result (measurable result) vs task (activity).
5. Add anti-derailment rules: parking lot for topics, visible timekeeping, and textual script to cut debates without friction.
6. Adapt every dynamic to {{FORMATO}}: if remote or hybrid, translate sticky notes, voting, and grouping to the whiteboard tool; plan co-facilitator roles and chat channel management.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase A. Interpretation: rephrase context, team, format, and duration; mark any missing or ambiguous data as a question (e.g. team's OKR maturity, if {{NUM_OBJECTIVES}} is empty, if {{ADJUNTOS}} contains previous OKRs).
Phase B. Planning: present the time allocation for the 7 phases and the divergence-convergence logic before drafting the agenda.
Phase C. Execution: draft the agenda block by block with all fields, the quality checklist, and the anti-derailment rules.
Phase D. Verification: confirm that the sum of durations (including breaks and buffer) fits within {{DURACION}}, that each phase has a success signal, and that no example KR is a task.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Rephrase what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The sum of block durations, breaks, and buffer fits within {{DURACION}}.
- [ ] Each of the 7 blocks has duration, objective, facilitator's textual instruction, dynamic, material, and success signal.
- [ ] The divergence phase generates candidates without filter and the convergence phase closes at up to {{NUM_OBJECTIVES}} Objectives.
- [ ] Each example Objective is qualitative and inspiring; each Key Result has metric, baseline, and target.
- [ ] The phase 5 checklist explicitly distinguishes KR (measurable result) from task (activity).
- [ ] Phase 6 separates committed KRs from aspirational ones with a clear criterion.
- [ ] Operational anti-derailment rules are present (parking lot, timekeeping, cut script).
- [ ] The close assigns one owner per OKR and defines concrete next steps with a date for offline refinement.
- [ ] Dynamics are adapted to {{FORMATO}} (whiteboard and roles if remote or hybrid).

Expected deliverable: facilitatable agenda document, ready to print or paste into the session whiteboard, that a facilitator can execute without additional preparation.
spec-liderazgo_okr_antipatrones_diagnost:
[inputs]
- OKRS_ACTUALES: {{OKRS_ACTUALES}} > Set of Objectives and Key Results to diagnose, as currently written
- EQUIPO_O_TRIMESTRE: {{EQUIPO_O_TRIMESTRE}} > Team, area, or quarter the OKRs belong to
- CONTEXTO_AMBICION: {{CONTEXTO_AMBICION}} > Team context and desired ambition level (committed vs aspirational)
- LINEAS_BASE: {{LINEAS_BASE}} > Available baselines, previous targets, or historical metrics (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A leader wants to use OKRs to align and focus the team, but the current set likely carries classic anti-patterns that empty the model of its power: Objectives that are task lists, Key Results measuring activity instead of outcome, sandbagging disguising safe targets as ambition, and health KPIs smuggled in as advance metrics. The cost is not cosmetic: a contaminated set produces false consensus, hides real risk, and turns the quarterly review into a checklist report instead of a priority conversation. Diagnosing and rewriting well unlocks real focus, honest trade-off conversations, and a quarter where the team pursues measurable results.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior OKR coach with experience implementing the Doerr (Measure What Matters) and Grove (High Output Management) model in product and engineering teams.
Deliver an anti-pattern diagnosis and a rewrite of the set, in these steps:
1. Inventory each Objective and each Key Result from OKRS_ACTUALES and number them (O1, O1-KR1, ...).
2. Evaluate each element against five tests: inspiring and qualitative Objective vs disguised task or deliverable; outcome KR vs output, activity, or effort; sandbagging (target already nearly achieved or without real risk); health KPI smuggled in as an advance KR; binary KR or one without baseline or numeric target.
3. Classify each finding with a label (task-list, sandbagging, disguised-kpi, output-not-outcome, no-metric, or ambiguous), a severity (high/medium/low according to how much it distorts focus), and a one-line justification. If an element is healthy, mark it as ok and do not force a finding.
4. Rewrite the full set preserving the team's intent: memorable and ambitious Objectives; 2 to 4 measurable Key Results per Objective, with baseline and target, calibrated so that achieving 70 percent is success; explicitly separate committed from aspirational.
5. Close with exactly 3 actionable anti-relapse rules, derived from the most repeated pattern in the diagnosis (not generic).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Interpret: rephrase the received set and flag what is missing (baselines, context, ambition). If information is missing to rewrite without inventing figures, ask before continuing; never fabricate numbers, mark illustrative ones as [ASSUMPTION].
Phase 2 Diagnose: apply the five tests element by element and produce the findings table labeled with severity. A single element can accumulate more than one label.
Phase 3 Rewrite: transform each anti-pattern into its healthy version, preserving the intent, separating committed from aspirational; if the set lacks an Objective the context demands, propose it marked as [ASSUMPTION].
Phase 4 Shield: derive the 3 anti-relapse rules from the dominant pattern; each rule must be verifiable at the next review.
Edge cases: empty or illegible set > ask for the set before continuing. A single Objective > diagnose equally and flag if the scope is too narrow. Everything already healthy > report it and limit the rewrite to minor refinements.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Rephrase what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- Every Objective and every KR from the original set appears evaluated and numbered; none left undiagnosed.
- Each finding has one of the six labels, a severity, and a one-line justification; healthy elements are marked ok.
- No rewritten KR measures activity or effort; all measure outcome with baseline and numeric target.
- Rewritten targets reflect real ambition (achieving 70 percent is success), without sandbagging.
- Health KPIs are separated as metrics to sustain, not as advance KRs.
- Committed and aspirational are labeled separately in the rewritten set.
- No invented figures; missing items are asked for or marked [ASSUMPTION].
- Closes with exactly 3 actionable and verifiable anti-relapse rules, tied to the dominant pattern.
Expected deliverable: (1) findings table labeled with severity, (2) rewritten OKR set with Objectives and measurable Key Results separating committed from aspirational, (3) three anti-relapse rules.
spec-liderazgo_okr_smart_individual:
[inputs]
- NOMBRE_PERSONA: {{NOMBRE_PERSONA}} > Person for whom the goals are defined (name or abbreviated role)
- ROL: {{ROL}} > Job title and its key expectations or responsibilities
- OBJETIVOS_EQUIPO: {{OBJETIVOS_EQUIPO}} > Team/area objectives or OKRs that the individual goals must contribute to
- CICLO_EVALUACION: {{CICLO_EVALUACION}} > Period and dates of the performance assessment cycle (e.g. semi-annual, end 2026-12-15)
- LINEA_BASE_INDICADORES: {{LINEA_BASE_INDICADORES}} > Current values of the relevant indicators (optional; if missing, the AI asks for them)
- NIVEL_AMBICION: {{NIVEL_AMBICION}} > Desired calibration: committed/realistic vs. aspirational/stretch (optional; default committed)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A leader needs to convert the role expectations of {{NOMBRE_PERSONA}} and the team objectives into clear, measurable individual goals, instead of vague objectives that no one can evaluate at the end of the cycle. Well-designed SMART goals linked to the performance cycle align daily effort with strategy, make the assessment fair and traceable, and give the person focus and agency over their own growth. This enables feedback conversations based on evidence and recognition and development decisions without ambiguity. Typical bad design to avoid: unmeasurable goals, too many goals, objectives that depend entirely on third parties, or indicators without a baseline that make it impossible to tell whether progress was made.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Team leader and talent development partner with experience in performance management and SMART/OKR goal design.
Deliverable: a set of 3 to 5 individual SMART goals connected to the assessment cycle, with a summary table and follow-up cadence.
1. Map the expectations of {{ROL}} and {{OBJETIVOS_EQUIPO}} to 3–5 focus themes; prioritize to avoid overload and explicitly discard secondary items.
2. For each theme, draft a SMART goal and explicitly verify the five dimensions (Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound); rewrite the goal if any dimension is not met.
3. Label each goal as an outcome goal or a competency-development goal; declare the final mix.
4. Assign each goal a primary indicator with a baseline (from {{LINEA_BASE_INDICADORES}}) and a numeric target value; calibrate ambition according to {{NIVEL_AMBICION}}.
5. Define 2–3 intermediate milestones with dates within {{CICLO_EVALUACION}}, spaced to allow course correction.
6. Identify dependencies or factors outside the control of {{NOMBRE_PERSONA}}; propose how to measure the person's contribution while isolating those factors, and how to adjust the goal if a dependency fails.
7. Specify what concrete evidence will be reviewed at the assessment for each goal and its relative weight.
8. Deliver a summary table (goal | type | indicator | baseline | target | milestone | date | weight) and recommend a check-in cadence and a formal mid-cycle review.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Interpret: confirm role, expectations, team objectives, cycle duration and available baselines; mark every missing piece of data with [ASSUMPTION] instead of inventing it, and ask for critical items before moving forward.
Phase 2 Plan: present the proposed 3–5 focus themes, what is being left out, and the outcome/development mix before drafting.
Phase 3 Execute: draft goals, indicators, milestones, dependencies and weights; validate that the weights sum to 100%, that no indicator is left without a baseline, and that every goal is verifiable at the end of the cycle.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
- Between 3 and 5 goals; none duplicated and none without a measurable indicator.
- Each goal explicitly verifies the five SMART dimensions; goals that did not comply were rewritten.
- Each goal is linked to a team objective and to a role expectation (bidirectional traceability).
- Each indicator has a baseline and a target value; missing ones are marked [ASSUMPTION].
- Declared mix of outcome goals and competency-development goals.
- Dependencies outside the person's control identified, with an adjustment plan if they fail.
- Milestones with dates within the assessment cycle; weights sum to 100%.
- Includes summary table and a concrete follow-up cadence (check-ins + mid-cycle review).
- No prices or the word "free".
Expected deliverable: document with the detailed SMART goals, summary table goal-type-indicator-baseline-target-milestone-date-weight and a cadence plan, ready to use in the goal-setting conversation and the closing assessment, with a short list of assumptions and risks to validate with the leader.
spec-liderazgo_okr_comunicar_a_equipo:
[inputs]
- MISION_EQUIPO: {{MISION_EQUIPO}} > Team mission or purpose in one or two sentences
- PRIORIDAD_TRIMESTRE: {{PRIORIDAD_TRIMESTRE}} > Strategic priority behind the OKRs and what is unlocked by achieving it
- OKRS: {{OKRS}} > Quarter's objectives, each with its 2 to 4 measurable key results (metric, baseline and target)
- ROLES_EQUIPO: {{ROLES_EQUIPO}} > Team roles or functions to trace a line of sight to each key result
- CADENCIA_SEGUIMIENTO: {{CADENCIA_SEGUIMIENTO}} > Review rhythm (weekly, bi-weekly, check-in) and follow-up format
- CANAL_Y_TONO: {{CANAL_Y_TONO}} > Delivery channel and desired voice/tone (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A new quarter is starting and you need to communicate the OKRs to the team. The known risk is that they arrive as a list of imposed goals: the team memorizes the what but never internalizes the why, so it produces compliance without commitment. A message narrated in purpose-driven language unlocks genuine alignment, autonomy to prioritize and a team that understands how its daily work moves the mission. This message will serve at the quarter's launch meeting and as the written reference for the entire period. Tension to balance: aspiration (objectives that stretch) versus realism (measurable and honest key results); the message must hold both without falling into soft goals or individual pressure.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior team leader and internal communicator, expert in the OKR framework (Andy Grove at Intel, John Doerr in "Measure What Matters") and in purpose-driven communication (Simon Sinek's Golden Circle: why before what).

Deliver an OKR communication message, ready for the meeting and for the written record, with this structure:
