1. Opening with a purpose statement connecting MISION_EQUIPO to the quarter that is starting, before naming any goal.
2. The why of the quarter: PRIORIDAD_TRIMESTRE explained and what is unlocked if it is achieved (impact on client, business or mission).
3. Each Objective in OKRS narrated as a shared aspiration (not as a task), with its measurable key results below (metric, baseline and target when available) and a sentence explaining why each one matters.
4. Line of sight: how the work of each role in ROLES_EQUIPO connects to specific key results; no role is left without at least one link.
5. Rules of the game: CADENCIA_SEGUIMIENTO, green/amber/red criteria, and an explicit note about what an OKR is NOT (not a task list, not an individual performance evaluation, not a bonus contract).
6. Close that invites commitment and opens space for questions, adjusted to CANAL_Y_TONO if provided.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Interpret: order the OKRS by hierarchy (aspirational objective, then its 2 to 4 measurable key results). Detect and report: key results without a metric or target, objectives that are actually tasks or deliverables, key results that are binary tasks instead of outcome measures, and roles without a clear line of sight. If there are more than 3 to 5 objectives, warn of the risk of dispersing focus.
Phase 2 - Plan: define the why, how, what narrative thread (Golden Circle) and which key result each role connects to; list gaps and assumptions to confirm before drafting.
Phase 3 - Execute: draft the message following the 6 sections of the Request. Narrate objectives as aspirations and key results as verifiable measurements. Do not invent figures: mark every missing piece of data as [to be filled in] and every unconfirmed reasoning as [ASSUMPTION].
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist before delivering:
- [ ] The why (mission + priority) appears before any specific goal.
- [ ] Each Objective is narrated as an aspiration, not as a task or to-do list.
- [ ] Each key result is measurable (outcome, not binary task); absent data is marked [to be filled in], no figures invented.
- [ ] Each team role has an explicit line of sight to at least one key result.
- [ ] Follow-up cadence and green/amber/red criteria are defined.
- [ ] There is a note about what an OKR is NOT (neither tasks, nor individual performance evaluation, nor bonus contract).
- [ ] The close invites commitment and opens questions, it does not merely inform.
- [ ] Anomalies in the OKR set (objectives that are tasks, KR without a metric, too many objectives, orphan roles) were flagged.
- [ ] No prices, no the word "free", neutral professional Spanish, no emojis.
Expected deliverable: OKR communication message in prose with titled sections, ready to read at the launch meeting and archive as the quarter's reference.
spec-liderazgo_okr_priorizacion_foco:
[inputs]
- LISTA_OBJETIVOS: {{LISTA_OBJETIVOS}} > Complete list of candidate objectives for the cycle, one per line
- HORIZONTE_CICLO: {{HORIZONTE_CICLO}} > Cycle duration (e.g. quarter, semester)
- CAPACIDAD_EQUIPO: {{CAPACIDAD_EQUIPO}} > Real capacity: people, available time and commitments already made that consume capacity
- PRIORIDAD_ESTRATEGICA: {{PRIORIDAD_ESTRATEGICA}} > The dominant strategic priority of the period against which everything is measured
- MAX_OBJETIVOS: {{MAX_OBJETIVOS}} > Maximum objectives to commit to (optional; default 3–5)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A team enters the cycle with an inflated list of objectives and ends up dispersing capacity across everything at once, without achieving anything in depth. The purpose of this exercise is to decide, with explicit and traceable criteria, the few objectives that truly matter for {{PRIORIDAD_ESTRATEGICA}} in {{HORIZONTE_CICLO}}. What is unlocked: real focus backed by capacity, a trimming conversation that does not depend on intuition or politics, and a decision defensible before the team and stakeholders. The bias to overcome is capacity optimism: almost always more is committed to than the team can execute.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior strategy and operations leader, specialist in OKR design and portfolio prioritization under capacity constraints.

Deliverable: the list of objectives reduced to a focused portfolio, classified into three groups with visible criteria. Steps:
1. Verify that you have LISTA_OBJETIVOS, HORIZONTE_CICLO, CAPACIDAD_EQUIPO and PRIORIDAD_ESTRATEGICA. If any is missing or vague, ask for it before evaluating; do not invent context. If MAX_OBJETIVOS is empty, assume 3–5 and declare it.
2. Evaluate each objective through three lenses on a scale of 1 to 5: Impact on PRIORIDAD_ESTRATEGICA, Focus (alignment versus dispersion) and Capacity (real executability given CAPACIDAD_EQUIPO). Calculate a combined score and record the assumption behind each score, marking [ASSUMPTION] when there is no hard data.
3. Detect dependencies and resource conflicts: flag whether one objective requires another to be completed first, or competes for the same people. An objective whose capacity depends on a discarded objective loses Capacity points.
4. Order in a table by combined score and draw the cut line respecting real capacity, not just the ranking; if the top items do not fit within CAPACIDAD_EQUIPO, lower the cut and explain it. Ties are broken by higher Impact, then higher Capacity.
5. Classify into COMMITTED (up to MAX_OBJETIVOS), ON HOLD (postponed, with the concrete and observable condition that would reactivate each one) and DISCARDED (abandoned, with the reason). Every objective that is cut carries a sentence explaining why.
6. Apply the final coherence test: if everything committed is achieved, is PRIORIDAD_ESTRATEGICA reached? Name the gap if there is one and say which ON HOLD objective would fill it.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: confirm context and capacity constraint before scoring; declare the assumed limit if MAX_OBJETIVOS is empty.
Phase 2 - Evaluation: apply the three lenses (Impact, Focus, Capacity) objective by objective with explicit assumptions.
Phase 3 - Relationships: map dependencies and resource conflicts among objectives before cutting.
Phase 4 - Cut: order, draw the line respecting capacity not just ranking; resolve ties with the declared rule.
Phase 5 - Classification: build the three groups with justification per objective and a reactivation condition for ON HOLD items.
Phase 6 - Coherence: validate that what is committed achieves the period's priority and flag the gap if it exists.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Every objective evaluated has an Impact, Focus and Capacity score (1–5) with a visible assumption and [ASSUMPTION] where there is no hard data.
- [ ] Dependencies and resource conflicts among objectives are marked; no COMMITTED objective depends on a DISCARDED one without noting it.
- [ ] The cut line respects CAPACIDAD_EQUIPO; if the ranking exceeds capacity, the cut is lowered and explained. Ties resolved by declared rule.
- [ ] COMMITTED items do not exceed MAX_OBJETIVOS (3–5 by default, declared if assumed).
- [ ] Each ON HOLD objective has a concrete and observable condition that would reactivate it; each DISCARDED objective has its reason.
- [ ] The coherence test answers whether what is committed achieves PRIORIDAD_ESTRATEGICA and flags the gap with its remedy if one exists.
- [ ] Zero objectives left unclassified.
Expected deliverable: prioritized portfolio in three groups (COMMITTED / ON HOLD / DISCARDED), scoring table with assumptions and relationships, cut line justified by capacity and coherence test verdict.
spec-liderazgo_contratacion_perfil_rol:
[inputs]
- ROL: {{ROL}} > Name and level of the position to open (e.g. Platform Engineering Lead)
- EQUIPO_Y_CONTEXTO: {{EQUIPO_Y_CONTEXTO}} > Team, size, stage and whom the role reports to
- HORIZONTE: {{HORIZONTE}} > Success windows to evaluate (e.g. 6 and 12 months); if only one window is given, derive an intermediate milestone
- VALORES_CULTURALES: {{VALORES_CULTURALES}} > Values or principles of the team that the role must embody
- METRICAS_CLAVE: {{METRICAS_CLAVE}} > Business indicators by which the role's success will be measured
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I am opening role {{ROL}} in {{EQUIPO_Y_CONTEXTO}} and I need the selection team to evaluate candidates against objective criteria, not against interview impressions. A clear Who-style scorecard unlocks defensible hiring decisions, reduces charisma and affinity bias, and aligns interviewers and the hiring manager on what success looks like before the first interview. Without a scorecard, every interviewer scores a different role and the decision becomes indefensible.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior talent leader with 12 years designing executive selection processes using the Who (A Method for Hiring) method by Geoff Smart and Randy Street.

Deliverable: a complete success scorecard for {{ROL}}. Steps:
1. Draft the role mission in a paragraph of 2 to 4 sentences: why the position exists and what business impact it produces, in outcome language, without jargon or a task list.
2. Define 4 to 6 prioritized and measurable expected outcomes, with a horizon according to {{HORIZONTE}}; each begins with a verb, anchors its metric in {{METRICAS_CLAVE}}, sets a baseline or target and declares the evidence of achievement. Mark the critical outcome that by itself would justify the hire.
3. List role competencies (5 to 8, specific to {{ROL}}) and cultural competencies (3 to 5, aligned to {{VALORES_CULTURALES}}); for each one, a one-line observable behavioral definition and the label must-have or nice-to-have.
4. For each critical competency, deliver a behavioral interview question plus the evidence that validates it and the signal that refutes it (red flag).
5. Close with a weighting table outcomes versus competencies (sums to 100 percent), a scoring note on a 1-to-5 scale per line and a declared minimum threshold to advance to the next filter.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Framing: confirm {{ROL}}, {{EQUIPO_Y_CONTEXTO}}, {{HORIZONTE}}, {{VALORES_CULTURALES}} and {{METRICAS_CLAVE}}; mark with [ASSUMPTION] any data you infer and ask for what is missing before generating the scorecard.
Phase 2 Mission and outcomes: derive the mission from the business purpose, not from tasks; translate each priority into a measurable outcome with a horizon and prioritize from most to least critical.
Phase 3 Competencies and calibration: separate role from culture, write observable behavioral definitions (what is seen, not abstract traits), label must-have or nice-to-have and pair each critical competency with a question and double evidence (validates and refutes).
Phase 4 Weighting and delivery: build the weights table summing to 100 percent, define the 1-to-5 rubric (1 far below, 3 meets, 5 exceeds) and the advancement threshold; verify that every outcome is measurable and that no competency is vague.
Edge cases: if {{METRICAS_CLAVE}} does not allow anchoring an outcome, propose a candidate metric marked [ASSUMPTION]; if the role is internal (promotion) adjust evidence to observed performance; if only one horizon is given, derive an intermediate milestone.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- Mission in outcome language, not tasks, in 2 to 4 sentences.
- Each outcome begins with a verb, is measurable, has a baseline or target and an explicit time horizon; the critical outcome is marked.
- Competencies separated into role versus culture, each with an observable behavioral definition and a must-have or nice-to-have label.
- Each critical competency has a behavioral interview question plus a validating piece of evidence and a refuting signal.
- Weighting table sums to 100 percent, 1-to-5 rubric per line and declared advancement threshold.
- Assumptions marked [ASSUMPTION]; no invented data or vague competencies.
Expected deliverable: one-page success scorecard, ready for the selection team to use in structured interviews.
spec-liderazgo_contratacion_jd_inclusiva:
[inputs]
- TITULO_PUESTO: {{TITULO_PUESTO}} > Name of the role to publish
- RESPONSABILIDADES_CLAVE: {{RESPONSABILIDADES_CLAVE}} > 3 to 6 actual day-to-day responsibilities
- SENIORITY: {{SENIORITY}} > Role level (junior, semi-senior, senior, lead) and real years that predict success
- MODALIDAD: {{MODALIDAD}} > In-person, hybrid or remote, location and time zone if applicable
- VALORES_EQUIPO: {{VALORES_EQUIPO}} > Team values, culture or ways of working (optional)
- BANDA_SALARIAL: {{BANDA_SALARIAL}} > Salary range or band to publish, or "Not defined" (optional)
- CANAL_AUDIENCIA: {{CANAL_AUDIENCIA}} > Publishing channel and target audience (job board, LinkedIn, referrals, communities) or "Not defined" (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A poorly worded vacancy narrows the pool before the first interview: it filters out qualified candidates through biased language, inflated requirements and signals that drive away diverse profiles. The goal is to publish a job description for {{TITULO_PUESTO}} that attracts the broadest and most qualified possible pool, without diluting the role's real standard. A good description unlocks better finalists, less bias in the funnel and a more defensible hiring decision. Scope: this prompt drafts and cleans up a description; it does not design the evaluation process or define final compensation, it only reflects {{BANDA_SALARIAL}} when it exists.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior recruiter and diversity and inclusion specialist, with experience writing evidence-based job descriptions and analyzing biased language.
Deliverable: a ready-to-publish job description plus a corrections note. Steps:
1. Separate requirements into must-haves (predict success in the role) and nice-to-haves (learnable on the job); cut inflated years of experience and non-essential degree requirements according to {{SENIORITY}}. Decision rule when in doubt: if a competent person can learn it in the first 90 days, it is a nice-to-have, not a must-have.
2. Rewrite in gender-neutral language; eliminate competitive superlatives (ninja, rockstar, warrior), internal jargon and coded demands that filter without justification (examples to watch: "digital native", "high-pressure environment", "recent graduate", "full availability", "cultural affinity valued").
3. Translate every requirement into an observable and verifiable capability so as not to lower the standard (example: instead of "expert mastery of X", write "can design and sustain Y using X").
4. Structure: purpose and impact of the role, day-to-day responsibilities (from {{RESPONSABILIDADES_CLAVE}}), must-haves, nice-to-haves, what the organization offers, {{BANDA_SALARIAL}} if available, and concrete inclusion signals (flexibility, reasonable accommodations, equitable evaluation). Adapt tone and length to {{CANAL_AUDIENCIA}} when it exists.
5. Close with an explicit invitation to apply even if not one hundred percent of the nice-to-haves are met.
Brand constraints: never invent salary amounts or publish them if they are not in {{BANDA_SALARIAL}}; never use the word "free"; neutral professional Spanish.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Diagnosis: read {{TITULO_PUESTO}}, {{RESPONSABILIDADES_CLAVE}}, {{SENIORITY}}, {{MODALIDAD}}, {{VALORES_EQUIPO}}, {{BANDA_SALARIAL}}, {{CANAL_AUDIENCIA}} and {{ADJUNTOS}}; flag critical gaps. Phase 2 Bias cleanup: detect gender-coded language, superlatives, jargon and inflated requirements. Phase 3 Drafting: produce the structured description with verifiable requirements. Phase 4 Closing: add the corrected-biases note. Missing data on must-haves (title, actual responsibilities, years that predict success) is asked for; never invented; reasonable assumptions are marked [ASSUMPTION]. Edge cases: if {{SENIORITY}} contradicts {{RESPONSABILIDADES_CLAVE}} (e.g. lead-level tasks required of a junior), flag it before drafting; if {{VALORES_EQUIPO}} contains exclusionary demands disguised as culture, reframe them as observable behaviors; if there is no {{BANDA_SALARIAL}}, omit the section without inventing a range.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Requirements divided into must-haves vs. nice-to-haves, applying the 90-day rule; no inflated years or non-essential degrees.
- [ ] Gender-neutral language; zero competitive superlatives, jargon or coded demands.
- [ ] Every requirement is an observable and verifiable capability (standard intact).
- [ ] Complete sections: purpose and impact, responsibilities, must-haves, nice-to-haves, what the organization offers, salary band if applicable, inclusion signals.
- [ ] Explicit invitation to apply without meeting one hundred percent of the nice-to-haves.
- [ ] Tone and length consistent with {{CANAL_AUDIENCIA}} when it exists.
- [ ] No invented amounts; no the word "free"; assumptions marked [ASSUMPTION]; critical gaps asked for, not invented.
Expected deliverable: ready-to-publish job description + a brief note that lists, in before > after format, every detected bias or inflated requirement and how it was corrected.
spec-liderazgo_contratacion_guia_entrevi:
[inputs]
- ROL: {{ROL}} > Position to fill and main job responsibilities
- SENIORITY: {{SENIORITY}} > Expected level (junior, semi-senior, senior, lead, managerial); calibrates the rubric bar
- COMPETENCIAS_CLAVE: {{COMPETENCIAS_CLAVE}} > Priority competencies to evaluate; if fewer than 4, infer from the role and context (optional)
- CONTEXTO_EQUIPO: {{CONTEXTO_EQUIPO}} > Team size, stage and dynamics where the person will join; adjusts relational and leadership competencies (optional)
- BANDERAS_ROJAS: {{BANDERAS_ROJAS}} > Eliminatory criteria or non-negotiables for the role, if any (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You are preparing a selection process for role {{ROL}} at level {{SENIORITY}} and you need all interviewers to evaluate the same things with the same yardstick. A competency-based structured interview guide with behavioral anchoring reduces interviewer bias, improves performance prediction compared to unstructured interviews and leaves auditable evidence to decide and defend the hire. It unlocks consistent panel decisions, calibration across evaluators and traceability of why someone was chosen, defensible before the candidate and the organization.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior organizational psychologist specializing in competency-based structured selection and behavioral rubric design (BARS), with the judgment to calibrate the bar to the role level.
Deliverable: a complete interview guide ready for a panel to use. Produce in this order:
1. Success profile (3–4 lines): what the person must achieve in the first 6–12 months to be a good hire; derive everything else from here.
2. Map of 4 to 6 critical competencies, each with a one-line operational definition (observable behavior) and a type label (technical / execution / relational / leadership). Use COMPETENCIAS_CLAVE if provided; fill in missing ones by inferring from ROL and CONTEXTO_EQUIPO. No overlap between competencies.
3. For each competency, one main STAR behavioral question asking for a real, past example ("tell me about a time when..."), never hypothetical, with a suggested time in parentheses.
4. For each question, 2 or 3 probing follow-up questions that isolate the candidate's individual Action ("what did you do, not the team") and the measurable Result ("how did you know it worked"); include at least one counter-evidence follow-up ("tell me about a time when that did not work").
5. BARS-anchored rubric from 1 to 5 per competency: describe levels 1, 3 and 5 with concrete observable response evidence, not adjectives; 2 and 4 are intermediate between neighboring anchors. Calibrate the bar to {{SENIORITY}} level (the same behavior scores differently at junior versus senior).
6. Evaluation sheet (table): competency, score 1–5, cited evidence (verbatim quote or paraphrase of what the person said) and flag (meets / does not meet / to calibrate), designed for independent scoring before the calibration meeting.
7. Panel calibration protocol: each evaluator scores alone and in writing before meeting; simultaneous reveal; focused discussion only where divergence exceeds 1 point; decision by cited evidence, not by affinity or hierarchy in the room.
8. Red flags / eliminatory criteria (use BANDERAS_ROJAS if provided) + brief actionable bias mitigation note: same set for all candidates, score by evidence and not by affinity, separate observation from interpretation, avoid halo effect, similarity bias and premature judgment, record evidence live and not from memory.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Interpret: derive the success profile from the role and select or infer competencies; mark with [ASSUMPTION] every inference that does not come from a piece of given data.
Phase 2 Design questions: per competency, draft the STAR question and its follow-ups, ensuring they target past behavior and individual contribution, and include the counter-evidence follow-up.
Phase 3 Anchor rubric: for each competency, write descriptors for levels 1, 3 and 5 with observable and differentiated evidence, adjusted to {{SENIORITY}}.
Phase 4 Assemble instruments: build the evaluation sheet, calibration protocol and bias mitigation note, maintaining neutral language and separating observation from interpretation.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Explicit success profile (6–12 months) from which competencies are derived.
- [ ] Between 4 and 6 competencies, each with an observable operational definition, type label and no overlap.
- [ ] Every main question is behavioral and past-focused (STAR), none hypothetical, with a suggested time.
- [ ] Each question has 2 or 3 follow-ups isolating individual Action and measurable Result, with at least one counter-evidence follow-up.
- [ ] The 1–5 rubric anchors levels 1, 3 and 5 with observable evidence, no vague adjectives, calibrated to seniority.
- [ ] The evaluation sheet allows independent scoring and evidence citation.
- [ ] Includes calibration protocol (prior independent scoring, simultaneous reveal, focus on divergences >1 point).
- [ ] Includes red flags if applicable and an actionable bias mitigation note; separates observation from interpretation.
- [ ] Inferences marked [ASSUMPTION]; missing ROL/SENIORITY/COMPETENCIAS_CLAVE requested before executing.
Expected deliverable: complete competency-based structured interview guide (success profile + competencies + STAR questions + follow-ups + BARS-anchored 1–5 rubric + evaluation sheet + calibration protocol + red flags + anti-bias note), ready for a panel to apply and calibrate.
spec-liderazgo_contratacion_entrevista_v:
[inputs]
- ROL: {{ROL}} > Position to fill, seniority level and key responsibilities
- VALORES_EQUIPO: {{VALORES_EQUIPO}} > Declared values or principles of the team/organization (short list)
- COMPOSICION_EQUIPO: {{COMPOSICION_EQUIPO}} > Profiles, perspectives and styles already present in the team (to detect what is missing to add)
- NUM_PREGUNTAS: {{NUM_PREGUNTAS}} > Number of main questions in the script (optional, default 6)
- SESGOS_A_VIGILAR: {{SESGOS_A_VIGILAR}} > Specific biases to control, e.g. affinity, halo, similarity, contrast, recency (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
We are about to interview candidates for {{ROL}} and we want to decide values fit without falling into homogeneous culture fit: the real risk is hiring copies of the current team, losing diversity of thought and disguising affinity bias as "cultural alignment". The goal is culture add: confirming that the person lives the team's non-negotiable values and, additionally, identifying what new perspective, experience or capability they add relative to {{COMPOSICION_EQUIPO}}. A good interview package unlocks defensible, candidate-comparable and visibly unbiased hiring decisions: same anchored questions for everyone, same rubric, same scoring protocol.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior Talent Acquisition Leader and structured interview designer, senior in values-based evaluation and bias reduction (BEI/STAR behavioral interviewing and behaviorally anchored rating scales, BARS).

Deliver a culture-add interview package with these components:
1. Values-to-behaviors matrix: for each value in {{VALORES_EQUIPO}}, define 2–3 observable behavioral indicators and classify each as NON-NEGOTIABLE or ADD-DESIRED. Each indicator describes an observable action, not a personality trait or stated attitude.
2. Structured BEI script: {{NUM_PREGUNTAS}} main past-behavior questions (STAR format: Situation, Task, Action, Result) with 1–2 probing follow-ups each; each question maps to an indicator in the matrix. Include per question a weak response signal (generic, hypothetical or without the candidate's own role) that prompts asking for a concrete example.
3. Culture-add questions: a minimum of two explicit questions exploring what the person contributes that is distinct relative to {{COMPOSICION_EQUIPO}} and how they have worked productively with people who think differently or have disagreed with them.
4. BARS-anchored rubric: per indicator, levels 1–4 with an observable descriptor for each level, shared across the entire panel. Define the minimum approval threshold for NON-NEGOTIABLE indicators and the non-compensation rule (a strong add does not compensate a non-negotiable below threshold).
5. Bias alarm signals: list of patterns to watch (affinity, halo, similarity, contrast, recency, and include {{SESGOS_A_VIGILAR}} if provided) with a concrete recentering action for each one (return to behavioral evidence, anchor to the rubric descriptor).
6. Panel calibration protocol: steps for each interviewer to score independently before discussing, rule for handling discrepancies greater than one level (review evidence, do not blindly average) and a hire / no hire / additional evidence needed criterion.
If {{ROL}}, {{VALORES_EQUIPO}} or {{COMPOSICION_EQUIPO}} are missing or ambiguous, ask for them before drafting the guide. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they contribute a job description or actual values.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Interpret: restate the role, the values and the team's perspective gap; explicitly confirm that add (adding a new perspective) is being sought, not fit (resembling the team).
Phase 2 - Decant values: separate non-negotiable values (ethical or safety-related, without which there is no hire) from replaceable cultural preferences; translate each one into observable behaviors and discard any formulation that measures opinion or personality.
Phase 3 - Design the script: draft past-behavior STAR questions anchored to indicators, plus the culture-add questions; verify that each one asks for a real example with the candidate's own role and result, not generic opinions or hypothetical scenarios.
Phase 4 - Build rubric and controls: anchor each level 1–4 to behaviors, set non-negotiable thresholds and non-compensation rule, list bias signals with recentering and define the calibration protocol with prior independent scoring.
Mark with [ASSUMPTION] any inferred criterion (e.g. what is non-negotiable when the values do not specify). Neutral professional Spanish, no emojis.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- Each value in {{VALORES_EQUIPO}} has 2–3 observable behavioral indicators and is classified non-negotiable vs. add-desired.
- Every main question is a past-behavior question (STAR) mapping to an indicator; none is hypothetical, leading or about personality, and each includes a weak response signal with a follow-up.
- There are at least two explicit culture-add questions focused on distinct contribution relative to {{COMPOSICION_EQUIPO}} and productive collaboration with difference.
- The rubric has levels 1–4 with observable descriptors, is shared across the entire panel, and defines non-negotiable thresholds + non-compensation rule.
- Bias alarm signals cover affinity, halo, similarity, contrast and recency (plus {{SESGOS_A_VIGILAR}} if applicable) and each has a recentering action.
- The calibration protocol requires prior independent scoring and has a rule for discrepancies greater than one level.
- Assumptions marked [ASSUMPTION]; no emojis; neutral professional Spanish.
Expected deliverable: culture-add interview package ready for the panel to use in a real hire, with values-to-behaviors matrix, BEI script, culture-add questions, BARS rubric with thresholds, bias signals and calibration protocol.
spec-liderazgo_contratacion_debrief_pane:
[inputs]
- VACANTE: {{VACANTE}} > Role, level and team of the position in debrief; indicate if it is a backfill or new headcount
- RUBRICA: {{RUBRICA}} > Competencies evaluated and agreed scoring scale for the panel; if not formal, derive 4–6 competencies from the role and mark them [ASSUMPTION]
- INSUMOS_ENTREVISTADORES: {{INSUMOS_ENTREVISTADORES}} > Independent evaluations from each interviewer (behavioral evidence and ratings), ideally without an overall verdict yet; indicate each interviewer's role relative to the candidate
- UMBRAL_DECISION: {{UMBRAL_DECISION}} > Agreed decision criterion: what constitutes advance, do not advance or require an additional round (optional; if missing, propose one and mark it [ASSUMPTION])
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
An interview panel must converge on a hiring decision for {{VACANTE}}. The risk is not a lack of opinions, but that they contaminate each other: the first strong verdict anchors the rest (anchoring) and the panel converges without supporting evidence (groupthink). Conducting the debrief with the correct sequence — evidence before voting — unlocks a defensible, traceable decision free from the loudest or most senior person in the room. A bad hire or a good candidate rejected due to bias are both costly and silent; this process makes the why of every decision visible.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior facilitator of structured hiring processes, with experience in panel design, competency rubrics and decision-making bias reduction.
Deliverable: a debrief record with an evidence matrix by competency, examination of divergences and a traceable hiring recommendation with an explicit confidence level.
Steps:
1. Verify that {{VACANTE}}, {{RUBRICA}} and {{INSUMOS_ENTREVISTADORES}} exist; if something is missing, ask for it before proceeding. If {{RUBRICA}} is not formal, propose 4–6 competencies from the role and mark them [ASSUMPTION].
2. Blind collection: extract from each interviewer, by competency, behavioral evidence with concrete examples and a rating, without yet reading their overall verdict.
3. Aggregate the evidence in a matrix by competency that marks convergence and divergence, and assign a signal (strong, mixed, weak) per competency, with coverage (how many interviewers observed it).
4. Examine each divergence: open question, responsible person assigned to clarify it and detected bias (anchoring, halo, affinity, recency, groupthink).
5. Only then request and record the overall verdicts, contrast them with the signal by competency and issue the recommendation according to {{UMBRAL_DECISION}}.
6. Close with conditions or risks to watch in onboarding (and a 30/60/90 plan if applicable) when the decision is to advance; declare the confidence level and what piece of data would change it.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Blind collection: separate evidence from verdict; reject inputs that are general impressions without behavioral observation and request them again. Distinguish "not observed" from "observed weak": a lack of evidence is not a negative signal.
Phase 2 Aggregation: consolidate by competency, not by person; the signal comes from the cited evidence, not from who stated it or their hierarchy. If a critical role competency was not covered, mark it as a process gap.
Phase 3 Divergences: make every real disagreement explicit, name the bias that might be operating and separate divergence due to different evidence (resolvable with data) from divergence due to interpretation (resolvable with panel calibration).
Phase 4 Decision: introduce the overall verdicts only at the end, contrast them with the signal by competency and resolve according to the threshold. If the signal contradicts the verdicts, prioritize the evidence and document the tension.
Edge case: a single strong verdict without behavioral evidence is NOT enough to advance; a single "no" without evidence is also NOT enough to reject.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
- Individual evidence was recorded before any overall verdict.
- Each signal by competency is sustained by cited behavioral evidence, not by the interviewer's hierarchy, and indicates its coverage.
- Every divergence has an open question, an assigned responsible person and a named bias, distinguishing divergence due to evidence from divergence due to interpretation.
- At least one anchoring control and one groupthink control were explicitly named, or their absence was justified.
- The final recommendation is traceable to the matrix, respects {{UMBRAL_DECISION}} and declares a confidence level and the piece of data that would change it.
- Coverage gaps on critical competencies are marked as a process risk.
- Evaluation focused on performance relative to the role, without demographic biases.
- Unconfirmed assumptions marked as [ASSUMPTION].
Expected deliverable: debrief record in neutral Spanish with an evidence matrix by competency (signal + coverage), examination of divergences, justified recommendation (advance / do not advance / additional round with its objective and scope), confidence level and, if advancing, onboarding conditions to watch.
spec-liderazgo_contratacion_referencias:
[inputs]
- ROL_Y_SENIORITY: {{ROL_Y_SENIORITY}} > Title and level of the finalist candidate (e.g. team lead, manager, director).
- COMPETENCIAS_CRITICAS: {{COMPETENCIAS_CRITICAS}} > 3–5 competencies or results this hire must secure.
- RELACION_REFERENTE: {{RELACION_REFERENTE}} > Reference's relationship with the candidate: role, period and interaction frequency.
- RIESGOS_A_DESCARTAR: {{RIESGOS_A_DESCARTAR}} > Doubts or risk signals you want to confirm or rule out (optional).
- DURACION_LLAMADA: {{DURACION_LLAMADA}} > Time available for the call, to calibrate the number of questions (optional).
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You are about to make a hiring decision on a finalist candidate and you are going to call one of their references. The risk is not a lack of information, but compliant information: most references respond positively out of courtesy or to avoid conflict, and a poorly designed script only confirms prior biases (halo effect, social desirability). A good script converts a courtesy call into a real source of signals about performance, working style, handling of pressure and risks, and unlocks a decision based on evidence rather than impression.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior talent acquisition specialist, expert in behavioral interviewing (STAR method) and reference checks for roles {{ROL_Y_SENIORITY}}.
Deliverable: a ready-to-use reference call script. Build it in these steps:
1. Draft a 2–3 sentence opening that builds trust, frames the call as confidential and clarifies the reference's exact relationship with the candidate (role, period, interaction frequency) using {{RELACION_REFERENTE}} as a basis.
2. Design 12 revealing questions in four blocks: (a) performance and results, (b) working style and collaboration, (c) handling of conflict and pressure, (d) development areas. Calibrate each block's weight according to {{COMPETENCIAS_CRITICAS}} and {{RIESGOS_A_DESCARTAR}}.
3. Ensure every question is open-ended, asks for concrete behavior (situation, action, result) and is hard to answer with a generic compliment; include at least 3 contrast or triangulation questions (asking for a specific example, asking how their peers would react, or inviting comparison to others who held the same role).
4. Annotate each question, in parentheses, with the signal you are looking for and the response that would be a red flag.
5. Close with the re-hire question ('would you hire them again, and exactly what type of role') and an open-ended closing question ('is there anything I did not ask you that I should know').
6. Add a signal-reading mini-rubric: how to distinguish a strong endorsement from a lukewarm one and what evasion patterns to watch (sustained vagueness, topic change, long silences, personality-only compliments with no results).
Ethical limit (non-negotiable): ask only about verifiable work behavior; do not elicit or record protected or discriminatory data (health, private life, beliefs, family situation). If an input is missing or ambiguous, ask for it before drafting instead of assuming it.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: set the relative weight of the four blocks based on the critical competencies and risks to rule out; if {{DURACION_LLAMADA}} is short, concentrate questions on the highest-weight blocks and reduce lower-priority ones without eliminating any block.
Phase 2 - Design: draft the opening, the 12 questions with their signal and red flag, and the closing, ensuring the language is open-ended and behavioral.
Phase 3 - Verification: confirm there are at least 3 triangulation questions, that no question admits a comfortable yes/no, that none touches protected data and that the rubric allows classifying a response as strong, lukewarm or evasive.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Confidential opening that validates the real reference-candidate relationship.
- [ ] 12 open-ended, behavioral questions, no comfortable yes/no option.
- [ ] All four blocks present and weighted according to competencies and risks.
- [ ] Minimum 3 contrast or triangulation questions.
- [ ] Each question with its sought signal and red flag in parentheses.
- [ ] Re-hire question with a role nuance and an open-ended closing question.
- [ ] Mini-rubric distinguishing a strong, lukewarm and evasion-pattern endorsement.
- [ ] No question elicits protected or discriminatory data.
Expected deliverable: reference script in structured text organized by blocks, ready to conduct the call and record responses.
spec-liderazgo_contratacion_oferta_cierr:
[inputs]
- NOMBRE_CANDIDATO: {{NOMBRE_CANDIDATO}} > Name of the candidate being made the offer
- ROL: {{ROL}} > Role title, level and team or area the person is joining
- MOTIVACIONES_CANDIDATO: {{MOTIVACIONES_CANDIDATO}} > What the candidate declared valuing during the process (purpose, growth, autonomy, impact, team, stability, flexibility)
- PROPUESTA_VALOR_ROL: {{PROPUESTA_VALOR_ROL}} > What the role offers beyond compensation: mandate, projects, mentorship, growth path, culture, scope
- TERMINOS_OFERTA: {{TERMINOS_OFERTA}} > Components of the offer to communicate: level, modality, benefits, start date, role scope (without amounts if not applicable)
- FECHA_DECISION: {{FECHA_DECISION}} > Target deadline for the candidate to respond
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A well-evaluated candidate is one step away from accepting or declining, and the offer call is the highest-leverage moment of the entire hire: it defines whether they join committed or merely by default. Preparing this script unlocks a conversation that connects what the candidate said matters to them with what the role truly offers, reduces the probability of a late rejection or a surprise counter-offer, and leaves a closing with an explicit commitment and written next steps. Base assumption: the decision to extend the offer has already been made and approved; this script communicates and closes, it does not reopen the evaluation.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior talent leader with proven experience closing candidates in competitive roles, who negotiates from honesty and never applies artificial pressure.

Deliverable: an offer call script for {{NOMBRE_CANDIDATO}} for role {{ROL}}, with first-person model phrases ready to say aloud (not descriptions), organized in five blocks:
1. Warm opening: reaffirm why we chose them and name a specific strength observed in the process.
2. Value proposition: tie each element of {{PROPUESTA_VALOR_ROL}} to a motivation from {{MOTIVACIONES_CANDIDATO}}, without centering the conversation on compensation.
3. Offer terms: present {{TERMINOS_OFERTA}} in order, with framing explaining the why of each component.
4. Probable objections: at least four (current counter-offer, growth doubts, change risk, team or modality issues) with a suggested response and a re-engagement question that returns focus to their motivations.
5. Close: ask for a commitment signal, agree on next steps and fix {{FECHA_DECISION}} in writing.

Also include: a motivation-value map (table candidate said -> role offers -> evidence) and a line for handling silences or a request for thinking time.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Interpret: confirm role, motivations, value proposition, terms and date. If any input is empty or ambiguous, ask before drafting; do not invent motivations or terms. What is not provided is marked [ASSUMPTION] or left as a question.
Phase 2 - Map: cross each declared motivation with the value proposition element or term that satisfies it; flag gaps where a motivation has no backing and mark them as a priority objection risk.
Phase 3 - Draft: produce the script in five blocks with first-person model phrases; in objections use the pattern listen, validate, respond with evidence, re-engage with a question.
Phase 4 - Verify: review against the Criteria checklist, adjust tone and promises, and confirm that no communicated term exceeds what has been approved.
Edge cases: (a) counter-offer or bidding war -> do not compete on figures, re-anchor on non-financial motivations and on what the counter-offer does not resolve; (b) candidate asks for more time -> offer a reasonable extension of {{FECHA_DECISION}} without penalizing; (c) candidate declines -> close with dignity, give thanks and leave the door open without insisting.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Each element of the value proposition is tied to a specific declared motivation, not generically.
- [ ] The opening cites a specific strength from the process, not a vague compliment.
- [ ] Each offer term carries framing of the why, not just the data point.
- [ ] There are at least four probable objections, each with a response and a re-engagement question.
- [ ] The motivation-value map exposes gaps without backing as an objection risk.
- [ ] The close asks for an explicit commitment signal and leaves the decision date and next steps in writing.
- [ ] The script delivers model phrases speakable aloud, not descriptions.
- [ ] No phrase uses artificial pressure, false urgency or unsustainable promises, nor communicates terms above what has been approved.
- [ ] What the user did not provide was left as a question or marked [ASSUMPTION], never invented.
Expected deliverable: five-block offer call script with model phrases, motivation-value map with gaps flagged, battery of at least four objections with re-engagements, handling of edge cases (counter-offer, request for time, decline) and close with commitment and written date.
spec-liderazgo_contratacion_plan_30_60_9:
[inputs]
- ROL_NIVEL: {{ROL_NIVEL}} > Role and level of the person joining (e.g. analyst, tech lead, area manager)
- RESPONSABILIDADES: {{RESPONSABILIDADES}} > Core responsibilities and expected outcomes of the position
- CONTEXTO_EQUIPO: {{CONTEXTO_EQUIPO}} > Size, maturity, and moment of the area receiving the person
- TIPO_TRANSICION: {{TIPO_TRANSICION}} > Nature of the transition: stable area, in-change, or start-up from scratch
- CRITERIO_EXITO: {{CRITERIO_EXITO}} > How success will be measured at the close of day 90
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A new person is joining the team and the first 90 days determine whether they reach their break-even point (when they contribute more value than they consume) or stagnate. A horizon-structured plan accelerates that point, reduces early turnover, and aligns expectations among the person, their leader, and the stakeholders. This prompt produces that actionable plan — not a generic welcome checklist.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: senior people manager and talent-onboarding specialist, trained in Michael Watkins' transitions framework (The First 90 Days, HBR Press).
Deliverable: a 90-day onboarding plan in three horizons (1-30 learn / 31-60 contribute / 61-90 lead with autonomy). For each horizon define in this order:
1. Horizon objective in one sentence.
2. Learning milestones: product, processes, tools, and customer, each with an observable completion criterion.
3. Contribution milestones: verifiable deliverables and realistic early wins for the role's level.
4. Key relationships: stakeholder archetypes (leader, peers, dependent teams, internal or external customer) and the purpose of each link.
5. Coaching rhythm: cadence of 1:1s, checkpoints, and who supports.
6. Early-warning signals that the transition is drifting, each with the suggested corrective action.
Calibration rules (apply, do not merely state):
- Transition type: start-up from scratch requires more diagnosis and context-building in horizon 1; in-change area requires stabilizing before proposing; stable area allows earlier wins.
- Role level: junior roles prioritize mastery and bounded deliverables; leadership roles prioritize reading the system, building trust, and team decisions.
Close with: (a) summary table of the three horizons; (b) list of conditions the leader must guarantee (access, assigned mentor or buddy, clarity of expectations, first deliverable defined); (c) explicit connection between horizon 90 and CRITERIO_EXITO.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: confirm ROL_NIVEL, RESPONSABILIDADES, CONTEXTO_EQUIPO, TIPO_TRANSICION, and CRITERIO_EXITO. If anything is missing, ask before proceeding; do not infer it.
Phase 2 - Diagnosis: adjust the depth of each horizon to the transition type and role level according to the calibration rules.
Phase 3 - Design: draft the six blocks per horizon, ensuring each milestone is observable and measurable, not a vague statement.
Phase 4 - Verification: check that early wins are realistic, that relationships cover all stakeholders in the context, that each warning signal has a corrective action, that horizon 90 connects with the success criterion, and that no data has been invented; flag every inference with [ASSUMPTION].
Edge cases: if the role has no direct reports, reinterpret "lead with autonomy" as end-to-end ownership of their area of responsibility; if the transition is remote or hybrid, adjust the coaching rhythm (more async checkpoints); if CRITERIO_EXITO is vague or unmeasurable, propose a reformulated version and flag it [ASSUMPTION].
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- The three horizons (30/60/90) are present and each one has the six blocks complete.
- Each learning and contribution milestone has an observable completion criterion (verifiable, not aspirational).
- Early wins are realistic for the role level and transition type (calibration applied, not merely named).
- Key relationships name stakeholder archetypes and the purpose of each link.
- Each early-warning signal has an associated corrective action.
- Horizon 90 connects explicitly with CRITERIO_EXITO.
- Every inference not backed by a provided data point is flagged with [ASSUMPTION].
- No invented names, metrics, or dates.
Expected deliverable: document with three sections per horizon, a final 90-day summary table, and a list of enabling conditions the leader must guarantee.
spec-liderazgo_contratacion_preboarding:
[inputs]
- ROL: {{ROL}} > Position or role of the person joining (title, level, and reporting line)
- MODALIDAD_TRABAJO: {{MODALIDAD_TRABAJO}} > On-site, remote, or hybrid; city or time zone if applicable
- TIEMPO_HASTA_INGRESO: {{TIEMPO_HASTA_INGRESO}} > Days or weeks between offer signing and the first day
- CULTURA_EQUIPO: {{CULTURA_EQUIPO}} > Rituals, tone, and values of the team receiving the person (optional)
- PRIORIDADES_NEGOCIO: {{PRIORIDADES_NEGOCIO}} > What the person is expected to unblock or address in their first weeks (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
The window between offer signing and the first day is the most fragile moment of the entire onboarding: the person has already said yes, but does not yet belong, is still exposed to counter-offers and pre-start regret, and every day of silence erodes the enthusiasm with which they accepted. A deliberate preboarding converts that wait into a bridge: it confirms the decision to join, reduces first-day anxiety, and shortens time to first contribution. Designing this sequence for {{ROL}} in {{MODALIDAD_TRABAJO}} mode unlocks an arrival where the person already knows faces, has access credentials, and knows what is expected of them — rather than a reactive, administrative day one. Risk to avoid: overwhelming the incoming person with tasks or documents during personal time before the contract starts; preboarding accompanies, it does not front-load unpaid work.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior people leader specialized in onboarding experience, with experience coordinating preboarding across leadership, human resources, technical teams, and systems.
Deliverable: an actionable preboarding sequence for the {{TIEMPO_HASTA_INGRESO}} period, adjusted to {{CULTURA_EQUIPO}} and {{PRIORIDADES_NEGOCIO}}, ready to execute. Steps:
1. Define 4 to 6 preboarding objectives (reduce anxiety, confirm the decision, accelerate time to first contribution, prevent pre-start regret) with one observable success signal each.
2. Build a milestone timeline across {{TIEMPO_HASTA_INGRESO}}; for each milestone indicate action, responsible party (leader, human resources, team, or systems), and channel. Distribute the rhythm: early contact after signing, a light intermediate cadence, increasing intensity in the final week.
3. Detail the four parallel workstreams with concrete actions for each: administrative and legal (contract, data, compliance); logistics and access (equipment, accounts, credentials, adjusted to the modality); social and cultural (team introduction, first-days mentor or companion, rituals); role and expectations (objectives for the first weeks, reporting line, first-30-day plan).
4. Draft the 3 key messages from the hiring leader: welcome after signing, team introduction, and day-one agenda.
5. List 3 to 4 warning signals (prolonged silence, unresolved doubts, probable counter-offer, delay in signing or returning documents) with a response action for each.
6. Deliver a day-before-day-one checklist confirming the person is ready across all four workstreams.
Adjust every recommendation to {{MODALIDAD_TRABAJO}}: in remote or hybrid settings, equipment shipping, credentials, and social connection carry more weight and need more lead time.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Interpret: restate role, modality, available time, culture, and priorities; flag any missing data with [ASSUMPTION] and ask for critical items in a single round before proceeding.
Phase 2 - Plan: define the objectives and sketch the timeline and four workstreams as a skeleton, without drafting the messages yet.
Phase 3 - Execute: develop the full sequence, draft the messages, add the warning signals, and close with the checklist.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- Each objective has an observable success signal, not a vague intention.
- Each timeline milestone has an explicit action, responsible party, and channel.
- All four workstreams (administrative and legal, logistics and access, social and cultural, role and expectations) are covered without gaps.
- Recommendations are adjusted to {{MODALIDAD_TRABAJO}}: remote and hybrid settings anticipate equipment, access, and social connection.
- The 3 hiring leader messages are drafted and ready to send, in neutral professional English, without emojis.
- Warning signals carry a concrete response action, not just the symptom.
- The timeline realistically fits within {{TIEMPO_HASTA_INGRESO}} and does not front-load unpaid work during personal time before the contract.
- Assumptions are flagged as [ASSUMPTION].
Expected deliverable: document with objectives and their signals, milestone timeline by responsible party and channel, the four workstreams in detail, the three drafted messages, the warning signals with their responses, and the day-before-day-one checklist.
spec-liderazgo_contratacion_buddy_system:
[inputs]
- NOMBRE_O_ROL_NUEVO_INGRESO: {{NOMBRE_O_ROL_NUEVO_INGRESO}} > Role or position of the newly hired person (e.g. semi-senior backend developer, commercial analyst)
- MODALIDAD: {{MODALIDAD}} > Work modality: on-site, remote, or hybrid (include time zones or overlap window if any)
- TAMANO_EQUIPO: {{TAMANO_EQUIPO}} > Number of people on the team receiving the new hire
- ONBOARDING_ACTUAL: {{ONBOARDING_ACTUAL}} > What currently exists in terms of onboarding, or "no formal process" (optional)
- OBJETIVO_PRIORITARIO: {{OBJETIVO_PRIORITARIO}} > Most important outcome to accelerate: social integration, early productivity, or retention (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A new hire decides in their first weeks whether they stay and whether they perform; the difference between a haphazard onboarding and a designed one is measured in speed of contribution, early retention, and load on the manager. Designing a buddy or mentor system converts integration into a repeatable process: the peer buddy covers social belonging and day-to-day questions without judgment, the mentor covers technical judgment and business context, and the manager is freed to lead instead of putting out fires. This unlocks consistent onboarding for every new {{NOMBRE_O_ROL_NUEVO_INGRESO}} hire in a {{MODALIDAD}} operation, without depending on the memory or availability of a single person.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior team leader and onboarding program designer, with proven experience building buddy and onboarding mentor systems in {{MODALIDAD}} teams.
Design, end-to-end, the buddy or mentor system for the first 90 days, considering a team of {{TAMANO_EQUIPO}} people, the current onboarding ({{ONBOARDING_ACTUAL}}), and the priority objective ({{OBJETIVO_PRIORITARIO}}). Produce, in this order:
1. Role definition: purpose, what each one DOES, what is NOT their responsibility, and the ideal candidate profile, separating peer buddy (social, cultural, day-to-day questions without judgment) from mentor (technical, business, development). Explicitly mark the typical gray zone (routine technical questions) and assign it to one of them.
2. Matching and sustainability: criteria for assigning buddy or mentor (affinity, seniority, proximity to the role — NOT the direct reporting line), how to recruit and recognize the role without financial incentives, a cap on simultaneous new hires per person, and how to protect their regular workload by freeing time, not adding to it.
3. Phase-by-phase cadence: meetings for day 1, week 1, days 2-30, days 31-60, and days 61-90, with frequency, duration, format (synchronous or asynchronous, according to {{MODALIDAD}}), and responsible party (peer or mentor). Define how frequency decays as autonomy rises.
4. Guiding topics and questions per meeting in two tracks: social-cultural and operational-technical.
5. A concrete script for the first buddy–new hire conversation (opening, topics, close), ready to use as-is.
6. Observable early-warning signals of poor integration (observable behaviors, not interpretations) and an escalation protocol to the manager with a clear trigger and channel.
7. Success indicators for the manager (e.g. time to first autonomous contribution, perceived onboarding quality, 90-day retention) with a responsible party per indicator and explicit handoffs between buddy, mentor, and manager (what is transferred, when, and how).
Close with: design limitations and 3 edge cases with their adaptation (team too small for a buddy candidate; remote modality with no time-zone overlap; several simultaneous new hires competing for the same buddies).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: confirm role, modality, team size, and objective; flag any missing data with [ASSUMPTION] (including a default priority objective if empty) rather than inventing it.
Phase 2 - Role design and matching: define buddy and mentor without overlap, resolve the gray zone, and fix match and sustainability criteria.
Phase 3 - Cadence and content: build the 90-day timeline with topics, guiding questions, and opening script.
Phase 4 - Safeguards and measurement: observable alerts, escalation, indicators with responsible party, handoffs, and edge cases.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
- Buddy and mentor are clearly differentiated, with no duplicated functions; the gray zone is resolved with an explicit rule.
- Matching avoids the direct reporting line and sets a cap on simultaneous new hires per person; role recognition does NOT use financial incentives.
- The cadence covers the five phases (day 1, week 1, 2-30, 31-60, 61-90) with specific frequency, duration, format, and responsible party, consistent with the modality.
- Each meeting has guiding topics and questions in both tracks (social-cultural and operational-technical).
- The first-conversation script is ready to use as-is, with no prior adaptation needed.
- Warning signals are observable (behaviors, not judgments) and escalation to the manager has a clear trigger and channel.
- Indicators are measurable, each with a responsible party; buddy–mentor–manager handoffs state what, when, and how something is transferred.
- Limitations and 3 edge cases with adaptation are included; assumptions are flagged [ASSUMPTION].
- Neutral professional English; without overloading buddy or mentor; no prices.
Expected deliverable: document structured in seven sections plus a closing limitations-and-edge-cases section, ready to implement from day 1 with the team's next hire.
spec-liderazgo_contratacion_check_in_90_:
[inputs]
- PERSONA_Y_ROL: {{PERSONA_Y_ROL}} > Person being evaluated, role, level, and start date
- EXPECTATIVAS_INICIALES: {{EXPECTATIVAS_INICIALES}} > Responsibilities, goals, expected behaviors, and onboarding milestones agreed at the start of the probationary period
- EVIDENCIA_OBSERVADA: {{EVIDENCIA_OBSERVADA}} > Behaviors and results observed during the 90 days, with concrete examples, dates, and sources where available
- FEEDBACK_PREVIO: {{FEEDBACK_PREVIO}} > Feedback already delivered during the period and the person's response or adjustment (optional)
- INCLINACION_Y_SENALES: {{INCLINACION_Y_SENALES}} > Preliminary decision inclination and risk or strength signals (optional)
- MARCO_POLITICAS: {{MARCO_POLITICAS}} > Legal, collective-bargaining, or organizational policy framework for the probationary period: timelines, formalities, and restrictions (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You are closing the 90-day probationary period for a team member. The goal is to transform scattered impressions into an evidence-based evaluation and to reach an unambiguous continuity decision: confirm, extend, or not continue. A well-conducted conversation protects the person (clarity and fair treatment), the team (a consistent standard applied equally), and the organization (a defensible and traceable decision). This unlocks honest communication, an actionable action plan, and, if applicable, a dignified transition. Risks to contain: recency or halo bias, anecdotal evidence replacing pattern, mixing underperformance with organizational-fit problems, and deciding or communicating without the prior validation the applicable framework may require.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: senior people leader with experience in probationary-period evaluation, evidence-based feedback (SBI model: Situation-Behavior-Impact), and difficult performance conversations.
Deliverable: 90-day check-in dossier + conversation script. Steps:
1. Reconstruct the agreed baseline of expectations at the start (responsibilities, goals, behaviors, onboarding milestones); flag as [ASSUMPTION] anything not documented in writing.
2. Build an expectation vs. observed evidence table with a rating (exceeds / meets / in progress / below), separating verifiable facts from interpretations; label expectations without sufficient evidence as "no data" rather than forcing a rating.
3. Draft 2-3 reinforcement messages and 2-3 adjustment messages in SBI format, actionable and free of personality judgments; each adjustment message includes the specific behavior expected going forward.
4. Recommend a single continuity decision (confirm / extend / not continue) with explicit reasoning and criteria; flag where HR or legal validation is required and distinguish a performance gap from a role or team fit problem.
5. Define the scenario plan (development focus; improvement plan with goals, review dates, and consequences; or respectful communication and transition points) and a conversation script.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 · Baseline: role, level, start date, and agreed expectations; distinguish documented from inferred [ASSUMPTION].
Phase 2 · Evidence by competency: expected vs. observed contrast with dated examples; rating per expectation; pattern over anecdote; facts separated from interpretations; explicitly declare evidence gaps.
Phase 3 · SBI feedback: concrete Situation, observable Behavior, measurable Impact; balance reinforcement and adjustment; no personality labels.
Phase 4 · Decision: single recommendation with reasoning, supporting criteria, conditions and timeline if extended, and prior-validation flags (HR / legal) before any communication; name the main risk and its mitigation.
Phase 5 · Plan and script: scenario plan with measurable goals and dates + script (opening, body, handling of likely reactions — defense, surprise, negotiation —, next steps and commitments with responsible party and date).
Label every inference [ASSUMPTION]; do not present interpretations as facts; do not make judgments about the person; neutral professional tone, no emojis.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
- Each expectation in the table has observable evidence and a rating, or is labeled "no data"; no interpretation is presented as fact.
- SBI messages describe behaviors, not personality traits, and propose a specific action or expected behavior going forward.
- The continuity decision is a single one (confirm / extend / not continue), with reasoning and verifiable criteria, and distinguishes a performance gap from a fit problem.
- Actions requiring HR or legal validation are flagged before any communication.
- The scenario plan has measurable goals, review dates, and clear consequences where applicable; script commitments have a responsible party and date.
- Every inference is tagged [ASSUMPTION]; neutral professional tone, no value judgments.
Expected deliverable: check-in dossier (baseline, expectation vs. evidence table, SBI reinforcement and adjustment block, single recommendation with validation flags, scenario action plan) + conversation script ready to conduct.
spec-liderazgo_contratacion_marca_emplea:
[inputs]
- ROL_CANDIDATO_IDEAL: {{ROL_CANDIDATO_IDEAL}} > Role being filled and traits of the person who fits, including expected behavioral signal (e.g. "senior data engineer, autonomous, comfortable with ambiguity, decides with little supervision and documents their decisions")
- MISION_EQUIPO: {{MISION_EQUIPO}} > The team's real mission or the problem it solves, tied to a tangible outcome and, if it exists, a metric (e.g. "enabling SMEs to access credit in 24h instead of weeks; today we process 800 applications/month")
- RETOS_HONESTOS: {{RETOS_HONESTOS}} > The genuine hard parts of the work, unvarnished (e.g. "inherited technical debt, shifting priorities, still-small team that does everything, rotating on-call")
- OPORTUNIDADES_CRECIMIENTO: {{OPORTUNIDADES_CRECIMIENTO}} > What they will learn or who they will become, with concrete examples and, if applicable, a time horizon (e.g. "lead the pipeline redesign in 6 months, direct mentoring from the CTO, exposure to product decisions")
- REALIDAD_CULTURA: {{REALIDAD_CULTURA}} > What it is really like to work here: pace, autonomy, decision-making, values in action (e.g. "remote, async, written decisions, no meetings on Fridays, direct feedback")
- CANAL_PUBLICACION: {{CANAL_PUBLICACION}} > Where and in what format it is published, with tone/length constraints (e.g. "LinkedIn post ~150 words", "job post section", "direct message to passive candidate")
- RESTRICCIONES: {{RESTRICCIONES}} > Hard lines, prohibited claims, benefits that CANNOT be confirmed, or "No additional restrictions"
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need to articulate why it is worth joining my team with an honest narrative of mission, challenge, and growth. The risk is twofold: an inflated message attracts those who are not a fit, raises early turnover, and burns the team's reputation; a generic message says nothing and lets the talent that would genuinely fit walk past. A well-built employee value proposition (EVP) does the opposite: it tells the attractive truth, attracts those who thrive under this challenge, gently deters those who are not a fit, and turns the message into a fit filter rather than bait. This unlocks better-qualified applications, more honest hiring conversations, and an onboarding free of the disappointment of "this was not what they sold me". The default bias to correct is optimism: we tend to highlight the good and hide the hard parts — exactly what produces early turnover.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior talent leader and employer branding specialist, expert in employee value propositions (EVP), honest recruitment narratives, and attraction messages that filter by genuine fit rather than inflating expectations.

Produce an attraction message and its supporting framework with these components:
1. Fit profile: who the message attracts (who thrives here) and who it deters (who is not a fit), derived from ROL_CANDIDATO_IDEAL and REALIDAD_CULTURA; the "deters" must be concrete, not a generic rejection.
2. The three pillars with evidence: Mission (why the work matters, tied to MISION_EQUIPO), Challenge (the genuine hard problems from RETOS_HONESTOS, unvarnished) and Growth (what they will learn or who they will become, from OPORTUNIDADES_CRECIMIENTO with concrete examples); each pillar with its evidence or a visible [ASSUMPTION].
3. Final attraction message adapted to CANAL_PUBLICACION: honest hook, development of the three pillars, and a clear low-friction next step; honor RESTRICCIONES.
4. Short version of 2 to 3 sentences for reuse in direct messages or headings, without losing the honesty of the Challenge.
5. Honesty test: for each promise in the message, what evidence supports it and what would have to be true for the candidate not to feel deceived upon joining; flag every promise without supporting evidence as [ASSUMPTION] to confirm.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Define fit: from ROL_CANDIDATO_IDEAL and REALIDAD_CULTURA, describe who thrives on this team and who does not, so the message attracts the former and deters the latter. Connect each fit trait to a concrete element of the culture.
Phase 2 - Build pillars: draft Mission (tied to MISION_EQUIPO), Challenge (from RETOS_HONESTOS, not softening the hard parts) and Growth (from OPORTUNIDADES_CRECIMIENTO, with concrete examples); justify each promise with evidence or flag it [ASSUMPTION]; never present an unsupported promise as fact. Recommended balance: Challenge carries at least as much weight as Mission; a message without honest tension is bait.
Phase 3 - Draft message: adapt tone and length to CANAL_PUBLICACION, open with an honest hook (not clickbait), develop the three pillars, and close with a clear low-friction next step; also produce the short version of 2 to 3 sentences. Honor RESTRICCIONES.
Phase 4 - Test for honesty: list each promise in the message with its evidence and the condition that would have to hold for it not to be misleading; flag promises that depend on an [ASSUMPTION] not yet confirmed. Never promise prices, never use the word free, never offer what the team cannot deliver.
Edge cases: if RETOS_HONESTOS arrives empty or cosmetic, ask for at least one real challenge before proceeding (a message without challenge does not filter). If MISION_EQUIPO is not tied to a tangible outcome, flag it [ASSUMPTION] and propose how to make it concrete. If CANAL_PUBLICACION is an open public channel, moderate the exposure of sensitive challenges without erasing them.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
The message is complete when:
- The fit profile explicitly states who it attracts and who it deters (both concrete), coherent with the real role and culture.
- The three pillars (Mission, Challenge, Growth) are present; the Challenge pillar names at least one genuinely hard part unvarnished and is not subordinated to Mission.
- Each promise has evidence or a visible [ASSUMPTION]; no inference is presented as fact.
- The final message is adapted in tone and length to CANAL_PUBLICACION, with an honest hook, three pillars, and a clear low-friction next step, plus the short version of 2 to 3 sentences that preserves the honesty of the Challenge.
- The honesty test covers all promises in the message with their truth condition and flags those depending on [ASSUMPTION].
- RESTRICCIONES are honored; no prices and no word free; text in neutral professional English, no emojis, no invented data.
Expected deliverable: document with fit profile (attracts / deters), the three pillars with evidence or [ASSUMPTION], the final attraction message ready for the channel, the short 2-to-3-sentence version, and the promise-by-promise honesty test.
spec-liderazgo_delegacion_niveles_autori:
[inputs]
- TAREA_O_AREA: {{TAREA_O_AREA}} > Task, project, or area of responsibility to delegate
- PERSONA_O_EQUIPO: {{PERSONA_O_EQUIPO}} > Who receives the delegation (role or name)
- NIVEL_MADUREZ: {{NIVEL_MADUREZ}} > Person's experience and maturity on this topic (high/medium/low with detail)
- APETITO_RIESGO: {{APETITO_RIESGO}} > Cost of an error and risk tolerance in this area
- CADENCIA_SEGUIMIENTO: {{CADENCIA_SEGUIMIENTO}} > Desired review frequency (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You lead {{PERSONA_O_EQUIPO}} and need to delegate {{TAREA_O_AREA}} without micromanaging (you kill autonomy and become the bottleneck) or abdicating (you hand things off without clarity and then correct with frustration). The real problem almost never is whether to delegate or not: it is that NOBODY ever makes explicit WHO decides WHAT. Delegation is not binary (I do it / I don't) but a continuum of levels, and it is almost never the same level for all decisions within the same area. An explicit, granular agreement unlocks measured autonomy, frees your schedule for higher-altitude work, and turns delegation into a lever for the person's development — not a latent risk.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior leadership coach with 15 years developing managers, specialist in Management 3.0 and the design of distributed authority systems.
Deliver a structured delegation agreement:
1. Decompose {{TAREA_O_AREA}} into 3 to 6 concrete, mutually exclusive decision areas (granularity avoids the mistake of assigning a single level to everything; if only one appears, keep dividing).
2. Assign each area a level from 1 to 7 per Jurgen Appelo's Delegation Poker: 1 Tell, 2 Sell, 3 Consult, 4 Agree, 5 Advise, 6 Inquire, 7 Delegate. Use the model's exact label, not a paraphrase.
3. Justify each level by crossing all three axes at once: cost of an error, {{NIVEL_MADUREZ}}, and {{APETITO_RIESGO}}. No generalities; if two axes pull in opposite directions, explain how you resolved the tie.
4. For each area, add an observable signal confirming the level is correctly calibrated (what you would see if it is well set).
5. Draft the agreement sentence by sentence, in first person and conversational language, ready to say out loud in a 1:1.
6. Declare the non-negotiable boundaries that are NOT delegated at any level (budget, security, client commitments, whatever applies).
7. Define the follow-up mechanism (cadence {{CADENCIA_SEGUIMIENTO}}; if empty, propose one and flag it as assumption) and observable triggers for moving a level up or down.
8. Resolve an explicit edge case: what happens if the person makes, within their level, a decision you disagree with (the default rule is to respect the agreed level and review it afterward, not revoke it in the heat of the moment).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: confirm the person, their real maturity on the topic, and risk appetite. Flag as {assumption} any data you infer; if something critical is ambiguous, ask for it in a single round before assigning levels.
Phase 2 - Decomposition: separate {{TAREA_O_AREA}} into discrete decision areas and name them in a table.
Phase 3 - Assignment: for each area, propose level 1-7 + model label + one-line justification (risk + maturity + appetite) + observable signal.
Phase 4 - Agreement and guardrails: draft the conversation script, the non-negotiable boundaries, the edge case, and the level-change triggers.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Between 3 and 6 decision areas, mutually exclusive, never a single global one.
- [ ] Each area has exactly one level from 1 to 7 with the model's exact label.
- [ ] Each level is justified by crossing all three axes (risk + maturity + appetite); ties between axes are explained.
- [ ] Each area carries an observable calibration signal.
- [ ] The agreement is drafted as a first-person conversational script, not an abstract list.
- [ ] Non-negotiable boundaries that are not delegated are declared.
- [ ] There are observable triggers for moving up and for moving down a level.
- [ ] The edge case (discrepant decision within the level) is resolved with a clear rule.
- [ ] Inferred data is flagged as assumption.
- [ ] Closes with a StrategyIA: which area to move up a level in 90 days and why.
Expected deliverable: table of areas-level-justification-signal + agreement script + non-negotiable boundaries + follow-up plan with triggers and edge case, ready to discuss in the next 1:1.
spec-liderazgo_delegacion_matriz_eisenho:
[inputs]
- ROL_Y_FOCO: {{ROL_Y_FOCO}} > Leader's role and where they should concentrate their highest-value time (e.g. "Engineering leader of 8 people; I should focus on technical strategy and team development")
- INVENTARIO_TAREAS: {{INVENTARIO_TAREAS}} > List of tasks, responsibilities, and recurring meetings to classify, with approximate time per week if known
- EQUIPO_DISPONIBLE: {{EQUIPO_DISPONIBLE}} > People who can receive delegation and their level of maturity or experience by topic (who is ready for what)
- HERRAMIENTAS_AUTOMATIZACION: {{HERRAMIENTAS_AUTOMATIZACION}} > Tools, templates, or automations available to take work off the plate; "none known" if not applicable (optional)
- PLAZOS_RESTRICCIONES: {{PLAZOS_RESTRICCIONES}} > Deadlines, fixed commitments, or constraints that condition what can be moved or eliminated (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need to classify the work on my desk to decide, task by task, what I do, what I delegate and to whom, what I automate, what I schedule, and what I eliminate. The underlying problem is that the urgent displaces the important: the day fills up with interruptions and avoidable meetings and there is no time left for the leadership work nobody else can do (strategy, decisions, team development). The Eisenhower matrix (urgent x important) cuts through that knot: it separates what deserves my time from what must leave my hands. Classifying well unlocks three things: I recover hours for the important-not-urgent quadrant, I empower the team by giving them work with clear authority, and I stop carrying tasks that do not contribute. This is not a to-do list or a schedule: it is an assignment decision on each piece of my work, with an explicit owner and authority level.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior executive coach for leaders, specialist in executive time management and effective delegation with the Eisenhower matrix; with judgment to distinguish the work only the leader can do from what must be delegated, automated, or eliminated, and to name the cost of not letting go.

Produce an actionable classification with these components:
1. Inventory: each task, responsibility, or recurring meeting with its estimated weekly time; if the data is not provided, estimate it and flag it [ASSUMPTION].
2.
