spec-liderazgo_coaching_skill_will_matri:
[inputs]
- NOMBRE_O_ROL: {{NOMBRE_O_ROL}} > Team member or role to diagnose (may be anonymized)
- TAREA_O_RESPONSABILIDAD: {{TAREA_O_RESPONSABILIDAD}} > Specific task, project, or responsibility to evaluate (the matrix is per task, not global)
- EVIDENCIAS_DESEMPENO: {{EVIDENCIAS_DESEMPENO}} > Results, delivery quality, recent milestones reflecting skill
- SENALES_MOTIVACION: {{SENALES_MOTIVACION}} > Energy, confidence, interest, incentives, and alignment observed
- INTERVENCIONES_PREVIAS: {{INTERVENCIONES_PREVIAS}} > What the leader has already tried and what effect it had (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
As a leader I need to decide the correct intervention style for {{NOMBRE_O_ROL}} on {{TAREA_O_RESPONSABILIDAD}}. Getting the style wrong is costly: micromanaging a capable person demotivates them; delegating to someone who does not yet have the skill causes failures and erodes trust; pressing for results in someone with no will worsens disengagement. A clear Skill-Will diagnosis unlocks the right conversation, concentrates my leadership energy where it pays, and turns a diffuse intuition into a traceable development plan.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior executive coach and team development facilitator, expert in Max Landsberg's Skill-Will matrix (The Tao of Coaching) and situational leadership.
Deliverable: a one-page Skill-Will diagnosis with the recommended style and a conversation plan. Steps:
1. If any input is missing or ambiguous, ask before evaluating; do not invent evidence or fill gaps with unmarked assumptions.
2. Evaluate SKILL for {{TAREA_O_RESPONSABILIDAD}} (experience, training, demonstrated results, understanding of the why) on a high or low scale, citing {{EVIDENCIAS_DESEMPENO}}.
3. Evaluate WILL (energy, confidence, interest, incentives, alignment with objectives) on a high or low scale, citing {{SENALES_MOTIVACION}}.
4. Place {{NOMBRE_O_ROL}} in a quadrant and name the style: Low skill/Low will = Direct; Low skill/High will = Develop; High skill/Low will = Motivate; High skill/High will = Delegate.
5. Deliver an actionable conversation plan and an observable signal of quadrant movement.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Framing: restate the case and explicitly separate the two axes; never merge skill and will in a single judgment. If {{INTERVENCIONES_PREVIAS}} exists, use it to avoid repeating what already failed and to read the root cause (e.g., low will may stem from a poor task fit, not the person).
Phase 2 Evidence: for each axis list the signals that support it; distinguish direct evidence from the inputs vs. inference. Mark as [ASSUMPTION] any inference not supported, and ask for the missing data if it is decisive for the quadrant. If the evidence for an axis is weak or contradictory, say so and lower the confidence of that axis rather than forcing a label.
Phase 3 Placement: situate the person in the quadrant with a confidence line (high/medium/low). If the case falls on the border between two quadrants, declare it and choose the more conservative style (the one that assumes less capacity or autonomy), justifying why. Translate the style into concrete leadership behaviors (what to do and what to stop doing) and warn of the risk of applying the wrong style in this specific case.
Phase 4 Plan: define the conversation opening, 3 to 5 open coaching questions (not leading, one idea per question), agreements to close, follow-up cadence, and the observable and verifiable signal indicating quadrant change. Add a re-evaluation trigger (when or at what event to revisit the diagnosis). Remind that the position is per task and moment, not a permanent label.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Skill and will evaluated separately, each high/low with cited evidence and listed signals.
- [ ] Inferences marked [ASSUMPTION]; missing data requested, not invented; axes with weak evidence declared with lower confidence.
- [ ] Quadrant and style (Direct/Develop/Motivate/Delegate) consistent with the matrix logic; border cases resolved toward the more conservative style with justification.
- [ ] Style translated into concrete do and stop-doing behaviors, contextualized to the task.
- [ ] Risk of the wrong style warned for this specific case.
- [ ] Explicit reminder: diagnosis per task and moment, not a label of the person; includes a re-evaluation trigger.
- [ ] Plan with opening, 3 to 5 open questions, agreements, cadence, and observable signal of movement.
- [ ] Professional tone centered on behaviors and evidence, without character judgments; no prices or promises of free service.
Expected deliverable: one-page Skill-Will diagnosis with skill axis, will axis, quadrant and style with confidence level, usage warning, conversation plan with follow-up and re-evaluation trigger.
spec-liderazgo_coaching_sucesion_rol:
[inputs]
- ROL_CRITICO: {{ROL_CRITICO}} > Name and level of the key role to protect (e.g., Data Architecture Lead)
- TITULAR_ACTUAL: {{TITULAR_ACTUAL}} > Person currently in the role, tenure, and departure probability or signals
- CANDIDATOS: {{CANDIDATOS}} > Potential internal successors with their current role; "Not identified" if none yet
- CONTEXTO_NEGOCIO: {{CONTEXTO_NEGOCIO}} > Area, team size, priorities, critical dependencies, and relevant constraints
- HORIZONTE_SUCESION: {{HORIZONTE_SUCESION}} > Target window to have a successor ready (e.g., 12-18 months)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A key role concentrates knowledge, relationships, and decisions that only one person maintains: if they leave without a prepared replacement, the team is exposed (high bus factor). The objective is to anticipate that departure, identify and prepare successors, and convert the continuity risk into a manageable development track. A solid plan unlocks retention of critical knowledge, defensible promotion decisions before HR and the sponsor, and peace of mind in the event of an unforeseen departure. Distinguish two urgencies: probable short-term departure (prioritize coverage and transfer) vs. preventive protection (prioritize pipeline and development).

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Talent and Organizational Development Director with fifteen years protecting the continuity of critical roles and designing succession pipelines.
Deliver a succession plan for {{ROL_CRITICO}} (incumbent {{TITULAR_ACTUAL}}, context {{CONTEXTO_NEGOCIO}}, candidates {{CANDIDATOS}}, horizon {{HORIZONTE_SUCESION}}, evidence {{ADJUNTOS}}) with these numbered components:
1. Criticality profile and bus factor: unique responsibilities, undocumented tacit knowledge, internal and external relationships maintained, decisions or systems only the incumbent operates, and the impact and time window in which their absence becomes critical. Classify the continuity risk as high / medium / low with justification.
2. Successor map: each candidate placed in a performance-by-potential matrix (9-box) with their availability classification (ready now / 1-2 years / 3+ years) and a recommendation on an external route if the internal pipeline does not cover the horizon. If {{CANDIDATOS}} = "Not identified", declare the gap and propose how to build the pipeline.
3. Gap analysis of the 2-3 most viable successors: technical, leadership, and business exposure gaps, separating what can be closed through development from what requires experience in the role.
4. Development plan per priority candidate: concrete actions (stretch assignment, shadowing the incumbent, knowledge transfer, mentoring, training), owner, horizon, and observable progress signal, sequenced in milestones within {{HORIZONTE_SUCESION}}.
5. Critical knowledge transfer plan (what to document, what to pair-program or shadow, what to systematize) and residual risks if the departure occurs before a successor is ready, each with mitigation and escalation trigger; close with interim coverage contingency plan and review checkpoints with HR and the area sponsor.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Criticality: decompose the role; if information on responsibilities, systems, or relationships is missing, ask for it in a single batch before proceeding.
Phase 2 - Pipeline: apply the 9-box model (performance x potential) and the availability classification; do not force candidates where there are none, recommend the external route and the continuity cost of having no pipeline.
Phase 3 - Gaps: contrast each successor against the criticality profile from Phase 1; distinguish development gap (closable through action) vs. experience gap (only closed in the role).
Phase 4 - Development and transfer: translate each closable gap into an action with owner, horizon, and progress signal; sequence milestones; document the tacit knowledge transfer, residual risks, and interim coverage.
Edge cases: incumbent with imminent departure (< 3 months) -> prioritize transfer and interim coverage over long-term development. Single candidate -> declare the concentration risk and recommend a backup. No candidates -> the deliverable is a pipeline-building plan + external route, not an empty map.
Do not invent names, metrics, or performance evaluations: mark any inference as [ASSUMPTION]. Treat people with care: use roles and placeholders, do not expose personal judgments. Neutral and professional Spanish.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- The criticality profile names concrete tacit knowledge and relationships — not generics — and classifies the risk as high / medium / low with justification.
- Each candidate has an explicit 9-box position and availability classification; if there are no candidates, there is a pipeline + external route plan.
- Gaps separate what can be closed through development from what requires real experience in the role.
- Each development action has an owner, horizon, and observable progress signal, sequenced in milestones.
- There is a knowledge transfer plan, residual risks with mitigation and trigger, interim coverage contingency, and review checkpoints with HR and sponsor.
- Zero invented names or metrics; all inferences marked [ASSUMPTION]; people's information treated as sensitive; neutral Spanish without emojis.
Expected deliverable: a succession plan structured in five blocks, ready to review with HR and the area sponsor, that reduces the role's bus factor to an actionable and manageable development track.
spec-liderazgo_desempeno_evaluacion_anua:
[inputs]
- NOMBRE_ROL_EVALUADO: {{NOMBRE_ROL_EVALUADO}} > Name or identifier and role of the person being evaluated (may be anonymized, e.g., "Senior data analyst")
- PERIODO_EVALUADO: {{PERIODO_EVALUADO}} > Cycle covered by the evaluation (e.g., "Fiscal year 2025, Q1-Q4"); defines the start of Q1
- EVIDENCIA_LOGROS_HECHOS: {{EVIDENCIA_LOGROS_HECHOS}} > Facts, achievements, metrics, and dates throughout the cycle; ideally one or more per quarter
- AREAS_MEJORA_OBSERVADAS: {{AREAS_MEJORA_OBSERVADAS}} > Behaviors or results to develop, already observed (optional)
- CRITERIOS_EVALUACION: {{CRITERIOS_EVALUACION}} > Competencies, values, or objectives from the formal framework; if there is a rating scale, indicate levels (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You are the leader responsible for closing the performance cycle of a team member and you need a balanced annual evaluation, ready for a face-to-face conversation. The central risk is recency bias: over-weighting what happened in the last few weeks and forgetting the rest of the year. An evaluation well anchored in dated evidence and balanced between achievements and development unlocks a fair conversation, defensible calibration decisions, and a credible growth plan for the next cycle. A biased or evidence-free evaluation erodes trust, exposes to legal or equity bias, and demotivates.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior team leader with experience in talent management, performance calibration, and development feedback.
Deliverable: a structured annual performance evaluation for {{NOMBRE_ROL_EVALUADO}} for {{PERIODO_EVALUADO}}, based on {{EVIDENCIA_LOGROS_HECHOS}}, {{AREAS_MEJORA_OBSERVADAS}}, and {{CRITERIOS_EVALUACION}}. Steps:
1. Build a timeline of evidence by quarter (Q1-Q4); mark any quarter without data as an evidence gap (do not fill in).
2. Draft at least three achievements using the Situation-Behavior-Impact (SBI) model, each with a concrete example, date, and metric or observable result; distribute achievements across quarters.
3. Draft two or three improvement areas using the same SBI model, framed as actionable behaviors (not personality traits), each with a verifiable suggested action and, when applicable, a concrete support resource.
4. Close with a global rating aligned to {{CRITERIOS_EVALUACION}} (mapping achievements/improvements to each competency or criterion), two or three SMART objectives for the next cycle, and a calibration note confirming temporal coverage of all four quarters and explicitly stating how recency bias was mitigated.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Temporal mapping: place each fact in its quarter using the declared start of Q1; detect late concentrations that reveal recency bias and flag imbalances.
Phase 2 - Achievements: apply SBI with dated evidence and observable results; balance across quarters and separate verifiable fact from interpretation.
Phase 3 - Development: translate observations into specific behaviors and verifiable improvement actions; developmental — not punitive — tone.
Phase 4 - Close and calibration: synthesize the global rating, SMART objectives, and the quarterly coverage note; declare assumptions and gaps.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
Edge cases: if evidence covers fewer than four quarters, declare the gaps and do NOT invent; if an observation sounds like a personality trait, reframe it as a behavior; if {{CRITERIOS_EVALUACION}} is not provided, use generic axes (results, collaboration, quality, initiative) and mark it [ASSUMPTION]; if there is a sensitive incident, describe it as behavior and impact without accusatory language.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] All four quarters (Q1-Q4) are represented; evidence gaps are declared, not invented.
- [ ] At least three achievements and two or three improvement areas, all in SBI format.
- [ ] Each achievement has a concrete example, date, and metric or observable result.
- [ ] Improvement areas describe actionable behaviors — never personality traits — and each has a verifiable action (and support when applicable).
- [ ] Global rating consistent with {{CRITERIOS_EVALUACION}} and mapped to its competencies; next-cycle objectives in SMART format.
- [ ] Calibration note confirms temporal coverage and explicitly states how recency bias was mitigated.
- [ ] Verifiable fact separated from interpretation; professional, specific, and respectful tone in neutral Spanish; no invented data (inferences marked [ASSUMPTION]).
Expected deliverable: annual evaluation document with sections Timeline, Achievements, Improvement areas, Global rating and objectives, and Calibration note, ready for the closing conversation.
spec-liderazgo_desempeno_autoevaluacion_:
[inputs]
- ROL_Y_NIVEL: {{ROL_Y_NIVEL}} > Job title, seniority level, and area; calibrates the expectations against which the role is measured
- PERIODO_EVALUADO: {{PERIODO_EVALUADO}} > Cycle covered by the self-evaluation (fiscal year, semester, quarter)
- OBJETIVOS_O_COMPETENCIAS: {{OBJETIVOS_O_COMPETENCIAS}} > Objectives, OKRs, goals, or formal competencies against which you are evaluated
- LOGROS_Y_EVIDENCIA: {{LOGROS_Y_EVIDENCIA}} > Candidate achievements, metrics, verifiable sources, and your specific role in each
- FORMATO_EMPRESA: {{FORMATO_EMPRESA}} > Format, length, rating scale, and tone required by the process (optional)
- FEEDBACK_PREVIO: {{FEEDBACK_PREVIO}} > Feedback from prior cycles, pending commitments, or areas flagged by your manager (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You need to write your performance self-evaluation for the period {{PERIODO_EVALUADO}} in the role {{ROL_Y_NIVEL}}. A strong self-evaluation is neither the most flattering nor the most humble: it is the most credible. If you exaggerate, you lose credibility with your evaluator and undermine your real achievements; if you minimize yourself, you leave unacknowledged contributions that deserve visibility and compensation. A calibrated, evidence-based self-evaluation unlocks fairer career conversations, supports promotion or raise decisions, and builds a reliable record of your trajectory. The difference between a forgettable draft and one that moves the needle almost always comes down to three disciplines: every statement anchored to data, every achievement distinguished from the collective result, every gap named with its plan. This prompt gets you there without inflating or inventing.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior performance and talent development coach, experienced in designing evaluation cycles (including peer calibration scales and committees) and training professionals to document their work in a fair, verifiable, and development-oriented way.

Deliverable: a structured and calibrated self-evaluation draft, ready to review and paste into the company format. Steps:
1. Reframe the received context (role, period, objectives, format, prior feedback) and confirm assumptions before drafting.
2. For each item in {{OBJETIVOS_O_COMPETENCIAS}}, collect the associated achievements from {{LOGROS_Y_EVIDENCIA}} and convert them from vague statements to evidence-backed statements (what I did, what result it produced, what data or source supports it).
3. Explicitly separate the team result from your personally verifiable contribution in each achievement.
4. Calibrate the tone: point out where the draft exaggerates without supporting data and where it undervalues a real achievement, and adjust to a defensible midpoint for a skeptical evaluator.
5. Cover objectives without clear evidence honestly: declare partial progress or non-completion with its cause, without embellishing.
6. Write honest improvement areas, each with the concrete action plan you have already started or will start, connecting with {{FEEDBACK_PREVIO}} when it exists.
7. Close with learnings and growth from the period, tied to the trajectory and expectations of the next level of the role.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: reframe context and objectives; if achievements, evidence, or key objectives are missing, ask for them before proceeding. Structure each achievement with STAR (Situation, Task, Action, Result) and use precise contribution language (I led / I coordinated / I contributed / the team achieved) to separate individual contribution from collective achievement.
Phase 2 - Conversion to evidence: for each objective, transform vague statements into statements anchored to a metric or source; mark as [ASSUMPTION] or pending confirmation any data not provided, without inventing or rounding figures upward.
Phase 3 - Tone calibration: detect exaggerations (statement without data), minimizations (undervalued real achievement), and undue attributions (team achievement presented as personal); adjust to a defensible position.
Phase 4 - Final draft: assemble the draft with the agreed sections, align length and scale to {{FORMATO_EMPRESA}}, and list at the end the data pending confirmation and the credibility risks detected.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reframe what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Each relevant achievement has a metric, source, or concrete evidence; no data was invented or inflated.
- [ ] Personal contribution is clearly separated from the team result in each achievement.
- [ ] Tone is calibrated: no inflated statements, no minimization of real achievements, no attribution of collective achievements to yourself.
- [ ] Unmet or partially met objectives are declared with their cause and are not omitted.
- [ ] Improvement areas are honest and each one includes a concrete action plan; prior feedback is linked when it exists.
- [ ] Missing data is marked as pending confirmation, not completed with undisclosed assumptions.
- [ ] The draft respects {{FORMATO_EMPRESA}} in structure, length, scale, and tone.
Expected deliverable: self-evaluation draft (4-to-6-line executive summary, achievements by objective, partially met or unmet objectives, improvement areas with plan, learnings), followed by a list of data pending confirmation and the detected credibility risks.
spec-liderazgo_desempeno_calibracion_ses:
[inputs]
- CICLO_Y_ESCALA: {{CICLO_Y_ESCALA}} > Evaluated period and rating scale with its meaning (e.g. 1-5, or categories such as Below/Meets/Exceeds); include whether the scale enforces a target distribution or is open
- POBLACION: {{POBLACION}} > People to calibrate grouped by level or role family; headcount, managers involved, and whether there are comparable subgroups
- RATINGS_PROPUESTOS: {{RATINGS_PROPUESTOS}} > Preliminary rating per person and proposing manager; ideally with prior-cycle rating if available
- EVIDENCIA_DISPONIBLE: {{EVIDENCIA_DISPONIBLE}} > Achievements, metrics, feedback, and dates supporting each rating; indicate source (self-evaluation, manager, peers, system data)
- TIEMPO_Y_PARTICIPANTES: {{TIEMPO_Y_PARTICIPANTES}} > Session duration, facilitator, and attending managers (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You are going to prepare a calibration session between managers who review the ratings of people at the same level or role family. The purpose is to equalize the yardstick across teams and protect the fairness of the cycle: a well-prepared calibration reduces complaints, sustains compensation and promotion decisions under audit, and prevents a rating from being decided by impression rather than evidence. Preparation unlocks a shorter and less defensive meeting, with sensitive cases already mapped and difficult questions already drafted in a neutral tone.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior performance calibration facilitator with experience in people analytics and fair evaluation process design. Stance: judge the quality of the evidence supporting each rating, never the person being evaluated nor the manager's judgment.
Deliverable: a session preparation package. Steps:
1. Reframe the cycle {{CICLO_Y_ESCALA}}, the scale with its meaning, and the {{POBLACION}} to calibrate; list information gaps and declare whether the scale allows a free distribution or imposes a target.
2. Build the distribution of {{RATINGS_PROPUESTOS}} by manager and flag deviations that suggest systematic leniency or severity, comparing each manager against the group, without forcing a normal curve. Distinguish a real deviation from a small sample (a manager with few evaluees may deviate by chance): mark it as a weak signal.
3. For each flagged case, classify {{EVIDENCIA_DISPONIBLE}} into: full-cycle performance vs. isolated recent event (recency); individual merit vs. halo from a single project or historical reputation. Also note, when the signal appears, contrast bias (rating influenced by comparing with a nearby peer) and affinity/similarity bias.
4. Draft 2–3 neutral challenge questions per flagged case, directed at the proposing manager, requiring observable and dated evidence, not impressions or personality traits.
5. Deliver a timed agenda, case review order (from highest to lowest bias risk), and a tiebreaker protocol when managers do not agree (criterion, who decides, how it is recorded).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: confirm scale, population, and rules; if {{CICLO_Y_ESCALA}}, {{RATINGS_PROPUESTOS}}, or {{EVIDENCIA_DISPONIBLE}} are missing, ask for them before proceeding. {{TIEMPO_Y_PARTICIPANTES}} and {{ADJUNTOS}} are optional: if missing, assume defaults and mark them [ASSUMPTION].
Phase 2 - Detection: analyze distribution by manager (leniency/severity, with weak-signal flag if the sample is small) and for each person cross-reference evidence against dates (recency) and against a single dominant attribute (halo). Mark each finding with the presumed bias, its evidence signal, and a confidence level (high/medium/low).
Phase 3 - Challenge preparation: draft neutral questions, the case profile card, and the agenda. Do not invent data about individuals; everything not provided goes as [ASSUMPTION]. In shareable outputs use codes (P-01, M-A) instead of names to preserve functional anonymity.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reframe what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Explicit reframing of cycle, scale (with meaning and free/target type), and population; gaps listed.
- [ ] Distribution by manager presented; leniency/severity flagged without imposing a forced curve; small samples marked as weak signal.
- [ ] Each flagged case distinguishes recency (dates) and halo (single attribute), with contrast/affinity when applicable, its evidence signal, and confidence level.
- [ ] Neutral challenge questions, centered on observable and dated evidence, not on person judgments or traits.
- [ ] Timed agenda + order by bias risk + actionable tiebreaker protocol (criterion, decision-maker, record).
- [ ] Zero invented data; assumptions marked [ASSUMPTION]; functional anonymity with codes in shareable outputs; neutral and professional English.
Expected deliverable: preparation document with (a) distribution table by manager, (b) profile card per flagged case with bias, classified evidence, and confidence level, (c) challenge question bank, (d) agenda and tiebreaker protocol.
spec-liderazgo_desempeno_matriz_9box:
[inputs]
- EQUIPO: {{EQUIPO}} > List of team members with, for each: name or alias, recent results against goals, examples of observable behavior, and potential signals
- PERIODO: {{PERIODO}} > Performance window to evaluate (recommended 6 to 12 months to avoid recency bias)
- OBJETIVOS: {{OBJETIVOS}} > Goals or reference objectives against which performance is measured
- DEFINICION_POTENCIAL: {{DEFINICION_POTENCIAL}} > What potential means in this context: agile learning, role ambition, adaptability, capacity to take on greater scope (optional; if missing, AI proposes a definition and requests confirmation)
- PROPOSITO: {{PROPOSITO}} > Why calibration is being done: development plans, succession, challenge assignments, career conversations (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A leader needs an honest and actionable reading of their team to decide on development, retention, and challenge assignments. The 9-box matrix (Performance x Potential Grid, popularized by McKinsey and GE) crosses current performance against growth potential in a 9-cell grid and converts diffuse impressions into a structured, evidence-based conversation. When well applied, it unlocks differentiated development plans, identifies successors and flight risks, and exposes biases before they contaminate career decisions. When poorly applied, it labels people and justifies cuts: this prompt avoids that use. Assumption: the leader has direct contact with the team and data for at least one cycle; if not, the output will be explicitly provisional.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Director of Talent and Organizational Development with experience facilitating 9-box calibration sessions in people committees.

Deliverable: a calibrated placement of the team in the 9-box matrix with differentiated actions by quadrant. Steps:
1. Align criteria: define the performance axis as sustained results against OBJECTIVES during PERIOD (not an isolated peak or personal affinity) and the potential axis according to DEFINICION_POTENCIAL (demonstrated capacity to take on greater scope, not tenure or charisma). Declare that both axes require observable evidence and set the minimum evidence threshold.
2. Verify data sufficiency per person in EQUIPO; if evidence for an axis is missing, mark the placement as provisional and indicate the missing data instead of inventing it.
3. Build the 9-box matrix placing each person in their cell with one line of evidence-based justification; flag border cases between two cells.
4. For each occupied quadrant, give its reading and 2 to 3 concrete differentiated actions aligned to PROPOSITO.
5. Emit calibration alerts (biases, border cases, risk concentrations) and open questions prior to irreversible decisions.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: set operational definitions of both axes and the minimum evidence threshold.
Phase 2 - Data sanitation: review EQUIPO person by person, separating facts from impressions and flagging gaps; discard data outside PERIODO to mitigate recency.
Phase 3 - Placement: assign each person to one of the 9 cells (low/mid/high performance x low/mid/high potential) with justification; flag anyone who falls on the border between two cells and explain why.
Phase 4 - Action by quadrant: translate each occupied cell into a reading + actions. Reference guide: high performance + high potential (star) = retention, succession, stretch; high potential + mid or low performance (enigma or new to role) = focused development and expectation clarity; high performance + mid or low potential (solid, reliable expert) = recognition, retention, and technical deepening; low potential and performance (at risk) = improvement plan with deadline and honest conversation. Labels are a reading, not a verdict.
Phase 5 - Calibration and close: list probable biases (halo, recency, leniency, contrast, affinity), risk concentrations (flight of multiple stars, succession vacuum, overload on a single person), and open questions.
Edge cases: single-person team (the matrix loses comparative power — declare this); all in the same cell (review criteria, possible leniency or poorly calibrated standard); data only on one of the two axes (place provisionally on that axis, request the other).
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reframe what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Each person placed in a single primary cell, with evidence-based justification (not impression).
- [ ] Placements with insufficient data marked as provisional, with the missing data made explicit.
- [ ] Both axes defined operationally and evidence threshold set before placing anyone.
- [ ] Each occupied quadrant has a reading + 2 to 3 differentiated and concrete actions aligned to PROPOSITO.
- [ ] Actions distinguish development, retention, career conversation, and improvement plan according to the cell.
- [ ] Biases, border cases, and risk concentrations section present.
- [ ] Applicable edge cases (single-person team, concentration in one cell, axis without data) addressed when they occur.
- [ ] No person labeled as expendable; no termination automatically derived from the 9-box.
- [ ] Open questions listed prior to irreversible decisions.
Expected deliverable: evidence-based 9-box matrix + differentiated actions by quadrant + calibration alerts + open questions, in professional English.
spec-liderazgo_desempeno_pip_plan_mejora:
[inputs]
- COLABORADOR_ROL: {{COLABORADOR_ROL}} > Role, level, and approximate tenure of the employee (without real name if anonymization is preferred)
- BRECHAS_DESEMPENO: {{BRECHAS_DESEMPENO}} > Observed gaps stated as concrete facts (what, when, impact), not as personality judgments
- EXPECTATIVAS_OBJETIVO: {{EXPECTATIVAS_OBJETIVO}} > Expected standard of the position against which performance is measured
- DURACION_PLAZO: {{DURACION_PLAZO}} > Plan horizon (e.g. 30, 60, or 90 days) and start date
- SOPORTE_DISPONIBLE: {{SOPORTE_DISPONIBLE}} > Real support resources: mentoring, training, workload reassignment, tools, time
- CONTEXTO_PREVIO: {{CONTEXTO_PREVIO}} > (optional) Feedback already delivered, background, legal or HR constraints
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
An employee is operating below the position standard and the situation requires formal intervention. A well-designed PIP converts a difficult conversation into a structured and fair opportunity: it gives clarity about what must change, support to achieve it, and transparent evaluation rules. Doing it well protects the person (real opportunity, dignified treatment), the leader (defensible and consistent decision), and the organization (HR-traceable process). A vague, punitive, or unsupported PIP destroys trust and creates labor risk. The goal is a plan that any third party would evaluate the same way with the same data.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior people leader with a background in performance management and HR coordination, accustomed to defensible, symmetric, and dignity-centered improvement plans.
Design a complete PIP and deliver, in this order:
1. Purpose framing in 3–4 sentences: respectful, improvement-oriented, without punitive language.
2. Gap table: one row per gap, with columns Observed Gap (fact) | SMART Expectation | Compliance Indicator | Evidence to Be Reviewed | Associated Support.
3. Support plan: what the organization offers (mentoring, training, resources, workload adjustments) and follow-up cadence (frequency and format of check-ins).
4. Schedule: start date, intermediate check-ins with date and focus, and closing date, aligned to the given timeline.
5. Closing criteria: list of SUCCESS criteria and list of EXIT criteria, symmetric, with numeric or binary thresholds (not adjectives), evaluable by a third party.
6. Opening script: sober 6–8-line draft for the initial conversation.
7. Evidence log: brief template to record at each check-in date, progress by expectation, and next steps.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Interpret: reframe role, gaps, and standard; separate facts from judgments; if a gap is written as a personality judgment, ask me to rewrite it as an observable fact (what happened, when, what impact) before including it; mark with [ASSUMPTION] any missing data and ask for the critical ones before proceeding; do not invent history or facts about the person.
Phase 2 - Plan: structure the PIP (framing, gap-to-expectations, support, schedule, criteria, script, log) and present the outline for validation.
Phase 3 - Execute: draft the 7 deliverables; verify that each expectation is SMART, that each success/exit criterion is measurable and symmetric, that no gap is left without expectation, indicator, evidence, or support, and that the timeline is respected; close by reminding to validate with HR and, if applicable, labor legal counsel before communicating to the employee.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reframe what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Each gap is stated as an observable fact, not as a personality judgment.
- [ ] Each expectation fulfills SMART (specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, time-bound).
- [ ] Each gap has an expectation, indicator, evidence, and associated support (no gaps).
- [ ] Success and exit criteria are symmetric, with numeric or binary thresholds evaluable by a third party.
- [ ] The schedule respects the given timeline and includes at least one intermediate check-in with a defined focus.
- [ ] The support is concrete and realistic, derived from what has been declared available (not vague promises).
- [ ] The evidence log allows each check-in to be documented in a traceable way.
- [ ] Professional and humane tone; zero punitive or intimidating language.
- [ ] Assumptions marked [ASSUMPTION]; nothing invented about the person or their history.
- [ ] Reminder to validate with HR and, if applicable, labor legal counsel before communicating.
Expected deliverable: a PIP document ready to review with HR and discuss with the employee, with framing, gap table, support plan, schedule, symmetric closing criteria, opening script, and evidence log.
spec-liderazgo_desempeno_conversacion_ca:
[inputs]
- NOMBRE_ROL: {{NOMBRE_ROL}} > Name or role of the person receiving the rating (e.g. "senior analyst on the data team")
- RATING: {{RATING}} > Rating being delivered and, if applicable, the one the person expected (e.g. "Partially Meets, expected Exceeds")
- MOTIVO_RATING: {{MOTIVO_RATING}} > Central reason and observable evidence supporting the rating (dated facts and examples, not judgments)
- FORTALEZA_A_RECONOCER: {{FORTALEZA_A_RECONOCER}} > What you genuinely value about the person and which is not in question
- RESULTADO_DESEADO: {{RESULTADO_DESEADO}} > How you want the person to feel when the conversation ends (optional)
- HISTORIAL: {{HISTORIAL}} > Prior conversations, warnings, or signals given before this cycle (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I am going to conduct a performance evaluation conversation in which I deliver to {{NOMBRE_ROL}} the rating {{RATING}}, lower than expected. The central reason is {{MOTIVO_RATING}} and I want to preserve {{FORTALEZA_A_RECONOCER}}. A poorly conducted conversation burns trust, triggers a defensive reaction, and leaves the person without a path to improvement; a well-conducted one sustains the relationship, makes the message irrefutable, and opens an actionable path. What is unlocked: clarity about the rating, dignity preserved, and an improvement plan the person can own.
Assumptions: the rating decision is already closed and will not be renegotiated in the room; the conversation is 1:1 and private; a formal performance cycle exists to support the process. If any of these do not apply, declare it and adjust.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior manager and performance coach with experience conducting high-impact feedback conversations, trained in separating observable behavior from identity and in sustaining emotion without renegotiating the message.
Deliver a conversation script ready to rehearse plus a reaction management kit. Steps:
1. Opening (2–3 sentences): name the purpose without suspense or preamble; frame the conversation as honest and forward-oriented.
2. Rating delivery: communicate {{RATING}} directly and sustain {{MOTIVO_RATING}} with two or three observable, specific, and dated examples, separating the person's behavior from who they are.
3. Recognition: integrate {{FORTALEZA_A_RECONOCER}} as a firm fact, not as a buffer or sandwich technique that dilutes the message.
4. Listening space: include phrases to invite the reaction, sustain the silence (3–5 seconds), and validate the emotion without yielding on the rating.
5. Forward-looking reframe: define two or three concrete, measurable, and date-bound actions, and the support the manager commits to providing.
6. Closing: confirm mutual understanding (not forced agreement) and set follow-up.
7. Reaction kit: anticipate denial, anger, and emotional breakdown with a model response for each.
8. Trap phrases: list two or three formulations to avoid (relativizing the message, blaming the system or third parties, promising what is not controlled) with their alternative.
9. 30-day follow-up plan with verifiable milestones.
Align the script with {{RESULTADO_DESEADO}} when it exists and consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as supporting evidence.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Diagnosis: validate that {{MOTIVO_RATING}} is supported by observable facts; if it relies on judgments or {{HISTORIAL}} of prior signals is missing, ask for the missing evidence before drafting. If there were no prior signals, say so transparently: it is a data point that changes the tone and should not be hidden.
Phase 2 - Structure: apply the sequence purpose > evidence > listening > path, keeping behavior and identity separate and a single central message undiluted.
Phase 3 - Rehearsal: draft the script in natural spoken language, brief, without HR jargon; mark with brackets the moments of pause and listening.
Phase 4 - Stress test: subject the script to the three probable reactions and adjust the model responses so that they validate the emotion without reopening the rating negotiation.
Edge cases: if the person asks to change the rating in the room, redirect to the formal process without promising a review; if they cry or shut down, offer a brief pause without canceling the message; if the conversation escalates to hostility, set a respectful limit and propose to reconvene.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reframe what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The opening names the purpose in the first 30 seconds, without suspense.
- [ ] The rating is delivered directly and supported by 2–3 observable and dated examples, not judgments.
- [ ] Behavior and identity are kept separate throughout the script.
- [ ] The recognition is genuine and does not function as a buffer or sandwich.
- [ ] There is an explicit listening space with phrases to sustain silence and emotion.
- [ ] The forward-looking actions are concrete, measurable, and date-bound.
- [ ] The kit covers denial, anger, and breakdown with responses that do not renegotiate the rating.
- [ ] Trap phrases are listed with their alternative.
- [ ] The 30-day plan has verifiable milestones.
- [ ] Edge cases (request for change, emotional shutdown, hostility) have a planned response.
- [ ] Dignified and respectful tone without diluting clarity.
Expected deliverable: rehearsable conversation script (opening, delivery, listening, reframe, closing) + management kit for three reactions + list of trap phrases with alternatives + 30-day follow-up plan with verifiable milestones.
spec-liderazgo_desempeno_separar_desempe:
[inputs]
- COLABORADOR: {{COLABORADOR}} > Name or alias and current role of the person to evaluate
- RESULTADOS_PERIODO: {{RESULTADOS_PERIODO}} > Goals, metrics, and verifiable milestones of the current period
- COMPETENCIAS_OBSERVADAS: {{COMPETENCIAS_OBSERVADAS}} > Observed behaviors: learning, aspiration, handling of ambiguity, influence
- ROL_OBJETIVO: {{ROL_OBJETIVO}} > Role or higher level the person could aspire to
- HORIZONTE: {{HORIZONTE}} > Potential evaluation window, e.g. 12-24 months (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You are going to calibrate an employee before a people committee. The most costly error in performance evaluation is collapsing two distinct questions into a single score: "what they delivered" (performance, a verifiable backward-looking view) and "how far they can go" (potential, a prospective bet). Conflating them produces two classic failures: promoting a high performer without runway until they reach their level of incompetence, and dismissing a high-potential employee because of a weak period. Two biases amplify the error: recency (over-weighting the last event) and halo (allowing one axis to contaminate the other). Separating both axes with evidence unlocks defensible promotion, development, and retention decisions under calibration.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior people leader with fifteen years calibrating talent in people committees, expert in the nine-cell talent matrix (9-box: performance x potential).

Deliverable: a calibration profile card for an employee with separate classification by axis, matrix placement, and a differentiated action plan. Guiding principle: one period is not a destiny and a strong period does not prove potential; data overrides impression. Steps:
1. Evaluate CURRENT PERFORMANCE only with facts from the period (met or unmet goals, quality, consistency, measurable impact). Classify as low / solid / outstanding with at least two concrete pieces of evidence per assigned level.
2. Evaluate POTENTIAL with prospective signals distinct from the period result: agile learning, aspiration and ambition, handling of increasing ambiguity and complexity, influence beyond the role. Classify as low / medium / high against ROL_OBJETIVO. Mark with [ASSUMPTION] every inference not supported by an observed behavior.
3. Declare a confidence level (high / medium / low) for each axis based on evidence sufficiency; if insufficient to classify, say so instead of forcing a score.
4. Place the person in the 9-cell matrix (performance x potential) and name the cell.
5. Explain the typical risk of misreading that quadrant (over-promotion, abandonment of potential, over-investment in a stagnant employee) and flag if recency or halo bias may have skewed your reading.
6. Deliver 3 differentiated development or management actions according to the cell, each with an owner and a horizon.
7. Close with a calibration question the leader must be able to answer with data before the committee.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 0 - Input verification: if RESULTADOS_PERIODO, COMPETENCIAS_OBSERVADAS, or ROL_OBJETIVO are missing, ask for them before classifying; do not invent evidence or fill gaps with impressions.
Phase 1 - Performance axis: tabulate period facts, assign level, cite evidence, set confidence.
Phase 2 - Potential axis: tabulate prospective signals, assign level, separate fact from inference with [ASSUMPTION], set confidence. Do not reuse performance evidence as a potential signal without justification.
Phase 3 - Synthesis: place in matrix, name cell, expose misreading risk, audit recency and halo biases, derive 3 differentiated actions with owner and horizon.
Phase 4 - Calibration: formulate the closing question answerable with data.
Edge case: if the period was atypical (role change, leave, reorganization) note it as an explicit mitigating factor before setting the performance score.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reframe what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Both axes evaluated separately, without the period result contaminating the potential reading.
- [ ] Each assigned level has at least two concrete pieces of evidence from the period or observed behaviors.
- [ ] Every inference without an observed behavior is marked [ASSUMPTION]; zero invented evidence.
- [ ] Each axis declares a confidence level; low confidence is named rather than forcing a score.
- [ ] The 9-cell matrix cell is named and its misreading risk explained, with recency and halo audit.
- [ ] The 3 actions are differentiated, coherent with the cell, and each has an owner and a horizon.
- [ ] The calibration question is answerable with data, not opinion.
Expected deliverable: calibration profile card ready for a people committee, with classification by axis, confidence level by axis, named cell, risk, 3 actions with owner and horizon, and closing question.
spec-liderazgo_desempeno_documentar_evid:
[inputs]
- EQUIPO: {{EQUIPO}} > Team size and composition (headcount, roles, seniority, location/remote)
- CICLO_EVALUACION: {{CICLO_EVALUACION}} > Cycle duration and dates (semi-annual, annual, target evaluation date) and whether there is cross-leader calibration
- COMPETENCIAS_OBJETIVOS: {{COMPETENCIAS_OBJETIVOS}} > Competencies, values, or objectives against which evaluation is conducted (rubric or levels if they exist)
- HERRAMIENTAS: {{HERRAMIENTAS}} > Available tools for recording (notes, spreadsheet, HR system, task manager, messaging)
- CADENCIA_DISPONIBLE: {{CADENCIA_DISPONIBLE}} > Realistic time and frequency the leader can dedicate to recording
- FUENTES_ADICIONALES: {{FUENTES_ADICIONALES}} > Whether employees, peers, or internal clients will contribute their own evidence (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Performance evaluations often fail because of a memory problem, not a judgment problem: the leader remembers the last few weeks with clarity and forgets achievements and incidents from the rest of the cycle (recency bias), producing conversations perceived as unfair and hard to defend. The purpose is to build the continuous capture infrastructure that documents observable and dated facts throughout the cycle, so that by the time the evaluation arrives the conversation is grounded in traceable evidence. This unlocks fair and defensible evaluations, specific real-time feedback, and promotion or calibration decisions based on facts. Limit: the system captures evidence; it does not replace the conversation or the leader's judgment.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Team leader and senior people manager, expert in performance management and evidence-based evaluations.
Deliverable: a continuous evidence capture system, composed of (1) an evidence log template with defined fields and a filled-in example, (2) a sustainable capture cadence, and (3) the structure of a per-person evidence dossier for the evaluation conversation. It is NOT an annual evaluation form or an individual improvement plan.
Steps:
1. Define what constitutes useful evidence: an observable and dated fact, not a judgment or personality label. Include the contrast between a bad entry and a good entry.
2. Deliver the log template in STAR format (Situation, Task, Action, Result) with fields: date, person, situation, observed behavior, impact, linked competency or objective, source, link, and data confidence level. Accompany it with a complete example row.
3. Propose the capture cadence: brief periodic routine plus immediate capture of significant events, with concrete triggers.
4. Define how to incorporate and cross-reference multiple sources (employee self-evidence, peers, internal clients), separating data from interpretation and recording both versions when they differ.
5. Explain how to synthesize the log into a per-person dossier, grouped by competency or objective, with a trend signal and a gap check (competencies without evidence or under-recorded individuals).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Record design: fix the useful evidence criterion (observable, dated, attributable) and produce the STAR log template with an example.
Phase 2 - Capture cadence: design the sustainable routine based on the declared time, with triggers that balance achievements and incidents to avoid both recency bias and negativity bias; include an anti-pattern to avoid (recording only when something goes wrong).
Phase 3 - Multiple sources: integrate self-evidence and peer and internal client feedback, with rules for cross-referencing versions and separating the observable from the interpreted; privacy note on what is recorded and how it is communicated to the team.
Phase 4 - Synthesis for evaluation: convert the accumulated evidence into a per-person dossier, grouped by competency or objective, with visible trend and gap coverage.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reframe what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- Each log entry is an observable and dated fact, never a personality judgment; the bad vs. good entry contrast is present.
- The template uses STAR format, includes a data confidence level, and links each piece of evidence to an evaluable competency or objective; it comes with a complete example row.
- The cadence is sustainable for the time declared in CADENCIA_DISPONIBLE and balances positive and improvement evidence (mitigates recency and negativity biases); the anti-pattern to avoid is declared.
- Multiple sources are integrated with an explicit rule for separating data from interpretation and for recording divergent versions.
- The final dossier is grouped by competency or objective, shows trend across the cycle, and includes a gap check.
- Assumptions are marked [ASSUMPTION]; no team or cycle data is invented; if an essential data point is missing it is requested before executing.
- Neutral and professional English, no emojis, no invented figures.
Expected deliverable: log template with fields and filled-in example, capture cadence with triggers and anti-pattern, and per-person evidence dossier structure, all actionable starting next week.
spec-liderazgo_desempeno_promocion_caso:
[inputs]
- COLABORADOR: {{COLABORADOR}} > Name or identifier of the person to be promoted and a summary of their role
- NIVEL_ACTUAL: {{NIVEL_ACTUAL}} > Level or position they hold today
- NIVEL_OBJETIVO: {{NIVEL_OBJETIVO}} > Level or position they are being nominated for
- RUBRICA_NIVEL_OBJETIVO: {{RUBRICA_NIVEL_OBJETIVO}} > Competencies and formal expectations of the target level (if no formal rubric exists, indicate that and it will be inferred from the role with [ASSUMPTION] mark)
- LOGROS_CON_METRICAS: {{LOGROS_CON_METRICAS}} > Employee achievements with measurable result, impact scope, and period
- FEEDBACK_STAKEHOLDERS: {{FEEDBACK_STAKEHOLDERS}} > Feedback from peers, internal clients, and leaders, including any known detractor (optional)
- TIEMPO_EN_ROL: {{TIEMPO_EN_ROL}} > Time in the current role and in the organization (optional)
- PAR_DE_REFERENCIA: {{PAR_DE_REFERENCIA}} > Peer already at the target level for equity comparison, or "No reference" (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I want to bring to the calibration committee the promotion case for an employee. The committee does not reward effort or potential: it approves those who ALREADY demonstrate, in a sustained way, the performance of the target level. A dossier built on impact evidence and with objections anticipated unlocks a fast and defensible decision, reduces evaluator bias, and protects process fairness. A dossier based on opinions falls apart at the first difficult question. The risk to avoid is twofold: overselling a weak case (costs credibility with the committee) or underselling a solid one (unfairly holds the person back).

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Act as a senior HR Business Partner, specialist in talent management, level rubrics, and calibration committee facilitation.
Deliver a promotion dossier with these six sections, in this order:
1. One-sentence thesis: why the employee ALREADY operates at the target level, not why they would get there.
2. Rubric map against the target level: one row per expected competency with concrete evidence (project, measurable result, impact scope, period). Mark GAP for every competency without solid evidence and [ASSUMPTION] for every inference not backed by a provided fact.
3. Level differential: three to five examples showing scope, autonomy, or influence belonging to the higher level and not to the current one; explicitly name what current-level behavior is being superseded.
4. Objection anticipation: table of probable committee objection + evidence-based response. Cover at least: time in role, lack of cross-area visibility, one detractor, comparison with a peer, and performance sustainability (one outstanding quarter is not a pattern).
5. Gap closure plan: if the committee asks to wait a cycle, verifiable milestones with a date and a success signal for each real gap.
6. Case maturity verdict: READY FOR COMMITTEE / READY WITH MINOR GAPS / NOT READY, with one line justifying it based on the ratio of demonstrated vs. gap competencies.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Interpretation: reframe who is being promoted, from and to what level, and what evidence is available.
Phase 2 - Data gap: identify what is missing (rubric, achievements with metrics, feedback, time in role, reference peer) and ask for it. Do not invent figures, achievements, or feedback; what is not provided is marked [ASSUMPTION] or as a gap.
Phase 3 - Mapping: cross each target level competency against the evidence; separate what is demonstrated from what is aspirational and from what is merely repeated at the current level.
Phase 4 - Argumentation: draft the thesis, level differential, and objection responses always anchored in facts, not opinion; if the central evidence does not support the thesis, say so directly.
Phase 5 - Plan and verdict: define verifiable milestones only for real gaps and issue the maturity verdict.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reframe what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The thesis affirms already-demonstrated performance at the target level, not future potential.
- [ ] Each competency in the rubric has evidence with a metric and period, or is marked GAP.
- [ ] The level differential distinguishes scope/autonomy/influence of the higher level from the current one and names what is superseded.
- [ ] Each probable objection has an evidence-based response, not opinion; time in role, cross-area visibility, detractor, peer comparison, and sustainability are all covered.
- [ ] No figure, achievement, or feedback was invented; missing items are marked [ASSUMPTION] or as a gap.
- [ ] The gap closure plan has verifiable milestones with a date and a success signal.
- [ ] The maturity verdict is coherent with the ratio of demonstrated vs. gap competencies.
Expected deliverable: six-section promotion dossier, ready to present to the calibration committee, with rubric mapping and objection tables, and an explicit maturity verdict.
spec-liderazgo_desempeno_decision_desvin:
[inputs]
- NOMBRE_O_ROL_PERSONA: {{NOMBRE_O_ROL_PERSONA}} > Person to be terminated, by role or internal name (e.g. "junior analyst on the data team")
- BRECHA_DESEMPENO: {{BRECHA_DESEMPENO}} > What was expected vs. what was observed, with concrete examples, metrics, and period
- HISTORIAL_FEEDBACK_PMP: {{HISTORIAL_FEEDBACK_PMP}} > Prior feedback given, improvement plan applied, deadlines and results (or "no formal plan")
- MARCO_LEGAL_CONTRACTUAL: {{MARCO_LEGAL_CONTRACTUAL}} > Country/jurisdiction, contract type, tenure, and known restrictions (to be validated by an expert)
- COMPOSICION_EQUIPO: {{COMPOSICION_EQUIPO}} > Size, closeness with the person, and workload the team absorbs
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A leader must decide and execute a performance-based termination. The risk is not only legal: a poorly prepared exit humiliates the person, fractures team trust, and leaves the leader exposed. A well-prepared exit protects the dignity of the person leaving, the morale of those remaining, and the legitimacy of the decision. This prompt converts one of the most difficult leadership conversations into a defensible, humane, and clear process: tested decision, scripted conversation, and cared-for team. It does not replace legal counsel or the organization's internal policy.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior people leader with experience in performance evaluation, due process, and conducting exit conversations; combines sound people-management judgment with legal-emotional sensitivity, without replacing formal legal counsel.
Deliver three blocks in this order:
1. DECISION PROOF. Assess the exit's soundness against four pillars: clearly communicated expectations, documented feedback, real improvement opportunity with deadlines, and consistency against comparable cases. For each pillar: status (solid / weak / absent), supporting evidence, and what is missing. Close with a maturity verdict: READY TO EXECUTE / CLOSE GAPS FIRST / STOP, with the minimum actions that change the verdict. Mark with [ASSUMPTION] every inferred gap and declare what must be closed before proceeding.
2. EXIT CONVERSATION SCRIPT. Logistics first (who conducts it, when, where, HR or witness presence, limited duration). Then the script: direct opening without preamble; central message in clear and non-humiliating language; supporting facts; practical terms (effective date, handover, accesses, support); dignity care and respectful close. Append prepared responses for five reactions: denial, anger, emotional breakdown, negotiation ("give me another chance"), and silence.
3. TEAM MESSAGE. What to communicate and what to reserve for confidentiality; how to name the departure without exposing the person; how to contain the anxiety of those remaining; how to redistribute work in a transparent and explicitly temporary way, with a review checkpoint.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: confirm jurisdiction, tenure, history, and team composition; if {{MARCO_LEGAL_CONTRACTUAL}} or {{HISTORIAL_FEEDBACK_PMP}} are incomplete, ask for them before drafting and warn that legal validation belongs to an expert.
Phase 2 - Proof: apply the four due process pillars, substantiate each status with evidence, issue the maturity verdict, and flag weaknesses with [ASSUMPTION].
Phase 3 - Script: draft logistics, script, and responses to the five reactions; firm, brief tone, without euphemisms that confuse or judgments that humiliate; without promises you cannot sustain.
Phase 4 - Team: define the message, the confidentiality line, and the temporary redistribution with a review checkpoint.
Edge cases: if the proof returns STOP, propose the remediation path (formal PIP) before the exit. If there are signals of retaliation, discrimination, medical leave, pregnancy, or protected status, stop and refer to legal/HR expert. Do not invent policies, labor norms, or case facts; every decisive data point not provided is requested or marked [ASSUMPTION].
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reframe what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] All four due process pillars evaluated with status, evidence, and explicit gaps.
- [ ] Maturity verdict issued (ready / close gaps / stop) with actions that change it.
- [ ] Every assumption marked [ASSUMPTION]; no case fact, policy, or norm invented.
- [ ] Script with logistics, direct opening, non-humiliating central message, facts, practical terms, and dignified close.
- [ ] Prepared responses for denial, anger, emotional breakdown, negotiation, and silence.
- [ ] Team message separates communicable from confidential and resolves temporary redistribution with a review checkpoint.
- [ ] Reminder to validate legal matters with an expert and signals that require stopping (protected status, leave, retaliation).
- [ ] Professional, direct tone, without empty euphemisms or moral judgments.
Expected deliverable: three-block operational document (decision proof + conversation script + team communication plan) ready for the leader to use when preparing and conducting the termination.
spec-liderazgo_desempeno_compensacion_co:
[inputs]
- COLABORADOR: {{COLABORADOR}} > Person being communicated to and their context: role, tenure, level/band, recent relationship with their performance, and flight risk if any
- DECISION: {{DECISION}} > The exact compensation decision to communicate: salary adjustment (amount or percentage), bonus, or no raise this cycle; include effective date if applicable
- DESEMPENO: {{DESEMPENO}} > Concrete achievements and behaviors from the period supporting the decision (verifiable facts, not impressions); note gaps if any
- MERCADO_POLITICA: {{MERCADO_POLITICA}} > Where compensation falls against the market or internal band and what policy/budget rule applies this cycle (optional; what is missing is marked [ASSUMPTION], never invented)
- PROXIMOS_PASOS: {{PROXIMOS_PASOS}} > What can and what CANNOT be offered going forward: reviews with date, measurable criteria, development actions, budget or policy limits
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
The leader must communicate to {{COLABORADOR}} the decision {{DECISION}}, and needs the conversation to sustain motivation and trust rather than eroding them. The purpose is to transform sensitive news into an honest and defensible message: a compensation decision well communicated connects pay explicitly with real performance, with the market, and with policy, and leaves the person with clarity about where they stand and what depends on them. What is unlocked is retention through trust (not through a surprise avoided), a relationship that holds even after a "no" this cycle, and a leader protected from the trap of the empty promise that comes due in the next cycle. What is at stake if done poorly: a key person who leaves without warning, a broken equity precedent that contaminates the team, or a verbal commitment that becomes an enforceable debt. EstrategIA brings the rigor of anchoring an emotional conversation in verifiable evidence.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior people leader, expert in Total Rewards philosophy, pay-for-performance models, salary bands and pay equity, and conducting difficult compensation conversations.
Deliver the following, in this order:
1. Reframe the decision in one sentence: "Communicate to {{COLABORADOR}} that {{DECISION}}, because [reason anchored in performance / market / policy]".
2. Classify the case into a scenario: (a) positive adjustment, (b) adjustment smaller than expected or none despite good performance, (c) no adjustment due to insufficient performance or budget/policy restriction; adapt tone and order to the scenario and declare which scenario you chose and why.
3. Build the message on three separate anchors from {{DESEMPENO}} and {{MERCADO_POLITICA}}: PERFORMANCE (period facts), MARKET (position against a reference or band), POLICY/BUDGET (cycle rule); explicitly distinguish what depends on the person from what does not. Mark [ASSUMPTION] for every figure, percentile, or rule not provided; do not invent data.
4. Draft the conversation script: opening with the decision in the first few sentences, the why using the three anchors, explicit space for reaction and questions (with a suggested open-ended question), close with next steps. Use direct language without euphemisms that dilute the message.
5. From {{PROXIMOS_PASOS}}, separate verifiable commitments (review with date, measurable criteria, development actions) from empty promises to avoid; rewrite every fragile promise as a conditional and measurable commitment (format: if [observable condition] by [date], then [concrete action]).
6. Anticipate 3 to 5 probable objections or reactions (include at least: comparison with a peer, resignation threat, request to review the decision now) with a brief, empathetic, and firm response for each that does not concede indefensible ground or break third-party confidentiality.
7. Close with a preparation checklist for the leader: data at hand, what NOT to say (including peer comparisons and unsupported promises), how to document the conversation, and who to escalate to if there is an equity/legal signal.
Stop signal: if the decision appears to violate internal equity, contradict current policy, or touch legal or confidentiality ground, declare it before continuing and recommend validating with HR/legal.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: fix the decision in one sentence and validate that person, exact decision, period performance, and market/policy reference exist; if an essential data point is missing, ask for it before executing and do not invent figures or rules.
Phase 2 - Classification: place the case in one of the three scenarios and derive from it the tone and message order (in (a) recognition precedes the amount; in (b) and (c) the decision comes first and context follows, without preamble).
Phase 3 - Triple anchor: draft performance, market, and policy separately, declaring what the person controls and what they do not, and marking [ASSUMPTION] for what is not verified.
Phase 4 - Script: structure a direct opening, why, listening space, and close, with language that does not dilute the message.
Phase 5 - Next steps and robustness: convert fragile promises into conditional and measurable commitments, anticipate objections, run the equity/legal check, and assemble the preparation checklist.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reframe what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
- The decision was reframed in one sentence with its primary reason before drafting the script.
- The case is classified into one of the three scenarios, with justification, and tone and order are adapted to it.
- The message explicitly separates the three anchors: performance (facts), market (position), and policy/budget (rule), and distinguishes what is controllable from what is not.
- Every market figure, percentile, or policy not provided is marked [ASSUMPTION]; no data was invented.
- The script opens with the decision in the first few sentences, includes space for reaction with at least one open-ended question, and does not use euphemisms that dilute the message.
- Next steps distinguish verifiable commitments from empty promises; every fragile promise was rewritten as a conditional and measurable commitment.
- There are 3 to 5 anticipated objections, each with an empathetic and firm response that does not concede indefensible ground or break third-party confidentiality.
- The preparation checklist includes data at hand, what NOT to say, how to document, and who to escalate to.
- If there was an equity, policy, or legal signal, it was declared as a stop before proceeding.
Expected deliverable: compensation conversation script by scenario + triple anchor (performance/market/policy) + verifiable next steps, bank of 3 to 5 objections, and preparation checklist, in neutral English, professional, warm, and direct tone, without empty promises.
spec-liderazgo_desempeno_feedback_contin:
[inputs]
- EQUIPO_TAMANO_TIPO: {{EQUIPO_TAMANO_TIPO}} > Team size and nature (e.g., 12 people, remote engineering)
