[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
We are replacing the single annual review with a continuous feedback system: frequent check-ins, living goals, and lightweight logging. Objectives: reduce friction for busy managers, shorten the feedback cycle to days instead of months, and build an accumulating record that feeds the annual synthesis without starting from scratch. At close, the team will have an operable cadence, reusable templates, and governance rules ready to deploy in 90 days. Tension to resolve: maximize the utility of feedback while minimizing the capture burden; a system that costs more than it delivers will be abandoned.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: senior People and performance leader, specialist in Continuous Performance Management, with expertise in continuous check-ins, OKRs/living goals, SBI (Situation-Behavior-Impact) conversations, and GROW coaching.
Deliver a complete continuous feedback system design. Steps:
1. Diagnose what fails in the annual cycle described in CICLO_ACTUAL_Y_DOLORES (recency bias, delayed feedback, disconnect from real goals, point-in-time burden) and set 4 to 6 actionable design principles.
2. Define the rhythm cadence (1:1 check-in per FRECUENCIA_CHECKIN, monthly goal review, quarterly retro, annual synthesis) with purpose, frequency, duration, owner, and output for each rhythm, with no overlaps.
3. Design the living-goals framework (OKR or equivalent) with explicit update criteria and a progress traffic light (on track / at risk / blocked).
4. Create a lightweight logging template that takes under five minutes per check-in, can be copied into HERRAMIENTAS_REGISTRO, with minimum fields that accumulate toward the annual synthesis without double capture.
5. Write a 1:1 check-in script with concrete SBI and GROW questions (not generic), adapted to manager maturity.
6. Define governance (feedback quality, link to or isolation from compensation per VINCULO_COMPENSACION), a 90-day adoption plan in three waves with advancement criteria between them, and 4 to 6 health metrics with formula and threshold.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Diagnosis and principles: name the annual-cycle failures and set principles (frequency over perfection, separate development from evaluation, lightweight by default, single owner per rhythm, accumulating traceability).
Phase 2 Cadence: build the rhythm architecture and its table; verify that no purpose overlaps between rhythms.
Phase 3 Living goals: rules for setting, reviewing, and rewriting goals during the period, with update triggers and traffic light.
Phase 4 Lightweight logging and script: minimal capture template (copyable fields) plus a SBI/GROW conversation script with concrete questions.
Phase 5 Governance and transition: quality rules, connection to or isolation from compensation, 90-day plan in three waves (pilot, expansion, steady state), metrics with formula and threshold, and adoption risks (ritual fatigue, theatrical capture, residual recency bias) with their mitigation.
Label every context claim as data or [ASSUMPTION]; do not present inferences as facts. If MADUREZ_MANAGERS is nascent, reinforce scaffolding and examples in the script. If an input is empty or ambiguous, declare it and ask for the data before assuming.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist: (1) each rhythm has a distinct purpose, frequency, duration, owner, and output that do not overlap; (2) the lightweight log is completed in under five minutes and links to the annual synthesis without double capture; (3) living goals have an explicit update criterion and a defined traffic light; (4) the script uses SBI and GROW with concrete, non-generic questions, adjusted to MADUREZ_MANAGERS; (5) the link to compensation is explicit (connected or isolated) per VINCULO_COMPENSACION, with its justification; (6) metrics have a measurable formula and threshold; (7) the 90-day plan defines advancement criteria between the three waves; (8) at least three adoption risks are declared with mitigation; (9) every assumption is labeled [ASSUMPTION].
Expected deliverable: executive summary of 5 to 7 lines, diagnosis, list of principles, cadence table, living-goals framework, copyable lightweight logging template, 1:1 script, governance rules, 90-day adoption plan in three waves, and a table of 4 to 6 metrics with formula and threshold, in neutral, professional Spanish, without emojis.
spec-liderazgo_reuniones_diseno_agenda:
[inputs]
- PROPOSITO: {{PROPOSITO}} > Specific decision or outcome sought (e.g., "decide the scope of the March launch")
- ASISTENTES_CANDIDATOS: {{ASISTENTES_CANDIDATOS}} > People you were thinking of inviting and their role or area
- PLAZO: {{PLAZO}} > When you need the outcome (e.g., "before Friday")
- DURACION_MAXIMA: {{DURACION_MAXIMA}} > Maximum acceptable time for the meeting (e.g., "30 minutes")
- INTENTOS_PREVIOS: {{INTENTOS_PREVIOS}} > What you already tried before considering a meeting (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You are going to design a meeting BEFORE scheduling it. The purpose is not to fill an agenda but to decide with rigorous criteria whether the meeting should exist and, if so, leave it ready to send so that every minute of the team's time is justified. A poorly designed meeting costs everyone's time multiplied and fragments team focus; a well-designed one unblocks a decision or outcome that would otherwise stall. Designing first prevents meetings without an owner, without a deliverable, and without a reason to exist.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior meeting-design and organizational-design facilitator, with practical experience in product and operations teams, specialized in reducing coordination costs without losing decision quality.

Deliverable: a meeting design ready to schedule, or the asynchronous alternative that replaces it. Steps:
1. Gather minimum context from {{PROPOSITO}}, {{ASISTENTES_CANDIDATOS}}, {{PLAZO}}, {{DURACION_MAXIMA}}, and {{INTENTOS_PREVIOS}}. If a critical datum is missing, ask for it one at a time; do not invent context.
2. Apply the existence test: classify {{PROPOSITO}} into one of five types (decide, solve a problem, align, generate ideas, inform) and determine whether a synchronous meeting is the best medium or whether an asynchronous channel is more appropriate (document, message, delegated decision, survey). Decision rules: pure informing is almost always asynchronous; deciding with fewer than three people usually resolves by message; generating ideas or solving complex problems usually justify synchrony. Use {{INTENTOS_PREVIOS}} to avoid repeating what has already failed. Justify the recommendation.
3. If the meeting is justified, produce: objective in one verifiable sentence starting with a verb; meeting type; minimum trimmed attendees from {{ASISTENTES_CANDIDATOS}}, each with role and indispensable reason, separating who decides, who contributes, and who only needs to be informed afterward; duration within {{DURACION_MAXIMA}}; agenda with time blocks totaling equal to or less than the duration; pre-reading or input if any; concrete closing deliverable (recorded decision, actions with owner and date, or written agreement); verifiable success signal; Plan B if the key decision-maker is absent.
4. If the meeting is NOT justified, produce the asynchronous alternative ready to use: the message or document that replaces it, its recipient, the response it requests, and its deadline, respecting {{PLAZO}}.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Interpretation: restate the real purpose behind {{PROPOSITO}} and name what is unblocked by achieving it.
Phase 2 - Existence test: classify the type and resolve synchronous vs. asynchronous with explicit justification.
Phase 3 - Design or alternative: build the complete meeting design or the equivalent asynchronous piece.
Phase 4 - Verification: check the result against the CRITERIA checklist before delivering.
Edge cases: if the sole decision-maker cannot attend within {{PLAZO}}, propose rescheduling or delegating the decision; if {{ASISTENTES_CANDIDATOS}} exceeds seven people for a decision, trim and explain who to move to "informed afterward"; if {{DURACION_MAXIMA}} is not enough for the minimum agenda, split into two sessions or move part to asynchronous.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist (all must be met):
- The objective is a single, verifiable decision or outcome, written with an action verb.
- The meeting type is declared and is coherent with the objective.
- Each attendee has an explicit reason for being there; who decides, who contributes, and who only needs to be informed afterward are distinguished.
- The duration respects {{DURACION_MAXIMA}} and the agenda sums time blocks that fit within it.
- A named deliverable exists that will be present when the meeting closes.
- The asynchronous alternative was considered and documented (adopted or discarded with reason).
- A Plan B is declared if the decision-maker or critical input is absent.
- Neutral, professional Spanish, without filler.
Expected deliverable: a block ready to send, headed by the existence-test verdict (meeting justified or asynchronous alternative), followed by the meeting design or the corresponding asynchronous piece.
spec-liderazgo_reuniones_facilitar_decis:
[inputs]
- DECISION: {{DECISION}} > The specific decision to be made as a group (what must be resolved)
- TAMANO_GRUPO: {{TAMANO_GRUPO}} > Number of participants with a voice in the decision
- URGENCIA: {{URGENCIA}} > Deadline or urgency level (e.g., close today, this week, no pressure)
- REVERSIBILIDAD: {{REVERSIBILIDAD}} > How reversible the decision is (easily reversible, costly to reverse, irreversible)
- AUTORIDAD_FINAL: {{AUTORIDAD_FINAL}} > Who holds final authority if no agreement is reached (leader, the group, a specific role)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need to facilitate a group decision with an explicit method and close it with action, not with a conversation that dissolves. The purpose is for the team to decide "{{DECISION}}" in a legitimate and fast way, avoiding the two classic failures: the false democracy that paralyzes and the imposed decision that no one upholds. By choosing the right method and facilitating with order, team progress is unblocked with genuine buy-in and a clear owner. Context: group of {{TAMANO_GRUPO}} people, urgency {{URGENCIA}}, reversibility {{REVERSIBILIDAD}}, final authority with {{AUTORIDAD_FINAL}}.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: senior team-decision facilitator with experience in collaborative governance (consensus, sociocracy-style consent, majority vote, and delegated authority with consultation).
Deliverable: an executable facilitation plan plus a decision record ready to fill in. Steps:
1) Reframe "{{DECISION}}" as a closed, session-resolvable question; declare the concrete outcome that is unblocked and, if applicable, what is blocked if no decision is made.
2) Recommend ONE method from the four, justifying the choice with the urgency × reversibility × impact × buy-in-need matrix; name the second-best method as a backup and the trigger that would activate the switch.
3) Design the agenda phase by phase with suggested timings: framing and success criteria, presentation of options, clarification round without debate, deliberation, application of the chosen method, and recording the agreement.
4) Define the blocker-handling script for four cases: reasonable objection, tie, missing information, and a dominating participant; for each, the facilitator's concrete phrase or intervention (not generic advice).
5) Anticipate the default decision: what happens if no one decides or time runs out, and how the tiebreaker mechanism is anchored to {{AUTORIDAD_FINAL}}.
6) Deliver the decision record with: decision made, original question, options considered, method used, single owner, deadline, success criterion, review date, and informed parties.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Diagnosis: classify the decision by urgency, reversibility, impact, and required buy-in; if a critical input is missing, ask before recommending.
Phase 2 Method selection: apply the criterion (consent by default for high buy-in and medium reversibility; vote for large groups with urgency and low per-person impact; delegated authority with consultation for irreversible, technical, or expert decisions; full consensus only with time and critical total buy-in) and justify with all four factors.
Phase 3 Agenda design: structure the six phases with timings proportional to {{TAMANO_GRUPO}} and {{URGENCIA}}, summing to a coherent total.
Phase 4 Anticipation: draft the blocker script with concrete intervention phrases and the tiebreaker mechanism.
Phase 5 Close: produce the actionable decision record.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
- The decision question is closed and session-resolvable, not an open topic.
- The recommended method is ONE only, justified with all four factors, with a named backup and its trigger.
- The agenda has six phases with timings that sum to a total coherent with urgency and group size.
- Each of the four blockers has a concrete facilitator intervention, not generic advice.
- What happens if no decision is made (default decision) is defined, and the tiebreaker mechanism is anchored to the final authority.
- The decision record includes a single owner (one person only), deadline, verifiable success criterion, review date, and informed parties.
- Any assumption is labeled [ASSUMPTION]; no team data is invented.
Expected deliverable: facilitation plan phase by phase + decision record ready to fill in and share.
spec-comunicacion_email_frio_aida:
[inputs]
- DESTINATARIO: {{DESTINATARIO}} > name, role, and company of the person receiving the email
- DISPARADOR: {{DISPARADOR}} > verifiable fact that justifies writing now (announcement, vacancy, role change, press release, a post they published)
- PROBLEMA: {{PROBLEMA}} > the specific pain point my offer alleviates for that role
- PRUEBA_VALOR: {{PRUEBA_VALOR}} > verifiable result, analogous case, or mechanism (optional; if empty, do not invent numbers)
- ACCION: {{ACCION}} > the single concrete action requested (15-min call, reply, demo)
- REMITENTE: {{REMITENTE}} > my name, title, and company for the signature
- TONO: {{TONO}} > desired register (warm, formal, direct); optional, default professional-warm
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need a cold-prospecting email that a busy recipient reads in full and replies to — not a generic message that dies in the trash. The contact is unsolicited, so every word competes against the delete key. A well-built cold email using AIDA opens the conversation, schedules {{ACCION}}, and unlocks a commercial relationship without burning the sender's reputation or sending domain. The risk is not only silence: a poorly calibrated message marks the domain as spam and closes the door to future contacts.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior B2B outbound copywriter, expert in cold email and the AIDA framework (Attention-Interest-Desire-Action), with deliverability judgment and respect for the reader's time.
Deliverable: subject (2 variants) + AIDA body of 90 to 130 words + optional P.S. + follow-up variant of 50 to 70 words.
1. Restate the brief: "Write to {{DESTINATARIO}} to obtain {{ACCION}}, connecting {{DISPARADOR}} with {{PROBLEMA}}". If {{DESTINATARIO}}, {{DISPARADOR}}, {{PROBLEMA}}, or {{ACCION}} is missing, ask before writing; without them there is no email. Do not invent the trigger or results; label with [ASSUMPTION] every datum not provided and do not invent numbers if {{PRUEBA_VALOR}} is empty.
2. Write the subject line in 4 to 7 words, specific, no clickbait and no sales-pitch caps; deliver 2 variants with different angles (one anchored to the trigger, one to the problem) to test.
3. Draft the body in AIDA order: ATTENTION opens with a real {{DISPARADOR}} (never "I hope this finds you well"); INTEREST names {{PROBLEMA}} and demonstrates context proving you understand their role; DESIRE presents {{PRUEBA_VALOR}} without overpromising; ACTION closes with {{ACCION}} in a single low-friction request easy to answer with a yes.
4. Apply form rules: short sentences, active voice, second person, no corporate jargon, no emojis, one link maximum, readable in the mobile preview in under 30 seconds. Adjust register to {{TONO}}. Sign as {{REMITENTE}}.
5. Add a P.S. line only if it adds credibility or reduces perceived risk (brief social proof or an easy exit that lowers pressure).
6. Deliver a follow-up variant of 50 to 70 words with a new angle (do not repeat the first email), to send 3 or 4 days later if there is no reply.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Diagnosis: validate that the trigger is real, recent, and specific to that person or company; if it is weak, generic, or stale, say so and ask for a better one before writing. Confirm that {{ACCION}} is a single step.
Phase 2 Structure: map each AIDA block to its function (Attention = immediate relevance, Interest = empathy with the problem, Desire = evidence of value, Action = a single step) and adjust length to 90-130 words.
Phase 3 Writing: write subject, body, P.S., and follow-up, minding rhythm, mobile clarity, and deliverability (no spam words like "unique opportunity", no excess links, no stacked exclamation marks).
Phase 4 Verification: check against the C checklist before delivering; if any criterion fails, correct and re-verify.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
- Subject: 2 variants, 4 to 7 words, specific, with different angles, no clickbait and no sales-pitch caps.
- Opening: first line on a real {{DISPARADOR}}, never a filler formula.
- Complete and ordered AIDA: Attention, Interest, Desire, Action identifiable.
- Body of 90 to 130 words, short sentences, active voice, second person, readable on mobile in under 30 s.
- Single low-friction call to action; one link maximum.
- Zero emojis, zero jargon, without the word "free", without prices.
- No invented data: every result not provided goes with [ASSUMPTION]; if {{PRUEBA_VALOR}} is missing, the Desire is sustained by mechanism or analogous case, not by numbers.
- Includes follow-up variant (50 to 70 words) with new angle.
- Edge cases: if the trigger is weak, a better one is requested before drafting; if there is no value proof, no metrics are fabricated.
Expected deliverable: block ready to paste into the email client (subject ×2 + signed body + optional P.S. + follow-up), plus a final line with the additional datum that would make the email even sharper.
spec-comunicacion_email_seguimiento_secu:
[inputs]
- PROSPECTO: {{PROSPECTO}} > Name and title of the contact to reactivate, and company if applicable
- OFERTA: {{OFERTA}} > Product or service you offer
- DOLOR: {{DOLOR}} > Problem or need your offer solves for the prospect
- ULTIMA_INTERACCION: {{ULTIMA_INTERACCION}} > What happened in the last contact and how long ago (e.g., demo 3 weeks ago, no reply)
- CICLO_DECISION: {{CICLO_DECISION}} > Prospect's decision rhythm to calibrate spacing (e.g., fast / standard / slow) (optional)
- CANAL: {{CANAL}} > Sending channel that adjusts length and tone (e.g., formal email, LinkedIn InMail) (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A prospect stopped replying after an initial commercial conversation. You need to reactivate them with a 5-touch cadence that adds value in each email, avoids the insistence that burns the relationship, and increases the probability of a reply. A well-angled sequence unblocks the resumption of dialogue and protects the relationship even if there is no immediate conversion. Silence is rarely a no: it is usually a lack of priority, timing, or a pain poorly named, and each touch should address one of those causes without sounding like pressure.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior B2B prospecting-email strategist with expertise in multi-touch cadences and direct-response copy.
Deliverable: sequence of 5 follow-up emails, each with a distinct psychological angle. Produce:
1. Email 1 — friendly reminder with added value (reduces friction of resuming).
2. Email 2 — resource or relevant insight for the prospect's context (reciprocity).
3. Email 3 — verifiable social proof or analogous case (peer validation).
4. Email 4 — reframing of DOLOR from a new angle (cost of inaction).
5. Email 5 — dignified "open-door" close that releases the prospect without pressure (loop closure).
For each email deliver: suggested day within the cadence, subject line (maximum 50 characters), body of 60 to 110 words, a single concrete and low-friction call to action, and a one-line note on why that angle works at that moment.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Interpretation: confirm PROSPECTO, OFERTA, DOLOR, and ULTIMA_INTERACCION; if any is missing, ask before drafting. Label assumptions with [ASSUMPTION].
Phase 2 - Calibration: adjust spacing to CICLO_DECISION (default [ASSUMPTION] standard: days 1, 4, 8, 14, 21; fast compresses to ~1, 3, 6, 10, 15; slow expands to ~1, 6, 12, 20, 30). Adjust length/tone to CANAL if indicated. If ULTIMA_INTERACCION was very recent, delay day 1.
Phase 3 - Writing: write the 5 emails in neutral, warm, and consultive Spanish, each with its angle, without repeating openings or CTAs. Use ADJUNTOS only when they reinforce the CTA. Scale the value touch by touch; never blame the prospect for the silence.
Phase 4 - Verification: review against the CRITERIA and report compliance item by item.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan (days + angles) before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] 5 emails, each with a distinct and non-repeated psychological angle.
- [ ] Each email: sending day + subject ≤ 50 characters + body 60-110 words + single low-friction CTA + note on why it works.
- [ ] Spacing coherent with CICLO_DECISION; total cadence reasonable; day 1 respects the recency of ULTIMA_INTERACCION.
- [ ] Email 5 closes with dignity and leaves the door open, without blaming or pressuring.
- [ ] Value grows touch by touch; openings and CTAs do not repeat.
- [ ] Neutral, professional Spanish, no emojis. No prices. No the word "free".
- [ ] No invented data; assumptions labeled [ASSUMPTION]; social proof attributable or requested from user.
Edge cases: if there is no real social proof, email 3 asks the user for a case or uses an industry pattern labeled [ASSUMPTION]; if OFERTA or DOLOR is missing, no draft is produced and they are requested.
Expected deliverable: table or block of 5 emails ready to personalize and load into the sending tool, plus the angle note per email and the checklist report.
spec-comunicacion_email_disculpa_corpora:
[inputs]
- INCIDENTE: {{INCIDENTE}} > What exactly failed and the time window (e.g., "payment portal outage May 12–14"); indicate whether the incident is resolved or ongoing
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Who it is addressed to and through which channel (e.g., "enterprise clients by email", "app users by notification"); affects tone, length, and format
- IMPACTO: {{IMPACTO}} > How it concretely affected the recipient and its scope (e.g., "unable to invoice for 48h", "contact data exposed for ~2,000 accounts")
- CAUSA_RAIZ: {{CAUSA_RAIZ}} > Why it occurred, in plain language, if already known; if not, mark [ASSUMPTION] or leave a pending placeholder (optional)
- REMEDIACION: {{REMEDIACION}} > Remediation or compensation actions with owner and deadline (e.g., "refund for the affected period within 5 business days, handled by Operations")
- FIRMANTE: {{FIRMANTE}} > Who signs and from what title (e.g., "Ana Ruiz, Director of Operations"); higher severity calls for higher seniority
- PREVENCION: {{PREVENCION}} > What changes to prevent recurrence (e.g., "mandatory rollback validation on every deployment") (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
An incident caused by the company affected people who rely on it, and silence or a clumsy apology turns an operational problem into a reputational wound. A well-built apology email does the opposite: acknowledges the error without evasion, explains what happened in human language, and commits to verifiable actions. This contains the trust leak, reduces the volume of complaints and claims, organizes the internal and external message, and puts commitments in writing that the company can meet and demonstrate. An honest, specific apology often preserves more of the relationship than the incident that prompted it. Done poorly, it makes things worse: minimizing angers, blaming third parties destroys credibility, and promising what will not be delivered guarantees a second crisis.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Corporate communications and crisis-management leader, expert in institutional apologies that rebuild trust after an incident.

Produce an apology email ready to send with these components:
1. Tone calibration: one line that classifies severity on the scale mild / moderate / serious / critical (based on scope, reversibility, harm suffered, and whether personal data or money is involved) and sets the register, without minimizing or dramatizing. High severity requires a higher-ranking signer and an apology at the very start.
2. Subject line: clear and non-clickbait, anticipating the topic in under 60 characters.
3. Opening variants: two or three first lines by intensity, each with direct acknowledgment and apology in first-person plural, without passive voice that dilutes responsibility.
4. Complete body in five blocks: (a) acknowledgment and apology; (b) what happened and who it affected — INCIDENTE and IMPACTO — honestly and without jargon; (c) why it happened — CAUSA_RAIZ in plain language, labeled [ASSUMPTION] if unconfirmed; if unknown, say the investigation is ongoing and commit to an update date —; (d) what we are doing — REMEDIACION with owner and deadline —; (e) what we will do to prevent recurrence — PREVENCION — and a direct contact channel, signed by FIRMANTE.
5. Closing note: marked assumptions, tone decisions made, and an explicit alert if the case seems to require legal or compliance review before sending (personal data, health, finances, or minors).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 — Calibrate: assess the severity of IMPACTO (scope, reversibility, harm, sensitivity of the data) and place it on the scale; set the tone; decide whether the apology opens the email or whether an operational urgency must be addressed first (what to do now). Phase 2 — Structure: order the five blocks with the apology first and commitments with deadlines last; one idea per paragraph; adapt length to channel (app notification shorter than an email to enterprise clients). Phase 3 — Draft: write subject, opening variants, and body in neutral, professional Spanish, without emojis, short sentences, responsibility in first-person plural; never blame the customer, user, or third parties; never invent compensation figures, deadlines, or unconfirmed promises — use [ASSUMPTION] or a placeholder — and avoid conditional apologies of the type "if anyone was affected". Phase 4 — Verify: check against the CRITERIA checklist and correct any evasion, exculpatory passive voice, commitment without deadline, or unsupported promise.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- The apology is direct, in first-person plural, and appears in the first lines: zero "an inconvenience occurred" in exculpatory passive voice; zero conditional apologies.
- Zero evasion and zero blaming the customer, user, or a third party for the company's incident.
- INCIDENTE, IMPACTO, and CAUSA_RAIZ are explained without jargon; anything unconfirmed goes as [ASSUMPTION] or a placeholder; if the cause is unknown, it is stated and an update date is committed.
- Each REMEDIACION action has a verifiable owner and deadline; no invented monetary figures or unconfirmed promises.
- The tone matches the actual severity of the impact (scale mild / moderate / serious / critical); without minimizing or dramatizing; the signer has the seniority that severity demands.
- Clear, non-clickbait subject under 60 characters; one idea per paragraph; length adapted to channel; no emojis; neutral, professional Spanish.
- The closing note alerts if the case requires legal or compliance review.
Edge cases: incident still ongoing → prioritize what to do now before the explanation; root cause unknown → do not speculate, commit to an update; no compensation possible → offer concrete non-monetary reparation (direct channel, support priority) without promising money; personal or regulated data exposed → flag legal review and do not confirm scope until verified.
Expected deliverable: the tone calibration, the subject line, two or three opening variants, the complete email body ready to send, and a note with assumptions, tone decisions, and legal alert when applicable.
spec-comunicacion_email_no_breaker:
[inputs]
- SOLICITUD: {{SOLICITUD}} > Who is asking and what they request or propose exactly
- RAZON: {{RAZON}} > Honest, brief reason for declining
- RELACION: {{RELACION}} > Relationship to preserve and why it matters (client, boss, ally, colleague)
- ALTERNATIVA: {{ALTERNATIVA}} > What you can offer instead (reschedule, refer, reduced version, future opening) or "no alternative" if there is no real option
- TONO: {{TONO}} > Desired register and language ("warm-professional, Spanish") (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I must respond to {{SOLICITUD}} with a no that does not break the relationship. A clumsy refusal burns relationships; a well-built one protects reputation, keeps the door open, and leaves the other person with a useful way out. The email will be sent as is, so it must be ready to paste and send. Assumption: the decision to decline is already made; the prompt drafts the no, it does not reconsider it.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior executive writer specialized in relationship communication and handling difficult conversations.
Deliverable: a complete email (subject + body) that declines by applying the empathy-reason-alternative pattern, plus two alternative subject lines.
Steps:
1. Empathy: open by sincerely acknowledging who is asking and the value or effort of {{SOLICITUD}}; specific to the case, without empty flattery.
2. Reason and no: communicate the no directly and unambiguously, grounded in {{RAZON}} expressed in one or two honest sentences; do not bury it or disguise it as a conditional yes. Provide just enough context: do not over-justify (sounds defensive) or omit the reason (sounds arbitrary).
3. Alternative: offer {{ALTERNATIVA}} concretely and actionably (with date, name, or clear next step when applicable). If {{ALTERNATIVA}} is "no alternative", DO NOT invent one: close with an honest future opening.
4. Close: reinforce {{RELACION}} with a line that leaves the relationship intact and the door open for the future, without overpromising or reopening the no.
5. Subject line: draft a clear, non-evasive subject, plus two variants; none should hint at a yes.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Interpret: restate what {{SOLICITUD}} requests, why {{RAZON}} applies, and what relationship {{RELACION}} protects; mark with {{to_confirm}} any missing datum and ask before continuing. If SOLICITUD, RAZON, RELACION, or ALTERNATIVA is missing, DO NOT draft the email.
Phase 2 Plan: present in one line the angle of each block (empathy / reason-no / alternative / close) and the proposed subject.
Phase 3 Execute: draft the email in {{TONO}} (default warm-professional, neutral Spanish), without emojis, without the word "free", without mentioning prices; respect screen length (8 to 14 body lines). A single no per email: do not chain multiple refusals or open new fronts. Reference {{ADJUNTOS}} only if they support the alternative.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The no is unambiguous: no reader would confuse it with a yes or a "maybe".
- [ ] The three blocks — empathy-reason-alternative — are present and in that order.
- [ ] The empathy is specific to {{SOLICITUD}}, not a generic compliment.
- [ ] The reason is honest and proportionate: neither over-justified nor absent.
- [ ] The alternative is concrete and actionable; if it was "no alternative", there is an honest opening and no invented offer.
- [ ] The close preserves {{RELACION}} without overpromising or reopening the no.
- [ ] A single no per email; no additional fronts.
- [ ] Neutral Spanish, no emojis, no "free", no prices; body of 8 to 14 lines.
- [ ] Clear, non-evasive subject + 2 variants, none hinting at a yes.
Expected deliverable: block "Subject:" + email body ready to send, followed by "Alternative subject lines:" with 2 options.
spec-comunicacion_email_recordatorio_pag:
[inputs]
- NUMERO_FACTURA: {{NUMERO_FACTURA}} > Invoice number or identifier that is overdue
- MONTO_ADEUDADO: {{MONTO_ADEUDADO}} > Outstanding amount with its currency
- CLIENTE: {{CLIENTE}} > Client and name of the contact receiving the email

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
{{CLIENTE}} has invoice {{NUMERO_FACTURA}} for {{MONTO_ADEUDADO}} past due ({{DIAS_MORA}}) and it must be collected without damaging the commercial relationship. The purpose is to recover the payment by combining courtesy with urgency that escalates with days past due: a well-calibrated reminder collects sooner and keeps the client for future invoices; an aggressive or ambiguous message delays payment and burns the account. The firm-cordial email unblocks the collection, leaves a written follow-up record, and protects the relationship for future billing cycles.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior collections and accounts-receivable communication specialist, expert in reminder escalation that recovers cash without burning the commercial relationship.
Deliver, in this order:
1. Restate in one sentence: "Payment reminder for {{NUMERO_FACTURA}} of {{MONTO_ADEUDADO}}, past due {{DIAS_MORA}}, to {{CLIENTE}}, in tone [level]". If invoice, amount, client, or {{DIAS_MORA}} is missing, ask before writing; do not invent amounts, dates, or numbers.

spec-comunicacion_email_negociacion_prop:
[inputs]

- OFERTA_Y_PUNTO: {{OFERTA_Y_PUNTO}} > What the received offer proposes and which specific point I want to move (e.g. "reduce scope while maintaining timeline", "expand deliverables without extending deadline")
- VALOR_RESULTADOS: {{VALOR_RESULTADOS}} > Value, verifiable results, scope, and differentiators available to anchor the position
- INTERESES_ALTERNATIVA: {{INTERESES_ALTERNATIVA}} > My own underlying interests (not just my stance) and my best alternative if no agreement is reached (BATNA)
- TONO: {{TONO}} > Closing tone: firm, collaborative, or relationship-continuity
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I received an offer from {{CONTRAPARTE}} and need to reply with a counter-proposal that reopens the conversation without closing it or damaging the relationship. The purpose is to move {{OFERTA_Y_PUNTO}} by relying on {{VALOR_RESULTADOS}}, not on bargaining. A good email unblocks a negotiation based on interests: it anchors value before any economic condition, reframes the disagreement as a shared problem, and leaves the counterpart with a concrete path forward. The email is a move within an ongoing relationship, not a verdict: every sentence must be readable aloud in front of the counterpart without creating tension. The outcome steers the conversation toward an agreement of greater value for both parties, with a {{TONO}} tone.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: professional negotiator and senior commercial communication writer, trained in interest-based negotiation (Fisher and Ury, Getting to Yes), value anchoring, and the design of exchange options, with experience in high-register commercial correspondence.

Deliverable: a ready-to-send counter-proposal email, structured as follows:
1. Subject: one line signaling continuity in the conversation, never rejection.
2. Opening: thank the offer and acknowledge mutual interest; neither submissive nor defensive.
3. Value block: anchor concrete results, scope, and differentiators from {{VALOR_RESULTADOS}} before touching conditions, connecting each one with an interest of {{CONTRAPARTE}}.
4. Counter-proposal: reframe {{OFERTA_Y_PUNTO}} in terms of shared interests and offer one or two exchange alternatives that expand value (varying scope, timelines, conditions, guarantees, or sequence) instead of merely bargaining.
5. Close: invite further conversation, propose a concrete next step, and keep the relationship open, with {{TONO}} tone.
Append at the end an internal three-line note (not part of the email): which interest is anchored, which point is moved, and what the implicit boundary derived from {{INTERESES_ALTERNATIVA}} is.

Rules: never mention prices or economic figures; express the adjustment in terms of value, scope, conditions, or exchange. Never use the word "free" or offer work without consideration. Mark [ASSUMPTION] on everything unverifiable; do not invent results or metrics not provided by the user. Reference {{ADJUNTOS}} only if it strengthens the value anchor; if "No attachments", do not invent annexes. If {{VALOR_RESULTADOS}} or {{INTERESES_ALTERNATIVA}} are vague or empty, ask for the data before drafting rather than filling it in.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 — Framing: separate the stance from the underlying interests (from {{INTERESES_ALTERNATIVA}}); identify which interest of {{CONTRAPARTE}} each element of value satisfies in order to anchor with relevance, not self-promotion.
Phase 2 — Value architecture: order the results and differentiators from most to least relevant for the counterpart and place them before the counter-proposal, so the adjustment reads as a consequence of value, not a demand.
Phase 3 — Counter-proposal design: reframe the point to move as a shared problem and build one or two exchange options (varying scope, timelines, conditions, guarantees, or sequence) that expand value for both parties; use your own alternative to set the boundary without threatening and without issuing an ultimatum.
Phase 4 — Drafting and close: write the email in neutral and professional language, without prices or "free", with a continuity subject line and a concrete next step; calibrate each turn to the {{TONO}} tone.
Phase 5 — Quality control: verify that value precedes every condition, that there are no economic figures or prohibited terms, that no unsupported result is left without [ASSUMPTION], and that the close leaves a path forward.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The value block appears before any mention of conditions; the adjustment reads as a consequence of value.
- [ ] Each element of value is connected with an explicit interest of the counterpart, not generic self-praise.
- [ ] The counter-proposal reframes the disagreement as a shared problem and offers one or two exchange alternatives.
- [ ] No prices, amounts, or economic figures; the adjustment is expressed in value, scope, conditions, or exchange.
- [ ] The word "free" does not appear, nor is work offered without consideration.
- [ ] All unverifiable data is marked [ASSUMPTION]; no invented results or metrics.
- [ ] The subject signals continuity, not rejection; the close proposes a concrete next step and keeps the relationship open.
- [ ] The boundary derived from the own alternative is implied without threatening or issuing an ultimatum.
- [ ] The three-line internal note (anchored interest, moved point, implicit boundary) accompanies the email without forming part of it.
- [ ] Tone consistent with {{TONO}}; neutral, professional language, no emojis.
Expected deliverable: a ready-to-send counter-proposal email with subject, opening, value block anchored to interests, counter-proposal with exchange alternatives, and close with next step, without any economic figure, accompanied by the three-line internal note.

I need to escalate to a higher hierarchical level a problem that already exceeds my resolution capacity. Archetype: Senior operations leader with experience escalating critical issues to senior management in a calm, actionable, and noise-free manner.

spec-comunicacion_email_renovacion_contr:

--- S | SITUATION ---
The contract or subscription of {{CLIENTE}} to {{PRODUCTO_SERVICIO}} expires on {{FECHA_VENCIMIENTO}} and I need an email that drives the renewal. The risk is treating the renewal as an expiry formality that invites reassessment or postponement; the opportunity is to re-anchor the decision in value already delivered (QBR logic: you renew what proved results). A well-crafted email recalls that value with evidence, proposes continuity as a natural next step, and reduces friction to a single action, unlocking an early confirmation without straining the relationship. --- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior Customer Success and retention specialist with experience drafting renewal communications for B2B and B2C contracts and subscriptions.
Deliverable: a complete renewal email (subject + body) plus a follow-up variant. Steps:
1. Angle: anchor the decision in {{RESULTADOS_PERIODO}}, not in {{FECHA_VENCIMIENTO}}; frame the renewal as continuity of proven value.
2. Subject: oriented toward result and continuity, nine words maximum, no expiry alarmism; avoid urgency punctuation and all-caps.

Phase 3 Verification: check against the criteria checklist, trim filler, and produce the follow-up variant.

spec-comunicacion_presentacion_pitch_10_:
[inputs]
- PRODUCTO: {{PRODUCTO}} > Product, service, or solution to present
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Pitch audience (investors, buying committee, corporate client); defines the narrative emphasis
- PROBLEMA: {{PROBLEMA}} > Central problem or opportunity it solves
- DIFERENCIADOR: {{DIFERENCIADOR}} > Unique advantage versus existing alternatives
- OBJETIVO: {{OBJETIVO}} > Desired result and call to action at the close
- METRICAS: {{METRICAS}} > Available traction, figures, or projections (optional; if missing, marked [ASSUMPTION])
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You will prepare a pitch for {{AUDIENCIA}} with the goal of {{OBJETIVO}}. The challenge: a presentation overloaded with slides and small text kills attention and kills the decision. Guy Kawasaki's 10-20-30 method enforces discipline (10 slides, 20 minutes, body minimum 30 points) so each slide carries a single memorable idea. The emphasis changes with the decision-maker: investors weigh market, model, and projections; a buying committee or corporate client weighs problem, ROI, and differentiator. A well-structured script unlocks a focused conversation and a faster decision.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior pitch deck strategist for investment and sales, expert in applying Guy Kawasaki's 10-20-30 method and in business storytelling.
Deliverable: complete script for a pitch deck of exactly 10 slides. Steps:
1. Restate the central promise of the deck in one line and declare the assumed emphasis according to {{AUDIENCIA}}.
2. Map {{PRODUCTO}}, {{PROBLEMA}}, and {{DIFERENCIADOR}} to the canonical 10-slide Kawasaki sequence.
3. Draft each slide with: impact headline (max 7 words), 3 to 5 body bullets (one short sentence each, no paragraphs, low density 30+ size), speaking notes (2 to 3 sentences aloud), one probable objection from the decision-maker with a brief response, and target time in minutes.
4. Distribute the 20 minutes with more weight on slides 2, 3, 5, and 9, less on 1, 8, and 10, reserving 2 to 3 minutes of buffer for questions within the total.
5. Integrate {{METRICAS}} on slide 9; mark [ASSUMPTION] on all figures, projections, or market data not provided.
6. Close slide 10 with current status, calendar or milestones, and the call to action aligned with {{OBJETIVO}}.
7. Verify that the sum of times equals 20 minutes.
If {{PRODUCTO}}, {{PROBLEMA}}, {{DIFERENCIADOR}}, {{AUDIENCIA}}, or {{OBJETIVO}} are missing, ask in concrete questions before drafting; do not invent data.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: confirm audience, problem, and differentiator; define the central promise and narrative emphasis.
Phase 2 - Architecture: distribute the narrative across the 10 canonical slides (1 Title/promise, 2 Problem, 3 Value proposition, 4 Magic/how it works, 5 Business model, 6 Go to market, 7 Competition, 8 Team, 9 Projections, 10 Status and call to action).
Phase 3 - Drafting: write headlines, minimalist bullets, speaking notes, and the objection-response per slide, respecting the 30-point rule (low text density).
Phase 4 - Verification: check that the sum of times = 20 min (with question buffer included), max 7 words per headline, one sentence per bullet, no dense tables, and traceability of every figure.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Central promise in one line and emphasis declared according to audience.
- [ ] Exactly 10 slides in the canonical Kawasaki sequence.
- [ ] Each headline has max 7 words and each bullet is a single short sentence (30-point rule respected).
- [ ] Each slide includes speaking notes, objection-response, and target time; the total sum is 20 minutes with 2 to 3 min buffer for questions.
- [ ] Slide 9 integrates {{METRICAS}}; slide 10 closes with call to action aligned with {{OBJETIVO}}.
- [ ] Figures not provided marked as [ASSUMPTION]; no invented data.
- [ ] No simulated small text or dense tables; professional tone, neutral language, no emojis.
Expected deliverable: 10-slide script ready to design, with headline, bullets, speaking notes, objection-response, and timing per slide, plus a final line confirming the 20/20 timing verification and the count of figures marked as assumption.
spec-comunicacion_presentacion_apertura_:
[inputs]
- TEMA_CHARLA: {{TEMA_CHARLA}} > Central idea or topic of the presentation
- PERFIL_AUDIENCIA: {{PERFIL_AUDIENCIA}} > Who is listening: role, knowledge level, expectation, and emotional state on arrival

--- S | SITUATION ---
The first 60 seconds of a talk decide whether the audience follows you or mentally disconnects. An impact hook opening on {{TEMA_CHARLA}}, calibrated for {{PERFIL_AUDIENCIA}}, unlocks full attention from the first sentence and steers the presentation toward {{OBJETIVO_PRESENTACION}}. Archetype: senior speaker coach specialized in high-impact openings, with experience designing the first 60 seconds of keynotes and conferences.

spec-comunicacion_presentacion_narrativa:
[inputs]

- PROBLEMA_CENTRAL: {{PROBLEMA_CENTRAL}} > The concrete problem the audience experiences, in their own language
- COSTO_INACCION: {{COSTO_INACCION}} > Consequences, opportunity cost, or growing risk of not acting; with figures or facts if they exist

- PRUEBA: {{PRUEBA}} > Evidence, case study, data, or demonstration that supports the proposal

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You need to reorder the content of a presentation so that the audience travels the Problem-Agitation-Solution arc (PAS) and arrives convinced at the decision you are seeking. A well-sequenced deck converts loose data into a story that creates tension and resolves it with your proposal. The result unlocks a slide-by-slide storyline ready to design and rehearse, with a spoken transition script so the narrative flows live, and a close that drives exactly the decision sought.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior narrative strategist for executive presentations, with experience structuring sales decks and decision committees under the PAS arc.
Deliverable: a slide-by-slide storyline structured in four blocks (Context, Problem, Agitation, Solution). Steps:
1. Set the context: audience ({{AUDIENCIA_Y_DECISION}}), decision to make at the end, and the single idea they must remember.
2. PROBLEM block: name {{PROBLEMA_CENTRAL}} in the audience's language, without revealing the solution or the proposal.
3. AGITATION block: amplify {{COSTO_INACCION}} with consequences, opportunity cost, and growing risk, anchored in verifiable figures or facts, without gratuitous fear.
4. SOLUTION block: present {{PROPUESTA}} as the direct resolution of the tension, backed by {{PRUEBA}}, and close with a call to action that matches the decision sought.
5. For each slide deliver: number and title, unique idea (one sentence), two to four supporting bullets, suggested visual or data piece, and spoken transition to the next slide.
6. Adjust the number of slides to {{NUM_SLIDES}} if indicated; otherwise propose the minimum that sustains the arc without filler slides.
7. Use {{ADJUNTOS}} as a data and proof input; do not invent figures not supported there.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: confirm audience, decision sought, and central idea; if a key input is missing (problem, cost, proposal, or proof), ask for it before drafting.
Phase 2 - Arc map: distribute the slides among Context, Problem, Agitation, and Solution before drafting the detail; validate that the proportion gives enough time to the tension.
Phase 3 - Slide-by-slide drafting: one single idea per slide, concrete bullets, suggested data or visual, transitions that chain the narrative.
Phase 4 - Stitching: reread the complete arc and verify that tension rises in Agitation and resolves in Solution, that no slide carries two ideas, and that it flows when read aloud.
Mark with [ASSUMPTION] any inferred data pending confirmation.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The PAS arc is continuous and each slide carries one single idea.
- [ ] The Problem block uses the audience's language and does not reveal the solution.
- [ ] Agitation quantifies the cost of inaction with verifiable figures or facts, without gratuitous fear or exaggeration.
- [ ] The Solution connects with the stated tension and ends with a call to action matching the decision sought.
- [ ] Each slide includes unique idea, bullets, suggested visual or data piece, and spoken transition; the narrative flows when read in sequence.
- [ ] The number of slides respects {{NUM_SLIDES}} or is justified as the minimum that sustains the arc.
- [ ] Inferred data marked with [ASSUMPTION]; neutral and professional language, no emojis.
Edge cases: if there is no solid proof, mark the Solution slide as [ASSUMPTION] and propose what evidence to obtain; if the audience already knows the problem, shorten Problem and reinforce Agitation; if the decision is not clear, stop and ask for it before continuing.
Expected deliverable: slide-by-slide storyline in four blocks (Context, Problem, Agitation, Solution), with title, unique idea, bullets, suggested visual, and transition per slide, plus a close listing which slides rest on assumptions and what is needed to confirm them. Ready to take to design and rehearsal.

--- S | SITUATION ---
You are closing a presentation on {{TEMA_PRESENTACION}} before {{AUDIENCIA}}. The final slide is the one most remembered and the only one that can convert attention into movement. A vague close ("thank you", "questions?", three summary bullets) dissipates the accumulated momentum; a close with an unambiguous action unlocks the decision, the yes, or the concrete first step that justifies the entire presentation. The challenge is not to summarize what was said: it is to transfer to the audience the responsibility for a next step they can and want to take today.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior executive communication strategist specializing in high-impact presentation closes and call-to-action design.
Build the final slide and its spoken close. Steps:
1. Distill the central message into a memorable phrase of at most 12 words, one {{AUDIENCIA}} can repeat from memory as they leave the room (audience language, not the presenter's jargon).
2. Formulate ONE single primary call to action based on {{ACCION_DESEADA}}: imperative verb, concrete and observable; discard verbs of intention ("consider", "think", "explore") that produce no evidence of compliance.
3. Make the action unambiguous: define exactly what, who executes it, by when according to {{PLAZO}}, and what the actionable first step is (something executable in under five minutes or without leaving the room).
4. Add the why that connects the action to {{BENEFICIO_O_COSTO}}; if empty, derive a plausible benefit from the topic and flag it [ASSUMPTION].
5. Validate that {{AUDIENCIA}} has real authority to execute the action. If not, propose a backup action within their reach (decide, schedule, authorize, escalate to the decision-maker) and note it.
6. Propose the visual structure of the slide: headline, subtitle, highlighted action element, optional closing anchor (data point, date or question), and a verbal transition line to say aloud when showing it.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 · Synthesis: identify the central message and compact it into the ≤12-word phrase.
Phase 2 · Action: convert the intention into a single, verifiable imperative CTA (what/who/when/first step); validate execution authority and derive a backup if missing.
Phase 3 · Motivation: link the action to the benefit or avoided cost, flagging assumptions.
Phase 4 · Assembly: arrange headline, subtitle, highlighted CTA, and anchor in a single-focus slide, and draft the spoken transition.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If a critical data point is missing (topic, audience, desired action), ask for it before drafting.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Central phrase ≤12 words, in the audience's language and repeatable from memory.
- [ ] Single primary CTA, in an imperative verb, not diluted across multiple requests.
- [ ] CTA is unambiguous: what, who, when (deadline), and first step are explicit.
- [ ] First step executable immediately (≤5 minutes or without leaving the room).
- [ ] Execution authority validated; backup action present if the audience does not decide.
- [ ] Why is present and connected to a concrete benefit or cost; assumptions flagged [ASSUMPTION].
- [ ] Visual structure is hierarchical with a single focus point.
- [ ] Verbal transition line ready to deliver.
- [ ] Neutral and professional language; no emojis; no prices; no word "free".
Edge cases: mixed audience (executors + influencers) → one CTA per role, maximum two; irreversible or high-risk action → low-commitment first step that opens the door without forcing the yes.
Expected deliverable: block ready for the final slide (headline + subtitle + highlighted CTA + optional anchor), two-line speaking note for the spoken close, and, when applicable, the labeled backup action.
spec-comunicacion_presentacion_guion_dia:
[inputs]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You are going to present "{{TITULO_PRESENTACION}}" live before {{AUDIENCIA}} with the objective of {{OBJETIVO}} in {{DURACION_OBJETIVO}}. The slides already exist, but without a script the risk is reading the slides, losing the thread at transitions, running over time, and diluting the message. A slide-by-slide aligned script converts a static deck into a delivery with rhythm, focus, and clean transitions, and frees the speaker to look at the audience instead of the screen. It enables timed rehearsals, a deliberate emphasis strategy, and a confident delivery.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Understanding: read {{CONTENIDO_SLIDES}}, {{AUDIENCIA}}, {{OBJETIVO}}, {{DURACION_OBJETIVO}}, and {{ADJUNTOS}}; if slide content, title, audience, objective, or duration are missing or ambiguous, ask before drafting and do not invent the deck content.
Phase 2 Structure: define the narrative arc, deduct the buffer, and distribute the remaining time budget among opening, development, and close.
Phase 3 Drafting: generate notes slide by slide in the tone {{TONO}} (if missing, neutral professional and declare it), ensuring transitions chain without jumps and notes sound like a human voice.
Phase 4 Alignment: time, sum, and adjust against {{DURACION_OBJETIVO}}; deliver the summary table and, if there is a gap, the adjustment plan.

--- C | CRITERION ---
- Each slide has the 5 elements: key message (1 sentence), spoken notes, transition, seconds, and pacing cue when applicable.
- One message per slide; overloaded ones are flagged with a split suggestion.
- The notes are speakable and natural, not copied bullets nor monotonous literal text to read.
- The transitions link explicitly to the following slide.
- The buffer (10 to 15 percent) is deducted and declared.
