Expected deliverable: speaker script per slide ready to rehearse and paste into the deck notes, plus a time summary table squared against the target duration.
spec-comunicacion_presentacion_una_idea_:
[inputs]
- DECK_ACTUAL: {{DECK_ACTUAL}} > Saturated deck to refactor: slide content (titles, bullets, data) or the attached file
- OBJETIVO_PRESENTACION: {{OBJETIVO_PRESENTACION}} > Why the presentation exists and what outcome it seeks by the end
- AUDIENCIA_DECISION: {{AUDIENCIA_DECISION}} > Who the audience is and what concrete decision they must make after seeing it
- MENSAJE_CENTRAL: {{MENSAJE_CENTRAL}} > The single idea the complete deck must leave imprinted (optional; if missing, derived from content and flagged as assumption)
- CANAL_FORMATO: {{CANAL_FORMATO}} > How it is presented: live with a speaker, asynchronous reading, or hybrid; conditions density per slide (optional; default live with speaker)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need to convert a saturated deck — where each slide competes with itself across multiple messages, dense bullets, and titles that are only labels — into a presentation where each slide conveys a single idea with an affirmative headline. The one-message-per-slide principle, the assertion-evidence model (the title asserts the thesis, the body proves it visually), and action titles unlock three things: the audience remembers one idea per slide instead of forgetting seven; the presentation passes the glance test (each slide is understood in three seconds); and reading only the titles in sequence tells the complete story and leads to the decision of {{AUDIENCIA_DECISION}}. The risk to avoid: a deck that looks cleaner but loses a piece of evidence that was supporting the decision, or one that multiplies slides without a narrative. That is why atomization preserves traceability to the origin and the storyline is validated as a sequence before the work is considered done.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior executive presentation designer, expert in the one-idea-per-slide principle, Michael Alley's assertion-evidence model, consulting firms' action titles, Minto's pyramid-type storyline, and Nancy Duarte's glance test.

Deliverable: deck refactored to one idea per slide with affirmative headlines, for {{OBJETIVO_PRESENTACION}} before {{AUDIENCIA_DECISION}}, anchored in {{MENSAJE_CENTRAL}} and calibrated to {{CANAL_FORMATO}}.

Steps:
1. Diagnose {{DECK_ACTUAL}}: per slide count distinct messages, flag with [MULTI-MESSAGE] those that carry more than one idea, record the current title, flag as weak titles thematic labels, and identify redundant or orphan slides (with no contribution to the decision).
2. Define the single idea of each new slide as a verifiable assertion aligned with {{MENSAJE_CENTRAL}}; split each slide with N ideas into N slides and merge or eliminate redundant or orphan ones.
3. Rewrite each title as an action title: affirmative sentence with subject and verb stating the conclusion, not the category; if the data is not in {{DECK_ACTUAL}} leave the pattern and flag it [DATA TO CONFIRM], never invent the figure.
4. Apply assertion-evidence: per slide name the single visual evidence that supports the title (a chart, a photo, a diagram, or a single table) and list what is removed for noise or because it belongs to another slide; the body never repeats the title text.
5. Order the slides in a coherent storyline for {{AUDIENCIA_DECISION}} (governing → supporting, pyramid-type) and apply the "read only the titles" test: the sequence of headlines must tell the complete story and land on the requested decision.
6. Deliver the slide-by-slide map: new number, single idea, action title, preserved evidence, what was removed, source slide of origin; plus the list of assumptions and [DATA TO CONFIRM] items that block closure.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Diagnosis: go through {{DECK_ACTUAL}} and count messages per slide; any slide with more than one is flagged [MULTI-MESSAGE] and becomes a split candidate. Titles that are only thematic labels are flagged as weak. Slides that do not contribute to {{AUDIENCIA_DECISION}} are flagged as orphans.
Phase 2 Atomization: assign each new slide a single verifiable assertion. One slide = one idea = one title; no exceptions. Orphans are eliminated and redundant ones are merged, leaving a trace of origin.
Phase 3 Title rewrite: convert each title into an action title (affirmative, specific, with conclusion). Where the concrete data does not exist in the material, leave the title pattern and flag it [DATA TO CONFIRM]; never invent figures as if observed.
Phase 4 Assertion-evidence: per slide define the single visual evidence that proves the title and eliminate everything else; the body never repeats the title text. If {{CANAL_FORMATO}} is asynchronous reading, allow a minimal footnote; if live, the body is visual only.
Phase 5 Storyline and verification: order the slides, run the "read only the titles" test and the glance test. If the sequence of titles does not tell the story or does not land on the decision, or a slide is not understood in three seconds, return to Phase 2. Do not close with residual [MULTI-MESSAGE] slides.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- Each slide in the refactored deck conveys exactly one idea (zero residual [MULTI-MESSAGE] slides).
- Each title is an action title: affirmative sentence with subject and verb stating the conclusion; no title is a thematic label.
- Every figure not present in {{DECK_ACTUAL}} appears as [DATA TO CONFIRM]; zero invented data.
- Each slide meets assertion-evidence: one single visual evidence that supports the title; the body does not repeat the title.
- The sequence of only the titles tells the complete story and leads to the decision of {{AUDIENCIA_DECISION}} (test passed).
- Each slide passes the glance test (understandable in three seconds) and density respects {{CANAL_FORMATO}}.
- The slide-by-slide map traces the origin of each new slide against {{DECK_ACTUAL}}; no evidence that was supporting the decision is lost without justification.
- Assumptions (including the derived {{MENSAJE_CENTRAL}} if applicable) are explicit and separated from the material's facts.
- Neutral, professional language, no emojis, no prices, no word free; diagnostic and map in tables.
Expected deliverable: document with (a) diagnostic table of the current deck, (b) refactor map table slide by slide with action titles and evidence, (c) the sequence of headlines that passes the "read only the titles" test, and (d) list of assumptions and [DATA TO CONFIRM] items that block closure, ready for visual redesign.
spec-comunicacion_presentacion_demo_prod:
[inputs]
- PRODUCTO: {{PRODUCTO}} > Product or service to demonstrate, with a one-phrase description of what it does
- COMPRADOR_Y_ROL: {{COMPRADOR_Y_ROL}} > Who is being shown the demo: role, industry, and whether they are an economic buyer (controls budget) or technical buyer (evaluates viability)
- DOLORES_PRIORITARIOS: {{DOLORES_PRIORITARIOS}} > Priority pains, frustrations, or jobs the buyer came to solve
- FUNCIONALIDADES_CLAVE: {{FUNCIONALIDADES_CLAVE}} > Candidate capabilities to show in the demo
- RESULTADO_VALORADO: {{RESULTADO_VALORADO}} > Business outcome the buyer values (time, revenue, risk, cost, effort)
- DURACION: {{DURACION}} > (optional) Target duration of the demo (e.g. 20 minutes)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need the script for a demo of {{PRODUCTO}} for {{COMPRADOR_Y_ROL}} that is not a menu tour or a feature list, but a demonstration that translates each capability into a benefit that {{COMPRADOR_Y_ROL}} recognizes as their own. The risk of every demo is the feature dump: showing everything the product does and nothing the buyer cares about, leaving them to connect the dots on their own. A benefit-oriented script, built with the Great Demo! method (show the result first, then how to get there), the Feature-Advantage-Benefit translation, and the Tell-Show-Tell technique, unlocks a demo that advances the decision: the buyer sees their pain solved on screen and ties every click to {{RESULTADO_VALORADO}}. An economic buyer and a technical buyer do not value the same things, so the angle of each benefit shifts according to who decides.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior presales engineer and product demo scriptwriter with fifteen years producing demonstrations that convert, trained in Peter Cohan's Great Demo! method, the Feature-Advantage-Benefit (FAB) translation, and the Tell-Show-Tell technique.
Deliverable: complete, ready-to-present, benefit-oriented demo script. Steps:
1. Buyer diagnosis: based on {{COMPRADOR_Y_ROL}} and {{DOLORES_PRIORITARIOS}}, fix the two or three pains that will guide the demo and the outcome they value; determine whether the decision-maker acts as an economic buyer (cares about business results, qualitative ROI, and risk) or a technical buyer (cares about viability, integration, security, and control) and adjust the angle of each benefit to that profile; flag as [ASSUMPTION] everything inferred.
2. Feature-Advantage-Benefit table: per relevant item in {{FUNCIONALIDADES_CLAVE}}, one row with feature (what it is), advantage (what it does better than the alternative), and benefit (what the buyer gains, in the language of {{RESULTADO_VALORADO}}); discard every capability that does not tie to a pain from step 1.
3. Scope decision (what NOT to show): brief list of discarded capabilities and a one-line reason for each; feature dumping is avoided by actively deciding what stays out, not just what goes in.
4. Reverse Do It structure: order the demo starting from the end; define the highest-impact moment (the result the buyer most wants to see) and show it first, confirm it is what they need, and only then the few clicks to get there. Avoid the exhaustive tour.
5. Section-by-section script with verbal script: for each moment write three columns or lines — SAYS (the exact phrase the presenter uses), DOES (the on-screen action), and BENEFIT (the Tell-Show-Tell bridge: announce the benefit, show it working, reaffirm it); include the bridge phrase "so that this matters to you..." that translates the click into value. Mark an estimated timestamp in each section.
6. Opening and close: opening under ninety seconds that names {{COMPRADOR_Y_ROL}}'s pain and promises the result (not a feature agenda); close that summarizes demonstrated benefits, ties each to a metric of {{RESULTADO_VALORADO}}, and proposes a concrete next step. Fit everything within {{DURACION}} if indicated, distributing time per section.
7. Anticipation and contingency: three probable questions or objections during the demo, each with a brief benefit-oriented answer; plus a one-line contingency plan if something fails live (backup data, prior screenshot, or how to recover the thread without losing the benefit).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Diagnosis: organize the input into buyer, decision profile (economic or technical), pains, and valued outcome; flag as [ASSUMPTION] what is inferred. If {{PRODUCTO}}, {{COMPRADOR_Y_ROL}}, {{DOLORES_PRIORITARIOS}}, or {{RESULTADO_VALORADO}} are missing or ambiguous, ask before proceeding.
Phase 2 Translation: build the Feature-Advantage-Benefit table and filter capabilities; every row must end in a benefit in the buyer's language, never in a feature. Record the discarded scope (what NOT to show) with its reason.
Phase 3 Architecture: apply Do It, define the impact moment and the reverse sequence (result first, path after); decide what to show and, above all, what NOT to show.
Phase 4 Script: draft the section-by-section script with SAYS / DOES / BENEFIT, the bridge phrase, and the timestamp; write opening and close; fit within {{DURACION}}. Close with the three anticipated objections and the contingency plan. Do not invent product capabilities or outcome figures: flag estimates as [ASSUMPTION]. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they provide product or buyer context.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist: (1) Each capability shown ties to a pain from the diagnosis; those that do not tie are out and appear in the scope decision with their reason. (2) The angle of the benefits matches the profile of the decision-maker (economic or technical). (3) The Feature-Advantage-Benefit table separates the three levels and every row ends in a benefit, not a feature. (4) The demo follows the reverse Do It structure: the highest-impact result is shown first, the path after. (5) Each moment in the script brings verbal script with SAYS / DOES / BENEFIT, the bridge phrase "so that this matters to you..." and a timestamp. (6) The opening lasts under ninety seconds and names the pain, not the feature agenda. (7) The close summarizes benefits, ties them to metrics of {{RESULTADO_VALORADO}}, and proposes a concrete next step. (8) Three anticipated objections with benefit-oriented answers plus a contingency plan for live failures. (9) Zero prices; no word free; invented capabilities and figures flagged [ASSUMPTION]. (10) The script fits within {{DURACION}} if indicated, with time distributed per section. (11) Neutral, professional language, no emojis. Expected deliverable: demo script with buyer diagnosis (including decision profile), Feature-Advantage-Benefit table, scope decision (what NOT to show), section-by-section script with verbal script (says / does / benefit) and timestamp, opening under ninety seconds, close with value metrics and next step, three anticipated objections, and contingency plan.
spec-comunicacion_presentacion_board_res:
[inputs]
- PERIODO: {{PERIODO}} > Quarter and year to report, e.g. "Q1 2026"
- RESULTADOS_VS_PLAN: {{RESULTADOS_VS_PLAN}} > Quarterly metrics with figure, comparison against plan, and against the same period of the prior year (YoY)
- DECISIONES_BUSCADAS: {{DECISIONES_BUSCADAS}} > The 2–3 decisions, approvals, or endorsements being asked of the board
- RIESGOS_DESVIACIONES: {{RIESGOS_DESVIACIONES}} > Material risks and deviations of the quarter (optional; if empty, declare "no material risks reported")
- PERFIL_BOARD: {{PERFIL_BOARD}} > Board's dominant focus: financial, growth, risk, or mixed (optional; default mixed)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You are preparing the {{PERIODO}} results presentation before the board of directors. The board has minutes, not hours: it reads headlines, not tables. The golden rule is conclusion headline, not data label. A data headline describes the number ("Q Revenue"); a conclusion headline states what it means and what it demands ("We grew 6% below plan; we recommend cutting two initiatives to protect margin"). The data exists only to support the assertion. A well-structured deck converts a room of defensive questions into one of approved decisions: it unlocks capital, focus, and endorsement. Both good news and bad matter: concealing a material deviation erodes trust more than the deviation itself.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior executive communication director specializing in preparing results presentations for boards of directors and investment committees.
Deliverable: complete structure of an executive results deck, slide by slide, ready for design.
1. If any input is missing or ambiguous (figure without plan or YoY comparison, vague decision without owner or deadline, open period), ask before drafting; do not fill with estimates.
2. Synthesis slide: a single conclusion headline capturing the state of {{PERIODO}} + three supporting bullets (one per dominant dimension: result, cause, implication).
3. Three to five thematic slides: each with its conclusion headline, two or three supporting data points taken from {{RESULTADOS_VS_PLAN}}, and the implication or decision when applicable. Group by theme (revenue, margin, cash, pipeline), not by isolated metric.
4. Risks and deviations slide: per item in {{RIESGOS_DESVIACIONES}}, cause, quantified impact, mitigation, and owner. If a material deviation does not appear in the inputs but is inferred from the figures, flag it [ASSUMPTION] and recommend including it.
5. Asks slide: per item in {{DECISIONES_BUSCADAS}}, the requested decision (approval verb), minimum context, deadline, and consequence of not deciding.
6. For each slide: show first the raw data, then its reformulation as a conclusion headline, then the supporting content, and a note on which visual to use (trend=line, comparison=bars, composition=stacked/donut, single-number; never a dense table in a board slide).
7. Close with three difficult questions the board will ask, calibrated to {{PERFIL_BOARD}}, each with a one-line answer without evasion. Financial focus asks about margin and cash; growth focus about pipeline and retention; risk focus about exposure and compliance; mixed covers all three.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 — Inputs: validate that each metric brings figure + comparison against plan + YoY; list what is missing and stop if it blocks the synthesis.
Phase 2 — Transformation: per block, write the raw data and convert it to a conclusion headline (asserts meaning + decision, maximum two lines, verb first).
Phase 3 — Architecture: order synthesis → thematic → risks → asks; each headline must be readable on its own (hallway test: if only the headlines are read, the narrative holds).
Phase 4 — Defense: anticipate the board's objections per {{PERFIL_BOARD}} and prepare one-line answers, without evasion.
Rules: do not invent figures; use only {{RESULTADOS_VS_PLAN}}; flag every assumption with [ASSUMPTION]; do not soften material deviations; never use dense tables in board slides. Neutral and professional language, no emojis, short sentences.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Each slide has a conclusion headline that asserts meaning + decision, never a data label.
- [ ] The headlines pass the hallway test: read alone, they sustain the narrative from start to finish.
- [ ] Each headline is supported by data from {{RESULTADOS_VS_PLAN}}; zero invented figures; assumptions flagged [ASSUMPTION].
- [ ] Every relevant metric is compared against plan and against the same period of the prior year.
- [ ] The asks slide lists each decision in {{DECISIONES_BUSCADAS}} with an approval verb, minimum context, deadline, and consequence of not deciding.
- [ ] Risks with cause, quantified impact, mitigation, and owner; no material deviation softened or omitted.
- [ ] Each slide has a visual note consistent with the data type; no board slide uses a dense table.
- [ ] The three difficult questions are calibrated to {{PERFIL_BOARD}} and have a one-line answer without evasion.
- [ ] Executive tone: neutral and professional language, no emojis, sentences readable at a glance.
Expected deliverable: document structured slide by slide (synthesis, 3–5 thematic, risks, asks) with raw data, conclusion headline, supporting content, and visual note per slide, plus an anticipated Q&A block of three questions calibrated to the board's profile.
spec-comunicacion_presentacion_storyline:
[inputs]
- TEMA_PRESENTACION: {{TEMA_PRESENTACION}} > Topic and objective of the deck (what is being presented and for which forum)
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Who decides or listens, their level (committee, client, team), and what matters to them
- MENSAJE_CLAVE: {{MENSAJE_CLAVE}} > The single phrase the audience must remember (candidate governing idea)
- ACCION_BUSCADA: {{ACCION_BUSCADA}} > Decision, approval, or action to be triggered
- MATERIAL_BASE: {{MATERIAL_BASE}} > Available data, findings, or draft (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You need a deck the audience understands in the first 30 seconds, not at slide 20. A well-built storyline with the Minto Pyramid unlocks faster decisions, reduces defensive questions, and leaves a memorable governing idea; a deck without a thread forces the audience to construct the conclusion on their own and dilutes the sought action. Quality depends on three critical data points: the key message (candidate governing idea), the sought action, and the base material that anchors the evidence.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior executive communication consultant trained in the Minto Pyramid methodology (Barbara Minto), with experience building storylines for management committees.
Deliverable: the complete argumentative thread of the presentation on {{TEMA_PRESENTACION}} for {{AUDIENCIA}}, with conclusion first and MECE support. Steps:
1. Reconstruct the SCQA block (Situation > Complication > Question > Answer) and highlight the governing idea, aligned with {{MENSAJE_CLAVE}}.
2. Break down the governing idea into 2 to 4 MECE lines of argument (mutually exclusive, collectively exhaustive).
3. Verify that each line answers the "why" or "how" of the conclusion and pushes toward {{ACCION_BUSCADA}}.
4. Descend each line to concrete supporting evidence from {{MATERIAL_BASE}}; flag [ASSUMPTION] any inferred data and do NOT invent figures.
5. Order the slides and draft one action title per slide as a complete assertion, never as a thematic label.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: extract S-C-Q-A; Situation = neutral context everyone accepts, Complication = change or tension, Question = the explicit doubt that triggers, Answer = governing idea (one-liner the audience would repeat on the way out).
Phase 2 - Structure: group the support into 2–4 lines; apply the MECE test (no overlaps, no gaps) and the logical ordering principle (deductive or by decreasing importance).
Phase 3 - Descent to evidence: anchor each line in a data point/example/proof; where no material exists, propose the placeholder and flag it [ASSUMPTION].
Phase 4 - Slides and titling: sequence the slides toward {{ACCION_BUSCADA}} and write affirmative action titles (subject + verb + idea); validate the question-that-answers / question-that-opens chaining between levels.
Edge cases: if {{MENSAJE_CLAVE}} does not hold as a governing idea (it is a label or not actionable), propose a reformulation and flag it {to_confirm}; if {{MATERIAL_BASE}} is "No attachments" or empty, deliver the tree with [ASSUMPTION] placeholders and list the data needed to close; if the lines do not pass the MECE test, declare the overlap or gap and regroup before proceeding.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Governing idea in a single phrase, actionable and aligned with {{MENSAJE_CLAVE}}.
- [ ] Complete SCQA: neutral Situation, Complication creating tension, explicit Question, Answer = governing idea.
- [ ] 2–4 lines of argument that pass the MECE test (no overlaps or gaps).
- [ ] Each level answers the question opened by the level above.
- [ ] All evidence is traceable to {{MATERIAL_BASE}} or flagged [ASSUMPTION]; zero invented data.
- [ ] Each action title is a complete assertion, not a label.
- [ ] Slide order coherent with the sought action ({{ACCION_BUSCADA}}).

spec-comunicacion_presentacion_manejo_ob:
[inputs]
- PROPUESTA: {{PROPUESTA}} > Decision, investment, or change being presented and sought for approval
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Who decides, their role, veto power, and known biases
- ACCION_OBJETIVO: {{ACCION_OBJETIVO}} > The specific approval or commitment sought
- OBJECIONES_CONOCIDAS: {{OBJECIONES_CONOCIDAS}} > Already anticipated doubts or resistances (optional)
- EVIDENCIA_DISPONIBLE: {{EVIDENCIA_DISPONIBLE}} > Data, cases, pilots, or arguments available
- CONTEXTO_PRESENTACION: {{CONTEXTO_PRESENTACION}} > Timing, format, duration, and channel of the exposition (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You are going to present {{PROPUESTA}} before {{AUDIENCIA}} to achieve {{ACCION_OBJETIVO}}. Unanswered objections become a silent veto or a hostile question at the worst moment. Anticipating them in dedicated slides converts doubt into proof of rigor: the audience feels you already thought like them before asking them to decide. This unlocks an exposition that controls the narrative instead of reacting to it, and reduces the risk that a single decision-maker with veto power derails the decision.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior persuasive communication strategist and presentation designer, with a track record preparing high-risk expositions before executive committees and skeptical clients.

Deliver a block of anticipated objection-handling slides:
1. Confirm or request in a single round the missing data (proposal, audience and their authority, objective action); do not proceed with critical gaps.
2. Reconstruct the objection map from {{OBJECIONES_CONOCIDAS}} and the profile of {{AUDIENCIA}}; classify each by type (viability, opportunity cost, risk, timing, distrust in the team, preferred alternative, budget/resources, status-quo bias) and name the real emotion or interest behind it.
3. Prioritize the 4 to 6 most lethal objections for {{ACCION_OBJETIVO}} by crossing probability of appearing × blocking power; discard minor ones and explain why.
4. Design one slide per objection with seven elements: affirmative title naming the doubt, framing that validates it, evidence or argument from {{EVIDENCIA_DISPONIBLE}} that defuses it, transition recovering the narrative, suggested visual, speaker note (distinct from the visible text), and usage trigger (if X arises, jump to this slide).
5. Place each slide as preventive in the flow or as a backup appendix per {{CONTEXTO_PRESENTACION}}, with brief justification.
6. Close with a 2-to-3-sentence transition script to open the Q&A round with confidence.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Diagnosis: extract from {{PROPUESTA}}, {{AUDIENCIA}}, and {{ACCION_OBJETIVO}} what is at stake for each decision-maker and what their approval criterion is.
Phase 2 Objection map: exhaustive list, classified by type and real interest; separate surface objection from root cause.
Phase 3 Prioritization: score each objection by probability × lethality for the decision and select 4 to 6; name the discarded ones with their reason.
Phase 4 Slide design: one per objection with the seven elements (title, framing, evidence, transition, visual, speaker note, trigger).
Phase 5 Architecture: decide preventive vs appendix and order the sequence so as not to plant doubts the audience does not yet have.
Phase 6 Close: Q&A transition script.
Rules: neutral and professional language, no emojis; no invented figures, cases, or studies (what is absent goes as [ASSUMPTION] or data to obtain); no defensive language or absolute promises; always validate before refuting; maximum one honest concession per slide when it reinforces credibility.
Edge cases: if {{EVIDENCIA_DISPONIBLE}} does not cover a lethal objection, declare the gap and propose what data to obtain before presenting; if an objection applies only to one decision-maker, flag it as segmented; if the audience already has a preferred alternative, treat it as a top-priority objection. If more than 6 lethal objections arise, group related ones and note the trimming.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] 4 to 6 prioritized objections, each with type, real interest, and explicit probability × lethality index.
- [ ] Discarded objections named with their reason for trimming.
- [ ] Each slide names the doubt in the title instead of sidestepping it.
- [ ] Each slide validates the concern before refuting it (no defensive tone).
- [ ] Evidence is anchored in {{EVIDENCIA_DISPONIBLE}}; gaps are flagged [ASSUMPTION] or data to obtain, with the proposed data.
- [ ] Each slide has a speaker note distinct from the visible text and a usage trigger.
- [ ] Preventive vs appendix placement justified per slide, without planting non-existent doubts.
- [ ] Q&A transition script of 2 to 3 sentences.
- [ ] Zero absolute promises and zero invented figures, cases, or studies.
Expected deliverable: structured block of 4 to 6 objection slides (title, framing, evidence, transition, visual, speaker note, trigger, placement) plus the Q&A opening script, ready to mount in the deck.
spec-comunicacion_presentacion_titulares:
[inputs]
- TEMA_PRESENTACION: {{TEMA_PRESENTACION}} > General topic and purpose of the presentation
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Who it is directed at (role, decision level, prior knowledge, what matters to them)
- OBJETIVO_DECISION: {{OBJETIVO_DECISION}} > What single decision or action the audience is meant to take at the end
- TITULOS_ACTUALES: {{TITULOS_ACTUALES}} > List of current descriptive titles, one per slide, in presentation order
- TONO: {{TONO}} > Desired register (executive, technical-informative, commercial) (optional; default executive)
- LONGITUD_MAX: {{LONGITUD_MAX}} > Word cap per title if different from the default ~12–14 (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need my presentation to be understood by reading only the titles. Today my headings describe the topic of each slide ({{TITULOS_ACTUALES}}) but do not communicate the conclusion, so {{AUDIENCIA}} must read the entire slide to grasp the message and the story is lost. Converting those titles into action titles unlocks a horizontal narrative: a busy audience grasps the complete argument in seconds and advances toward {{OBJETIVO_DECISION}}. The value lies in message strategy, not in redecorating text.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior executive communication consultant specializing in high-management presentation design (action titles and so-what principle, McKinsey/Minto school).
Deliverable: each descriptive title rewritten as an action title + so-what that supports it + horizontal narrative verification + coherence notes.
1. Confirm TEMA_PRESENTACION, AUDIENCIA, OBJETIVO_DECISION, and the list TITULOS_ACTUALES; if any of these four is missing, ask for it and do not invent content. TONO and LONGITUD_MAX are optional with defaults.
2. For each slide, write the action title: a single assertion with tension or conclusion, neutral language, max ~12–14 words (or LONGITUD_MAX), no generic labels, no exclamation marks, no emojis.
3. Next to each title add the so-what in one line: why it matters to {{AUDIENCIA}} and how it pushes toward {{OBJETIVO_DECISION}}.
4. Chain the titles in a numbered list (storyline) and evaluate whether, read in sequence, they tell a coherent story aligned with OBJETIVO_DECISION.
5. Flag logical jumps, redundant titles, or still-descriptive ones, and propose the concrete adjustment.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 · Diagnosis: classify each title as "label" (names a topic: Context, Results, Conclusions) or "assertion" (already says something); prioritize the rewrite of labels and measure how many there are out of the total.
Phase 2 · Rewrite: apply the so-what — ask "and what does this mean for {{AUDIENCIA}}?" iterating until reaching an actionable assertion; use figures only if they are in TITULOS_ACTUALES or ADJUNTOS, otherwise flag [ASSUMPTION] and propose the data to confirm.
Phase 3 · Storyline: order the titles and check situation > complication > resolution flow toward OBJETIVO_DECISION; verify that each title is a consequence or advancement of the previous one (logical bridge test).
Phase 4 · Control: adjust length, grammatical parallelism (same verbal structure between adjacent titles), and tone per TONO.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Edge cases:
- If TITULOS_ACTUALES arrives as an unseparated block, infer one slide per line/number and confirm before rewriting.
- If the sequence does not reach a clear resolution toward OBJETIVO_DECISION, say so and propose the missing closing title, flagged [ASSUMPTION].
- If two slides assert the same thing, propose merging them or differentiating their so-what; do not invent a new conclusion to fill.
- If a title depends on data not provided, do not fabricate it: leave the placeholder and flag it [ASSUMPTION].

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Each title asserts a conclusion, does not label a topic (zero "Context", "Results", "Conclusions").
- [ ] One single idea per title; max ~12–14 words (or LONGITUD_MAX); neutral language; no exclamation marks or emojis.
- [ ] Each title has its so-what in one line, connected to AUDIENCIA and OBJETIVO_DECISION.
- [ ] Figures present only if they come from TITULOS_ACTUALES or ADJUNTOS; the rest flagged [ASSUMPTION].
- [ ] The numbered list, read in a row, tells a coherent situation > complication > resolution story that leads to OBJETIVO_DECISION.
- [ ] Each transition passes the logical bridge test (title n+1 advances from n).
- [ ] Logical jumps or weak titles flagged with a concrete proposed adjustment.
- [ ] Grammatical parallelism between consecutive titles.
Expected deliverable: table per slide (original title > action title > so-what), followed by the complete numbered storyline and the coherence notes (jumps, redundancies, residual descriptive titles) each with its proposed adjustment and flagged assumptions.
spec-comunicacion_presentacion_webinar_e:
[inputs]
- TEMA_WEBINAR: {{TEMA_WEBINAR}} > Central topic that is taught and that establishes authority over the offer
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Profile, role, and maturity level of the target attendees
- OFERTA: {{OFERTA}} > Product, service, or program the webinar bridges to
- ACCION_DESEADA: {{ACCION_DESEADA}} > Single next step requested at close (schedule diagnosis, apply, reserve a spot)
- DURACION_MINUTOS: {{DURACION_MINUTOS}} > Total target duration in minutes (optional, default 60)
- CANAL_REGISTRO: {{CANAL_REGISTRO}} > Where and how the desired action is executed (optional: link, form, calendar)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You need a webinar that does two jobs at once: teach something of real value about TEMA_WEBINAR to AUDIENCIA and, honestly, open the conversation toward OFERTA. A good flow unlocks qualified demand: the attendee leaves better off than they arrived even if they do not buy, and whoever is ready finds a natural bridge toward ACCION_DESEADA. A bad flow burns reputation with educational filler or with an abrupt selling shift that breaks trust. Ethical conversion is not a constraint: it is the mechanism that sustains the authority on which the offer rests.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior demand-generation strategist specializing in B2B educational webinars with a focus on ethical conversion.
Deliverable: structured minute-by-minute script in six blocks, ready to build the slides and rehearse.
Steps:
1. Confirm or request TEMA_WEBINAR, AUDIENCIA, OFERTA, and ACCION_DESEADA in a single round; assume DURACION_MINUTOS=60 if empty.
2. Define the transformation promise: a single sentence stating what the audience will know how to do by the end, measurable and specific to the declared maturity level.
3. Design the six arc blocks: Opening and promise, Problem framing, Educational core, Transition bridge, Offer, Close and Q&A.
4. In the Educational core deliver a named proprietary framework of 3 to 5 actionable steps the audience can apply without buying; each step with its observable deliverable.
5. Articulate OFERTA by value and result, not by features; never by price or with the word that suggests absence of cost. Position the offer as the accompanied and fast way to achieve what the framework permits doing alone.
6. Close with the arc summary table and three conversion errors the flow prevents.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: fix promise, audience, golden rule (teach genuinely), and the single conversion objective (ACCION_DESEADA via CANAL_REGISTRO).
Phase 2 - Architecture: distribute the minutes across the six blocks with proportion guidance (Educational core ~40–50%, Offer ≤20%, remainder distributed); adjust to DURACION_MINUTOS and leave an explicit margin for Q&A.
Phase 3 - Script per block: for each deliver minutes assigned, objective, 3–5 presenter script points (not literal transcript), one slide visual element, and the verbal micro-transition to the next block.
Phase 4 - Transition and offer: build the bridge from the limit of doing it alone (effort, time, risk of error) toward OFERTA, without artificial urgency or invented scarcity; name one anticipated objection and how the script defuses it.
Phase 5 - Close and control: state ACCION_DESEADA as a single verifiable step, add the arc summary table and three prevented errors. Flag all external unverified data as [ASSUMPTION].
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- Transformation promise in one sentence, measurable and aligned to AUDIENCIA's maturity level.
- Six blocks present, each with minutes, objective, script, visual, and micro-transition; minutes sum to DURACION_MINUTOS.
- Educational core receives the largest proportion and delivers a named proprietary framework of 3–5 steps applicable without buying, each with an observable deliverable.
- The transition is natural: connects what was taught with the limit of doing it alone and defuses one objection, without an abrupt shift or artificial urgency.
- OFERTA articulated by value and result; no prices; no word suggesting absence of cost.
- ACCION_DESEADA is a single next step, clear and verifiable, with the execution channel indicated.
- Three conversion errors prevented, each linked to a concrete decision in the script.
- External data verified or labeled [ASSUMPTION]; neutral and professional language, no emojis.
Expected deliverable: webinar script in six blocks with transformation promise, named proprietary framework, arc summary table, and three conversion errors prevented.
spec-comunicacion_copy_titular_4u:
[inputs]
- PRODUCTO_SERVICIO: {{PRODUCTO_SERVICIO}} > Product or service being advertised and what it does in one line
- PUBLICO_OBJETIVO: {{PUBLICO_OBJETIVO}} > Who it is directed at: role, sector, dominant pain or desire
- BENEFICIO_PRINCIPAL: {{BENEFICIO_PRINCIPAL}} > Main verifiable benefit; include a real figure or deadline if one exists
- CANAL: {{CANAL}} > Where it is published: paid ad, email subject line, landing page heading, or other
- LIMITE_CARACTERES: {{LIMITE_CARACTERES}} > Character cap per headline (optional)
- TONO: {{TONO}} > Desired register: direct, consultative, technical, aspirational (optional; default neutral professional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Headlines are needed that win attention at first glance and move the reader to act. The 4U formula (Useful, Urgent, Unique, Ultra-specific, by Michael Masterson / AWAI) elevates a generic headline to one that converts: each U covers a distinct axis of persuasion, and a strong headline rarely maximizes all four at once, so the choice depends on the channel and funnel stage. A set of variants with contrasting angles unlocks A/B tests with clear rationale, reduces spend on messages that do not resonate, and reveals which persuasion axis truly moves the audience.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior direct-response copywriter with a track record optimizing headlines for ads and high-conversion landing pages.
Deliverable: 8 headline variants scored with the 4U formula, with an evaluation table and a final recommendation of 2 finalists for A/B.
1. Confirm the inputs; if PRODUCTO_SERVICIO, PUBLICO_OBJETIVO, BENEFICIO_PRINCIPAL, or CANAL are missing, ask before drafting.
2. Draft 8 numbered variants, each in a distinct angle: direct benefit, resolved objection, competitive contrast, concrete data, before/after transformation, provocative question, proof or authority, and cost of not acting.
3. For each variant include a table with the score from 1 to 5 for Useful, Urgent, Unique, and Ultra-specific, a one-sentence justification per U, and the total score (sum of the 4).
4. If a variant requires data not provided, insert a placeholder in brackets (e.g. [savings figure]) instead of inventing it.
5. If LIMITE_CARACTERES was given, indicate the character count of each headline and adjust those that exceed the cap.
6. Recommend the 2 strongest variants to test, justify the selection criterion, and declare the hypothesis each one validates (which persuasion axis it puts to the test).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Interpret: identify the dominant desire or pain of the audience and the verifiable benefit to highlight; restate in 1–2 lines what is being advertised, for whom, and which persuasive axis the channel prioritizes.
Phase 2 Plan: assign each U a concrete resource (Useful = tangible benefit; Urgent = real deadline or window; Unique = differentiator versus the competition; Ultra-specific = figure or detail). Define the 8 angles and verify they do not overlap.
Phase 3 Execute: draft, score each U with justification, calculate totals, apply the character limit if it exists, and select the 2 finalists with their A/B hypothesis.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
- The 8 variants differ in angle, not reformulations of the same idea.
- Each variant explicitly scores all 4 Us from 1 to 5 with a one-sentence justification and shows the total score.
- No figure or assertion is invented; absent data remains as a placeholder in brackets.
- Zero price mentions; zero use of "free" or equivalents; neutral and professional language, no emojis.
- If LIMITE_CARACTERES was given, all variants respect it and show their count.
- Close with 2 recommended finalists, explicit selection criterion, and A/B hypothesis for each.
Expected deliverable: block of 8 numbered headlines with their 4U table and total score, plus a final recommendation paragraph with A/B hypothesis, ready for A/B testing.
spec-comunicacion_copy_landing_pas:
[inputs]
- PUBLICO_OBJETIVO: {{PUBLICO_OBJETIVO}} > Who you are speaking to: profile, context, level of problem awareness, and the visitor's actual language
- OFERTA: {{OFERTA}} > Product, service, or program being promoted that solves the problem; include the mechanism or core idea if there is one
- PROBLEMA_CENTRAL: {{PROBLEMA_CENTRAL}} > The single pain point or pending result that motivates the audience to act
- ACCION_DESEADA: {{ACCION_DESEADA}} > The only CTA: what the visitor must do (schedule a demo, leave their email, request access, etc.)
- PRUEBA: {{PRUEBA}} > Testimonials, data, cases, logos, or guarantee available; if none, write "No proof"
- TONO_MARCA: {{TONO_MARCA}} > Voice and desired formality level; if not indicated, use neutral professional and approachable
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need the body of a landing page that converts visitors into action. The purpose is to move PUBLICO_OBJETIVO to execute ACCION_DESEADA by solving PROBLEMA_CENTRAL with OFERTA. A focused page with a single CTA converts better than a scattered one: this copy must sustain one promise from start to finish and eliminate every friction and distraction that pulls away from the click. The deliverable is laid out afterward, so each block must be self-contained and reorderable without losing meaning.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: senior conversion copywriter, expert in the PAS framework (Problem-Agitation-Solution) and in direct-response landing pages.
Deliverable: the complete landing body, ready for layout, with marked blocks and a single coherent CTA. Steps:
1. Restate the assignment in one sentence: "Convince PUBLICO_OBJETIVO to ACCION_DESEADA by solving PROBLEMA_CENTRAL". If PUBLICO_OBJETIVO, OFERTA, PROBLEMA_CENTRAL, ACCION_DESEADA, or PRUEBA is missing, ask for it before writing. Do not invent figures or testimonials: use [DATA: ...] markers when evidence is missing, and indicate what evidence would close the gap.
2. PROBLEM: headline that names the problem or desired result in the audience's language (not the brand's), plus a subheadline that makes it concrete; without mentioning the offer yet. Offer 2 headline variants and mark the recommended one with a line explaining why.
3. AGITATION: 2 to 4 brief paragraphs on the cost of not solving it (time, money, opportunity, peace of mind), with specific and verifiable consequences; agitate the real problem, not generic fears or guilt.
4. SOLUTION: present OFERTA as a bridge to the result; 3 to 5 features translated into benefits ("feature, what that means for you"); insert PRUEBA at its highest-impact point (next to the promise or before the CTA); anticipate 2 to 3 real objections with a brief response. If PRUEBA is "No proof", substitute with a process guarantee or demonstrable benefit and mark it as an assumption.
5. SINGLE CTA: one call to action aligned with ACCION_DESEADA, repeated with the same verb and promise in every appearance; exact button text (action + benefit, never "Submit" or "Click here") and one-line microcopy that reduces perceived risk (what happens after the click, no commitment, estimated time).
6. Close with 2 to 3 assumed assumptions to validate and, if applicable, a measurement note (which event defines conversion).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Framing: restate the assignment and confirm or request missing inputs.
Phase 2 Pain research: list the audience's actual language, consequences, and objections before writing; awareness level defines how much context to give in the headline.
Phase 3 PAS writing: write Problem, Agitation, and Solution in that order, one idea per block, without previewing the offer in the problem block.
Phase 4 Conversion close: write the single CTA, button, and microcopy; verify that no competing action or distracting link exists.
Phase 5 Polish: apply style rules, flag assumptions, and verify that every claim is backed by PRUEBA or left as [DATA: ...].
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- The assignment was restated in one sentence with audience, action, and problem.
- Complete PAS structure in order, with marked blocks (Headline, Subheadline, Agitation, Solution, Proof, Objections, CTA, Microcopy); each block is self-contained.
- Headline in the audience's language, not the brand's; the problem block does not preview the offer.
- A single CTA, with no competing secondary actions; same verb and promise in every appearance.
- Features translated into benefits in "feature, what that means for you" format.
- 2 to 3 anticipated objections with a brief and honest response.
- Every claim is backed by PRUEBA or left as [DATA: ...]; zero invented figures or testimonials.
- Button text is action- and benefit-oriented (not "Submit") with microcopy that reduces risk.
- Neutral and professional English, short sentences, second person, no emojis; no prices or the word "free".
Expected deliverable: landing body in marked blocks, ready for layout, with 2 headline variants, plus a list of 2 to 3 assumptions to validate and a conversion measurement note when applicable.
spec-comunicacion_copy_propuesta_valor:

spec-comunicacion_copy_bullets_beneficio:
[inputs]

I have a flat list of features of {{PRODUCTO}} that describes what the product does, but not what {{CLIENTE_OBJETIVO}} gains. A list of features forces the reader to translate value on their own, and most don't: they leave. I need to convert those features into bullets that answer the only question that matters, what's in it for me, to achieve {{RESULTADO_DESEADO}}. Archetype: Senior direct-response copywriter with twelve years writing converting bullets for landing pages, proposals, and product sheets, expert in the Features-Advantages-Benefits (FAB) model and in the laddering technique "and what does that mean for the customer?".
