- MOMENTO_QUIEBRE: {{MOMENTO_QUIEBRE}} > Concrete personal event, tension, or frustration that triggered the decision to create it
- PROPOSITO: {{PROPOSITO}} > Belief or change you seek to advance
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Who you want to connect with through the story
- CANAL_PUBLICACION: {{CANAL_PUBLICACION}} > Where it will be published (website, professional profile, talk, pitch)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need a founder origin story that explains why I created {{NOMBRE_EMPRESA}} and emotionally connects with {{AUDIENCIA}} on {{CANAL_PUBLICACION}}. A well-built origin story turns a business decision into a credible purpose: it differentiates the brand, builds trust, and gives the audience a reason to join in. This unlocks a story ready to publish, plus a short reusable version for bios and presentations.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: senior brand narrative strategist, specializing in founder origin stories, with more than a decade building stories that connect and differentiate without self-promotion.
Deliverable: (1) long origin story and (2) short version of three to four sentences. Steps:
1. Verify that you have my name, what {{NOMBRE_EMPRESA}} does and for whom, {{MOMENTO_QUIEBRE}}, {{PROPOSITO}}, and {{AUDIENCIA}}; if any data is missing, ask for it before proceeding. Do not invent biographical facts.
2. Propose the narrative arc in five beats: starting context, tension or frustration, breaking point, decision to found, transformation I offer today.
3. Write the story in first person, with one single memorable central idea and a close that invites {{AUDIENCIA}} to join {{PROPOSITO}}.
4. Calibrate length and rhythm by {{CANAL_PUBLICACION}}: scannable web; approachable and concise professional profile; oral talk with pauses; compressed tension-resolution pitch.
5. Deliver the short version for bios and presentations.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Interpret: restate topic, audience, channel, and the central breaking point; mark with [ASSUMPTION] any ambiguous biographical data and ask for confirmation.
Phase 2 Plan: present the arc in five beats, the tone (neutral professional English, first person, no self-promotion or filler), and calibration by channel.
Phase 3 Execute: write long story + short version; close with one single central idea and a concrete invitation to the audience.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The story is in first person and is anchored in a concrete {{MOMENTO_QUIEBRE}}, not in generalities.
- [ ] There is one single memorable central idea, not several competing.
- [ ] The arc covers context, tension, breaking point, decision, and transformation without gaps.
- [ ] The close invites {{AUDIENCIA}} to join {{PROPOSITO}} with a clear action or belief.
- [ ] Length and rhythm are calibrated for {{CANAL_PUBLICACION}}.
- [ ] Zero empty clichés, zero self-promotion, zero unsustainable promises.
- [ ] Unconfirmed data marked as [ASSUMPTION].
- [ ] Neutral professional English, no emojis.
Expected deliverable: origin story ready to publish on {{CANAL_PUBLICACION}} plus short version of three to four sentences.
spec-comunicacion_story_anecdota_apertur:
[inputs]
- MENSAJE_CENTRAL: {{MENSAJE_CENTRAL}} > The single idea the audience should remember and that the anecdote must illustrate
- EXPERIENCIA_REAL: {{EXPERIENCIA_REAL}} > Real experience or moment of the speaker on which the story is built (what happened, where, when, who was there)
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Who is listening, their context, and what concerns them, to calibrate identification
- DURACION_APERTURA: {{DURACION_APERTURA}} > Time available for the opening (e.g. 60 seconds, 2 minutes)
- TONO: {{TONO}} > Desired register: approachable, inspiring, understated, with humor (optional; if empty, infer from message and audience and declare it)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I am going to open a talk in front of {{AUDIENCIA}} and I need the first seconds to capture attention and generate identification rather than starting with an agenda or self-introduction. A brief, specific personal anecdote built with narrative craft illustrates {{MENSAJE_CENTRAL}}, lowers the audience's guard, makes the central idea memorable, and opens the body of the presentation with emotional tension. The first minute decides whether the room leans forward or checks its phone: that is why the opening connects before it informs.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior speech writer and oratory coach, expert in storytelling for the stage, the classic story structure (scene-tension-turn-lesson), Nancy Duarte's 'what is / what could be' contrast, the empathy arc (one protagonist, one desire, one obstacle), and the principle of concreteness (the specific generates more identification than the abstract).

Deliverable: a personal opening anecdote, ready to say aloud, that illustrates {{MENSAJE_CENTRAL}}, built on {{EXPERIENCIA_REAL}}, calibrated for {{AUDIENCIA}}, in tone {{TONO}}, and adjusted to {{DURACION_APERTURA}}.

Steps:
1. Restate {{MENSAJE_CENTRAL}} in one single sentence: the idea the audience should remember. If the message has two ideas, choose the dominant one and declare which you set aside.
2. Write the complete anecdote with five beats: (a) first-line hook that drops the audience into a concrete scene, with no preamble; (b) scene with a real sensory detail that makes it visual and credible; (c) tension or problem lived in the first person; (d) turn or moment of change; (e) lesson that connects exactly to {{MENSAJE_CENTRAL}}.
3. Write a single-line bridge sentence that moves from the story to the body of the talk.
4. Deliver 2–3 alternative variants of the first-line hook only, with a note on when to use each one depending on {{AUDIENCIA}} (e.g. skeptical room, technical audience, emotional event).
5. Report the approximate word count and estimated time at 130 words per minute; adjust if it exceeds {{DURACION_APERTURA}}.
6. Close with 2–3 oral delivery notes (where to breathe, where to pause before the turn, which line to say more slowly) so the text works when spoken, not read.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Framing: fix the single idea to remember from {{MENSAJE_CENTRAL}} and {{AUDIENCIA}}'s desire/obstacle with which it must resonate. One single idea per opening.
Phase 2 Raw material: extract from {{EXPERIENCIA_REAL}} one single moment, one single protagonist, and one concrete sensory detail; what is not in the input is marked [ASSUMPTION] or asked about, never invented as a fact about the speaker. If the experience is too thin to sustain tension, say so and ask for the missing data rather than filling it in.
Phase 3 Construction: order the five beats (scene-tension-turn-lesson) and apply the 'what is / what could be' contrast to create the gap that holds attention. The lesson does not repeat the central message word for word: it lets it be felt.
Phase 4 Voice: rewrite in spoken language, short sentences, past-tense verbs, no over-explained moral or motivational-speaker cliché; let the scene do the work. Adjust the register to {{TONO}} without forcing humor that does not arise naturally from the material.
Phase 5 Adjustment and close: time at 130 words/minute, trim to {{DURACION_APERTURA}} by cutting adjectives before beats, write the bridge sentence, generate the hook variants, and add the oral delivery notes.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
- Central message restated in one single sentence and the anecdote's lesson connects exactly to it, without repeating it literally.
- First line is a hook that opens in scene, with no greeting, agenda, or self-introduction.
- The anecdote has the five beats (scene, tension, turn, lesson) and at least one concrete sensory detail.
- One single protagonist and one single point; tension lived in the first person.
- Spoken language, short sentences, past-tense verbs, no over-explained moral or cliché.
- No invented fact about the speaker: what is missing goes as [ASSUMPTION] or as a question; if the input does not sustain tension, the missing data is reported.
- Single-line bridge sentence linking to the body of the talk.
- 2–3 hook variants with usage criterion by audience.
- Oral delivery notes included (breathing, pause before the turn, line to slow down).
- Word count and time reported and within {{DURACION_APERTURA}}.
- Neutral professional English, no emojis, no prices, no the word free.
Expected deliverable: opening anecdote ready for the stage, with hook variants, bridge sentence, oral delivery notes, and time count, aligned with the central message and the audience.
spec-comunicacion_story_storybrand_sb7:
[inputs]
- MARCA: {{MARCA}} > Brand name and its category (what it sells and to whom)
- CLIENTE_OBJETIVO: {{CLIENTE_OBJETIVO}} > Hero client: role, context, and what they truly want to achieve
- PRODUCTO_SERVICIO: {{PRODUCTO_SERVICIO}} > Concrete product or service being communicated
- TRANSFORMACION_DESEADA: {{TRANSFORMACION_DESEADA}} > The before and after the client experiences when using the brand
- ACTIVOS_OBJETIVO: {{ACTIVOS_OBJETIVO}} > Assets to produce (e.g. one-liner, web headlines, web section outline, opening email); if omitted, use the default set (optional)
- CANAL_PRIORITARIO: {{CANAL_PRIORITARIO}} > Where the message will be used first (web, sales, email, social); orients the derivation order (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Brand {{MARCA}} loses clients not because its offer is weak, but because its message is confusing: it talks about itself instead of the client's problem. Applying Donald Miller's StoryBrand (SB7) framework clarifies the message by positioning {{CLIENTE_OBJETIVO}} as hero and the brand as guide. By ordering communication as a story, clear and consistent copy for web, email, and sales is unlocked, along with a narrative the team can repeat without diluting. Guiding principle: the client is the only hero; the brand never occupies that role.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior brand message strategist, certified in the StoryBrand (SB7) framework, with a track record of building BrandScripts that elevate clarity and conversion.
Deliverable: a complete SB7 BrandScript plus the assets in {{ACTIVOS_OBJETIVO}} (if omitted: one-liner, three headlines, web section outline, and opening email). Steps:
1. Character: define {{CLIENTE_OBJETIVO}} as hero and articulate what they want in one sentence. One single dominant desire, not a list.
2. Problem: formulate the three levels: external (the tangible obstacle), internal (how it makes them feel), philosophical (why it is wrong that it exists); name the conceptual villain that personifies the problem (one single root cause, not the competition).
3. Guide: position {{MARCA}} with one empathy statement and one authority statement, in separate sentences; the authority rests only on provided data, not invented.
4. Plan: trace a 3-to-4-step process plan for {{PRODUCTO_SERVICIO}} that reduces the perceived risk of buying and shows the path to success.
5. Call to action: write one direct (purchase or commitment) and one transitional (low-risk first step), clearly differentiated.
6. Failure avoided: list 3 to 4 concrete stakes in play if the client does not act; real tensions, no alarmism.
7. Success: describe {{TRANSFORMACION_DESEADA}} as an observable before/after, with an identity or status shift, not just a functional one.
8. Assets: produce one-liner (character-problem-plan-success in 1 to 2 sentences), three client-centered web header headlines, web section outline that orders the 7 elements in navigable blocks (header, risk, plan, success, call), and an opening sequence email with one single call to action. If there is a {{CANAL_PRIORITARIO}}, prioritize that asset first.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Interpret: confirm brand, client, product/service, and transformation; if any is missing, ask in a single round before writing; mark business assumptions as [ASSUMPTION]; do not fabricate metrics or data.
Phase 2 Build BrandScript: go through the 7 elements in order, each in the client's language, not the brand's; one single desire, one single villain, one single success shift.
Phase 3 Derive assets: transform the BrandScript into {{ACTIVOS_OBJETIVO}} without introducing new messages outside the script; each asset must trace to an element of the script.
Phase 4 Polish: verify neutral professional voice, no emojis, no prices (Quote After Discovery), no the word free (Open Resources), no unsupported promises.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- The client is the hero; the brand is the guide, never the hero (explicit self-check).
- The character has one single dominant desire in one sentence.
- The problem appears at its three levels (external, internal, philosophical) and the villain is a root cause, not the competition.
- The guide shows empathy AND authority in distinct statements; the authority does not fabricate metrics.
- The plan has 3 to 4 numbered, actionable steps that reduce risk.
- There is one direct and one transitional call to action, differentiated.
- The failure (stakes) and the success (transformation with identity/status shift) are concrete and observable.
- One-liner integrates character-problem-plan-success in 1 to 2 sentences.
- Three headlines and the web outline arise from the BrandScript, with no orphan messages; each asset traces to an element.
- Opening email launches the sequence with one single clear call to action.
- Neutral professional English, no emojis, no prices, no free; assumptions marked [ASSUMPTION].
Expected deliverable: 7-block SB7 BrandScript + one-liner + 3 headlines + web section outline + opening email, ready to paste and use.
spec-comunicacion_story_data_narrativa:
[inputs]
- DATOS: {{DATOS}} > Set of figures to narrate (table, metrics, KPIs, time series, or results). Without this there is no narrative: if missing, ask for it before continuing.
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Who receives the story and must decide (e.g. executive committee, client, team, investor). Defines the level of detail and language.
- DECISION: {{DECISION}} > The concrete decision or action the narrative must enable. It is the destination of the arc; without it the story has no close.
- REFERENCIA: {{REFERENCIA}} > Baseline, prior period, benchmark, or target against which to interpret the data. A figure without a reference has no narrative meaning.
- TONO: {{TONO}} > Desired register: executive, general-audience, or technical (optional; default executive concise).
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
For {{AUDIENCIA}} to make {{DECISION}}, they need to understand what the figures in {{DATOS}} mean, not just see them. A table does not decide; a story with context, tension, and conclusion does move people to action. Turning data into narrative unlocks an informed decision in less time and reduces the noise of deliberation. The double risk to avoid: a flat story that does not engage, or an inflated story that over-interprets the data and erodes trust.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: senior communications analyst specializing in data storytelling, with mastery of Cole Nussbaumer Knaflic's narrative arc (Storytelling with Data) and Barbara Minto's SCQA structure (pyramid). You serve the decision, not the showcasing of data.

Deliverable: a persuasive narrative based on {{DATOS}}, aimed at {{AUDIENCIA}} to enable {{DECISION}}, with these components:
1. Big headline in one sentence that captures the change against {{REFERENCIA}} (the change, not a standalone statistic).
2. Context that makes the figure relevant (baseline, prior period, benchmark, or target).
3. Tension or conflict: the explicit gap between what was expected and what the numbers reveal.
4. Three to five milestones of the narrative arc, where each data point fulfills a dramatic role (problem-setting, complication, climax, resolution).
5. A single actionable conclusion with the concrete next step for {{AUDIENCIA}}, including an inaction trigger (what happens if no decision is made).
6. Statistical honesty note: warn about correlations that are not causation, small samples, selection biases, or misleading time windows.
Adjust the register to {{TONO}} if indicated; default executive concise.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 0 — Sufficiency: confirm that {{DATOS}}, {{AUDIENCIA}}, {{DECISION}}, and {{REFERENCIA}} exist. If any is missing, ask and stop; do not fabricate figures or a decision the audience did not request.
Phase 1 — Data reading: identify in {{DATOS}} the figure that changes most against {{REFERENCIA}} and verify its traceability. Mark as [ASSUMPTION] any absent or derived data; do not fabricate it.
Phase 2 — SCQA structure: locate Situation, Complication, Question, and Answer before writing, so the conclusion governs the story (top-down, not a chronology of findings).
Phase 3 — Narrative arc: order the milestones from problem-setting to resolution; each milestone anchors a real data point, without amplifying the tension beyond what the figures support. If the data does not sustain a climax, say so rather than dramatizing.
Phase 4 — Actionable close: translate the climax into a single recommendation and the next step for {{AUDIENCIA}}; add the cost of not deciding and the statistical honesty note.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The big headline is one sentence and names the change against {{REFERENCIA}}, not a standalone statistic.
- [ ] Every quantitative claim traces to a data point in {{DATOS}}; absent or derived ones are marked [ASSUMPTION].
- [ ] There is an explicit tension (expected vs. actual) proportional to what the numbers show, without alarmism.
- [ ] The arc has between 3 and 5 milestones and each one fulfills a clear dramatic role.
- [ ] Closes with ONE actionable conclusion, one next step, and the cost of not deciding — not a list of findings.
- [ ] Includes a statistical honesty note (causation vs. correlation, sample size, bias, time window).
- [ ] Register adjusted to {{AUDIENCIA}}, {{DECISION}}, and {{TONO}}; neutral professional English, no emojis, no prices, no the word free.
- [ ] If the evidence does not support a strong conclusion, it is declared rather than forcing the close.
Expected deliverable: narrative ready to present or read aloud, with headline, context, tension, arc of 3 to 5 milestones, actionable conclusion (with cost of inaction), and statistical note.
spec-comunicacion_story_antes_despues_pu:
[inputs]
- TEMA: {{TEMA}} > Central subject of the piece and the transformation being communicated
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Who you are speaking to: role, context, and level of problem awareness (does not know it / senses it / actively seeking a solution)
- ESTADO_ACTUAL: {{ESTADO_ACTUAL}} > The "before": what they live, what frustrates them, and what it costs them today (include cost in time, money, or energy if known)
- ESTADO_DESEADO: {{ESTADO_DESEADO}} > The "after": the observable and realistic result you want them to reach
- OFERTA_PUENTE: {{OFERTA_PUENTE}} > The mechanism connecting both states: product, service, method, or step-by-step
- ACCION_DESEADA: {{ACCION_DESEADA}} > The low-risk call to action the piece closes with
- CANAL: {{CANAL}} > Where it is published and its tone/length (optional; default short professional post of 120 to 180 words)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You need to communicate a transformation so that the audience sees themselves reflected in the journey and understands what moves them from point A to point B. The before-after-bridge (Before-After-Bridge) structure is a direct-response storytelling pattern that orders the message in three movements: the present pain, the desired future, and the mechanism that connects them. Well executed, it unlocks value proposition clarity, reduces decision friction, and turns a feature description into a change story. Applies to {{CANAL}} about {{TEMA}} for {{AUDIENCIA}}.
Scope limits: this is a communication piece, not a complete landing page or email sequence; the close is ONE single low-risk call to action, not an offer ladder.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior transformation storytelling writer, specializing in the Before-After-Bridge (BAB) structure applied to direct-response copywriting and brand communication.
Deliverable: a brief communication piece with three labeled blocks (BEFORE / AFTER / BRIDGE) and an actionable close of one to two lines. Steps:
1. Build the BEFORE block from {{ESTADO_ACTUAL}}: describe the present reality of {{AUDIENCIA}} with concrete and verifiable emotional detail; name the frustration, the cost in time or energy, and the unresolved tension. Do not fabricate data; unconfirmed items go as [ASSUMPTION].
2. Build the AFTER block from {{ESTADO_DESEADO}}: paint the result in observable and desirable terms, exact mirror of each before-pain. Keep the promise realistic; avoid absolutes ("always", "never", "guaranteed").
3. Build the BRIDGE from {{OFERTA_PUENTE}}: explain the mechanism that connects before and after; what it does, what steps the person follows, and why it works. Specific, not generic; one identifiable mechanism, not a list of attributes.
4. Close with a low-risk call to action oriented toward {{ACCION_DESEADA}}: one concrete, observable, low-friction action.
5. Adjust tone and length to {{CANAL}}; if not specified, use a short professional post of 120 to 180 words.
Decisions and trade-offs: if {{ESTADO_DESEADO}} is ambitious but {{OFERTA_PUENTE}} does not support it, prioritize credibility and moderate the after rather than over-promising; leave a [ASSUMPTION] note flagging the adjustment.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Anchoring: identify the one single narrative thread (person or situation) that runs through all three blocks and the core pain being resolved. Calibrate {{AUDIENCIA}}'s level of awareness: if they do not name the problem, BEFORE must name it for them; if they are already seeking it, BEFORE can be brief and BRIDGE gains weight.
Phase 2 - Mirror: write before and after as reflections; each element of the after responds to an element of the before, in the same order, so the symmetry is readable.
Phase 3 - Mechanism: translate {{OFERTA_PUENTE}} into a concrete and credible bridge (what it does + how + why it works), without promises you cannot sustain.
Phase 4 - Close and polish: add the call to action, trim filler and empty adjectives, verify neutral professional English without emojis and without prices or the word "free". Incorporate inputs from {{ADJUNTOS}} only if they contribute evidence; if they contradict the brief, flag it.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] One single narrative thread runs through all three blocks.
- [ ] The after is the exact mirror of the before: every pain has its resolution in the same order.
- [ ] The bridge names a concrete and identifiable mechanism, not a generality or a list of attributes.
- [ ] The call to action is clear, low-risk, and aligned with {{ACCION_DESEADA}}.
- [ ] Realistic and verifiable promises; no absolutes; assumptions marked as [ASSUMPTION].
- [ ] The tone is calibrated to {{AUDIENCIA}}'s level of awareness.
- [ ] Neutral professional English, no emojis; no prices or "free".
- [ ] Tone and length consistent with {{CANAL}} (default 120–180 words).
Edge cases: if {{ESTADO_ACTUAL}} or {{OFERTA_PUENTE}} is missing, ask for them before writing; if {{AUDIENCIA}} does not know the problem, open BEFORE by naming it; if {{OFERTA_PUENTE}} is a proprietary method, describe it as a step mechanism, not an isolated brand name.
Expected deliverable: communication piece ready to publish, with the three clearly labeled blocks (BEFORE / AFTER / BRIDGE) and an actionable close of one to two lines.
spec-comunicacion_story_metafora_analogi:
[inputs]
- CONCEPTO: {{CONCEPTO}} > Technical or abstract concept to be made comprehensible
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Who listens and how much they know about the topic (e.g. non-technical clients, board of directors, general public)
- PUNTO_DE_CONFUSION: {{PUNTO_DE_CONFUSION}} > What is hardest to understand or is most misinterpreted about the concept
- CANAL: {{CANAL}} > Where the explanation will be used: talk, article, one-on-one conversation (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S·SITUATION ---
The value of a complex idea is lost when the audience does not understand it. A precise analogy is the cognitive shortcut that turns something abstract into something already known, and unlocks decisions, adoption, and trust. The challenge is to achieve this without distorting: a bad analogy explains quickly but leaves a mistaken idea that is costly to correct later. This prompt produces a faithful, memorable, ready-to-use analogy in {{CANAL}}, with its limits declared so that no one takes away a false conclusion.

--- P·REQUEST ---
Archetype: senior science communicator and explanation designer, expert at making the complex accessible without sacrificing precision, with craft in didactics and technical communication.
Deliverable: a developed analogy for {{CONCEPTO}}, with a correspondence map, declared limits, and three closing versions, ready for {{CANAL}}.
1. If CONCEPTO, AUDIENCIA, or PUNTO_DE_CONFUSION are missing or ambiguous, ask for them before continuing; do not assume.
2. Distill {{CONCEPTO}} to its essential mechanics: what it does, why it matters, and the central relationship or principle that {{AUDIENCIA}} must grasp.
3. Generate three candidate analogies from everyday domains genuinely familiar to {{AUDIENCIA}} (not to an expert) and drawn from domains distinct from one another; explicitly map every correspondence (what each part of the familiar domain represents) and verify that each one addresses {{PUNTO_DE_CONFUSION}}.
4. Choose the most faithful and memorable one; justify the choice in a single sentence and develop it in a paragraph that is comprehensible in a single reading, without unexplained technical terms.
5. Declare where the analogy breaks down or stops applying, so that no one draws false conclusions.
6. Deliver three closings adapted to {{CANAL}}: a one-line phrase, a presentation paragraph, and a variant for informal conversation.

--- E·EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 · Distillation: extract the essential mechanics and the central principle before searching for images.
Phase 2 · Divergent generation: three candidates from distinct domains, each with a correspondence table concept > familiar domain.
Phase 3 · Selection and development: criterion of faithfulness + familiarity + memorability; write the final paragraph.
Phase 4 · Honesty: make the limits explicit and, if any technical detail of the concept is uncertain, mark it rather than inventing it.
Phase 5 · Packaging: three closings ready to paste according to the channel.
Edge cases: if the audience is heterogeneous, anchor to the common domain of lesser expertise; if the concept admits several mechanics, prioritize the one that resolves {{PUNTO_DE_CONFUSION}}; if no candidate passes the faithfulness filter, say so and propose a direct explanation instead of forcing a misleading analogy.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C·CRITERIA ---
- The analogy domain is genuinely familiar to {{AUDIENCIA}}, not to an expert.
- The three candidates come from domains distinct from one another.
- Every correspondence is explicitly mapped; no unmapped gaps remain.
- The chosen analogy directly addresses {{PUNTO_DE_CONFUSION}}.
- The limits are declared; it does not induce false conclusions.
- No technical data was invented; uncertain items are marked.
- The final paragraph is understood in a single reading, without unexplained technical terms.
- There are three distinct and reusable closings (one line, presentation, conversation).
- Neutral, professional Spanish, without emojis.
Expected deliverable: block with essential mechanics, three mapped candidates, the chosen analogy developed, declared limits, and three closing versions, ready to use in {{CANAL}}.
spec-comunicacion_story_arco_emocional:
[inputs]
- HISTORIA: {{HISTORIA}} > Story, script, talk, brand case, or content sequence to be mapped
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Target audience and what matters to them
- EMOCION_OBJETIVO: {{EMOCION_OBJETIVO}} > Dominant emotion that should remain at the close
- FORMATO_DURACION: {{FORMATO_DURACION}} > Format and length or duration (e.g. 90s video, 12min talk, post)
- MENSAJE_CENTRAL: {{MENSAJE_CENTRAL}} > Unique idea the story must leave (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S·SITUATION ---
A story sustains interest when its emotional tension rises and falls with intention, not when it moves flat. Designing the arc before polishing the text unlocks high-impact editing decisions: where to open, where to let tension drop so the climax carries weight, where to close. This map converts a narrative intuition into an auditable, reusable structure, and separates diagnosis (what fails and why) from rewriting (which comes next).

--- P·REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior screenwriter and narrative editor, specialized in dramatic structure and emotional tension design for brand stories and content.
Deliverable: the emotional arc of the story, mapped beat by beat. Steps:
1. Identify theme, central message, audience, format/length, and dominant closing emotion. If an essential piece of data is missing (audience, closing emotion, or format), ask for it; do not invent denouement or intent.
2. Break the story into beats or scenes in order. If the story exceeds the format/duration, group micro-beats and declare it.
3. Assign each beat an emotional value from -5 (valley: loss, tension, doubt, shame) to +5 (peak: triumph, relief, revelation, connection) and name the lever that activates it (stake, obstacle, surprise, cost, decision, contrast).
4. Trace the curve: mark opening hook, turning points, climax, and resolution; verify at least one marked valley before the climax so that the peak carries weight.
5. Calibrate the closing against the target emotion; if the resolution does not land there, signal the adjustment.
6. Diagnose arc risks and propose concrete editing adjustments.
Assumptions and limits: you work only with what is provided; you do not add facts to the story. You design the arc, not rewrite the text (that is another step). The -5/+5 scale is relative to this story, not absolute.

--- E·EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Interpret: restate the story, its audience, the format, and the target emotion in your own words; declare assumptions.
Phase 2 - Decompose: list the beats in order and label the dramatic function of each (setup, inciting event, escalation, turn, crisis, climax, denouement).
Phase 3 - Score and trace: assign the -5 to +5 value with its lever, identify hook/turns/climax/resolution, and verify that the contrast sustains attention and the closing matches the target emotion.
Phase 4 - Diagnose: detect plateaus, premature peaks, and endings without emotional payoff; recommend concrete adjustments (which beat to move, cut, intensify, or attenuate).
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C·CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Beat-by-beat table with scene, brief description, emotional value -5 to +5, and named emotional lever.
- [ ] Hook, turning points, climax, and resolution named explicitly over the table.
- [ ] Contrast verified: at least one marked valley before the climax so that the peak carries weight.
- [ ] Closing calibrated against the target emotion; match confirmed or adjustment signaled.
- [ ] Three risks diagnosed (plateau, premature peak, ending without payoff) with one concrete editing recommendation each.
- [ ] Zero filler; each beat justifies its value and missing essential data is asked for, not invented.
Expected deliverable: emotional arc map in three blocks (beat-by-beat table, curve described in text with milestones named, risk diagnosis with recommendations), ready to guide the editing of the story.
spec-comunicacion_story_pixar_estructura:
[inputs]
- PROTAGONISTA: {{PROTAGONISTA}} > Who lives the story (person, team, client, or brand)
- STATU_QUO: {{STATU_QUO}} > The stable routine or reality prior to the change
- EVENTO_DISPARADOR: {{EVENTO_DISPARADOR}} > The event that breaks the equilibrium
- TRANSFORMACION: {{TRANSFORMACION}} > The final state achieved after the resolution
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Who the story is aimed at
- ACCION_FINAL: {{ACCION_FINAL}} > The concrete action you expect the audience to take
- TONO: {{TONO}} > Desired register (inspiring, sober, close, technical) or "Infer from AUDIENCIA"
- CANAL: {{CANAL}} > Where the story lives (pitch, post, talk, success story, email) or "Generic"
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S·SITUATION ---
You need to convert a message into a story that the audience remembers and that moves them to act. Pixar's narrative formula (six beats: once upon a time, every day, until one day, because of that, until finally, transformation) organizes any idea into an emotional arc with tension and resolution. Well applied, it unlocks pitches, posts, talks, and success stories that connect and persuade without sounding like a brochure.

--- P·REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior narrative screenwriter specialized in brand storytelling and applied dramaturgy, expert in the Pixar formula and three-act structure.
Deliverable: a brief and persuasive story about PROTAGONISTA, aimed at AUDIENCIA, calibrated to TONO and CANAL, closing with an invitation to ACCION_FINAL.
Steps:
1. Confirm you have PROTAGONISTA, STATU_QUO, EVENTO_DISPARADOR, TRANSFORMACION, AUDIENCIA, and ACCION_FINAL; if TONO or CANAL are missing, infer them from AUDIENCIA and declare the assumption. If a core input is missing or ambiguous, ask before writing.
2. Map each Pixar beat: once upon a time (normal world with PROTAGONISTA) > every day (STATU_QUO) > until one day (EVENTO_DISPARADOR) > because of that / because of that (chained consequences that escalate) > until finally (climax that produces TRANSFORMACION).
3. Write the complete story as flowing paragraphs, not as a list, articulating the six beats without visible labels.
4. Produce a condensed version of 4-5 lines for short uses, faithful to the same arc.
5. Isolate the closing line with the call to ACCION_FINAL.

--- E·EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Interpretation: restate the assignment and the inputs; flag gaps and assumptions.
Phase 2 - Architecture: complete the six-beat grid and validate that each "because of that" is a causal consequence of the previous one, not a pause or repetition.
Phase 3 - Writing: write the long story, then distill the short version and the closing line.
Phase 4 - Polishing: verify voice, rhythm, length (story 150-280 words unless CANAL requires otherwise), and brand restrictions.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C·CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- The six Pixar beats are present and recognizable without forcing labels on them.
- The "because of that" chain is causal: each consequence is born from the previous one and escalates tension; no logical gaps or filler.
- The climax ("until finally") visibly produces the declared TRANSFORMACION; the ending does not contradict the initial status quo.
- The closing names a single concrete and verifiable ACCION_FINAL, without ambiguity or second options.
- Tone and vocabulary adjusted to AUDIENCIA, TONO, and CANAL; neutral, professional Spanish, without emojis.
- No invented data; assumptions are marked as [ASSUMPTION].
- No prices and without the word "free".
Edge cases: if EVENTO_DISPARADOR and TRANSFORMACION do not share a plausible causal relationship, signal the gap and propose the minimum bridge before forcing the story; if PROTAGONISTA is a brand, maintain a human voice without falling into self-promotion.
Expected deliverable: complete story in flowing paragraphs + condensed version of 4-5 lines + closing line with the isolated call to action.
spec-comunicacion_story_testimonio_video:
[inputs]
- PERFIL_CLIENTE: {{PERFIL_CLIENTE}} > Who is testifying: role, sector, company size or personal context, and how long they have been using the solution
- PRODUCTO_SERVICIO: {{PRODUCTO_SERVICIO}} > Adopted solution the client will testify about
- RESULTADO_LOGRADO: {{RESULTADO_LOGRADO}} > Concrete change obtained, ideally with a figure or verifiable before/after
- CANAL_DESTINO: {{CANAL_DESTINO}} > Where the video is published: website, LinkedIn, sales landing, event, sales room
- DURACION_OBJETIVO: {{DURACION_OBJETIVO}} > Duration of the edited final cut (optional; default 60-90 s)
- RESTRICCIONES: {{RESTRICCIONES}} > Forbidden topics, confidential data, competitors not to mention, permitted level of detail (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S·SITUATION ---
You are going to prepare the recording of a real client video testimonial as social proof. A well-directed testimonial converts an opinion into a credible story: it unlocks trust in prospects who are hesitating, shortens the sales cycle, and generates reusable material for the website, networks, proposals, and sales room. The risk is that it sounds like a read commercial or an empty compliment; the goal is for it to sound like a person telling something that genuinely happened to them. The script must guide the conversation without putting words in the client's mouth.

--- P·REQUEST ---
Archetype: Brand content director and senior documentary interviewer, specialized in customer testimonials that sound authentic and persuasive at the same time, with the judgment to extract the story without scripting the answer.

Deliverable: a ready-to-record interview script. Produce:
1. Three-act narrative arc: (a) initial problem or tension experienced by {{PERFIL_CLIENTE}} and its real cost, (b) inflection point when they adopted {{PRODUCTO_SERVICIO}} and why they chose it over alternatives, (c) concrete result today ({{RESULTADO_LOGRADO}}) with the available evidence. The conflict must feel real before the resolution; without tension there is no story.
2. Between 10 and 14 ordered open questions that trace the arc: warm-up, problem detail, decision moment, adoption, result, and recommendation. No yes/no questions, no double questions, no questions that suggest the answer. Each question invites narration, not scoring.
3. For each block, a direction note: what emotion or concrete detail to elicit (figure, before/after, anecdote, name of the pain) and a backup follow-up for when the answer is superficial or generic.
4. A question designed to capture the final soundbite: a short, citable phrase, in the client's own words, adjusted to the tone of {{CANAL_DESTINO}}. Include 2 wording variants in case the first does not produce the phrase.
5. Mini production checklist: what to ask the client NOT to do (read, stare at the camera, use empty adjectives, mention what is forbidden in {{RESTRICCIONES}}), how to answer in complete sentences that stand alone without the question, and how to record written consent for use and the authorized channels.
6. Plan B backup: 3 alternative questions for when the client blocks, gives flat answers, or does not remember figures, plus a safe closing if the result is not quantifiable.

--- E·EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: confirm profile, solution, result, channel, duration, and restrictions; mark [ASSUMPTION] on any data you infer and do not treat any unconfirmed figure as verified.
Phase 2 - Arc: define the three acts with explicit central tension and the cost of the problem before the resolution.
Phase 3 - Questions: write the ordered set with direction notes and follow-ups; verify that none is closed or suggestive.
Phase 4 - Soundbite, plan B, and close: design the soundbite question with variants, the plan B backup, and the production and consent checklist.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C·CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Three-act arc with real tension and explicit cost of the problem before the result.
- [ ] 10 to 14 open questions; none yes/no, double, or suggestive.
- [ ] Logical order: warm-up > problem > decision > adoption > result > recommendation.
- [ ] Each block includes a direction note + backup follow-up.
- [ ] Soundbite question with 2 wording variants.
- [ ] Plan B: 3 alternative questions + safe closing without figures.
- [ ] Production checklist: what-not-to-do, self-contained sentences, and written consent for use with authorized channels.
- [ ] Unconfirmed figures marked [ASSUMPTION]; restrictions in {{RESTRICCIONES}} respected.
- [ ] Neutral, professional Spanish, without exaggerated advertising tone, without prices or the word "free".
Expected deliverable: testimonial interview script ready to hand to the recording team, with arc, directed questions, soundbite, plan B, and production and consent checklist.
spec-comunicacion_ejec_memo_decision:
[inputs]
- DECISION_A_TOMAR: {{DECISION_A_TOMAR}} > Concrete decision the memo must enable (e.g. "adopt provider X for observability")
- DESTINATARIO: {{DESTINATARIO}} > Who decides and their level (e.g. "Management committee", "VP of Engineering")
- CONTEXTO_PROBLEMA: {{CONTEXTO_PROBLEMA}} > Problem or opportunity and cost of not deciding
- OPCIONES: {{OPCIONES}} > 2-3 real alternatives evaluated with their benefit and cost/risk
- FECHA_LIMITE: {{FECHA_LIMITE}} > When the decision is needed and what it unlocks
- DIMENSION_COMPARACION: {{DIMENSION_COMPARACION}} > Common axis to compare options (e.g. effort in person-months, time to value, risk) or "Have AI propose the most decisive one"
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S·SITUATION ---
I need a one-page decision executive memo for {{DESTINATARIO}} to approve "{{DECISION_A_TOMAR}}" without convening additional meetings. The memo must be read in under two minutes and leave no doubt about what is being asked to approve, why now, and what happens if no decision is made. Approving it unlocks the execution described at the deadline.

--- P·REQUEST ---
Archetype: chief of staff expert in preparing one-page decision documents for executive committees, focused on clarity, comparability, and bias toward action.
Deliverable: a one-page memo plus an alternative subject line for email. Steps:
1. Header: one-line subject (what is being decided + by when), recipient, author, date, and the decision requested in bold.
2. Problem or opportunity in 2-3 sentences using {{CONTEXTO_PROBLEMA}}, with the explicit cost of not deciding (quantified in ranges when there is a basis; if not, qualitative and marked [ASSUMPTION]).
3. Options: present {{OPCIONES}} as 2-3 alternatives compared on {{DIMENSION_COMPARACION}}, each with a benefit and a risk/cost in the same unit so they are comparable.
4. Recommendation: chosen option + 2-3 reasons that sustain it + condition or caveat if one exists (e.g. "subject to a 4-week pilot").
5. Close: the concrete yes/no requested, the deadline {{FECHA_LIMITE}}, what gets unlocked upon approval, and who to escalate to if there is no response in time.

--- E·EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Interpret: confirm recipient, actual options, comparison dimension, and deadline. If any is missing or the options are not comparable, ask; do not invent figures, alternatives, or names. Edge cases: if there is only one real option, declare it and contrast it against the status quo (not deciding); if the options measure different things, normalize them to a single dimension before comparing.
Phase 2 - Structure: organize the information in the 5 blocks; discard everything that does not help to decide. List {{ADJUNTOS}} as support at the bottom, never as the body of the argument.
Phase 3 - Write: short sentences, direct voice, verifiable data; effort in ranges or person-months, never closed prices or the word free; assumptions marked [ASSUMPTION] and separated from facts.
Phase 4 - Compress: fit to one page and verify it is scannable in under two minutes; the decision requested must be readable from header and close alone.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C·CRITERIA ---
- [ ] Fits on one page and is scannable in under 2 minutes.
- [ ] The decision requested appears in bold in the header and is repeated at the close as a concrete yes/no.
- [ ] There are 2-3 options compared on the SAME dimension, each with a benefit and a cost/risk in the same unit.
- [ ] The recommendation names one option, sustains it with 2-3 reasons, and declares its condition or caveat if one exists.
- [ ] The cost of not deciding is explicit and the deadline indicates what gets unlocked and who to escalate to.
- [ ] Facts and [ASSUMPTION] are separated; zero closed prices; effort in ranges or person-months; without the word free.
- [ ] Attachments listed as support at the bottom, not as argument.
- [ ] No emojis; neutral, professional Spanish.
Expected deliverable: one-page memo in the 5 blocks + 1 alternative subject line for email.
spec-comunicacion_ejec_resumen_ejecutivo:
[inputs]
- DOCUMENTO: {{DOCUMENTO}} > Extensive document to summarize (report, study, proposal, minutes, paper), pasted as text or attached. Single source of truth: no figure in the summary may come from outside it.
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Role, level, and decision bias of the reader: management committee, investor, direct manager, client, technical team. Defines jargon, granularity, and angle.
- DECISION_PENDIENTE: {{DECISION_PENDIENTE}} > Concrete decision or action the summary must unlock in the reader (approve, prioritize, allocate budget, discard, escalate).
- EXTENSION: {{EXTENSION}} > Maximum length (optional; e.g. half page, 200 words, 5 bullets). If missing: maximum one page, 250 to 300 words.
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments". Supporting context only; not a source of citable figures unless the document incorporates them.

[prompt]

--- S·SITUATION ---
{{AUDIENCIA}} receives {{DOCUMENTO}}, an extensive text they do not have time to read in full, and needs to decide on {{DECISION_PENDIENTE}}. The purpose of the summary is to invert the logic of the original document: put conclusion and recommendation first, evidence after, so that {{AUDIENCIA}} decides in under three minutes without losing rigor. A well-crafted executive summary unlocks the decision, prevents the long document from going unread, and leaves a reusable piece for committee, email, or presentation. The risk to neutralize is twofold: a summary that merely shrinks the text without reordering it by relevance, and one that fills gaps with invented figures or responsible parties. EstrategIA contributes here the rigor of executive synthesis applied to a real decision.

--- P·REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior executive editor, expert in high-level communication, the BLUF principle (Bottom Line Up Front), and Minto's pyramid (conclusion first, hierarchical evidence after).
Deliver the following, in this order:
1. Restate in one sentence what {{DOCUMENTO}} is and what the summary will be used for before {{AUDIENCIA}}; if document, audience, or decision is missing, ask before executing and do not invent figures or responsible parties.
2. Identify the central thesis: the single conclusion {{AUDIENCIA}} must retain if they read only one line.
3. Write a BLUF block of 2 to 3 sentences (conclusion + recommendation) oriented to {{DECISION_PENDIENTE}}, without preambles or 'this document is about'.
4. List 3 to 5 key findings, one line each, ordered by impact for {{DECISION_PENDIENTE}}, each with a concrete piece of data from the document.
5. Explicitly separate facts from interpretations; mark [ASSUMPTION] on every inference not literally supported by the document.
6. Close with actions or next steps: what is decided, who, by when, and what gets unlocked; if the document does not provide responsible parties or deadlines, explicitly declare it rather than inventing them.
7. Calibrate language to {{AUDIENCIA}} and respect {{EXTENSION}} (if not indicated, maximum one page, 250 to 300 words).
Edge cases: if the document is ambiguous or contradicts itself, name the tension rather than choosing a side at random; if there is no clear decision, propose the most likely decision and mark it [ASSUMPTION]; if the document exceeds your reading capacity, declare which sections were not covered rather than simulating full coverage.

--- E·EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: confirm document, audience, decision to unlock, and length; if an essential piece of data is missing, ask before executing.
Phase 2 - Reading and extraction: read the full document, identify the central thesis and the data that supports it, discarding what is accessory.
Phase 3 - Pyramidal inversion: reorder from conclusion to evidence (BLUF at the top, findings by impact, context only if it contributes to the decision).
Phase 4 - Fact vs. interpretation separation: label [ASSUMPTION] on every inference; verify that no figure comes from outside the document or from {{ADJUNTOS}} not incorporated.
Phase 5 - Calibration and trimming: adjust jargon to the audience, compress to the length limit, and eliminate every sentence that does not help to decide.
Phase 6 - Final verification: re-read as {{AUDIENCIA}} would with three minutes; confirm the decision is unlocked and the summary opens with the conclusion.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C·CRITERIA ---
- The summary opens with the conclusion and recommendation (BLUF), not with context or 'this document is about'.
- There is a clear central thesis, retainable in a single line.
- Key findings are between 3 and 5, one line each, ordered by impact for the decision and each backed by a piece of data from the document.
- Facts and interpretations are separated; every inference carries [ASSUMPTION] and no figure comes from outside the document.
- The actions section indicates what is decided, who, and by when, or explicitly declares what the document does not specify.
- Language is calibrated to the indicated audience and respects the maximum length.
- Document tensions or contradictions are named rather than resolved at random.
- Every sentence contributes to the decision; no filler, unnecessary jargon, or emojis.
Expected deliverable: an executive summary in neutral Spanish, with BLUF + thesis + key findings + actions, ready to paste into email, committee, or report cover, within the requested length.
spec-comunicacion_ejec_brief_proyecto:
[inputs]
- NOMBRE_PROYECTO: {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}} > Name or codename of the initiative to document
- PATROCINADOR: {{PATROCINADOR}} > Executive sponsor who approves, funds, and unblocks decisions
- CONTEXTO_DISPARADOR: {{CONTEXTO_DISPARADOR}} > What event, problem, or opportunity triggered the project and why now
- RESULTADO_NEGOCIO: {{RESULTADO_NEGOCIO}} > The measurable change in the business that justifies investing effort (optional; if empty, derive from the trigger and mark [ASSUMPTION])
- RESTRICCIONES: {{RESTRICCIONES}} > Time, effort, team, technology, or dependency limits (optional)
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Who will read and approve the brief (committee, sponsor, executing team); adjusts detail level
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S·SITUATION ---
A project that launches without a one-page document that aligns sponsor and team carries the most frequent root cause of rework, friction, and scope drift: unresolved initial ambiguity. This executive brief fixes objective, boundary, deliverables, and success criteria before the first milestone, so that every subsequent decision has a common reference point and a single source of truth. Completing it unlocks kickoff, assignment of responsible parties, and formal approval from {{PATROCINADOR}}. The cost of not having it is paid in weeks of rework; the cost of having it is one hour of disciplined writing.

--- P·REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior project director with fifteen years articulating initiative launches before executive committees; thinks in business outcomes, not activities, and knows that a brief is won or lost at its scope boundary.
Deliverable: a one-page executive brief, in Markdown, calibrated for {{AUDIENCIA}}, with six blocks in this order:
1. Objective: a single sentence declaring the business outcome sought ({{RESULTADO_NEGOCIO}}) and why it matters now. Outcome, not activity.
2. Context and problem: two or three lines that start from {{CONTEXTO_DISPARADOR}}, name the pain, and say what gets unlocked upon completing the project.
3. Scope: two columns, Includes and Does not include, with at least three items each; the Does not include seals the boundary and is the defense against drift.
4. Deliverables: three to six concrete and verifiable products, each with a single nominal owner (a name or role, never "the team").
5. Success criteria: two to four observable metrics, each with a target value, baseline if one exists, and measurement date; nothing vague or binary without a threshold.
6. Restrictions, assumptions, and milestones: derived from {{RESTRICCIONES}}, each assumption marked with [ASSUMPTION] and its risk if it falls, and includes tentative closing date and critical dependencies (on whom or what the start depends).

--- E·EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Interpret: restate in one sentence the project, the sponsor, and the trigger; list missing data (especially the measurable business outcome and the Does not include boundary) and ask for them before writing. Do not invent metrics, dates, or responsible parties.
Phase 2 Plan: confirm the skeleton of the six blocks, how you will keep everything on one page, and what you will assume as [ASSUMPTION] if a non-blocking piece of data is missing.
Phase 3 Execute: write with direct business language, without jargon or filler adjectives; each block in a few lines. Distinguish facts from assumptions. If a blocking piece of data is missing and cannot be responsibly assumed, stop and ask rather than filling in.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C·CRITERIA ---
- Fits on a single page and contains the six blocks in order.
- Objective in a single sentence oriented to a business outcome, not an activity.
- Context links the trigger to what gets unlocked.
- Scope with explicit Includes and Does not include, minimum three items each.
- Each deliverable has a single nominal owner.
- Each success criterion is observable and carries a target value and measurement date.
- Restrictions and assumptions differentiated; each [ASSUMPTION] indicates its risk if it falls.
- Closing milestone with a tentative date and visible critical dependencies.
- No jargon, no vague goals, no collective responsible parties.
- Data not provided remains as [ASSUMPTION] or as a question, never invented.
Expected deliverable: a one-page executive brief in Markdown, ready to circulate to {{PATROCINADOR}} and the team at kickoff and to sustain formal approval.
spec-comunicacion_ejec_actualizacion_est:
[inputs]
- PROYECTO: {{PROYECTO}} > Name of the project or initiative and, if applicable, its objective in one sentence
- PERIODO: {{PERIODO}} > Period covered by the report (e.g. week, sprint, month) and cut-off date
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Who it is addressed to (e.g. management committee, sponsor, client) and their expected detail level
- AVANCES: {{AVANCES}} > Milestones achieved, progress metrics, and deliverables completed since the last report
- RIESGOS_BLOQUEOS: {{RIESGOS_BLOQUEOS}} > Open risks, blockers, and deviations in scope, schedule, budget, or quality
- DECISIONES_REQUERIDAS: {{DECISIONES_REQUERIDAS}} > Decisions, approvals, or resources needed from the committee (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S·SITUATION ---
I need to communicate the status of the project to an executive audience that decides in minutes and does not read operational detail. A well-built RAG traffic-light report converts progress into a single readable screen: it unlocks quick decisions, exposes risks before they escalate, and leaves an auditable record of what was requested and when. The goal is not to report for the sake of reporting, but to move the committee to act on what is amber or red. A good report is measured by the decisions it triggers, not by its length.

--- P·REQUEST ---
Archetype: PMO Director with experience presenting project and portfolio status to executive committees and sponsors.
Deliver a RAG traffic-light status report, in neutral, professional Spanish without emojis, with this structure:
1. One-line headline: global project status and its color (green/amber/red).
2. Executive summary of 3 to 4 sentences: what advanced, what decision or help you need, and by when.
3. Dimensions table (scope, schedule, budget, quality, risks): color, one sentence of verifiable evidence, and the change versus the previous period (improving/same/worsening).
4. Detail only for amber or red dimensions: root cause, impact if not acted upon, proposed action, responsible party, and date.
5. Committee requests: each as a binary decision (approve/reject) with a deadline and the consequence of not deciding.

--- E·EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 — Interpret: classify each dimension with the color rule: green = on plan, no action required; amber = recoverable deviation with a plan in progress; red = deviation that requires a committee decision now. Every color is backed by evidence from AVANCES or RIESGOS_BLOQUEOS, never by a feeling; if a piece of data does not exist, mark it [ASSUMPTION] and do not invent metrics. If an essential input (PROYECTO, PERIODO, AUDIENCIA, AVANCES, or RIESGOS_BLOQUEOS) is missing or arrives ambiguous, ask for it in a single batch before writing. Adjust depth to the detail level declared by AUDIENCIA without breaking the one-screen limit.
Phase 2 — Plan: order the report from highest to lowest severity (red, then amber, then green) so that the critical items are read first; group committee requests at the close. If DECISIONES_REQUERIDAS arrives empty and no amber/red requires it, explicitly declare "No decisions required this period". Edge case: if all dimensions are green, keep the headline, summary, and table, omit the detail block, and note that there are no open items.
Phase 3 — Execute: write headline, summary, table, amber/red detail, and requests. Keep a single reading screen; move extensive detail (schedules, supporting metrics, ADJUNTOS appendixes) to a referenced appendix. Do not mix colors within a single dimension: if there is nuance, choose the higher-severity color and explain the nuance in the detail.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C·CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist before delivering:
- [ ] The headline declares global status and color in a single line.
- [ ] The executive summary (3-4 sentences) says what advanced, what is needed from the committee, and by when.
- [ ] Each dimension has color, verifiable evidence, and direction of change versus the previous period.
- [ ] Every amber and every red carries root cause, impact, action, responsible party, and date; no green carries an action.
- [ ] The order goes from highest to lowest severity (red, amber, green).
- [ ] Each request to the committee is a binary decision with a deadline and the consequence of not deciding; if there are none, this is explicitly declared.
- [ ] Zero invented data; unconfirmed data goes as [ASSUMPTION]; no emojis; neutral Spanish.
- [ ] The report fits on one screen; additional detail lives in a referenced appendix.
Expected deliverable: a RAG traffic-light status report ready to send to the committee or paste into the tracking tool, with an actionable decisions-required block.
spec-comunicacion_ejec_comunicado_cambio:
[inputs]

- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Who it is addressed to (affected team, area, entire organization) and their level of exposure to the change

- FIRMANTE: {{FIRMANTE}} > Who signs the announcement (name and title)
- SENSIBILIDAD: {{SENSIBILIDAD}} > Level of the change: routine, relevant, or critical/sensitive (layoffs, closure, merger). Determines care and sequencing (optional)
- TONO: {{TONO}} > Desired nuance: empathetic-close or formal-institutional (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S·SITUATION ---
A relevant organizational change is about to be communicated and the way it is announced will determine whether the team receives it with clarity or with rumor. A well-built announcement reduces uncertainty, protects trust, and accelerates adoption; an ambiguous one opens space for anxiety and erroneous interpretations that take weeks to correct afterward. Silence and euphemism are not neutral: every gap is filled by rumor. This prompt produces the ready-to-send announcement.

--- P·REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior Internal Communications Director with experience in change management (ADKAR framework) and executive communication in organizations undergoing transformation.

Deliverable: a ready-to-send internal announcement (subject + structured body + signature) plus a note of assumptions and data to confirm. Steps:
1. Write a clear subject line and a direct announcement of the change in the first sentence of the body, without preambles.
2. Explain the why: connect the decision to the business reality and the strategy, in honest language without empty jargon or euphemisms that hide the substance.
3. Detail the concrete impact: what changes, what stays the same, and who it affects, from {{FECHA_VIGENCIA}}.
4. Describe the support available ({{SOPORTE}}): channels, accompaniment, training, and a point of contact with a name.
5. Close with next steps, key dates, an explicit and nominal space for questions, and the signature of {{FIRMANTE}}.

--- E·EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Interpretation: map the change onto ADKAR (Awareness of the why, Desire to accompany, Knowledge of the impact, Ability via support, Reinforcement via next steps). Mark as [ASSUMPTION] any data not provided and request any critical missing item before writing. If an assumption could cause reputational or legal harm (layoffs, figures, names), do not assume it: ask.
Phase 2 - Anti-rumor matrix: list the 2-3 most probable fears of {{AUDIENCIA}} (stability of my position, my manager, my workload, my team) and ensure the body addresses them head-on rather than leaving them to interpretation.
Phase 3 - Structure: direct announcement > why > impact (what changes / what stays the same) > support > next steps and questions.
Phase 4 - Writing: neutral, professional, and empathetic Spanish; acknowledge legitimate uncertainty without minimizing it; without unverifiable promises; without emojis. If {{SENSIBILIDAD}} is critical (closure, layoffs, merger, departure of a leader): prioritize the dignity of the people, avoid language that dehumanizes, and do not announce collectively what requires individual conversation first; flag it as a note to the signatory.
Phase 5 - Tone adjustment according to {{TONO}} if indicated, and reference {{ADJUNTOS}} when they exist.
Phase 6 - Close: deliver the announcement and, below, the note of [ASSUMPTION]s made and data to confirm before distributing.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C·CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The announcement of the change appears in the first sentence of the body, without detours.
- [ ] The why connects to the business reality and strategy, without empty jargon or euphemisms.
- [ ] The impact explicitly distinguishes what changes and what stays the same, with the effective date.
- [ ] The 2-3 most probable fears of the audience are addressed head-on, not implied.
- [ ] The support lists channels and a concrete point of contact with a name.
- [ ] The close includes next steps, dates, and an explicit space for questions.
- [ ] Empathetic tone that acknowledges uncertainty; zero unkept promises; zero emojis.
- [ ] If the change is sensitive: dignified language and a note about prior individual conversations.
- [ ] Data not provided marked [ASSUMPTION]; critical and sensitive missing items requested before writing.
Expected deliverable: complete internal announcement (subject + structured body + signature) ready to copy and send, followed by a brief note of assumptions and data to confirm.

A C-level spokesperson will face a public or stakeholder appearance where every phrase is interpreted, quoted, and can escalate to a headline. It unlocks the confidence to rehearse, consistency across spokespersons, and narrative control.

--- P·REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior executive communications advisor and media trainer, with a track record preparing C-level spokespersons for interviews, panels, town halls, and appearances before investors and media.

Deliverable: a set of talking points ready to rehearse aloud. Steps:

2. Build three supporting key messages; each with its proof or data point (only from {{HECHOS_VERIFICABLES}}) and a verbal bridge back to the central message.
3. Build a bank of 6 to 8 difficult and hostile questions, including the worst possible question, with model answers using the ABC technique (Acknowledge without repeating the negative premise, Bridge with a natural transition, Communicate the key message); each answer with its "what NOT to say".

Phase 3 (Support): produce key messages + proofs + bridges; do not invent figures or statements, mark inferences as [ASSUMPTION].
Phase 4 (Stress-test): generate the most uncomfortable questions and resolve them with ABC; estimate read time and adjust to under 30 seconds per answer.
Phase 5 (Close): deliver closings and mined zones, and signal what to rehearse first and what piece of data is still missing to confirm.

--- C·CRITERIA ---

--- S·SITUATION ---
I need to convert an internal initiative into a one-pager that fits on one page and allows {{SPONSOR_O_AUDIENCIA}} to decide in a single reading, without prior context meetings. The document sells {{INICIATIVA}} upward: it unlocks an approval, a resource, or a prioritized decision. A well-structured one-pager shortens the approval cycle and turns a scattered idea into an evaluable bet. It competes against the scarce time of the decision-maker: if it doesn't fit on one page or requires external context, it fails.

--- P·REQUEST ---
Archetype: senior executive communication leader specialized in internal business cases that get approved in a single reading.
Produce a one-pager selling the initiative with this exact structure:
1. A one-line headline capturing the bet (what changes and why now); must stand on its own if it is the only thing read.
2. Problem or opportunity: the cost of inaction per {{COSTO_DE_NO_ACTUAR}}, in concrete business terms (lost time, risk, stalled capacity, ceded advantage), never generic.
3. Proposed solution: two or three sentences anyone can understand, without jargon or technical dependencies.
4. How it works: two to four main milestones or phases within {{HORIZONTE_TIEMPO}}, with the moment the benefit materializes.
5. Cost-benefit: required effort or investment (person-months, resources, or capabilities; NEVER invented monetary figures) versus the expected return and the risk of not acting.

Phase 1 - Interpret: extract from {{INICIATIVA}} and {{ADJUNTOS}} the problem, solution, and benefit; identify which critical data is missing to support each claim. If {{COSTO_DE_NO_ACTUAR}} or {{PEDIDO_CONCRETO}} are missing or vague, ask before continuing.
Phase 2 - Plan: build the skeleton of the six blocks (headline plus five body sections); mark with [ASSUMPTION] every figure or statement without backing and, if it is critical to the decision, ask before drafting rather than inventing it.
Phase 3 - Execute: draft the one-pager in neutral, professional English, no filler, with impact verbs; verify it fits on one page and prioritize the problem and the ask if cuts are needed.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C·CRITERIA ---
- Fits on one page (high density, zero filler).
- All six blocks are present: headline, problem, solution, how it works, cost-benefit, ask.
- The cost of inaction is framed in specific business terms, not generic ones.
- No invented monetary figures; effort is expressed in person-months, resources, or capabilities.
- Unsupported statements are marked [ASSUMPTION] or were asked; no critical one was invented.
- How it works has milestones within the horizon and signals when the benefit arrives.
- The ask is a single specific action, in bold, with a target date and who decides.
- One-line headline that supports the bet on its own.
Expected deliverable: a one-pager ready to circulate to {{SPONSOR_O_AUDIENCIA}}, on one page, with headline, five body blocks, and ask in bold.

--- S·SITUATION ---
The organization needs to announce a fact to media and achieve coverage without looking like advertising. A well-built press release allows a journalist to publish the story with minimal rewriting: a reusable newsworthy headline, a lead that covers everything in the first paragraph, and a quote that gives a human voice. The journalist decides in seconds whether there is news; if the text sounds like a brochure, it gets discarded. A good release unlocks media coverage, third-party credibility, and a reusable asset for the web, social media, and the press room.

--- P·REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior journalist and media relations specialist, skilled in the inverted pyramid and with editorial judgment to distinguish news from self-promotion.
Deliverable: a complete, distributable press release in structured plain text. Steps:
1. Confirm you have a date, location, figures, the spokesperson's name and title, and press contact details; if anything essential is missing, ask before drafting and never invent it. Mark with [ASSUMPTION] everything you assume.
2. Header: embargo line per EMBARGO (FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE or EMBARGOED UNTIL date and time) and dateline with location and date at the start of the lead.
3. Surtitle + newsworthy headline of no more than 12 words centered on the fact, not the brand; optional one-line subheadline adding the second most relevant data point.
4. Inverted lead: first paragraph answering the five Ws (what, who, when, where, why) in two or three sentences.
5. Two or three body paragraphs in inverted pyramid, from most important data to secondary context, integrating DATOS_CLAVE; each material figure with its source or reference.
6. A verbatim quote attributed to PORTAVOZ that adds vision or meaning, without repeating already stated data; optional second quote only if there is a relevant partner or third party.
7. Close: "About ORGANIZACION" paragraph, press contact block, and boilerplate of attachments per ADJUNTOS.
8. Final distribution note: who to send to within AUDIENCIA_MEDIOS, suggested email subject line, and missing assets.

--- E·EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: define the news angle (what changes for the reader) and discard what only interests the brand. If the fact is not newsworthy, say so and propose a stronger angle.
Phase 2 - Hierarchy: rank facts in descending relevance; dispensable content goes at the end and must be cuttable without breaking meaning (inverted-pyramid rule).
Phase 3 - Drafting: third person, short sentences, verifiable, neutral professional English, without superlatives or empty adjectives; expand acronyms on first use; figures with source; mark assumptions with [ASSUMPTION].
Phase 4 - Quote: draft a statement that sounds like a real person and adds meaning, vision, or commitment — not filler or repeated data.
Phase 5 - Close and review against checklist; add the distribution note.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C·CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Embargo line in header consistent with EMBARGO; dateline (location, date) at the start of the lead.
- [ ] Headline of no more than 12 words, newsworthy, not promotional.
- [ ] Lead answers the five Ws in the first paragraph.
- [ ] Body in verifiable inverted pyramid; each material figure with source; zero invented data ([ASSUMPTION] where info is missing).
- [ ] Verbatim quote attributed with name and title, adds vision and does not repeat data.
- [ ] "About" paragraph + press contact block + complete attachment reference.
- [ ] Third person, neutral professional English, acronyms expanded, no empty superlatives or promotional language.
- [ ] Distribution note: recipients, suggested email subject line, and missing assets.
Edge cases: if the fact is not newsworthy, propose an alternate angle; if the quote only repeats figures, rewrite it with vision; if a five-W data point is missing, ask for it and do not publish an incomplete release.
Expected deliverable: a press release ready to send to media, in structured plain text, reusable for the press room and social channels, with distribution note.

--- S·SITUATION ---
An organization must send its investors or stakeholders a periodic business update. The purpose is to sustain trust through transparency: a letter that balances achievements, challenges, and vision, directed at someone who entrusted their capital or support. A strong letter reduces reader uncertainty, sets the narrative before rumors do, creates a written record of how the business is governed, and builds the credibility that enables the next cycle of backing. Doing it poorly — hiding the bad, inflating the good, or burying bad news in jargon — erodes the relationship sustaining the organization and is paid for dearly in the next round or vote.

--- P·REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior Director of Investor Relations, with experience writing annual shareholder letters and stakeholder updates, trained in Warren Buffett's candor principle (address the reader as an absent partner; report good and bad with equal rigor; explain the business, not just the numbers).

Deliverable: the complete letter, ready to send, following these steps:
1. Verify that ORGANIZACION, PERIODO, AUDIENCIA, LOGROS, DESAFIOS, and VISION are present; if any is missing or ambiguous, ask before drafting. FIRMANTE and TONO_ESPECIAL are optional; if missing, assume signer to be confirmed and standard tone. Do not invent metrics, figures, or milestones.
2. Define the central message of the period in one sentence, which anchors the whole letter.
3. Draft the opening: acknowledge the reader as a partner and state the central message; if TONO_ESPECIAL indicates bad news, name it upfront, do not bury it.
4. Achievements section: each one with its evidence or metric, explaining why it matters for the long-term thesis, not just what happened.
5. Challenges section: name them without euphemisms, with root cause and concrete corrective action in progress, with responsible party or timeline when data exist.
6. Vision section: focus for the next period, bets, and how progress will be measured; connect each bet to an achievement or challenge already mentioned.
7. Closing: reaffirm the commitment, thank the reader for their trust, and indicate the next contact point or report if the data exist.

--- E·EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 — Interpretation: confirm organization, period, audience, and inputs; flag gaps; detect the sensitive moment via TONO_ESPECIAL.
Phase 2 — Message architecture: set the central message and the achievements/challenges/vision balance before writing prose; verify that each achievement has a metric and each challenge has an action.
Phase 3 — Drafting: develop sections with an adult-to-adult tone; every unsupported data point is marked [ASSUMPTION]; no empty jargon or superlatives without evidence.
Phase 4 — Candor check: verify that no challenge is softened, no achievement inflated, no figure invented, and no bad news buried; confirm zero prices and zero return projections.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C·CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Explicit central message in one sentence in the opening.
- [ ] Achievements with verifiable metric or milestone and their relevance to the thesis, not just description.
- [ ] Challenges named without euphemisms, each with root cause and concrete corrective action.
- [ ] Vision with focus, bets, and measurable advancement criterion, connected to cited achievements or challenges.
- [ ] Bad news (if TONO_ESPECIAL indicates it) declared upfront, not buried.
- [ ] Professional, sober, adult-to-adult tone; neutral professional English; no emojis.
- [ ] Zero prices, return projections, or invented figures; every assumption marked [ASSUMPTION].
- [ ] Real balance between achievements and challenges (this is not a good-news letter).

spec-comunicacion_ejec_mensaje_crisis:
[inputs]
- INCIDENTE: {{INCIDENTE}} > What happened, when, and who is affected, in one or two sentences

- CANAL: {{CANAL}} > Emission medium and format (press release, email, LinkedIn post, press statement, internal message, SMS/push)
