Make every growth, margin, and reinvestment assumption explicit, and verify internal consistency: sustained growth requires proportional CapEx and working capital.
3. WACC: cost of equity via CAPM (risk-free rate + beta × market risk premium) and after-tax cost of debt, weighted by the target capital structure (not the current one if it differs from steady state).
4. Terminal value: Gordon growth model (perpetuity rate g, with g < WACC and g ≤ the long-run nominal growth rate of the economy) and, as a cross-check, an exit multiple EV/EBITDA. Reconcile both: if they differ by more than ~15%, explain why. Report what percentage of total value the terminal contributes.
5. Value bridge: discount FCFF and terminal value at WACC (mid-period convention if flows are uniform) → enterprise value; subtract net debt → equity value. Build WACC × g sensitivity table; optionally two-dimensional with margin or growth.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Input validation: if historical statements, beta, capital structure, net debt, or growth/margin assumptions are missing, ask before projecting; do not invent historical data. Use ADJUNTOS as a basis when they exist.
Phase 2 - Construction: project FCFF in a table, discount each flow with its WACC discount factor, calculate terminal value by both methods, and bring everything to the valuation date.
Phase 3 - Bridge and range: derive enterprise value and equity value; run the WACC × g sensitivity and, if applicable, exit multiple.
Phase 4 - Critical reading: identify the 3 levers that most move value, warn when terminal weight is excessive (>75% of value), and flag where the thesis turns negative. If the valuation implies unrealistic final multiples (e.g. terminal EV/EBITDA outside the sectoral range), flag it.
Mark every figure not provided by the user as [ASSUMPTION] with its justification and source or comparable used.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] FCFF built correctly: NOPAT + D&A − CapEx − change in working capital, without mixing firm-level and equity-level flows.
- [ ] Reinvestment coherent with growth: no sustained growth without proportional CapEx or working capital.
- [ ] WACC broken down: CAPM for equity, after-tax cost of debt, weighting by target capital structure.
- [ ] Terminal value with g < WACC and g ≤ long-run nominal growth; cross-check and reconciliation with exit multiple.
- [ ] Rate-flow consistency: nominal WACC with nominal flows (or real with real); consistent taxes.
- [ ] Terminal value weight over total value reported, with a warning if >75%.
- [ ] Clear enterprise-to-equity bridge subtracting net debt at the correct date.
- [ ] WACC × g sensitivity table delivered; implied exit multiple verified against sectoral range.
- [ ] Every figure not provided marked [ASSUMPTION] with justification; no invented historical data.
Expected deliverable: FCFF projection table year by year, WACC breakdown, terminal value by both methods with weight and reconciliation, enterprise-to-equity value bridge, sensitivity table, and the 3 main value levers with critical reading.
spec-finanzas_estructura_modelo_buenas_p:
[inputs]
- MODELO: {{MODELO}} > Financial model to restructure or its description: type (3-statement, DCF, LBO, budget, unit economics), current tabs, key formulas, and known problems
- PROPOSITO: {{PROPOSITO}} > What it is used for and who consumes it (investment decision, annual budget, valuation, committee report, due diligence)
- HORIZONTE_PERIODICIDAD: {{HORIZONTE_PERIODICIDAD}} > Time horizon and granularity (e.g. 5 years monthly, 3 years annual)
- HERRAMIENTA: {{HERRAMIENTA}} > Spreadsheet or environment (Excel, Google Sheets, other) and relevant constraints (no macros, cloud-shared, mobile version)
- NIVEL_CONTROL: {{NIVEL_CONTROL}} > Required governance rigor (light internal use, committee, due diligence, formal audit) (optional; default: committee)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A financial model loses value when no one other than its author can read it: assumptions buried in formulas, tabs that reference each other in circles, and results impossible to reconstruct. The risk is not theoretical: a single forgotten hardcoded value or a broken cross-reference can skew a valuation or a budget without anyone noticing. Restructuring it under separated layers (inputs, calculations, outputs) with formatting and traceability turns it into an auditable asset that outlives its creator, withstands the scrutiny of a committee or a due diligence, and reduces the risk of silent errors in cells. This unlocks defensible decisions and deliverables that inspire confidence.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior financial modeler specializing in spreadsheet model governance and auditability, with mastery of the FAST Standard and model risk management practices.
Restructure {{MODELO}} for {{PROPOSITO}}, over horizon {{HORIZONTE_PERIODICIDAD}}, on {{HERRAMIENTA}}, at control level {{NIVEL_CONTROL}}, and deliver:
1. Antipattern diagnosis: hardcoded values in formulas, scattered assumptions, formulas that mix input and calculation, cross-references without control, unlabeled cells, unintended circular dependencies, inconsistent formulas in the same row.
2. Tab architecture: Cover/Index, Assumptions, Calculations by block, Outputs/Dashboard, and Source Data if applicable, with a one-way dependency flow (inputs toward outputs).
3. Formatting convention: differentiated style for editable inputs, internal formulas, and cross-tab linked cells; one row per assumption with unit, value, source, and date; a single replicable formula per row.
4. Traceability scheme: every assumption with origin and date; every output reconstructible by following references back to the input, with no opaque jumps or embedded constants.
5. Control layer: tie-check cells that must return zero (e.g. assets = liabilities + equity, reconciled cash flow), balances that must match, error flags, sanity ranges per assumption, and a version log.
6. Migration plan: steps ranked by risk, from the safest to the most delicate change, with a before-and-after validation method that confirms identical results (or explains each difference).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Diagnosis: map tabs, dependency flow, and antipatterns; classify findings by severity (breaks the model / hinders auditability / cosmetic) and estimate correction effort.
Phase 2 - Design: define the three-layer architecture and the formatting convention; justify each decision against the separation-and-one-way-flow principle; flag trade-offs when the tool is limiting (e.g. no advanced conditional formatting).
Phase 3 - Traceability and control: specify how each assumption is documented and what tie-checks and sanity ranges guarantee integrity; define what happens when an error flag activates.
Phase 4 - Migration: rank the changes by risk and define how to validate that the model delivers the same results after restructuring (key-output snapshot before/after, acceptable tolerance).
Do not invent model figures; mark everything unconfirmed as [ASSUMPTION] and ask for the missing data point. Do not propose a change that breaks a formula without explicitly flagging the risk and how to mitigate it. If {{NIVEL_CONTROL}} is not specified, assume committee and declare it.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- Inputs, calculations, and outputs are in separated layers with a one-way flow, no outputs feeding inputs.
- Zero hardcoded values in calculation formulas; every assumption lives in the input layer with unit, source, and date.
- Every output is reconstructible by following references back to the input, with no opaque jumps or embedded constants.
- The formatting convention visually distinguishes editable inputs, formulas, and linked cells, and applies a single replicable formula per row.
- Verifiable tie-check cells exist (must return zero or match), sanity ranges, and a version log.
- The migration plan is risk-ordered, executable without breaking results, and includes before-and-after validation.
- Every change that could break a formula comes with its risk and mitigation made explicit.
- No invented figures; unconfirmed assumptions are marked [ASSUMPTION].
Expected deliverable: structured document with (a) prioritized antipattern diagnosis by severity and effort, (b) new tab architecture map and flow, (c) formatting convention, (d) assumption-to-output traceability scheme, (e) control check list with sanity ranges and error flags, (f) risk-ordered migration plan with before-and-after validation, and a closing with what is now auditable and what remains pending confirmation.
spec-finanzas_auditoria_modelo_existente:
[inputs]
- TIPO_DE_MODELO: {{TIPO_DE_MODELO}} > Nature of the inherited model (3-statement projection, DCF valuation, unit economics, operating budget, pricing model, LBO, etc.)
- DECISION_A_TOMAR: {{DECISION_A_TOMAR}} > Decision that will be supported by the model (approve investment, set budget, close round, define price)
- HORIZONTE: {{HORIZONTE}} > Period and granularity covered by the model (e.g. 5 years monthly, 3 years annual)
- MONEDA: {{MONEDA}} > Base currency of the model and whether it handles conversions
- VERSION_O_FECHA: {{VERSION_O_FECHA}} > Version, date, or known author of the file (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You inherit a financial model that nobody on your current team built and must trust its numbers before using them for {{DECISION_A_TOMAR}}. An undetected formula error, an implicit assumption, or a hardcode inside a formula can tip the decision in the wrong direction and cost credibility and capital. The typical opacity of an inherited model (undocumented logic, absent author, layers of versions) is precisely what this audit neutralizes so the decision is made on evidence rather than on faith in a spreadsheet.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior financial controller (FP&A) specialized in spreadsheet model auditing and integrity, with the judgment of an independent reviewer.
Produce an audit report of the {{TIPO_DE_MODELO}} model (horizon {{HORIZONTE}}, currency {{MONEDA}}, version {{VERSION_O_FECHA}}). Steps:
1. Map the architecture: tabs, calculation flow, input vs. output cells, main drivers, and dependencies between statements.
2. Trace the formulas tab by tab and log each finding with: severity (critical / high / medium / low), exact location (tab and cell or range), type (broken or circular reference, embedded hardcode, sign error, unit or period inconsistency, broken carry-forward logic, non-uniform formula in a row), quantified or estimated impact on the result, and suggested correction.
3. Validate cross-cutting consistency: reconciliations between statements, totals that add up, coherent signs, a balance that closes, a cash flow that reconciles with the result, and sensitivities that respond to driver changes.
4. Extract implicit assumptions, flag undocumented or unjustified ones, and list the data needed to confirm them.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Reconnaissance: identify purpose, scope, tab structure, and the 3–5 drivers that move the result; separate inputs from calculated cells.
Phase 2 Formula tracing: walk cell by cell through the calculation zones; isolate embedded hardcodes, broken or circular references, and rows with non-uniform formulas.
Phase 3 Reconciliations and consistency: verify the integrity of statements, signs, totals, balance closure, cash-flow reconciliation, and sensitivity response.
Phase 4 Assumptions and verdict: document assumptions, prioritize findings by severity and impact, and issue the verdict.
Rules: do not invent figures or assumptions; anything unverifiable is tagged [ASSUMPTION] with the required data point. If the file or a key piece of data is missing, ask for it before proceeding. If only screenshots or partial excerpts are available, state that the audit is partial and indicate which areas you did not cover. Always distinguish a real defect from a deliberate modeling choice.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- Each finding has severity, exact location (tab and cell), type, impact, and correction.
- Findings ordered by severity and impact on the result, not by order of appearance.
- Statement reconciliations verified explicitly (or flagged as unverifiable with reason).
- Implicit assumptions documented; unjustified ones flagged as [ASSUMPTION] with the missing data point.
- Zero invented figures; every assertion traceable to a cell or to an [ASSUMPTION].
- Real defect distinguished from intentional modeling choice.
- Unambiguous verdict: reliable to decide / conditionally reliable (with conditions) / not fit until corrected.
Deliverable: audit report with (1) executive summary, (2) model architecture map, (3) prioritized findings table, (4) reconciliation validation, (5) list of assumptions to confirm, and (6) verdict with conditions.
spec-finanzas_modelo_suscripcion_arr:
[inputs]
- ARR_INICIAL: {{ARR_INICIAL}} > ARR of the base period from which the projection starts (in the currency and unit you specify)
- HORIZONTE_PERIODOS: {{HORIZONTE_PERIODOS}} > Number and granularity of periods to project (e.g. 8 quarters, 5 years)
- ARR_NUEVO_PERIODO: {{ARR_NUEVO_PERIODO}} > ARR contributed by new logos each period (fixed amount, series, or acquisition growth rate)
- TASA_EXPANSION: {{TASA_EXPANSION}} > % of the existing base gained through upsell and cross-sell per period
- TASA_CONTRACCION: {{TASA_CONTRACCION}} > % of the existing base lost through downgrades without cancellation per period
- TASA_CHURN: {{TASA_CHURN}} > % of the existing base lost through total cancellation per period
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need to understand and communicate how annual recurring revenue (ARR) evolves in a subscription business, separating the effect of each movement driver so I can decide where to invest: new-logo acquisition, base expansion, or retention. A period-by-period chained ARR bridge unlocks defensible investor projections, early leak detection, and the conversation about whether growth is healthy or depends solely on burning acquisition spend.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior subscription finance analyst (SaaS), expert in recurring revenue metrics and revenue bridges.
Deliverable: ARR dynamics model with a period-by-period table, consolidated bridge, and diagnostic. Steps:
1. Validate the inputs; if ARR_INICIAL, HORIZONTE_PERIODOS, ARR_NUEVO_PERIODO, or any of the three rates is missing, ask before calculating. Do not invent figures; tag assumptions [ASSUMPTION] and keep them editable.
2. Set and declare conventions: the expansion, contraction, and churn rates are applied to the beginning ARR of the period (existing base, BEFORE adding new ARR); confirm granularity, currency, and unit.
3. For each period apply the bridge: ending ARR = beginning ARR + new ARR + expansion − contraction − churn.
4. Chain: the ending ARR of one period is the beginning ARR of the next.
5. Calculate per period NRR, GRR, growth rate, and percentage contribution of each driver to the net change.
6. Build the period-by-period table and the bridge from the first to the last period.
7. Issue a diagnostic: which driver growth depends on, where the largest leak is (contraction vs. churn), and the sensitivity of ending ARR to +/−1 point in the churn rate.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 – Validation: confirm inputs and conventions (rate calculation base, granularity, currency, unit). If rates come as annual and granularity is quarterly, adjust or tag the conversion [ASSUMPTION]. Phase 2 – Chaining: run the bridge period by period in a traceable way, showing the five components. Phase 3 – Metrics: derive NRR (= (beginning ARR + expansion − contraction − churn) / beginning ARR), GRR (= (beginning ARR − contraction − churn) / beginning ARR), ARR growth, and percentage contributions to the net change. Phase 4 – Sensitivity and diagnostic: recalculate ending ARR with churn +/−1 point and deliver table + bridge + executive narrative. Edge cases: NRR > 1 = growth without acquisition (positive net expansion, sign of a healthy base); GRR > NRR = calculation error (always GRR ≤ NRR); any exit rate > 100% of the period = inconsistent, stop and alert. Brand restrictions: never cite plan prices or promotions; operate only in ARR and rates.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The bridge balances: ending ARR = beginning ARR + new + expansion − contraction − churn in every period.
- [ ] The ending ARR of each period is the beginning ARR of the next (correct chaining).
- [ ] NRR and GRR calculated only over the existing base (excluding new ARR); GRR ≤ NRR holds in all periods.
- [ ] Period-by-period table with five bridge components + NRR, GRR, growth, and contribution of each driver.
- [ ] Consolidated bridge from the first to the last period and sensitivity of ending ARR to +/−1 point of churn.
- [ ] Diagnostic of leak (contraction vs. churn) and growth dependency (acquisition vs. base).
- [ ] Calculation conventions, granularity, currency, and unit declared; assumptions tagged [ASSUMPTION]; no invented figures; no prices or promotions.
Expected deliverable: ARR projection table by period, consolidated ARR bridge with churn sensitivity, and 4–6-line executive narrative on model health and priority levers.
spec-finanzas_waterfall_ingreso_ebitda:
[inputs]
- ENTIDAD_O_UNIDAD: {{ENTIDAD_O_UNIDAD}} > Company, business unit, or line whose margin bridge is being built
- PERIODO_ANALIZADO: {{PERIODO_ANALIZADO}} > Starting period (e.g. current quarter or fiscal year)
- PERIODO_COMPARACION: {{PERIODO_COMPARACION}} > Base period for deltas (e.g. same period prior year, budget, or forecast)
- MONEDA_Y_UNIDAD: {{MONEDA_Y_UNIDAD}} > Presentation currency and scale (e.g. thousands, millions)
- PARTIDAS_NO_RECURRENTES: {{PARTIDAS_NO_RECURRENTES}} > Criterion or list of items to isolate for adjusted EBITDA (optional; if empty, use standard criterion and declare it [ASSUMPTION])
- FUENTE_DATOS: {{FUENTE_DATOS}} > Source income statement or accounting detail
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Revenue alone does not explain the health of the business: between the top line and EBITDA there is a chain of levers (cost of sales, opex by nature, depreciation, non-recurring items) that erode or add margin. A revenue-to-EBITDA waterfall makes each lever visible, attributes margin variation to concrete causes, and unlocks cost control, pricing, and reported-vs.-adjusted reconciliation decisions for a committee or due diligence. Without the bridge, the committee discusses the final figure without understanding what moved it, and the buyer discounts adjusted EBITDA due to lack of traceability.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior financial controller with experience in FP&A, margin reporting, and reported/adjusted EBITDA reconciliation.
Build the bridge for {{ENTIDAD_O_UNIDAD}} from net revenue for {{PERIODO_ANALIZADO}} to reported and adjusted EBITDA, vs. {{PERIODO_COMPARACION}}, in {{MONEDA_Y_UNIDAD}}, with data from {{FUENTE_DATOS}}:
1. Set net revenue for the period as the starting step and validate that it reconciles with the source.
2. Break down cost of sales by component (raw materials, direct labor, indirect production costs) and arrive at gross margin.
3. Break down operating expenses by nature (commercial, administrative, marketing, R&D) and arrive at EBIT.
4. Add back depreciation and amortization for reported EBITDA; isolate non-recurring items per {{PARTIDAS_NO_RECURRENTES}} for adjusted EBITDA, with an explicit reconciliation bridge between the two.
5. For each step calculate absolute value, weight over revenue (cumulative margin %) and delta vs. {{PERIODO_COMPARACION}}, with sign (+ adds / − removes margin).
6. Express the EBITDA margin variation in basis points.
7. Write the narrative for the three highest-impact levers: volume, price/mix, or cost efficiency when the data allows separation.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 – Input validation: confirm the income statement, comparison period, non-recurring criterion, and currency; if any is missing, ask before calculating and do not invent figures.
Phase 2 – Bridge structure: arrange steps in cascade (revenue > gross margin > EBIT > reported EBITDA > adjusted EBITDA) verifying that each subtotal closes arithmetically.
Phase 3 – Quantification: calculate absolutes, % of revenue, and deltas; the EBITDA margin variation in basis points. Keep sign consistent between delta and impact.
Phase 4 – Attribution and narrative: identify dominant levers, separate recurring from non-recurring effect, and explain the why without filler.
Phase 5 – Audit: tag each estimate [ASSUMPTION]; confirm the bridge EBITDA equals the source EBITDA and, if there is a difference, report it as a reconciling item instead of forcing it.
Edge cases: ambiguous gross vs. net revenue, discounts/returns above or below the line, IFRS-16 leasing altering the comparison base, periods of different duration, currency restatement. Declare these before calculating.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The bridge starts from net revenue and each subtotal (gross margin, EBIT, EBITDA) closes arithmetically.
- [ ] Cost of sales and opex are broken down by component/nature, not in a single block.
- [ ] Each step shows absolute value, % of revenue, and signed delta vs. {{PERIODO_COMPARACION}}.
- [ ] Reported EBITDA is distinguished from adjusted EBITDA with an explicit reconciliation bridge.
- [ ] The EBITDA margin variation is in basis points.
- [ ] The comparison base is consistent (same duration, same accounting definition); any adjustment is declared.
- [ ] No invented data; estimates tagged [ASSUMPTION]; missing items requested before calculating.
- [ ] Bridge EBITDA equals the source EBITDA or the difference is reported as a reconciling item.
Expected deliverable: step-by-step revenue-to-EBITDA bridge table (absolute, %, and signed delta), reported vs. adjusted EBITDA reconciliation block, EBITDA margin % indicator and basis-points variation, narrative of the three highest-impact levers, and list of [ASSUMPTION] items and caveats at the close.
spec-finanzas_modelo_capacidad_recursos:
[inputs]
- DEMANDA_PROYECTADA: {{DEMANDA_PROYECTADA}} > Expected work volume per period (tickets, cases, transactions, orders) with its unit; if there is seasonality or trend, a description of the profile
- HORIZONTE: {{HORIZONTE}} > Planning window and granularity (e.g. 12 months monthly; 6 weeks weekly)
- INVENTARIO_RECURSOS: {{INVENTARIO_RECURSOS}} > Resource types, quantity per type, net productive hours per period, and standard time per unit of work; flag if a type only processes certain demand (non-fungible resource)
- UTILIZACION_OBJETIVO: {{UTILIZACION_OBJETIVO}} > Target utilization per resource type and expected shrinkage (absenteeism, training, downtime), as a percentage or fraction
- ESCENARIOS: {{ESCENARIOS}} > Scenarios to simulate (e.g. base, demand stress +30%, hiring freeze, attrition −10%) (optional; default: base only)
- RESTRICCIONES: {{RESTRICCIONES}} > Operational limits: overtime cap, hiring lead time and ramp curve, non-fungible resources, SLA or healthy utilization cap (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need to size my operation before committing headcount: to know whether current resources can absorb the projected demand, in which period capacity breaks, and how much it costs to sustain the operation. A good capacity model unlocks three decisions: how much to hire and when, where the bottleneck limiting throughput is, and how much slack or deficit each period carries. Without this model, headcount is decided by intuition and the break is discovered when it is already too late to act within the hiring lead time.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior capacity and operations financial planning analyst (capacity planning + workforce/resource modeling), fluent in demand-supply balancing, theory of constraints (TOC), and FTE-month costing.
Deliverable: a capacity and cost model with a period-by-period table, bottleneck, compared scenarios, and sizing recommendations. Steps:
1. Translate DEMANDA_PROYECTADA into workload per period: volume × standard time, expressed in hours or equivalent work units; respect seasonality or trend if described.
2. Calculate available capacity by resource type from INVENTARIO_RECURSOS: quantity × net productive hours, adjusted by UTILIZACION_OBJETIVO and discounting shrinkage (tag shrinkage [ASSUMPTION] with range if not provided; typical range 15–30%).
3. Cross demand against capacity in each period of HORIZONTE: calculate actual utilization, slack or deficit, and identify the bottleneck resource that limits aggregate throughput. Respect non-fungible resources: demand is only served by the enabled type, even if another type has slack.
4. Express cost in FTE-months (NEVER in money, NEVER "free"): total installed capacity cost, idle slack cost, and deficit covered by overtime or hiring cost. Convention: 1 FTE-month = net productive hours of a full-time resource in one month; declare the equivalence used.
5. Simulate ESCENARIOS respecting RESTRICCIONES; for each one report the break period (when actual utilization exceeds 100% or the defined healthy cap) and the incremental headcount in FTE-months to close it, discounting hiring lead time and the ramp curve (a new resource does not perform at 100% in the first period).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Interpret: confirm demand unit, standard time, utilization definition, and shrinkage composition; if DEMANDA_PROYECTADA, INVENTARIO_RECURSOS, standard times, or UTILIZACION_OBJETIVO is missing, ask before modeling and do not invent figures.
Phase 2 Plan: declare the calculation chain (demand to workload, resource to capacity, cross to utilization, utilization to FTE-month cost), the equivalence of 1 FTE-month, and list each [ASSUMPTION] with its sensitive range and the direction in which it moves the result.
Phase 3 Execute: run the model period by period, isolate the bottleneck (TOC: the constraint governs aggregate throughput), compare scenarios against the base, and derive recommendations prioritized by impact on the deficit and by feasibility within the lead time.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Workload is derived from volume × standard time, not estimated by eye.
- [ ] Capacity discounts shrinkage and applies target utilization by resource type.
- [ ] Actual utilization, slack, and deficit are calculated per period within the horizon.
- [ ] The bottleneck is named and justified by throughput (TOC), not assumed; non-fungible resources are respected.
- [ ] All cost is expressed in FTE-months with equivalence declared; zero monetary figures and zero use of "free".
- [ ] Each figure not provided by the user carries [ASSUMPTION] with sensitive range and direction of impact.
- [ ] Each scenario reports its break period and incremental headcount, discounting lead time and ramp.
- [ ] Recommendations are prioritized by impact on the deficit and temporal feasibility.
Edge cases to cover: demand with seasonality (do not average the peak period); bottleneck that migrates between types over the horizon; non-fungibility constraint that leaves unusable slack; break that falls within the hiring lead time (not closeable in time: flag as risk).
Expected deliverable: (1) capacity table by period (demand, capacity, utilization, slack/deficit), (2) bottleneck resource named and justified, (3) scenarios compared with break point, (4) three sizing recommendations prioritized by impact on the deficit, all in FTE-months.
spec-finanzas_consolidacion_multientidad:
[inputs]
- NOMBRE_GRUPO: {{NOMBRE_GRUPO}} > Name of the group or holding to consolidate
- PERIODO: {{PERIODO}} > Reporting period (e.g. annual close 2025, Q2 2026)
- ENTIDADES_Y_PARTICIPACION: {{ENTIDADES_Y_PARTICIPACION}} > Entities in the scope with ownership percentage, type of control (control / significant influence / joint venture), functional currency, and entry or exit date if applicable
- MONEDA_PRESENTACION: {{MONEDA_PRESENTACION}} > Single presentation currency of the consolidated statements
- TIPOS_DE_CAMBIO: {{TIPOS_DE_CAMBIO}} > Period-average rate (results) and closing rate (balance sheet) for each functional currency; historical rate for equity if provided
- OPERACIONES_INTERCOMPANY: {{OPERACIONES_INTERCOMPANY}} > Intercompany transactions: sales/purchases, loans, interest, dividends, unrealized margin in inventory and in transferred fixed assets (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
The {{NOMBRE_GRUPO}} group needs a consolidated view of {{PERIODO}} that represents the economic reality of the group as a single entity, not the sum of its parts. Consolidating correctly unlocks management decisions, reporting to the board or investors, IFRS compliance, and period-over-period comparability. Without proper intercompany elimination and currency conversion, the figures inflate revenues, distort margins, and break auditability.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior consolidation controller with experience in multi-entity groups and mastery of IFRS 10 (control and scope), IAS 21 (foreign currency translation), intercompany eliminations, unrealized margin, and non-controlling interest.

Deliverable: consolidated income statement and balance sheet of {{NOMBRE_GRUPO}} for {{PERIODO}} in {{MONEDA_PRESENTACION}}, with eliminations sheet, conversion adjustments, minority interest, reconciliation, and assumptions. Steps:
1. Confirm the scope from {{ENTIDADES_Y_PARTICIPACION}}: entities included, ownership, and method based on effective control (full consolidation if control; equity method for associates with significant influence; proportionate consolidation only for joint ventures when applicable).
2. Normalize each entity's chart of accounts and accounting policies to a common structure, with aligned recognition criteria and the same closing date, before aggregating.
3. Sum individual results and balance sheets of the scope line by line.
4. Identify and eliminate intercompany transactions from {{OPERACIONES_INTERCOMPANY}}: internal sales/purchases, loans and interest, internal dividends, unrealized margin in inventory and in transferred fixed assets; each elimination with its counterpart.
5. Convert each entity from its functional currency to {{MONEDA_PRESENTACION}} with {{TIPOS_DE_CAMBIO}}: results at average rate, balance sheet at closing rate; record the cumulative translation difference in equity (other comprehensive income), never in profit or loss.
6. Calculate minority interest on equity and on profit where ownership is below 100%, separating controlling from non-controlling interest.
7. Present the consolidated view with reconciliation and flag every imbalance with amount and probable cause.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 – Framing: validate scope, ownership, consolidation method, functional currency of each entity, entry/exit dates, and presentation currency. Tag every missing data point [ASSUMPTION] and ask; do not invent figures.
Phase 2 – Aggregation: map charts of accounts and harmonize policies to a common structure; sum individuals line by line.
Phase 3 – Eliminations: record each intercompany transaction with debit/credit and counterpart; cancel internal revenues and expenses; defer unrealized margin in inventory and fixed assets until realized with third parties.
Phase 4 – Conversion: apply average rate to results, closing rate to balance sheet, and historical rate to equity if provided; isolate the translation difference in equity.
Phase 5 – Minorities and close: separate controlling from non-controlling interest in equity and profit; build reconciliation: sum of individuals minus eliminations plus/minus conversion equals consolidated.
Edge cases to treat explicitly: cross or layered holdings; entity acquired or sold mid-{{PERIODO}} (partial consolidation by months); hyperinflationary economy (IAS 29); already-accrued dividends; goodwill or acquisition difference if reported.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Scope and consolidation method explicit per entity, derived from effective control.
- [ ] Chart of accounts and accounting policies normalized, with the same closing date, before summing.
- [ ] Every intercompany transaction eliminated with its documented counterpart; unrealized margin deferred.
- [ ] Results at average rate and balance sheet at closing rate; translation difference isolated in equity, not in profit or loss.
- [ ] Controlling and non-controlling interest calculated where ownership < 100%.
- [ ] Reconciliation balances: individuals − eliminations +/− conversion = consolidated; imbalances flagged with amount and cause.
- [ ] Applicable edge cases addressed (partial by months, hyperinflation, dividends, goodwill).
- [ ] Zero invented figures; assumptions tagged [ASSUMPTION] and auditability limits declared.
Expected deliverable: consolidated income statement and balance sheet in {{MONEDA_PRESENTACION}}, intercompany debit/credit eliminations sheet, detail of conversion adjustments, minority interest, auditable reconciliation table, assumptions block, and caveats block.
spec-personal_gtd_captura_universal:
[inputs]
- DOMINIOS: {{DOMINIOS}} > Life areas to sweep in the mind-sweep, in the desired order (e.g. "work, personal projects, home, finances, health, relationships, learning")
- TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE: {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}} > Minutes or hours available for the session; governs pace and depth (e.g. "30 minutes", "1 hour")
- DESTINO_INBOX: {{DESTINO_INBOX}} > Where the consolidated inbox will live (e.g. "an Apple Notes note", "a document", "my task app")
- NIVEL_DETALLE: {{NIVEL_DETALLE}} > Depth of triggers: light (quick sweep, 1–2 triggers per area) or exhaustive (extended trigger list). If omitted, calibrate by TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
My mind is saturated with open commitments, loose ideas, and pending items that keep circling without being recorded anywhere trustworthy, generating stress and attention leakage. I need to execute the GTD Capture step: completely empty my mind and consolidate everything into a single inbox in {{DESTINO_INBOX}}, without processing or organizing yet. A thorough sweep unlocks immediate mental clarity — the mind-like-water feeling — because everything that had my attention passes to live outside my head, in a system I trust. I work over the domains {{DOMINIOS}} in {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}}.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior personal productivity coach certified in Getting Things Done (David Allen), specialized in the Capture step and in facilitating trigger-guided mind-sweeps.

Deliverable: a single consolidated inbox with all my pending items captured, produced through a guided, interactive session:
1. Framing: confirm DOMINIOS, TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE, DESTINO_INBOX, and NIVEL_DETALLE; remind me that this session only captures (it does not process, prioritize, or organize) and set the golden rule: a captured concern no longer occupies the mind — everything is released, even the trivial.
2. Domain-by-domain mind-sweep: go through {{DOMINIOS}} one at a time, launching concrete triggers per area (what worries or circles you here; what you promised and did not deliver; what you left half-done; what decision you are postponing; what is waiting for someone else's response; what reminder or date you fear forgetting). Work in short rounds and wait for my responses before continuing.
3. Literal capture: record each thing as a loose item, exactly as I say it, without reformulating into jargon, grouping by affinity, or converting it into a next action. Mark vague items with [clarify] without discarding or interpreting them.
4. Domain close: before moving to a new area, ask "anything else in this area?".
5. Consolidation: deliver the single inbox as a flat numbered list, grouped only by source domain, with ambiguous items tagged [clarify].

Explicit assumptions: the session is conversational and turn-based; you do not fill in on my behalf. If a domain does not apply, I declare it empty and we move on. I work in first person and you only transcribe.
Limits: do not propose GTD categories, labels, contexts (@home, @office), or next actions at this stage; that belongs to Clarify/Organize. Do not estimate effort or urgency. Do not discard an item as trivial.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 – Framing and rules: validate inputs and state the golden rule. If NIVEL_DETALLE is empty, calibrate by TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE (under 20 min = light; more = exhaustive) and declare it.
Phase 2 – Guided sweep: advance domain by domain with triggers adapted to the detail level, in short interactive rounds, waiting for responses. Manage the clock: if time is running out, alert and prioritize closing pending domains with a quick sweep rather than deepening a single one.
Phase 3 – Faithful capture: note each item literally and individually as it appears; nothing is filtered, grouped, or reinterpreted. If I mention several things in one sentence, I separate them into distinct items without changing the words.
Phase 4 – Final consolidation: gather all items into the single inbox, numbered and grouped by source domain, with ambiguous items in [clarify]. Report the total count by domain.
Edge cases: if I enter process/prioritize mode, gently remind me that is Clarify and we continue capturing. If an item is repeated, keep it once and note it. If I am stuck in a domain, offer 2–3 additional triggers and, if it remains empty, move on.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- All DOMINIOS indicated were swept and closed with the "anything else?" question.
- Each item is captured as a loose, literal, unreformulated element; nothing was grouped by affinity or converted into a next action.
- Ambiguous items are tagged [clarify], not discarded or interpreted.
- No pending items were invented that I did not mention.
- The session respected scope: Capture only; no processing, prioritization, or organization.
- The level of detail applied was declared and the session respected TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE.
- The close reports count by domain and reminds me that the next GTD step is Clarify, in a separate session.
Expected deliverable: a single consolidated inbox for {{DESTINO_INBOX}}, flat numbered list grouped by source domain, with ambiguous items in [clarify], ready to clarify later.
spec-personal_gtd_clarificar_bandeja:
[inputs]
- BANDEJA_ENTRADA: {{BANDEJA_ENTRADA}} > Raw content to process: pending emails, notes, ideas, reminders, papers, messages (paste list or text)
- CONTEXTOS: {{CONTEXTOS}} > GTD contexts available for routing actions (e.g. "office, home, calls, errands, computer"); if omitted, infer a minimal set and tag it [ASSUMPTION]
- DELEGADOS: {{DELEGADOS}} > People you can delegate to and their role (e.g. "assistant, partner, marketing team"); if omitted, do not delegate and note the gap
- REGLA_DOS_MINUTOS: {{REGLA_DOS_MINUTOS}} > Threshold for the do-now rule; default "2 minutes" (optional)
- HORIZONTE: {{HORIZONTE}} > Calendar window for deferring tasks with a date (e.g. "this week", "next 14 days") (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
My inbox has accumulated elements of different natures that I have not yet decided what they are or what to do with them, and that ambiguity creates mental load and things that fall through the cracks. I need to process {{BANDEJA_ENTRADA}} until it reaches zero, transforming each element into a clear destination following the Getting Things Done method. Clarifying well unlocks a mind confident that nothing is lost: each thing will end up as a concrete next action, a project, a calendar appointment, or a storage location, ready to execute without thinking about it again. The value is not just emptying the inbox but having each decision made only once.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior personal productivity coach certified in Getting Things Done (David Allen), expert in the Clarify phase of the five-step workflow (capture, clarify, organize, reflect, engage). Discipline: one decision per item, without reprocessing.

Deliverable: an inbox processed to zero, where each item in {{BANDEJA_ENTRADA}} is resolved. Proceed as follows:
1. Framing: confirm the item inventory, the {{CONTEXTOS}} available, and the list of {{DELEGADOS}}. If {{BANDEJA_ENTRADA}} is empty, illegible, or a single block without clear separators, ask for clarification or propose how to segment it before continuing.
2. Process each item sequentially, one by one, skipping none and returning nothing to the inbox. Anti-loop rule: a touched item is not reopened; if it generates new work, that work is a separate item.
3. For each item apply the decision tree in strict order: first "what is it" (define the desired outcome), then "does it require action."
4. If NOT actionable, assign exactly one of three outputs: delete (trash/expired), incubate in Someday / Maybe (possible but not now), or archive as Reference (useful information, no action). Do not mix these three.
5. If YES actionable, define the physical and visible next action; if it takes less than {{REGLA_DOS_MINUTOS}}, mark it do-now; if not, choose delegate (responsible from {{DELEGADOS}} + expected deliverable back + reminder in "Waiting") or defer: calendar only if it has a fixed day/time (within {{HORIZONTE}}), or context list if it only depends on where/with what tool. Key distinction: calendar = hard-date commitment; context list = done when possible.
6. If the desired outcome requires more than one step, also register it as a project with its associated visible next action; the project's next action goes into the corresponding context list.
7. Close with a quantitative summary by output and the list of new projects.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 – Inventory: list the items numbered as they arrived; do not edit their content yet. Declare the total N at entry.
Phase 2 – Clarification item by item: for each one apply the decision tree and produce a card with: (a) original text, (b) actionable yes/no, (c) assigned output, (d) next action as a concrete physical infinitive verb (not a topic; e.g. "call Ana to set a date", not "Ana meeting"), (e) context from {{CONTEXTOS}}, (f) responsible party and date if applicable. Tag [ASSUMPTION] every inference about my intent and flag it for confirmation; if an item is genuinely ambiguous or multivalent, ask instead of guessing. Do not invent contexts or delegates outside those provided.
Phase 3 – Consolidation: group outputs into lists (Do now, Next actions by context, Waiting/delegated, Calendar, Someday/Maybe, Reference, Deleted) and extract detected projects with their next action.
Phase 4 – Verification: deliver the count by output and verify that the sum of all outputs equals N. If it does not balance, identify the lost or duplicated item and correct before closing.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] All items in {{BANDEJA_ENTRADA}} were processed; none remained in the inbox, none was omitted, none was reopened.
- [ ] The actionable / non-actionable distinction was applied before any other classification.
- [ ] Each actionable item has a next action worded as a physical infinitive verb, not a vague topic.
- [ ] Non-actionable outputs are correctly separated into delete, Someday/Maybe, and Reference, without mixing.
- [ ] Do-now items respect the {{REGLA_DOS_MINUTOS}} threshold; deferred ones distinguish calendar (fixed day/time) from context list.
- [ ] Every delegation names a real responsible party from {{DELEGADOS}} and the expected deliverable back, with a reminder in Waiting.
- [ ] Projects (more than one step) are identified and each has its associated next action in a context list.
- [ ] No contexts or delegates were invented outside those provided.
- [ ] Inferences are tagged [ASSUMPTION] and ambiguous items generated a question, not a guess.
- [ ] The final count by output totals exactly N items at entry.
- [ ] No prices.
Expected deliverable: inbox at zero with the decision card for each item, consolidated lists by output, new projects with their next action, and the quantitative summary confirming full coverage (sum = N).
spec-personal_gtd_siguiente_accion:
[inputs]
- TAREA_VAGA: {{TAREA_VAGA}} > The task or pending item formulated vaguely or stuck that you want to land
- CONTEXTO_GTD: {{CONTEXTO_GTD}} > Context where you will execute the action: desk, phone, street, home, errands (optional)
- HERRAMIENTAS_DISPONIBLES: {{HERRAMIENTAS_DISPONIBLES}} > Resources or people at hand: computer, phone, agenda, key contact (optional)
- RESTRICCIONES_TIEMPO: {{RESTRICCIONES_TIEMPO}} > Time or real window available to start (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A vague task trapped in the mind consumes attention and blocks action because it does not say what to do first. The purpose is to transform it into the concrete physical next action per GTD (David Allen): the single visible and specific step that is executed without thinking again. Defining it well unblocks progress, frees mental load, and converts inertia into movement. A poorly defined action (mental verb, hidden multi-step, other-dependent) reproduces the stuck state; that is why the quality criterion is strict.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior personal productivity coach trained in the Getting Things Done (GTD) method, specialist in the next-action discipline and in distinguishing projects from actions.
Deliverable: the concrete physical next action, ready to paste into a task list. Steps:
1. Diagnose why TAREA_VAGA is stuck: a multi-step project disguised as a task, absence of a physical verb, dependency on a third party, diffuse ending, or lack of prior information that prevents concretizing the verb.
2. If it requires several steps to complete, name it as a project (statement of the desired outcome) and isolate only its next action; do not deliver the full list.
3. Draft ONE single next action that starts with a physical observable verb (call, write, open, search, draft, send, print, schedule); never decide, organize, plan, or think.
4. Ensure it marks the real first move, can start ideally in under two minutes, and is associated with CONTEXTO_GTD, HERRAMIENTAS_DISPONIBLES, and RESTRICCIONES_TIEMPO when they exist.
5. Connect the action with the outcome it unblocks in one sentence.

Edge rules:
- Dependency on a third party: the next action is yours, not theirs (draft and send the message; not "wait for reply"). "Waiting for X" is noted separately, not as an action.
- If TAREA_VAGA is already a clear physical action, confirm it and refine it (verb + context); do not invent an unnecessary project.
- If a data point essential to concretizing the verb is missing (to whom, where, with what), formulate ONE question and stop before delivering.
Limits: one single action per delivery; do not invent tools, contacts, or deadlines not declared; neutral, professional English, no emojis.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Interpret: restate TAREA_VAGA in your own words and classify its type of stuck state.
Phase 2 Plan: decide whether it is a single action or a project; choose the physical verb and context; identify missing data points.
Phase 3 Execute: draft the next action, validate it against the criteria checklist, and deliver it with its connecting sentence.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The action starts with a physical observable verb (not decide, organize, plan, or think).
- [ ] It is ONE single action, not a list or an objective.
- [ ] It describes the real first move and can start ideally in under two minutes.
- [ ] It is associated with an executable context and, if known, with tools and time window.
- [ ] If it was multi-step, the project was named separately and its next action isolated.
- [ ] If it depended on a third party, the delivered action is your own (not "wait").
- [ ] Includes the sentence connecting the action with the outcome it unblocks.
- [ ] No tools, contacts, or deadlines were invented that were not declared.
Expected deliverable: block with the next action ready to paste, its context, and if applicable the name of the associated project, plus the connecting sentence; or ONE single question if a data point essential to concretize the verb is missing.
spec-personal_gtd_listas_contexto:
[inputs]
- VOLCADO_TAREAS: {{VOLCADO_TAREAS}} > Raw list of pending items, ideas, and reminders as written, ideally one per line (the unprocessed capture)
- CONTEXTOS_DISPONIBLES: {{CONTEXTOS_DISPONIBLES}} > Contexts where you spend time and want to use as lists (e.g. @calls, @computer, @errands, @home, @office, @agenda); leave empty to use the GTD default (optional)
- HERRAMIENTAS_RECURSOS: {{HERRAMIENTAS_RECURSOS}} > Tools and resources at hand that condition where you can do each thing (phone, computer, car, access, another person's presence); used to disambiguate context (optional)
- DELEGADO_ESPERANDO: {{DELEGADO_ESPERANDO}} > Things you already requested or delegated to third parties and are waiting to get back, with who and since when if you remember (optional)
- REGLA_ENERGIA_TIEMPO: {{REGLA_ENERGIA_TIEMPO}} > How you decide what to do (energy criteria, time blocks, today/week horizon) to sharpen the labels; default: high/medium/low energy and estimated minutes (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I have a task dump: a raw mix of unprocessed pending items, ideas, and reminders. In that state it is not useful for execution, because it forces a re-decision at every gap and that exhausts attention. I need to reorganize it into context lists following the Getting Things Done (GTD) method by David Allen: group the next actions by the resource they require (place, tool, or person) so that at any moment I look only at the list for the context I am in and choose by energy and available time, not by willpower. The missing step is Clarify + Organize: convert each entry into a physical and visible next action, filter the non-actionable, and label by context. Well-built lists unlock friction-free execution: I use the gaps (a call while in line, an errand in passing) and stop reopening the same decision over and over.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior personal productivity coach expert in Getting Things Done (GTD) by David Allen, specialized in the Clarify and Organize steps and in designing actionable context lists.

Produce my GTD context lists with these components:
1. Actionability triage: for each item in the dump decide whether it is actionable. Route non-actionable items to Someday/Maybe, Reference, or Delete; mark anything taking less than two minutes "Do-it-now" without sending it to a list.
2. Next actions: rewrite each actionable item as a physical and visible next action starting with a verb (not "quarterly report" but "draft the revenue section of the Q3 report"). If an item requires more than one step, mark it Project and extract only its single next action.
3. Context assignment: place each next action in a single context from those available (GTD default: @calls, @computer, @errands, @home, @office, @agenda). Use HERRAMIENTAS_RECURSOS to disambiguate when an item could fit in two. Add to each action an energy label (high/medium/low) and a time estimate.
4. Delegated and conversations: send anything waiting from third parties to @waiting-for with who and since when (integrating DELEGADO_ESPERANDO); send anything depending on a conversation to @agenda grouped by person.
5. Calendar vs. context: if an item has a hard date/time or attached commitment (not a mere preference for when), flag it as Calendar and do NOT put it in a context list; context lists are only for actions without a fixed date.
6. Separate output blocks: Projects (with their next action), Someday/Maybe, and Items-to-clarify (ambiguous ones, each with the specific question you need answered).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 – Clarify: go through the dump item by item applying the GTD decision tree (actionable yes/no; one step or several; under two minutes or not; hard date or not). Do not add tasks not in the dump; tag [ASSUMPTION] every inference.
Phase 2 – Reformulate: convert each actionable item into a next action with a verb, concrete and visible; if multi-step, separate the Project and its single next action.
Phase 3 – Organize: assign single context, energy, and time; set aside Calendar; separate @waiting-for and @agenda; group the rest into Projects and Someday/Maybe.
Phase 4 – Verify: confirm each action lives in one single context, starts with a verb, and is executable without further thought; send ambiguous ones to Items-to-clarify with their question. If the dump arrives empty, ask for the capture before continuing.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- Each next action starts with a verb and is physical, visible, and executable without thinking again about what it means.
- No actionable item is left without a context; no action appears in two contexts at once.
- Multi-step items are marked Project and only their single next action appears in the lists.
- Non-actionable items are correctly routed (Someday/Maybe, Reference, or Delete) and under-two-minute ones marked "Do-it-now".
- Items with a hard date/commitment are in Calendar, not in context lists.
- @waiting-for includes who and since when; @agenda is grouped by person.
- No tasks were invented; inferences are tagged [ASSUMPTION] and ambiguous ones in Items-to-clarify with their specific question.
- Each action carries an energy label (high/medium/low) and a time estimate.
- Traceability: each item from the original dump appears exactly once in some output (list, block, or Delete), with no losses or duplicates.
Expected deliverable: a set of context lists, one section per context, each next action on a line with its energy and time labels, plus separate blocks for Projects (with next action), @waiting-for, @agenda, Calendar, Someday/Maybe, and Items-to-clarify, ready to paste into your task manager and execute.
spec-personal_gtd_proyectos_resultados:
[inputs]
- LISTA_PENDIENTES: {{LISTA_PENDIENTES}} > Raw list of mixed commitments, pending items, ideas, and projects, one per line or separated by commas
- AREA_FOCO: {{AREA_FOCO}} > Life area or current focus framing the review (e.g. work, home, health, career transition)
- CRITERIO_PRIORIDAD: {{CRITERIO_PRIORIDAD}} > How to order the projects (e.g. urgency, available energy, impact, deadline); if more than one is given, the first is the primary criterion and the rest break ties
- HORIZONTE_SUPERIOR: {{HORIZONTE_SUPERIOR}} > (optional) Areas of responsibility or larger objectives to link the projects to; if omitted, infer from the list and mark the link as inferred
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I have a raw list of mixed commitments, pending items, and ideas without structure. Without separating the actionable from the multi-step, and without defining where each thing is going, the system generates anxiety instead of control. The goal is a clean project inventory where each outcome is clear and each project has a single next action ready to execute, so that when I sit down I know exactly what to do without rethinking the whole project. Current focus: {{AREA_FOCO}}. Priority: {{CRITERIO_PRIORIDAD}}.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior coach certified in GTD (Getting Things Done by David Allen), specialized in refining personal productivity systems and in the desired-outcome + next-action discipline.
Deliverable: project inventory in a table with columns Project | Desired outcome | Next action | Context | Horizon/Notes, ordered by {{CRITERIO_PRIORIDAD}}, plus a separate list of single actions.
Steps:
1. Process each element in {{LISTA_PENDIENTES}} and classify it: single action (one step) vs. project (requires more than one step).
2. For each project, draft the desired outcome as an already-fulfilled, verifiable success statement: it will be true the day the project is complete.
3. Define the single next action: physical, visible, and concrete, starting with a verb, with the context indicating where or how it is executed (call, draft, buy, search, schedule).
4. Assign the horizon: operational project or its link to {{HORIZONTE_SUPERIOR}}; if the action cannot yet be executed, record in Notes the dependency, wait (who/what is being waited for), or date.
5. Order the table by {{CRITERIO_PRIORIDAD}} and list the single actions that are not projects separately.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Capture: normalize the list, separate each element, remove obvious duplicates.
Phase 2 Clarify: apply the single-step vs. multi-step rule; if a next action is still multi-step it is a sub-project and is broken down.
Phase 3 Organize: complete the five columns per project; verify each outcome is verifiable and each action is physical and unambiguous.
Phase 4 Prioritize: order by the criterion and flag blocks or waits.
Explicit assumptions: a vague element without an action verb is treated as a project until clarified; ideas or "someday/maybe" items are listed separately as incubation, not as active projects.
Edge cases: if two elements are the same project, they are merged; if an element mixes two different outcomes, it is split into two projects.
Limits: no items, outcomes, or dates are invented; ambiguous items are tagged {to confirm} or asked about before executing.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
- Each project has exactly one desired outcome drafted as an already-fulfilled, verifiable success statement.
- Each project has exactly one physical, visible next action starting with a verb and with an explicit context.
- No next action is itself multi-step (if it were, it is broken down into a sub-project).
- Single actions that are not projects are listed separately, not mixed in; "someday/maybe" ideas go to a separate incubation list.
- Each project has an assigned horizon: operational or linked to {{HORIZONTE_SUPERIOR}} (marked as inferred if deduced).
- The table is ordered by {{CRITERIO_PRIORIDAD}} and records dependencies, waits, or dates in Notes.
- No missing data is invented: it is asked for or tagged {to confirm}.
Expected deliverable: table Project | Desired outcome | Next action | Context | Horizon/Notes, plus the separate list of single actions and, if applicable, the incubation list.
spec-personal_gtd_regla_dos_minutos:
[inputs]
- BANDEJA_ENTRADA: {{BANDEJA_ENTRADA}} > List of pending items to process: emails, notes, errands, loose reminders, messages to reply to. One per line or separated by dashes
- CONTEXTO_DISPONIBLE: {{CONTEXTO_DISPONIBLE}} > Tools and resources at hand right now (open email, phone, document, access to someone to delegate to). Defines which micro-actions can be executed immediately
- VENTANA_TIEMPO: {{VENTANA_TIEMPO}} > Time block available for this processing session (e.g. 20 minutes)
- CRITERIO_DELEGACION: {{CRITERIO_DELEGACION}} > Personal rule for delegating instead of doing it yourself (e.g. delegate if you are not the right person or if it exceeds 10 minutes). If omitted, assumed: delegate only when another person is clearly more suitable and the responsible party is named (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I process my pending inbox to reach GTD's mind-like-water state: zero accumulation of micro-tasks generating mental friction. The two-minute rule prevents dozens of trivial actions from becoming a list that costs more to manage than to execute. Processing this batch well unlocks focus for subsequent deep work and reduces the cognitive cost of open pending items in the mind.
Limits: this flow clarifies and organizes, it does not execute actions longer than two minutes or send anything on my behalf; it only leaves the text or micro-guide ready. It does not replace a complete weekly review of all GTD systems.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: senior personal-productivity coach specialized in David Allen's GTD (Getting Things Done) method, with mastery of the capture-clarify-organize flow and the principle that clarifying is not doing.
Deliverable: a processing log of the inbox with each item classified into a single category and micro-actions under two minutes executed or ready to execute right now.
Steps:
1. Go through BANDEJA_ENTRADA item by item; for each one first determine whether it requires action. If not, mark it as eliminate, archive as reference (with where to store it), or incubate (someday / waiting, with a review trigger).
2. If it requires action, define the concrete next physical action (verb + object, executable without sub-decisions) and realistically estimate its duration.
3. If the next action takes less than two minutes, mark it Do it now and deliver the exact text or micro-guide to execute it immediately using CONTEXTO_DISPONIBLE.
4. If it takes more than two minutes, classify it as delegate (according to CRITERIO_DELEGACION, naming the responsible party and what is expected), schedule (with date/time because it only happens on that day), or defer (next actions, with @ context if applicable).
5. Respect VENTANA_TIEMPO: if the batch of micro-tasks exceeds it, prioritize those with the greatest unblocking effect or lowest delay cost and defer the rest with an explicit note.
Edge cases: item that is a multi-step project disguised as a task -> separate it and capture only the next action + project note; ambiguous item with no clear action -> incubate and mark for clarification; <2 min micro-task that depends on a third party -> not Do it now, goes to waiting.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Clarify: for each item apply the GTD decision tree (requires action / what is the next action / how long does it take / is it a project).
Phase 2 Sift two minutes: separate micro-tasks (<2 min) from larger tasks; for micro-tasks that depend on data or a decision only the user knows, ask before drafting — never invent recipients, figures, or commitments.
Phase 3 Execute and log: draft or describe the micro-action ready to run and consolidate the final table by category (now / delegate / schedule / defer / eliminate-archive) with its estimated time.
Bias to watch: the micro-task is only done now because the inbox is already being processed; do not interrupt focused work to slip in two-minute actions. Second bias: do not inflate the threshold; if uncertain between 2 and 3 minutes, treat as more than two so as not to break the processing flow.
Assumed trade-off: the two-minute threshold optimizes processing fluency, not strategic priority; a trivial micro-task may be done now even though a deferred task is more important, because its management cost exceeds its execution cost.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Every item in BANDEJA_ENTRADA was classified into exactly one category (now / delegate / schedule / defer / eliminate-archive).
- [ ] Every action starts with a concrete verb and describes the next physical executable action, not a vague area or a multi-step project.
- [ ] The two-minute threshold was applied consistently and the duration estimate is realistic.
- [ ] No micro-action includes invented data, recipients, or figures; anything missing was asked about.
- [ ] The Do it now batch respects VENTANA_TIEMPO; the excess was deferred with a priority justification.
- [ ] Delegated items name the responsible party and scheduled items carry a date; incubated items carry a review trigger.
Expected deliverable: processing log with a table per category, two-minute micro-actions ready to execute (text or micro-guide included), and the total estimated batch time versus VENTANA_TIEMPO.
spec-personal_gtd_revision_diaria:
[inputs]
- FECHA: {{FECHA}} > Day of the review; anchors deadlines and overdue items (optional, defaults to today)
- CALENDARIO_HOY: {{CALENDARIO_HOY}} > Meetings and fixed blocks with their schedule (e.g. 9:00-10:00 standup); base for calculating discretionary time
- SIGUIENTES_ACCIONES: {{SIGUIENTES_ACCIONES}} > List of next actions, ideally with context, estimated duration, and deadline
- ENERGIA_DISPONIBLE: {{ENERGIA_DISPONIBLE}} > Level and hours of real expected focus today (e.g. high 3h in the morning)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
At the start of the day I need to decide my focus before the day decides it for me. A well-executed GTD daily review converts a vague list of pending items and a packed calendar into 1 to 3 realistic priorities. This unlocks entering execution with clear criteria, avoids overload, and protects discretionary time for what truly moves the needle.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior productivity coach specialized in GTD (Getting Things Done by David Allen), with mastery of contexts, next actions, the two-minute rule, and the task vs. project distinction.
Deliverable: a day plan on a single screen. Steps:
1. Restate the calendar {{CALENDARIO_HOY}} and energy {{ENERGIA_DISPONIBLE}}; calculate the remaining discretionary time for {{FECHA}} by subtracting fixed blocks.
2. Take {{SIGUIENTES_ACCIONES}} and group them by context (computer, calls, errands, waiting-for, home) when the data exists.
3. Recommend 1 to 3 priorities that fit within the discretionary time, justifying each one by impact and deadline.
4. Explicitly declare what will NOT be done today and why it is deferred.
5. Flag overdue actions or those at risk and every item that is a project disguised as a task (requires more than one action) and reformulate it as its concrete next physical and visible action.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Interpret: confirm date, fixed commitments, and energy; if CALENDARIO_HOY, SIGUIENTES_ACCIONES, or ENERGIA_DISPONIBLE are missing or ambiguous, ask for them and do not invent commitments.
Phase 2 Plan: subtract calendar, estimate discretionary time, sort candidates by impact and due date, pre-select 1 to 3, and apply the two-minute rule to trivial items.
Phase 3 Execute: deliver the plan on a single screen with time blocks, priorities, the first next action for each, and the list of deferrals.
Edge cases: day with no discretionary time (meetings only) > deliver only alerts and deferrals; low energy > prioritize low cognitive-effort actions; no deadlines > prioritize by declared impact.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Discretionary time calculated by explicitly subtracting the calendar.
- [ ] Between 1 and 3 priorities, each justified by impact and deadline.
- [ ] Sum of estimated durations of priorities <= discretionary time.
- [ ] Visible list of what will NOT be done today with the reason for deferral.
- [ ] Overdue or at-risk actions flagged; projects disguised as tasks identified and reformulated as next actions.
- [ ] Each priority expressed as a concrete next action starting with a verb.
- [ ] Two-minute rule applied to trivial items (do now, do not schedule).
- [ ] No invented data or commitments; assumptions marked [ASSUMPTION]; no prices.
Expected deliverable: day plan on a single screen (time blocks + 1 to 3 priorities with their first next action + deferrals + alerts), ready to execute.
spec-personal_gtd_someday_maybe:
[inputs]
- VOLCADO_IDEAS: {{VOLCADO_IDEAS}} > Raw list, loose notes, or paragraph with the ideas, desires, and eventual projects to incubate
- AREAS_DE_VIDA: {{AREAS_DE_VIDA}} > Focus areas for grouping (e.g. career, health, finances, relationships, learning, travel, creative projects)
- FRECUENCIA_REVISION: {{FRECUENCIA_REVISION}} > Desired review cadence (weekly, bi-weekly, or monthly)
- MOMENTO_VITAL: {{MOMENTO_VITAL}} > Energy and current context for calibrating the enthusiasm of each idea (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I have ideas, desires, and eventual projects scattered in my mind and in loose notes that do not require action now but that I do not want to lose or turn into a source of guilt. I need a GTD-style Someday/Maybe list: a reliable incubator that frees my mind and can be reviewed without pressure. Curating it well gives me mental clarity, prevents valuable ideas from fading, and separates what is already ready for action from what only needs to keep maturing.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior personal-productivity coach certified in the Getting Things Done (GTD) methodology by David Allen, specialized in designing idea incubators and no-pressure review rituals.

Deliverable: a curated and categorized Someday/Maybe list plus a review ritual ready to operate. Steps:
1. Validate inputs; if VOLCADO_IDEAS or AREAS_DE_VIDA are missing or ambiguous, ask before continuing; never invent absent ideas.
2. Capture without filtering and classify each entry: Someday/Maybe (no commitment) versus next action or active project (separate and mark to exit the incubator).
3. Refine duplicates, merge repeated intentions, and reformulate each entry as an evocative and specific phrase, understandable without context.
4. Organize by AREAS_DE_VIDA (or by type: learn, create, acquire, experience, contribute) and assign a light enthusiasm signal (high/medium/low) calibrated with MOMENTO_VITAL; the signal is indicative, never a commitment.
5. Define the review ritual with a three-exit criterion per entry (Activate/Keep/Release) and brief guiding questions.
6. Deliver: curated incubator list; separate list of extracted actions/projects; review calendar with the chosen cadence; 5-minute review mini-script.

Explicit assumptions: the dump may mix real tasks with vague desires; most entries will be pure incubation. If MOMENTO_VITAL is not provided, enthusiasm is only noted when the idea itself suggests it and it is noted that calibration is missing. If there are no attachments, work only with the received text.
Limits: no deadlines, goals, or metrics are set for the ideas (that would remove them from the incubator); they are not prioritized beyond the indicative enthusiasm signal; no new ideas are generated to fill gaps.
Edge cases: an idea that is both a desire and an immediate action > duplicate as an incubator entry (the aspiration) and as an extracted action (the concrete step). Repeated idea with different nuances > merge while preserving the richer nuance. Ambiguous idea or unclear intention > mark {pending_confirmation} instead of guessing. An idea that no longer resonates > leave it in the list but flag it as an explicit Release candidate for the next review.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Capture: collect all VOLCADO_IDEAS without judging; no idea is too small or too ambitious.
Phase 2 Clarify: separate pure incubation from real actions/projects; reformulate as desires or possibilities, not as tasks with imperative verbs.
Phase 3 Organize: group by area or type, assign indicative enthusiasm signal, refine and merge.
Phase 4 Ritualize: set the FRECUENCIA_REVISION cadence, codify the Activate/Keep/Release criterion with guiding questions, and write the 5-minute script.
Phase 5 Deliver: present the four components in order and actionable, with {pending_confirmation} entries flagged for resolution at the first review.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- Every idea from VOLCADO_IDEAS appears, refined and without duplicates; no new ideas were invented.
- Real actions and projects are separated and marked, outside the incubator.
- Each entry is reformulated as an evocative and specific phrase, readable without future context and without an imperative task verb.
- The list is categorized by AREAS_DE_VIDA or by type, with a light, indicative, non-obligatory enthusiasm signal.
- The ritual includes an explicit cadence derived from FRECUENCIA_REVISION, the three-exit criterion (Activate/Keep/Release), and guiding questions.
- Ambiguous ideas are marked {pending_confirmation}, not force-classified.
- The tone is serene, without pressure or guilt; the incubator frees the mind.
Expected deliverable: document with four blocks (1) curated and categorized incubator list, (2) list of extracted actions/projects, (3) review calendar, (4) 5-minute review mini-script.
spec-personal_gtd_lista_espera:
[inputs]
- ITEMS_PENDIENTES: {{ITEMS_PENDIENTES}} > List of things delegated or expected from others, with whatever information you have for each (what you are waiting for, from whom, via which channel, since when, committed date). If empty or ambiguous, the AI must ask before continuing.
- CADENCIA_REVISION: {{CADENCIA_REVISION}} > Frequency for reviewing the list (e.g. weekly on Mondays, twice a week). "(optional)" default weekly on Mondays.
- POLITICA_ESCALAMIENTO: {{POLITICA_ESCALAMIENTO}} > Grace days after the committed date before escalating and to whom to escalate. "(optional)" default 2 business days and escalate to the responsible party's direct manager.
- ZONA_HORARIA: {{ZONA_HORARIA}} > Time zone for calculating follow-up dates and reminders. "(optional)" default America/Bogota (UTC-5).
- TONO_MENSAJES: {{TONO_MENSAJES}} > Tone of the follow-up templates (e.g. cordial and firm, formal, friendly). "(optional)" default cordial and firm.
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Delegating and asking things of others multiplies your capacity, but what leaves your mind and enters someone else's tends to evaporate. The GTD Waiting For list is the only place where every third-party commitment with a responsible party and a date lives, so that follow-up is systematic and does not depend on your memory. Operating it well unlocks peace of mind (nothing delegated gets lost), recovers stuck deliverables before they cost time or relationships, and provides an objective basis for reminding and escalating without friction or guilt.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior personal-productivity coach certified in David Allen's Getting Things Done (GTD), specialized in delegation tracking systems.

Deliverable: an operational and reusable Waiting For system. Steps:
1. Waiting For master table with columns: ID, item awaited (concrete and verifiable deliverable), responsible party (person or organization), delegation channel, delegation date, committed follow-up date, next reminder, status (Waiting / To Escalate / Overdue / Closed), notes. Populate it with ITEMS_PENDIENTES.
2. Calculate status and next reminder per row with ZONA_HORARIA and POLITICA_ESCALAMIENTO: Overdue if the committed date has passed; To Escalate if the grace days were exceeded. When the committed date is missing, propose a default (e.g. delegation date + 5 business days) and mark it [to be confirmed].
3. Classification rules: what enters Waiting For (depends on a third party) versus own action or project; how to write items oriented toward a verifiable deliverable; when and how to close a row when the awaited item arrives.
4. Review routine with CADENCIA_REVISION cadence: review order, overdue detection, criterion for sending a reminder, criterion and recipient for escalation. Integrate it with the GTD weekly review.
5. At least three message templates in TONO_MENSAJES tone: approaching due date, overdue, and escalation, all with curly-brace fields for personalization.

Explicit assumptions to declare: definition of business day, treatment of holidays, reminder window prior to the committed date, and age criterion for items without a date. Do not invent data: the unknown goes as [to be confirmed].

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Capture: collect ITEMS_PENDIENTES; if empty or ambiguous, ask for them before continuing. Do not invent responsible parties or dates; mark the unknown as [to be confirmed].
Phase 2 - Structure: empty each commitment into a row, with a clear deliverable verb; separate own actions into a side note and do not mix them into the list.
Phase 3 - Status and reminders: calculate status and next reminder per row according to dates, ZONA_HORARIA, and POLITICA_ESCALAMIENTO; make explicit the assumptions of business day, holidays, and reminder window used.
Phase 4 - Operations: deliver classification rules, review routine, and follow-up and escalation templates.
Phase 5 - Close: summarize overdue items and follow-up next actions prioritized by urgency; list in a separate block the [to be confirmed] data that limit precision.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Every row has a named responsible party and a follow-up date; no invented data (the unknown goes as [to be confirmed]).
- [ ] Only items that depend on third parties appear; no own action is in the list.
- [ ] Each item is written as a concrete and verifiable deliverable, not a vague topic.
- [ ] Status and next reminder are consistent with the dates, time zone, and escalation policy, with business day and holiday assumptions declared.
- [ ] The review routine specifies order, how to detect overdue items, when to remind, and when/to whom to escalate.
- [ ] There are at least three templates ready to use (approaching due date, overdue, and escalation).
- [ ] There is a final block with [to be confirmed] data that limit precision.
Expected deliverable: populated Waiting For master table, classification rules, review routine with the indicated cadence, three or more follow-up and escalation templates, and a closing block with prioritized overdue items and next actions plus data pending confirmation.
