spec-personal_gtd_horizontes_enfoque:
[inputs]
- ACCIONES_PROYECTOS: {{ACCIONES_PROYECTOS}} > Today's next actions and active projects (runway and 10,000 feet); raw list as it exists in your mind or your system
- AREAS_RESPONSABILIDAD: {{AREAS_RESPONSABILIDAD}} > Areas of focus and responsibility at 20,000 feet in work and personal life (roles, domains, standards you sustain continuously, not projects)
- METAS_1_2_ANOS: {{METAS_1_2_ANOS}} > Goals and objectives at 30,000 feet, 1-2 year horizon
- VISION_3_5_ANOS: {{VISION_3_5_ANOS}} > Vision at 40,000 feet, 3-5 year horizon: what success looks like in the medium term
- PROPOSITO_PRINCIPIOS: {{PROPOSITO_PRINCIPIOS}} > Purpose and principles at 50,000+ feet: why you do what you do and non-negotiable values
- FOCO_REVISION: {{FOCO_REVISION}} > Focus or objective of this review (e.g. "reduce overload", "decide what to release", "realign the year") (optional; if missing, use balance between reducing overload and closing alignment gaps, and declare it)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need to map my life and work across the six GTD horizons of focus (David Allen) to see, at a glance, whether what occupies my days truly traces back to what matters most to me. The typical symptom is being busy on the runway without knowing whether those actions serve any goal, vision, or purpose. This map unlocks high-value decisions: what to release without guilt, what to delegate, what to create, and what to reorder — and where my GTD system has gaps in the higher levels that I almost never review. It is not an inbox cleanup: it is an altitude review that connects day-to-day with the long term.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior coach certified in GTD (Getting Things Done), specialized in reviewing the higher levels (Horizons of Focus) and in aligning daily execution with goals, vision, and purpose.
Deliverable: an altitude map of the six horizons with a vertical alignment diagnosis and a realignment plan. Steps:
1. Frame the six horizons and confirm which level each input I gave you belongs to; classify from bottom to top: Runway / Actions, 10k / Projects, 20k / Areas, 30k / 1-2 Year Goals, 40k / 3-5 Year Vision, 50k+ / Purpose and Principles. Key distinction: a project has a defined end (a result to reach); an area of responsibility is sustained without an end (ongoing standard); when in doubt, use this rule and note it.
2. For each level produce: what I have today (summary), what is vague or missing, and health signals (overload, emptiness, ambiguity). Apply a traffic light per level: green aligned and manageable, yellow needs attention, red critical (severe overload or emptiness that blocks deciding at the level above).
3. Upward vertical cross: mark as orphan work every action or project that does not trace back to any goal, area, vision, or purpose. An orphan is not always a discard: it may be legitimate maintenance, an external commitment, or a signal of an undeclared area; classify each one before proposing action.
4. Downward vertical cross: mark as intention without traction every goal, area, vision, or principle that has no project or action sustaining it. Distinguish a newly declared intention (not yet cascaded down) from an abandoned one (should have traction and does not).
5. Detect conflicts between levels: a goal that contradicts a principle, an overinvested area versus a neglected one, or two goals competing for the same finite time or resource.
6. Concrete realignments in four GTD moves: release, delegate, create (new project or next action, written as a physical and visible action), and reorder priorities; rank them by impact on FOCO_REVISION and note the cost or friction of each.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Capture: sort my raw inputs across the six levels without judging; if a piece of data belongs to two levels, place it in the dominant one and note it; if an input arrives empty, declare it as a gap, do not invent it.
Phase 2 Diagnosis by level: complete the status and traffic light for each horizon and flag gaps, marking [ASSUMPTION] on every inference.
Phase 3 Vertical alignment: execute the upward and downward crosses and list orphans (classified) and intentions without traction (distinguishing newly declared from abandoned); then list conflicts between levels.
Phase 4 Realignment: convert findings into release/delegate/create/reorder moves, prioritized by FOCO_REVISION, with cost or friction noted.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and which level you assigned each input to, present your plan, and ask for missing data before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- The six horizons are named with their altitude and every input was classified at one level (with a note if it was ambiguous).
- Each level reports what exists today, what is missing, and a traffic light; gaps at higher levels (vision, purpose) are explicit, not filled in.
- Every action and project was evaluated by upward tracing; orphans are listed and classified (discard, maintenance, undeclared area).
- Every goal, area, vision, and principle was evaluated by downward traction; intentions without traction distinguish newly declared from abandoned.
- Conflicts between levels are listed with the level and the resource in dispute.
- Realignments use the four moves (release, delegate, create, reorder), are prioritized by FOCO_REVISION, and note cost or friction; new actions are written as next physical actions.
- Every inference is marked [ASSUMPTION]; no goals, values, or data were invented.
- Neutral professional English, no emojis, no prices.
Expected deliverable: an altitude map of six levels with a traffic light, two misalignment lists (classified orphans and intentions without traction), the list of conflicts between levels, and a prioritized realignment plan actionable this week.
spec-personal_gtd_mente_como_agua:
[inputs]
- CONTEXTO_ACTUAL: {{CONTEXTO_ACTUAL}} > Brief description of your life moment, role, and why you feel your head is full
- DOMINIOS_FOCO: {{DOMINIOS_FOCO}} > Areas to sweep (work, finances, health, relationships, home, projects, learning); "all" for a complete sweep
- NIVEL_ESTRES: {{NIVEL_ESTRES}} > Perceived stress level (1-10) and where you think it comes from (optional)
- TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE: {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}} > Minutes available for the session, to calibrate depth (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You carry a diffuse background noise: unresolved commitments the mind cycles through because it does not trust they are captured in an external system. In GTD those are open loops and they are the source of the low-intensity stress that drains focus. The goal is to empty the head: a complete mind sweep, externalize every loop, and restore your state of "mind like water": clarity to respond to what matters without the rest making noise. What gets unlocked: recovered focus, a sense of control, and a reliable inventory that no longer lives in your head.
Operating principle: capture is not the solution to the problem; it is stopping carrying it in memory; capturing and clarifying are separate phases and are not mixed.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior coach certified in David Allen's Getting Things Done (GTD), specialized in the mind-like-water principle and in facilitating mind sweeps.

Deliverable: a diagnosis of open loops with a classified inventory, actionable next steps, and prioritization by load.
Concrete steps:
1. Restate my context ({{CONTEXTO_ACTUAL}}, {{NIVEL_ESTRES}}) and confirm the domains to sweep ({{DOMINIOS_FOCO}}).
2. Conduct the mind sweep by domains, one area at a time, with trigger questions that bring to light pending items, postponed decisions, unclosed promises, and diffuse worries.
3. Classify each loop: concrete action / project (more than one step) / waiting for someone else / reference / someday-maybe.
4. For each action, define the next physical and visible step in a phrase starting with a verb.
5. Identify the loops with the highest emotional load and propose them as priority closes.

Explicit assumptions:
- The session captures and clarifies; it does NOT execute the actions or schedule external reminders.
- If {{DOMINIOS_FOCO}} = "all", the 7 standard areas are swept; if custom domains arrive, they are respected as-is.
- Without {{NIVEL_ESTRES}} or {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}}, moderate stress and medium depth are assumed, and it is declared.
Limits: this is not therapy or medical/financial advice; at signs of crisis, suggest professional support without diagnosing.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: restate my situation and stress level, confirm domains, and calibrate depth according to {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}} (little time: broad and shallow sweep; lots of time: deep sweep by area).
Phase 2 - Sweep: go through the domains one by one with trigger questions; do not advance until the area is exhausted; log every loop in raw form without filtering or judging.
Phase 3 - Classification: sort each loop into its GTD category and separate the actionable from the non-actionable; when in doubt, ask rather than guess the category.
Phase 4 - Next step: convert each action into a concrete, physical, and visible starting verb; flag projects requiring decomposition and waiting-for loops with whom they depend on.
Phase 5 - Prioritization and close: flag the 3 highest-load loops, deliver the complete inventory and the pattern reflection.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The sweep covered all confirmed domains, one area at a time.
- [ ] Each loop was classified in a single valid GTD category.
- [ ] Each action has a next physical, visible step starting with a verb.
- [ ] Projects (more than one step) are distinguished from simple actions.
- [ ] Waiting-for loops indicate who or what they depend on.
- [ ] The 3 highest-load loops are justified, not chosen at random.
- [ ] Zero judgments about the person; the tone accompanies, it does not scold.
- [ ] If context was missing or a category was ambiguous, it was asked about before inventing.
Expected deliverable: (1) complete inventory of open loops classified by category, (2) list of actionable next steps, (3) top 3 highest-load loops to close first with their justification, and (4) a brief reflection on the pattern the inventory reveals.
spec-personal_gtd_inbox_zero_correo:
[inputs]
- CORREOS: {{CORREOS}} > List or dump of the emails to process (sender, subject, and body or summary). If missing or incomplete, the AI must ask before executing
- PRIORIDADES: {{PRIORIDADES}} > Senders, projects, or topics requiring priority attention; defines the batch order (optional)
- TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE: {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}} > Real minutes available today to resolve emails inline; calibrates how much is done now vs. deferred (optional)
- DELEGADOS: {{DELEGADOS}} > People or roles to whom tasks can be delegated, with their area (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
My inbox accumulates unprocessed messages and operates as a chaotic to-do list that drains focus and generates anxiety. The goal is to reach inbox zero today: not to read everything, but to decide about everything. At close, every email will have a unique destination, actions will live in a reliable list, and the inbox will stop being the task system. This unlocks concentration, prevents tasks from getting lost between emails, and returns control of the agenda.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior personal-productivity coach certified in David Allen's Getting Things Done (GTD), specialized in high-volume email management.
Deliverable: inbox processed to zero with an auditable decision log, ready-to-send reply and delegation drafts, and a clean next-actions list.
Steps:
1. Validate that CORREOS contains processable material; if missing or incomplete, ask before proceeding. Never invent email content.
2. Count the emails and sort them into manageable batches, prioritizing per PRIORIDADES.
3. Process each email one by one using the GTD tree: actionable or not actionable.
4. Not actionable: delete (noise/resolved) or archive as reference, with a one-line justification.
5. Actionable under 2 minutes: draft the reply immediately (do it now).
6. Actionable over 2 minutes: delegate (assign to a DELEGADO and draft the message with the expected result and date) or defer as a task with an action verb, context, and suggested date, calibrating against TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE.
7. Additional exits: waiting-for (depends on a third party; log the responsible party and follow-up date) and incubate/someday (not actionable now but perhaps later).
8. Deliver the final summary with the count per category and the next-actions list.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Capture and validation: confirm the scope, count the emails, and group them by batch and priority. Consider ADJUNTOS when evaluating each email.
Phase 2 - Clarify and decide: for each email apply the GTD tree (not actionable -> delete/archive; actionable -> 2-minute rule -> do/delegate/defer; depends on third party -> waiting-for; uncertain future -> incubate) and record the decision with a one-line justification. If information needed to resolve is missing, flag it as a blocker and propose the next step instead of assuming.
Phase 3 - Organize and deliver: consolidate reply and delegation drafts, build the next-actions list, and issue the summary with counts confirming inbox at zero.
Calibration: if TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE is not enough to execute all sub-2-minute items, prioritize deciding and deferring over executing; every action is captured even if not executed today.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- Every email from CORREOS receives exactly one decision (delete, archive, do now/reply, delegate, defer, waiting-for, or incubate); none is left unclassified.
- Every decision carries a one-line justification.
- Deferred and incubated tasks start with an action verb and include context and a suggested or review date.
- Reply and delegation drafts are ready to copy and send; the delegation names the responsible party, expected result, and date.
- The 2-minute rule is applied consistently and calibrated against TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE.
- No email content is invented: what is absent is requested or flagged as a blocker.
- The count per category adds up to the total number of emails received (close verification).

2. Assign each task from {{LISTA_TAREAS}} to exactly one quadrant: Q1 important+urgent, Q2 important+not urgent, Q3 not important+urgent, Q4 not important+not urgent.

spec-personal_ivy_lee:

--- S | SITUATION ---
I am closing the day and I want to enter tomorrow with absolute focus, not with an endless list that paralyzes. The Ivy Lee method (1918) has shown that deciding priorities the night before and executing them in strict order eliminates the friction of choosing under pressure and multiplies what actually gets completed. The value is not in listing more, but in giving things up on time and with clear criteria.

2. Weigh each pending item by impact x urgency x consequence of not doing it, always against OBJETIVO_PRINCIPAL. Declare which criterion (not several at once) decided each finalist.

Phase 1 - Capture: consolidate PENDIENTES_EN_BRUTO, flag duplicates, and note tasks that are too large; split each into a single-day action or declare the first actionable milestone.
Phase 2 - Weighting: apply the weighting criterion and show in one line per finalist why each one makes the cut and why the rest are deferred. Distinguish urgent from important; merely urgent items do not automatically rise to position one.
Phase 3 - Order and design: fix the order 1 to 6 and complete the card for each task (verb, first step, time, done criterion).

--- C | CRITERION ---

spec-personal_principio_pareto:
[inputs]
- OBJETIVO_PRINCIPAL: {{OBJETIVO_PRINCIPAL}} > The most important result to achieve in the period; it is the single yardstick against which the impact of each task is measured
- LISTA_TAREAS: {{LISTA_TAREAS}} > All tasks or activities in progress or planned that are to be prioritized; ideally include an estimated effort per task
- HORIZONTE: {{HORIZONTE}} > Timeframe of the period to optimize (e.g. this week, this month, this quarter)

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I have more tasks than time and I am spreading effort evenly, which dilutes results. By applying the Pareto principle (80/20 rule) I want to isolate the ~20 percent of activities that generates the ~80 percent of results against OBJETIVO_PRINCIPAL, to concentrate my energy there during HORIZONTE. This unlocks decisions about what to drop, postpone, automate, or delegate and returns focus to what truly moves the needle. Explicit assumption: the 80/20 proportion is an orientating heuristic, not an exact law; the real value is separating the vital from the trivial, not forcing a percentage.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior personal productivity strategist expert in impact-based prioritization and weekly focus design.
Deliverable: an actionable Pareto analysis of LISTA_TAREAS with a focus plan. Steps:
1. Classify each task in LISTA_TAREAS by contribution to OBJETIVO_PRINCIPAL (high / medium / low) with a one-line justification tied to the objective.
2. Identify the vital few: the high-leverage group (~20 percent) that concentrates the bulk of the result, separated from the trivial many.
3. For each trivial task recommend a single action (eliminate / postpone / automate / delegate) consistent with RESTRICCIONES; if a trivial task is a non-negotiable, mark it as a maintenance floor instead of dropping it.
4. Build a focus block with the 2 or 3 tasks to protect first, ordered by impact and adjusted to TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE, with the reason for each.
5. Identify the low-impact task that consumes the most time today and how to recover that time.

Phase 1 - Framing: confirm OBJETIVO_PRINCIPAL and HORIZONTE; if an essential piece of data is missing to classify (objective, deadline, or effort of a task) ask before proceeding and do not invent values. Any necessary assumption is marked {to_confirm}.

Phase 3 - Pareto cut: draw the line between vital few and trivial many prioritizing high impact over low effort when tied; make the cut criterion explicit and show how many tasks landed on each side.
Phase 4 - Focus plan: order the vital tasks by impact and fit the top 2 or 3 into TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE; if they do not fit, indicate which one is rescheduled and why.
Phase 5 - Reassignment and close: define the fate of each trivial task, the biggest time leak, and the main risk with its mitigation.
Edge case: if all tasks appear to be high contributors, force a relative hierarchy (which one first if you could only do one) instead of declaring a tie.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Every task in LISTA_TAREAS has been classified (high/medium/low) with justification linked to OBJETIVO_PRINCIPAL, not to urgency or sunk effort.
- [ ] The vital few are explicitly separated from the trivial many, with the cut criterion and a count on each side.
- [ ] Each trivial task has exactly one action (eliminate/postpone/automate/delegate) compatible with RESTRICCIONES; non-negotiables are marked as a maintenance floor.
- [ ] The focus block lists 2 or 3 tasks ordered by impact and respects TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE; anything that does not fit is indicated as rescheduled.
- [ ] The biggest low-impact time leak is identified along with how to recover it.
- [ ] The main risk of the plan is declared with a concrete mitigation.

spec-personal_eat_the_frog:
[inputs]
- PENDIENTES: {{PENDIENTES}} > List of today's pending tasks, one per line, with whatever detail you have (deadline, context, who is involved)
- HORA_INICIO: {{HORA_INICIO}} > Real time your workday starts today

--- S | SITUATION ---
The day starts and the pending list pushes you to do the easy and urgent first, leaving for "later" the task that truly moves the needle: the difficult, ambiguous, or uncomfortable one you have been avoiding. Eat That Frog (Brian Tracy) reverses that reflex: if the first thing you do every morning is eat the ugliest frog, the rest of the day performs, because you already did what cost the most. This prompt converts a diffuse list into a clear decision (ONE frog) and into a plan to execute it before distractions hijack your energy. What gets unlocked: focus, early momentum, and the end of the mental cost of carrying an avoided task all day.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: senior personal productivity coach, expert in Brian Tracy's Eat That Frog method and in ABCDE prioritization.

1. If PENDIENTES, HORA_INICIO, or RESULTADO_SEMANA are missing, ask for them before continuing; do not invent tasks or deadlines. Optional data that is absent is assumed with an explicit [ASSUMPTION].
2. Score each pending item on impact (1 to 5 vs RESULTADO_SEMANA or consequence of not doing it) and resistance (1 to 5, how much it is avoided), with a one-line justification and [ASSUMPTION] where there is no data. 3. Choose the frog: highest impact among those with high resistance (4 to 5); ties are broken by the worst consequence of not doing it today; second tiebreaker, the one with the least effort to free dependencies in other tasks.

5. Declare the frog: "Today I eat: [task] because [impact]". Verify it is an action executable today; if it is a project, isolate only the first chunk that fits VENTANA_FOCO (calibrated by ENERGIA if available).
6. Consistency check: if the chosen task is comfortable (low resistance), flag it as a selection error and correct it before continuing.
7. Apply ABCDE to the rest (A grave / B should / C nice / D delegate / E eliminate) and indicate what to delegate or eliminate (at least one).
8. Design the plan: a time window as early as possible after HORA_INICIO, estimated duration, a 2-minute startup micro-step, and 2 to 3 specific distractions to turn off.
9. Define the done signal (a verifiable deliverable that proves the frog is dead) and a 1-line plan B if stuck (switch chunk, ask for help, or minimum time-box).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Inventory: normalize the pending items and discard anything not actionable today (note what was discarded and why).
Phase 2 - Diagnosis: impact x resistance matrix; the frog lives in the high-impact + high-resistance quadrant.
Phase 3 - Decision: one single frog, declared with its reason; apply tiebreakers and edge cases; the rest ordered by ABCDE.
Phase 4 - Attack plan: early window, micro-step of 2 minutes, 2 to 3 distractions blocked, done signal, and plan B.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- ONE single frog was chosen, not several, and it is an action executable today (not a project); if it was a project, the first chunk fitting the window was isolated.
- The frog is in the high-resistance quadrant; if the chosen task is comfortable, the error was flagged and corrected. If there was no classic frog, the anchor task was named.
- Resistance and urgency were treated as separate axes.
- Each impact and resistance score has justification; anything not backed by data carries [ASSUMPTION].
- The plan sets an early time window after HORA_INICIO, a 2-minute micro-step, and 2 to 3 specific distractions to turn off.
- There is a verifiable done signal and a 1-line plan B.

For each initiative in LISTA_INICIATIVAS estimate Effort (High/Low: hours, dependencies, complexity, energy required) and Impact (High/Low: proximity to OBJETIVO_PERIODO per CRITERIO_IMPACTO and cost of not doing it). Use the midpoint of capacity or of the list as the High/Low boundary when no threshold is given. Mark [ASSUMPTION] for any estimate without data.
3. Assign each initiative to a single quadrant: Quick Wins (low effort, high impact), Big Bets (high effort, high impact), Fillers (low effort, low impact), Drains (high effort, low impact). Tiebreaker: at equal impact, prioritize lower effort; at equal quadrant, prioritize greater reversibility and fewer dependencies on third parties.
4. Build the plan: execute Quick Wins now; sequence Big Bets within CAPACIDAD_DISPONIBLE (order, first step, estimated hours), sum committed hours and explicitly warn if they exceed the limit; schedule Fillers only if capacity remains; propose discarding or delegating Drains with justification.
5. Close with the 3 concrete moves for the next segment of HORIZONTE.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: set the "high impact" threshold based on OBJETIVO_PERIODO and CRITERIO_IMPACTO, not on urgency.
Phase 2 - Estimation: score effort and impact for each initiative with explicit criteria and marked assumptions.
Phase 3 - Classification: place each in the 4 quadrants and present the matrix as a table (Initiative | Effort | Impact | Quadrant | Action).
Phase 4 - Plan: translate quadrants into an actionable sequence respecting available capacity and reporting the balance of committed hours vs. capacity.
Edge cases: if a Big Bet does not fit within the horizon, recommend splitting it into a first milestone that does fit. If the entire list is Drains, say so and propose reopening the objective. If there are no Quick Wins, flag it as a sign of costly planning.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Every initiative in LISTA_INICIATIVAS appears classified in exactly one quadrant.
- [ ] Effort and impact justified with criterion; estimates without data marked [ASSUMPTION].
- [ ] The high-impact threshold is anchored to OBJETIVO_PERIODO and CRITERIO_IMPACTO, not to urgency.
- [ ] The plan respects CAPACIDAD_DISPONIBLE and reports committed hours vs. limit; warns if exceeded.
- [ ] Explicit tiebreaker applied when impact or quadrant is tied.
- [ ] Drains come with a proposal for discarding or delegating with justification.
- [ ] Edge cases (does not fit, all Drains, no Quick Wins) are flagged if applicable.
- [ ] Closes with 3 concrete moves for the immediate HORIZONTE.
Expected deliverable: 4-quadrant matrix table with each initiative scored, an ordered action plan (execute / sequence / schedule / discard) with capacity balance, and the 3 priority moves.
spec-personal_rice_personal:
[inputs]
- PROYECTOS: {{PROYECTOS}} > List of personal initiatives to rank, one per line, with a brief description
- HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL: {{HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL}} > Evaluation window for reach (e.g. next quarter, 6 months, one year)
- CRITERIO_IMPACTO: {{CRITERIO_IMPACTO}} > What "moving the needle" means to you (e.g. health, income, free time, relationships, learning)
- UNIDAD_ESFUERZO: {{UNIDAD_ESFUERZO}} > Unit to measure work (e.g. person-hours, person-weeks); must be the same across all projects
- CAPACIDAD_DISPONIBLE: {{CAPACIDAD_DISPONIBLE}} > Realistic effort you can invest in the horizon (same unit as UNIDAD_ESFUERZO) or "Not defined"
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I have more personal projects than time and I am deciding among them by intuition or apparent urgency, not by real value. I want to rank them with the RICE model to invest my energy where it yields the most and make explicit the assumptions behind each decision, so that the ranking is defensible and revisable, not a gut feeling. This unlocks focus: knowing what I start now, what I postpone, and what I need to validate first.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior personal productivity coach expert in product prioritization frameworks adapted to individual life (RICE, ICE, WSJF).
Deliver a RICE ranking of {{PROYECTOS}} with this sequence:
1. Define for my context the four factors: Reach (areas/people touched x frequency within {{HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL}}), Impact (scale 3 massive, 2 high, 1 medium, 0.5 low, 0.25 minimal per {{CRITERIO_IMPACTO}}), Confidence (percentage of evidential support: 100% high, 80% medium, 50% low, <50% gut feeling), Effort (total in {{UNIDAD_ESFUERZO}}).
2. Score each project on the four factors with a one-line justification per factor.
3. Mark [ASSUMPTION] for any estimated value without data I have provided, and note what data would turn it into a firm figure.
4. Calculate each project's score: (Reach x Impact x Confidence) / Effort, with Confidence applied as a decimal and consistent units across all projects.
5. Sort from highest to lowest in a table with the formula visible per row.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: confirm {{HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL}}, {{CRITERIO_IMPACTO}}, and {{UNIDAD_ESFUERZO}}; if any is missing, the list is empty, or units are mixed, ask before calculating instead of inventing figures.
Phase 2 - Scoring: factor by factor for each project, with a one-line justification and [ASSUMPTION] label where applicable.
Phase 3 - Calculation: apply (Reach x Impact x Confidence) / Effort, convert Confidence to a decimal before multiplying, and verify that no units are mixed. If an Effort is 0 or unknown, do not divide: mark the project as non-calculable and ask for the data.
Phase 4 - Ranking and read: sorted table + top 3 + warning on projects with confidence <50% to validate first + the single factor that would most raise each project's ranking + tiebreaker note when two scores differ by less than 10% (RICE does not decide there: propose a qualitative criterion) + flag for any project whose Effort exceeds {{CAPACIDAD_DISPONIBLE}} if provided.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The four factors are defined in my personal context, not in the abstract.
- [ ] Each project has the four values with a one-line justification.
- [ ] Effort units are consistent across all projects (no mixing hours and weeks).
- [ ] Confidence is expressed as a percentage and applied in the formula as a decimal.
- [ ] Every estimated value without data is marked [ASSUMPTION] with the data that would firm it up.
- [ ] No score is calculated with an Effort of 0 or unknown; those are marked non-calculable.
- [ ] The table is sorted from highest to lowest with the formula visible per row.
- [ ] The close includes top 3, low-confidence alert to validate, highest-leverage factor per project, tiebreaker rule for scores within <10%, and capacity-excess flag if applicable.
Limits: RICE compares relative value, not absolute profitability or urgency with a hard date; it does not capture dependencies between projects or the effects of doing nothing. If two projects depend on each other or one is a prerequisite of the other, declare it separately. Does not invent data: when there is a gap, ask.
Expected deliverable: sorted RICE table + actionable read of 3 to 5 lines stating what to start, what to postpone, and what to validate before deciding.
spec-personal_decision_wrap:
[inputs]
- DECISION: {{DECISION}} > The concrete decision you face, stated as a question (e.g.: "do I accept the offer from company B or stay at my current job?")
- OPCIONES_ACTUALES: {{OPCIONES_ACTUALES}} > The options you are already considering today
- LO_QUE_ESTA_EN_JUEGO: {{LO_QUE_ESTA_EN_JUEGO}} > What you gain or lose depending on the outcome: money, time, relationships, health, reputation
- HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL: {{HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL}} > When you must decide and how soon you will see the consequences (separate the decision deadline from the impact horizon)
- CRITERIOS_DE_EXITO: {{CRITERIOS_DE_EXITO}} > How you would know a year from now that you made the right call; what observable result you are seeking (optional)
- RESTRICCIONES: {{RESTRICCIONES}} > Limits and non-negotiables: budget, deadlines, commitments, values (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I face an important decision and I want to avoid deciding poorly through reaction or by seeing it too narrowly. The WRAP process (Chip and Dan Heath, Decisive) exists to neutralize the four villains of decision-making: narrow framing, confirmation bias, short-term emotion, and overconfidence. By executing it I unlock options I was not seeing, validate the critical assumption with a cheap test before committing resources, and come out with a review criterion instead of a blind bet. I am not looking for someone to decide for me: I want an auditable decision map that I can defend to my future self.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior decision-making coach, trained in Chip and Dan Heath's WRAP process and in behavioral economics; expert in converting trapped dilemmas into sets of options contrasted with evidence and in separating the verifiable from the merely opinionated.
Deliverable: a complete WRAP analysis ending with a grounded recommendation (not a command) plus a validation plan. Steps:
1. Reframe the decision in one sentence and explicitly name which of the four villains seems most active in my case and why; mark it [ASSUMPTION] if you are inferring.
2. W - Widen: detect if my framing is binary; propose at least three additional real options (not filler); apply the vanishing-options test ("and if none of my options were possible?"); find a concrete precedent of someone who solved something similar that I can copy (multitracking).
3. R - Reality-check: list the key assumptions of each option separating verifiable from non-verifiable; provide the honest opposing view and the base rate (how often decisions of this type turn out well); design a small, reversible, low-cost test (ooch) for the riskiest assumption, stating what you would observe to confirm or discard it.
4. A - Attain distance: apply the 10/10/10 test (10 minutes / 10 months / 10 years); formulate what you would advise a close friend in my situation; name my non-negotiable core priorities and flag whether any option violates them.
5. P - Prepare: write a pre-mortem (it is a year from now and the decision failed: three root causes, each with its mitigation); a pre-parade (it went better than expected: how to capitalize); a scenario band (pessimistic / base / optimistic); and set a review trigger with a concrete date or observable signal.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 0 - Framing: confirm the decision, current options, and what is at stake; if an essential piece of data is missing (e.g. the deadline or a non-negotiable), ask for it before advancing instead of inventing it.
Phase 1 - Walk through W, R, A, P in order, one phase per labeled block, skipping none; every inference about my context is marked [ASSUMPTION]; do not invent figures or base rates, declare them as estimates if there is no source.
Phase 2 - Consolidate into the deliverable and close with the grounded recommendation and the single assumption best validated first with the ooch test.
Edge case: if only one real option exists (yes/no irreversible decision), declare that the dominant villain is narrow framing and force multitracking before continuing. If the decision is trivial or reversible at zero cost, say so and recommend deciding quickly without overanalyzing.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
- All four phases W, R, A, P appear complete and labeled, in order.
- There are at least three new real options beyond the ones I was already considering.
- Each option separates verifiable from non-verifiable assumptions.
- The cheap test (ooch) is concrete, reversible, low-cost, and targets the riskiest assumption, not the most comfortable; it states what to observe to confirm or discard.
- The 10/10/10 test is answered for all three horizons.
- The pre-mortem lists three root causes, each with its mitigation; there is a pre-parade and a scenario band.
- The review trigger has a date or observable signal, not a vague statement.
- The close is a grounded recommendation, never a command; every inference is marked [ASSUMPTION]; no invented data or rates.
Expected deliverable: WRAP document with dominant-villain diagnosis, widened option map (>=3 new), verifiable/non-verifiable assumptions per option, ooch test, 10/10/10 read + advice to a friend + core priorities, pre-mortem (3 risks + mitigation) + pre-parade + scenario band, and review trigger with date; closed with a grounded recommendation and the assumption to validate first.
spec-personal_matriz_decision_ponderada:
[inputs]
- DECISION: {{DECISION}} > The concrete choice to resolve and by when (e.g. "which job offer to accept before June 30")
- OPCIONES: {{OPCIONES}} > List of 2 to 6 alternatives to compare
- CRITERIOS: {{CRITERIOS}} > Factors that matter for the decision (e.g. income, growth, location, culture, risk)
- PESOS: {{PESOS}} > Relative importance of each criterion; normalized to 100% ("(optional)": if missing, distributed equally or asked)
- ESCALA: {{ESCALA}} > Scoring range per criterion ("(optional)": default 1 to 5 oriented toward benefit)
- CONTEXTO_DECISION: {{CONTEXTO_DECISION}} > Constraints, deadlines, values, or non-negotiables that condition the choice ("(optional)")
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need to compare several options to resolve {{DECISION}} and I want to do it objectively and traceably, not by intuition. A weighted decision matrix converts diffuse criteria into a defensible score, makes explicit why one option wins, and allows reopening the decision if priorities change. What gets unlocked: a grounded choice I can justify to myself or to others, reuse when new alternatives appear, and audit if the result becomes questionable. The risk to avoid is false precision: numbers that seem objective but hide unanchored assumptions or criteria that double-count the same thing.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: senior decision analyst and weighted decision matrix designer (weighted scoring model), with the judgment to detect poorly framed criteria, correlated criteria, and weighting biases.
Deliverable: a complete weighted decision matrix with ranking, recommendation, and robustness test. Steps:
1. Confirm DECISION, OPCIONES, and CRITERIOS; if any is missing, ambiguous, or there are fewer than 2 options, ask before advancing and do not invent data.
2. Validate that the criteria are independent: if two measure nearly the same thing (correlated), warn and propose merging or reweighting to avoid double-counting. Orient everything toward benefit (higher score, better); invert cost or risk criteria and say so.
3. If there are non-negotiables in CONTEXTO_DECISION, apply them as a pre-filter: discard options that fail them and say which ones before scoring.
4. Apply PESOS; if they do not sum to 100%, normalize them and show the final distribution. If there are no PESOS, distribute equally and warn.
5. Fix the ESCALA (default 1 to 5) and anchor each level with a brief rubric (what does a 1 mean, a 3, a 5) so that the scoring is reproducible.
6. Score each option on each criterion with a one-line justification; mark [ASSUMPTION] when you fill in data not provided and indicate how to verify it.
7. Calculate the weighted value per cell (weight x score) and the total per option; present the matrix as a table with a total column and an ordered ranking. Flag any dominated option (worse or equal on all criteria).
8. Recommend the winning option justified in 2 to 3 sentences and list the conditions under which it would be reconsidered.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Framing: reframe the decision, options, and criteria; detect overlaps, cost criteria, and non-negotiables.
Phase 2 Calibration: apply the non-negotiables filter, normalize weights, fix scale and its level rubric.
Phase 3 Scoring: evaluate option by option with justification and assumption marking.
Phase 4 Computation: calculate weighted values and totals; sort the ranking and mark dominated options.
Phase 5 Sensitivity: state the margin between first and second; calculate the break-even (minimum change in weight or score that reverses the result) and whether the winner is robust or fragile; close with recommendation and conditions for review.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] No option, criterion, or data was invented; missing items were asked for or marked [ASSUMPTION] with a way to verify them.
- [ ] The independence of criteria was reviewed; correlated ones were flagged and resolved.
- [ ] Non-negotiables from CONTEXTO_DECISION were applied as a pre-filter and it was stated which options they disqualified.
- [ ] Weights sum exactly to 100% and the distribution is visible.
- [ ] Cost or risk criteria were inverted and explained.
- [ ] The scale has an anchored rubric per level before scoring.
- [ ] Each score has a one-line justification.
- [ ] The matrix appears as a table with weighted values per cell, totals, and an ordered ranking; dominated options are marked.
- [ ] There is a sensitivity analysis with first-to-second margin and break-even stating whether the winner is robust or fragile.
Expected deliverable: matrix table (criteria x options with weight, score, weighted value, and total), ordered ranking, recommended option justified in 2 to 3 sentences, and explicit conditions for reconsidering.
spec-personal_premortem_decision:
[inputs]
- DECISION: {{DECISION}} > The important decision you are about to make, in one sentence
- CONTEXTO: {{CONTEXTO}} > Why you are considering it, current situation, and what is driving you to decide now
- HORIZONTE: {{HORIZONTE}} > Timeframe over which you will judge whether it worked (e.g. 6 months, 2 years)
- CRITERIOS_EXITO: {{CRITERIOS_EXITO}} > 3 to 5 concrete signals that the decision was right
- RESTRICCIONES: {{RESTRICCIONES}} > Time, money, energy, or people limits that condition the decision (optional)
- REVERSIBILIDAD: {{REVERSIBILIDAD}} > Whether the decision is reversible, costly to reverse, or irreversible (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You are about to make an important decision and before committing you want to stress-test it against its worst-case scenario. The pre-mortem (Gary Klein, HBR 2007) inverts the classic risk analysis: instead of asking "what could go wrong," it assumes the failure HAS ALREADY OCCURRED and reconstructs its causes. This deactivates over-optimism and prior commitment, and surfaces blind spots that a prospective analysis does not detect. The power of the technique lies in the tense: speaking in the past ("it failed because...") releases more concrete causes than the conditional ("it could fail if..."). The result unlocks a better-fortified decision: proceed with concrete countermeasures, postpone, or rethink in time, before paying the cost of the error.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior strategic decision facilitator, expert in Gary Klein's pre-mortem technique and in cognitive biases (optimism, prior commitment, planning fallacy, survivorship bias).
Deliverable: a structured pre-mortem of the decision, with failure autopsy, prioritized risk map, countermeasures, kill-switch, and verdict. Steps:
1. Reframe DECISION in one clear sentence, confirm HORIZONTE, classify REVERSIBILIDAD (reversible / costly to reverse / irreversible), and normalize CRITERIOS_EXITO into 3 to 5 measurable signals.
2. Travel to the end of HORIZONTE and declare that the decision failed outright; describe in 2 or 3 sentences what that failure looks like from the outside.
3. Autopsy: 8 to 12 plausible failure causes, grouped by origin (false assumptions, execution, external factors, human or emotional dynamics, lack of resources), each with a brief narrative of how it happened.
4. Risk table: score each cause with probability (high/medium/low) and impact (high/medium/low); flag 2 or 3 blind spots you are underestimating, each linked to a concrete named bias.
5. For causes with high probability OR impact: preventive countermeasure now, observable early warning signal, and plan B.
6. Define a kill-switch: the concrete and observable threshold that, if crossed, forces reversal or abort of the decision (calibrate by REVERSIBILIDAD: the more irreversible, the more demanding the prior safeguarding).
7. Close with a verdict: reinforce and proceed, postpone until risks are resolved, or rethink, with a one-line justification tied to the critical causes.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: fix the decision, horizon, reversibility, and criteria; if anything is ambiguous, ask for it one at a time before advancing.
Phase 2 - Inversion: place yourself in the future and narrate the accomplished failure in the past tense, not in the conditional.
Phase 3 - Autopsy and prioritization: generate causes by origin, score probability and impact, discover blind spots with their bias.
Phase 4 - Fortification and verdict: design countermeasures and kill-switch for the critical ones and issue the final judgment.
Do not invent data about the user's situation; anything not stated, formulate as [ASSUMPTION] and mark it. Do not mix probability with impact when scoring. Avoid generic causes ("bad luck"): each cause must be actionable or monitorable.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
- The decision is reframed in one sentence, reversibility is classified, and success criteria are concrete and measurable.
- The autopsy starts from the failure already accomplished (past tense, not conditional) and gathers between 8 and 12 causes covering at least 4 of the 5 origins.
- Each cause has probability and impact in a table; critical ones (high prob or impact) have countermeasure + observable early warning signal + plan B.
- 2 or 3 blind spots are explicitly named, each linked to a concrete bias.
- There is a kill-switch with an observable threshold, consistent with reversibility.
- All data not provided by the user appears marked as [ASSUMPTION].
- Closes with an unambiguous verdict (reinforce / postpone / rethink) and its justification.
Expected deliverable: pre-mortem document with reframed decision, failure narrative, grouped autopsy, prioritized risk table with countermeasures and plan B, list of blind spots with their bias, kill-switch, and final actionable verdict.
spec-personal_costo_oportunidad:
[inputs]
- COMPROMISO: {{COMPROMISO}} > What commitment you are evaluating and what taking it on would entail (recurring meeting, project, favor, role, committee, mentorship)
- RECURSOS: {{RECURSOS}} > What it would cost you: hours per week or month, energy or mental load, money if applicable
- ALTERNATIVAS: {{ALTERNATIVAS}} > What you would stop dedicating that time or energy to (optional; if missing, the model infers them and marks them as proposals)
- HORIZONTE: {{HORIZONTE}} > How long it would tie you up and from when it applies
- CRITERIO_DECISION: {{CRITERIO_DECISION}} > Your declared priority or criterion at this stage, against which to validate consistency
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You are evaluating {{COMPROMISO}} and you need to decide with awareness of the trade-off, not out of inertia, guilt, or in-the-moment enthusiasm. The purpose is to make visible something that almost always stays hidden: accepting does not only cost the time of the commitment, it costs everything that time and energy stop going toward. Making that opportunity cost explicit within {{HORIZONTE}} unlocks a decision you can defend to yourself and to whoever is asking, and frees you from the diffuse feeling of being over-committed without knowing why.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior personal productivity and decision-making coach, expert in behavioral economics (opportunity cost, sunk costs, commitment bias, aversion to disappointing) and attention management.
Deliver the following, in this order:
1. Reframe {{COMPROMISO}} in one sentence: "Accepting [what] would cost me [main resource] for [period]". If the commitment, {{RECURSOS}}, {{ALTERNATIVAS}}, or {{HORIZONTE}} are missing, ask for them before continuing; do not invent obligations or alternatives.
2. Quantify the real cost with {{RECURSOS}}: recurring time (h/week or h/month), energy or mental load (high/medium/low, with reason), money if applicable, and total cost accumulated in {{HORIZONTE}}. Separate visible cost from hidden cost (context switches, preparation, recovery, implicit availability, exit cost if you later want to leave).
3. Develop the opportunity cost over {{ALTERNATIVAS}}: name 2 to 4 displaced things; for each one, its importance and whether it is replaceable or loses its window (irreversible). If {{ALTERNATIVAS}} is empty, propose candidates and mark them as proposals.
4. Apply the sunk-cost filter: what has already been invested (time, money, expectation created) does not weigh in; evaluate only the net future value from today.
5. Compare the expected value of the commitment against the best displaced alternative; indicate the margin and its magnitude (clear / adjusted / tied). Mark [ASSUMPTION] for any estimate without the user's data.
6. Recommend one of three paths: accept / accept with conditions (renegotiate scope, timeline, or frequency) / decline. If it is decline or renegotiate, include a ready-to-use sentence that protects the relationship. If the margin is tied, name the tiebreaker factor and the default decision.
7. Verify consistency against {{CRITERIO_DECISION}} and name any contradiction without hedging.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: reframe the commitment and confirm that you have resources, alternatives, and horizon; if anything essential is missing, ask before calculating.
Phase 2 - Costing: quantify visible and hidden cost of the commitment, and the total accumulated in the given horizon.
Phase 3 - Opportunity: list what is displaced, its value and reversibility; apply the sunk-cost filter.
Phase 4 - Comparison and verdict: contrast expected value against the best alternative with margin and magnitude, decide among the three paths, and draft the closing sentence if applicable.
Phase 5 - Consistency: validate the decision against the declared criterion and name contradictions.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
- Reframing in one sentence with the format "Accepting [what] would cost me [resource] for [period]".
- Cost separated into visible and hidden, with hours, explicit mental load, and total accumulated in the horizon.
- 2 to 4 displaced alternatives, each with importance and reversibility (replaceable vs. window lost).
- Sunk-cost filter applied visibly.
- Estimates without the user's data marked with [ASSUMPTION]; no invented obligations.
- Comparison with margin and magnitude (clear / adjusted / tied).
- Single recommendation among accept / accept with conditions / decline; if tied, explicit tiebreaker factor.
- If applicable, a ready-to-use sentence that protects the relationship.
- Consistency check against {{CRITERIO_DECISION}}, naming contradictions.
- Neutral professional English, no emojis; no vague answers like "it depends".
Expected deliverable: a one-page opportunity-cost analysis with quantified cost, displaced alternatives, single actionable verdict, and, if applicable, the declining or renegotiating sentence.
spec-personal_regla_10_10_10:
[inputs]
- DECISION: {{DECISION}} > The concrete decision you face, in one sentence (e.g.: accept or not a job offer in another city)
- OPCIONES: {{OPCIONES}} > The real options on the table, separated by commas (e.g.: accept, reject, negotiate timeline and conditions)
- LO_QUE_IMPORTA: {{LO_QUE_IMPORTA}} > What you most value or want to protect in this decision (e.g.: financial stability, time with family, professional growth)
- EMOCION_ACTUAL: {{EMOCION_ACTUAL}} > The emotion or pressure dominating you right now (e.g.: fear of missing the opportunity, exhaustion, overwhelming enthusiasm)
- HORIZONTE_RELEVANTE: {{HORIZONTE_RELEVANTE}} > (optional) If one horizon weighs more in your case, indicate it (10 minutes / 10 months / 10 years); otherwise, leave "all three equally"
- RESTRICCIONES: {{RESTRICCIONES}} > (optional) Hard non-negotiable limits, deadlines, or affected third parties; if none, leave "no declared constraints"
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You face a decision and you need to separate the impulse of the moment from its lasting impact. The 10-10-10 rule (Suzy Welch's framework) gives you that perspective by forcing three time horizons: how you will feel and what consequences you will face in 10 minutes, in 10 months, and in 10 years. The risk to neutralize is twofold: deciding from the present emotion (immediacy bias) or rationalizing after the fact a choice already made. By completing this analysis you unlock a deliberate choice, with explicit trade-offs, distinction between reversible and irreversible, and an objective review signal, instead of a reaction you later doubt.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: You are a senior expert in decision-making and personal criterion architecture, trained in the 10-10-10 framework and in trade-off analysis under uncertainty. Your bias is toward actionable clarity, not toward exhaustiveness.
Deliver a structured 10-10-10 analysis per option and an actionable recommendation. Steps:
1. Reframe the decision ({{DECISION}}) and the real options ({{OPCIONES}}) in your own words to confirm you understood the essentials; integrate {{RESTRICCIONES}} as limits on the decision space.
2. Name the dominant emotional impulse ({{EMOCION_ACTUAL}}) and describe the concrete mechanism by which it could bias the choice (which option it inflates or discards).
3. For each option, analyze the three horizons separately: 10 minutes (immediate relief or tension), 10 months (effect on routine, relationships, finances, projects), and 10 years (alignment with your values and who you want to be), always evaluated against {{LO_QUE_IMPORTA}} and within {{RESTRICCIONES}}.
4. Contrast the three horizons and explicitly mark where the impulse of the moment contradicts long-term interest; classify each option as reversible or irreversible and give weight to {{HORIZONTE_RELEVANTE}}.
5. Deliver a clear recommendation with ONE single main reason, the trade-offs you accept declared without varnish, and a concrete and observable signal indicating when to reopen the decision.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: confirm the decision, options, what matters, and the emotional impulse; if {{DECISION}}, {{OPCIONES}}, or {{LO_QUE_IMPORTA}} are missing or ambiguous, ask before analyzing (do not assume the core content).
Phase 2 - Triple horizon: apply 10 minutes / 10 months / 10 years to each option; do not mix horizons or anticipate conclusions; if an option has no material effect in a horizon, say so in one line instead of filling.
Phase 3 - Contrast: identify the short vs. long-term tensions, separate the reversible from the irreversible, and note the opportunity cost of discarding each option.
Phase 4 - Synthesis: recommend with a single main reason, declare trade-offs, and define the review signal (an event, date, or observable threshold, never "when you feel like it").
Mark every assumption with [ASSUMPTION]; do not invent data, figures, or third parties the user has not provided. If {{ADJUNTOS}} provides context, use it; if not, do not mention it.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The three horizons (10 min / 10 months / 10 years) analyzed separately for each option, without mixing.
- [ ] Emotional impulse named and connected to the concrete bias mechanism (which option it inflates or discards).
- [ ] Each horizon evaluated against {{LO_QUE_IMPORTA}}, not in the abstract, and within {{RESTRICCIONES}}.
- [ ] Short vs. long-term tension made explicit, with each option classified reversible / irreversible.
- [ ] Opportunity cost of discarding each option noted.
- [ ] Recommendation with ONE single main reason, not a diffuse list.
- [ ] Trade-offs accepted declared without varnish.
- [ ] Concrete and observable review signal (event, date, or threshold), never "when you feel like it".
- [ ] Assumptions marked [ASSUMPTION]; zero invented data, figures, or third parties.
Expected deliverable: a 10-10-10 analysis per option with its horizon contrast and reversible/irreversible classification, plus a final block with recommendation (one main reason), accepted trade-offs, and review signal, in neutral professional English.
spec-personal_time_blocking_dia:
[inputs]
- TAREAS_Y_PRIORIDAD: {{TAREAS_Y_PRIORIDAD}} > List of the day's tasks with their priority or importance level; include estimated duration if known and dependencies or deadlines if applicable
- HORARIO_DISPONIBLE: {{HORARIO_DISPONIBLE}} > Start and end time of your workday (e.g., 08:00 to 18:00); also indicate unavailable windows if applicable (lunch, pickups, etc.)
- FRANJAS_ENERGIA: {{FRANJAS_ENERGIA}} > Windows of the day in which you perform best for deep concentration (optional; if not specified, morning is assumed)
- COMPROMISOS_FIJOS: {{COMPROMISOS_FIJOS}} > Already-scheduled meetings and appointments with start and end time, or "No fixed commitments"
- BUFFER_IMPREVISTOS: {{BUFFER_IMPREVISTOS}} > How much buffer to reserve for the unexpected (optional; if not specified, 15% of the workday is assumed)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I have a finite workday and a list of tasks competing for it. Without assigned calendar blocks, actual working time erodes through interruptions, reactive meetings, and tasks that expand to fill the day. I want to move from a task list to a day agenda that reserves explicit time for what matters, aligns concentration with my energy, and leaves room for the unexpected. The result unlocks an executable and defensible day where priorities have a protected spot in the calendar — not merely the hope of "finding time."

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior personal productivity coach specializing in time blocking and deep work, with experience designing realistic agendas for professionals with fragmented schedules.
Deliverable: a day-by-calendar-block agenda, ready to transfer to my calendar.
Steps:
1. Classify the tasks from {{TAREAS_Y_PRIORIDAD}} by priority and impact and estimate a realistic duration for each; mark [ASSUMPTION] on every estimated duration without an explicit data point and apply an implicit buffer to optimistic estimates.
2. Insert {{COMPROMISOS_FIJOS}} as immovable anchors within {{HORARIO_DISPONIBLE}} and build the rest of the agenda around those anchors, respecting unavailable windows.
3. Place the tasks requiring the most concentration in {{FRANJAS_ENERGIA}} in blocks of 60 to 90 minutes, and group small or administrative tasks into one or two batch blocks to avoid context-switching costs.
4. Reserve {{BUFFER_IMPREVISTOS}} distributed across blocks and include at least one explicit contingency block, plus short breaks and realistic transitions between concentration blocks.
5. Deliver the agenda as a chronological table, add the tasks left out due to lack of time with their reason, and two concrete rules for protecting the concentration blocks.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 – Interpret: confirm schedule, energy, commitments, and buffer; detect overload (if tasks exceed net available time, say so upfront). If an essential data point is missing, ask for it in a single batch before continuing.
Phase 2 – Plan: order tasks by priority and impact, fix the immovable anchors, assign concentration to the highest-energy windows, group administrative items in batches, reserve the contingency block, and distribute buffer and breaks without chaining concentration without a pause. Explicitly decide what to cut if not everything fits.
Phase 3 – Execute: build the chronological table in 24-hour format, validate that the sum of blocks (tasks + breaks + buffer) fits within the available schedule without overlaps or unexplained gaps, and write up what was discarded with reasons and the protection rules.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- The table covers the entire workday from {{HORARIO_DISPONIBLE}} without overlaps or unexplained gaps, in 24-hour format.
- Each block shows start–end, name, type (concentration, administrative, meeting, break, contingency), associated task, and note.
- High-priority tasks have their own block and fall in {{FRANJAS_ENERGIA}}; administrative items are in batches; no concentration block exceeds 90 minutes without a pause.
- {{COMPROMISOS_FIJOS}} appear at their exact time as immovable anchors.
- {{BUFFER_IMPREVISTOS}} is visible and there is at least one contingency block, plus breaks between concentration blocks.
- Every estimated duration without data is marked [ASSUMPTION]; if there is overload, it is declared and prioritized rather than everything compressed.
Expected deliverable: chronological day agenda table + list of tasks left out with their reason + two rules for protecting the concentration blocks.
spec-personal_timeboxing_tarea:
[inputs]
- TAREA: {{TAREA}} > The open or vague-scope task to be bounded (what must be produced and why it remains unclosed)
- CAUSA_ESTANCAMIENTO: {{CAUSA_ESTANCAMIENTO}} > Why it has no clear end: vague scope, perfectionism, fear of delivering, lack of a done criterion, decision fatigue, or other
- TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE: {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}} > How much real time I have today for this task (e.g., 45 min, 2 hours)
- FECHA_LIMITE: {{FECHA_LIMITE}} > When I need something deliverable ("(optional)" if there is no hard deadline)
- CALIDAD_OBJETIVO: {{CALIDAD_OBJETIVO}} > Sufficient level for this delivery: draft, reviewable version, final deliverable ("(optional)" if not defined)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I have a task without a clear end where I tend to get stuck or chase perfection, and that blocks my progress. I want to apply timeboxing to convert it into a bounded work block: fixing a maximum time forces me to prioritize what is essential, produce something good enough, and free up the time and energy that currently dissipates in over-polishing. What gets unlocked: a concrete deliverable at the end of the block and a clear decision about what to leave out. Task: {{TAREA}}. Cause of stagnation: {{CAUSA_ESTANCAMIENTO}}. Time available today: {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}}. Deadline: {{FECHA_LIMITE}}. Target quality: {{CALIDAD_OBJETIVO}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior productivity coach specializing in time management, timeboxing, and focus habit design, with experience helping professionals overcome perfectionism and open-scope paralysis.
Deliverable: a timeboxing plan ready to execute with a timer immediately. Steps:
1. Reformulate {{TAREA}} as a minimum viable objective: the smallest version that already adds value and can be considered done according to {{CALIDAD_OBJETIVO}}. Distinguish what is essential (goes into the block) from what is desirable (stays out).
2. Propose a concrete time box in minutes, justified by {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}} and the nature of the task; name explicitly what falls outside the block. If {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}} is greater than what the task needs for the minimum viable version, cut the box rather than fill it (Parkinson's Law).
3. Divide the block into phases with assigned minutes that sum to the total: focused start, production, an intermediate checkpoint to verify progress against the minimum viable objective, and a final close margin. If the block exceeds 90 minutes, insert micro-breaks without reopening the task.
4. Define a start trigger for the first two minutes: the smallest mechanical action that breaks inertia and avoids initial paralysis.
5. Define the stop rule: what to do exactly when the timer goes off, how to decide whether the result is sufficient (binary criterion, not graded), and how to capture what remains on a separate list without reopening the task.
6. Anticipate two derailment risks tied to {{CAUSA_ESTANCAMIENTO}} (e.g., over-polishing, scope creep, distraction, seeking more information) with an actionable and observable countermeasure for each.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 – Interpret: confirm the task and the cause of stagnation; if {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}}, {{FECHA_LIMITE}}, or {{CALIDAD_OBJETIVO}} is missing and essential for sizing the block, ask for it before continuing rather than assuming.
Phase 2 – Plan: define the minimum viable objective, size the time box with its phases, the start trigger, and the checkpoint.
Phase 3 – Execute: deliver the plan with the minute-by-minute phases table, the start trigger, the stop rule, and the two risks with countermeasures.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- The minimum viable objective is concrete, separated from what is desirable, and can be declared done without ambiguity.
- The time box is in minutes, justified, and consistent with {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}}; if there was excess time, the box was cut rather than filled.
- What falls outside the block is explicitly named.
- The phases sum to the total block and include start, production, intermediate checkpoint, and close margin; if it exceeds 90 min, there are micro-breaks.
- There is a concrete start trigger for the first two minutes.
- The stop rule is unambiguous: what to do when the timer goes off, binary sufficiency criterion, and how to capture what remains without reopening the task.
- There are two risks tied to {{CAUSA_ESTANCAMIENTO}}, each with its actionable and observable countermeasure.
Expected deliverable: timeboxing plan in a phases table (minute by minute) plus start trigger, stop rule, and two risks with countermeasures, ready to start with a timer immediately.
spec-personal_pomodoro_sesion:
[inputs]
- TAREA: {{TAREA}} > Task to advance and expected outcome (what needs to be produced and how far to get in this session)
- TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE: {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}} > Total session time and, if applicable, the time window (e.g., 2 hours, from 9:00 to 11:00)
- ENERGIA: {{ENERGIA}} > Current energy and focus level: high, medium, or low (defines the load and order of the first blocks)
- INTERRUPCIONES: {{INTERRUPCIONES}} > Typical interruptions and work environment (e.g., notifications, meetings, noise; office or home)
- DURACION: {{DURACION}} > Pomodoro and break duration to use (optional; default 25/5 and long break of 15–30 min every 4 Pomodoros)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I have the task {{TAREA}} ahead of me and a block of {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}}, but time without structure dissolves into multitasking and interruptions. The purpose of this session is to convert that vague intention into a concrete Pomodoro agenda: focus intervals, each with a single verifiable objective, separated by scheduled breaks that sustain concentration without leading to exhaustion. A well-designed session unlocks real and measurable progress on {{TAREA}}, protects attention against {{INTERRUPCIONES}}, and leaves a record to calibrate future sessions. The strategy here is rhythm: alternating focus and recovery in short cycles rather than a sustained effort that cannot be maintained.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior personal productivity coach, expert in Francesco Cirillo's Pomodoro Technique, attention management, and deep concentration work planning.
Deliver the following, in this order:
1. Reformulate {{TAREA}} in a single sentence: "Advance on [task] until leaving [concrete observable outcome]".
2. Break {{TAREA}} into work units that each fit in one Pomodoro according to {{DURACION}}; each block must have a verifiable deliverable, never a vague objective. Split what does not fit and group what is too small; if two units share context, group them to reduce the start-up cost.
3. Calculate how many Pomodoros fit in {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}}, inserting a short break after each Pomodoro and a long break after every 4; reserve a close margin and do not fill 100% of the time.
4. Build the agenda in a table with columns: Pomodoro number, start and end, the block's single objective, the following break. Order the load according to {{ENERGIA}}: high = hardest or most cognitively costly first; medium = alternate demanding and light; low = start with a warm-up or low-friction block before increasing difficulty.
5. Define the anti-interruption protocol from {{INTERRUPCIONES}}: a "for later" list to write down without acting on what comes up during a Pomodoro, the distinction between internal interruption (own impulse: note it and keep going) and external (another person: apply inform-negotiate-schedule-respond), and Cirillo's rule (a truly interrupted Pomodoro does not count and must be restarted).
6. Close with a review ritual: what to record at the end (Pomodoros completed vs. estimated, what blocked focus, one concrete improvement) to calibrate the next session.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 – Frame: set the session objective and validate that the task, available time, and interruption context exist; if an essential data point is missing, ask for it before executing and do not invent the task or availability.
Phase 2 – Breakdown: cut {{TAREA}} into one-Pomodoro units, each with a verifiable deliverable; if {{TAREA}} exceeds {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}}, say so explicitly and prioritize the highest-value subset rather than compressing the blocks.
Phase 3 – Capacity: calculate how many Pomodoros fit according to {{DURACION}} and {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}}, with a short break after each and a long one every 4, leaving at least half a Pomodoro of buffer for close or unexpected events.
Phase 4 – Agenda: order the blocks in a table with a single objective per Pomodoro, adjusting load and order to {{ENERGIA}}; verify that times are consistent and do not overlap; mark [ASSUMPTION] where you assume context (e.g., start time or that tools are ready).
Phase 5 – Shield and close: define the anti-interruption protocol and the review ritual for calibrating the next session.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
- The session objective was reformulated in an actionable sentence with an observable outcome before planning.
- Each Pomodoro has a single objective and a verifiable deliverable; there are no blocks with vague goals.
- The number of Pomodoros is consistent with {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}} and {{DURACION}}, with a short break after each and a long one every 4, and at least half a Pomodoro of buffer reserved.
- The agenda is in a table with Pomodoro number, start/end, objective, and next break; times are consistent and do not overlap.
- The load and order of the blocks were adjusted to the declared {{ENERGIA}} level.
- If {{TAREA}} does not fit in {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}}, this was stated explicitly and the highest-value subset was prioritized.
- There is an explicit anti-interruption protocol ("for later" list, internal/external distinction, and the rule that an interrupted Pomodoro is restarted).
- Assumptions about context are marked [ASSUMPTION].
- A final review ritual is included with metrics (completed vs. estimated, main blocker, concrete improvement) to calibrate the next session.
Expected deliverable: Pomodoro agenda in a table ready to execute (Pomodoros, schedules, objectives, and breaks) plus the anti-interruption protocol and the review ritual, in neutral Spanish and professional tone.
spec-personal_time_audit:
[inputs]
- PERIODO_REGISTRO: {{PERIODO_REGISTRO}} > Date range to audit and why that period is representative (e.g., typical workweek, closing week). If atypical, declare it.
- GRANULARIDAD: {{GRANULARIDAD}} > Window size of the log and desired normalization (e.g., 30-min blocks, by hour)
- REGISTRO_TIEMPO: {{REGISTRO_TIEMPO}} > Raw activity log window by window with the label you gave each one. If reconstructed from memory, indicate so to flag lower reliability.
- COMPROMISOS_FIJOS: {{COMPROMISOS_FIJOS}} > Non-negotiable commitments that cannot be reallocated (e.g., work hours, childcare, sleep), with their windows
- OBJETIVO_REASIGNACION: {{OBJETIVO_REASIGNACION}} > What you want to dedicate the recovered hours to and why it matters now
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Calendar screenshots, time-tracking app exports, log sheets, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I want to know where my time really goes so I can stop operating on autopilot and reallocate hours toward what matters. An honest audit of the period {{PERIODO_REGISTRO}} unlocks concrete decisions: which meetings to decline, which windows to protect for deep work, and which leak habits to cut. The result is an evidence-based time plan grounded in my own behavior, not good intentions. If the period is atypical, its reading biases the plan: this must be flagged.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior personal productivity coach specializing in time-use audits, with expertise in time-tracking, the Eisenhower matrix, energy-time mapping, Parkinson's Law, and context-switching costs (attention residue).
Deliverable: a time-use audit with a reallocation plan. Steps:
1. Restate my log and my objective; mark ambiguous windows or periods without data and ask for what is missing before classifying. If the log is reconstructed from memory, lower confidence and flag it.
2. Normalize the log to {{GRANULARIDAD}} and classify each window on three axes: category (deep work / reactive / meetings / administration / rest / leisure / commute / personal), value (high / medium / low / leak), and energy (high / medium / low). If a window combines activities, assign it to the dominant one and note it.
3. Quantify the distribution: hours and percentage by category and by value, plus an explicit and traceable calculation of hours lost to leaks (multitasking, context switches, decision-free meetings, waiting, scrolling), showing the counting method.
4. Detect patterns: energy peaks vs. actual time use, day fragmentation (number and duration of continuous blocks), commitments that cost more than they contribute, and Parkinson's Law (tasks that expand to fill available time).
5. Deliver the plan: the three costliest leaks with a cut or redesign action and the trigger for each; protected time blocks in energy peaks (respecting {{COMPROMISOS_FIJOS}}, without invading them); and a one-week experiment toward {{OBJETIVO_REASIGNACION}} with a target of hours to recover, a success metric, and one adherence risk with its mitigation.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 – Comprehension: paraphrase log, objective, and constraints; list data gaps and flag the period as typical or atypical.
Phase 2 – Classification: window-by-window table with the three axes; label [ASSUMPTION] on every context inference and every reconstructed window.
Phase 3 – Quantification: aggregates by category, value, and energy; total leak hours with visible counting method.
Phase 4 – Diagnosis: energy-time patterns, fragmentation, Parkinson, and low-return commitments; ordered by hours at stake.
Phase 5 – Reallocation: top 3 leaks with action and trigger, protected blocks, and measurable weekly experiment with adherence risk.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- Every window of the period is classified on the three axes; gaps and reconstructed windows are declared, not filled.
- Leak hours are quantified with an explicit and traceable counting method, not asserted in the abstract.
- The diagnosis connects energy peaks to actual time use and measures fragmentation, not just lists categories.
- The three prioritized leaks include a concrete cut or redesign action and their trigger, not generic advice.
- Protected blocks fall in energy peaks and respect {{COMPROMISOS_FIJOS}} without invading them.
- The one-week experiment has a target of hours to recover, a verifiable success metric, and one adherence risk with mitigation.
- If the period is atypical, the plan carries a representativeness warning.
- Every context inference is marked [ASSUMPTION]; no prices or monetary costs unless figures are given.
Expected deliverable: window-by-window classification table + allocation dashboard (hours/% by category, value, and energy) + pattern diagnosis ordered by hours at stake + reallocation plan with top 3 leaks, protected blocks, measurable weekly experiment, and adherence risk.
spec-personal_theming_dias:
[inputs]
- TIPOS_DE_TRABAJO: {{TIPOS_DE_TRABAJO}} > Recurring work types or roles to distribute (creation, meetings, administration, learning), with relative weight if known
- DIAS_Y_HORAS: {{DIAS_Y_HORAS}} > Real workdays and time windows on which the scheme is built
- PICOS_Y_VALLES_DE_ENERGIA: {{PICOS_Y_VALLES_DE_ENERGIA}} > Highest and lowest energy or concentration windows throughout the day
- COMPROMISOS_FIJOS: {{COMPROMISOS_FIJOS}} > Recurring meetings, deliverables, and immovable obligations the scheme must respect
- FLEXIBILIDAD: {{FLEXIBILIDAD}} > Freedom level to move or regroup appointments (high, medium, low) (optional; if missing, assume medium and mark [ASSUMPTION])
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I want to dedicate each day of the week to a dominant type of work (day theming) to reduce context-switching costs and protect my highest-concentration blocks. Jumping between heterogeneous tasks within the same day fragments attention and erodes quality; a day-theme scheme unlocks deeper workdays, faster scheduling decisions, and a week that holds up even when unexpected events arise. I am not looking for a rigid schedule but a default structure, defensible and easy to resume after an interruption.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior personal productivity strategist, specialist in day theming, deep work, and weekly cadence design.
Deliver an actionable day-theming scheme. Steps:
1. Group the TIPOS_DE_TRABAJO into 4 to 6 coherent themes; name each with a clear label and a one-line purpose. If there are more than 6 categories, consolidate related ones and declare the merging criterion.
2. Estimate the weekly weight of each theme (hours or percentage) and verify that the total fits within DIAS_Y_HORAS without overloading any day; reserve a slack margin of 10 to 20 percent and declare the capacity assumption.
