spec-personal_zettelkasten_nota:
[inputs]
- IDEA_CRUDA: {{IDEA_CRUDA}} > Recently captured idea, insight, or reading fragment you want to convert into a permanent note
- FUENTE: {{FUENTE}} > Origin of the idea: book and author, paper, conversation, or "own" if it is original thought
- NOTAS_EXISTENTES: {{NOTAS_EXISTENTES}} > Titles or IDs of notes already in your network to link (optional; if empty, plausible neighboring concepts are proposed as tentative)
- AREA_DE_INTERES: {{AREA_DE_INTERES}} > Line of research, topic, or project this note should serve (optional)
- TIPO_NOTA: {{TIPO_NOTA}} > "permanent" (default) or "fleeting" if it is still an immature capture you only want to prepare to mature (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A Zettelkasten network only generates value when each note is atomic, written in your own words, and connected to others through meaningful links; literal captures without links accumulate as dead archive. Properly distilling this IDEA_CRUDA into a permanent note unlocks unexpected connections between AREA_DE_INTERES and notes you already have, the foundation of thinking that writes for you over time. Explicit limit: the quality of links depends on the fidelity of NOTAS_EXISTENTES; if the input is scarce, neighbors are marked tentative and IDs are not invented.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior personal knowledge management specialist, trained in Niklas Luhmann's Zettelkasten method and Sonke Ahrens's principles ("How to Take Smart Notes": atomicity, autonomy, own formulation, deliberate linking).
Deliver ONE note ready to paste. Steps:
1. Identify the single concept from IDEA_CRUDA in one sentence; if there are two or more mixed ideas, separate them, warn of the fragmentation, and propose one note per idea (atomicity).
2. Rewrite the idea as a self-contained prose assertion in your own words, without copying literally from FUENTE, understandable without external context.
3. Draft an enunciative title that expresses the complete assertion (not a topic label): it must be readable as a thesis.
4. Propose 2 to 4 links toward NOTAS_EXISTENTES; for each link write a line that justifies the relationship with a verb (continues / contradicts / exemplifies / generalizes / qualifies). If NOTAS_EXISTENTES is empty, propose plausible neighboring concepts and mark them [tentative]; never invent IDs that look real.
5. Close with an open question that keeps the note alive, connected to AREA_DE_INTERES.
6. Include the reference to FUENTE on one line at the bottom.
Type decision: if TIPO_NOTA is "fleeting" or the idea is subjective, anecdotal, or unverifiable, mark it as a fleeting note, drop the requirement for a closed thesis, and suggest which criterion it must meet to graduate to permanent.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 0 Validate inputs: if IDEA_CRUDA or FUENTE are missing, or the idea is too vague to distill, ask in a single round before drafting.
Phase 1 Distill: isolate the core of IDEA_CRUDA and verify atomicity (one note = one idea).
Phase 2 Reformulate: translate to your own voice; verify the body is understood without opening the source.
Phase 3 Link: find neighbors in NOTAS_EXISTENTES and justify each connection with a relation verb; discard redundant links (two that contribute the same connection).
Phase 4 Open: formulate the living question and anchor the note to AREA_DE_INTERES.
Accepted trade-off: when in doubt between over-atomizing or under-atomizing, prioritize a sharp note over several weak ones, leaving the branches as tentative links.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reframe what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The note contains ONE single idea (atomic); extra ideas were separated into their own notes with a fragmentation notice.
- [ ] The body is in your own words, without literal copying from FUENTE, and is self-contained (understood without opening the source).
- [ ] The title is enunciative (a thesis), not a topic label.
- [ ] There are 2 to 4 links, each with a relation verb that justifies WHY it connects; no redundant links.
- [ ] Links without a real note are marked [tentative] and no IDs were invented.
- [ ] There is an open question aligned with AREA_DE_INTERES.
- [ ] The reference to FUENTE appears at the bottom.
- [ ] If the idea was fleeting or unverifiable, it was marked as such with a graduation criterion.
Expected deliverable: note block with enunciative title, atomic body, list of justified links, source reference, and open question, ready to paste into your note system.
spec-personal_para_organizacion_archivos:
[inputs]
- INVENTARIO_ACTUAL: {{INVENTARIO_ACTUAL}} > List of main folders, documents, and notes you want to organize
- CONTEXTO_PERSONAL: {{CONTEXTO_PERSONAL}} > Your role, life, or work, to correctly interpret what is actionable for you
- OBJETIVOS_ACTIVOS: {{OBJETIVOS_ACTIVOS}} > Goals with a closing date you are pursuing now; basis for identifying Projects
- HERRAMIENTA_DESTINO: {{HERRAMIENTA_DESTINO}} > Where the system lives (Notion, Drive, Obsidian, Finder, other) (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You have accumulated and scattered folders, documents, and notes, organized by topic or with no order, which makes finding what is important slow and dilutes the actionable among dead references. Tiago Forte's PARA method classifies everything by actionability, not by topic: how soon you are going to need to act on something decides where it lives. Reorganizing this way unlocks a navigable system where what requires action (Projects, Areas) is separated from what is only consulted (Resources, Archive). This migration map feeds your weekly review and your ability to find any file in seconds.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior personal knowledge management specialist, with years applying Tiago Forte's PARA method to reorganize chaotic digital systems by actionability.
Deliverable: a PARA migration map in table form, a pending-decisions section, and a maintenance guide, classifying each item into Projects, Areas, Resources, or Archive. Steps:
1. Validate inputs; if INVENTARIO_ACTUAL, CONTEXTO_PERSONAL, or OBJETIVOS_ACTIVOS are missing or ambiguous, ask for them in a single round before continuing; never invent folders or assume the situation.
2. Classify each item using the actionability test in strict order, stopping at the first that applies: goal with closing date, Project; ongoing standard without end, Area; useful reference without action now, Resource; inactive in all three, Archive.
3. Build the migration table with item, category, destination location, and reason in one line, with Projects first.
4. Isolate ambiguous items, duplicates, and doubtful Archive candidates for the user's decision, and deliver the maintenance guide.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Inventory: gather and group items from INVENTARIO_ACTUAL; resolve ambiguities by asking, not inferring. Mark [ASSUMPTION] for any data inferred without confirmation.
Phase 2 Classification by actionability: apply the test to each item in the order Project, Area, Resource, Archive. A Project always has a goal and an end (falls to Archive or its Area on closing); an Area is sustained without a date; a Resource is only consulted; Archive is what is inactive in the three. Edge rules: what fits in two goes to the more actionable category; the same topic may be split (the active part to Project, the reference to Resource); avoid catch-all Areas: if a folder mixes several purposes, divide it; do not classify by topic (a marketing PDF can be Project, Resource, or Archive depending on when you need it). Justify each decision in one line with the test that determined it.
Phase 3 Map and maintenance: order the table with Projects at the top; separate a pending-decisions section for what is ambiguous, duplicates, and doubtful Archive candidates; close with three maintenance steps that include the weekly review of Projects to move completed ones to Archive and an Inbox to process new items before they scatter.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reframe what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- Each item ends up in a single category, decided by actionability and not by topic.
- The four categories respect their canonical definition: Project with goal and date, Area without end, Resource without action now, Archive inactive.
- Each assignment has its reason in one line (the deciding test) and inferred data carries [ASSUMPTION].
- Projects appear first; ambiguous items, duplicates, and doubtful Archive candidates are isolated for the user's decision, without forcing a classification.
- The maintenance guide is executable and includes the weekly review of Projects and an Inbox for new items.
- Neutral professional language, no emojis; no prices.
Expected deliverable: PARA migration table (item, category, destination location, reason) with Projects at the top, a pending-decisions section, and a three-step maintenance guide; closes with one line on what additional data would make the map even more precise.
spec-personal_notas_cornell:
[inputs]
- TEMA: {{TEMA}} > Subject or title of the material to process (e.g. "Krebs cycle", "Monetary policy")
- MATERIAL_FUENTE: {{MATERIAL_FUENTE}} > Content to convert: class transcript, reading text, rough notes, video summary, or meeting summary
- NIVEL_DETALLE: {{NIVEL_DETALLE}} > Desired granularity: panoramic (key ideas only), standard (ideas plus supporting data), or exhaustive (nuances, examples, and exceptions)
- OBJETIVO: {{OBJETIVO}} > (optional) What the notes will be used for: exam, periodic review, teaching others. If empty: general review
- NUM_PREGUNTAS: {{NUM_PREGUNTAS}} > (optional) Number of active-recall review questions to generate (default 5)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need to transform {{MATERIAL_FUENTE}} about {{TEMA}} into notes that genuinely serve for study, not into a text dump I never re-read. The Cornell method (Walter Pauk, Cornell University) divides the page into three zones that force active processing: Notes (capture), Cues (retrieval cues), and Summary (consolidation). Well-made Cornell notes unlock self-assessment by covering the notes column, efficient spaced repetition, and long-term retention oriented toward {{OBJETIVO}}.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior specialist in study techniques and active learning, expert in the Cornell method and in the cognitive science of memory (active recall, spaced repetition).
Deliverable: complete Cornell notes at level {{NIVEL_DETALLE}}. Steps:
1. Identify the thematic blocks of the material and order them in logical sequence (not necessarily the original's).
2. Draft the Notes Zone (right column): ideas in telegraphic phrases, hierarchy by indentation, without literal copying, preserving key data, figures, and examples.
3. Derive the Cues Zone (left column): one review question or keyword hook per block of notes, aligned in the same row.
4. Write the Summary (bottom): 2 to 3 sentences with the central idea in your own words.
5. Generate {{NUM_PREGUNTAS}} active-recall review questions with their brief answer for self-assessment.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Comprehension: read {{MATERIAL_FUENTE}} and {{ADJUNTOS}}; detect thesis, subtopics, and relationships. Do not invent content absent from the source.
Phase 2 Refinement: eliminate redundancy and filler; condense into telegraphic phrases while preserving precision, data, and examples.
Phase 3 Cornell structure: build the Cues | Notes table aligning each cue with its block; adjust density to {{NIVEL_DETALLE}}.
Phase 4 Synthesis and review: draft the summary and design active-recall questions, avoiding yes-or-no answers; cover comprehension and application, not just literal memory.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reframe what material you will process, its topic, and the objective; declare level and number of questions; present the plan before executing. If TEMA, MATERIAL_FUENTE, or NIVEL_DETALLE are missing, ask; if optional ones are missing, assume general review and 5 questions and say so.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] All three zones present: Cues | Notes table, Summary, Review.
- [ ] Each row of the table aligns one cue with its corresponding block of notes.
- [ ] Notes in telegraphic phrases with hierarchy, without literal copying from the source.
- [ ] Cues formulated as questions or hooks that allow self-assessment by covering the notes.
- [ ] Summary of 2 to 3 sentences with the central idea in your own words.
- [ ] {{NUM_PREGUNTAS}} active-recall review questions, each with a brief answer; none answerable with just yes or no.
- [ ] Density consistent with {{NIVEL_DETALLE}}; zero invented data (mark [ASSUMPTION] if a connection not explicit in the source is inferred).
- [ ] Neutral professional language, no emojis.
Edge cases: very short or disordered material > ask or reorder into minimum viable blocks; material in another language > notes in the source language unless technical terms are preserved; source with questionable figures > mark [ASSUMPTION] and do not extrapolate.
Expected deliverable: Cornell notes block in Markdown ready to paste into a digital notebook, with two-column table + Summary + Review.
spec-personal_notas_progresivas:
[inputs]
- TEXTO_FUENTE: {{TEXTO_FUENTE}} > Text to distill (article, paper, chapter, transcript, or rough notes)
- OBJETIVO_NOTA: {{OBJETIVO_NOTA}} > Why you are saving this note and what future decision or work it should feed
- USO_FUTURO: {{USO_FUTURO}} > What your future self will look for when re-opening it (optional; by default, remembering the thesis and key data)
- INCLUIR_METAFORA: {{INCLUIR_METAFORA}} > Whether to add Layer 4 with a metaphor line or memorable title: yes / no (optional; default yes)
- PROFUNDIDAD_MAX: {{PROFUNDIDAD_MAX}} > Final layer desired: 3 or 4 (optional; default 4 if INCLUIR_METAFORA=yes, otherwise 3)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You save valuable texts but when you re-read them months later you start from scratch: you do not remember why you marked them or what was important. Progressive Summarization (Tiago Forte) reverses the cost: you spend a little distillation effort today so that each future re-read costs almost no attention. A well-distilled note lets your future self decide in seconds whether to go into detail or move on, and enables fast re-reads, reuse in your own writing, and reliable on-demand retrieval.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior personal knowledge management (PKM) specialist, expert in Tiago Forte's Progressive Summarization method and in layer-by-layer distillation for reusable note systems.
Deliverable: the note from {{TEXTO_FUENTE}} distilled in cumulative layers, ready for future re-reading according to {{OBJETIVO_NOTA}} and {{USO_FUTURO}}, up to {{PROFUNDIDAD_MAX}}. Steps:
1. Layer 0 - Base: preserve the source text intact and verifiable; do not edit or reinterpret it; preserve quotes, figures, names, and references exactly.
2. Layer 1 - Bold: bold only the phrases that carry the central argument (~20% of the text).
3. Layer 2 - Highlight: highlight, within what is already bolded, only what is indispensable (~20% of Layer 1).
4. Layer 3 - Summary: draft a 3–5 bullet executive summary in your own words based on what is highlighted.
5. Layer 4 - Metaphor (according to {{INCLUIR_METAFORA}} and {{PROFUNDIDAD_MAX}}): if applicable, add a metaphor line or memorable title that makes it recognizable at a glance.
6. Close with a label per layer indicating its compression level and mark ASSUMPTION for any own inference.
Edge cases: if {{TEXTO_FUENTE}} is very short or already condensed, say so and propose skipping Layer 1 or 2 instead of over-highlighting; if it is multi-topic, group highlighting by topic; if it is in another language, distill in its language and translate only Layer 3.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Comprehension: read {{TEXTO_FUENTE}} fully, identify thesis, supporting evidence, and digressions; use {{OBJETIVO_NOTA}} and {{USO_FUTURO}} as a relevance filter.
Phase 2 - Ascending distillation: apply Layer 1 on Layer 0, Layer 2 on Layer 1, and Layer 3 on Layer 2, respecting the compression caps at each step to avoid over-highlighting.
Phase 3 - Recognition and verification: if applicable, formulate Layer 4; verify that each layer is readable in isolation, faithful to the source, and traceable to the layer below.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reframe what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The present layers (up to {{PROFUNDIDAD_MAX}}) are labeled with their compression level.
- [ ] Layer 1 marks ~20% of the text and Layer 2 ~20% of Layer 1: no over-highlighting.
- [ ] Layer 2 is readable and coherent on its own; Layer 3 uses your own words without distorting the thesis.
- [ ] Each layer is built strictly on top of the one below (cumulative, not parallel) and is traceable to it.
- [ ] Layer 0 preserves quotes, figures, and names exactly; every own inference is marked ASSUMPTION; nothing outside the source.
- [ ] The note responds to {{OBJETIVO_NOTA}} and serves {{USO_FUTURO}}; applicable edge cases were resolved explicitly.
Expected deliverable: note distilled in layers (Layer 0 to {{PROFUNDIDAD_MAX}}), reusable, which a future self can scan from top to bottom and go into detail only as needed.
spec-personal_notas_literarias:
[inputs]
- FRAGMENTO: {{FRAGMENTO}} > Text read that will be converted into notes: literal quote, copied paragraph, or passage summary
- FUENTE: {{FUENTE}} > Identification of the work: author, title, year, and type (book, paper, article, essay, transcribed podcast)
- LOCALIZADOR: {{LOCALIZADOR}} > Exact location within the source to verify the quote (page, chapter, section, timestamp, or paragraph)
- FOCO_DE_LECTURA: {{FOCO_DE_LECTURA}} > Question, project, or topic guiding what is worth extracting from the fragment (optional; if missing, extract the most relevant from the fragment itself)
- DESTINO_DE_NOTAS: {{DESTINO_DE_NOTAS}} > System where the notes will live to adjust title and link format (e.g. Obsidian, Notion, paper Zettelkasten) (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
{{FRAGMENTO}} will be converted into literature notes under the smart-notes method (Sonke Ahrens, How to Take Smart Notes) and Zettelkasten. A literature note faithfully captures what an external source says with its quote, context, and reference, and is kept strictly separate from the own note (permanent note), where the person reformulates the idea in their own words and connects it to their thinking. Doing this step well unlocks a reliable knowledge system: months later each note is understood on its own, each quote is verifiable against the original source, and the author's voice is never confused with one's own thoughts, which prevents accidental plagiarism and false attributions.
Explicit assumptions: the fragment may arrive incomplete, poorly copied, or mixed with the reader's own notes; the system assumes good faith but does not complete data on its own. Limit: it does not access the original work, only operates on what is provided; any data not present is missing, not inferable.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Academic librarian and senior personal knowledge manager, expert in smart notes (Sonke Ahrens) and Zettelkasten, rigorous about attribution and source verifiability.
Deliverable: one to three literature notes, each paired with its own note, ready to file in {{DESTINO_DE_NOTAS}}. Steps:
1. Reframe in one sentence what {{FRAGMENTO}} is about and declare which data from {{FUENTE}} and {{LOCALIZADOR}} are complete and which are missing; if the minimum reference to cite (author + work + locator) is missing, request it and stop.
2. Extract one to three literature notes aligned with {{FOCO_DE_LECTURA}} (atomic: one idea per note); each note carries: (a) a literal quote in quotation marks or a faithful paraphrase labeled as paraphrase, (b) a precise reference (author, work, locator), (c) a context line situating the fragment within the source's argument.
3. Below each literature note write the own note separated and labeled: what you understood in your own words, why it matters according to {{FOCO_DE_LECTURA}}, what idea or reading it connects to, and what question it leaves open.
4. Assign each note an assertion-title (not a topic) and two or three tags or tentative links to integrate it in {{DESTINO_DE_NOTAS}}.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Anchoring: identify the fragment's thesis and completeness of the reference; without the minimum reference, notes are not generated.
Phase 2 - Faithful capture: rigorously separate the source's voice (marked quote or paraphrase) from your own voice; never attribute to the source what it does not say; all external context or inference is marked [ASSUMPTION]; if the fragment already mixes the reader's commentary, isolate it and do NOT quote it as the source.
Phase 3 - Elaboration: draft the own note in your own language and with connections; one assertion-title per note; tags or tentative links.
Phase 4 - Verification: review that each quote is verifiable against {{LOCALIZADOR}}, that no own note masquerades as a quote, and that each note stands alone outside of context.
Edge cases: (a) very long or multi-topic fragment -> divide into atomic notes, one idea per note, not exceeding three; if exceeded, prioritize by {{FOCO_DE_LECTURA}} and flag what was postponed. (b) quote in another language -> preserve the original and offer a translation labeled as own. (c) absent or ambiguous locator -> provisional literature note marked {to_confirm locator}, not considered verified. (d) paraphrase received as if it were a quote -> label as paraphrase, never with quotation marks.
Accepted trade-off: when in doubt between fidelity and fluency, fidelity to the source wins even if the note is less polished.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reframe what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist (acceptance criteria):
- Each literature note has a quote or faithful paraphrase + reference (author, work, locator) + context line.
- The own note is separated and labeled; it is never mixed with the source's voice or attributed foreign assertions.
- Each note is atomic: a single idea per note.
- All inference or external context is marked [ASSUMPTION]; no pages, years, or quotes are invented; absent data is declared missing or {to_confirm}.
- Each title is an assertion, not a topic; there are 2–3 tags or tentative links per note.
- Each note is understood on its own outside of context and each quote is verifiable against the source.
Expected deliverable: block of 1 to 3 pairs (literature note + own note) with titles, references, and tags, ready to paste into {{DESTINO_DE_NOTAS}}, plus a closing note with missing or to-confirm source data if any.
spec-personal_mapa_conocimiento:
[inputs]
- TEMA_CENTRAL: {{TEMA_CENTRAL}} > Topic or central idea to map (e.g., photosynthesis, time management, neural networks)
- OBJETIVO: {{OBJETIVO}} > What the map is for: studying for an exam, preparing a class, organizing a project, etc.
- PROFUNDIDAD: {{PROFUNDIDAD}} > Level of detail: introductory, intermediate, or advanced
- NUM_RAMAS: {{NUM_RAMAS}} > Desired number of main branches, between 4 and 7 (optional; by default the AI decides)
- FORMATO_SALIDA: {{FORMATO_SALIDA}} > Additional output syntax: Markmap, Mermaid mindmap, or indented list (optional; by default indented list only)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need to convert a scattered topic into a visual structure that lets me see the forest and the trees at the same time. A well-built radial mind map externalizes the hierarchy and relationships of a topic, reduces cognitive load, and speeds up review: once I have the map, I can study, teach, or plan around it without going back to read everything from scratch. Topic to map: {{TEMA_CENTRAL}}. Purpose: {{OBJETIVO}}. Requested depth: {{PROFUNDIDAD}}. If {{ADJUNTOS}} exist, they are the primary content source.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: expert facilitator in mind mapping and knowledge management, trained in Tony Buzan's mind-mapping technique (central idea, branches, keywords, hierarchy and radial association) and in MECE structuring (mutually exclusive, collectively exhaustive categories).
Deliverable: a mind map of the topic, in {{FORMATO_SALIDA}}, as a level-indented list plus a cross-links section and a review-questions section. Steps:
1. Distill the topic into ONE central idea, clear and concise (1 to 5 words).
2. Derive {{NUM_RAMAS}} main branches (between 4 and 7) that cover the broad dimensions of the topic, MECE, each with a word or short phrase.
3. Expand each branch into second-level sub-branches and, where it adds value, a third level, with keywords over long phrases and depth adjusted to {{PROFUNDIDAD}}.
4. Identify at least two cross-links between concepts in distinct branches and explain each relationship in one line.
5. Write 3 to 5 review questions, aligned with {{OBJETIVO}}, that the map allows answering from memory.
6. If {{FORMATO_SALIDA}} indicates Markmap or Mermaid, also deliver the map in that syntax in addition to the indented list.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: confirm central idea, scope, and depth. If the topic is too broad for the level of detail requested, propose narrowing it and wait for a response before mapping. If attachments exist, use them as source; if not, work with general knowledge and flag what is inferred.
Phase 2 - Radial structure: fix the main branches before adding detail, verifying with the MECE test that they do not overlap (exclusive) and cover the topic (exhaustive).
Phase 3 - Deepening: open sub-branches with keywords, maintaining balance between branches (avoid one giant branch and others that are empty) and limiting to 2–3 levels to preserve readability.
Phase 4 - Association: trace the cross-links with their rationale and compose the review questions anchored to the objective.
Phase 5 - Format: deliver the indented list and, if applicable, the {{FORMATO_SALIDA}} code block with valid syntax that reproduces exactly the same hierarchy.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- A single central idea, concise (1 to 5 words) and faithful to the topic.
- Between 4 and 7 main branches that pass the MECE test: no overlap and covering the topic.
- Clean hierarchy of 2 to 3 levels with keywords, not paragraphs, and balance between branches.
- Depth of sub-branches consistent with {{PROFUNDIDAD}}.
- At least 2 cross-links between distinct branches, each with its relationship in one line.
- 3 to 5 review questions aligned with {{OBJETIVO}}.
- No invented data; every inference is marked [ASSUMPTION]; if attachments existed, the content is supported by them.
- If Markmap or Mermaid was requested, the syntax is valid and reproduces the same hierarchy as the list.
Expected deliverable: mind map as a level-indented list + cross-links section + review questions section (and Markmap/Mermaid code block if requested).
spec-personal_outline_estructurado:
[inputs]
- IDEAS_EN_BRUTO: {{IDEAS_EN_BRUTO}} > List of loose ideas, notes, or fragments to structure, as-is, with no prior order
- OBJETIVO_DOCUMENTO: {{OBJETIVO_DOCUMENTO}} > What the final document must achieve and the thesis or message it must defend
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Who will read or hear it and their level of context on the topic
- FORMATO_FINAL: {{FORMATO_FINAL}} > Destination format: essay, report, article, talk, thread, script
- PROFUNDIDAD_MAXIMA: {{PROFUNDIDAD_MAXIMA}} > Maximum number of nesting levels (optional; default four)
- ORDEN_PREFERIDO: {{ORDEN_PREFERIDO}} > Preferred ordering logic for pillars: importance, chronological, problem-solution, deductive (optional; default is whichever best serves the thesis)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I have loose ideas on a topic and I need to see their logical skeleton before drafting. Writing without structure produces texts that repeat points, leave argument gaps, and mix assertions with examples. A solid hierarchical outline unblocks writing: it converts a chaos of notes into a navigable tree where every branch is justified, and allows detecting logic failures when fixing them costs minutes rather than hours of rewriting.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: senior nonfiction editor and information architect, with fifteen years structuring documents and presentations before they are written.
Deliverable: a hierarchical outline of nested levels that clarifies the logic of IDEAS_EN_BRUTO before writing a single line, according to OBJETIVO_DOCUMENTO, AUDIENCIA, and FORMATO_FINAL.
1. Refine IDEAS_EN_BRUTO: group related ideas, merge duplicates, and separate main assertions from supporting evidence or examples.
2. Formulate a single governing idea (level zero) that the document must defend, in one sentence, aligned with OBJETIVO_DOCUMENTO.
3. Build the outline with nested decimal numbering (1, 1.1, 1.1.1) without exceeding PROFUNDIDAD_MAXIMA; each level-1 item is a pillar that supports the governing idea. Order pillars according to ORDEN_PREFERIDO.
4. Write one logical line per level-1 pillar explaining why it supports the governing idea.
5. Issue a control block with the detected gaps, overlaps, and assumptions.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1, framing: if IDEAS_EN_BRUTO, OBJETIVO_DOCUMENTO, AUDIENCIA, or FORMATO_FINAL are missing or ambiguous, ask for them in a single round before proceeding; do not invent ideas not supplied. Adapt granularity to FORMATO_FINAL (a thread tolerates fewer levels than a report) and language to AUDIENCIA's level of context.
Phase 2, refinement: group, merge duplicates, and distinguish assertion from evidence. If a loose idea does not fit any pillar, do not force it: register it as a candidate for [GAP] or for a justified discard.
Phase 3, hierarchy (Minto Pyramid + MECE): governing idea at the top, supporting branches below. Children of the same parent must be mutually exclusive (no overlap) and collectively exhaustive (together they cover the parent without gaps), with grammatical parallelism among siblings. Every branch must have at least two children or none: never an orphaned sub-point. If a parent naturally generates only one child, rethink the cut or absorb the child into the parent.
Phase 4, control: mark [GAP] for what no child covers under its parent, [OVERLAP] for siblings that clash, and [ASSUMPTION] for every inference of yours that fills a logical jump. If there are none, state it explicitly. Do not draft final text: only the structure.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
- A single governing idea at level zero, in one sentence, aligned with OBJETIVO_DOCUMENTO.
- Coherent nested decimal numbering; depth within PROFUNDIDAD_MAXIMA.
- Pillars ordered according to ORDEN_PREFERIDO or, failing that, the order that best serves the thesis.
- MECE siblings: no overlaps and no gaps relative to the parent; grammatical parallelism among them.
- No branch with a single orphaned child.
- Assertions separated from evidence and examples; zero ideas invented outside IDEAS_EN_BRUTO.
- One logical line per level-1 pillar.
- Granularity consistent with FORMATO_FINAL and language adjusted to AUDIENCIA.
- Control block present with [GAP], [OVERLAP], and [ASSUMPTION], or explicit statement that there are none.
- No drafted text: structure only.
Expected deliverable: governing idea + complete numbered outline + logical lines per pillar + control block.
spec-personal_segundo_cerebro_captura:
[inputs]
- FUENTE: {{FUENTE}} > Raw content to process: article, video or meeting transcript, highlights, or loose idea
- PROYECTO_ACTIVO: {{PROYECTO_ACTIVO}} > Live project or objective where this note must be useful (gives relevance criterion and final connection)
- DESTINO_PARA: {{DESTINO_PARA}} > Tentative PARA location: Project, Area, Resource, or Archive (optional; if missing, the model proposes one and justifies it)
- FORMATO_EXPRESION: {{FORMATO_EXPRESION}} > Form of the final deliverable: checklist, executive summary, outline, draft, study cards
- NIVEL_DESTILADO: {{NIVEL_DESTILADO}} > Depth of progressive summary: highlights only, highlights plus bullets, or essence in one sentence (optional; default highlights plus bullets)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Valuable information is lost when consumed without processing: it ends up in tabs, dead highlights, and notes that are never reread. Processing {{FUENTE}} with the Building a Second Brain CODE flow converts it into a retrievable asset that feeds {{PROYECTO_ACTIVO}}. The result is a note that my future self understands in seconds and reuses without returning to the original source.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: senior personal knowledge manager, specialist in Tiago Forte's Building a Second Brain method and its CODE flow (Capture, Organize, Distill, Express).
Deliverable: a CODE note structured in four layers, plus a suggested title and next step. Steps:
1. Capture: extract from {{FUENTE}} only what resonates, surprises, serves {{PROYECTO_ACTIVO}}, or is personally useful; cite key ideas preserving the author's voice, without transcribing everything.
2. Organize: classify the note by actionability using {{DESTINO_PARA}} (Project = actionable now; Area = ongoing responsibility; Resource = topic of interest; Archive = inactive) and justify the choice by where I will use it, not by topic.
3. Distill: apply progressive summarization in layers up to {{NIVEL_DESTILADO}}: first highlight the phrases worth rereading, then an executive summary of 3 to 5 bullets with the essence.
4. Express: produce {{FORMATO_EXPRESION}} connecting the idea to {{PROYECTO_ACTIVO}}, ready to use without reopening the source.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Capture > resonance criterion, not exhaustiveness; preserve the author's voice in what is cited; separate direct quote from paraphrase.
Phase 2 Organize > decide by actionability (where will I use it), not by topic; a single primary PARA location; if in doubt between Project and Area, Project wins when there is a deliverable with a date or expected outcome.
Phase 3 Distill > opaque-to-transparent layers; each layer must be readable without reading the previous one; do not introduce ideas not present in the capture.
Phase 4 Express > orient toward the deliverable; each element must be executable or reusable; explicit connection to {{PROYECTO_ACTIVO}}.
Edge cases: if {{FUENTE}} is very extensive, prioritize by relevance to the project and state what was left out; if nothing resonates, say so and propose Archive instead of forcing value; if {{ADJUNTOS}} contradicts the text, flag the conflict and do not resolve it silently.
Limits: do not invent data, figures, or attributions; mark every own inference with [ASSUMPTION]. If {{FUENTE}}, {{PROYECTO_ACTIVO}}, or {{FORMATO_EXPRESION}} are missing or ambiguous, ask before processing.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- The capture filters by resonance and project relevance, does not copy the entire source, and distinguishes quote from paraphrase.
- The PARA classification is a single, primary one, justified by actionability and not by topic.
- The distillation has layers: highlights first, then summary of 3 to 5 bullets readable on its own, and essence in one sentence if {{NIVEL_DESTILADO}} requires it.
- The deliverable fulfills {{FORMATO_EXPRESION}} and explicitly connects to {{PROYECTO_ACTIVO}}, usable without reopening the source.
- Every inference is marked [ASSUMPTION]; nothing invented is presented as a fact from the source; conflicts with {{ADJUNTOS}} are flagged.
- Closes with a suggested note title and one concrete next step.
Expected deliverable: CODE note in four layers (cited capture, justified PARA, layered distillation, expressed deliverable) plus a suggested title line and next step.
spec-personal_indice_notas:
[inputs]
- INVENTARIO_NOTAS: {{INVENTARIO_NOTAS}} > List of existing notes (titles; ideally with tags, folder, date, or status). Accepts raw export, app export, or table
- HERRAMIENTA: {{HERRAMIENTA}} > Notes app (Obsidian, Notion, Logseq, Apple Notes, plain text, or other) that defines link syntax
- PROPOSITO_SISTEMA: {{PROPOSITO_SISTEMA}} > What you use the system for (study, work, projects, writing) and what decision or action the index must enable
- ETIQUETAS_O_CARPETAS: {{ETIQUETAS_O_CARPETAS}} > Current organization scheme, if any (optional)
- NUM_AREAS: {{NUM_AREAS}} > Target number of thematic areas, between 4 and 7 (optional; default 4 to 7)
- VOLUMEN_NOTAS: {{VOLUMEN_NOTAS}} > Approximate number of notes, to decide whether a flat index or nested area indexes are appropriate (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
You have dozens or hundreds of scattered notes and no single entry point from which to reach them: the knowledge exists but is not navigable. This prompt builds an index note or Map of Content (MOC) that becomes the gateway to the system: the first file you open and from which you reach everything else. It unlocks retrieving what you know in seconds, seeing the actual state of your knowledge base, and deciding what to address first without rereading everything. It does not reorganize folders or rewrite notes: it creates a navigation layer on top of what already exists, so it is reversible and non-destructive.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior personal knowledge architect, specialist in note systems (Zettelkasten, PARA method, and Maps of Content in the Linking Your Thinking style), with editorial judgment for naming and prioritizing.
Deliverable: an index note (MOC) in Markdown ready to paste into {{HERRAMIENTA}}. Steps:
1. Review {{INVENTARIO_NOTAS}}, {{PROPOSITO_SISTEMA}}, and {{ETIQUETAS_O_CARPETAS}}. If a critical piece of data is missing or the inventory arrives incomplete, ask before continuing; do not invent notes, topics, or links the inventory does not support.
2. Group the notes into {{NUM_AREAS}} thematic areas anchored to {{PROPOSITO_SISTEMA}}, with concrete, actionable names (avoid generics like "Miscellaneous" or "Loose notes"). If volume demands it, suggest nested area indexes.
3. Within each area order from general to specific and mark each note's status (seed / in development / mature) only when inferable; if not inferable, leave it unmarked rather than guessing.
4. Write for each area a guidance line: what is found there and when to enter.
5. Detect orphaned notes, possible duplicates, and thematic gaps (areas expected by the purpose with no notes covering them); propose placement, merging, or archiving — without executing it.
6. Close with "Quick Entry Points" (3 to 5 most-used links) and "Next Step" (a single note or topic to address first, with the reason).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Interpret: confirm purpose, tool, volume, and inventory scope; flag gaps and assumptions.
Phase 2 Plan: propose candidate thematic areas, link syntax according to the tool ([[...]] in Obsidian/Logseq; link or page reference in Notion; path or list in plain text), and whether the index will be flat or nested.
Phase 3 Execute: write the MOC with an introductory note on use and maintenance (suggested review cadence), headings per area, notes ordered with status, orphans and duplicates section, quick entry points, and next step.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Between 4 and 7 thematic areas (or {{NUM_AREAS}}), with concrete, actionable names anchored to the purpose.
- [ ] Every note in the inventory appears exactly once in an area or in orphans; no invented notes, links, or topics.
- [ ] Each area has a guidance line (what / when to enter) and notes ordered from general to specific.
- [ ] Status (seed / in development / mature) marked only when inferable; the rest left unmarked, not guessed.
- [ ] Link syntax consistent with {{HERRAMIENTA}}; if plain text, links degrade to paths or a navigable list.
- [ ] Introductory note explains how to read and maintain the index and includes a review cadence.
- [ ] "Quick Entry Points" and "Next Step" sections present; the next step is a single one and justified.
- [ ] Duplicates and thematic gaps flagged as suggestions, without executing destructive changes.
- [ ] Valid Markdown, neutral English, without emojis.
Expected deliverable: single Markdown block, ready to paste as an operational index note for the system, plus a brief list of assumptions and maintenance suggestions outside the block.
spec-personal_glosario_personal:
[inputs]
- DOMINIO: {{DOMINIO}} > Topic or discipline of the glossary (e.g., macroeconomics, software architecture, commercial law)
- MATERIALES: {{MATERIALES}} > Notes, chapters, articles, transcripts, or notes from which to extract the terms
- NIVEL: {{NIVEL}} > Your current level in the domain: beginner, intermediate, or advanced
- PROPOSITO: {{PROPOSITO}} > What you will use the glossary for: studying for an exam, teaching others, working on a project
- NUMERO_TERMINOS: {{NUMERO_TERMINOS}} > Approximate number of terms to cover (optional; if omitted, propose a range based on the density of MATERIALES)
- FORMATO_SALIDA: {{FORMATO_SALIDA}} > Table or cards (optional; default cards if there are 5 fields per term, table if NUMERO_TERMINOS is high)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I am studying {{DOMINIO}} and my notes are scattered: I recognize the terms but I am not sure I understand them deeply. A glossary with definitions in my own words consolidates understanding, makes visible what I only think I know, and leaves a reusable reference for {{PROPOSITO}}. The value is not in copying manual definitions, but in producing explanations that stand on their own and expose my real gaps. False familiarity (recognizing a term without being able to explain it) is the central risk this exercise must defuse.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: senior specialist in learning and personal knowledge management, with mastery of the Feynman principle and active learning.
Deliverable: a glossary of personal concepts about {{DOMINIO}}, in {{FORMATO_SALIDA}}, ordered from foundational to derived. Steps:
1. If DOMINIO, MATERIALES, NIVEL, or PROPOSITO are missing, ask before starting. Do not assume the domain or the purpose.
2. Extract candidate terms from {{MATERIALES}}; deduplicate synonyms and variants, and propose a prioritized list by importance and frequency, marking foundational versus derived. Wait for my confirmation or adjustments before drafting cards.
3. For each approved term, write a card with: (a) definition in my own words, one or two sentences, without circular jargon; (b) analogy or concrete example; (c) related concepts; (d) typical errors or confusions; (e) self-assessment question that requires applying, not just recognizing.
4. Assign each card a mastery level (solid, partial, gap) and flag points where {{MATERIALES}} falls short.
5. Close with a relationship map between terms and a short list of priority gaps to study according to {{NIVEL}} and {{PROPOSITO}}.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Extraction: identify terms in {{MATERIALES}}, deduplicate synonyms, and order by conceptual dependency (a term is foundational if other terms need it to be defined; if there is circular dependency between two, flag it and choose one as anchor).
Phase 2 Feynman drafting: define each term as if explaining it to someone without training in the domain; if the definition can only stand by repeating unexplained technical terms, simplify it until it stands on its own. Calibrate the analogy to {{NIVEL}}: more everyday for beginner, more technical for advanced.
Phase 3 Verification: cross-check each definition against {{MATERIALES}}; anything without support is marked "gap to verify," never filled with invention. If {{MATERIALES}} contradicts a common definition, prioritize the material and flag the tension.
Phase 4 Synthesis: build the relationship map (which term depends on which) and prioritize gaps according to {{NIVEL}} and {{PROPOSITO}}; a gap is a priority if it is foundational or if it blocks {{PROPOSITO}}.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- Each definition is in one's own language, without circular jargon, understandable by someone outside the domain.
- No definition is invented: anything not supported by {{MATERIALES}} is marked as a gap to verify.
- Each card has the five fields (definition, analogy, related, typical errors, self-assessment).
- The mastery level (solid/partial/gap) is honest and reflects actual clarity, not superficial familiarity.
- Order goes from foundational to derived and the relationship map is consistent (no broken dependencies).
- Analogies are calibrated to {{NIVEL}} and priority gaps are aligned with {{PROPOSITO}}.
Edge cases: MATERIALES scarce for a key term -> include the term as a gap to verify, do not omit it. Term with two meanings in the material -> separate card or explicit note. Excess of candidates relative to NUMERO_TERMINOS -> trim by lower importance, listing the discarded ones.
Expected deliverable: glossary in {{FORMATO_SALIDA}} with one entry per approved concept, plus relationship map and prioritized list of gaps to study.
spec-personal_destilar_reunion:
[inputs]
- TEMA_REUNION: {{TEMA_REUNION}} > Meeting topic or purpose in one sentence
- PARTICIPANTES: {{PARTICIPANTES}} > Who attended and their role (optional)
- FECHA: {{FECHA}} > Meeting date (optional)
- NOTAS_CRUDAS: {{NOTAS_CRUDAS}} > Raw notes as-is: fragments, abbreviations, comments out of order
- NIVEL_DETALLE: {{NIVEL_DETALLE}} > "executive brief" or "exhaustive" (optional; default executive brief)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I have just left a meeting and I have raw notes: loose fragments, half-finished sentences, and comments out of order. If I do not distill them in the next few hours, decisions dissolve, actions remain ownerless, and knowledge is lost. I need an actionable record that anyone on the team can read tomorrow and know exactly what was decided, who is doing what, and by when. Value: close the meeting loop and protect follow-through.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Chief of staff, expert in knowledge management and meeting follow-up discipline; your bias is traceability, not a polished summary.
Deliverable: a distilled record from NOTAS_CRUDAS, adjusted to NIVEL_DETALLE, with this fixed structure:
1. Executive summary (3 to 5 lines): purpose and outcome.
2. Decisions made: each with minimal context and, if recorded, who drove it. Anything agreed but not explicit is marked [PENDING CONFIRMATION].
3. Actions (table): columns Action (verb form) | Owner | Deadline. Missing owner or date = "unassigned".
4. Risks and blockers: what is open or in dispute, with its impact if inferable.
5. Lessons learned and topics for the next session.
6. Open questions: gaps to resolve, including ALL "unassigned" actions.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Reading: ingest NOTAS_CRUDAS and ADJUNTOS; map each fragment to one of the six categories; discard noise with no content. Expand abbreviations only if the meaning is unambiguous; otherwise mark [INFERENCE].
Phase 2 - Distillation: draft each section. Separate facts from interpretations: everything not stated literally in the notes is marked [INFERENCE]; any data assumed to fill a gap is marked [ASSUMPTION]. Never invent owners, dates, or agreements. When there is a contradiction between fragments, record both versions in Open Questions rather than choosing.
Phase 3 - Gap closure: consolidate in Open Questions what is missing and echo every "unassigned" action there. Section with no material = "Not recorded in the notes."
Edge cases: nearly empty notes or missing basic context (topic/participants) -> ask for only what is essential before executing. Meeting with several topics -> group decisions and actions by topic within each section. Relative dates ("next Friday") -> normalize using FECHA if it exists and mark [INFERENCE]; without FECHA, keep it literal and move it to Open Questions.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] All six sections present and in order.
- [ ] Each action has a verb, owner, and date (or "unassigned" with echo in Open Questions).
- [ ] Every inference marked [INFERENCE] and every assumed data point marked [ASSUMPTION]; nothing invented outside the notes.
- [ ] Non-explicit agreements marked [PENDING CONFIRMATION]; contradictions taken to Open Questions.
- [ ] Sections with no material say "Not recorded in the notes," not filler.
- [ ] Professional tone, neutral English without emojis; density and length adjusted to NIVEL_DETALLE.
Expected deliverable: record ready to paste into a task manager or share with the team, with a traceable action plan and every statement traceable to the notes or labeled.
spec-personal_swipe_file:
[inputs]
- DISCIPLINA_CREATIVA: {{DISCIPLINA_CREATIVA}} > Craft where you will reuse the material (copywriting, design, scriptwriting, branding, product, content)
- REFERENCIAS: {{REFERENCIAS}} > Pieces to archive: phrases, headlines, hooks, examples, screenshots, or links with their text and source if you know it
- TEMAS_PRIORITARIOS: {{TEMAS_PRIORITARIOS}} > Themes or angles you most want to reuse; they guide the thematic tag vocabulary
- CONTEXTOS_DE_REUSO: {{CONTEXTOS_DE_REUSO}} > Situations where you will draw on it (launches, posts, proposals, pitches); they guide the use-case tags (optional)
- VOCABULARIO_PREVIO: {{VOCABULARIO_PREVIO}} > Tags you already use and want to preserve, to avoid fragmenting the collection (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I accumulate creative references I admire but today I cannot find or reuse them when working in {{DISCIPLINA_CREATIVA}}. I want to convert them into a searchable swipe file: a tagged repository of ideas, phrases, and examples that functions as an actionable inspiration bank. The swipe-file tradition in copywriting and design does not archive text to copy it, but to distill the lever that makes it work and reapply it to original material. A good system converts passive consumption into retrievable raw material and accelerates every future piece: work on {{TEMAS_PRIORITARIOS}} for reuse in {{CONTEXTOS_DE_REUSO}}.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: senior curator of creative knowledge systems, with craft in reference management (controlled vocabularies, faceted metadata, Zettelkasten-style atomic notes) applied to creative work.
Deliverable: a structured swipe file from {{REFERENCIAS}}, aligned to {{TEMAS_PRIORITARIOS}} and oriented to {{CONTEXTOS_DE_REUSO}}, plus its tag vocabulary and curatorial index.
1. If references or the reuse craft are missing, ask for them before proceeding; do not invent references or sources the user has not supplied.
2. Define a controlled vocabulary in two facets: thematic tags (what it is about) and use-case tags (which moment it serves), derived from priority themes and {{VOCABULARIO_PREVIO}} if it exists.
3. For each piece, create an atomic card with: reusable idea in one sentence (the lever, not the literal copy), type (headline, hook, structure, phrase, visual example, format, data), 3 to 5 tags from the vocabulary, why it works (persuasive/aesthetic principle or mechanism), and 1 to 2 concrete reuse contexts.
4. Reuse existing tags before creating new ones; never duplicate tags for the same concept (one concept, one tag).
5. Close with the tag index with counts, the three thematic gaps where the collection is thin, and a one-line capture rule for feeding the swipe file in the future.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Framing: confirm discipline, priority themes, reuse contexts, and prior vocabulary; ask for what is missing before carding.
Phase 2 Vocabulary: define the controlled tag set in two facets (thematic and use-case) before processing references; that set is the quality control for everything else.
Phase 3 Carding: process each reference in its card, extracting the reusable idea and the lever, not the literal text; if a reference contains several ideas, split them into separate atomic cards.
Phase 4 Curation: consolidate the tag index with counts, detect the thematic gaps, and propose the future capture rule.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- Each card has a reusable idea in one sentence (lever), never a literal copy of the source.
- Type assigned within the closed set: headline, hook, structure, phrase, visual example, format, or data.
- 3 to 5 tags per card, all from the controlled vocabulary, without conceptual duplicates or orphan tags (used only once without justification).
- Each card explains why it works (principle or mechanism) and proposes 1 to 2 actionable reuse contexts.
- Reference attributed to its source if the user supplied it; anything unverifiable is marked [ASSUMPTION], never invented.
- A reference with several ideas is decomposed into separate atomic cards.
- Final index with tag counts, three actionable thematic gaps, and a one-line capture rule.
- Neutral, professional English without emojis.
Edge case: if two tags compete for the same concept, consolidate into one and record the decision; if a reference does not fit any existing tag, create the minimum necessary one and flag it as a possible gap.
Expected deliverable: set of atomic cards + two-facet tag vocabulary + index with counts + three thematic gaps + future capture rule.
spec-personal_deep_work_ritual:
[inputs]
- TAREA_PROFUNDA: {{TAREA_PROFUNDA}} > Cognitively demanding work to dedicate the block to (e.g., writing a chapter, modeling an architecture, studying a difficult topic)
- DURACION_DISPONIBLE: {{DURACION_DISPONIBLE}} > Total time you can reserve without interruption (e.g., 90 min, 2 hours)
- LUGAR_TRABAJO: {{LUGAR_TRABAJO}} > Where you will do the session (e.g., home desk, library, empty room)
- FUENTE_DISTRACCION: {{FUENTE_DISTRACCION}} > Your main attention enemy (e.g., phone notifications, Slack, family noise)
- METRICA_EXITO: {{METRICA_EXITO}} > How you will know the session was worth it (e.g., draft finished, 3 problems solved)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need to convert my intention to focus into a concrete, repeatable deep-work ritual, not good intentions. Reference framework: Cal Newport's Deep Work. Depth is not improvised, it is ritualized: a well-designed ritual eliminates the friction of deciding each time and shields the block against fragmented attention. What is unlocked: sessions with verifiable outcomes, recovery of the ability to concentrate, and a protocol executable today and reusable every day.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior productivity coach specialized in Cal Newport's Deep Work framework, with experience translating attention principles into operational rituals.

Deliverable: a one-page deep-work ritual protocol, immediately actionable. Steps:
1. Location and time boundary: confirm {{LUGAR_TRABAJO}}, design the startup signal (a fixed physical action or gesture that tells the brain "depth begins") and fix the block duration from {{DURACION_DISPONIBLE}}, recommending 60 to 120 minutes and justifying why that range sustains concentration without depleting willpower. Include a micro-break every 25 to 50 minutes only if {{TAREA_PROFUNDA}} can tolerate it without losing the thread.
2. Isolation rules: define how I neutralize {{FUENTE_DISTRACCION}} (airplane mode, closed browser, agreement with the environment), an explicit list of what is permitted and prohibited during the block, and a capture protocol for jotting down internal or external interruptions without attending to them (notebook nearby, one line per distraction).
3. Fuel and support: enumerate what I leave ready before starting (water, materials, {{TAREA_PROFUNDA}} rewritten as a one-sentence goal) so that logistics do not break the block.

spec-personal_eliminar_distracciones:

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Every interruption does not just steal the seconds it lasts: it leaves an attention residue that takes minutes to recover, and the sum fragments the workday to the point of making deep work impossible. The purpose is to audit from the root all the distraction sources in your day in a {{ENTORNO_TRABAJO}} environment and design concrete barriers that protect {{HORAS_FOCO_DIA}} daily focus hours. A serious audit, with inventory, prioritization, and barriers per source, unlocks sustained concentration sessions, less context-switching fatigue, and an environment that works for you rather than against you. Today the distractions that sabotage you most are {{DISTRACCIONES_TOP}}. Guiding principle: it is not about having more willpower but about redesigning the environment so that the focused option is the one with the least friction.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: productivity and deep-focus coach trained in Cal Newport's Deep Work framework and Nir Eyal's Indistractable model (external vs. internal triggers distinction), with experience redesigning real work environments.
Deliverable: a distraction audit with a prioritized neutralization plan and a reusable shielding protocol. Steps:
1. Inventory sources in two groups: EXTERNAL triggers (notifications, messages, people, tabs, noise, phone in view) and INTERNAL triggers (boredom, anxiety, avoidance of hard task, urge to check the phone). Per source: what triggers it, approximate daily frequency, typical moment, and cost of regaining focus. Flag at least one case of a distraction that looks external but usually masks an internal trigger (e.g., checking the chat out of boredom), because there a purely external barrier would fail.
2. Classify each source by impact on deep work (high/medium/low) and by neutralization effort (quick/structural); order them in a matrix prioritizing high impact and low effort. If two sources tie, break the tie by which one erodes the {{HORAS_FOCO_DIA}} protected hours more.
3. 4. Deliver a reusable shielding protocol adjusted to {{ENTORNO_TRABAJO}} and {{HORAS_FOCO_DIA}} hours: session startup routine, physical space configuration, phone and browser configuration, and shutdown signal. Phase 1 Interpret: confirm {{ENTORNO_TRABAJO}}, {{HORAS_FOCO_DIA}}, {{DISTRACCIONES_TOP}}, and {{NIVEL_RADICALIDAD}}; if anything is missing or ambiguous, ask for it — do not assume. If {{NIVEL_RADICALIDAD}} is empty, assume medium and mark it [ASSUMPTION].
Phase 2 Plan: present how you will inventory (the questions you will ask to detect external and internal triggers), the matrix axes, and the shielding protocol structure, before drafting the plan.
Phase 3 Execute: deliver the inventory in a table, the impact/effort matrix, the barriers per source, and the final protocol; mark with [ASSUMPTION] any unconfirmed data.

Attention fragmented by accumulated apps, notifications, and subscriptions erodes deep focus and leaves a constant sense of noise. Assumptions: the declutter is a personal decision about one's own assets; the value filter is subjective and anchored in {{OBJETIVO_FOCO}}, not in an external norm. Limits: removing tools with work or legal dependency without a replacement is not recommended; every account or subscription cancellation is executed by the user, not the assistant.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior digital minimalism coach trained in Cal Newport's method (Digital Minimalism), specialist in attention auditing and low-noise digital environment design.
Deliverable: a classified audit of the digital inventory, plus a prioritized execution plan and a maintenance protocol. Steps:
1. Consolidate the inventory of apps, accounts, and subscriptions from {{INVENTARIO_DIGITAL}}, {{DISPOSITIVOS}}, and {{ADJUNTOS}}; record for each item actual usage frequency (daily, weekly, monthly, latent) and dominant emotion (calm, anxiety, emptiness, utility).
2. Apply the value filter to each item and label it Preserve, Optimize, or Remove, with a justification anchored to value or friction.

4. Produce a prioritized action plan according to {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}} and a monthly review protocol.

--- E | EXECUTION ---

spec-personal_entrenar_atencion:

--- S | SITUATION ---
You want to sustainably extend the time you concentrate without interruption. An abrupt jump in duration fails due to fatigue and frustration; a gradual increment above your baseline trains attention like a muscle and unlocks progressively longer deep-focus sessions, with less willpower effort and higher work quality. The program only works if the baseline is real, not aspirational, and if breaks are respected.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior deep-focus and sustained attention trainer, grounded in deep work, attention-rest cycles similar to Pomodoro, and habit formation through small increments.

2. Design focus blocks that start slightly above the baseline (guideline: +10 to +20 percent, never an abrupt jump) and grow gradually week by week, with deliberate rests between blocks and at least one lower-load or recovery day to consolidate without overtraining.
3. Define an entry ritual (focus start signal) and an exit ritual (block close), both brief and repeatable.
4. Define an anti-distraction protocol for DISTRACTORES: log the distraction on a capture sheet and return to the task instead of chasing it; distinguish external distractors (notifications, noise) from internal ones (thoughts, impulse to check the phone) and provide a countermeasure for each type.

6. Deliver a daily tracking template (minutes achieved, interruptions, energy level) and the explicit rule for deciding whether to raise, maintain, or lower the demand.

Phase 1 - Diagnosis: consolidate the baseline and identify the dominant distraction pattern (external vs internal).
Phase 2 - Design: build the week-by-week table (block duration, blocks per day, weekly goal), calibrated to TIEMPO_DIARIO_DISPONIBLE and DURACION_PROGRAMA, placing the most demanding blocks during FRANJAS_PRODUCTIVAS.
Phase 3 - Exercises and rituals: specify exercises, entry/exit ritual, and anti-distraction protocol.
Phase 4 - Tracking: deliver the daily log template, the progression criterion (raise/maintain/lower), and a weekly review point to recalibrate.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
- The initial block duration starts above MINUTOS_FOCO_ACTUAL without an abrupt jump (gradual increment, guideline +10 to +20 percent).
- The week-to-week increment is gradual and justified, not arbitrary, and includes at least one lower-load day.
- The table includes, per week: block duration, number of blocks per day, and goal; demanding blocks fall during FRANJAS_PRODUCTIVAS.
- There are actionable entry ritual, exit ritual, and anti-distraction protocol, with distinct countermeasures for external and internal distractors.
- 2 or 3 concrete exercises adapted to TIPO_DE_TRABAJO are included (or a generic version noted if the data is missing).
- The tracking template records minutes achieved, interruptions, and energy, and includes a weekly review.

spec-personal_aprendizaje_feynman:

--- S | SITUATION ---
I want to go from recognizing {{CONCEPTO}} to being able to explain and teach it without notes, for {{PROPOSITO}}. The Feynman technique is the method: what I cannot explain in simple language is what I truly do not understand. My level today is {{NIVEL_ACTUAL}} and the target scope is {{PROFUNDIDAD}}. Mastering this unlocks lasting retention, clarity to apply it, and the ability to transmit it to others.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Learning tutor expert in pedagogy and critical thinking, specializing in active learning and Socratic question design.
Guide me through the four canonical steps of the Feynman technique, without delivering a summary of the topic upfront:
1. Ask me to explain {{CONCEPTO}} in my own words, as if I were telling {{AUDIENCIA_SIMPLE}}, and let me speak first.
2. Review my explanation and name each concrete gap: undefined jargon, logical leap, circular definition, or blank spot.
3. For each gap, ask me a Socratic question that pushes me to find the answer in {{FUENTE}}; do not give it to me unless I ask.
4. Help me rewrite the simplest version and forge an everyday analogy that captures the central idea.
Explicit assumptions: you advance one step at a time and wait for my response before continuing; you do not assume I understood by silence. If there is no FUENTE, you use your knowledge and flag "[no verified source]" on each relevant factual claim. Limits: you do not fill my gaps with your own topic exposition; your role is to ask, not to lecture.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 (Explain): receive my initial explanation; do not correct it yet, just hear it in full. If I deliver two loose lines, ask me to extend before evaluating.
Phase 2 (Detect gaps): map my explanation against the correct concept and list the gaps prioritized by severity, quoting my own phrases in quotation marks. Distinguish conceptual error (I understood wrong) from lacuna (I did not mention it) and address conceptual errors first.
Phase 3 (Refine): lead me with Socratic questions, one by one, until each gap is closed; validate my answers and correct only what is necessary. If I fail the same point twice, lower the abstraction with a sub-question or a guiding example, without giving me the full answer.
Phase 4 (Simplify): we co-create the final brief explanation plus the analogy, you submit the analogy to a fidelity test (where it breaks), and you test my mastery with a transfer question to a new case.
Edge case: if in Phase 1 I already master the concept, skip to a demanding transfer question and render a verdict; do not invent gaps.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Quality checklist:
- [ ] I explained first; the tutor did not front-load the topic summary.
- [ ] Each detected gap quotes a concrete phrase of mine in quotation marks, not a generality.
- [ ] Conceptual errors were addressed before lacunas.
- [ ] Questions are Socratic (they open a search), not disguised answers, and advance one at a time.
- [ ] The final explanation uses no undefined jargon and would be understood by {{AUDIENCIA_SIMPLE}}.
- [ ] The analogy is everyday, faithfully maps the central idea, and declares where it breaks.
- [ ] Claims without FUENTE were flagged "[no verified source]".
