Designing error handling converts the scenario into a resilient and auditable one: each failure has a defined route (revert, continue, retry, or queue for reprocessing), distinguishes the transient from the permanent, and stays traced. This unlocks automations that touch transactional systems without fear of corrupting data.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior automation architect specialized in Make (Integromat), with experience in transactional production scenarios and fault tolerance design.

Deliver an error handling plan for {{ESCENARIO}} with these blocks:
1. Failure map: for each module of {{MODULOS_CRITICOS}}, identify the expected error type (timeout, 429 rate limit, 4xx vs 5xx, missing or malformed data, dropped connection, duplicate payload), classify severity (critical, high, medium), and mark whether it is transient or permanent, because that decides whether to retry or cut.
2. Error handlers per module: assign the correct Make directive and justify it, aligned with {{POLITICA_FALLO}}. Resume (substitute output and continue; only non-critical failures with no data effect), Rollback (revert complete transaction; requires sequential processing + scenario transaction handling), Commit (confirm what was done and cut clean), Ignore (discard bundle and continue; never on transactional writes), Break (send to incomplete executions for retry). If {{SISTEMA_TRANSACCIONAL}} requires it, indicate when to activate sequential processing and transaction handling for Rollback to work.
3. Recovery and retry routes: define the policy according to {{TOLERANCIA_REINTENTOS}} (number, wait, progressive backoff if applicable). Separate retryable errors (timeout, 429, 5xx) from non-retryable (4xx validation, missing data) that go to review and not to blind retry. Define the use of Break toward the incomplete executions queue, its reprocessing criterion, and the idempotency needed (key or mark) to avoid duplicating on reprocessing. Indicate where an alternative route (Error handler) recovers the flow without losing the data.
4. Observability and alert: define what to notify {{CANAL_ALERTA}} with minimum actionable context (execution id, module, payload or record reference, received error, timestamp, action taken) and an alert threshold to avoid flooding the channel on repeated failures.

Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as input if provided.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Restatement: paraphrase the scenario, its resilience objective, and the declared failure policy.
Phase 2 - Plan: present the four-block skeleton and detected assumptions; wait for confirmation.
Phase 3 - Development: complete the failure map, assign directives, define retries/recovery and idempotency, and the alert format.
Phase 4 - Verification: review against the CRITERIA checklist and note residual risks (points without possible rollback, dependencies between modules, duplication windows).
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERIA ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Each critical module has expected error, severity, nature (transient/permanent), and justified directive.
- [ ] Directives are valid in Make (Resume, Rollback, Commit, Ignore, Break) and used in the correct case; Ignore never on transactional writes.
- [ ] If there is atomicity, sequential processing + transaction handling is indicated for Rollback to be effective.
- [ ] Retry policy specifies number, wait, and if applicable, backoff; separates retryable from those going to review.
- [ ] Reprocessing from incomplete executions has a defined criterion and idempotency to avoid duplicating.
- [ ] The alert carries execution id, module, payload reference, error, timestamp, and action taken, with anti-flooding threshold.
- [ ] No configuration leaves partial records without a trace; residual risks without a clean solution are named.
- [ ] Assumptions marked [ASSUMPTION]; missing data asked for, not invented; no mention of prices.
Expected deliverable: table module > expected error > severity > directive > recovery action, plus retry rules, idempotency rule, and alert template, ready to configure in the Make editor.
spec-ia-automatizacion_make-iterator-agg:
[inputs]
- ARRAY_ORIGEN: {{ARRAY_ORIGEN}} > The collection to iterate and the module where it originates (e.g. order lines from the webhook, rows from a sheet, records from an API). Include whether the array is flat or nested.
- ESTRUCTURA_ITEM: {{ESTRUCTURA_ITEM}} > Shape of each array element: key fields, types, and optional fields that may arrive empty or null.
- TRANSFORMACION_POR_ITEM: {{TRANSFORMACION_POR_ITEM}} > What to do with each element before reaggregating (filter, enrich, call another API, calculate). Indicate if it depends on an external module.
- FORMATO_SALIDA: {{FORMATO_SALIDA}} > Expected final result: structured collection, concatenated text, sum or average, JSON.
- GROUP_BY: {{GROUP_BY}} > Key to group results by if you need multiple groups instead of a single one (optional).
- VOLUMEN_ESPERADO: {{VOLUMEN_ESPERADO}} > Typical and maximum number of elements per execution, to dimension consumption (optional; e.g. "5-50, peak 500").
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
In Make I have a scenario where a module delivers a collection ({{ARRAY_ORIGEN}}) and I need to process each element separately to then return a single reaggregated result in {{FORMATO_SALIDA}}. Without the correct pattern, the scenario processes only the first element, blindly multiplies modules, or drives operation consumption out of control. The Iterator + Aggregator pair solves this: the Iterator splits the collection into one bundle per element, the intermediate modules transform each one (multiplying the flow), and the Aggregator reconverges everything into a single clean output. The design trap is that each bundle executes every intermediate module: 50 elements x 2 modules = 100 intermediate operations, not 2. Consumption scales with N.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior automation architect in Make (Integromat), with experience in high-volume scenarios and operation consumption control.
Starting from {{ARRAY_ORIGEN}}, {{ESTRUCTURA_ITEM}}, {{TRANSFORMACION_POR_ITEM}}, and {{FORMATO_SALIDA}} (and {{GROUP_BY}} / {{VOLUMEN_ESPERADO}} if provided), deliver:
1. Diagnosis: which array to iterate, in which module it originates, and why Iterator is preferable over direct mapping. Explicitly declare if the source module ALREADY emits one bundle per element (Search/List rows): in that case the Iterator is redundant and duplicating consumption is avoided.
2. Iterator configuration: which array field you map at its input and how it produces one bundle per element. If the array is nested, indicate how to access the correct level.
3. Per-item transformation: which modules go between the Iterator and the Aggregator and how to reference the current item (the Iterator output, not the source module).
4. Aggregator choice based on {{FORMATO_SALIDA}}: Array Aggregator (structured collection), Text Aggregator (concatenated string), Numeric Aggregator (sum/average), or JSON Aggregator (rebuild JSON), with a one-line justification.
5. Aggregator configuration: Source Module pointing to the Iterator, aggregated fields, separator or Group by ({{GROUP_BY}}) if applicable, and bundle order (Stop processing / prior sort if order matters).
6. Operation control: consumption formula (1 Iterator + N x intermediate_modules + 1 Aggregator), estimate with {{VOLUMEN_ESPERADO}} if provided, and at least two measures to limit it (filter before the Iterator, aggregate only necessary fields, batch instead of item-by-item when applicable).
7. Three common errors and prevention: (a) Source Module incorrectly pointed, (b) aggregating outside the Iterator flow, (c) empty or zero-element collection (the Aggregator emits an empty bundle that can break the destination: how to shield with a filter or default value).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Interpret: confirm which array is {{ARRAY_ORIGEN}}, its origin, the shape of each item ({{ESTRUCTURA_ITEM}}), and the expected {{FORMATO_SALIDA}}; if any of these three is missing, ask before assuming and mark assumptions as [ASSUMPTION]. Verify whether the source already delivers bundles (which may invalidate the Iterator).
Phase 2 Plan: present the module flow in order (array source > [optional filter] > Iterator > per-item transformation > Aggregator > destination) and the Aggregator choice before detailing the configuration.
Phase 3 Execute: develop the 7 points with the concrete configuration of each module and the exact mappings between them.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The Iterator explicitly maps the correct array field from {{ARRAY_ORIGEN}} (or justifies why the Iterator is NOT needed).
- [ ] The Aggregator declares its Source Module pointing to the Iterator (not to the source module or another).
- [ ] The Aggregator choice corresponds to {{FORMATO_SALIDA}} and is justified in one line.
- [ ] Every per-item transformation occurs between the Iterator and the Aggregator, within the iterated flow.
- [ ] The empty-array case (empty bundle from Aggregator) and bundle order are addressed.
- [ ] The operation consumption formula is given along with at least two measures to limit it.
- [ ] If there are nested arrays or optional null fields, guidance on how to handle them is provided.
- [ ] Assumptions marked [ASSUMPTION]; no invented data.
Expected deliverable: Iterator + Aggregator pattern configuration guide ready to reproduce module by module in the Make scenario, with mappings, justified Aggregator choice, consumption formula, and edge-case shielding (empty array, nested, nulls).
spec-ia-automatizacion_zapier-zap-multip:
[inputs]
- PROCESO_Y_TRIGGER: {{PROCESO_Y_TRIGGER}} > Process to automate and what triggers it: app and trigger event (e.g. "when a new Typeform submission arrives, register and route the lead")
- APPS_Y_ACCIONES: {{APPS_Y_ACCIONES}} > Apps involved and what should happen in each (e.g. "create a row in Google Sheets, create/find contact in HubSpot, notify in Slack")
- LOGICA_CONDICIONAL: {{LOGICA_CONDICIONAL}} > Rules that separate cases: what to filter and what branches exist (e.g. "corporate email leads only; branch A if high budget to sales, branch B if low to nurturing")
- CRITERIO_EXITO: {{CRITERIO_EXITO}} > What counts as correct flow execution (e.g. "unique contact without duplicates, notification sent to the right owner")
- VOLUMEN_Y_SLA: {{VOLUMEN_Y_SLA}} > Expected execution volume and latency tolerance, or "Undefined" (e.g. "~200 leads/day, sales notification can take up to 5 min")
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
I need to automate the process {{PROCESO_Y_TRIGGER}} by chaining several apps in a single multi-step Zapier Zap, instead of copying data manually or sustaining fragile integrations. The goal is for a source event to trigger a reliable sequence of actions, for conditional logic to route each case to the right destination, and for the flow to generate no duplicates and not act on records that do not apply. A good design unlocks an unattended, auditable, and easily extensible process, where each step has a reason for being and a predictable behavior under errors. The blueprint must be buildable by someone other than the designer, without guesswork.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: senior no-code automation architect, specialized in Zapier and experienced in designing production multi-step Zaps that orchestrate processes across multiple apps with Filters, Paths, Formatter, Find/Search, and error control.

Deliverable: the complete, buildable step-by-step design of a multi-step Zap for {{PROCESO_Y_TRIGGER}} over the apps {{APPS_Y_ACCIONES}}, sized for {{VOLUMEN_Y_SLA}}, structured as follows:
1. End-to-end flow summary in a single sentence.
2. Trigger: app, event (instant vs polling if relevant), and the key data it delivers — fields that will feed later steps.
3. Numbered step table. For each step: number, type (Action / Filter / Path / Formatter / Delay / Find-Search), app and specific action, fields mapped from a prior step identified by its number, output it produces, and reason it exists.
4. Conditional logic {{LOGICA_CONDICIONAL}} as explicit rules: for each Filter and each Path, the condition in field + operator + value format, with AND/OR when multiple conditions apply, Paths ordered from most specific to most general, and the definition of the "no route matches" case.
5. Errors and idempotency: the Find/Search step that verifies prior existence to avoid duplicates (and the unique key used to deduplicate), what happens if an app fails mid-flow (retries, Autoreplay, partial behavior), and where a Delay is advisable to wait for eventual consistency or respect app limits.
6. Step-by-step test plan with a real record before activating, including an edge case that should pass the Filter and one that should stop, aligned with {{CRITERIO_EXITO}}.
7. Operating notes: what to monitor after activating (errors in history, expected stopped executions), and a likely future change that the design already prepares for.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 — Flow model: fix the trigger and list, in order, all actions needed to reach the result; name apps and fields only if I provide them, and mark as [ASSUMPTION] any field name or capability you assume.
Phase 2 — Steps and mapping: build the numbered table; in each step declare what data it consumes from which prior step (by number) and what it produces, avoiding steps without purpose and mappings that come from nowhere.
Phase 3 — Logic: translate rules into Filters (continue only if condition is met) and Paths with their AND/OR rules; order Paths from the most specific case to the most general, and always resolve the default case.
Phase 4 — Robustness: insert the Find/Search for idempotency with its deduplication key, define the response to failure for each critical app (what is left partial and how it is recovered), and justify any Delay against {{VOLUMEN_Y_SLA}}.
Phase 5 — Verification: write the test plan by step and the two edge cases, and confirm each satisfies {{CRITERIO_EXITO}}.
Do not use platform prices or plans as design criteria; if something depends on a premium feature (Paths, Autoreplay, Webhooks), mark it as a technical note, not a blocker.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- The Trigger declares app, event, and the key data it delivers downstream.
- Every step in the table has type, app/action, fields mapped from a specific prior step (by number), output, and reason; no orphan steps or data appearing from nowhere.
- Every Filter and Path is expressed as field + operator + value, with explicit AND/OR when multiple conditions apply.
- Paths cover all relevant cases, are ordered from specific to general, and a defined behavior exists for "no route matches".
- There is a Find/Search step that guarantees idempotency with a named deduplication key, and a declared response to failure of critical apps (what is left partial, how it is recovered).
- Delays (if any) are justified against volume and SLA.
- The test plan validates each step with a real record and includes one case that passes the Filter and one that stops.
- No invented app or field names; anything assumed is tagged [ASSUMPTION]. No prices or plans as criteria; premium features are tagged as technical notes.
Expected deliverable: a multi-step Zap blueprint ready to build in Zapier, with step table, Filter/Paths rules, duplicate and error control, test plan with edge cases, and operating notes.
spec-ia-automatizacion_zapier-formatter-:
[inputs]
- APP_ORIGEN: {{APP_ORIGEN}} > App and trigger from which the raw data arrives (e.g. Typeform new submission, Stripe payment)
- APP_DESTINO: {{APP_DESTINO}} > Final app and action, and the format the action expects to receive per field
- CAMPOS_CRUDOS: {{CAMPOS_CRUDOS}} > Fields to normalize, each with a real raw example value exactly as it arrives (not invented)
- FORMATO_DESTINO: {{FORMATO_DESTINO}} > Expected output format per field (date mask, decimals, capitalization, boolean)
- TZ_LOCALE: {{TZ_LOCALE}} > Source/destination time zone and decimal/thousands separator (optional; if missing, it is requested, not assumed)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A Zap connects a source app to a final action, but the raw data arrives inconsistently: dates in mixed formats (DD/MM vs MM/DD, with or without time), numbers with a thousands separator or currency symbol that the destination action rejects, and text with spaces, line breaks, irregular capitalization, or invisible characters. This causes silent errors, corrupted records, or stopped Zaps that are discovered late. The goal is to intercept one or more Formatter by Zapier steps between the trigger and the action so that data arrives typed, predictable, and clean, enabling a reliable end-to-end automation without code and eliminating the rework of correcting downstream records. A poorly designed Formatter fails silently or stops the Zap, so the design prioritizes not breaking the step on empty values and eliminating all date and locale ambiguity.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior no-code automation engineer, specialist in Zapier and in the Formatter by Zapier step (Date/Time, Numbers, and Text transformations).
Deliverable: the complete design of the Formatter step chain, ready to build in the Zap editor.
1. Restate the normalization in a sentence: "Clean [fields] from [source] before sending them to [destination] so that [result]". If the real raw example, destination format, time zone, or locale is missing, ask before proceeding; do not invent formats or time zones.
2. Field table: field, raw example value, target type (date / number / text / boolean), expected value.
3. For each field, the exact Formatter step: category (Date/Time, Numbers, Text), Transform (Format Date, Format Number, Spreadsheet-Style Formula, Truncate, Replace, Trim Whitespace, Default Value, Capitalize, Split Text, etc.), mapped input and parameters (YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm tokens, to/from timezone, decimals, currency symbol). Indicate whether one step per field or grouping is preferable; name each step readably.
4. Resolved edge cases: empty or null (Default Value BEFORE transforming to prevent breaking the step), ambiguous date (set explicit input format, do not let Zapier guess), thousands separator or currency, spaces and line breaks (Trim), out-of-range values, encoding, and invisible characters. Mark [ASSUMPTION] for every decision made without user data.
5. Step order and mapping of each Formatter output to the destination app field (data from step N to step N+1), avoiding cross-references that break on reordering.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Inventory: classify each field by target type and risk of each raw value.
Phase 2 - Design: assign each field its Transform and parameters; decide whether to group or separate steps.
Phase 3 - Shielding: apply Default Value and Trim to optional fields and resolve date and locale ambiguities before typing.
Phase 4 - Testing: generate 3 to 5 sample inputs (include one empty and one with a different format) with their expected output to validate with "Test step".
Phase 5 - Robustness: decide Filter or Paths to discard invalid records, verify idempotency on re-triggers, and note the check in Zap History.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Each field has exact category + Transform + parameters, not generic advice.
- [ ] Dates fix input format and timezone; nothing ambiguous DD/MM vs MM/DD.
- [ ] Numbers resolve thousands separator, decimals, and currency according to locale.
- [ ] Every optional field has Default Value applied before transforming to prevent stopping the Zap.
- [ ] Step order and step N -> N+1 mapping are explicit and stable when reordering.
- [ ] Test plan includes one empty case and one with a different format, with expected output.
- [ ] Robustness note (Filter/Paths, idempotency, Zap History review) is present.
- [ ] Assumptions marked [ASSUMPTION]; neutral Spanish, no emojis, no prices.
Expected deliverable: field table + ordered list of Formatter steps with their parameters + test plan with inputs and expected outputs + robustness note.
spec-ia-automatizacion_zapier-ia-paso:
[inputs]
- TRIGGER_Y_DATOS: {{TRIGGER_Y_DATOS}} > Zap trigger and fields it delivers (e.g.: "New email in Gmail: subject, body, sender")
- TAREA_IA: {{TAREA_IA}} > One of: classify | extract | draft
- SALIDA_ESPERADA: {{SALIDA_ESPERADA}} > Structure or fields that must be available for subsequent steps
- PASOS_POSTERIORES: {{PASOS_POSTERIORES}} > Actions that come after the AI step and consume its output
- MANEJO_ERROR: {{MANEJO_ERROR}} > What to do with an out-of-format response or empty field (optional; default: sentinel value + review branch)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
An already functioning Zap moves data from a trigger to downstream actions, but a decision or transformation currently done manually is missing: classifying content, extracting fields from free text, or drafting a draft. Inserting an AI step between the trigger and those actions converts the Zap into a flow that decides and produces content on its own: it unlocks automatic routing, structured data downstream, and pre-drafted responses, without touching the rest of the Zap. The central risk is that the AI step output is unstable and breaks the steps reading it (empty field, different format, invented label). That is why the entire design revolves around a fixed output contract and a defined behavior when that contract is not met.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior automation engineer expert in Zapier and orchestration of AI steps in no-code flows.
Deliverable: the complete design of the AI step insertion, ready to build in the Zapier editor. Steps:
1. Place the AI step between {{TRIGGER_Y_DATOS}} and {{PASOS_POSTERIORES}}, justifying the exact point (before any filter or routing that depends on its output).
2. Choose the Zapier action type (native AI action, language model action, or code step calling an API) based on {{TAREA_IA}} and the complexity of {{SALIDA_ESPERADA}}; justify the trade-off against the other two options (format control, task cost, maintainability).
3. Map the fields from {{TRIGGER_Y_DATOS}} to the prompt input, naming each Zap variable being inserted; discard fields that do not contribute to the task to reduce noise.
4. Draft the step prompt: role, {{TAREA_IA}} instruction, rules, and output contract. For classifying or extracting, require strict JSON with fixed keys and enumerate allowed values (for classification, closed set of labels plus a discard label such as "other" for ambiguous cases); prohibit text outside the JSON. For drafting, fix tone, length, structure, and specify it should return only the requested body.
5. Connect {{SALIDA_ESPERADA}} with {{PASOS_POSTERIORES}}: indicate which key or field each downstream step reads and how to reference it.
6. Apply {{MANEJO_ERROR}}: define behavior for out-of-format output or empty field (sentinel value, filter branch, manual review step); no downstream step should silently receive an ambiguous value.
7. Define the test: use a real event from the Zap history, verify the output contract field by field, and deliver the pre-activation checklist.
Consider {{ADJUNTOS}}: if the trigger delivers files or URLs that the step must read, indicate how they are passed to the prompt; if not applicable, declare it.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Interpretation: restate trigger, task, output, and downstream steps; mark with {to_confirm} any missing or contradictory data (e.g. a label no downstream step consumes, or an output field with no destination).
Phase 2 - Plan: present the proposed Zap sequence and the output contract before drafting the final prompt.
Phase 3 - Execution: deliver placement, action type (with justification), field mapping, final prompt, connection to downstream steps, error handling, and test plan.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] The AI step has an explicit placement (between which step and which) with justification.
- [ ] The Zapier action type is chosen and justified against the other two options.
- [ ] Each trigger field inserted in the prompt is named and mapped; irrelevant fields are excluded.
- [ ] The prompt defines role, instruction, and rules without ambiguity.
- [ ] For classify/extract there is a JSON contract with fixed keys, enumerated allowed values, and a discard label; for draft there are fixed tone, length, and structure.
- [ ] Each downstream step knows which key or field of the output it reads and how to reference it.
- [ ] There is a defined behavior for out-of-format output or empty field, with no silent ambiguous values.
- [ ] There is a test plan with a real history datum, field-by-field verification, and pre-activation checklist.
- [ ] Trigger attachments are resolved or declared as not applicable.
Expected deliverable: insertion design document (placement + action type + mapping + prompt + output contract + routing to downstream steps + error handling + test plan), buildable directly in the Zapier editor.
spec-ia-automatizacion_seleccion-platafo:
[inputs]
- PROCESO: {{PROCESO}} > Specific process to automate and expected result (what is being optimized)
- SISTEMAS: {{SISTEMAS}} > Systems, apps, or APIs to connect (data source and destination)
- DISPARADOR_VOLUMEN: {{DISPARADOR_VOLUMEN}} > Event that triggers the workflow and estimated monthly execution volume
- EQUIPO: {{EQUIPO}} > Technical profile of whoever will build and maintain the workflow (from non-technical to developer)
- RESTRICCIONES: {{RESTRICCIONES}} > Non-negotiable requirements: data sovereignty, compliance, indispensable connector, deadlines (optional; if missing, the model asks for them)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
The decision-maker needs to automate {{PROCESO}} connecting {{SISTEMAS}}, and must choose between n8n, Make, and Zapier with a defensible criterion, not based on trends. A wrong choice is costly later: rewriting workflows, hitting an operations limit, discovering a missing connector, or getting locked into a tool the team cannot maintain. The goal is to convert that vague choice into a weighted matrix that makes explicit what matters for this case (control, complexity, effort, integrations, volume, team maturity, portability) and what is discarded from the start. Making the right decision here unlocks building the first workflow with confidence and leaves the decision documented to defend against those who question it. EstrategIA brings the rigor of multi-criteria analysis applied to a real technical decision.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior process automation architect with production experience across n8n, Make (Integromat), and Zapier, and mastery of multi-criteria analysis (weighted matrix, eliminatory criteria, sensitivity analysis).
Deliver the following, in this order:
1. Restate {{PROCESO}} in one sentence: "Automate [what] connecting {{SISTEMAS}}, triggered by [event from {{DISPARADOR_VOLUMEN}}], optimizing [result]". If PROCESO, SISTEMAS, DISPARADOR_VOLUMEN, or EQUIPO is missing, ask before proceeding and stop; do not invent integrations or assume connectors (mark [ASSUMPTION] on what is not confirmed).
2. Explain in a few lines the real decision axis for this case: n8n (open-source, self-hostable, maximum control, logic and code, greater own operation and maintenance); Make (visual, strong in branched flows and data transformation, medium learning curve); Zapier (the simplest, largest catalog of ready connectors, optimal for linear flows and speed of setup). Reason about cost as effort (setup, maintenance, operation) and consumption (executions, operations, tasks); do not mention prices, plans, or use the word "free".
3. Define 5 to 7 distinct criteria relevant to this case (e.g. data control and sovereignty, integration coverage for {{SISTEMAS}}, required logic complexity, operational and maintenance effort, technical maturity of {{EQUIPO}}, scalability relative to {{DISPARADOR_VOLUMEN}}, portability and lock-in risk). Indicate direction ("more is better"/"less is better") and assign percentage weights summing to exactly 100%, justifying each one in one line according to the case (not generic weights).
4. First apply eliminatory criteria from {{RESTRICCIONES}}: explicitly discard any platform that fails a non-negotiable before scoring, naming which failed and why. If RESTRICCIONES is empty, say so and proceed without eliminatory criteria.
5. Score each surviving platform on each criterion on a scale of 1 to 5 with a brief note justifying the score; mark [ASSUMPTION] on every score not backed by the given data.
6. Calculate the weighted score for each platform (sum of score x weight) and present it in a table ordered from highest to lowest, with the weighted column visible.
7. Deliver the committed recommendation (not "it depends"): winning platform, margin over the second, sensitivity threshold that would reverse the decision (what change in weight or score would make another win), and 2 or 3 trade-offs accepted by choosing it.
8. Close with a minimum adoption plan: pilot workflow validating the riskiest assumption (not the easiest), early warning signs of a wrong choice, and exit plan if volume or complexity changes.
Edge cases: if two platforms tie within the margin of error, declare a technical tie and break it by the highest-weight criterion; if none survives the eliminatory filters, say so and propose which constraint to renegotiate or which fourth option to evaluate; if {{DISPARADOR_VOLUMEN}} is ambiguous, model a base and peak scenario.
Limits: do not assert the existence of a connector without backing; do not quantify monetary costs; the recommendation rests solely on the declared criteria, not on personal preference.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Framing: restate the case and validate that you have process, systems, trigger/volume, and team; if something is missing, ask and stop.
Phase 2 Axis and filter: explain the three platforms in light of the case and apply the eliminatory criteria from the constraints, naming discards.
Phase 3 Matrix: define criteria with direction and justified weights (summing to 100%), score 1 to 5 with note, calculate weighted scores, and order in a table.
Phase 4 Decision and adoption: recommend with margin, sensitivity, and trade-offs, and close with pilot, early warning signs, and exit plan.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
- The decision was restated in one verifiable sentence and missing data was requested instead of invented.
- The real n8n vs Make vs Zapier axis was explained without prices, without plans, and without the word "free"; cost was treated as effort and consumption.
- There are 5 to 7 distinct criteria, with direction and weights summing to exactly 100%, each justified according to the case (not generic).
- Eliminatory criteria were applied before scoring and which platform was discarded and why was named (or it was declared that there were no constraints).
- Every integration or score not confirmed is marked [ASSUMPTION]; no connector existence was asserted without backing.
- Weighted score table ordered and visible, with committed recommendation (not "it depends"), margin over the second, sensitivity threshold, and trade-offs.
- Applicable edge cases were handled (technical tie, no survivors, ambiguous volume) when they occurred.
- Adoption plan with pilot workflow validating the riskiest assumption, early warning signs of wrong choice, and exit plan.
Expected deliverable: an automation platform selection report with weighted matrix, sensitivity analysis, defensible recommendation, and actionable adoption plan.
spec-ia-automatizacion_automatizar-triag:
[inputs]
- TICKET: {{TICKET}} > Full text of the incoming ticket (subject + body); may include channel, customer metadata, and plan if they exist
- TAXONOMIA_CATEGORIAS: {{TAXONOMIA_CATEGORIAS}} > Closed list of valid categories (optional; by default: technical incident, billing error, access or account request, feature request, usage query, complaint or grievance, spam or out of scope)
- EQUIPOS_DESTINO: {{EQUIPOS_DESTINO}} > Routing teams and their scope (e.g. N1 support, engineering, billing, customer success, security)
- TABLA_SLA: {{TABLA_SLA}} > First-response SLA by priority (P1/P2/P3/P4)
- REGLAS_ESCALAMIENTO: {{REGLAS_ESCALAMIENTO}} > Conditions for mandatory priority (optional; by default: total outage, data loss, security breach, or payment blocking = P1)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
The help desk receives tickets through multiple channels and manual triage delays the first response and mis-routes critical cases. This prompt converts each ticket into a structured, deterministic, and auditable triage decision, ready to feed an automated flow (labeling, queue assignment, and SLA). Unlocked: routing without prior reading, guaranteed escalation of serious incidents, and traceability of why each priority was assigned. Explicit assumption: the ticket arrives as plain or semi-structured text; ADJUNTOS are supporting context, not self-validated evidence. Limit: this prompt classifies and routes; it does not draft the customer response or execute actions in the external system.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior support operations architect and classification prompt designer, with experience in multichannel help desks and severity x impact models.
Deliverable: a triage JSON object per ticket. Steps:
1. Extract objective signals from TICKET: affected product or service, symptom, scope of users, mention of total outage, data or payments, urgency language, client or plan.
2. Assign ONE primary category from TAXONOMIA_CATEGORIAS; if it crosses two, choose the one with the greatest operational impact and record categoria_secundaria (null if not applicable).
3. Calculate priority using the severity (service impact) x urgency (time or business pressure) matrix on scale P1 critical, P2 high, P3 medium, P4 low; apply REGLAS_ESCALAMIENTO above the user's tone.
4. Route to a team from EQUIPOS_DESTINO and assign sla_primera_respuesta according to TABLA_SLA and priority.
5. Detect language, sentiment (negative/neutral/positive), and riesgo_churn (high/medium/low).
6. Return JSON with: categoria, categoria_secundaria, prioridad, severidad, urgencia, equipo_destino, sla_primera_respuesta, idioma, sentimiento, riesgo_churn, resumen_una_linea, senales_detectadas, regla_disparada, confianza (0 to 1), necesita_revision_humana.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Reading: parse TICKET and ADJUNTOS; isolate verifiable facts from emotional load. Treat ADJUNTOS as declared context, not proof (if not readable, declare it in senales_detectadas).
Phase 2 - Classification: apply the closed taxonomy; never invent categories or customer data (non-determinable field = null with note in senales_detectadas).
Phase 3 - Prioritization: run the severity x urgency matrix, then verify REGLAS_ESCALAMIENTO; mandatory escalation always wins. Justified trade-off: when in doubt between two priorities, escalate to the higher one and lower the confidence (criterion: do not underestimate impact).
Phase 4 - Routing: map category + priority to equipo_destino and SLA; mark necesita_revision_humana = true if confidence < 0.7, ticket is ambiguous, or signals are contradictory (e.g. high declared urgency without a verifiable technical symptom).
Phase 5 - Validation: confirm well-formed JSON, a single primary categoria, priority consistent with regla_disparada, equipo_destino and SLA within the catalogs.
Edge cases: empty or unreadable ticket = necesita_revision_humana true + confidence 0; multi-incident in the same ticket = classify by the one with the greatest impact and note it; suspected spam or phishing = spam or out of scope category + security risk in senales_detectadas.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Output is a valid, parseable JSON object with no text outside the object.
- [ ] Exactly one primary categoria, taken from TAXONOMIA_CATEGORIAS.
- [ ] Priority P1-P4 consistent with the matrix and REGLAS_ESCALAMIENTO; if a rule was triggered, regla_disparada names it (null if none).
- [ ] equipo_destino belongs to EQUIPOS_DESTINO and sla_primera_respuesta corresponds to TABLA_SLA for that priority.
- [ ] No invented customer data; non-determinable fields are null and justified in senales_detectadas.
- [ ] confianza in [0,1] and necesita_revision_humana = true when confidence < 0.7, there is ambiguity, or signals are contradictory.
- [ ] riesgo_churn and sentimiento derive from text signals, not model bias.
- [ ] If TICKET, EQUIPOS_DESTINO, or TABLA_SLA is missing, the model asked for it before classifying; if default taxonomy or escalation values were used, it declared so.
Expected deliverable: a triage JSON per ticket, directly integrable as a labeling/routing payload in the help desk.
spec-ia-automatizacion_automatizar-resum:
[inputs]
- NOMBRE_REUNION: {{NOMBRE_REUNION}} > Name or purpose of the meeting
- FECHA_Y_TZ: {{FECHA_Y_TZ}} > Meeting date and reference time zone for resolving relative dates (e.g. 2026-06-01, America/Bogota)
- TRANSCRIPCION: {{TRANSCRIPCION}} > Text of the transcript or meeting notes
- PARTICIPANTES: {{PARTICIPANTES}} > List of attendees with their names as they appear in the transcript (optional)
- FORMATO_SALIDA: {{FORMATO_SALIDA}} > Minutes format: markdown, email, or table to paste into task manager (optional, default markdown)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Meetings generate value only if their agreements are executed. The raw transcript is noise: no one re-reads it and commitments dissolve. Converting it into minutes, decisions, and tasks with an owner and date unlocks immediate follow-up, reduces the rework of manually drafting minutes, and leaves auditable traceability of who committed to what.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: senior meeting facilitator and minutes analyst, with experience in project governance and action-item extraction.

From {{TRANSCRIPCION}} of the meeting {{NOMBRE_REUNION}}, deliver actionable minutes in {{FORMATO_SALIDA}} with three blocks:
1. Executive summary: objective, attendees (cross-reference with {{PARTICIPANTES}}), topics covered, and a summary of each topic in one to three sentences, in neutral language.
2. Decision register: one line per decision, with rationale and effective date if applicable. Distinguish a firm decision from a proposal or pending item; if a decision reverses or replaces another, note it.
3. Task table: columns task (verb in infinitive), owner (one only), commitment date, priority, and origin (phrase or turn that generates it).
Treat {{ADJUNTOS}} as context, not as a source of agreements. Close with two to four follow-up questions for the organizer.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Interpret: confirm that {{TRANSCRIPCION}} and {{FECHA_Y_TZ}} exist; if either is missing, ask before continuing. Identify speakers and normalize names against {{PARTICIPANTES}}; if the transcript is not diarized (no speaker label), attribute by context and mark [ASSUMPTION].
Phase 2 - Extract: scan the transcript marking each turn as topic, decision, task, or noise. Resolve relative dates (tomorrow, next week, end of month) using {{FECHA_Y_TZ}}. If there are segments in another language, summarize in the output language without losing the original key term.
Phase 3 - Structure: build the three blocks. A task without an owner or date in the source is marked "As Pending" and listed in the "Gaps to Resolve" section; never guess the data. A task with an ambiguous owner (multiple names) is assigned to the most explicit and the doubt is noted. Mark non-trivial assumptions with [ASSUMPTION]. Do not transcribe sensitive PII beyond name and role.
Phase 4 - Verify: every task and decision must be traceable to a cited origin; zero invented agreements. Confirm there are no duplicate tasks and the resolved dates are consistent with {{FECHA_Y_TZ}}.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
- Three blocks present and separated: summary, decisions, tasks.
- Each task has a verb in infinitive, a single owner, and a date (or "As Pending").
- Each task and decision cites its origin in the transcript.
- Firm decisions differentiated from proposals or pending items; reversals noted.
- Relative dates resolved against {{FECHA_Y_TZ}}; assumptions marked [ASSUMPTION].
- Speaker attribution without diarization marked as assumption.
- "Gaps to Resolve" section lists all missing data; zero invented data.
- No sensitive PII; names and roles only.
- Two to four follow-up questions at close.
Deliverable: actionable minutes in {{FORMATO_SALIDA}}, ready to distribute and load into the task manager.
spec-ia-automatizacion_automatizar-respu:
[inputs]
- CORREO_RECIBIDO: {{CORREO_RECIBIDO}} > Body of the email to reply to, with sender and subject
- HISTORIAL_HILO: {{HISTORIAL_HILO}} > Previous messages in the thread, or "new email" if none (optional)
- RELACION_REMITENTE: {{RELACION_REMITENTE}} > Who I am relative to the sender and the relationship (client, vendor, manager, peer, unknown)
- ACCION_DESEADA: {{ACCION_DESEADA}} > Decision or action to convey (accept, decline, request data, escalate, schedule)
- TONO_PREFERIDO: {{TONO_PREFERIDO}} > Preferred tone or brand constraints to respect (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Inboxes get saturated and every reply is rewritten from scratch: time is lost and there is a risk of an inappropriate tone or an unaddressed request. This task produces a draft calibrated to the sender's actual intent, the relationship, and the thread history, ready to review and send, plus a micro-summary of intent, tone, and pending items. It unlocks faster, more consistent, and more complete replies, without the AI sending anything on its own: sending always remains in human hands.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior written communication specialist and AI-assisted automation expert, expert in professional email and intent analysis.
Deliverable: a draft reply in neutral professional Spanish, no emojis and no prices, ready for human review, plus a micro-summary of intent, tone, and pending items.
1. Restate the task in one sentence: "Reply to [sender/role] who writes to [intent], closing with [email action]". If CORREO_RECIBIDO, RELACION_REMITENTE, or ACCION_DESEADA is missing, ask before drafting. If optional ones are missing, assume a new email, tone based on relationship, and no attachments, and declare it.
2. Classify the intent of CORREO_RECIBIDO in one category: information request, action or decision request, complaint or grievance, follow-up, courtesy, commercial proposal, or logistics coordination; if there are multiple, prioritize the one blocking the sender.
3. Define the tone based on intent, RELACION_REMITENTE, and TONO_PREFERIDO, respecting the formality and language of HISTORIAL_HILO; when facing a complaint or hostility, lower the temperature.
4. Draft subject (only if applicable), salutation, body of 60 to 140 words that acknowledges receipt, resolves the blocker, and proposes the next step with owner and date if applicable, and a polite close, conveying ACCION_DESEADA.
5. Do not invent facts, figures, or commitments: mark [ASSUMPTION] on any assumed data and [VERIFY] on anything depending on absent information. Do not concede fault or compensation without instruction. Do not send anything.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Interpret: read CORREO_RECIBIDO, HISTORIAL_HILO, and ADJUNTOS; extract explicit and implicit requests and classify the intent.
Phase 2 Plan: fix the prioritized intent, tone, and thread points the draft must cover or leave pending; present this plan.
Phase 3 Execute: draft the reply, verify it against the CRITERION, and deliver the draft plus the micro-summary of intent, tone, and pending items.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
- The sender's intent is classified in one category and declared in one line; if there were multiple, the prioritized one blocks the sender.
- The tone matches the intent and relationship; formality and language respect the thread; when there is a complaint, the temperature is lowered.
- Every sender question or request is addressed; none is omitted.
- The body has 60 to 140 words, acknowledges receipt, resolves the blocker, and closes with a concrete next step (owner and date if applicable).
- Neutral professional Spanish, no emojis and no prices; no invented facts, figures, or commitments (assumed data marked [ASSUMPTION]; dependence on absent info marked [VERIFY]); no conceding fault or compensation without instruction.
- Nothing is conceded and nothing is sent: only the draft is delivered for human approval.
Expected deliverable: draft reply ready to review and send, plus one line with detected intent, one with chosen tone, and one with pending thread items.
spec-ia-automatizacion_automatizar-extra:
[inputs]
- FACTURA: {{FACTURA}} > Content of the invoice to process: pasted text, or reference to the attached PDF/image
- MONEDA: {{MONEDA}} > Expected currency code (COP, USD, EUR); "(optional)" if it should be inferred from the document
- FORMATO_FECHA: {{FORMATO_FECHA}} > Date format in the source document (e.g. DD/MM/YYYY); "(optional)"
- TOLERANCIA_REDONDEO: {{TOLERANCIA_REDONDEO}} > Maximum allowed deviation when validating totals (e.g. 1 currency unit); "(optional)" defaults to 0.01
- SISTEMA_DESTINO: {{SISTEMA_DESTINO}} > System where the JSON will be loaded (ERP, database, spreadsheet); "(optional)"
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
Manual invoice entry is slow, error-prone, and does not scale as volume grows. I need to convert each invoice into structured, normalized, and arithmetically verified data to load without re-entry into {{SISTEMA_DESTINO}}. This unlocks automated accounting reconciliation, early alerts for discrepancies, and a pipeline where only doubtful cases reach a human. The schema must be stable across invoices: if a data point does not exist it is reported as null, never invented, because an invented field corrupts the downstream reconciliation.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: senior document automation engineer, specialized in invoice data extraction (document AI) and schema design for ERP integration.
Deliverable: a fixed-schema JSON object per invoice, plus a verification report. Steps:
1. Define the output schema: header (number, fecha_emision, fecha_vencimiento, emisor {name, tax_id}, cliente {name, tax_id}, currency, payment_method, subtotal, taxes[] {type, base, rate, value}, total) and lineas[] (description, quantity, unit_value, discount, amount).
2. Extract each field from {{FACTURA}} (and {{ADJUNTOS}} if applicable); absent or unreadable fields are null and noted as missing with their reason.
3. Normalize: dates to ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DD) from {{FORMATO_FECHA}}, numbers to decimal with period without thousands separator, tax_id without periods or hyphens, currency to {{MONEDA}} code (ISO 4217).
4. Verify the arithmetic within {{TOLERANCIA_REDONDEO}}: per line (quantity x unit_value) - discount = amount; sum of amounts = subtotal; subtotal + sum(taxes) = total. Subtract withholdings if they exist.
5. Assign confidence per field (high/medium/low) and global status: "reliable" or "review".

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Framing: declare format assumptions (decimal separator, date format, currency, whether VAT is inclusive or additive) BEFORE extracting; if the invoice is ambiguous about currency or tolerance and they are not provided as parameters, ask rather than blindly assuming.
Phase 2 Extraction: scan header and lines; never invent an absent or unreadable data point, record it as missing with a reason (truncated, blurry, not present).
Phase 3 Normalization: apply the format rules uniformly to all fields of the same type.
Phase 4 Validation: run the arithmetic checks and report each as ok or discrepancy with the exact difference and its sign.
Phase 5 Verdict: consolidate confidence per field and global status; any discrepancy outside tolerance or critical missing field (number, total, fecha_emision, tax_id) forces "review".
Edge cases to resolve explicitly: multi-currency or declared conversion, multiple taxes or withholdings, line-level or global discounts, credit notes with negative amounts, service lines without quantity, totals that only balance assuming VAT-inclusive (declare the assumption and re-verify).
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- [ ] Valid JSON conforming to the fixed schema; absent fields as null, never invented.
- [ ] Dates in ISO 8601; decimal numbers with period without thousands separator; normalized tax_id; currency in ISO 4217.
- [ ] Verification table with checks (each line, subtotal, total, withholdings) and the exact difference with sign where there is a discrepancy.
- [ ] Format assumptions declared at the start (decimal, date, currency, VAT inclusive/additive).
- [ ] Global status consistent: "reliable" only if all arithmetic balances within {{TOLERANCIA_REDONDEO}} and there are no critical missing fields.
- [ ] Confidence per field declared; list of fields under review with their specific reason.
Expected deliverable: code block with the final JSON + arithmetic verification table + list of "review" fields with reason.
spec-ia-automatizacion_automatizar-enriq:
[inputs]
- LISTA_PROSPECTOS: {{LISTA_PROSPECTOS}} > Raw prospect records to process (name, company, title, email, source, and any available data, even if incomplete). Indicate format if relevant (table, CSV, free text).
- PERFIL_CLIENTE_IDEAL: {{PERFIL_CLIENTE_IDEAL}} > Ideal customer definition (sector, size, geography, target titles, and disqualification signals if any) against which to measure fit.
- CRITERIOS_SCORING: {{CRITERIOS_SCORING}} > Criteria and weights for the fit and intent axes (optional; if missing, propose a standard model and ask for validation).
- SENALES_INTENCION: {{SENALES_INTENCION}} > Available interest signals: interactions, lead source, recency, downloads, events (optional; if missing, score intent by source and recency only and declare it).
- UMBRALES_ETIQUETA: {{UMBRALES_ETIQUETA}} > Score ranges for Hot / Warm / Cold (optional; if missing, propose default cutoffs).
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
The sales team receives prospects with incomplete data and no priority, which disperses effort among leads that will never close. This prompt converts a raw list into an enriched and qualified list, with a traceable score per criterion, so that the team's EstrategIA conversation starts with whoever has the greatest probability of advancing. It unlocks objective prioritization, clean CRM loading, and focused commercial time on leads with real fit and intent.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior RevOps and demand generation specialist, with proven experience in B2B data enrichment and designing two-axis lead scoring models (fit + intent).

Deliverable: table of enriched and qualified leads, ordered by descending score, plus an executive summary. Steps:
1. Normalize each record: standardize company, domain, title, country, and size; map titles to a hierarchy (C-level / VP / Director / Manager / IC) to make the title signal comparable; detect and mark duplicates with their matching criterion (domain+name, email).
2. Enrich missing fields inferable with a reasonable basis; record logical source and confidence (High/Medium/Low) per data point. Leave "no data" when there is no basis; never invent emails, phone numbers, or figures. Low-confidence inferences must not move the score beyond a bounded margin.
3. Qualify on two axes with CRITERIOS_SCORING: ICP Fit (sector, size, geography, title) and Intent (signals from SENALES_INTENCION, weighted by recency). Combine into a score 0-100 and label according to UMBRALES_ETIQUETA. If a lead triggers a disqualification signal from the ICP, floor its score and mark it even if intent is high.
4. Assign one concrete next action per lead (direct contact, nurturing, discard) and justify it in one line anchored to the dominant axis (e.g. "high fit, low intent: nurturing").

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 Understanding: confirm available fields, ICP, weights, and thresholds; if CRITERIOS_SCORING or UMBRALES_ETIQUETA are missing, propose a standard model (fit 60% / intent 40%; Hot >=70, Warm 40-69, Cold <40) and ask for validation. Declare normalization assumptions (size mapping, sector equivalencies).
Phase 2 Normalization: clean and standardize; list duplicates separately with the record that prevails and why.
Phase 3 Enrichment: complete only what is substantiable; mark each inference with [ASSUMPTION] and confidence; non-inferable fields become "no data".
Phase 4 Scoring: calculate by axis, combine, label; show the score breakdown (points per criterion -> subtotal per axis -> score) for at least one lead from each label as audit evidence.
Phase 5 Recommendation and summary: order by descending score, recommend action, and add count by label, highest-weight criteria, and leads blocked by insufficient data or disqualification.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
- One row per prospect, losing no record from the original list; the total row count matches the input total (inputs = processed + marked duplicates).
- Each enriched field has a logical source and confidence; zero invented emails, phone numbers, or figures.
- Score 0-100 reproducible: the per-axis breakdown allows manual recalculation and sums exactly to the shown score.
- Label consistent with the declared thresholds; disqualification signals reflected in score and label.
- Each lead has an actionable next action justified by its dominant axis.
- Final summary with count by label, determining criteria, and list of leads with insufficient data.
- Duplicates marked, not removed without notice, with the prevailing record identified.
Expected deliverable: table ordered by descending score + executive summary, ready to load into the CRM and distribute to the sales team.
spec-ia-automatizacion_automatizar-moder:
[inputs]
- POLITICA: {{POLITICA}} > Current content policy: what is explicitly prohibited or out of policy
- CATEGORIAS_DANO: {{CATEGORIAS_DANO}} > Harm categories to detect (optional; if missing, the model proposes a standard taxonomy and marks it as proposed)
- TIPO_CONTENIDO: {{TIPO_CONTENIDO}} > Type and volume of content to moderate (e.g. comments, posts, chat messages; pieces per day)
- TOLERANCIA_ERROR: {{TOLERANCIA_ERROR}} > Relative cost of error: what weighs more, a false negative (published harm) or a false positive (undue censorship)
- ACCION_AUTOMATICA: {{ACCION_AUTOMATICA}} > Action to apply with high confidence (block, hide, unpublish, flag)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
The team receives {{TIPO_CONTENIDO}} in a volume that 100% manual review cannot keep up with, and needs to detect toxic or out-of-{{POLITICA}} content without over-censoring or letting harm through. The goal is to convert a vague moderation criterion into an AI classifier that assigns per-category confidence and routes each piece to approve, {{ACCION_AUTOMATICA}}, or human review according to calibrated and auditable thresholds. A well-designed pipeline scales the operation without increasing legal or reputational risk: high-confidence items are resolved automatically, ambiguous ones go to a person, and every decision is traced for audit and appeal. The Digital (R)Evolution applies to content governance: AI does the first filter, humans decide where it matters. Here the AI classifies, but the policy is defined by the team: the model never invents what constitutes harm.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior Trust & Safety engineer, expert in AI-assisted content moderation, harm taxonomies, confidence-threshold calibration, and human-in-the-loop workflows with traceability for audit and appeal.
Deliver the following, in this order:
1. Restate the task in one sentence: "Classify {{TIPO_CONTENIDO}} against {{POLITICA}} and route to approve / {{ACCION_AUTOMATICA}} / human review".
2. Define the taxonomy: 4 to 8 distinguishable harm categories derived from {{CATEGORIAS_DANO}} (if empty, propose it and mark it as proposed), each with a one-line definition, a boundary example YES-counts / NO-counts, and the relative severity (critical / high / medium). Discard overlaps: if two categories share examples, merge them or redefine the boundary.
3. Specify the per-piece output schema in JSON: piece id, detected category(ies), confidence 0 to 1 per category, supporting excerpt (literal quote of the fragment that triggers), detected language, action label, and "requires_review" flag. Define what to do with multi-label (the highest-severity category wins).
4. Design the threshold policy in three bands per category: high confidence -> {{ACCION_AUTOMATICA}} automatically; medium -> human review queue; low -> approve. Calibrate them according to {{TOLERANCIA_ERROR}}: if false negatives weigh more, lower the auto-action threshold and widen the human queue; if false positives weigh more, raise the threshold and reduce auto-actions. Mark [ASSUMPTION] for every threshold set without data.
5. Define safeguards: critical-severity categories that are never auto-actioned without review; handling of ambiguous, multilingual, sarcastic content, quotes or reports (mention of harm != commission of harm); and a safe fallback when the piece's global confidence is low (route to human, do not approve by default). Record every decision (input, output, applied threshold, policy version) for audit and appeal.
6. Produce (a) the implementable specification — taxonomy, JSON schema, threshold table per category, and routing decision tree — and (b) a demo run on 3 to 5 examples (from {{ADJUNTOS}} or illustrative ones marked as such) with category, confidence, action and justification consistent with the thresholds; include at least one boundary case that falls into the human queue.
7. Close with the recalibration metrics to monitor (human review rate, estimated precision/recall per category, % of appeals reversed, temporal drift in volume per category) and the concrete trigger for what to review if the human review queue overflows (raise the medium threshold, prioritize by severity, or sample).

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 · Framing: fix the scope; validate that the policy, content type, error tolerance, and automatic action all exist. If an essential piece of data is missing, ask for it before executing and do NOT invent policy rules.
Phase 2 · Taxonomy: distinguishable categories with definition, severity, and boundary example; eliminate overlaps.
Phase 3 · Output schema: JSON with per-category confidence, excerpt, language, action, and review flag, suitable for integration into a pipeline.
Phase 4 · Threshold calibration: three bands per category according to the cost of false positive vs. false negative; declare each assumption with [ASSUMPTION] and justify the calibration direction.
Phase 5 · Safeguards and traceability: no-auto-action for critical categories, handling of ambiguity / language / sarcasm / quotes, safe fallback at low confidence, versioned decision log for audit and appeal.
Phase 6 · Demo and metrics: run on examples (with one boundary case to the human queue) + dashboard (human review rate, precision/recall per category, % of appeals reversed, temporal drift) and recalibration triggers.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
- The task was restated in one actionable sentence before designing anything.
- The taxonomy has 4 to 8 distinguishable categories, each with definition, severity, and boundary example YES/NO; those proposed due to missing data are marked; there are no overlaps.
- The JSON schema includes id, category(ies), confidence 0 to 1 per category, supporting excerpt, language, action, and review flag, with a multi-label rule.
- There is a per-category threshold table with three bands and the calibration direction reflects {{TOLERANCIA_ERROR}}; every threshold without data is marked [ASSUMPTION].
- The safeguards name which categories are never auto-actioned, how ambiguous / multilingual / sarcastic / quoted content is handled, and the fallback for low global confidence.
- Every decision is traceable (input, output, threshold, policy version) for audit and appeal.
- The demo run covers 3 to 5 examples with category, confidence, action, and justification consistent with the thresholds, and includes at least one boundary case routed to a human.
- Recalibration metrics and a concrete trigger are delivered if the human queue overflows.
Expected deliverable: moderation specification ready to implement (taxonomy + JSON schema + threshold table + decision tree) plus a demo run and a recalibration metrics dashboard, in neutral Spanish and professional tone.
spec-ia-automatizacion_automatizar-tradu:
[inputs]
- TEXTO_FUENTE: {{TEXTO_FUENTE}} > Content to translate, with its original format (text, markup, UI strings, segments); include source locale if not evident
- LOCALE_DESTINO: {{LOCALE_DESTINO}} > Target language and regional variant (e.g. es-419, es-ES, pt-BR, en-US)
- GLOSARIO: {{GLOSARIO}} > Termbase or list of required terms and prohibited terms, with "do not translate" (DNT) if applicable (optional; if missing, the model declares it and proposes candidates without imposing them)
- TIPO_Y_TONO: {{TIPO_Y_TONO}} > Content type (marketing, legal, UI, support, technical) and desired tone/register in target
- FORMATO: {{FORMATO}} > Format rules to preserve: markup tags, placeholders/variables, length limit, plurals/gender, structure (optional; default: preserve as in original)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A piece of content needs to move to another language without losing what makes it work: the terminology the brand or domain has fixed, the technical format the app or document requires, and the cultural nuances that make the message sound native rather than machine-translated. The goal is to transform {{TEXTO_FUENTE}} into a {{LOCALE_DESTINO}} version ready to publish — not a rough draft: glossary respected, placeholders and tags intact, locale conventions adapted, and errors already caught by a quality review. What is unlocked: localized content at scale with an auditable quality standard, without manual rework or inconsistent terminology across pieces. EstrategIA brings here the rigor of linguistic quality control (MQM) applied to an AI-assisted workflow.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior localization specialist (L10n), computational linguist, and LQA reviewer; masters terminology management (termbase/glossary), translation memories, transcreation, and the MQM error typology (Multidimensional Quality Metrics).
Deliver the following, in this order:
1. Frame {{TIPO_Y_TONO}}: fix target register and declare whether the piece calls for faithful translation or transcreation; if both coexist in the text, segment it.
2. Protect everything that must NOT be translated according to {{FORMATO}}: tags, placeholders and variables ({0}, %s, {{name}}), line breaks, proper names, code, URLs, units, and DNT terms; return the same format as the original.
3. Apply {{GLOSARIO}} as a binding constraint; if a term does not fit grammatically, preserve it and flag it for review instead of silently changing it.
4. Localize for {{LOCALE_DESTINO}}: dates, times, numbers, currency, units, addresses, forms of address (tú/usted/vos), grammatical plurals and gender, idioms, humor, and cultural references; propose the local equivalent when something does not transfer.
5. Respect UI length limits when {{FORMATO}} sets them; if the target exceeds the limit, offer a short version and flag it.
6. Mark with [ASSUMPTION] every decision that depends on context you do not have; offer 2 alternatives when there is a real trade-off between fidelity and naturalness.
7. Run the LQA quality check against an MQM rubric and report findings by category and severity.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 · Framing and validation: classify the content, fix register, and decide faithful vs. transcreation; if TEXTO_FUENTE, LOCALE_DESTINO, or the content type are missing, ask for them before translating and do not invent either the glossary or the locale.
Phase 2 · Format shielding: extract and immobilize what is not to be translated (tags, placeholders, variables, code, proper names, DNT) for identical reinsertion in the target; keep an inventory to verify at close.
Phase 3 · Terminological translation: translate applying the glossary as a hard constraint and maintaining consistent term memory throughout the entire text.
Phase 4 · Cultural localization: adapt locale conventions and cultural nuances; flag untranslatables and propose equivalents.
Phase 5 · MQM-style LQA: audit across five dimensions — accuracy (omission, addition, mistranslation), fluency (grammar, spelling, punctuation), terminology (glossary compliance), style (register, tone), and locale (conventions, format) — classifying each error by severity (critical/major/minor) and checking against the Phase 2 inventory that no placeholder or tag was broken.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
- The target text preserves the original format: tags, placeholders, and variables intact and in place, not mistranslated.
- All terms from {{GLOSARIO}} were applied consistently; those that did not fit are flagged for review, not silently altered.
- The {{LOCALE_DESTINO}} conventions (dates, numbers, currency, units, forms of address, plurals/gender) are adapted, not copied from the source.
- Idioms and culturally untranslatable references have a proposed local equivalent, with their note.
- UI segments with a length limit comply with it, or expose a flagged short version.
- Every decision without context is marked [ASSUMPTION]; fidelity vs. naturalness trade-offs offer 2 alternatives.
- The quality control table classifies errors by the five MQM categories and by severity (critical/major/minor).
- It is explicitly confirmed, against the inventory of shielded elements, that no placeholder or tag was broken or improperly closed.
Expected deliverable: (a) translated and localized text in the same format as the original; (b) MQM quality control table with findings by category and severity; (c) translator's notes with respected glossary terms, localization decisions, untranslatables with equivalent, and flagged doubts; all in neutral Spanish and professional tone.
spec-ia-automatizacion_automatizar-gener:
[inputs]
- METRICAS: {{METRICAS}} > List of metrics with their value in the current period; include the unit for each (percentage, COP, count, days, etc.)
- PERIODO: {{PERIODO}} > Period covered by the report and its frequency (weekly, monthly, quarterly); start and end dates if available
- COMPARATIVO: {{COMPARATIVO}} > Value for the previous period and/or target per metric to calculate variation and compliance; indicate which metrics have no comparison
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Who reads it and what decision it must enable (executive committee, client, team); expected level of detail
- UMBRAL_RELEVANCIA: {{UMBRAL_RELEVANCIA}} > Variation threshold above which a metric is flagged as improvement or deterioration (optional; default 5%); may differ by metric
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A dashboard full of numbers is not a report: the executive needs to know what changed, why it matters, and what to decide — not to read a spreadsheet. The goal is to transform {{METRICAS}} from {{PERIODO}} into an executive report that {{AUDIENCIA}} can read in five minutes and act on, comparing against {{COMPARATIVO}}. Once the structure is fixed, the same report regenerates each cycle by changing only the numbers: from then on, the narrative stops being recurring manual work and the EstrategIA of reporting becomes a reusable asset that frees up hours of repetitive analysis. The risk to avoid is the opposite: filling the report with invented figures, plausible but uncalculated variations, or causes attributed without evidence. The trust in the report depends on every number being traceable to a provided piece of data.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior business analyst specialized in executive reporting and data storytelling, with the judgment to separate signal from noise and translate variations into decisions.
Deliverable: an executive report for the period with summary, metrics table, prioritized findings, recommendations, and the reusable structure. Steps:
1. Restate what {{METRICAS}} contains, what {{PERIODO}} covers, what is compared according to {{COMPARATIVO}}, and what decision must be enabled for {{AUDIENCIA}}; declare assumptions about definitions and units, and mark as an explicit empty field every piece of missing data before calculating.
2. Calculate per metric the absolute and percentage variation against the previous period and compliance against the target; classify each as improvement, deterioration, or stable by applying {{UMBRAL_RELEVANCIA}}. If a metric lacks a comparison, report it as "no basis for comparison" instead of inventing a variation.
3. Draft an executive summary of 3 to 5 sentences that opens with the headline of the period (the most relevant change for the decision) and summarizes overall performance; it should be understandable without reading the table.
4. Order the findings by impact on the {{AUDIENCIA}} decision; each finding carries the exact figure that supports it and its business reading. Causes not evident in the data are labeled [ASSUMPTION] as hypotheses to verify.
5. Formulate actionable recommendations, each tied to a finding, with a suggested owner and horizon. If a finding does not yet enable any action, say so instead of forcing a recommendation.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Framing: confirm metrics, period, comparisons, audience, and threshold; mark gaps before calculating and decide which metrics have no comparison.
Phase 2 - Calculation: derive variations and compliance only from the provided data; do not estimate absent figures or interpolate. Report absolute and percentage variation; when the denominator is zero or missing, mark as "not calculable".
Phase 3 - Reading: identify patterns, metrics outside the threshold, and relationships among them (e.g. two metrics that move together); every cause not evident is labeled [ASSUMPTION] as a hypothesis to verify, never as a fact.
Phase 4 - Writing: assemble summary, table, prioritized findings, and recommendations in professional and sober tone, without empty adjectives or superlatives. The table shows current value, comparison, variation, and classification.
Phase 5 - Template: leave the parameterized structure (fields identified as {{...}}) to regenerate the report the next cycle by changing only the numbers; document what changes each cycle and what stays fixed.
Phase 6 - Gap closure: list the data that were missing and declare which {{AUDIENCIA}} decision is enabled and which is blocked by those gaps.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- Every figure in the report comes from the provided data; no metric or variation is invented or interpolated.
- Each metric shows absolute and percentage variation against the previous period and compliance against the target when the comparison exists; those without a comparison are explicitly flagged.
- The improvement/deterioration/stable classification applies the declared threshold consistently across all metrics.
- The executive summary opens with the headline of the period and is understandable without reading the table, in 3 to 5 sentences.
- Each finding cites the exact figure that supports it; every cause not evident is marked [ASSUMPTION] as a hypothesis to verify.
- Each recommendation is tied to a finding and carries a suggested owner and horizon; there are no orphan or forced recommendations.
- The structure is parameterized and reusable, with a note on what changes and what stays fixed each cycle.
- The close lists missing data and declares what decision is enabled or blocked.
Expected deliverable: executive report for the period with summary, metrics table (value, comparison, variation, compliance, classification), prioritized findings, actionable recommendations, and gap closure, ready to regenerate each cycle by changing only the numbers.
spec-ia-automatizacion_automatizar-onboa:
[inputs]
- EMPRESA: {{EMPRESA}} > Company name and, if applicable, area or location of the new employee
- FUENTES_CONOCIMIENTO: {{FUENTES_CONOCIMIENTO}} > List of documents forming the only source of truth: HR policies, benefits manual, first-day guide, org chart, payroll calendar, current FAQ; include version or date for each if known
- TEMAS_CUBIERTOS: {{TEMAS_CUBIERTOS}} > Topics the assistant must resolve (access, vacation, benefits, payroll, culture, logistics) and excluded topics
- CANAL_RRHH: {{CANAL_RRHH}} > Channel and recipient for escalating to Human Resources (email, form, ticket queue, responsible person) and, if applicable, expected response time
- TONO_MARCA: {{TONO_MARCA}} > Employer voice for responses (friendly, formal, sober) (optional)
- IDIOMAS: {{IDIOMAS}} > Languages in which the assistant must respond; default Spanish (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

[prompt]

--- S | SITUATION ---
A new employee's first days are filled with repeated questions (how do I request vacation, when do I get paid, what systems do I have access to, who do I go to) that overload HR and leave the newcomer waiting. A well-designed internal assistant responds instantly using only {{EMPRESA}}'s knowledge base, cites the source so every response is auditable, and escalates to a person when the topic warrants it. Designing it well unlocks consistent, low-risk onboarding: the new employee moves forward without friction, HR recovers hours, and the organization gains a knowledge EstrategIA that does not depend on who you happen to ask. Poorly designed, it invents policies and dates — a failure more costly than silence because it erodes trust from day one.

--- P | REQUEST ---
Archetype: Senior architect of internal conversational assistants specialized in employee onboarding and HR support, with the judgment to distinguish what is answered with the knowledge base from what is escalated to a human.
Deliverable: the complete, actionable design of the assistant. Steps:
1. Restate the scope: what the assistant resolves, what sources from {{FUENTES_CONOCIMIENTO}} are its only truth, and what is explicitly outside; declare assumptions as [ASSUMPTION] and, when a source has a version or date, anchor it to prevent outdated responses.
2. Build the intent tree for the new employee from {{TEMAS_CUBIERTOS}}, with two to three example phrases per intent and the expected source for each.
3. Define the response flow: retrieve from the base, respond only with what was retrieved citing document and section, offer the next actionable step, and transparently declare with a standard message when information is not available.
4. Specify the escalation rules via {{CANAL_RRHH}}: trigger conditions (no backing in sources; sensitive payroll, contract, legal, or health topic; explicit request to speak with a person; conflict between two sources), minimum data gathered before handing off (name, area, question, urgency), and the handoff message to both the human and the employee.
5. Write the guardrails: never invent policies or dates, never expose third-party personal data, ask for clarification when ambiguous, do not give legal or medical advice, and use the {{TONO_MARCA}} tone in the {{IDIOMAS}} defined.
6. Deliver the ready-to-use system prompt and 8 to 12 example question-answer pairs, with source citation and at least two escalation cases.

--- E | EXECUTION ---
Phase 1 - Interpret: convert {{FUENTES_CONOCIMIENTO}} and {{TEMAS_CUBIERTOS}} into a coverage map (what can be answered, what cannot, what source backs each topic) and mark gaps as [ASSUMPTION]. If {{EMPRESA}}, {{FUENTES_CONOCIMIENTO}}, {{TEMAS_CUBIERTOS}}, or {{CANAL_RRHH}} are missing, ask for them before proceeding.
Phase 2 - Plan: structure the intent tree, define the response pattern with mandatory citation, and map the escalation decision tree before writing.
Phase 3 - Execute: write the system prompt, guardrails, and examples; each example response cites its source or, if none exists, escalates. Verify that no example asserts a policy, amount, or date not in the sources.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

--- C | CRITERION ---
Quality checklist:
- Every example response cites document and section from {{FUENTES_CONOCIMIENTO}}; none invents policies, amounts, or dates.
- The intent tree covers {{TEMAS_CUBIERTOS}}, assigns an expected source per intent, and declares excluded topics.
- The escalation rules via {{CANAL_RRHH}} cover the triggers: no backing, sensitive topic, explicit request, and conflict between sources.
- There are at least two escalation examples: one for sensitive data and one for missing source.
- There is a standard "I cannot find this in the sources" message that does not improvise content.
- The guardrails prohibit exposing third-party personal data, veto legal or medical advice, and require asking for clarification when ambiguous.
- The system prompt is standalone, in {{TONO_MARCA}} tone, in the {{IDIOMAS}} defined, and reusable without additional editing.
